F107 / provisional KI#430 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED ADVCIV SIDE-CONSTRUCTION BUG
PREEMPTIVEWAR BUILDS OUR PRESENT AND PREDICTED CITY BASES INCONSISTENTLY
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PreEmptiveWar::evaluate compares the rival side's projected city ratio with our
side's projected city ratio to estimate whether a currently threatening rival is
likely to become more dangerous over the long run.

The rival side is constructed consistently. For each rival player, teammate or
vassal, an existing vassal is included at half weight in BOTH current and
predicted cities, while a newly predicted capitulation is included at half
weight in predicted cities only.

Our side is not constructed symmetrically. It starts with team-wide city counts:

    scaled rOurPredictedCities = kOurTeam.getNumCities()
            - (int)militAnalyst().lostCities(eWe).size();
    scaled rOurCurrentCities = kOurTeam.getNumCities();

and then handles our vassals as follows:

    if (existing vassal)
        rOurCurrentCities += 0.5 * (cities - predicted losses);
    else if (new predicted capitulation)
        rOurPredictedCities += 0.5 * (cities - predicted losses);

An EXISTING vassal is therefore present in our current baseline but disappears
entirely from our predicted baseline. Even if the simulated war changes nothing
about that vassal, merely having the vassal can make our side appear to shrink
between present and future. This directly biases rTheirEdge upward and can create
or magnify PreEmptiveWar utility against the rival.

There is a related multi-member-team mismatch: the initial city base is the
whole team's kOurTeam.getNumCities(), but projected losses subtract only
lostCities(eWe) for the one player whose aspect is currently being evaluated.
Losses predicted for our living teammate therefore remain counted in the team
future-city numerator. Because WarEvaluator evaluates living team members
separately, this produces member-specific partial versions of what is otherwise
a team-level power forecast rather than one coherent future team city total.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 contains this present/predicted construction. The archaeology
shows the existing-vassal asymmetry is longstanding, not introduced by SAS. The
clean repair shape is to construct current and predicted "our side" from the same
participants and weights, applying predicted city changes only to the predicted
copy. Existing vassals should contribute to both; newly capitulating vassals only
to predicted. For multi-member teams, projected losses/gains should likewise be
aggregated consistently for the whole team if the base quantity is team-wide.


F108 / provisional KI#431 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED ADVCIV VARARGS UB
ULTERIORMOTIVES UWAI LOG FORMAT HAS THREE CONVERSIONS BUT ONLY TWO ARGUMENTS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
UlteriorMotives contains the following report call in a live UWAI logging path:

    log("Attitude level towards %s: %d, refusal thresh: %d",
            m_kReport.leaderName(eThey), towardThem());

The format string requires three values after the format string (%s, %d, %d),
but only two are supplied. CvString::formatv therefore reads a nonexistent third
vararg for the "refusal thresh" conversion when the report is enabled. This is
undefined behavior: the log can print arbitrary stack/register data and the call
has no valid C/C++ varargs contract.

A mechanical audit of every log(...) call in WarUtilityAspect.cpp found no other
format/argument-count mismatch, so this is a bounded defect rather than evidence
of a wider report-format family.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 has the same call. The direct repair is to pass the actual
DeclareWarRefuseAttitudeThreshold (or whatever threshold the report intended to
show) as the third argument, or remove the third conversion/text if the value is
not needed.


F109 / provisional KI#432 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED ADVCIV WRONG-OBJECT / WEIGHT
KINGMAKING VALUES A NEW RIVAL VASSAL FROM THE RIVAL'S ASSET POOL AND FULL WEIGHT
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
KingMaking::theirRelativeLoss loops over the rival, its teammates, existing
vassals and teams predicted to capitulate to the rival. In the branch for a NEW
predicted vassal, eTheirAlly correctly identifies that future vassal:

    if (kCapitulationsAccepted.count(kTheirAllyTeam.getID()) > 0)
    {
        scaled rAssets;
        netLostRivalAssetScore(NO_PLAYER, &rAssets);
        scaled rTheirGain = rVassalFactor *
                remainingCityRatio(eTheirAlly) * rAssets;
        ...
    }

But netLostRivalAssetScore(NO_PLAYER, &rAssets) is a WarUtilityAspect helper
whose rival/victim is implicitly the current aspect opponent eThey. It does not
take eTheirAlly as the player whose assets should be measured. The branch thus
multiplies the CURRENT RIVAL player's asset pool by the NEW VASSAL's remaining-
city ratio. A small new vassal can inherit a large rival's asset value, or a large
new vassal can be valued from a small rival's asset pool.

The same branch also applies the wrong vassal weight. rVassalFactor is divided
by two only when kTheirAllyTeam.isAVassal() is true NOW. A team that is not yet a
vassal but is predicted by the military analysis to capitulate therefore enters
this future-vassal gain branch at full 1.0 weight. Nearby PreEmptiveWar provides
a strong internal policy control: it explicitly applies half weight when either
bNewVassal OR isAVassal() is true.

Both defects are present in base AdvCiv 1.14. The repair needs to obtain the
prospective vassal player's/team's own asset base and apply the intended vassal
factor to a predicted capitulation as well as an existing vassal.


F110 / provisional KI#433 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED ADVCIV PLAYER-LOCAL MODEL
KINGMAKING USES PLAYER QUANTITIES FOR TEAM-SHARED VICTORY STATE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
KingMaking stores likely winners as PlayerTypes and evaluates several victory
conditions with player-local quantities even though Civ4 victory ownership is
team-level. This produces at least two independently proven normal-game
manifestations in multi-member teams / Permanent Alliances.

1. SCORE / TIME VICTORY LEADERSHIP

The actual game score used for score/time victory is CvGame::getTeamScore. Civ4
constructs team score by summing the member player scores. KingMaking's
addLeadingPlayers instead ranks:

    m_kGame.getPlayerScore(ePlayer)

or, in the predicted case:

    militAnalyst().predictedGameScore(ePlayer)

The latter is also explicitly player-level: it begins from that player's game
score and stores a per-player simulation result.

A two-member team with player scores 600 + 600 therefore genuinely leads a solo
1000 team by 1200 to 1000, while KingMaking can identify the solo 1000 player as
the score leader and omit both 600-point members. The model can consequently
misidentify who is actually closest to winning a Time/score game.

2. PREDICTED DOMINATION SETBACK

CvPlayerAI's Domination victory-stage calculation derives the relevant progress
from TEAM population/land. KingMaking anyVictory therefore starts from a
team-derived AI_VICTORY_DOMINATION3/4 flag. When predicting whether military
losses thwart that victory, however, it computes:

    max(0, kPlayer.getTotalPopulation() - iLostPop)

and compares that INDIVIDUAL player's remaining population share against the
Domination target share, which is a team victory threshold.

A Permanent Alliance can remain above the Domination population threshold in
aggregate while each member individually is far below it. Losing a few cities
from one member can therefore make KingMaking falsely declare the team's
Domination trajectory thwarted even though the team's combined population still
satisfies it.

The shared root is not simply "replace PlayerTypes with TeamTypes everywhere":
KingMaking's culture/space/conquest heuristics have player-specific inputs, and
predictedGameScore also folds simulation details that require care when summed.
The repair should make each genuinely team-owned victory test team-aware, with a
proper predicted team-score/team-population estimator rather than blindly
summing helpers that may already contain vassal or simulation adjustments.


UNRESOLVED CHALLENGE AFTER F110
-------------------------------
KingMaking keeps m_winningPresent and m_winningFuture as std::set<PlayerTypes>
and later uses set size as the number of competing "winning civs", while also
checking eWe and kOurTeam.getLeaderID() in different places. This may cause
additional team-game double counting or self-recognition problems beyond the two
proven F110 manifestations. It remains under challenge; do not count it as F111
unless an independent behavioral consequence survives.

C014-WIP04 APPEND -- WarUtilityAspect.cpp continued adversarial / team audit
===============================================================================

F109 / provisional KI#432 -- BROADENED -- WRONG-OBJECT ASSET REUSE IS GENERAL
KINGMAKING THEIRRELATIVELOSS REVALUES eThey FOR TEAMMATES / VASSALS TOO
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The WIP03 wording proved the wrong-object bug in the NEW-vassal branch. A direct
reread shows that the same root is broader and more damaging than that wording.

KingMaking::theirRelativeLoss iterates eTheirAlly over all major players and
selects the current rival, its teammates, existing vassals and prospective new
vassals. But in the ordinary current-rival/team-member/existing-vassal branch it
again calls:

    scaled rAssets;
    scaled rLostAssets = netLostRivalAssetScore(
            NO_PLAYER, &rAssets, eIgnoreGains);

netLostRivalAssetScore has no eTheirAlly parameter. Its rival/victim is the
aspect's current eThey. Therefore every accepted loop entry reuses eThey's asset
pool and eThey's projected loss rather than measuring the actual loop player.

A two-player rival team A+B can consequently count A's assets/losses once for A
and then again for B. An existing vassal likewise contributes a half-weighted
copy of A rather than its own assets. The previously proven prospective-vassal
branch has the same wrong-object problem and additionally fails to apply the
future-vassal half weight because rVassalFactor is halved only for a team that
is already a vassal.

So F109 is best normalized as a general wrong-object construction in
KingMaking::theirRelativeLoss: the loop is over eTheirAlly, but asset/loss
queries remain pinned to eThey. The new-vassal weighting error is a coupled
second manifestation. Base AdvCiv 1.14 contains the same structure.

A repair should make the asset/loss helper capable of evaluating the actual
loop player (or factor the calculation into a helper that takes PlayerTypes),
and separately apply the intended vassal factor to both existing and predicted
vassals.


F110 / provisional KI#433 -- BROADENED -- PLAYER WINNER SETS DUPLICATE TEAM STATE
KINGMAKING REPRESENTS TEAM-SHARED VICTORY CANDIDACY AS set<PlayerTypes>
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The earlier two F110 manifestations remain valid: Score/Time leadership uses
player rather than team score, and predicted Domination setback uses individual
population against a team threshold. The winner-set challenge now proves that
the representation itself causes further multi-member-team distortions.

KingMaking stores likely present/future winners in:

    std::set<PlayerTypes> m_winningPresent;
    std::set<PlayerTypes> m_winningFuture;

but later treats set cardinality as the number of competing winning
civilizations/competitors:

    scaled rCatchUpVal = ... / m_winningPresent.size();
    int iWinningRivals = m_winningFuture.size();

and uses player membership tests such as:

    m_winningFuture.count(eThey)
    m_winningFuture.count(eWe)
    m_winningFuture.count(kOurTeam.getLeaderID())

For team-owned victory conditions, two members of one Permanent Alliance can
therefore occupy two set entries despite representing one winning team. This
can:

* inflate the number of alleged competing winners and lower the KingMaking
  competition/catch-up utility;
* allow essentially the same team-level winning state to be processed once per
  winning member as WarUtilityAspect evaluates player opponents;
* suppress preEvaluate's "we'll be the only winners" shortcut because our
  leader may be present while m_winningFuture.size() is 2 solely because our
  teammate is another member of the same winning team;
* make self-recognition depend on which member PlayerTypes happens to represent
  the team in a given helper.

These are not a new root beyond F110; they are additional consequences of the
same player-local KingMaking model for team-shared victory state. A robust
repair should distinguish truly player-owned race inputs from team-owned
victory candidacy and should count a winning team once.


F111 / provisional KI#434 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED ADVCIV WRONG-OBJECT TEST
DIPLOMACY/AP CONQUEST WEIGHT TESTS THE CONQUEROR'S FULL MEMBERSHIP, NOT OLD OWNER
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
MilitaryVictory::progressRatingDiplomacy builds weighted conquests made by a
partner and then explicitly adjusts each conquered city based on its OLD owner:

    PlayerTypes const eCityOwner = kCacheCity.city().getOwner();
    // Weight for old owner
    if (!GET_TEAM(eCityOwner).isHuman())
    {
        /* AP: Conquests from non-full members are always worthwhile
           b/c, as full members, we can make their votes count twice. */
        if (bSecular || kThey.isFullMember(eVS))
        {
            AttitudeTypes const eOwnerTowardUs =
                    GET_PLAYER(eCityOwner).AI_getAttitude(eWe);
            ...
        }
    }

The comment, the eCityOwner local and the subsequent attitude lookup all refer
to the old owner. Yet the Apostolic-Palace membership branch tests kThey -- the
current rival/partner who conquered the city -- instead of eCityOwner.

That distinction is live precisely in the third-party-conquest case supported
by addConquestsByPartner: the conqueror and old owner need not have the same AP
membership status. Full membership changes the vote interpretation the comment
is trying to model, so the wrong-object test can either discount population that
should not be discounted or fail to discount population that already gave the
favorable/full-member vote contribution.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 has the same condition. For the non-secular AP branch, the test
should query the old owner, e.g. GET_PLAYER(eCityOwner).isFullMember(eVS), while
preserving kThey-based membership tests in the distinct code paths that really
do describe the conquering/new owner.


F112 / provisional KI#435 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED ADVCIV WRONG-TEAM DIVISOR
UWAI WAR-ANGER CACHE SPLITS AN ENEMY-TEAM CONTRIBUTION BY OUR TEAM SIZE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
UWAICache::updateWarAnger first attributes the owner's total war-weariness anger
to ENEMY TEAMS:

    aiAngerContrib[enemyTeam] = ourTeam.getWarWeariness(enemyTeam, true)

It then stores one cached anger value for each LIVING ENEMY PLAYER. The source
comment correctly states the required normalization:

    // Turn per-team into per-civ

but the division is:

    scaled(aiAngerContrib.get(itEnemy->getTeam()), iTotalAngerContribs) /
        GET_TEAM(kOwner.getTeam()).getNumMembers()

The contribution being split belongs to itEnemy's team, so dividing by the
OWNER team's member count is the wrong side of the relation. PublicOpposition
later consumes angerFromWarWeariness(eThey) once for each living enemy player,
and WarEvaluator separately evaluates every living agent member. Thus the wrong
denominator directly changes aggregate war utility rather than merely changing
how a report is displayed.

Concrete controls:

* solo owner vs a two-player enemy team: the same enemy-team contribution can be
  stored at full strength for both enemy players and then counted twice;
* two-player owner team vs solo enemy: each owner player's cached signal is
  divided by two even though there is only one enemy player representing that
  enemy-team contribution, so the aggregate signal can be halved;
* equal team sizes can accidentally hide the defect.

Because the consumer/player iterator is CIV_ALIVE, a dead assigned enemy member
should not dilute this split. The natural denominator is therefore the ENEMY
team's alive member count, not either side's getNumMembers(). This also avoids a
secondary F096 dead-member distortion.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 contains the identical wrong-owner-team denominator.

C014-WIP05 APPEND -- WarUtilityAspect.cpp wrong-ID / team-slot audit
===============================================================================

F113 / provisional KI#436 -- CONFIRMED -- BROAD INHERITED PLAYER/TEAM-ID MIXUP
WARUTILITYASPECT PASSES PlayerTypes DIRECTLY TO GET_TEAM; kTheirTeam MACRO IS WRONG
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WarUtilityAspect defines both a correct rival-team ID and a rival-team object:

    #define kThey           (getRivalPlayer())
    #define eThey           (kThey.getID())
    #define kTheirTeam      (GET_TEAM(eThey))
    #define eTheirTeam      (TEAMID(eThey))

The two last lines are NOT equivalent. eThey is PlayerTypes. GET_TEAM expects a
TeamTypes and indexes the global team array directly; TEAMID(eThey) instead asks
the player which team it currently belongs to.

There is no Civ4 invariant that PlayerTypes numerically equals the player's
TeamTypes. CvPlayer::setTeam explicitly changes the player's team association in
CvInitCore without changing the PlayerTypes ID, and the normal Permanent-
Alliance transition uses this mechanism. Configured team games and Shuffle
Teams can likewise assign player and team IDs independently.

Therefore, after player B joins survivor team A through a Permanent Alliance:

    eThey == B                    // still PlayerTypes B
    eTheirTeam == TEAMID(B) == A  // correct current team
    kTheirTeam == GET_TEAM(B)     // WRONG numeric team slot B

The old B team slot can by then have zero members and otherwise contain stale or
irrelevant team state. The macro is used throughout the file (43 source
occurrences including its definition), so this is not a single cosmetic lookup.
Representative affected consumers include:

* lossesFromFlippedTiles -- getNumMembers(); the obsolete team slot can contain
  zero members and become an actual divisor;
* tech/research state in Loathing-related asset logic;
* capitulation/vassal checks;
* AP/diplomatic membership decisions;
* HiredHand and Assistance team state;
* victory-stage and KingMaking checks;
* Risk war count / war success;
* IllWill, Affection and Distraction war/vassal state;
* FairPlay contact, war and shared-war state;
* ThirdPartyIntervention scheme/land-target and war-rand logic;
* DramaticArc vassal/team-size normalization.

The divisor manifestation is especially sharp. lossesFromFlippedTiles does:

    int const iRivalMembers = kTheirTeam.getNumMembers();
    ...
    r /= iRivalMembers;

If eThey is an absorbed PA member and its old numeric team slot has no members,
the same wrong-ID root can turn this into a divide-by-zero path when flipped
losses are evaluated.

The file also contains explicit non-macro instances of the same type error,
where locals that are demonstrably PlayerTypes are passed directly to GET_TEAM:

    GET_TEAM(eCityOwner)      // progressRatingDiplomacy / addConquestsByPartner
    GET_TEAM(ePartner)        // Fidelity
    GET_TEAM(eAlly)           // HiredHand
    GET_TEAM(eTheirAlly)      // KingMaking::theirRelativeLoss
    GET_TEAM(eVassal)         // Risk
    GET_TEAM(eTheirVassal)    // Affection

These can independently read the wrong team in ordinary configured team games
or after team reassignment. Some overlap already-proven semantic findings --
e.g. F111's old-owner AP block and F109's KingMaking loop -- but the ID-domain
error is broader and survives even after those wrong-object formulas are fixed.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 contains the same kTheirTeam/eTheirTeam macro pair and the same
style of direct PlayerTypes-to-GET_TEAM calls, so F113 is inherited rather than
introduced by current SAS. Reachable pre-SAS source history also contains the
pattern, making this a longstanding team-game/PA oversight.

Repair direction:

* define the rival object through the actual team association, e.g.

      #define kTheirTeam (GET_TEAM(eTheirTeam))

  or GET_TEAM(kThey.getTeam());
* replace every explicit GET_TEAM(ePlayerVariable) whose variable is
  PlayerTypes with GET_TEAM(TEAMID(ePlayerVariable)) / GET_PLAYER(...).getTeam()
  as appropriate;
* retain direct GET_TEAM calls only where the argument is genuinely TeamTypes;
* after repair, re-run the multi-member/PA normalization cases because F113 can
  currently mask or exaggerate several other UWAI findings.

C014-WIP06 APPEND -- F113 cross-file UWAI type-domain expansion
===============================================================================

F113 / provisional KI#436 -- BROADENED -- UWAI-WIDE PLAYER/TEAM-ID LOOKUP FAMILY
WARUTILITYASPECT IS ONE MANIFESTATION; UWAICACHE AND UWAI::PLAYER SHARE THE ROOT
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The WIP05 root is substantially broader than WarUtilityAspect.cpp. A directed
cross-file type audit proves that the same PlayerTypes -> GET_TEAM misuse occurs
inside the per-player UWAI cache and per-player UWAI agent.

The crucial type boundary is explicit in the headers:

    UWAICache::m_eOwner       : PlayerTypes
    UWAI::Player::m_eAgent    : PlayerTypes
    UWAI::Team::m_eAgent      : TeamTypes

Therefore a textual grep for GET_TEAM(m_eAgent) cannot be fixed blindly: uses
inside UWAI::Team are type-correct, while uses inside UWAI::Player are not.
Likewise, GET_TEAM(m_eOwner) in UWAICache is wrong because m_eOwner is always a
player ID.

REACHABILITY IS NORMAL, NOT PA-ONLY
-----------------------------------
UWAI::Player::init(PlayerTypes ePlayer) does:

    m_eAgent = ePlayer;
    m_cache.init(ePlayer);

and UWAI::Player::turnPre() calls m_cache.update() every turn. Thus every player
has a player-owned cache; these aren't leader-only cache objects. CvPlayer::
setTeam independently rewrites GC.getInitCore().setTeam(getID(), eTeam) without
changing the player's ID. Consequently an ordinary configured multi-player team
already supplies a normal PlayerTypes != TeamTypes case for any member whose
player slot differs from the shared team slot; Permanent Alliances are merely a
particularly clear later-game way to create the same mismatch.

UWAICACHE GAMEPLAY MANIFESTATIONS
---------------------------------
UWAICache.cpp repeatedly indexes GET_TEAM directly with m_eOwner. Representative
live uses include:

* createTeamPathFinders / updateCities -- pathfinders and own/foreign-city
  classification are built from GET_TEAM(m_eOwner);
* goldPerProdVictory -- owner victory stage and rival iteration use that team;
* updateWarUtility / updateWarUtilityIgnDistraction -- leader gating and the
  team whose war state is evaluated are selected from that slot;
* leaderCache -- deciding whether this cache is the leader cache, and which
  player's cache to redirect to, both use GET_TEAM(m_eOwner);
* feature-tech, tech-trade, bonus-obsolescence/reveal checks -- use the wrong
  team's technology state;
* reportWarEnding -- owner war success, chosen-war state and at-war duration use
  the wrong team;
* reportCityCreated -- AI_deduceCitySite uses the wrong team;
* is/setReadyToCapitulate and onTeamLeaderChanged -- leader identity/routing are
  resolved through the wrong team slot.

This means a nonleader teammate's cache can be populated using another numeric
team slot's pathing, technology, war-history and leader-cache state. After a PA,
the wrong slot can instead be the absorbed player's old now-empty/dead team.

UWAI::PLAYER GAMEPLAY MANIFESTATIONS
------------------------------------
After UWAI::Player::Player() establishes m_eAgent as PlayerTypes, numerous
player-level methods likewise call GET_TEAM(m_eAgent) directly. Confirmed live
examples include:

* considerDemand -- reparationsToHuman is taken from numeric team slot m_eAgent;
* considerPlea -- force-peace, canDeclareWar and sneak-attack-ready state;
* willTalk / isPeaceDealPossible -- surrender, team-leader and peace-reluctance
  state;
* canTradeAssets -- AI_techTradeVal;
* tradeValUtilityConversionRate -- team yield-rate estimates;
* confidenceFromWarSuccess -- current-war counters and war success;
* warConfidenceAllies -- whether the player belongs to a multi-member team.

Several of these functions are called through GET_PLAYER(...).uwai() for the
individual player (e.g. CvPlayerAI offer/will-talk logic and InvasionGraph), so
the wrong lookups are not confined to a leader-only path.

INITIALIZATION SIBLING
----------------------
UWAI::initNewPlayerInGame(PlayerTypes eNewPlayer) currently does:

    GET_TEAM(eNewPlayer).uwai().init(TEAMID(eNewPlayer));
    GET_PLAYER(eNewPlayer).uwai().init(eNewPlayer);

The first line selects the team object by PlayerTypes but initializes that
object with the player's actual TeamTypes. If a dynamically created player's
IDs differ, this can initialize the wrong CvTeamAI::uwai() object as another
team. This is the same ID-domain defect at a state-transition boundary; the
ordinary per-player cache manifestations above do not depend on this dynamic-
player case and already prove the root's normal reachability.

ANCESTRY / CONTROL
------------------
Base AdvCiv 1.14 contains the same UWAICache GET_TEAM(m_eOwner) calls, the same
post-UWAI::Player-constructor GET_TEAM(m_eAgent) calls and the same
initNewPlayerInGame line. The family is inherited.

The important negative control is UWAI::Team. Its m_eAgent is declared
TeamTypes; direct GET_TEAM(m_eAgent) calls in that class are correct and must not
be mechanically replaced as though they were part of F113.

REPAIR/AUDIT SHAPE
------------------
Treat F113 as a typed audit, not a search-and-replace:

* WarUtilityAspect PlayerTypes locals/macros: resolve through TEAMID(player);
* UWAICache::m_eOwner: resolve team through TEAMID(m_eOwner) or
  GET_PLAYER(m_eOwner).getTeam();
* UWAI::Player::m_eAgent: same player-to-team conversion;
* UWAI::initNewPlayerInGame: select GET_TEAM(TEAMID(eNewPlayer));
* UWAI::Team::m_eAgent: leave direct GET_TEAM(m_eAgent) intact;
* audit other UWAI files by declared enum type, because both enum domains are
  integer-compatible at the call site and therefore compile silently.

This expansion does not consume F114; it is the same F113/KI#436 invariant and
explains why some team-game/PA symptoms can appear outside WarUtilityAspect.

F113 / provisional KI#436 -- ADDITIONAL EXPLICIT WARUTILITYASPECT SITE
ILLWILL::EVALANGEREDPARTNERS PASSES A PLAYERSET MEMBER DIRECTLY TO GET_TEAM
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The continuing typed sweep found another explicit same-root manifestation not
listed in WIP05/WIP06. IllWill::evalAngeredPartners obtains:

    PlyrSet const& kWeDecl = militAnalyst().getWarsDeclaredBy(eWe);

and iterates that set with PlyrSetIter. Therefore *it is PlayerTypes. It then
executes:

    if (GET_TEAM(*it).isAVassal() || eTheirTeam == TEAMID(*it))
        continue;

The TEAMID use on the second half is type-correct; the direct GET_TEAM(*it) on
the first half is not. In a configured team game or after reassignment, the
vassal filter can inspect the numeric team slot matching the target player's ID
rather than that player's actual team. This belongs under the already-broadened
F113 typed-audit family and consumes no new finding ID.

A useful control from the same file is GreedForVassals: its apparent
GET_TEAM(*it) use occurs under TeamSetIter, so *it is genuinely TeamTypes and
that call is correct. This reinforces that F113 repair must follow declared enum
types rather than textual patterns.


F114 / provisional KI#437 -- CONFIRMED -- FAIRPLAY COUNTS TARGET TEAMMATES AS
"OTHER ENEMIES" / "ALLIES" OF THE TARGET AND DILUTES THE DOGPILE PENALTY
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
FairPlay::evaluate contains an early block whose stated purpose is:

    // Avoid big dogpiles (or taking turns attacking a single target)
    scaled rOtherEnemies; // Apart from us

It then loops:

    for (PlayerAIIter<FREE_MAJOR_CIV,KNOWN_POTENTIAL_ENEMY_OF>
            itOther(eOurTeam); ...)

and excludes only:

    if (kOther.getID() == eThey ||
        !kTheirTeam.isHasMet(kOther.getTeam()))
        continue;

This is player-local exclusion where the loop's semantic domain is third
parties relative to the TARGET SIDE. A second living member of eTheirTeam is a
known potential enemy of eOurTeam and has a different PlayerTypes ID from
eThey, so it passes the filter even though it can never be an independent enemy
of its own team.

Two concrete consequences survive independently of F113:

1. TARGET TEAMMATES INFLATE THE DENOMINATOR

The code increments iPotentialOtherEnemies immediately after the filter. Later:

    rFromOtherEnemies = ... /
        (sqrt(max(1, iPotentialOtherEnemies)) - 1/3);

Thus each teammate of the current target player is counted as another potential
third-party enemy, increasing the denominator and reducing the fairness cost of
dogpiling that team.

2. A TARGET TEAMMATE CAN BE CLASSIFIED AS AN "ALLY OF eThey"

If the teammate is not counted as an enemy, FairPlay evaluates:

    else if (kTheirTeam.AI_shareWar(kOther.getTeam()))

For a target teammate, kOther.getTeam() == eTheirTeam. CvTeamAI::AI_shareWar
loops the team's current enemies and returns true when one of them is at war
with the supplied team. Therefore AI_shareWar(ownTeam) is true whenever the
team has any war enemy. FairPlay can consequently log the target's own teammate
as:

    "An ally of eThey"

and subtract from rOtherEnemies. This does more than dilute the denominator: it
can directly reduce the perceived dogpile pressure merely because the target
has teammates.

The declared loop role gives a strong repair invariant. Independent third
parties must exclude the entire current target team, not just eThey. A nearby
internal control already implements that distinction correctly:
IllWill::nukeCost skips

    kThirdPlayer.getTeam() == eTheirTeam

when iterating independent third players.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 contains the same FairPlay filter and shared-war branch, so the
defect is inherited rather than SAS-specific.

Minimal repair shape:

    if (kOther.getTeam() == eTheirTeam ||
        !kTheirTeam.isHasMet(kOther.getTeam()))
        continue;

This naturally excludes eThey and every teammate before either
 iPotentialOtherEnemies or enemy/ally history is touched. Re-audit behavior
with F113's kTheirTeam lookup repaired, but F114 itself is independent of F113.


REJECTED / CONTROLLED LATE HYPOTHESES
-------------------------------------
AFFECTION ONE-SIDED TEAM NORMALIZATION -- REJECTED

Affection says pairwise affection needs a correction in team games, but applies
it only when kOurTeam.getNumMembers() > 1. At first glance a solo agent versus a
two-member target looks asymmetric. The WarEvaluator outer loop and the history
of the correction explain the asymmetry, however: a solo player can legitimately
carry separate pairwise friendship costs toward two distinct rival players,
whereas a multi-member AGENT team would otherwise duplicate the same team-war
decision once for every agent member. The pre-SAS commit that introduced the
normalization used the agent-team-size gate from inception. This is therefore
not strong enough for F115.

THIRDPARTYINTERVENTION ALL-ZERO DEFENSIVE-POWER DIVISOR -- REJECTED

preEvaluate computes:

    m_rLostDefPowRatio = rOurLostPow /
        max(m_rDefPow, m_rDefPow + rGainedPow);

without an explicit epsilon. When current, gained and lost defensive power are
all zero, ScaledNum ultimately reaches Win32 MulDiv with divisor zero. For the
signed fixed-point type used here, MulDiv returns its -1 error sentinel; the
immediately following

    m_rLostDefPowRatio.clamp(0, 0.5);

raises that tiny negative value to zero, and evaluate exits on
rOurLostPowRatio <= 0. Later ThirdParty power divisions require a path where
positive current or gained power has already supplied a denominator. So this is
untidy arithmetic but not a demonstrated live gameplay root.

THIRDPARTYINTERVENTION COLLECTIVE TEAM POWER -- STILL UNDER CHALLENGE

The nonlinear <=50% power cutoff is still computed from the current rival
player plus vassals, not rival teammates, despite team-level intervention
eligibility. Two individually sub-threshold teammates can therefore both yield
zero even if their collective team power would be dangerous. However,
WarEvaluator deliberately aggregates player-local contributions in several
team-game aspects, and the later team-size normalization complicates the
intended policy. Keep this candidate open; do not promote it without a harder
source/consumer invariant.

C014-WIP08 APPEND -- F115 + late-aspect controls / next DramaticArc challenge
===============================================================================

F115 / provisional KI#438 -- CONFIRMED -- THIRDPARTYINTERVENTION COMPUTES A
GAME-SPEED-ADJUSTED PEACE DURATION, THEN DISCARDs IT AND DECAYS FROM RAW TURNS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ThirdPartyIntervention::evaluate contains a long-peace anti-stalemate decay:

    int iAtPeaceTurns = kOurTeam.AI_getAtPeaceCounter(eTheirTeam);
    int iThresh = (5 * PEACE_TREATY_LENGTH) / 3 - 1;
    if (iAtPeaceTurns > iThresh)
    {
        scaled rAtPeaceTurns = fixp(1.5) * iAtPeaceTurns /
            (per100(m_kSpeed.getGoldenAgePercent()) + fixp(0.5));
        scaled rMult = std::max(fixp(1/3.),
            1 - scaled(iAtPeaceTurns - iThresh, 30));
        ...
        rInterventionProb *= rMult;
    }

The local rAtPeaceTurns is never read after being computed. The actual gate and
linear decay both continue to use the raw iAtPeaceTurns.

This is unusually strong evidence of an accidental missing use rather than
merely an alternative heuristic:

1. THE UNUSED EXPRESSION HAS A CLEAR GAME-SPEED NORMALIZATION ROLE

The factor

    1.5 / (GoldenAgePercent / 100 + 0.5)

is exactly 1 on Normal speed (GoldenAgePercent=100), so the omission is hidden
there. It changes systematically on every other shipped SAS game speed:

    Nitro       55
    Turbo       60
    Quick       80
    Normal     100
    Epic       125
    Marathon   200
    Slow       300
    Very Slow  400

Thus the dead local is not redundant arithmetic. It computes a distinct
normalized peace duration everywhere except Normal.

2. THE DEAD LOCAL WAS PRESENT FROM THE ORIGINAL ASPECT INTRODUCTION

The pre-SAS commit that introduced ThirdPartyIntervention
(f39e13df87, "Add ThirdPartyIntervention war utility aspect", 2021-11-19)
already contains the exact sequence: compute rAtPeaceTurns, then ignore it and
use iAtPeaceTurns in the multiplier. Base AdvCiv 1.14 still contains the same
code. This is therefore an inherited construction error, not a SAS refactor
regression or an abandoned variable left by a later rewrite.

3. THE CURRENT RESULT IS SPEED-DEPENDENT IN THE WRONG UNIT

With the default PEACE_TREATY_LENGTH=10, iThresh is 15. At 31 RAW peace turns,
current code gives approximately:

    1 - (31 - 15) / 30 = 0.467

before the 1/3 floor -- on every game speed.

On Very Slow, however, the expression that the code itself computes gives:

    normalized peace turns ~= 1.5 * 31 / (4 + 0.5) ~= 10.3

so the normalized peace duration has not even reached the intended 15-turn
threshold yet. Current code has already cut intervention fear by more than half.
On faster-than-Normal modes the error reverses: the raw-turn schedule decays
more slowly than the prepared normalized schedule.

The semantic purpose is explicit in the surrounding comment:

    // Avoid stalemates: don't be afraid of interventions forever

That policy can reasonably scale with game speed, but the source already
contains the attempted scaling and then fails to consume it.

REPAIR BOUNDARY

Do not merely substitute rAtPeaceTurns into the existing multiplier while
leaving the raw-turn threshold unchanged. On slow speeds that could enter the
raw iAtPeaceTurns > iThresh block while normalized peace duration is still
below iThresh, producing a multiplier greater than 1 before clamping logic.
The coherent repair is to compute the normalized duration first and use the
same normalized unit for BOTH:

- the comparison to the long-peace threshold; and
- the excess duration used by the decay.

The exact scaling convention should be reviewed against current SAS turn-scaling
policy, but the current compute-and-discard implementation is demonstrably
self-contradictory.

--------------------------------------------------------
TACTICALSITUATION PER-RIVAL-MEMBER EVALUATION -- NOT PROMOTED

A repeated team-game execution initially looked like a possible duplicate-team
charge. Direct tracing shows TacticalSituation::evalEngagement is substantially
player-local on both sides: the current eWe member's military/cities are judged
against the current eThey player's military/cities, and WarEvaluator
intentionally evaluates living agent members separately. That does not furnish
the hard team-level invariant available for F112/F114. Keep the existing code
under ordinary heuristic scrutiny, but do not promote this repetition by
itself.

ASPECT-OBJECT STATE ACROSS AGENT MEMBERS -- NO SECOND F101 ROOT FOUND

WarUtilityAspect objects deliberately retain cumulative m_iU while evaluating
multiple living members. Their extra mutable state was checked for stale-member
leakage. The relevant fields are either overwritten per member (e.g.
MilitaryVictory, ThirdPartyIntervention, DramaticArc) or deliberately cumulative
with a safe uniqueness rule (e.g. Revolts::m_countedCities prevents a city from
being charged through multiple primary-area relations). No independent stale
member-state defect survived.

RISK / EFFORT LATE ARITHMETIC -- NO NEW ROOT SO FAR

The dense loss/power/vassal pass mostly produced further F113 typed-lookup
manifestations. Once those are conceptually repaired, the examined ratios have
positive structural domains or explicit clamps. No independent divisor/sign
root survived this pass.

THIRDPARTYINTERVENTION COLLECTIVE TEAM POWER -- STILL UNDER CHALLENGE

The earlier nonlinear <=50% military threshold remains suspicious because it
uses the current rival player's army plus vassals rather than that rival team's
teammates, even though intervention eligibility is team-level. Two individually
40%-strength teammates can each be thresholded to zero despite 80% collective
team power. However, WarEvaluator intentionally aggregates player-local terms in
some team-game calculations. F115 is independent of this question. Do not
promote the collective-power hypothesis without a stronger intended-aggregation
invariant.


NEXT LIVE CHALLENGE -- DRAMATICARC HASMET / TURNSATPEACE TOLERANCE
------------------------------------------------------------------
DramaticArc currently does roughly:

    int iAtPeace = getTurnsAtPeace(eSecond);
    // With tolerance b/c the has-met counter isn't exact
    if (abs(AI_getHasMetCounter(eSecond) - iAtPeace) >= 8)
        ...
    // else assume always at peace

The comment/history claim that HasMet is inexact conflicts with CvTeamAI's
counter implementation, which deliberately does NOT randomize HasMet (nor
AtWar) because callers assume an exact count. Historical archaeology shows that
this mistaken rationale was already present when DramaticArc was amended to use
exact TurnsAtPeace.

That comment error is not yet enough for F116. Need finish the lifecycle proof:
trace makeHasMet / war / peace reset and increment ordering, quantify the normal
difference after a short early war, and decide whether the 8-turn tolerance has
a defensible policy role (e.g. intentionally ignoring very short early wars) or
causes a demonstrably contradictory DramaticArc classification. Keep UNDER
CHALLENGE.

C014-WIP09 APPEND -- F116 DramaticArc exact-counter lifecycle correction
===============================================================================

F116 / provisional KI#439 -- CONFIRMED -- DRAMATICARC'S 8-TURN "INEXACT HASMET"
TOLERANCE CAN MISCLASSIFY A RECENT SHORT WAR AS "ALWAYS AT PEACE"
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DramaticArc::preEvaluate currently tries to distinguish pairs that have always
been peaceful from pairs whose exact TurnsAtPeace counter was reset by war:

    int iAtPeace = itFirst->getTurnsAtPeace(eSecond);
    // With tolerance b/c the has-met counter isn't exact
    if (abs(itFirst->AI_getHasMetCounter(eSecond) - iAtPeace) >= 8)
        iLoopMinCounter = std::min(iLoopMinCounter, iAtPeace);
    // (else assume that they've always been at peace)

The stated premise is false. CvTeamAI::AI_doCounter explicitly documents the
opposite:

    // No randomization for atWar and hasMet. These are used by the AI in
    // several places that more or less assume an exact count.

HasMet is incremented deterministically once per alive-team turn after contact.
CvTeam's exact TurnsAtPeace is likewise incremented once per alive-team turn
whenever the pair is not at war, and declaration of war resets BOTH directions
to zero.

Thus the 8-turn tolerance is not compensating for randomized counter noise.
It can erase real, recent warfare from DramaticArc's global-tension history.

NORMAL REPRODUCTION

Take two teams that have not previously met, after DramaticArc's early-game
25-normalized-turn gate:

1. They meet through a declaration of war. The declaration resets exact
   TurnsAtPeace to 0 while HasMet begins its exact contact history.
2. They remain at war for e.g. 3 counted team turns.
3. They make peace and remain peaceful for e.g. 1-2 counted turns.

At that point, approximately:

    HasMet        = 4-5
    TurnsAtPeace  = 1-2
    difference    = 3   (< 8)

Current code therefore takes the ELSE path and "assume[s] that they've always
been at peace." iLoopMinCounter remains initialized to iElapsedTurns, so a
peace that began only one or two turns ago can be represented as roughly the
whole elapsed game age.

This directly contradicts DramaticArc's source/history purpose: to encourage
war when there "hasn't been any warfare for a long time" and discourage it when
there is too much. A real war that ended almost immediately before evaluation
must not be reclassified as no prior warfare merely because it lasted fewer
than eight turns.

COUNTER LIFECYCLE GIVES A CLEANER EXACT TEST

The two exact counters have a useful directional relation:

- TurnsAtPeace starts accumulating from game start even before two teams meet.
- HasMet starts accumulating only after first contact.
- In a never-at-war relationship, therefore, HasMet <= TurnsAtPeace.
- A declaration of war resets TurnsAtPeace to 0 but does not reset HasMet.
- After at least one counted war turn, HasMet > TurnsAtPeace; once peace resumes,
  both counters increment together, preserving that strict inequality.

So, assuming the separate PA counter-merge defect F098 is repaired, a much more
source-faithful discriminator is conceptually:

    if (AI_getHasMetCounter(eSecond) > iAtPeace)
        // Actual counted warfare has occurred: use exact iAtPeace.
    else
        // No counted war since contact: treating the pair as always peaceful is
        // consistent with the counter history.

A declaration and peace occurring entirely within one counter tick can leave
both counters equal; treating such a zero-count-duration war as negligible is a
small transition edge, not justification for an arbitrary eight-turn band.

HISTORY / ANCESTRY

The chronology makes the mistaken premise unusually clear:

- dc322128c7 (2022-02-15), "Keep exact count of turns at peace", introduced the
  exact CvTeam TurnsAtPeace state.
- 03f2a56482, shortly afterward, introduced DramaticArc using the RANDOMIZED AI
  AtPeace counter and a comment that "these counters aren't exact."
- 17652fd75b (2022-02-16), "Minor amendment to 'Dramatic Arc' commit", switched
  DramaticArc from AI_getAtPeaceCounter to exact getTurnsAtPeace but retained a
  tolerance because it claimed "the has-met counter isn't exact," reducing the
  threshold only from 10 to 8.
- The corresponding commit message states the same mistaken rationale: "since
  the has-met count is also randomized..." Yet CvTeamAI deliberately keeps
  HasMet non-randomized because callers assume an exact count.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains this exact code and rationale. F116 is therefore an
inherited logic defect, not a SAS regression.

REPAIR BOUNDARY

Remove the fictitious random-noise tolerance. Prefer a predicate based on the
actual exact-counter lifecycle (e.g. HasMet > TurnsAtPeace means counted war
history exists) or another explicit persisted war-history predicate if one is
chosen. Do not merely lower the threshold: any positive arbitrary tolerance can
still turn a genuine short recent war into "always at peace."

Keep F098 in mind when implementing/testing: Permanent-Alliance merging can
currently make exact HasMet/TurnsAtPeace histories asymmetric. F116 is
independent and should be evaluated with F098 conceptually repaired.

THIRDPARTYINTERVENTION COLLECTIVE TEAM POWER -- STILL NOT PROMOTED

The nonlinear <=50% intervention-power threshold remains suspicious for
multi-member potential-intervening teams because it measures current rival
player + vassals, not rival teammates, before later member normalization. The
architecture intentionally aggregates player-local terms elsewhere, however,
and no hard source-level aggregation invariant has yet been established. Keep
under challenge; do not assign F117 from intuition alone.

C014-WIP10 APPEND -- F117 PublicOpposition scenario-state bug + F113 expansion
===============================================================================

F117 / provisional KI#440 -- CONFIRMED -- PUBLICOPPOSITION MIXES HYPOTHETICAL
NEW-WAR RELIGION ANGER WITH CURRENT-STATE ANGRY POPULATION
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PublicOpposition::evaluate intentionally runs against the MilitaryAnalyst's
simulated war state:

    if (kWe.isAnarchy() || !militAnalyst().isWar(eWe, eThey) || ...)
        return;

For every city it then estimates the religious anger attributable to THIS
simulated enemy:

    scaled rAngry = pCity->angryPopulation(...);
    rFaithAnger += std::min(rAngry,
        pCity->getReligionPercentAnger(eThey) * pCity->getPopulation() /
        GC.getPERCENT_ANGER_DIVISOR());

The two operands of that min are not from the same world state.

- CvCity::getReligionPercentAnger(PlayerTypes ePlayer) calculates the potential
  anger contributed by that specified player's state religion. It can therefore
  be used for a prospective enemy that we are not currently fighting.
- CvCity::angryPopulation(), however, is a CURRENT-city-state quantity.
  CvCity::unhappyLevel feeds it the no-argument getReligionPercentAnger(), whose
  implementation loops only PlayerIter<CIV_ALIVE,ENEMY_OF> -- actual current
  enemies. A merely simulated future enemy is absent from that total.

Thus PublicOpposition projects a hypothetical anger source, then caps it by a
consequence count that does not yet include that hypothetical source.

NORMAL NEW-WAR REPRODUCTION

Suppose a currently peaceful/content city has:

    current angryPopulation = 0

but a prospective target has a state religion present strongly enough in that
city that war with that target would create, say, 3 religiously angry citizens.
MilitaryAnalyst's war scenario makes isWar(eWe,eThey) true, and the explicit
getReligionPercentAnger(eThey) call correctly computes that prospective anger.
Current code then does conceptually:

    min(currentAngry = 0, hypotheticalFaithAnger = 3) = 0

So the aspect can assign ZERO religious public-opposition cost to a new war that
would itself create unhappy citizens.

SECOND MANIFESTATION -- REUSING THE SAME CURRENT ANGRY CITIZENS

WarEvaluator evaluates rival players separately. For existing/multiple enemies,
each rival's religious anger is independently capped by the same current
angryPopulation. A city with 5 actual angry citizens and two enemy-specific
religion contributions each large enough for 5 can therefore contribute 5+5
across two rival evaluations even though there are only 5 angry citizens total.
The same current unhappy population can be attributed repeatedly to different
wars instead of computing a scenario-level/marginal anger change.

This is not F112. F112 concerns how cached WAR-WEARINESS anger is split from a
team quantity into per-enemy-player contributions. F117 concerns religion anger
mixing a SIMULATED source with a CURRENT-state cap and independently reusing
that cap across rivals.

ANCESTRY / INTENT

Base AdvCiv 1.14 contains the same code. The initial PublicOpposition
implementation in reachable AdvCiv history already used the same

    min(current angryPopulation, getReligionPercentAnger(theyId) * pop / divisor)

construction. Later tuning did not repair the state mismatch.

The source itself labels the neighboring war-weariness input as a known issue
for new wars (cached WW is zero when not currently at war). By contrast, the
explicit per-player religion overload is plainly being used to estimate the
prospective-war contribution; capping it by current angryPopulation defeats
that projection in exactly the happy-city case above.

REPAIR BOUNDARY

Do not simply delete the cap without thinking through city happiness. The
quantity wanted is the MARGINAL/SCENARIO public opposition caused by the
simulated war set. A robust repair should evaluate total city unhappiness with
scenario religion-war anger (or reconstruct the relevant marginal angry
population) and apportion that finite result once. In particular:

- prospective religion anger must be allowed to CREATE angry citizens that are
  absent from current angryPopulation; and
- the same finite set of angry citizens must not be independently credited to
  multiple enemy players.

If a cheaper pairwise approximation is retained, use a shared/marginal cap
against the scenario total rather than current angryPopulation independently
for every rival.


F113 / provisional KI#436 -- MATERIAL EXPANSION -- THE PLAYER-ID-AS-TEAM-ID
FAMILY REACHES THE CORE MILITARY SIMULATION, NOT ONLY ASPECT/CACHE HELPERS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WIP05-WIP07 established the same root in WarUtilityAspect, UWAICache,
UWAI::Player and initialization: a PlayerTypes value is used directly where a
TeamTypes identity/index is required. Further tracing now proves that the root
also penetrates MilitaryAnalyst and InvasionGraph -- the machinery that builds
almost every WarUtilityAspect scenario.

MILITARYANALYST STARTS FROM THE WRONG TEAM FOR A NONLEADER TEAM MEMBER

MilitaryAnalyst stores:

    PlayerTypes m_eWe;

but its constructor begins with:

    CvTeamAI const& kAgent = GET_TEAM(m_eWe);

WarEvaluator deliberately constructs one MilitaryAnalyst for EACH living agent
player. For an ordinary teammate or PA-absorbed player whose player slot differs
from the shared team slot, this selects the team whose NUMERIC TEAM ID equals
that player ID, not the player's actual TEAMID(m_eWe).

The same constructor repeatedly performs GET_TEAM(ePlayer) while ePlayer comes
from PlayerIter, and even uses GET_TEAM(*it1) where *it1 comes from PlyrSet.
These calls determine master/vassal sides, war allies, extra targets and whether
simulated declarations of war are already active. Thus F113 can corrupt the
scenario itself before the aspect formulas run.

NON-GET_TEAM MANIFESTATION: TEAM ARRAY WRITTEN WITH PLAYER INDEX

MilitaryAnalyst declares:

    std::vector<TeamSet> m_capitulationsAcceptedPerTeam;

and its public accessor takes TeamTypes:

    getCapitulationsAccepted(TeamTypes eMaster)

but prepareResults writes each Node's team-level capitulation output to:

    m_capitulationsAcceptedPerTeam[ePlayer]

where ePlayer is PlayerTypes. Elsewhere the same information is read via
TEAMID(ePlayer). When player ID != team ID, the result is stored under one
numeric slot and queried under another. This is the same semantic F113 root even
though GET_TEAM is not involved syntactically: player identity has been used as
a team-array index.

INVASIONGRAPH HAS THE SAME TYPE-DOMAIN ASSUMPTION IN LIVE SIMULATION LOGIC

InvasionGraph::Node explicitly stores BOTH:

    PlayerTypes m_ePlayer;
    PlayerTypes m_eAgent;

Yet live logic contains calls such as:

    GET_TEAM(m_ePlayer).isAtWar(...)
    GET_TEAM(m_eAgent).isAtWar(...)
    CvTeamAI const& kAttTeam = GET_TEAM(kAttacker.m_ePlayer);
    CvTeamAI const& kDefTeam = GET_TEAM(m_ePlayer);

and InvasionGraph::willingness(PlayerTypes eAggressor, PlayerTypes eTarget)
uses GET_TEAM(eAggressor) and GET_TEAM(eTarget) directly.

These affect target selection, current-war detection, master/vassal logic,
capitulation eligibility, sneak-attack classification, willingness and other
simulation state -- not merely log output.

This also supplied an important negative control for a BorderDisputes candidate:
InvasionGraph explicitly states that newly conquered cities cannot be attacked
by third parties or reconquered in the simulation, so per-player conquest sets
are mutually exclusive for a city; BorderDisputes' first matching conqueror is
not order-dependent under this model.

ANCESTRY / IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE

Base AdvCiv contains these same MilitaryAnalyst/InvasionGraph patterns. The F113
repair audit should therefore be SYSTEMATIC across the UWAI subsystem, not just
replace the WarUtilityAspect `kTheirTeam` macro.

Use actual declared/derived types:

- PlayerTypes p -> TEAMID(p), GET_PLAYER(p).getTeam(), then GET_TEAM(team)
- TeamTypes t   -> GET_TEAM(t) directly

Audit array/vector indices whose semantic domain is team as well as GET_TEAM
calls. Do not blind-replace every `GET_TEAM(variable)`: e.g. the UWAI::Team
agent member really is TeamTypes and several TeamSet iterators are already
correct. The bug is a TYPE/DOMAIN mismatch, not a macro-name problem.


CONTROLS / OPEN QUESTIONS SINCE WIP09
-------------------------------------
- AI_countVSNonMembers(VoteSourceTypes) counts living MAJOR PLAYERS. Therefore
  MilitaryVictory's per-player AP obstacle numerator and that denominator are
  in compatible units; no new root there.
- BorderDisputes' first-conqueror break is safe under InvasionGraph's explicit
  no-recapture/no-third-party-recapture simulation model.
- Effort's 15-raw-turn grace threshold followed by game-speed-scaled escalation
  is unit-inconsistent-looking, but both pieces were introduced together and
  there is no hard intent contradiction. Keep as design-review only unless
  stronger evidence appears; do not promote F118 from aesthetics.
- ThirdPartyIntervention collective teammate power remains under challenge;
  the <=50% cutoff is player-local before aggregation, but a hard intended team
  aggregation invariant is still required.

C014-WIP11 CONTINUATION -- AUTHORITATIVE F113 RETRACTION + F118/F119
===============================================================================

IMPORTANT CORRECTION -- F113 / provisional KI#436 RETRACTED
------------------------------------------------------------
DO NOT IMPLEMENT KI#436 FROM WIP05-WIP10.

The broad PlayerTypes-as-TeamTypes GET_TEAM diagnosis was a false positive.
WarUtilityAspect.cpp includes CoreAI.h, which deliberately replaces GET_TEAM
with an overloaded accessor:

    __forceinline CvTeamAI& getTeam(TeamTypes eTeam)
    { return CvTeamAI::AI_getTeam(eTeam); }

    __forceinline CvTeamAI& getTeam(PlayerTypes ePlayer)
    { return CvTeamAI::AI_getTeam(TEAMID(ePlayer)); }

CvGamePlay.h provides the same overload pattern for non-AI CvTeam access.
Therefore expressions such as GET_TEAM(eThey), GET_TEAM(m_eOwner),
GET_TEAM(m_eAgent), GET_TEAM(eRival), GET_TEAM(eCityOwner), and the analogous
InvasionGraph/MilitaryAnalyst calls are type-resolved correctly whenever the
argument's declared type is PlayerTypes. They do NOT index the numeric team slot
whose integer happens to equal the player ID.

This mechanism is inherited in Base AdvCiv 1.14 and is intentional advc.003u.
Current SAS archaeology had independently reached the same conclusion for the
older KI#311 candidate: suspected PlayerTypes-as-TeamTypes GET_TEAM misuse was
rejected specifically because GET_TEAM(PlayerTypes) resolves through TEAMID.
That existing control should have been consulted earlier.

Consequently, all WIP05-WIP10 text describing the WarUtilityAspect kTheirTeam
macro, UWAICache GET_TEAM(m_eOwner), UWAI::Player GET_TEAM(m_eAgent),
initNewPlayerInGame GET_TEAM(eNewPlayer), MilitaryAnalyst GET_TEAM(m_eWe),
InvasionGraph GET_TEAM(m_ePlayer/m_eAgent), AI_paranoiaRating GET_TEAM(eRival),
and similar overload-backed calls as wrong-team lookups is RETRACTED.

Preserve those historical sections only so the same false hypothesis is not
rediscovered. F113 is no longer a live file-014 root. The provisional KI#436
number remains historical/retracted; later KI numbering is NOT renumbered.

F104 / provisional KI#427 BROADENED -- WRONG RESOURCE-COUNT UNIT TOO
-------------------------------------------------------------------
The existing off-by-one remains: comment and constant say first FOUR resource
trades, but the counter is incremented and then tested with >= 4, so the fourth
resource-deal is already skipped.

A second manifestation is now source-proven. partnerUtilFromTrade scans every
TradeData item in a deal but collapses resources to one boolean:

    bool bWeReceiveResource = false;
    ...
    if (pItem->m_eItemType == TRADE_RESOURCES)
        bWeReceiveResource = true;
    ...
    if (bWeReceiveResource)
        iResourceTrades++;

Thus iResourceTrades counts DEALS containing at least one resource, not resource
TRADE ITEMS. AdvCiv's AI counterproposal code can repeatedly insert multiple
TRADE_RESOURCES items into one CLinkList deal; CvDeal then processes and saves
each resource item separately. One bundled deal containing several resources
therefore consumes only one of the nominal four-resource slots and can let more
than four individual resource trades through.

Normalize F104 as: partnerUtilFromTrade's intended first-four-resource cap uses
both the wrong boundary and the wrong counting unit. Repair by counting actual
TRADE_RESOURCES items and accepting exactly the first four items, independent
of how they are bundled into deals. Preserve the existing per-deal AI_dealVal
semantics carefully when implementing; this finding is about the cap/count,
not an instruction to value a bundled deal multiple times naively.

F118 / provisional KI#441 -- REVOLTS CAN TURN NEGATIVE ASSET LOSS INTO WAR GAIN
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONFIRMED, inherited Base AdvCiv.

Revolts::evaluate uses each threatened city's UWAICache::City::getAssetScore()
directly in the expected revolt-loss numerator:

    int const iCityAssets = pCacheCity->getAssetScore();
    iTotalAssets += iCityAssets;
    ...
    rLossesFromRevolts += iCityAssets * rLossMult;
    ...
    rRevoltCost = ... * rLossesFromRevolts / iTotalAssets;
    m_iU -= rRevoltCost.round();

Per-city asset score can be negative because CvPlayerAI::AI_assetVal subtracts
city/civic/other-city maintenance. This very file documents that domain in
Risk::evaluate:

    // Per-city score can be negative (maintenance)

and explicitly raises aggregated LOST assets to at least zero there. Revolts
has no corresponding protection.

Reachable sign failure: a valuable safe city keeps iTotalAssets positive, while
a revolt-prone high-maintenance city has negative asset score. Its contribution
makes rLossesFromRevolts negative; if the net expected revolt loss stays below
zero, rRevoltCost is negative and `m_iU -= rRevoltCost` ADDS positive war
utility. War is then rewarded for increasing revolt risk in our own city.

That is not a coherent 'good to shed maintenance' model. CvCity::doRevolt can
damage garrison units, impose occupation and, in non-flip revolts, later kill
population; the owner does not simply discard the maintenance liability when a
revolt occurs. The original Revolts implementation and Base AdvCiv retain the
same unguarded multiplication.

Repair guidance: revolt-threat value must not become negative. Prefer handling
negative per-city asset scores explicitly (e.g. nonnegative threatened-value
input) so a liability neither creates positive war utility nor cancels genuine
revolt exposure in other cities. A final aggregate clamp prevents the sign
inversion but can still let negative cities offset positive threatened value,
so it is the weaker repair.

F119 / provisional KI#442 -- TEAM-INDEXED CAPITULATION RESULTS WRITTEN BY PLAYER ID
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONFIRMED, inherited Base AdvCiv. This is the REAL raw PlayerTypes/TeamTypes
index defect that had previously been hidden inside false F113.

MilitaryAnalyst declares:

    std::vector<TeamSet> m_capitulationsAcceptedPerTeam;

sizes it to MAX_CIV_TEAMS, and exposes:

    getCapitulationsAccepted(TeamTypes eMaster)
        -> m_capitulationsAcceptedPerTeam[eMaster]

All normal consumers therefore address this table by TEAM identity. However,
prepareResults loops PlayerTypes ePlayer and writes:

    pNode->getCapitulationsAccepted(
        m_capitulationsAcceptedPerTeam[ePlayer]);

There is no overloaded accessor here: the enum value is used directly as a
vector index.

InvasionGraph::Node::setCapitulated makes the intended semantics especially
clear. When a team accepts a capitulation, it inserts the capitulated team into
m_capitulationsAccepted of EVERY live member node of the master team. During
result preparation those duplicate member-node team results should be unioned
into the master's TEAM slot. Instead current code scatters them into the member
PLAYER slots.

Concrete configured-team reproduction:
- P0 belongs to Team1; P1 belongs to Team0 (or any mapping where player and team
  IDs differ).
- A capitulation accepted by Team1 is present in P0's node.
- prepareResults stores it in vector slot 0.
- consumers ask getCapitulationsAccepted(Team1), i.e. slot 1.
The result can therefore be absent from the actual master and, when another
team uses the numerically matching slot, appear under the wrong team.

A multi-member team whose member IDs do not include its team ID can leave its
true slot empty entirely. Even when one member ID happens to match, other member
writes can pollute unrelated team-number slots.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 has the identical line. Archaeology shows the older original
form already used `capitulationsAcceptedPerTeam[civId]`, so the defect is
inherited rather than SAS-created.

Surgical repair:

    pNode->getCapitulationsAccepted(
        m_capitulationsAcceptedPerTeam[TEAMID(ePlayer)]);

getCapitulationsAccepted(TeamSet&) inserts/merges into the destination set, so
multiple member nodes naturally union into the one proper master-team slot.
Audit other raw team-indexed arrays separately; unlike GET_TEAM(PlayerTypes),
raw operator[] has no type-aware conversion layer.

THIRDPARTY COLLECTIVE-POWER CANDIDATE -- STRONGER, STILL NOT PROMOTED HERE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
The earlier team-power concern gained a hard internal inconsistency after the
GET_TEAM correction. ThirdPartyIntervention's probability path calls
AI_paranoiaRating(eThey,...). Its rival-team accessor is SAFE through the
PlayerTypes overload and AI_paranoiaRating then uses actual team power, team war
plans, team worst-enemy state, etc. Later ThirdPartyIntervention constructs
rTheirPow from only kThey's player-local ARMY cache plus vassals and applies the
nonlinear <=50% early return before any member aggregation.

Because a DoW by one member commits the full team, this may discard an already
team-level intervention probability merely because the currently evaluated
member alone is weak (e.g. two 40% teammates individually fail although their
team fields 80%). This is now a strong F120 candidate, but retain it under
challenge until the intended member-aggregation/team-size normalization is
fully reconciled with the original ThirdParty design.

F120 / provisional KI#443 -- FAIRPLAY NONZERO-START FIX DOUBLE-COUNTS LATER-ERA START POSITION
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONFIRMED against current SAS and inherited Base AdvCiv.

FairPlay's early-human protection says:

    // All bets off by turn 100 ...
    int iTargetTurn = 100 + m_kGame.getStartTurn();
    ...
    int const iElapsed = (m_kGame.getElapsedGameTurns() / rTrainMod).uround();
    int iTurnsRemaining = iTargetTurn - iElapsed
            - GC.getInfo(eStartEra).getStartPercent();

The `+ getStartTurn()` term is NOT arbitrary dead code. Reachable AdvCiv history
contains a targeted 2021 fix for FairPlay when start turn > 0. The intent was to
avoid prematurely expiring the early-game protection in games whose game-turn
counter starts above zero.

The problem is that CvGame::setStartTurnYear proves getStartTurn contains the
ORDINARY LATER-ERA BASELINE too:

    iStartTurn = sum(game-speed turn increments);
    iStartTurn *= StartPercent(startEra);
    iStartTurn /= 100;

FairPlay then separately subtracts that same era's StartPercent. Thus the old
fix conflates two different quantities:
1. an exceptional/nonstandard extra start-turn offset that may deserve
   compensation; and
2. the normal calendar/game-progress baseline caused merely by selecting a
   later starting era, which FairPlay already tries to shorten through
   StartPercent.

CURRENT SAS NUMERIC CONTROL

Current CIV4GameSpeedInfo totals and CIV4EraInfos give on NORMAL:

    total scheduled turns = 526
    Industrial StartPercent = 50 -> baseline startTurn = 263
    Modern     StartPercent = 65 -> baseline startTurn = 341 (integer floor)
    Future     StartPercent = 80 -> baseline startTurn = 420 (integer floor)

At elapsed turn 0 and neutral map-density factor, current FairPlay therefore
starts with approximately:

    Industrial: 100 + 263 - 50 = 313 normalized fair-play turns remaining
    Modern:     100 + 341 - 65 = 376
    Future:     100 + 420 - 80 = 440

Yet the entire normal-speed game remaining after those baselines is only about:

    Industrial: 526 - 263 = 263 actual turns
    Modern:     526 - 341 = 185
    Future:     526 - 420 = 106

The supposed early-game protection can therefore remain positive for the entire
remaining later-era game even before considering map-density scaling. Slower
speeds make the absolute mismatch still larger because startTurn scales with
full game length while the separately subtracted StartPercent is only 0..100.

This is stronger than merely saying two coordinate systems look mixed: current
XML plus CvGame initialization gives a deterministic shipped reproduction.

ANCESTRY / REPAIR BOUNDARY

The historical nonzero-start fix was sensible for the case it targeted, so do
NOT simply delete all start-turn compensation. Repair should distinguish the
EXTRA start-turn component from the normal starting-era baseline, and compare
all terms in one normalized elapsed-time unit. One conceptual baseline is:

    normalEraStartTurn = totalScheduledTurns * StartPercent / 100
    extraStartOffset   = max(0, getStartTurn() - normalEraStartTurn)

then normalize only the extra component consistently with rTrainMod (or replace
the whole grace calculation with a direct normalized elapsed-since-start gate).
Preserve the existing crowded-map and era-advance modifiers after the timebase
is made coherent.


F121 / provisional KI#444 -- "LEAVE THE START ERA" USED AS A TEMPORARY STARTUP CLOCK CAN NEVER EXPIRE IN TERMINAL-ERA STARTS
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONFIRMED, inherited Base AdvCiv; two independent UWAI manifestations.

ROOT

Several UWAI systems use

    currentEra <= startEra

as a proxy for "we are still too early after game start to trust this signal."
That is a plausible settling heuristic when there is guaranteed to be a later
era transition. It is not a bounded time condition. If the game starts in the
last defined era, no later era exists and the temporary guard becomes permanent.

MANIFESTATION A -- KINGMAKING PERMANENTLY DISABLED

KingMaking::preEvaluate says:

    // Scoreboard ranks just aren't meaningful off the bat, even if the game
    // starts in the Modern era. Leaving m_winningPresent empty causes 0 utility.
    if (m_eGameEra <= m_kGame.getStartEra())
        return 0;

The comment explicitly describes a temporary "off the bat" grace period. Current
SAS's final defined era is ERA_FUTURE (StartPercent 80). A Future-era start has
no era after Future, so currentEra can never become greater than startEra.
KingMaking therefore remains disabled for the entire game -- including late
score/time/victory-stage situations the aspect exists specifically to police.

MANIFESTATION B -- LONG-TERM THREAT / PREEMPTIVEWAR PERMANENTLY ZERO

UWAICache::calculateThreatRating has the same proxy:

    // Can't reliably estimate yield rates in the early game
    if (GC.getGame().getCurrentEra() <= GC.getGame().getStartEra())
        return 0;

Threat ratings are refreshed from this function. PreEmptiveWar then begins from
ourCache().threatRating(eThey) and immediately returns when it is below 0.15.
Thus a terminal-era start permanently reports zero long-term threat and disables
PreEmptiveWar as well.

REACHABILITY / CONTROL

SAS defines ERA_FUTURE as an ordinary EraInfo and uses it throughout start-era
building/tech logic; there is no later EraInfo to advance into. Even apart from
the normal custom-game era selector, scenarios can set InitCore era directly.
The root therefore does not require a hypothetical future era or XML modmod.

The neighboring DramaticArc startup gate is a strong control: it uses normalized
elapsed turns (`elapsed * speedMult < 25`) and therefore expires even when the
game begins in the terminal era. That is the correct kind of bounded startup
clock for an "off the bat" concern.

REPAIR BOUNDARY

Do not special-case only ERA_FUTURE if avoidable. Replace these temporary
"must leave the start era" gates with a bounded normalized elapsed-time/game-
progress grace, optionally retaining an era-advance shortcut if desired. That
preserves the intent for Ancient/Modern starts and remains well-defined at the
terminal era.


CONTROLS / OPEN QUESTIONS AT WIP12
----------------------------------
- Revolts::m_countedCities does not leak between separate war evaluations:
  WarEvaluator constructs and destroys a fresh aspect set per war/peace
  scenario. The set intentionally persists only across member/rival passes in
  one scenario. No new root.
- ThirdPartyIntervention's player-local <=50% power gate remains under challenge.
  Its intervention probability is partly team-derived, but the original aspect
  was designed as pairwise member utility with later team-size normalization.
  No F122 without a harder invariant.
- FairPlay F120 is specifically a partial historical start-turn fix that
  overcompensates the normal later-era baseline; it is NOT a claim that all use
  of getStartTurn is wrong.

F096 / KI#418 -- ADDITIONAL WARUTILITYASPECT MANIFESTATION -- LOATHING MIXES
LIVING-PLAYER COUNTS WITH ASSIGNED TEAM MEMBER COUNTS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
This remains the existing dead-roster semantic root, not a new F-number.

Loathing::evaluate() computes the number of relevant free civilization players
from living-player iteration:

    int iFreeCivPlayers = countFreeRivals<false>();

and its joint-war ally loop likewise uses PlayerIter<FREE_MAJOR_CIV,...>, i.e.
living free major civilizations. If our team is not a vassal, however, it then
adds:

    iFreeCivPlayers += kOurTeam.getNumMembers();

and finally says:

    // Count Loathing only once per team member
    ... / (iFreeCivDivisor * kOurTeam.getNumMembers())

WarEvaluator's outer contribution loop is MemberIter and therefore evaluates only
living members of the agent team. An eliminated-but-still-assigned teammate thus
has two independent effects despite contributing no Loathing evaluation of its
own: it increases the supposed number of free civilization players before the
sqrt divisor is computed, and it increases the final team-member divisor.

This gives Loathing a particularly clean F096 manifestation because both nearby
quantities are explicitly framed in PLAYER units and the actual evaluator consumes
living players. getAliveCount()/alive-player counting is the coherent denominator
here. This is additional evidence for the WIP02 F096 broadening; it does not imply
that every getNumMembers() in UWAI is automatically wrong.


F122 / provisional KI#445 -- TACTICALSITUATION CAN REUSE THE SAME AGENT UNIT
AGAINST MULTIPLE MEMBERS OF ONE ENEMY TEAM
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONFIRMED against current SAS and inherited Base AdvCiv 1.14.

ROOT / EXACT LOCAL INVARIANT

TacticalSituation::evalEngagement() builds `weThreaten` from the current agent
player's groups. When it inspects threatened plots, it counts only units whose
combat owner is the CURRENT rival player eThey. It then explicitly enforces:

    // Count at most one enemy unit per unit of ours as "entangled",
    // i.e. count pairs of units.
    iTheirUnits = std::min(iTheirUnits, iOurUnits);

That cap is correct only inside one rival-player pass. WarUtilityAspect::evaluate
iterates every living `KNOWN_POTENTIAL_ENEMY_OF` player in the military analysis
and invokes the same TacticalSituation aspect once for each rival. Therefore the
agent-side `weThreaten` inventory and its per-plot iOurUnits cap are rebuilt and
reused independently for every living member of the same hostile team.

DETERMINISTIC TEAM-PARTITION REPRODUCTION

Let player A have one relevant unit able to attack a visible plot. The hostile
team has players B and C, with one unit from each on that same plot.

B pass:
    iOurUnits = 1
    B-owned units on plot = 1
    entangled = min(1, 1) = 1

C pass:
    the same A unit is rebuilt into `weThreaten`
    iOurUnits = 1
    C-owned units on plot = 1
    entangled = min(1, 1) = 1

Across the two rival-player evaluations, the single A unit has therefore supplied
two "pairs" despite the source-authored invariant saying to count at most one
enemy unit per unit of ours.

If the identical two hostile units are instead both owned by B, the one B pass is:

    iOurUnits = 1
    B-owned units = 2
    entangled = min(2, 1) = 1

Thus merely repartitioning an otherwise identical hostile team force between
teammate ownership changes TacticalSituation utility. Team warfare itself has not
changed, yet the nonlinear one-to-one cap is reset at the player boundary.

RELATED MANIFESTATION

The same structural boundary affects `iOurExposed`. For each current rival player,
TacticalSituation asks:

    kWe.AI_getPlotDanger(..., eThey)

and can count the same damaged agent unit as exposed independently to B and then C.
The entanglement invariant is the stronger exact proof, so F122 is normalized
around agent-side tactical quantities being independently consumable by several
members of one enemy team; it does not assert that every per-player Tactical term
must be team-aggregated.

ANCESTRY / NEGATIVE CONTROL

Base AdvCiv 1.14 contains the same player-filtered tactical code. Its history also
contains commit ac91311251477c426ac9d2230a9603b9d93a73b4, titled:

    Fix UWAI bug with counting of entangled units

The surviving multi-member-team case crosses the per-rival evaluation boundary
that the local cap cannot see. This historical concern about double-counting
strengthens the interpretation of the explicit current comment rather than merely
suggesting a different tuning preference.

REPAIR DIRECTION

Do not merely divide final TacticalSituation utility by enemy-team size: a linear
normalizer cannot restore a one-to-one relationship after the nonlinear per-player
cap has already been applied. Safer directions are to aggregate relevant hostile
units/danger across eTheirTeam before applying the caps, or to maintain shared
per-enemy-team tactical accounting so one agent unit cannot be consumed again by
another teammate pass. Preserve genuinely player-specific terms where ownership
matters.


NEGATIVE CONTROLS RETAINED BEFORE F123
--------------------------------------
- The broad claim "TacticalSituation should never run once per rival player" is
  NOT promoted. Several subterms are intentionally player-specific. F122 is the
  narrower cross-pass reuse defect proved by the one-pair invariant.
- ThirdPartyIntervention's player-local power cutoff remains under challenge; its
  pairwise architecture and later team-member normalization still leave intent
  ambiguous enough that it is not assigned a root here.
- The prior GreedForVassals zero-city/capital-null idea remains unpromoted under
  current SAS game rules; normal established zero-city majors are eliminated.
- Revolts' m_countedCities lifetime remains clean because aspect objects are fresh
  per war/peace scenario and persist only across the intended member/rival passes.
