F123 / provisional KI#446 -- BELLICOSITY'S ANTI-THIRD-PARTY LOSS CAP IS RESET
FOR EACH MEMBER OF ONE ENEMY TEAM
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv defect / team-partition nonlinearity.

CURRENT CODE / INTENDED SAFEGUARD

Bellicosity::evaluate() is invoked separately for each rival player. For every
relevant military branch it computes:

    rOurLostPow = militAnalyst().lostPower(eWe, eBranch);
    rOurMinusTheirLostPow +=
        min(2.35 * rOurLostPow,
            militAnalyst().lostPower(eThey, eBranch))
        - 0.75 * rOurLostPow;

The surrounding comment says that, if the rival loses much more than we do,
"chances are that a third party is causing this." Historical ancestry makes the
purpose even less ambiguous: AdvCiv commit ed1826faf199f4a18442c9196f181a46797e79c1
explicitly records:

    Fixed an issue with war utility from "bellicosity" counting war successes
    of allies.

That commit introduced the current min(2.35 * ourLost, theirLost) cap in place
of the former direct enemy-loss subtraction. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS
retain the same implementation.

ROOT

MilitaryAnalyst::lostPower(PlayerTypes, branch) is player-local. The eWe loss
therefore has one fixed value for the current agent member, while the generic
WarUtilityAspect rival loop calls Bellicosity once for every living rival player.
Against a multi-member hostile team, the same agent loss budget is consequently
reused once per teammate and the nonlinear anti-third-party cap is restarted at
each player boundary.

DETERMINISTIC PARTITION REPRODUCTION

Take one branch, current aggressive power 100 and agent loss 10.

If a one-player enemy side loses 20:

    min(23.5, 20) - 7.5 = 12.5

If an otherwise identical two-player enemy team has the same total 20 losses
split 10 + 10:

    B pass: min(23.5, 10) - 7.5 = 2.5
    C pass: min(23.5, 10) - 7.5 = 2.5
    total = 5

The war-side loss balance is identical, but merely repartitioning ownership
between teammates cuts the Bellicosity signal from 12.5 to 5.

The nonlinearity can bend the other way too. With total enemy loss 40:

    one player: min(23.5, 40) - 7.5 = 16
    20 + 20:    12.5 + 12.5 = 25

So this is not a missing constant team-size divisor. The result depends on where
the min cap is applied. The later per-rival glory-rate calculation can introduce
additional nonlinear saturation through decreaseTo(1).

WHY THE TEAM BOUNDARY MATTERS HERE

Bellicosity's own source describes a "good war" as one "that we win." The 2018
repair is specifically trying not to credit enemy losses caused by allies or
third parties. In a Civ4 team war, B and C are one war side; resetting the same
A-loss comparison separately for B and C defeats that safeguard. Player-local
loss storage is fine, but the side-level comparison cannot be reconstructed by
applying min/subtraction independently and summing afterward.

REPAIR DIRECTION

Aggregate the relevant lost power of living members on eTheirTeam (and whatever
other side membership the intended model explicitly wants) before applying the
anti-third-party cap against eWe's loss once for that hostile team. Ensure the
team is charged only once in this aspect. Preserve player-specific reachability
or personality conditions deliberately rather than blindly replacing every
PlayerTypes quantity with a team quantity.

Do not repair by dividing the final utility by team size: linear normalization
cannot undo the partition-sensitive min and later saturation.


F124 / provisional KI#447 -- THIRDPARTYINTERVENTION USES FULL RIVAL-TEAM POWER
TO ESTIMATE INTERVENTION PROBABILITY, THEN HARD-GATES DANGER ON ONE MEMBER'S ARMY
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv team-partition defect. This is independent of F115's
game-speed peace-decay bug.

THE INTERNAL UNIT SWITCH

For a prospective third party eThey, ThirdPartyIntervention first estimates the
chance of intervention through:

    kWe.AI_paranoiaRating(eThey, iOurDefPow, false, true)

AI_paranoiaRating immediately resolves:

    CvTeamAI const& kRivalTeam = GET_TEAM(eRival);
    int const iTheirPower = kRivalTeam.getPower(true);

and uses that full team power together with team war state, enemy-power percent,
worst-enemy state and team no-war probability. ThirdPartyIntervention also uses
kTheirTeam's DogpileWarRand, LimitedWarRand and MaxWarRand.

After a positive intervention probability has been established, however, the
threat-strength model switches to:

    rTheirPow = kThey.uwai().getCache().getPowerValues()[ARMY]->power();

It then adds half the ARMY power of eTheirTeam's vassals, but never adds the army
power of eThey's ordinary teammates. UWAICache military branches are created for
one PlayerTypes owner, so this is genuinely player-local power rather than a
hidden team aggregate.

The player-local value is then subjected to the decisive nonlinear gate:

    rTheirPowToOurs = rTheirPow / rOurPow;
    if (rTheirPowToOurs <= 0.5)
        return;

Only much later, after all nonlinear ratio shaping, does the aspect divide cost
by a function of both teams' member counts.

TEAM-WAR CONTRACT

CvTeam::declareWar changes the at-war state of the declaring TeamTypes and the
target TeamTypes. The declaration is therefore not a war by one player while a
teammate remains neutral; all living members of the rival team are on that war
side. That matches the team-level power already used by AI_paranoiaRating.

DETERMINISTIC THRESHOLD REPRODUCTION

Let our relevant post-loss power be 100. Let a two-member potential-intervening
team have 40 ARMY power in B and 40 in C, no relevant vassals/losses, and hold
other player-local probability inputs equal/positive.

The paranoia path can see the rival team at power 80 for either member. Yet the
severity path evaluates:

    B: 40 / 100 = 0.40 -> return
    C: 40 / 100 = 0.40 -> return

Total intervention cost is therefore zero.

If the same team-wide 80 ARMY power is instead concentrated under B:

    B: 80 / 100 = 0.80 -> passes the 0.50 gate

and a nonzero cost can be produced. Team military capacity and the team-wide war
that would result are unchanged; only teammate ownership partition changed.

The later

    rCost *= 2;
    rCost /= (kOurTeam.getNumMembers() + kTheirTeam.getNumMembers());

cannot repair this because it executes only after the hard return. More generally,
the power-ratio transform is nonlinear, so summing separately transformed member
powers is not equivalent to transforming the combined intervening-side power.

ANCESTRY / INTENT CONTROL

The player-local power block, vassal addition, 0.5 floor and later member-count
normalization all date back to the original 2021 AdvCiv ThirdPartyIntervention
commit f39e13df870c036c2e5d0db26437254760898bdf. Later 2023 commits explicitly
retuned intervention probabilities and the power-ratio estimate but retained
this team/member boundary. Base AdvCiv 1.14 therefore inherits it unchanged.

That history cautions against replacing the whole pairwise model: intervention
probability intentionally contains player-specific attitude, memory, closeness,
victory-stage and capital-distance terms. F124 is narrower. Once the aspect asks
"how dangerous would this intervention be?", the hard power gate must represent
the team that will actually enter the war, especially because the immediately
preceding paranoia model already measures that team's collective power.

REPAIR DIRECTION

Keep genuinely player-specific probability/influence terms if desired, but build
the threat-strength ratio and its 0.5 gate from the combined living military
power of the intervening team, with vassal treatment reviewed once at team scope.
Then ensure the resulting team-level severity is not independently charged in
full once per teammate; a canonical team pass or another explicit aggregation is
safer than relying on the later linear member-count divisor.


CONTROLS BEFORE NEXT ROOT
-------------------------
- F115/KI#438 remains the independent ThirdPartyIntervention game-speed bug: a
  normalized peace-duration local is computed and discarded. F124 does not
  subsume it.
- F113/KI#436 remains retracted. GET_TEAM(eThey) is safe because the AdvCiv AI
  accessors overload PlayerTypes and resolve TEAMID(eThey); F124 does not depend
  on the rejected raw-array interpretation.
- The mere fact that ThirdPartyIntervention evaluates player pairs is NOT called
  defective. F124 is the narrower contradiction between its team-level danger /
  declaration model and the nonlinear player-local military gate.
- DramaticArc's existing F116 exact-counter bug remains independent. A possible
  additional team-partition effect in its per-player action/fairness gates is
  the next challenge; it is not promoted here.

F096 / KI#418 -- ADDITIONAL WARUTILITYASPECT MANIFESTATIONS -- DEAD ASSIGNED
TEAM MEMBERS DILUTE THIRDPARTYINTERVENTION AND DRAMATICARC
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
EXISTING ROOT broadened only; no new F-number.

The CvTeam audit established that getNumMembers() includes dead players still
assigned to the team, whereas the WarEvaluator/WarUtilityAspect evaluation
surface iterates living player members. WIP02 and WIP13 already proved this
mismatch in normalizeUtility, flipped-tile losses, GreedForVassals and Loathing.
Two more late-aspect uses have the same consumer-level proof:

ThirdPartyIntervention ends with:

    rCost *= 2;
    rCost /= (kOurTeam.getNumMembers() + kTheirTeam.getNumMembers());

DramaticArc ends with:

    rUtil /= scaled(kOurTeam.getNumMembers() + kTheirTeam.getNumMembers(), 2);

Both aspects are reached through the generic per-rival WarUtilityAspect loop,
which evaluates living rival players; WarEvaluator itself evaluates living
members of the agent team. A dead assigned teammate therefore contributes no
corresponding aspect pass or military/player state, but still enlarges these
normalization denominators and dilutes utility/cost.

This is the same F096 roster-cardinality contract already established elsewhere,
not a reason to replace every getNumMembers use mechanically. In particular,
consumer semantics still need to be proved case by case.


F125 / provisional KI#448 -- DRAMATICARC'S PLAYER-LOCAL SAFETY AND ACTION GATES
CAN LICENSE THE SAME TEAM-WIDE WAR THROUGH ANOTHER TEAMMATE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv team-partition defect, independent of F116's exact
peace-counter bug and F096's dead-member denominator distortion.

INTENDED ROLE / HISTORY CONTROL

AdvCiv commit 03f2a564827127bc9f32cfa85362ab42aad6f7ec introduced the
"Dramatic Arc" war-utility aspect to slightly encourage war after an unusually
quiet period and discourage it when there is too much warfare. Four days later,
commit 1c62194c840c55304b61e1e86a96618a8f299037 was explicitly titled:

    UWAI: be careful about attacking humans for dramatic reasons

and added the current human-capital-loss safeguard. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current
SAS retain the same DramaticArc::evaluate implementation.

CURRENT GATES

For a simulated transition into war with eTheirTeam, each rival-player pass
starts from the same team-wide transition:

    bWillBeAtWar = militAnalyst().isWar(eWe, eThey);
    if (bWillBeAtWar == kOurTeam.isAtWar(eTheirTeam))
        return;

When positive dramatic utility would encourage a new war, however, fairness and
"enough action" are checked through the current rival player:

    iTheirLostCities = militAnalyst().lostCities(eThey).size();

    if (iTheirLostCities > 2 ||
        (kThey.isHuman() && iTheirLostCities == 1 && kThey.hasCapital() &&
         lostCities(eThey).count(kThey.getCapital()->plotNum()) > 0 && ...))
        return;

    if ((iTheirLostCities == 0 && conqueredCities(eWe).empty()) ||
        lostPower(eWe, ARMY) + lostPower(eThey, ARMY) < ourArmy / 20)
        return;

MilitaryAnalyst lostCities/lostPower are explicitly PlayerTypes result sets and
values. The generic aspect loop invokes this independently for every living
member of the hostile team.

MANIFESTATION A -- THE HUMAN-SAFETY COMMIT CAN BE BYPASSED BY THE HUMAN'S AI
TEAMMATE

Take a two-member target team B+C, where B is human and C is AI. The simulated
new war is a team-wide war against B+C. Suppose B is predicted to lose exactly
its capital under the conditions targeted by the 2022 safeguard.

B's pass sees kThey.isHuman() and returns, correctly refusing to award positive
"dramatic" utility for that dangerous war.

C's pass evaluates the same team-wide war transition but kThey.isHuman() is
false. The explicit human-protection gate disappears. If C's player-local action
checks pass, positive dramatic utility is still added for entering the war that
B's pass deliberately rejected.

The final team-size divisor can reduce the surviving C contribution, but it
cannot restore a safety return that was applied only to B.

MANIFESTATION B -- THE MINIMUM-ACTION GATE DEPENDS ON OWNERSHIP PARTITION

Let our current ARMY power be 100, so the minimum predicted combined-loss gate
is 5. Assume we conquer at least one target-team city, our own predicted ARMY
loss is 0, and the hostile team loses 8 ARMY power total.

If one teammate owns all 8 lost power, that member's pass clears the 5-point
threshold and can add dramatic utility.

If the same team-wide loss is split 4 + 4 between B and C, then both passes test
only their own 4 against the same threshold and both return. The military event
and war side are otherwise identical; merely repartitioning losses between
teammates changes whether the war is judged sufficiently "real" to encourage.

ROOT

DramaticArc wants to decide whether a TEAM-WIDE war transition is a fair and
substantive event before using it to steer global warfare tension. Its hard
safety/action gates are nevertheless scoped to whichever PlayerTypes happens to
be the current rival pass. A hard return is nonlinear; independently applying it
per teammate and then summing/dividing cannot reproduce one team-war decision.

REPAIR DIRECTION

Evaluate the "safe/fair/substantive enough to use for dramatic tension" predicate
once for the hostile team: aggregate relevant lost cities and ARMY loss across
living members, and preserve the human-safety intent if any affected team member
meets the protected human-capital condition. Then charge the team-wide dramatic
transition canonically once, or otherwise ensure the aggregate decision is not
reopened by another teammate pass.

Keep F116 separate: the 8-turn HasMet tolerance remains an exact-counter/time
bug even in one-player teams. Keep F096 separate: dead-member normalization is a
roster-cardinality defect, not the live-member nonlinear gate here.


F126 / provisional KI#449 -- DISTRACTION CHARGES THE SAME TEAM-WAR OPPORTUNITY
COST ONCE PER LIVING ENEMY TEAMMATE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv team/player aggregation defect. Current SAS's newer
winning-war cap can modulate the amount but did not create this root.

WHY BOTH TEAMMATES ARE EVALUATED

WarUtilityAspect::evaluate(MilitaryAnalyst const&) loops every living known
potential enemy player that is part of the military analysis. For a prospective
war against target team T, MilitaryAnalyst::doWePlanToDeclWar(ePlayer) returns
true whenever TEAMID(ePlayer) == WarEvalParameters::getTarget(); therefore every
living known member of T is inserted into ourFutureOpponents/theirSide and then
m_partOfAnalysis. For an existing war, living members are likewise included by
the currently-at-war construction.

Distraction::evaluate is thus called once for B and once for C when B+C are one
multi-member target team, provided the ordinary player-pair reachability guard is
satisfied for both.

THE COST IT COMPUTES IS LARGELY THE SAME TEAM-WAR COST

After the reachability check, the core inputs are team-scoped:

    iWarDuration = kOurTeam.AI_getAtWarCounter(eTheirTeam);

    rWarUtilityVsThem = normalizeUtility(
        ourCache().warUtilityIgnoringDistraction(eTheirTeam));

normalizeUtility's parameter is explicitly named rUtilityTeamOnTeam, and both B
and C have the same eTheirTeam. Alternative targets are iterated as TeamTypes;
their war plans, declaration legality, reachability and cached war utility are
team quantities too.

Most decisively, every qualifying actual alternative war plan adds a fixed:

    rDistractionCost += 5.5;

under the comment:

    The war against eThey distracts us from our war against eAltTarget.

For B and C on one target team, "the war against eThey" is the same Civ4 team
war. Yet the fixed 5.5 is added independently in B's pass and C's pass. There is
no final division or canonical-team guard before:

    m_iU -= rDistractionCost.round();

DETERMINISTIC DUPLICATION CONTROL

Choose a two-member hostile team B+C such that both player pairs are reachable,
no member is eliminated/almost-done, and our team has one qualifying alternative
team D with an existing AI war plan. Hold all other optional opportunity-cost
terms at zero if desired.

Against a one-player target team, that alternative plan contributes the fixed
5.5 distraction nudge once.

Against an otherwise identical two-player target team B+C:

    B pass: +5.5 distraction cost for the D war plan
    C pass: +5.5 distraction cost for the same D war plan

so the same opportunity cost becomes 11 before rounding. Team-size handling
inside normalizeUtility applies only to the cached team-on-team war-utility
inputs; it does not scale this fixed nudge or the final rDistractionCost.

The broader opportunity-cost branch has the same structural duplication because
its duration/current-target/alternative-target inputs are team-scoped and the
result is again subtracted per rival pass. Player-local reachability and the
"almost done" city multiplier can legitimately differ, but those differences do
not justify charging a common team-war opportunity cost repeatedly once both
passes clear their guards.

ANCESTRY / INTERNAL CONTROLS

Base AdvCiv 1.14 contains the same generic Distraction structure and fixed 5.5
actual-war-plan nudge. Historical AdvCiv work explicitly describes/tunes the
negative utility counted by "Distraction" and later refactors alternative war
targets to teams; the current source itself labels the cached utility input as
team-on-team.

Current SAS adds a winning-war cap using target TEAM city count, TEAM power and
TEAM war success. That addition further confirms the target-war quantity's team
scope, but the duplicated per-member charge predates SAS and survives even when
that cap never fires.

REPAIR DIRECTION

Compute Distraction once per hostile team (or nominate a canonical living member
for the team-level charge), while retaining player-pair reachability only as a
question of whether the war side is meaningfully reachable. Review the existing
player-local almost-done multiplier separately: elimination of one member can be
a real detail, but it should modulate one team-war distraction estimate rather
than create multiple copies of the common opportunity cost.

Do not "fix" this by dividing every per-rival result blindly by team size. Some
Distraction guards are player-specific, and the fixed/common team cost plus
nonlinear maxima/aggregation make canonical team-level evaluation clearer and
less partition-sensitive.


CONTROLS / NEXT CHALLENGE
-------------------------
- LoveOfPeace superficially has the same per-rival shape, but current SAS data
  leaves iLoveOfPeace at 0; do not promote a dormant mod-mod configuration path
  as a current defect merely for symmetry.
- Revolts' m_countedCities lifetime remains a closed false positive: aspect
  objects are fresh per WarEvaluator scenario, while the set intentionally
  persists only across rival/member passes inside that scenario.
- Distraction F126 is independent of the SAS winning-war cap. The inherited
  fixed 5.5 duplicate is sufficient proof by itself.
- F123 Bellicosity and F124 ThirdPartyIntervention remain separate nonlinear
  partition roots; they are not collapsed into a vague umbrella issue.

C014-WIP16 CONTINUATION -- GLOBAL VICTORY CAPS + TEAM-KEYED HIRED-HAND OBLIGATION
===============================================================================

CHECKPOINT BASIS

F127 / provisional KI#450 -- MILITARYVICTORY CAPS GLOBAL DOMINATION/DIPLO
PROGRESS SEPARATELY INSIDE EACH RIVAL-PLAYER PASS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv global-threshold aggregation defect. This is distinct
from F105's exact Domination equality/divisor bug and F111's AP wrong-owner test.

ARCHITECTURE

MilitaryVictory is an ordinary WarUtilityAspect. For each living agent-team
member, WarUtilityAspect::evaluate(MilitaryAnalyst const&) calls
MilitaryVictory::evaluate() once for every living known rival player that is
part of the analysis. MilitaryVictory then computes progress toward the agent's
shared/global victory thresholds from the current eThey player's predicted
losses.

This player-by-player decomposition is harmless only while the progress function
is additive. The current implementation applies global completion caps BEFORE
rival contributions are combined.

DOMINATION -- THE SOURCE'S OWN COMMENT STATES THE INVARIANT

progressRatingDomination() uses the agent team's current global threshold:

    iPopToGo = iPopTarget - kOurTeam.getTotalPopulation();

It accumulates population gained from cities lost by the CURRENT rival player
and then explicitly says:

    // No use in population beyond the victory threshold
    rPopGained.decreaseTo(iPopToGo);

That is exactly the correct conceptual cap for the full military scenario: once
we have gained the remaining required population, additional projected conquest
cannot make us more than 100% complete on that Domination component.

But the cap is reset for every eThey pass. MilitaryVictory::evaluate then clamps
that rival's progress again to [0,1] and immediately converts it to utility.
There is no later aggregate cap across rivals.

DETERMINISTIC DOMINATION REPRODUCTION

Suppose the agent team needs only 5 effective population to satisfy the remaining
Domination population threshold, and land/city conditions are such that this
component controls progress.

If projected conquest from B supplies 6 population and C supplies none:

    B pass: rPopGained -> capped to 5 -> 100% progress
    C pass: 0

If the same military scenario instead takes cities worth 6 population from B
AND 6 from C:

    B pass: independently capped to 5 -> 100%
    C pass: independently capped to 5 -> 100%

The global threshold has been credited twice. This can arise from two enemy teams
or, especially cleanly, two members of one hostile team. Merely repartitioning
otherwise equivalent conquered cities between members can change how many times
the completion cap is reached.

DIPLOMACY HAS THE SAME ROOT

progressRatingDiplomacy() uses the global remaining vote requirement cached by
preEvaluate:

    m_iVotesToGo = kOurTeam.AI_votesToGoForVictory();

After accumulating expected population/votes from the CURRENT rival's losses it
caps:

    rPopGained.decreaseTo(m_iVotesToGo);
    rProgress = rPopGained / m_iVotesToGo;

Again, if only 5 votes remain and B's projected conquests provide 6 while C's
provide another 6, each rival pass can independently report 100% vote progress.
The same five-vote global deficit is completed twice.

The AP-obstacle subcomponent is player-count based and was already checked as a
separate control; F127 does not relabel that numerator/denominator as defective.
The defect is specifically the repeated GLOBAL vote/population completion cap.

AGENT-TEAM MEMBERS CAN ALSO REPEAT THE GLOBAL CAP

WarEvaluator reuses the aspect set while evaluating every living member of the
agent team. Domination and diplo victory are team-owned conditions, but each
agent member can contribute projected conquests through its own eWe pass. Thus
the same global remaining threshold can be independently capped not only across
rivals but also across agent-member/rival-member pairs when multiple teammates
contribute to the projected gains.

ANCESTRY / INTENT CONTROL

The original AdvCiv MilitaryVictory implementation already had this per-rival
architecture and per-rival [0,1] progress cap. Later commits increased the value
of military-victory progress and added capitulation contributions without moving
the global threshold cap outside the player pass. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current
SAS remain identical here.

The comment "No use in population beyond the victory threshold" is the strongest
intent control: the implementation itself wants surplus progress discarded, but
its scope allows the same surplus boundary to reset once per player.

REPAIR DIRECTION

Aggregate projected Domination population/city progress and diplomatic-vote
progress across the entire relevant military scenario before applying the
remaining-threshold cap and converting progress to utility. A natural approach
is one pre/global computation per agent team (or a cumulative marginal-progress
budget shared across player passes), while leaving genuinely opponent-specific
costs such as nukes separately attributable if desired.

Do not simply divide final MilitaryVictory utility by rival/team size: the error
is a reset global cap, not a linear scale problem. Conquest progress should be
reviewed separately because eliminating distinct rivals can legitimately be
additive; F127 is already proven by Domination and Diplomacy without claiming
that every MilitaryVictory subcomponent must be globalized identically.


F128 / provisional KI#451 -- HIREDHAND COUNTS ONE TEAM-KEYED SPONSORSHIP /
OBLIGATION ONCE PER LIVING MEMBER OF THE SPONSORED-WAR TARGET TEAM
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv team-duplication defect.

TEAM-KEYED CONTRACT

UWAICache exposes:

    int bountyAgainst(TeamTypes eTeam) const;
    PlayerTypes sponsorAgainst(TeamTypes eTeam) const;

HiredHand::evaluate therefore looks up the already-accepted sponsorship with:

    eSponsor = ourCache().sponsorAgainst(eTheirTeam);
    iOriginalUtility = ourCache().bountyAgainst(eTheirTeam);

This describes one payment/obligation for war against a target TEAM, not a
separate payment against every member player.

Once the sponsorship is found, the main branch adds:

    rUtility += eval(eSponsor, iOriginalUtility, 20);

HiredHand::eval in turn measures how long the hired side has fought through the
TEAM at-war counters against eTheirTeam. Its output therefore also describes the
same team-war obligation.

WHY IT IS DUPLICATED

HiredHand is an ordinary concernsOnlyWarParties aspect. Against a multi-member
hostile team B+C, both B and C are part of the analysis and the generic aspect
loop calls HiredHand for each living player.

For a continuing sponsored war, getWarsContinued(eWe).count(eThey) can be true
for both B and C. Then:

    B pass -> sponsorAgainst(team B+C), same bounty, same war counter -> obligation
    C pass -> sponsorAgainst(team B+C), same bounty, same war counter -> obligation

There is no member-count normalization or canonical-team guard before the two
results accumulate into m_iU.

DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCTION

Assume D paid us once to fight target team B+C; original sponsorship utility is
25 and the obligation ratio currently makes eval return, say, 20.

A one-player target team contributes +20 HiredHand utility.

With two living members B+C, holding all ordinary guards true:

    B pass: +20 for the D sponsorship against team B+C
    C pass: +20 for the same D sponsorship against team B+C
    total:  +40

No second payment or promise occurred. Only the target team's player count
changed.

SECOND INDEPENDENT MANIFESTATION -- HISTORICAL ROLE

The fallback scenario rule says that, if we have been at war since the start of
the game, we should play along for a while:

    if (kOurTeam.AI_getAtWarCounter(eTheirTeam) >=
        m_kGame.getElapsedGameTurns())
        rUtility += eval(NO_PLAYER, 50, 12);

That condition and eval timer are again entirely team-scoped. A scenario war
against B+C therefore receives the same historical-role obligation once on B's
pass and once again on C's.

The branch where WE hired an ally contains some player-specific memory detail
and should be reviewed on its own; F128 does not require it. The accepted
sponsorship branch and historical-role branch already prove the root.

ANCESTRY / INTERNAL CONTROL

The original AdvCiv HiredHand implementation already queried sponsorship by
TEAMID(theyId) and used the target team's at-war counter. Historical fixes later
adjusted obligation duration/payment behavior (including a bug where a hired AI
continued doggedly after the sponsor made peace) but retained the per-rival
aspect placement. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS HiredHand::evaluate are
textually identical.

REPAIR DIRECTION

Charge team-keyed HiredHand obligations once per hostile target team, e.g. by a
canonical living target member or an explicit per-team pass. Preserve truly
player-specific relationship/memory pieces separately where they matter. The
sponsorship bounty and historical-role timer themselves should not be multiplied
by the number of living players assigned to the enemy team.


CONTROLS / NEXT CHALLENGE
-------------------------
- GreedForCash supplies a useful positive control: its comment explicitly says
  "Only one team member will pay" and uses normalizeUtility(4), showing that this
  codebase does deliberately normalize a team-level fixed amount when evaluated
  through player passes.
- Rebuke explicitly documents that counting capitulation utility multiple times
  across team members is acceptable there because the underlying rebuke memory
  is player-pair specific. Do not generalize F128 to every repeated team call.
- MilitaryVictory's Conquest subcomponent remains under separate review; F127
  does not need it and should not overclaim it.

C014-WIP17 APPEND -- WarUtilityAspect.cpp / vassal-score team-domain audit
===============================================================================

F129 / provisional KI#452 -- VASSAL CURRENT-TECH SCORE IS TEAM-OWNED BUT CACHED
PER PLAYER AND SUMMED ONCE PER VASSAL MEMBER
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv team-duplication defect.

ROOT CONTRACT

UWAICache stores the value through a player-keyed map:

    int vassalTechScore(PlayerTypes ePlayer) const;
    CivPlayerMap<int> m_aiVassalTechScore;

and updateVassalScore(PlayerTypes eRival) computes it by iterating every tech and
asking:

    GET_PLAYER(eRival).canTradeItem(m_eOwner,
        TradeData(TRADE_TECHNOLOGIES, eLoopTech), false)

then adding:

    GET_TEAM(m_eOwner).AI_techTradeVal(
        eLoopTech, TEAMID(eRival), true)

Despite the PlayerTypes cache key, this CURRENT-TECH quantity is team-owned for
the purpose being measured.

WHY TEAMMATES RECEIVE THE SAME TECH SCORE

The technology branch of CvPlayer::canTradeItem uses the source player's TEAM:

    kOurTeam.isHasTech(eTech)
    !kOurTeam.isNoTradeTech(eTech)

and the fixed recipient team's ownership/research legality. updateVassalScore
passes bTestDenial=false, so player-specific AI/human trade willingness is not
consulted. canPossiblyTradeItem(TRADE_TECHNOLOGIES) is likewise team/game-option
state.

Therefore, for two living players B and C on the same prospective vassal team,
and a fixed master player A:

    vassalTechScore(B) == vassalTechScore(C)

for the existing-tech component, because B and C expose the same team technology
inventory and the same source TeamTypes to AI_techTradeVal.

The actual trade confirms the unit of ownership. CvDeal executes a technology
item with:

    GET_TEAM(eToPlayer).setHasTech(...)

so the recipient TEAM acquires the technology. Once A's team receives Tech X
from member B, member C cannot independently provide a second copy of Tech X.

CONFIRMED CONSUMER A -- acceptVassal SUMS THE DUPLICATE PLAYER CACHES

UWAI::Team::acceptVassal explicitly iterates every member of eVassal:

    for (MemberIter itVassalMember(eVassal); itVassalMember.hasNext(); ++itVassalMember)
    {
        iResourceScore += leaderCache().vassalResourceScore(
                itVassalMember->getID());
        iTechScore += leaderCache().vassalTechScore(
                itVassalMember->getID());
    }

The resulting iTechScore is converted to utility as one of the benefits of
accepting that VASSAL TEAM.

If team B+C owns one tradable technology worth 1000 trade value to A:

    one-member team B:      tech score = 1000
    two-member team B+C:    B cache 1000 + C cache 1000 = 2000

Nothing about the technology inventory changed. Only the number of players
sharing that inventory changed.

The later rVassalUtility.decreaseTo(25) can mask sufficiently large totals, but
it does not repair the defect: below the cap, or when combined with other
benefits/costs near the acceptance threshold, team membership changes the
valuation of the same set of technologies.

CONFIRMED CONSUMER B -- GreedForVassals REUSES THE SAME CURRENT-TECH COMPONENT
ON EACH MEMBER PASS

GreedForVassals::evaluate is called through the ordinary per-rival aspect loop.
For each member of a newly capitulating target team it reads:

    scaled const rTechScore = ourCache().vassalTechScore(eThey);

and adds that score to the member's future research-income estimate before the
per-pass tech-trade cap/reduction. Thus the same already-owned team technologies
can also be credited once on B's pass and again on C's pass. The future research
income itself is player-local and may legitimately be additive; F129 concerns
the duplicated CURRENT technology inventory component.

RESOURCE SCORE IS A USEFUL NEGATIVE CONTROL

The neighboring vassalResourceScore is also cached per player, but its core
availability check uses:

    GET_PLAYER(eRival).getNumAvailableBonuses(eLoopBonus)

Resources are actually owned/connected per player. B and C can therefore bring
different tribute resources to the same team, so summing their resource scores
can be meaningful. That contrast reinforces that the technology score is stored
at the wrong ownership granularity rather than proving that every per-member
vassal quantity should become team-wide.

ANCESTRY

The original AdvCiv WarAndPeaceCache implementation already used a per-player
vassalTechScores[civId] cache and acceptVassal already summed the score once per
vassal member. Later EnumMap/refactor commits preserved the ownership model.
Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain the same updateVassalScore,
GreedForVassals and acceptVassal behavior. This is inherited, not SAS-created.

REPAIR DIRECTION

Compute/cache the already-owned tradable technology value once per prospective
vassal TEAM (or deduplicate techs across member caches before summing). Keep
player-local future research income and player-owned resource availability
separate.

For acceptVassal, do not sum identical current-tech inventories across MemberIter.
For GreedForVassals, ensure the team-owned existing-tech benefit is charged once
per newly acquired vassal team while preserving player-local commerce/research
contributions as intended.

C014-WIP18 APPEND -- WarUtilityAspect.cpp / Risk team-owned vassal-state costs
===============================================================================

F130 / provisional KI#453 -- RISK COUNTS TEAM-OWNED VASSAL/CAPITULATION COSTS
ONCE PER AGENT/RIVAL MEMBER PASS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv team-duplication defect; two independent manifestations.

ROOT

Risk mixes ordinary player-local loss accounting with costs whose ownership and
state are explicitly TEAM-level. WarEvaluator, however, reuses the Risk aspect
while evaluating every living agent-team member, and WarUtilityAspect then calls
Risk::evaluate once for every relevant rival player. The team-owned pieces have
no normalization/canonical-member guard.

MANIFESTATION A -- ONE TEAM CAPITULATION GETS A FIXED 100 COST PER PLAYER PAIR

Risk::evaluate tests:

    militAnalyst().getCapitulationsAccepted(eTheirTeam).count(eOurTeam) > 0

This is one predicted capitulation of the AGENT TEAM to the RIVAL TEAM. The
condition is identical for every member pair A_i / B_j belonging to those two
teams.

When true, Risk halves that pair's ordinary loss estimate and then adds:

    int const iCostForCapitulation = 100;
    rUtility += iCostForCapitulation;

The source comment describes the value as an extra cost "because of
capitulation"; there is no player-pair memory or asset quantity behind the fixed
100.

DETERMINISTIC 2-v-2 REPRODUCTION

Let agent team A contain A1+A2 and rival team B contain B1+B2, with the military
analysis predicting that A capitulates to B. Assuming the capitulation-result
lookup is available (including after F119/KI#442's team-slot repair):

    A1 / B1 pass: +100
    A1 / B2 pass: +100
    A2 / B1 pass: +100
    A2 / B2 pass: +100

The same team capitulation therefore contributes +400 Risk cost before the
pair-local lost-asset pieces are considered. A one-player-vs-one-player mapping
contributes +100 for the same team-state event.

This is not repaired by the preceding `rUtility /= 2`: that division applies to
each pair's ordinary loss estimate before the fixed 100 is added.

F119 INTERACTION

F119/KI#442 established that MilitaryAnalyst currently writes the team-indexed
capitulation result through a raw PlayerTypes slot. That can hide, swap or lose
the predicted capitulation in some team-ID mappings. F130 is a separate consumer
bug: whenever the team result is visible under the requested slot -- and
certainly after F119 is repaired -- Risk multiplies one team capitulation by the
number of member pairs. Do not treat the F119 storage repair as fixing F130.

MANIFESTATION B -- PRE-EVALUATION RECOUNTS OUR TEAM'S SAME VASSAL LOSSES FOR EACH
AGENT MEMBER

Risk::preEvaluate has an explicit non-rival block:

    // Handle potential losses of our vassals here
    for (PlayerIter<ALIVE,VASSAL_OF> itVassal(eOurTeam); ...)

It computes the projected loss of each vassal of eOurTeam, including a material
loss cost up to 33 and a possible break-away cost, and returns the negative sum.

`preEvaluate()` is invoked by WarUtilityAspect::evaluate(MilitaryAnalyst const&)
for every agent player. WarEvaluator constructs the aspect set once, then calls:

    evaluate(itMember->getID(), apAspects)

for every living member of the agent team. There is no one-shot guard around the
vassal-loss block and no division by the agent team's participant count.

Thus even the simplest fixed material part duplicates:

    one agent member + same vassal loses 100% assets -> about 33 cost
    two agent members + same team-owned vassal loss -> about 33 + 33

Only the roster of the master team changed; the same vassal and same projected
vassal losses are being valued repeatedly.

The break-away subcomponent is additionally player-partition-sensitive because
its denominator uses eWe's player-local army cache/gained power, even though
breaking free is a vassal-vs-master TEAM relation. F130 does not need that harder
modeling question: the identical material-loss component already proves the
member duplication.

ANCESTRY / HISTORY CONTROL

AdvCiv history shows that the vassal-loss code was deliberately moved from the
ordinary per-rival Risk::evaluate path into Risk::preEvaluate (practical 1291,
"Toward v0.92") so it could be handled outside the current `they` rival. The
move introduced/retained the global vassal loop but did not add agent-team
normalization.

The fixed 100 capitulation cost also exists in the original AdvCiv UWAI lineage.
Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains both behaviors. Current SAS adds a one-shot team-level
faraway-target gate near the beginning of Risk::preEvaluate (KI#425), but the
inherited vassal-cost block below it remains unguarded; F130 is not SAS-created.

INTERNAL CONTROL

GreedForCash explicitly uses `normalizeUtility(4)` with the comment "Only one
team member will pay" when a fixed team-level payment is evaluated through the
same player/member architecture. Risk's fixed team capitulation cost has the
same ownership problem but no corresponding normalization.

REPAIR DIRECTION

Keep player-local lost-city/blockade/nuke Risk costs attributable to the relevant
player pair, but charge team-owned state changes once at team scope.

- The fixed capitulation penalty should be applied once for the predicted
  eOurTeam -> eTheirTeam capitulation, or shared through a team/member
  normalization that yields the same aggregate regardless of roster partition.
- Vassal material-loss/break-away pre-evaluation should likewise be computed once
  per master team (or normalized across agent members). For break-away danger,
  review whether master-side power should be combined team power rather than the
  current eWe player denominator.

Do not simply divide all of Risk by team sizes; ordinary asset and military
losses are player-owned and are intentionally accumulated across players.

C014-WIP19 APPEND -- WarUtilityAspect.cpp physical city-site identity audit
===============================================================================

F131 / provisional KI#454 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED ADVCIV DUPLICATE-PLOT VALUE
GREEDFORSPACE CAN COUNT ONE PHYSICAL CITY SITE ONCE PER ELIMINATED TEAMMATE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv player-cache/team-aggregation defect.

ROOT

GreedForSpace values settlement opportunities that become available when a rival
player is eliminated. City-site recommendations are cached separately by
CvPlayerAI, but the object being valued is a physical map plot. Two teammates can
therefore recommend the same plot independently, while one physical plot can
ultimately host only one city.

Current GreedForSpace::evaluate nevertheless runs once per rival player and
counts each eliminated player's cached site list independently. There is no
cross-member plot-identity deduplication.

SOURCE CONTRACT -- CITY-SITE LISTS ARE PLAYER-LOCAL

CvPlayerAI::AI_updateCitySites scans every map plot and accepts a candidate when:

    iValue > iMinFoundValueThreshold && !AI_isPlotCitySite(kPlot)

AI_isPlotCitySite checks only this CvPlayerAI instance's m_aeAICitySites vector:

    std::find(m_aeAICitySites.begin(), m_aeAICitySites.end(),
              kPlot.plotNum())

The selected plot is then pushed only into that player's vector. Found values are
also stored/evaluated for getID(). There is no teammate-site reservation or
team-wide duplicate check in this pipeline.

Thus, in a supported team game, B1 and B2 can both have the same physical plot P
in their city-site lists. Shared team visibility can make this especially
natural; different player found-value rankings are not required for overlap.

GREEDFORSPACE CONSUMER

For the current rival eThey, GreedForSpace first requires:

    militAnalyst().isEliminated(eThey)

It then loops that player's recommendations and increments iTheirSites for each
visible/relevantly-visible site. The resulting count feeds:

    rExpectedSites = iOurSites + 0.63 * iTheirSites

and ultimately positive utility for the expansion space supposedly released by
eliminating that player.

WarUtilityAspect evaluates the same GreedForSpace object separately for every
relevant rival player. Therefore, if B1 and B2 are members of the same target
team, both are eliminated by the scenario, and both cached plot P as a city site:

    B1 pass: P contributes one orphaned site
    B2 pass: P contributes one orphaned site

The aggregate evaluation has valued two future settlement opportunities even
though P can be settled only once.

This is a physical-identity double count, not merely a debate over how much a
multi-member team should be worth. Reassigning the same plot recommendation from
one target-team member to two members can increase war utility without creating
any additional settleable land.

AUTO-RAZE / DISTINCT-SITE CONTROL

GreedForSpace also adds auto-razed cities conquered from the current rival to
its site count. Those city plots are owner-specific physical losses and should
remain additive when distinct. Likewise, genuinely different recommended plots
held by B1 and B2 represent different expansion opportunities.

The repair therefore should NOT simply divide all GreedForSpace utility by team
size. The duplicated object is the plot ID itself.

ANCESTRY / HISTORY CONTROL

Current SAS and Base AdvCiv 1.14 have normalized-identical implementations of
both GreedForSpace::evaluate and CvPlayerAI::AI_updateCitySites for this behavior.
The defect is inherited.

Practical 2949 ("Some minor tweaks to UWAI war evaluation") is a useful local
historical control. In one adjacent patch it expanded GreedForSpace's site scan
to respect visibility; immediately below, it changed GreedForCash from a raw
fixed +4 to:

    normalizeUtility(4) // Only one team member will pay

Thus the lineage was already correcting a team-duplication problem in the same
small aspect neighborhood, but GreedForSpace's player-local site lists remained
aggregated without physical-plot deduplication.

ADVERSARIAL NON-FINDING CONTROL -- OPEN BORDERS

The preceding sweep also challenged Assistance/IllWill's fixed Open Borders
partner value. That does not presently meet the F131 standard. The original UWAI
implementation treats the OB term as part of the value of a particular partner,
alongside that player's trade/technology/military utility; access to two
teammates' separate territories can plausibly carry more strategic value than
access to one. A team-to-team treaty alone is therefore insufficient evidence of
double counting. No finding is promoted for that family here.

REPAIR DIRECTION

When valuing space released by elimination of multiple members of one rival team,
collect the relevant recommended site plot IDs at the team/scenario level and
count their UNION. Preserve distinct sites and distinct auto-razed city plots.

A localized alternative is a per-evaluation set of already-counted plotNums that
persists across rival-member passes for the same target team, with careful reset
between independent WarEvaluator scenarios. Do not normalize by raw member count.

C014-WIP20 APPEND -- Revolts cross-rival accumulator/denominator audit
===============================================================================

F132 / provisional KI#455 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED ADVCIV ORDER-DEPENDENT RATIO
REVOLTS PERSISTS THE "COUNTED CITY" SET BUT RESETS ITS NUMERATOR/DENOMINATOR
ON EVERY RIVAL PASS, MAKING UTILITY DEPEND ON WHICH PLAYER CLAIMS A CITY FIRST
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv state-partition / player-iteration-order defect,
independent of F118/KI#441's negative-asset sign inversion.

ROOT

Revolts is evaluated once per relevant rival player. A member field:

    std::set<PlotNumTypes> m_countedCities;

persists across those rival calls, and the source explicitly says:

    // Count each city only once

However, the quantities used to turn those city risks into utility are LOCAL to
each individual Revolts::evaluate call:

    scaled rLossesFromRevolts;
    int iTotalAssets = 0;

For every newly encountered city, the current call adds its asset score to
`iTotalAssets` and its expected revolt loss to `rLossesFromRevolts`. At the end
of that one rival pass it charges:

    rRevoltCost = (1 + amortizationMultiplier) *
                  50 * rLossesFromRevolts / iTotalAssets;

The next rival pass preserves which cities have already been claimed through
m_countedCities, but resets both numerator and denominator to zero. The final
aspect therefore sums NORMALIZED RATIOS OF ARBITRARY FIRST-CLAIM SUBSETS rather
than normalizing the union of cities that the persistent set was designed to
count once.

WHY m_countedCities IS CROSS-RIVAL STATE

Within one rival pass, the code loops map areas and then our cities in each area.
A city belongs to only one CvArea, so the member set is not needed merely to stop
the same city recurring in that local area traversal. It matters when different
rivals regard the same area as primary and Revolts::evaluate is called again.

WarUtilityAspect keeps the same Revolts object through its rival-player loop;
resetRival() does not clear m_countedCities. The object itself is fresh for the
next independent WarEvaluator scenario, which is why the earlier lifetime audit
correctly rejected a cross-scenario leak. F132 concerns the intended intra-
scenario persistence combined with per-call reset of the ratio accumulators.

DETERMINISTIC PLAYER-ITERATION-ORDER REPRODUCTION

Let our threatened cities X and Y each have asset score 100, revolt probability
at or above the 10% cap, and no hopeless-revolt exclusion. Their individual loss
multipliers are therefore both 0.5.

Let two simultaneous war enemies B and C satisfy the ordinary Revolts gates such
that:

    B has a primary area containing X but not Y
    C has primary areas containing both X and Y

Both players and all military/game state can be held fixed. Only their numeric
player iteration order changes.

CASE 1 -- B is visited first

B pass:
    newly counted: X
    numerator = 50, denominator = 100 -> ratio 0.5

C pass:
    X is skipped by m_countedCities; newly counted: Y
    numerator = 50, denominator = 100 -> ratio 0.5

Aggregate normalized ratio contribution: 1.0 (before common multiplier).

CASE 2 -- C is visited first

C pass:
    newly counted: X + Y
    numerator = 100, denominator = 200 -> ratio 0.5

B pass:
    X already counted; no newly counted assets -> returns

Aggregate normalized ratio contribution: 0.5.

The same cities, same revolt probabilities, same enemies, same wars and same
primary-area relationships therefore produce roughly DOUBLE the Revolts cost
solely from PlayerTypes iteration order / which rival gets first claim on X.
That cannot be defended as a multi-front modeling choice.

F118 SEPARATION

F118/KI#441 established that negative per-city asset scores can make revolt loss
negative and hence create positive war utility. F132 remains even when every
asset score is strictly positive, as in the 100/100 reproduction above. A repair
for one does not repair the other.

ANCESTRY

The original AdvCiv UWAI introduction already contains the same structural
combination:

    double revoltLoss = 0;
    int totalAssets = 0;
    ...
    if (countedCities.count(c->plotNum()) > 0) continue;
    countedCities.insert(c->plotNum());
    ...
    uMinus = ... * revoltLoss / totalAssets;

and declares `countedCities` as a Revolts member set. Later refactors merely
converted the arithmetic to scaled/fixed-point and renamed the member.
Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain the same behavior. F132 is inherited,
not SAS-created.

REPAIR DIRECTION

The normalization domain must match the uniqueness domain.

Preferred: evaluate the union of all relevant threatened own-city plot IDs once
per agent member/scenario, accumulate one nonnegative expected-loss numerator
and one corresponding asset denominator, then apply the Revolts formula once.
This can naturally be combined with the F118 repair.

If keeping per-rival callbacks, persistent cumulative numerator/denominator
state must be used in a way that changes the aspect by only the delta of the
single global ratio; simply retaining m_countedCities while restarting local
ratios is not sufficient.

Do not remove m_countedCities without replacement: that would reintroduce the
more obvious duplicate-city count when several enemies share a primary area.

C014-WIP21 APPEND -- WarUtilityAspect.cpp victory-domain broadening + advc.035 ratio audit
===============================================================================

F127 / provisional KI#450 -- AUTHORITATIVE BROADENING -- CONQUEST TOO
PLAYER ELIMINATION IS TREATED AS 100% CONQUEST PROGRESS EVEN WHEN THEIR TEAM
STILL BLOCKS THE ACTUAL TEAM-LEVEL CONQUEST VICTORY
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WIP16 established F127 from Domination and Diplomacy: global/team victory
completion caps are restarted inside each rival-player pass, so the same
remaining global threshold can be independently completed more than once.
The subsequent victory-boundary audit proves that Conquest belongs under the
same root too, for an even more direct ownership-domain mismatch.

ACTUAL VICTORY CONTRACT

CvGame::testVictory evaluates Conquest for TeamTypes eTeam. After requiring the
candidate team to own a city, it iterates every other ALIVE non-same team and
rejects victory while any non-vassal OTHER TEAM still owns at least one city:

    if (kVictory.isConquest())
    {
        if (kTeam.getNumCities() <= 0)
            return false;
        for (TeamIter<CIV_ALIVE,NOT_SAME_TEAM_AS> itOther(eTeam);
            itOther.hasNext(); ++itOther)
        {
            if (!itOther->isVassal(eTeam) && itOther->getNumCities() > 0)
                return false;
        }
    }

The blocker is therefore the opposing TEAM, not each member player separately.
Eliminating one member of a multi-member free team does not remove that team's
Conquest obstruction while another member still has cities.

MILITARYVICTORY MODEL

MilitaryVictory::progressRatingConquest() instead begins:

    if (militAnalyst().isEliminated(eThey) ||
        militAnalyst().getCapitulationsAccepted(eOurTeam).count(eTheirTeam))
    {
        log("They're conquered entirely");
        return 1;
    }

`eThey` / `isEliminated(PlayerTypes)` is player-local. Thus for target team B+C:

* military simulation predicts all B cities lost;
* C remains alive, free, and owns cities;
* actual CvGame::testVictory still sees team B+C as a Conquest blocker;
* B's MilitaryVictory pass nevertheless logs "They're conquered entirely" and
  returns the maximum 1.0 Conquest progress;
* C is then evaluated in its own player pass as well.

This is not merely a different heuristic scale: a state labeled 100% Conquest
progress by the aspect is explicitly insufficient for the engine's Conquest
victory condition.

`countFreeRivals<false>()` also iterates PlayerTypes rather than blocking teams,
which reinforces the player-domain approximation in the partial-progress path.
Distinct member losses can of course be genuinely incremental, so this does NOT
prove that all partial Conquest asset loss should simply be deduplicated. The
hard defect is that the full-completion condition and its surrounding progress
normalization do not respect the team-level victory blocker.

ANCESTRY

The original local UWAI introduction already contains:

    if(m->isEliminated(theyId) ||
       m->getCapitulationsAccepted(agentId).count(TEAMID(theyId))) {
        log("They're conquered entirely");
        return 1;
    }

so player elimination -> full Conquest progress existed from birth. Base
AdvCiv 1.14's current `progressRatingConquest` is textually identical to current
SAS for this behavior. Later numeric/scaled refactors did not repair the domain.

F127 NORMALIZED ROOT AFTER BROADENING

MilitaryVictory measures shared global/team victory progress through independent
rival-player passes and applies nonlinear completion/caps before those passes are
combined. Proven manifestations now are:

1. Domination: the same global remaining population/land threshold can be
   independently saturated on multiple rival-player passes;
2. Diplomacy: the same global remaining vote threshold can be independently
   saturated on multiple rival-player passes;
3. Conquest: eliminating one member is treated as full 1.0 progress although
   the member's still-free team can continue to block the actual victory.

Repair should move completion/saturation to the same team/global domain as the
victory condition, while preserving genuinely additive marginal gains from
separate players. Do not mechanically divide every player-local loss by team
size.


F133 / provisional KI#456 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED SUPPORTED-CONFIG RATIO DEFECT
EXCLUSIVE-RADIUS FLIPPED-TILE LOSS IS ADDED TO LOSS NUMERATOR AFTER THE TOTAL
ASSET DENOMINATOR IS FROZEN; LOSS RATIOS CAN EXCEED 100%
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: NEW CURRENT SUPPORTED-CONFIGURATION DEFECT. Shipped/default SAS sets
`OWN_EXCLUSIVE_RADIUS=0`, so defaults mask it; the option is nevertheless an
explicit maintained AdvCiv configuration, documented in GlobalDefines_advc.xml:

    [advc.035] If set to 1, tiles that are only within the radius of one city
    belong to the owner of that city regardless of culture. Recommended: 0 ...

The audit therefore treats value 1 as a supported non-default configuration,
not as an invented unsupported retuning.

ROOT ORDERING DEFECT

WarUtilityAspect::netLostRivalAssetScore accumulates city/nuke loss into
`rNetLoss` and city assets into `rTotal`. It then deliberately raises total to
cover non-city nuke loss:

    rNetLoss += lossesFromNukes(eThey, eTo);
    rTotal.increaseTo(rNetLoss);

After that point it computes blockade loss from `(rTotal - rNetLoss)`, adds the
blockade component, and only THEN adds advc.035 flipped-tile loss:

    rNetLoss += rFromBlockade;
    rNetLoss += lossesFromFlippedTiles(eThey, eTo); // advc.035
    if (prTotalScore != NULL)
        *prTotalScore = rTotal;

Thus flipped-tile loss contributes to the numerator returned to every caller,
but never to the `prTotalScore` denominator returned alongside it.

The mismatch is not bounded elsewhere. UWAICache::updateLostTilesAtWar counts
all contested plots that the owner team would lose under OWN_EXCLUSIVE_RADIUS;
it stores that integer with no upper cap. lossesFromFlippedTiles then uses:

    if (abs(iVictimLostTiles) <= 4 * iRivalMembers)
        return 0;
    r = scaled(125 * iVictimLostTiles,
               max(5, GET_PLAYER(eVictim).getTotalLand()));
    r /= iRivalMembers;

For a solo rival, just five qualifying lost tiles clear the threshold. On a
small empire the flipped-tile score can therefore be of order 125 while the
asset denominator is independently based on visible/deduced city asset scores.
There is no invariant requiring that city-based denominator to be >= the later
flipped-tile score.

EXPLICIT INTERNAL INVARIANT FAILURE -- Assistance

Assistance::assistanceRatio() is the clearest consumer:

    scaled rTheirAssets;
    scaled rTheirLostAssets = netLostRivalAssetScore(NO_PLAYER, &rTheirAssets);
    if (rTheirAssets <= 0)
        return 0;
    scaled r(rTheirLostAssets / rTheirAssets);
    r.increaseTo(0);
    FAssert(r <= 1);

The source explicitly asserts that this loss ratio cannot exceed 100%. With
advc.035 enabled, numerator-only flipped-tile loss invalidates that assertion.
In non-assert builds the value can continue above 1, so Assistance can value a
non-eliminated partner as losing more than 100% of the denominator used to
measure its assets. If capitulation is also predicted, the subsequent

    r += 0.5 * (1 - r)

operates on an already out-of-domain ratio rather than repairing the root.

OTHER CONSUMERS / CONSEQUENCE SCOPE

This shared helper/denominator mismatch is not Assistance-only:

* Loathing::lossRating uses `rTheirLostAssets / rTheirAssets` as one of its
  relative-loss terms; flipped tiles can inflate it beyond the asset-total
  domain that `rTheirAssets` purports to normalize.
* MilitaryVictory::progressRatingConquest uses the same pair; it later caps its
  partial ratio to 1, masking the overflow numerically but still saturating
  Conquest progress from a numerator that the denominator never included.
* IllWill's punishment ratio likewise uses the returned loss/assets pair,
  although its final utility is capped separately.
* ThirdParty/Risk-related helper consumers that ask for a total score inherit
  the same numerator/denominator inconsistency whenever this advc.035 component
  is included.

One root should repair the shared helper rather than patching the Assistance
assert alone.

ANCESTRY

The local advc.035 introducing diff added exactly:

    r += lossesFromFlippedTiles(theyId, to);
    if(returnTotal != NULL)
        *returnTotal = total;

with the flipped-tile addition inserted after `total` had already been fixed.
The helper introduced in that same commit already used the 125 * lostTiles /
landTiles weighting and per-rival-team-member split. Thus the domain mismatch
was introduced with advc.035 itself, not by SAS.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains the same ordering and Assistance assertion. Current SAS
also retains it; only formatting/modern accessor details differ in the helper.

REPAIR DIRECTION

If flipped-tile loss is to be represented in the same "fraction of total
assets lost" ratios, the denominator must be extended consistently with that
asset component before it is returned, or the tile effect must be modeled as a
separate bounded dimension rather than silently appended to only the numerator.
Whichever model is chosen, restore the explicit Assistance invariant that a
non-elimination loss ratio lies in [0,1].

Do not merely clamp Assistance to 1: that hides the assertion but leaves
Loathing, Conquest partial progress and other shared-helper consumers with the
same mismatched measurement domains.

C014-WIP22 APPEND -- WarUtilityAspect.cpp IllWill team-war capability audit
===============================================================================

F134 / provisional KI#457 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED PLAYER/TEAM POWER-DOMAIN DEFECT
ILLWILL PRICES TEAM-WIDE REVENGE/DOGPILE MILITARY RISK THROUGH ONE PLAYER'S
ARMY POWER, SO NONLINEAR THRESHOLDS DEPEND ON HOW A TEAM'S POWER IS PARTITIONED
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: NEW CURRENT INHERITED DEFECT ROOT. The diplomatic motive represented by
IllWill can legitimately differ by player, but the military capability used to
cross its revenge/dogpile danger thresholds does not match the team-wide war
that those motives can trigger.

PLAYER-LOCAL POWER HELPER

IllWill::theirToOurPowerRatio() computes:

    scaled rOurPow = ourCache().getPowerValues()[ARMY]->power() +
            militAnalyst().gainedPower(eWe, ARMY);
    ...
    scaled rTheirPow = kThey.uwai().getCache().getPowerValues()[ARMY]->power() +
            militAnalyst().gainedPower(eThey, ARMY);
    ...
    return rTheirPow / scaled::max(10, rOurPow);

Both sides are therefore one PlayerTypes member at a time. The nearby comment
only says not to include vassals; it does not say that ordinary teammates should
be excluded from the military side.

The helper is then fed into NONLINEAR gates in evalRevenge:

    if (rTheirToOurPow > 1.45 && ...team war-success tests...)
        ... hopeless-stalemate cost ...

and, for prospective revenge after our simulated DoW:

    if (rTheirToOurPow > 0.7)
        rRevengeCost += 4;

    scaled rPowRatioMult = rTheirToOurPow - 1;
    rPowRatioMult.clamp(0, 1);
    rRevengeCost += rPowRatioMult * 28 * rAttitudeMult;

Because these thresholds/clamps are applied BEFORE separate rival-player
contributions are combined, evaluating members independently is not equivalent
to evaluating the military side that would actually fight the war.

DETERMINISTIC TEAM-PARTITION REPRODUCTION

Take an agent side with 100 relevant ARMY power and a prospective enemy TEAM
with two ordinary teammates B and C, each with 60 ARMY power after the military
analysis. Ignore human-confidence modifiers and give both the same ordinary
attitude for the control.

Current IllWill evaluates B and C separately:

    B : 60 / 100 = 0.60 -> below 0.70 -> no fixed revenge-danger cost
    C : 60 / 100 = 0.60 -> below 0.70 -> no fixed revenge-danger cost

The power-ratio multiplier is also clamped from (0.60 - 1) to zero on both
passes. Thus the military-capability part of prospective revenge contributes
zero.

Now place the exact same 120 enemy ARMY power in one member D of an otherwise
equivalent enemy team:

    D : 120 / 100 = 1.20 -> passes 0.70, adds the fixed 4,
                             and has a positive (1.20 - 1) multiplier.

The same team-side military capacity therefore changes IllWill solely because
it is split among teammates. Summing two player-local results cannot repair a
threshold that has already zeroed both members.

The ongoing-war 1.45 branch has the same mismatch and an especially clear
mixed-domain structure: the surrounding war-success conditions are explicitly
team-on-team (`kTheirTeam.AI_getWarSuccess(eOurTeam)`,
`kOurTeam.AI_getWarSuccess(eTheirTeam)`, and
`kTheirTeam.AI_getWarSuccessRating()`), while the decisive "they're far more
powerful than we are" gate is still the current rival player's army divided by
the current agent player's army.

TEAM-WAR CONTRACT / INTERNAL CONTROL

This is not merely a preference for different UWAI granularity.
CvTeam::declareWar accepts TeamTypes eTarget, gathers MemberIter populations
from BOTH teams and then executes:

    setAtWar(eTarget, true);
    kTarget.setAtWar(getID(), true);

A revenge war initiated by any one member therefore commits the member's
ordinary teammates and their military capacity too.

The inherited non-UWAI war/peace logic uses that same domain. For example,
CvTeamAI::AI_endWarVal compares:

    getPower(true)

against the opposing team's defensive power. CvTeamAI::AI_doWar likewise
computes `iOurPower = getPower(true)` and tests target-team defensive power when
selecting wars. CvTeamAI::AI_getAttitude(TeamTypes) separately averages the
member-to-member diplomatic values. Those functions provide a useful design
control: diplomatic motivation can be assembled from player attitudes while
military capability is team power.

IllWill currently preserves the player-specific motive (`towardUs()`, human
status, trade/partner consequences) but also narrows the capability signal to
that same player. It is the latter transition that creates the partition bug.

SECOND CONSUMER -- ANGERED PARTNERS

IllWill::evalAngeredPartners() reuses theirToOurPowerRatio() in the part that
models exposure to a dogpile after worsening a partner's attitude:

    ... + (bWillDisplease ? min(14.5, 9 * SQR(rTheirToOurPow)) : 0);

The relationship penalty itself is appropriately player-specific, but the
extra danger term is again the military ability of a TEAM-WIDE war response
measured through one member's army. The square makes this nonlinear too, so
member-by-member summation is not invariant under redistributing the same team
power. This is a second manifestation of the same helper-domain root, not F135.

ANCESTRY

The original local UWAI introduction already implemented evalRevenge with
player-local `ourCache` / `theirCache` ARMY power plus player-local gainedPower,
then applied the 0.7 revenge threshold. Later AdvCiv added the ongoing-war
hopeless-stalemate branch but reused the same player-local power ratio alongside
team war-success state.

Current SAS and Base AdvCiv 1.14 have byte-for-byte identical implementations
of all three relevant IllWill members:

* IllWill::evalRevenge
* IllWill::theirToOurPowerRatio
* IllWill::evalAngeredPartners

This is therefore inherited AdvCiv behavior, not a SAS regression.

REPAIR DIRECTION

Keep player-specific relationship/motivation inputs where they belong, but
compute the military-capability ratio over the alive ordinary members of the
relevant teams before applying the 0.70 / 1.45 thresholds and nonlinear squared
or clamped power terms. The existing comment intentionally excludes vassals;
that policy can remain unless separately redesigned.

Human-confidence adjustment needs care in mixed human/AI teams: aggregate the
physical/military side first and apply confidence consistently to the relevant
human-controlled component or team policy rather than accidentally multiplying
the entire mixed team because the current rival member happens to be human.

Do not merely normalize the finished per-player utility by member counts. Once
a nonlinear gate has independently converted two 0.60 members to zero, a later
divisor cannot reconstruct the 1.20 team-side threat.

C014-WIP23 APPEND -- ThirdParty decisive-target scope + cache contract controls
===============================================================================

F135 / provisional KI#458 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED ADVCIV TARGET-SCOPE DEFECT
THIRDPARTY "WINNING DECISIVELY" SHORTCUT CAN FIRE WHILE TARGET TEAM SURVIVES
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: NEW CURRENT INHERITED DEFECT ROOT. Static evidence strong. Independent
of F124/KI#447's later intervention-severity power gate and of F119/KI#442's
raw player/team vector-index bug.

ROOT CONTRACT

ThirdPartyIntervention::evaluate() contains an early-return shortcut documented
as:

    /*  When already at war and winning decisively, try to wrap it up
        before worrying about 3rd parties. */

The shortcut is enabled while the WarEvaluator is considering peace with its
specific TeamTypes target eTarget:

    (m_kParams.isConsideringPeace() && eTarget != NO_TEAM &&
    (militAnalyst().isEliminated(GET_TEAM(eTarget).getLeaderID()) ||
     !militAnalyst().getCapitulationsAccepted(eOurTeam).empty()))

Both predicates are only PROXIES for the stated condition. Neither actually
establishes that the evaluated target team has been decisively defeated.

MANIFESTATION A -- HYPOTHETICAL ELIMINATION OF THE CURRENT REAL TEAM LEADER

CvTeam::getLeaderID() simply returns the team's stored m_eLeader. The real game
updates that member through CvTeam::updateLeaderID when actual player state
changes. MilitaryAnalyst/InvasionGraph, however, is a hypothetical simulation;
it does not kill real CvPlayers and does not mutate CvTeam::m_eLeader.

MilitaryAnalyst::isEliminated accepts a PlayerTypes and tests exactly that
player's simulated city losses:

    InvasionGraph::Node const* pNode = m_pInvGraph->getNode(ePlayer);
    ...
    return (((int)lost.size()) == GET_PLAYER(ePlayer).getNumCities());

Therefore, for a current target team T={B,C} whose stored real leader is B, the
simulation can predict:

    B : all cities lost -> isEliminated(B) == true
    C : cities remain   -> target team T still survives and fights

while:

    GET_TEAM(T).getLeaderID() == B

still holds because the simulation never runs CvTeam::updateLeaderID on the
real team. The shortcut returns immediately and ThirdPartyIntervention assigns
zero intervention cost even though the target TEAM has not been wrapped up.

This is not merely a stale-leader corner case. Permanent/multi-member teams are
represented player-by-player in InvasionGraph and MilitaryAnalyst; individual
members can be eliminated independently. F127's independently proven Conquest
mismatch already provides another control that one player's elimination does
not mean the whole non-vassal team has ceased to block team-level state.

Moreover, InvasionGraph's capitulation test itself requires the defending real
team to have at most one currently alive member (`kDefTeam.getAliveCount() <=
1`). Thus a two-alive-member target team can reach precisely the state above --
one member predicted eliminated while another survives -- without target-team
capitulation rescuing the intended shortcut premise.

MANIFESTATION B -- ANY CAPITULATION TO OUR TEAM, NOT THE TARGET'S CAPITULATION

The second predicate is broader still:

    !militAnalyst().getCapitulationsAccepted(eOurTeam).empty()

The result is a TeamSet of every simulated team whose capitulation was accepted
by eOurTeam. It is not filtered by eTarget.

MilitaryAnalyst explicitly includes wars other than the evaluated target war.
Its constructor gathers every player currently at war into `currentlyAtWar`,
constructs the InvasionGraph from those wars, and, in the WAR scenario of a
peace evaluation, continues the existing wars. In the recursive PEACE scenario
it removes the evaluated target side while unrelated current wars remain.

Consequently a concrete solo-agent control is sufficient and avoids any
interaction with F119's multi-member result-storage defect:

    A is currently at war with target team T and unrelated enemy team U.
    WarEvaluator is considering peace with T.
    MilitaryAnalyst predicts U capitulating to A.
    T itself remains undefeated / does not capitulate.

Then:

    getCapitulationsAccepted(Ateam) == { U }

is nonempty, so ThirdPartyIntervention returns under the comment that A is
"winning decisively" and should "wrap it [the target war] up." U's unrelated
capitulation does not establish that premise for T.

This manifestation survives a correct F119 repair. F119 changes which TeamTypes
slot the accepted-capitulation set is stored in; F135 is that the correctly
retrieved set is queried with `.empty()` instead of asking whether the relevant
target team is the capitulating team.

HISTORY / ANCESTRY

Reachable AdvCiv history practical 3485 / commit f39e13df87 is titled:

    Add ThirdPartyIntervention war utility aspect

and introduces this exact early-return condition, including both the current
real target leader's PlayerTypes elimination and the unfiltered nonempty
capitulations-accepted set. No later history correction found in the local
reachable diffs changes the scope of this shortcut.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 contains the same block verbatim. Current SAS also retains it
unchanged. This is therefore inherited from the aspect's introduction, not a
SAS regression.

WHY THIS IS ONE ROOT AND NOT TWO

Both manifestations violate the same documented predicate: "the evaluated
TARGET war is already being won decisively." The first substitutes one current
representative player for the target team; the second substitutes any accepted
capitulation for the target team's capitulation. Either can make the shortcut
true while the target remains an active opponent.

The repair should therefore make the shortcut target-scoped rather than patch
its two syntax shapes independently.

REPAIR DIRECTION

For the elimination side, require that the evaluated target team is actually
eliminated in the simulated state -- e.g. all relevant alive target-team member
nodes are eliminated -- rather than asking about the real team's pre-simulation
leader player.

For capitulation, test the evaluated target specifically, e.g. the target's
simulated capitulation state or membership of eTarget in the accepted set,
rather than `.empty()` on all capitulations accepted by eOurTeam.

Keep the existing high-level policy if desired: when the TARGET really is
nearly/fully defeated, suppressing concern about third-party intervention can
still be intentional. F135 is about the predicates failing to prove that
condition.

Do not fold this into F124/KI#447. F124 remains the separate later nonlinear
power-threshold domain mismatch for the prospective third party eThey; fixing
that power calculation does nothing to this early target-war shortcut.

  WarUtilityAspect consumers of MilitaryAnalyst conquest/loss sets; no null
