C014-WIP24 APPEND -- partner-tech ownership + recent-root normalization matrix
===============================================================================

F136 / provisional KI#459 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED TEAM-TECH PARTNER DUPLICATION
PARTNERUTILFROMTECH COUNTS THE SAME TEAM-OWNED FORESEEABLE TECHNOLOGY TRADES
ONCE PER FRIENDLY TEAMMATE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: NEW CURRENT INHERITED DEFECT ROOT. Narrowly scoped to the team-owned
technology opportunity inside the partner helper; does NOT claim that trade,
resource, military, attitude or commerce partner value is generally identical
between teammates.

TEAM-OWNED INPUT INSIDE A PLAYER-PARTNER HELPER

WarUtilityAspect::partnerUtilFromTech() is called with the current rival player
eThey, and appropriately contains some player-specific inputs such as human
status, pairwise attitude and estimated player commerce. But its concrete
near-future technology inventory is read from the two TEAMS:

    bool bWeHaveIt = (kOurTeam.isHasTech(eTech) ||
            kOurTeam.getResearchProgress(eTech) > 0);
    bool bTheyHaveIt = (kTheirTeam.isHasTech(eTech) ||
            (bCanSeeResearch && kTheirTeam.getResearchProgress(eTech) > 0));

    if (bWeHaveIt && !bTheyHaveIt)
        iWeCanOffer++;
    else if (bTheyHaveIt && !bWeHaveIt)
        iTheyCanOffer++;

and then:

    scaled rNearFutureTrades = std::min(iWeCanOffer, iTheyCanOffer);
    ...
    r += fixp(10/3.) * scaled::min(3, rNearFutureTrades);

For ordinary teammates B and C, `kTheirTeam` is the exact same CvTeam. Known
technologies and research progress are team state. With identical visibility /
no hidden-progress complication, the `iWeCanOffer`, `iTheyCanOffer` and
`rNearFutureTrades` sets/counts are therefore the same on B's and C's passes.

REAL TRADE EFFECT IS TEAM-OWNED TOO

CvPlayer::canTradeItem(TRADE_TECHNOLOGIES) checks source and recipient through
team state:

    kOurTeam.isHasTech(eTech)
    !kOurTeam.isNoTradeTech(eTech)
    !kToTeam.isHasTech(eTech)

and CvDeal::startTrade applies a technology trade with:

    GET_TEAM(eToPlayer).setHasTech(..., TECH_ACQUISITION_TRADE);

Thus one actual trade through member B changes the recipient TEAM's technology
ownership. If B and teammate C both currently provide the same technology X,
X is not two independently consumable trade opportunities: after it is traded
through either member, the shared team-tech difference is gone.

The denial implementation reinforces that technology willingness itself has a
team contract. CvPlayer::getTradeDenial routes TRADE_TECHNOLOGIES to:

    kOurTeam.AI_techTrade(eTech, TEAMID(eWhoTo));

and CvTeamAI::AI_techTrade applies team attitude plus member-personality rules.
This does not mean every player-facing approximation inside partnerUtilFromTech
must be discarded; it does make the team ownership of the technology inventory
non-optional.

CONCRETE DUPLICATION THROUGH ILLWILL

A team-wide declaration of war against T={B,C} causes MilitaryAnalyst to mark
war against both living members, and WarUtilityAspect evaluates IllWill once for
B and once for C. In `IllWill::evalLostPartner`, each new-war member contributes:

    partnerUtilFromTrade() +
    (bTheyCapitulated ? 0 : partnerUtilFromTech()) +
    partnerUtilFromMilitary();

Choose B and C as equally friendly AI teammates, both visible, with equal
player-local commerce for the simple control, and suppose the shared T tech
inventory versus our team yields three foreseeable near-future trades.

Then B's `partnerUtilFromTech` receives the bonus for those same three shared
team-tech differences, and C's pass receives it again. The war does end the
technology partnership with T, but it does not destroy two copies of each team
technology or two independent chances to exchange the same three differences.

Even without requiring the helper's commerce-derived base term to be treated
team-wide, the `rNearFutureTrades` component is deterministically duplicated.
That is sufficient for the root.

SECOND CONSUMERS

The same shared helper also feeds:

* Assistance: expected loss of a trading partner is weighted by
  `sqrt(assistanceRatio) * partnerUtilFromTech()`. When multiple members of one
  partner team are damaged, the same team technology inventory can be valued
  repeatedly even though surviving teammates may preserve the team-tech trade
  channel.
* IllWill::evalAngeredPartners: the cost assigned to alienating a prospective
  partner includes `partnerUtilFromTech()` once per current rival player.

These are manifestations of the helper's ownership mismatch, not additional
F-numbers.

NEGATIVE CONTROL -- PARTNERUTILFROMTRADE IS NOT THE SAME ROOT

Do not globalize the entire partner-value family. `partnerUtilFromTrade()`
walks CvDeals between the two actual players, player-owned bonus trades and
trade routes whose partner city owner is exactly eThey. Those quantities can
legitimately differ and add across teammates. F104's resource-item counting bug
is separate.

Likewise, player-specific relationship/willingness and commerce contribution in
partnerUtilFromTech can remain relevant. F136 is specifically that a shared
technology inventory / set of foreseeable tech differences is converted into a
per-player reusable opportunity.

RELATION TO F129 / KI#452

F129 established another team-tech duplication in a DIFFERENT producer and
consumer chain: UWAICache stores prospective-vassal current-tech value in a
PlayerTypes-keyed `m_aiVassalTechScore`, then acceptVassal sums that score over
vassal members.

F136 shares the technology-ownership principle but not the repair locus:

* repairing/rekeying `m_aiVassalTechScore` does not change partnerUtilFromTech;
* repairing partnerUtilFromTech does not change the vassal-score cache or
  acceptVassal member sum.

Under the Album's one-practical-root rule these therefore remain separate roots,
with the shared domain fact recorded as a cross-control rather than merging two
independent implementations.

RELATION TO F103 / KI#426

F103's current SAS repair fixes a concrete old wrong-object bug where the helper
ignored its ePlayer argument and used the AGENT leader's tech-refusal threshold
for the rival too. F136 does not retract that repair: selecting the queried
player's personality is strictly more coherent than substituting our leader.

The full live tech denial is team-level and can be stricter than the helper's
pairwise approximation in permanent teams. That is useful robustness context,
but F136 does not require promoting a second willingness-threshold defect; its
proof uses equally friendly teammates so willingness cannot explain the
inventory duplication.

ANCESTRY

The original local AdvCiv/UWAI introduction of partnerUtilFromTech already
iterated team technology ownership/research progress while exposing the result
through a rival-player partner call. The same near-future-trade construction
survives through Base AdvCiv 1.14.

Current SAS changed `techRefuseThresh` for F103/KI#426 but did not alter the
team-tech inventory counting or add a canonical partner-team allocation. The
F136 root is therefore inherited rather than created by the recent SAS repair.

REPAIR DIRECTION

Separate the helper's genuinely team-owned technology opportunity from its
player-specific relationship/economic modifiers.

A robust design could compute foreseeable shared technology differences once
per partner team, then assign/weight that team opportunity according to whether
there is at least one viable trading contact / the team's actual denial model.
Alternatively, keep player callbacks but maintain a per-team allocation so the
same current/progress tech differences cannot be consumed again by the next
teammate pass.

Do not simply divide the entire partnerUtilFromTech result by team size. Team
members can differ in attitude, human status, commerce contribution and contact
viability; only the shared inventory/opportunity needs identity-aware handling.


ADVERSARIAL NORMALIZATION PASS -- F122 THROUGH F136
----------------------------------------------------
Purpose: challenge the recent high-density team/state findings for accidental
splitting of one code defect, generic "team games are different" reasoning, or
repairs that would automatically fix several numbered roots.

RESULT: no retraction or mandatory merge established. The roots fall at distinct
state owners / nonlinear operations:

F122 / KI#445 -- TacticalSituation
    Shared scarce object: one agent tactical unit is independently consumed by
    per-rival entanglement caps. Repair locus is TacticalSituation engagement
    accounting / shared unit identity.

F123 / KI#446 -- Bellicosity
    Shared budget: the same agent lost-power budget is independently reused in
    the historical anti-third-party `min` safeguard. Repair locus is
    Bellicosity's loss aggregation before the cap.

F124 / KI#447 -- ThirdPartyIntervention severity
    Domain switch: intervention probability is team-aware, then the nonlinear
    50% severity gate uses one prospective intervener member's ARMY. Repair
    locus is the later threat-strength ratio/gate.

F125 / KI#448 -- DramaticArc
    Team-wide tension transition is licensed through player-local human-safety
    and minimum-action gates. Repair locus is DramaticArc's gate aggregation.

F126 / KI#449 -- Distraction
    Team-war opportunity cost / fixed current-war-plan nudge is charged once per
    target member. Repair locus is canonical hostile-team evaluation of the
    Distraction cost.

F127 / KI#450 -- MilitaryVictory
    Global/team victory completion budgets are reset per rival player; Conquest
    also confuses one player elimination with team-level victory progress.
    Repair locus is scenario/global victory-progress aggregation.

F128 / KI#451 -- HiredHand
    Sponsor/bounty/history obligation is keyed by TeamTypes but consumed per
    target player. Repair locus is team-keyed obligation accounting.

F129 / KI#452 -- vassal current-tech cache
    Team-owned existing technology value is cached under PlayerTypes and summed
    over prospective vassal members. Repair locus spans UWAICache vassal-tech
    storage and its explicit member-summing consumers.

F130 / KI#453 -- Risk
    Team-owned capitulation/vassal state costs are emitted through agent/rival
    member passes, including a fixed 100 capitulation cost. Repair locus is Risk
    team-state charging; ordinary player asset losses must remain separate.

F131 / KI#454 -- GreedForSpace
    Physical identity: the same plot can exist in two player city-site lists and
    be counted twice. Repair locus is plot-ID union/deduplication, not team-size
    normalization.

F132 / KI#455 -- Revolts
    Persistent uniqueness state (`m_countedCities`) is combined with reset local
    numerator/denominator state, causing player-iteration-order dependence.
    Repair locus is ratio/uniqueness lifetime alignment.

F133 / KI#456 -- shared loss helper
    Supported OWN_EXCLUSIVE_RADIUS tile loss augments only the numerator after
    total assets are frozen. Repair locus is the shared asset-measurement domain,
    independent of team-member iteration.

F134 / KI#457 -- IllWill
    Player-local ARMY capability crosses nonlinear revenge/dogpile thresholds
    for a team-wide war. Repair locus is IllWill's military-capability helper;
    diplomatic motive remains player-specific.

F135 / KI#458 -- ThirdPartyIntervention decisive-target shortcut
    Target-scoping failure: one pre-simulation leader player's elimination or
    ANY capitulation to us is accepted as decisive victory over eTarget. Repair
    locus is the early target-war shortcut. It is in the same aspect as F124 but
    a correct F124 power repair cannot affect this branch.

F136 / KI#459 -- partnerUtilFromTech
    Team-owned technology differences are exposed as reusable per-player partner
    opportunities. Repair locus is the shared partner-tech helper and its
    allocation; F129's vassal-tech cache repair cannot affect it.

WHY THESE ARE NOT ONE GENERIC ARCHITECTURE KI

WarUtilityAspect intentionally uses pairwise player evaluation. Numerous clean
controls in the same file genuinely require player ownership: resource deals,
trade routes, attitudes, city assets, nuke source/victim accounting, distinct
settlement plots, etc. Replacing the base loop with one TeamIter would break
valid semantics.

The recent findings survive only where an additional invariant identifies a
more specific ownership/normalization domain -- a unique physical object, an
explicit TeamTypes-keyed state, a team/global victory threshold, a team-wide war
capability, a persistent uniqueness set, or an explicit target-scoped comment.
Their repairs consequently remain local and independent rather than one common
change to WarUtilityAspect::evaluate.

CURRENT-REACHABILITY CHALLENGE

The team-partition findings use ordinary supported multi-member teams/Permanent
Alliances, not malformed IDs or dead code. Where a finding instead requires a
nondefault rule, it is called out explicitly (F133: documented
OWN_EXCLUSIVE_RADIUS=1). LoveOfPeace remains deliberately unpromoted because
current SAS data sets its personality value to zero throughout; that contrast
continues to enforce the current-reachability bar.

No F122-F136 root was retracted by this normalization pass. This is not a claim
that every possible numerical reproduction is equally severe; it is a claim
that each numbered root has an independent current code condition and repair
locus that survives the challenge.

C014-WIP25 CONTINUATION -- PREEMPTIVEWAR TEAM-THREAT OWNERSHIP + CLOSURE PASS

STATUS: WIP / append-only continuation of authoritative C014-WIP24.

F137 / provisional KI#460 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED TEAM-THREAT DUPLICATION
PREEMPTIVEWAR CONSUMES A TEAM-OWNED THREAT / SIDE FORECAST ONCE PER RIVAL PLAYER
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: NEW CURRENT INHERITED ADVCIV DEFECT ROOT. Static proof strong.

ROOT CONTRACT

PreEmptiveWar::evaluate() is entered through WarUtilityBroaderAspect's ordinary
per-rival-player callback. WarUtilityAspect::evaluate(MilitaryAnalyst const&)
therefore invokes it once for each known potential-enemy PLAYER, including every
living member of the same rival team.

Its first substantive input looks player-keyed:

    scaled const rCurrThreat = ourCache().threatRating(eThey);

but UWAICache::calculateThreatRating(PlayerTypes eRival) ultimately returns:

    return teamThreat(TEAMID(eRival));

apart from an individual rival-cache reachability early return. teamThreat then
uses the rival TEAM's attitude, long-term TEAM/master-side power, victory stage,
and alternative-target count. Thus, whenever two teammates B and C can both
reach our capital, threatRating(B) == threatRating(C): they expose the same
TeamBC threat through two PlayerTypes slots.

PREEMPTIVEWAR THEN RECONSTRUCTS THE SAME TEAM SIDE

The rest of the calculation does not make that shared threat player-specific.
For the current eThey it builds the rival side by looping all major players and
accepting anyone whose:

    kTheirAlly.getMasterTeam() == GET_PLAYER(eThey).getMasterTeam()

(or who is a newly accepted vassal of eTheirTeam).

For teammates B and C, getMasterTeam() and eTheirTeam are identical. Therefore
both callbacks aggregate the same current/predicted B+C+vassal city side. Within
one MilitaryAnalyst evaluation eWe is fixed too, so the current/predicted agent
side, rTheirEdge, threat-change transform, rival-team victory-stage modifier,
and agent distrust factor are also identical.

DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCTION

Take one agent player A and a two-member rival team B+C. Assume:

* B and C are both known potential enemies and both can reach A's capital;
* teamThreat(TeamBC) is above the 0.15 gate;
* the simulated scenario changes TeamBC's side enough for rTheirEdge != 0.

B pass:

    rCurrThreat = teamThreat(TeamBC)
    rival city side = B + C + their vassals
    -> utility X

C pass:

    rCurrThreat = teamThreat(TeamBC)
    rival city side = B + C + their vassals
    -> the same utility X

The aspect total receives 2X. Moving the same players into one-member teams, or
merely changing team membership while holding the combined military/economic
side fixed, changes the long-term-threat utility because the same TeamBC threat
is exposed once per member.

PLAYER-SPECIFIC REACHABILITY DOES NOT RESCUE THE MODEL

calculateThreatRating has one player-local gate before returning teamThreat: it
checks whether the particular rival player's cache says our capital is
reachable. This can make one teammate's slot zero and another's nonzero, but it
does not justify counting the common team threat twice when both are reachable.
It also exposes the deeper ownership mismatch: a team capability is cached under
PlayerTypes after filtering it through one member's reachability.

A robust repair should decide team reachability/capability explicitly (e.g. any
material member can project force) and expose/canonicalize the resulting threat
at team scope, rather than relying on whichever player slot is being consumed.

ANCESTRY

This is inherited, not SAS-created.

* Current SAS and Base AdvCiv 1.14 have normalized-identical
  PreEmptiveWar::evaluate().
* Current SAS and Base AdvCiv 1.14 also have normalized-identical
  UWAICache::calculateThreatRating and UWAICache::teamThreat.
* The original local UWAI introduction (reachable-history practical 1253,
  f6ff6a182f) already created a player-indexed threatRatings[civId] entry whose
  calculateThreatRating(civId) returned teamThreat(TEAMID(civId)), and the
  simultaneously introduced PreEmptiveWar iterated rival players while
  rebuilding their master-team/vassal city side.

So the player/team ownership mismatch exists from the feature's birth.

RELATION TO F107 / KI#430

Keep separate.

F107 proves that PreEmptiveWar constructs present/predicted sides
inconsistently: existing vassals disappear from our predicted baseline and a
team-wide current-city base subtracts only the current agent member's losses.
Correcting those baselines does NOT prevent a correct team forecast from being
consumed once for B and again for teammate C.

Conversely, evaluating/caching the long-term threat once per rival team does NOT
repair F107's existing-vassal and teammate-loss asymmetries inside that one team
forecast. The two roots therefore have different invariants and repair loci.

RELATION TO F121 / KI#444

F121's terminal-start manifestation forces calculateThreatRating to zero forever
while currentEra <= startEra. That startup-clock bug can hide F137 in a
terminal-era-start test, but fixing the clock merely allows the duplicated team
threat to become active. The roots are independent.

REPAIR DIRECTION

Prefer a team-owned long-term threat object/calculation and consume its change
once per distinct rival team (or otherwise allocate it exactly once), while
preserving genuinely player-specific diplomatic/economic quantities elsewhere.
If the reachability precondition remains, aggregate it at the same team scope
rather than using one player's cache as a hidden switch for a teamThreat value.
Do not simply divide every PreEmptiveWar result by team size without first
fixing F107's side construction and deciding how team reachability should work.


CLOSURE-PASS NOTE -- DERIVED MEMBER STATE
-----------------------------------------
The first derived-member lifetime inventory after WIP24 did NOT establish a
second root:

* MilitaryVictory::preEvaluate overwrites m_iVotesToGo/m_bEnoughVotes for each
  agent member from the same agent-team victory state.
* KingMaking::preEvaluate explicitly clears both winner sets on every member
  call before repopulating them.
* Risk::m_bSASContactGateEvaluated is intentionally scenario-wide after
  KI#425/F102 so the team-wide hard contact gate fires only once.
* IllWill::preEvaluate/evaluate overwrite the scratch scalar state needed for
  each member before use.
* ThirdPartyIntervention and DramaticArc overwrite their precomputed scalars on
  every member preEvaluate call.
* Revolts::m_countedCities is deliberately scenario-wide; its mismatch with
  reset per-call numerator/denominator state is already F132/KI#455.

This closes the obvious derived-state-lifetime surface without manufacturing a
new finding.

C014-WIP26 CONTINUATION -- TACTICAL OPERATIONAL READINESS TARGET-TEAM DUPLICATION
===============================================================================
STATUS: WIP / append-only continuation of authoritative C014-WIP25.

F138 / provisional KI#461 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED TARGET-TEAM COST DUPLICATION
TACTICALSITUATION::evalOperational CHARGES ONE AGENT READINESS DEFICIT ONCE PER TARGET MEMBER
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: NEW CURRENT INHERITED ADVCIV DEFECT ROOT. Static proof strong.

EXPLICIT INTENT / DOMAIN

TacticalSituation::evalOperational begins with an unusually clear scope comment:

    Evaluate our readiness only for the target that we want to invade
    (not its vassals or allies from def. pact)

and enforces:

    if (m_kParams.getTarget() != eTheirTeam)
        return;

The quantity being priced is therefore the current AGENT PLAYER's operational
readiness for one target TEAM/war plan: attacker count, cargo capacity, escorts,
preparation time and whether the planned target requires naval deployment.

PER-PLAYER CALLBACK STILL REPEATS THAT TEAM COST

TacticalSituation itself remains a normal WarUtilityAspect. Its evaluate() is
called once for every rival player that belongs to the military analysis:

    if (!militAnalyst().isWar(eWe, eThey)) return;
    if (kOurTeam.isAtWar(eTheirTeam)) evalEngagement();
    else evalOperational();

For a new planned war against a multi-member target team B+C, both B and C are
part of the simulated enemy side. Since both have eTheirTeam == target, both
callbacks enter evalOperational.

Within a fixed agent-member MilitaryAnalyst evaluation, almost every material
input is then the same on both passes:

* our attacker UNITAI inventory;
* our logistics/cargo power;
* our sea escort inventory;
* our city count;
* total/limited and naval/land war mode;
* m_kParams.getPreparationTime();
* the initial preparation-time configuration;
* whether our army can bombard.

The target-player inputs do not prevent a deterministic duplicate. Teammates
share team technologies and can trivially be in the same era; choose B and C
both with at least one reachable city and the same current-era factor. Then
rTargetAttackers, readiness, passed preparation portion and the final
`iUnreadinessCost` are identical.

DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCTION

Agent A plans war against TeamBC, which has two living members B and C. A is at
60% operational readiness and has progressed far enough through preparation for
an unreadiness cost X > 0. Both B and C have reachable cities and are in the
same era.

B callback:

    target == TeamBC -> evalOperational
    A readiness = 60%
    -> m_iU -= X

C callback:

    target == TeamBC -> evalOperational
    same A readiness = 60%
    -> m_iU -= X again

The scenario is one war preparation by A against one target team, but its
readiness deficit is charged 2X solely because TeamBC has two players.

This differs from genuinely additive rival-player quantities: A does not have a
second copy of its attack stack, transport capacity or elapsed preparation just
because another teammate owns cities on the same target team.

AGENT TEAM MEMBERS ARE A DIFFERENT DIMENSION

WarEvaluator also evaluates each living AGENT team member separately. That is
not the root here: A and teammate A2 own different unit inventories, so separate
readiness assessments for A and A2 can be meaningful. F138 concerns repeated
charging of one fixed agent member's readiness across multiple members of the
SAME target team.

ANCESTRY

Current SAS and Base AdvCiv 1.14 have normalized-identical
TacticalSituation::evalOperational(). Reachable history shows the original UWAI
introduction (practical 1253 / f6ff6a182f) already implemented the same design:

    if(params.targetId() != TEAMID(theyId)) return;
    ... compute our attackers/cargo/escort/preparation readiness ...
    u -= unreadiness cost

inside the ordinary per-rival-player TacticalSituation callback. The root is
therefore inherited from the feature's birth, not caused by SAS.

RELATION TO F122 / KI#445

Keep separate despite sharing TacticalSituation.

F122 concerns evalEngagement during an EXISTING war: the same physical agent
unit can be consumed independently by rival-specific threat/entanglement caps.
Its repair needs shared physical-unit accounting across rival engagement passes.

F138 concerns evalOperational before the target war exists: one aggregate
agent-force/preparation deficit is charged once per target-team member. Its
repair can simply canonicalize/aggregate the target-team readiness calculation
once for each agent member.

Fixing the engagement unit-identity accounting does not touch evalOperational;
canonicalizing pre-war readiness does not fix ongoing-war unit reuse.

REPAIR DIRECTION

Evaluate operational readiness once per agent member for the configured target
TEAM, not once per target player. Target-specific era/reachability inputs should
also be aggregated at team scope (e.g. relevant/reachable target members) rather
than choosing one arbitrary member if the calculation is canonicalized.

Do not divide the whole TacticalSituation aspect by target team size: the
engagement branch contains genuinely player-owned enemy units/cities and needs
its own F122 identity-aware repair.

C014-WIP27 CONTINUATION -- ILLWILL WAR-ON-FRIEND TEAM-EVENT COUNTING + CLOSURE CONTROLS
===============================================================================
STATUS: WIP / append-only continuation of authoritative C014-WIP26.
COMPLETED FILES: 13 / 169.
CURRENT FILE: 014 CvGameCoreDLL/WarUtilityAspect.cpp OPEN.
NO REPOSITORY SOURCE FILES MODIFIED.

F139 / provisional KI#462 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED TEAM-EVENT / PLAYER-SET COUNTING DEFECT
ILLWILL::evalAngeredPartners CAN COUNT ONE DECLARATION-OF-WAR-ON-FRIEND MEMORY ONCE PER VICTIM-TEAM MEMBER
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: NEW CURRENT INHERITED ADVCIV DEFECT ROOT. Static producer/consumer proof strong.

ROOT CONTRACT

IllWill::evalAngeredPartners estimates the diplomatic penalty that an outside
player eThey will assign to the AGENT PLAYER eWe for wars newly declared in the
MilitaryAnalyst scenario. The actual relation event being modeled is
MEMORY_DECLARED_WAR_ON_FRIEND.

MilitaryAnalyst, however, represents declarations through player sets:

    PlyrSet const& kWeDecl = militAnalyst().getWarsDeclaredBy(eWe);

PlayerResult::setDoWBy accepts PlayerTypes, and the war-scenario construction
crosses the declaring side with the opposing side. Thus, if A declares war on a
two-member TeamBC, A's player result contains both B and C even though Civ4 has
one team declaration against TeamBC.

IllWill then loops those PLAYER entries and converts each one back to its team:

    for (PlyrSetIter it = kWeDecl.begin(); it != kWeDecl.end(); ++it)
    {
        if (GET_TEAM(*it).isAVassal() || eTheirTeam == TEAMID(*it))
            continue;
        if (kThey.AI_disapprovesOfDoW(eOurTeam, TEAMID(*it)))
        {
            ...
            rPenalties += rPenaltyPerDoW;
        }
    }

For B and C, TEAMID(*it) is the same TeamBC. The same observer predicate and
same fixed -1/-2 memory-attitude weight can therefore be added twice.

REAL DIPLOMACY PATH IS THE DECISIVE CONTROL

CvTeamAI::AI_preDeclareWar receives one `TeamTypes eTarget`. For each living
member of the aggressor team it loops the outside observers once and does:

    if (kPlayer.AI_disapprovesOfDoW(getID(), eTarget))
        kPlayer.AI_rememberEvent(kOurMember.getID(),
                MEMORY_DECLARED_WAR_ON_FRIEND);

A declaration A -> TeamBC therefore gives qualifying observer D one
war-on-friend memory toward A for that victim TEAM. The real code does not loop
B and C and record the same memory twice merely because TeamBC has two players.

This makes F139 stronger than a generic team-game weighting disagreement:
IllWill is trying to predict a concrete diplomacy-memory effect and can predict
more events than the real declaration path creates.

DETERMINISTIC TWO-MEMBER REPRODUCTION

Let A be the current agent player. TeamBC contains living B and C. Outside
player D likes TeamBC enough that:

    D.AI_disapprovesOfDoW(TeamA, TeamBC) == true

and D's leader uses the usual -1 war-on-friend attitude weight.

Military analysis for A's single declaration on TeamBC stores:

    getWarsDeclaredBy(A) = { B, C }

D's IllWill pass then evaluates:

    B entry -> AI_disapprovesOfDoW(TeamA, TeamBC) -> rPenalties += 1
    C entry -> AI_disapprovesOfDoW(TeamA, TeamBC) -> rPenalties += 1

so the forecast is two relation points. The real AI_preDeclareWar call for that
same TeamBC victim records one MEMORY_DECLARED_WAR_ON_FRIEND event toward A.
The downstream partner-loss, dogpile-danger and diplomatic-victory costs are all
scaled from the inflated rPenalties value.

AGENT TEAM MEMBERS ARE NOT THE DUPLICATE

CvTeamAI::AI_preDeclareWar deliberately records the observer memory separately
toward every living member of the AGGRESSOR team. WarEvaluator likewise evaluates
each agent member separately. Therefore A and teammate A2 can legitimately each
incur one memory with D.

The defect is only the VICTIM side: within A's one member evaluation, B and C
are two PlayerTypes representations of one target-team declaration.

CASCADING / DEFENSIVE-PACT WARS

MilitaryAnalyst can also add declarations against Defensive-Pact allies. Those
are distinct victim teams and correspond to additional real team declarations;
they must remain separately chargeable. The correct aggregation is therefore
not "one penalty total" but "one penalty per DISTINCT victim TeamTypes".

A practical repair is to collect/deduplicate TEAMID(*it) from kWeDecl before
calling AI_disapprovesOfDoW and adding rPenaltyPerDoW. Player-local report names
can use a canonical/representative member only for logging.

ANCESTRY

The original local UWAI introduction (practical 1253 / f6ff6a182f) already
implemented IllWill::evalAngeredPartners by iterating
`m->getWarsDeclaredBy(weId)`, which was a PlayerTypes set, and adding one fixed
penalty for every qualifying entry. Later advc.130h replaced the direct
player-attitude test with AI_disapprovesOfDoW(agentId, TEAMID(*it)), making the
team-domain contract even more explicit without deduplicating the player set.

Current SAS and Base AdvCiv 1.14 have normalized-identical
IllWill::evalAngeredPartners implementations for this behavior. The real
AI_preDeclareWar memory path likewise remains team-targeted. F139 is inherited
from UWAI's player-set representation of declarations, not SAS-created.

RELATION TO F134 / KI#457 AND F136 / KI#459

Keep separate.

* F134 concerns IllWill::theirToOurPowerRatio: team-wide revenge/dogpile military
  capability is measured through one player's army before nonlinear thresholds.
* F136 concerns partnerUtilFromTech: the same team-owned technology opportunity
  can be valued once per teammate.
* F139 exists even if military capability and partner-tech value are both fixed:
  the input relation-penalty COUNT itself can contain two predicted memory hits
  for one real team declaration.

REPAIR DIRECTION

Within evalAngeredPartners, transform the PlayerTypes declaration set into the
set of distinct victim teams before applying the war-on-friend observer test and
memory-attitude penalty. Preserve separate penalties for genuinely separate
victim teams (including cascading Defensive-Pact declarations), and preserve
per-agent-member evaluation because the real memory is stored separately toward
each aggressor player.


F114 / provisional KI#437 -- ADVERSARIAL REVALIDATION -- REMAINS LIVE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The closure pass briefly challenged F114's assumption that a target teammate
passes FairPlay's:

    kTheirTeam.isHasMet(kOther.getTeam())

filter. A shallow read of CvTeam::reset would suggest a team does not meet
itself because m_aiHasMetTurn defaults to -1. The complete initialization trace
proves otherwise and therefore REVALIDATES F114 rather than retracting it.

CvGame::initDiplomacy explicitly executes for every team:

    itTeam->meet(itTeam->getID(), false);

CvTeam::meet then calls makeHasMet on that same team object; the first call sets:

    m_aiHasMetTurn.set(eOther, iGameTurn);

with eOther == self. Hence isHasMet(self) is true in an initialized game. A
second living member C of target TeamBC therefore is not filtered by the
has-met condition merely because C shares eTheirTeam with B.

The second F114 manifestation also survives: CvTeamAI::AI_shareWar(ownTeam)
iterates the team's current enemies and returns true when an enemy is at war
with the supplied own team. Therefore a target teammate that reaches the branch
can indeed be classified as an "ally" of eThey while the target team is at war.

No album correction is required: WIP07's F114 diagnosis remains authoritative.
This note is retained so the tempting but incomplete "teams do not meet
self" counterargument is not rediscovered later.

F124 / provisional KI#447 -- AUTHORITATIVE BROADENING -- THREAT-STRENGTH RATIO
IS PLAYER-LOCAL ON THE AGENT SIDE TOO
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WIP14 established F124 from the potential intervener side: ThirdPartyIntervention
estimates intervention probability with rival TEAM power/state, then switches to
one rival PLAYER's cached ARMY before the nonlinear 0.50 severity gate. The final
closure pass proves that the denominator has the symmetric team/member mismatch.

PROBABILITY PATH ALREADY USES AGENT TEAM POWER

For the paranoia branch, ThirdPartyIntervention computes:

    int iOurDefPow = kOurTeam.getDefensivePower();
    ...
    kWe.AI_paranoiaRating(eThey, iOurDefPow, false, true);

So its intervention-probability model explicitly supplies the full agent TEAM's
defensive power.

SEVERITY PATH SWITCHES TO CURRENT AGENT PLAYER

preEvaluate() instead initializes:

    m_rDefPow = ourCache().getPowerValues()[ARMY]->power();

`ourCache()` belongs to current PlayerTypes eWe. The subsequent ally loop is:

    PlayerAIIter<MAJOR_CIV,OTHER_KNOWN_TO> itAlly(eOurTeam)

and AgentIterator's `OTHER_KNOWN_TO` predicate explicitly requires:

    getTeam(kAgent) != m_eTeam

(the enum comment likewise says "Not incl. the first agent's team, but incl. its
vassals"). Therefore an ordinary teammate A2 on eOurTeam is categorically NOT
added to m_rDefPow. Vassals and qualifying defensive-pact teams can be added at
half weight; same-team members cannot.

Later evaluate() uses this player-local value as:

    scaled rOurPow = m_rDefPow;
    ...
    scaled rTheirPowToOurs = rTheirPow / rOurPow;
    if (rTheirPowToOurs <= fixp(0.5))
        return;

This is the same nonlinear gate already proven under F124.

DETERMINISTIC AGENT-PARTITION REPRODUCTION

Let agent TeamA have two ordinary members A1 and A2 with 40 relevant ARMY power
each (80 combined), and let potential intervener B have 30 relevant ARMY power.
Ignore vassals/losses and hold the probability path positive.

On A1's aspect pass:

    rOurPow = 40
    rTheirPowToOurs = 30 / 40 = 0.75 -> passes the 0.50 gate

On A2's pass, the same calculation occurs again. But the team that B would have
to fight has 80 combined power:

    30 / 80 = 0.375 -> should fail the aspect's own "too weak to matter" gate

Conversely, concentrating the same team power into one member changes the
nonlinear result despite identical war-side military capacity. The later linear
member-count divisor cannot undo a gate that has already passed/returned.

This is especially strong because the preceding paranoia calculation already
uses `kOurTeam.getDefensivePower()`: the same aspect first asks how likely B is
to intervene against the TEAM, then judges how dangerous that intervention is
against only the current member's army.

ANCESTRY / REPAIR NORMALIZATION

The original ThirdPartyIntervention introduction already initialized m_rDefPow
from current-player cache power and iterated OTHER_KNOWN_TO for allies; Base
AdvCiv 1.14 retains the same boundary. Later power-projection retuning did not
change it.

F124 is therefore best normalized as one root: ThirdPartyIntervention's
nonlinear threat-strength ratio is built from member-local ordinary-team power
on BOTH sides despite modelling a team-wide intervention. Keep genuinely
player-specific probability/attitude inputs if desired, but construct the
severity power ratio from the actual war sides before the nonlinear floor/gate.


F122 / provisional KI#445 -- AUTHORITATIVE BROADENING -- PHYSICAL AGENT EXPOSURE
AND EVACUATION CAN ALSO BE REUSED ACROSS TARGET-TEAM MEMBER PASSES
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WIP13's decisive F122 proof remains the explicit one-agent-unit/one-entangled-
enemy cap. Two neighboring TacticalSituation::evalEngagement quantities share
the same physical-asset reuse boundary and should be handled by the same repair.

1. `iOurExposed`

For every current rival player eThey, the function walks the SAME current agent
groups and asks:

    kWe.AI_getPlotDanger(kGroupPlot, 1, false, iGroupSize, false, eThey)

CvPlayerAI::AI_countDangerousUnits honors that final PlayerTypes filter by
counting only units whose combat owner equals eAttackPlayer. Thus a damaged A
unit threatened by both B and teammate C can be counted as exposed in B's pass
and then the exact same physical A unit can be counted again in C's pass.

2. `iOurEvac`

`evacPop(eWe, eThey)` walks the SAME physical cities of current agent eWe. For an
evacuating city it again uses player-filtered plot danger:

    kOwner.AI_getPlotDanger(..., eInvader) >= 2

The source comment says this filter exists only to avoid attributing evacuation
to an unrelated third party. Against two members B and C of the SAME hostile
team, one physical evacuating city/population can satisfy the danger threshold
for both passes and be charged twice.

These do not need separate roots: they are the same F122 state-domain defect as
entanglement -- agent-side physical tactical assets are independently consumable
inside rival-player callbacks even though the assets themselves cannot be lost,
exposed, evacuated or paired twice merely because enemy ownership is partitioned
between teammates.

Repair should aggregate/deduplicate the relevant target-team danger/engagement
before applying physical-agent-asset caps. Do not simply globalize every
TacticalSituation term; genuinely player-owned enemy units/cities remain valid
inputs.


F127 / provisional KI#450 -- AUTHORITATIVE BROADENING -- CONQUEST FULL COMPLETION
CAN ALSO REPEAT ACROSS AGENT-TEAM MEMBERS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WIP21 proved that `progressRatingConquest()` treats elimination of one rival
PLAYER as full Conquest progress even while that player's TEAM can remain an
actual CvGame::testVictory blocker.

There is an additional aggregation manifestation under the already-established
F127 global/team-victory root. Its first condition is:

    if (militAnalyst().isEliminated(eThey) || ...)
        return 1;

The `isEliminated(eThey)` result is independent of which living agent-team member
currently owns eWe. WarEvaluator evaluates the shared MilitaryVictory aspect for
A1 and then A2. If B is predicted eliminated, both agent-member passes can reach
that same unconditional 1.0 completion state for the same team-owned Conquest
objective.

for Domination/Diplomacy; this note simply brings Conquest's later WIP21
broadening under the same normalization. No new root is needed.

The repair remains scenario/team-level victory-progress aggregation before any
single global completion cap/full-completion state is converted to utility.

F140 / provisional KI#463 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED ADVCIV TEAM-STATE DUPLICATION
GREEDFORVASSALS CHARGES ONE CAPITULATED-VASSAL DIPLOMATIC DOWNSIDE PER MEMBER
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv player-loop/team-vassal-state defect.

ROOT

`GreedForVassals::evaluate()` is entered through the ordinary per-rival-player
WarUtilityAspect loop. It first decides whether the CURRENT RIVAL TEAM becomes a
new vassal of the agent team:

    TeamSet const& kNewVassals =
        militAnalyst().getCapitulationsAccepted(eOurTeam);

    if (kNewVassals.count(eTheirTeam) <= 0 || ...)
        return;

After valuing member-local research income, resources, trade routes and military
support, the function unconditionally applies:

    if (!kWe.AI_atVictoryStage(AI_VICTORY_CONQUEST3))
        rUtility -= 5; // To account for the diplo penalty from capitulated vassals

The condition that creates this cost is one `TeamTypes` capitulation relation,
but the cost is emitted from a `PlayerTypes` callback. If target team V contains
living members V1 and V2 and V capitulates to eOurTeam, both member evaluations
see the same `kNewVassals.count(V)` result:

    V1 pass: -5
    V2 pass: -5

Hence one capitulated-vassal team relation contributes a fixed -10 downside
solely because the vassal team contains two players. With one living member the
same relation contributes -5. The final `max(0, rUtility)` can mask the extra
subtraction when a member's benefit is already small, but it does not repair the
ownership error; whenever both passes remain above zero, the duplicated fixed
cost survives directly, and near zero it can change whether an otherwise useful
member contribution is discarded entirely.

HISTORICAL INTENT IS EXPLICITLY TEAM-STATE-LIKE

The original UWAI introduction did not merely contain an unexplained magic -5.
Its comment was:

    To account for downsides of vassals, in particular wars with third parties
    that dislike the vassal

Practical 2261 later shortened this to today's
"diplo penalty from capitulated vassals" while adding love-of-peace handling;
the -5 itself was preserved. Base AdvCiv 1.14 still has the same fixed cost in
the same per-rival-player callback.

Both stated downsides are consequences of acquiring a VASSAL TEAM, not of
receiving the same team relation once for every player stored on that team.

REAL DIPLOMACY CONTROL -- RIVAL-VASSAL ATTITUDE ITERATES VASSAL TEAMS

The live attitude system gives a particularly strong ownership-domain control.
`CvPlayerAI::AI_getRivalVassalAttitude(ePlayer)` computes dislike of another
player's vassal bloc by iterating:

    for (TeamIter<CIV_ALIVE,VASSAL_OF> itVassal(TEAMID(ePlayer)); ...)

and, for each capitulated vassal TEAM, derives one score from:

    itVassal->getNumCities()
    itVassal->getCapitulationTurn()

That `rCapitulatedScore` is then used in the rival-vassal attitude modifier. If
one capitulated team owns eight cities, repartitioning those same eight cities
between one or two player members does not produce a second TeamIter entry or a
second capitulation relation. The score remains based on the same vassal team's
aggregate city count and capitulation age.

This team granularity is not a late SAS reinterpretation. K-Mod's original
`AI_getRivalVassalAttitude` also queried the target player's TEAM and its vassal
count/power; AdvCiv later refined the formula while retaining team-level vassal
ownership.

REAL GAME-STATE CONTROL -- VASSALAGE ITSELF IS ONE CvTeam RELATION

`CvTeam::setVassal(TeamTypes eMaster, ...)` changes one team's `m_eMaster`,
records one team capitulation/voluntary-vassal event, and updates wars/war plans
through TeamTypes state. A multi-member team does not call `setVassal` once for
each player member. The forced-war liability highlighted by the original UWAI
comment therefore also originates from one team relation.

WHY THIS IS NOT F129 AND NOT A BLANKET VASSAL NORMALIZATION

F129/KI#452 concerns a different object: an already-owned TECHNOLOGY SET is
team-owned but cached/credited once per vassal player. Fixing that cache does not
touch this fixed -5 line.

Conversely, many neighboring GreedForVassals benefits really can be member-local:

* future commerce/research capacity can differ by player;
* connected resource availability is player-owned (the negative control already
  recorded under F129);
* trade-route city counts and military branches are player-local contributions.

Those quantities should not be blindly divided by team size. F140 is only the
fixed downside whose own condition/comment and the real diplomacy/vassal systems
identify it as one team-level capitulated-vassal state.

RELATION TO F130 / WHY A SEPARATE ROOT IS USEFUL

F130/KI#453 proves the same broad architectural hazard inside `Risk`: fixed
capitulation cost and master-team vassal losses are re-emitted through member
callbacks. F140 is not merged into F130 because the two defects have independent
repair loci and independent modeled quantities:

* F130 is Risk's own loss/capitulation accounting;
* F140 is GreedForVassals' approximation of the diplomatic/forced-war downside
  of ACQUIRING a vassal team.

Repairing Risk cannot change GreedForVassals, and repairing the latter cannot
change Risk. This follows the C014-WIP24 normalization rule that similar
player/team smells remain separate when their state owners and nonlinear/fixed
operations are independently emitted.

ANCESTRY

The fixed vassal-downside subtraction is present in the original UWAI lineage.
Practical 2261 changed only the surrounding comment/peace-personality treatment,
and later scaled-number/refactor commits retained the behavior. Current SAS and
Base AdvCiv 1.14 still contain the same per-member emission. F140 is therefore
inherited, not SAS-created.

REPAIR DIRECTION

Charge the fixed capitulated-vassal diplomatic/forced-war downside once per newly
acquired VASSAL TEAM, or apportion one team-level cost across whatever living
member callbacks are retained so the aggregate is roster-partition invariant.

Do not normalize the whole GreedForVassals result. Keep genuinely player-local
benefits additive, and handle F129's duplicated current-tech inventory at its own
ownership boundary.

C014-WIP30 APPEND -- C++ polymorphic-lifetime closure + F141
===============================================================================

F141 / provisional KI#464 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED ADVCIV C++ LIFETIME DEFECT
WARUTILITYASPECT HAS NO VIRTUAL DESTRUCTOR BUT DERIVED ASPECTS ARE DELETED THROUGH BASE POINTERS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STATUS
------
NEW CURRENT INHERITED C++ DEFECT ROOT. Static language-contract evidence is
conclusive; practical severity depends on compiler/optimizer/runtime because the
operation is undefined behavior, but current derived classes contain non-trivial
members whose destruction genuinely matters.

ROOT CONTRACT
-------------
`WarUtilityAspect` is a polymorphic base class. Its current declaration contains
multiple virtual functions, including:

    virtual int evaluate(MilitaryAnalyst const& kMilitaryAnalyst);
    virtual UWAI::AspectTypes xmlID() const=0;
    virtual void evaluate()=0;
    virtual int preEvaluate();
    virtual bool concernsOnlyWarParties() const;

but it declares no destructor at all. There is no
`virtual ~WarUtilityAspect()` in the header, cpp file, or any derived class.
Consequently the compiler supplies a non-virtual implicit base destructor.

`WarEvaluator::fillWithAspects` then allocates concrete derived objects and
stores them behind base pointers:

    vector<WarUtilityAspect*> apAspects;
    ...
    v.push_back(new GreedForAssets(params));
    ...
    v.push_back(new KingMaking(params));
    ...
    v.push_back(new Revolts(params));
    ...

After evaluation, `WarEvaluator::evaluate` destroys every object through that
base pointer:

    delete apAspects[i];

For a delete-expression whose static pointee type is a base class but whose
dynamic object is derived, the base destructor must be virtual. Here it is not.
Deleting any of these derived aspect objects through `WarUtilityAspect*` is
therefore undefined behavior in C++.

THIS IS NOT MERELY A STYLE/WARNING ISSUE
----------------------------------------
Two current derived classes make the missing derived destruction concretely
important:

`KingMaking` owns:

    std::set<PlayerTypes> m_winningFuture;
    std::set<PlayerTypes> m_winningPresent;

and `Revolts` owns:

    std::set<PlotNumTypes> m_countedCities;

Their implicit derived destructors must destroy those sets. With a non-virtual
base destructor, deleting the objects through `WarUtilityAspect*` does not have
a valid language-level path that guarantees those derived destructors run.
Under the ordinary implementation exhibited by a local C++03 compiler, only the
base destructor is called, so dynamically allocated set nodes owned by the
derived subobject are not released. The C++ rule itself is stronger: because the
program has undefined behavior at the delete-expression, no particular runtime
consequence should be assumed or relied upon.

The base class also owns a `std::vector<PlotNumTypes>`, but that does not rescue
the hierarchy: ordinary implementations can still destroy the base subobject
while skipping the derived subobject, and the standard already makes the whole
operation undefined when the base destructor is non-virtual.

LOCAL COMPILER CORROBORATION -- ILLUSTRATIVE, NOT THE PROOF
-----------------------------------------------------------
A minimal C++03 reproduction with a polymorphic base lacking a virtual
destructor and a derived class owning `std::set<int>` was compiled locally with:

    g++ -std=c++03 -Wall -Wextra -Wdelete-non-virtual-dtor

GCC 14.2 emits:

    warning: deleting object of polymorphic class type 'Base' which has
    non-virtual destructor might cause undefined behavior

and the illustrative run prints only the base destructor, not the derived
one. This corroborates the practical mechanism but is intentionally not used as
a claim about the exact Visual C++ 2003 manifestation; undefined behavior permits
implementation-dependent outcomes.

CURRENT CALL/LIFETIME REACHABILITY
----------------------------------
This delete path is not dormant. Every uncached `WarEvaluator::evaluate` scenario
constructs the aspect vector, evaluates it for the agent-team members, and then
loops over the vector and executes `delete apAspects[i]` for every concrete
aspect. War evaluation is a core UWAI path, so the invalid polymorphic deletion
is repeatedly reachable during normal AI play.

The non-trivial derived sets allocate only when populated, so a visible leak from
those containers can vary by game state. `Revolts::m_countedCities` is populated
when relevant cities are processed; `KingMaking`'s winner sets are populated once
that aspect becomes active. The source-level undefined behavior, however, exists
for every derived-object deletion regardless of whether those sets happen to be
empty in a particular call.

ANCESTRY -- INHERITED FROM THE ORIGINAL advc.104/UWAI CLASS INTRODUCTION
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Base AdvCiv 1.14 has the same defect:

* `WarUtilityAspect.h` declares the same polymorphic base without a virtual
  destructor;
* `WarEvaluator::fillWithAspects` allocates derived aspects into
  `vector<WarUtilityAspect*>`;
* `WarEvaluator::evaluate` executes `delete apAspects[i]` through those pointers;
* no `~WarUtilityAspect`, `~KingMaking` or `~Revolts` declaration exists.

The original practical-1253 / advc.104 introduction already created the hierarchy
this way. Its newly added `WarEvaluator::evaluate` constructed
`vector<WarUtilityAspect*> aspects`, filled it with `new DerivedAspect(...)`, and
then executed:

    delete aspects[i];

while the simultaneously introduced `WarUtilityAspect` declaration contained
virtual methods but no virtual destructor. The original `Revolts` class already
owned a `std::set<int> countedCities`, so a non-trivial derived destructor was
required from the beginning. Later KingMaking evolution added further `std::set`
members without changing the base destruction contract.

A scan of the retained current commit-diff corpus finds no later
`~WarUtilityAspect` addition/removal or manual compensating derived-destructor
scheme. Current source and Base 1.14 therefore preserve the original lifetime
bug.

COLLISION / ROOT ACCOUNTING
---------------------------
No current reviewed Known-Issues entry or prior album root owns the missing
virtual destructor / delete-through-base contract. Searches for virtual
/destructor/delete-through-polymorphic-base wording found no collision.

This is independent of every WarUtilityAspect semantic/modeling finding F101-
F140. Repairing the destructor cannot change any utility arithmetic, player/team
normalization or scenario-state predicate; conversely none of those repairs makes
`delete apAspects[i]` language-defined.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Give the polymorphic base a public virtual destructor. The project remains on an
old C++ toolchain, so a conservative C++03-compatible declaration is preferable,
for example:

    public:
        virtual ~WarUtilityAspect() {}

or declare it in the header and define an empty destructor in the cpp file.

It must be public because `WarEvaluator`, an unrelated caller, deletes through
`WarUtilityAspect*`. Do not use C++11-only `= default` merely for this repair.
Once the base destructor is virtual, the implicit derived destructors run in the
proper order and clean their standard-library members before the base subobject
is destroyed.

Do not paper over the issue by manually clearing the current `std::set` members:
that would leave the delete-expression undefined for every derived class and
would regress again when another derived class gains a non-trivial member.


EFFORT STRONGEST-RIVAL POWER CHALLENGE -- NOT PROMOTED
------------------------------------------------------
The closure pass also challenged `Effort::preEvaluate`, which estimates the
future usefulness of our surviving military by taking the maximum
`CvPlayer::getPower()` among known potential-enemy players. A hostile side with
one 120-power player therefore yields a different benchmark from an otherwise
similar two-member team split 60+60.

This is structurally player-partition-sensitive, but the source describes the
quantity as the power of our "most dangerous rival," and unlike F124/F134 there
is no hard nonlinear war-legality/capability predicate or direct real-game team
contract proving that this heuristic was intended to use combined team power.
Independently controlled civ/player armies can reasonably be treated as separate
post-war rivals even when teamed. No contradictory historical repair/comment has
been found.

Therefore this remains a DESIGN/MODELING REVIEW NOTE, not F142 (nor the former
F141 candidate). The audit should not convert every player-power approximation
into a team-power correctness defect merely because team partition can change a
heuristic.


C++ LIFETIME / OWNERSHIP CLOSURE CONTROLS
-----------------------------------------
- The missing virtual destructor is the only delete-through-polymorphic-base
  contract established in this file hierarchy. Searches found no custom derived
  destructors whose logic would mask or replace it.
- The unchecked `ourCache().lookupCity(...)` dereferences remain covered by the
  InvasionGraph/MilitaryAnalyst producer contract already recorded in WIP23;
  no competing pointer-lifetime root was established.
- Derived aspect members that intentionally persist across agent-member/rival
  callbacks were rechecked in WIP25. The only proven persistent/local partition
  defect remains F132 (`Revolts` numerator/denominator reset around
  `m_countedCities`); the destructor issue here concerns object destruction only
  after the entire scenario evaluation.
- The current practical-6267 `WarUtilityAspect.cpp`/header hierarchy remains

C014-WIP31 APPEND -- final denominator/API pass + exclusive-radius domain audit

RECONCILIATION / SCOPE
----------------------
This continuation remains grounded in the reconciled practical-6267 tree:

    HEAD 52e0f9c06718fb444208840cf5cea7b7723267e0

`WarUtilityAspect.cpp` is still byte-for-byte identical to the earlier source
underlying WIP28-WIP30. Current source and the reviewed Known-Issues ledger remain
authoritative; no repository source file was modified by this audit.

The closure pass resumed from F142 unused. Several superficially dangerous
construction/division paths were challenged before promoting anything:

* The base/derived constructor initializer order is unusual -- `m_kAgentTeam`
  appears early in the initializer list although it is declared after protected
  state -- but C++ declaration-order initialization remains safe here. None of
  the members initialized before `m_kAgentTeam` depends on it, `m_iU` is
  initialized before use, and `reset()` initializes the per-evaluation scratch
  state. No second construction-order root accompanies F141.
* ThirdPartyIntervention can start from zero defensive ARMY power, but the
  MilitaryAnalyst gained/lost-power contract prevents a reachable positive-cost
  divide-by-zero state through that route. If both current and gained defensive
  power are zero, lost power is zero and evaluation exits; positive projected
  gain raises `m_rDefPow` before later divisions. No F142 there.
* A second ThirdParty denominator challenge involving
  `confidenceAgainstHuman()` also collapses in the current implementation:
  `CvPlayerAI::confidenceAgainstHuman()` returns 1. The multiplication therefore
  cannot zero the denominator under current code/data.
* The remaining Risk/victory/partner ratio paths inspected in this pass have
  explicit positive floors, producer guarantees, or map directly to established
  F105/F127/F133 rather than defining another root.

These controls matter because the finding below is not being inferred from a
scary division alone. It has an explicit ownership-domain contradiction and a
partition-invariant reproduction.


F142 / provisional KI#465 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED SUPPORTED-CONFIG TEAM/PLAYER DOMAIN DEFECT
EXCLUSIVE-RADIUS LOST-TILE CACHE IS TEAM-WIDE BUT IS NORMALIZED BY EACH RIVAL
PLAYER'S LAND BEFORE THE INTENDED TEAM-SIZE SPLIT; THE SAME PHYSICAL TILE LOSS
CHANGES WITH TEAM ROSTER PARTITION
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: NEW CURRENT SUPPORTED-CONFIGURATION DEFECT ROOT. Shipped/default SAS uses
`OWN_EXCLUSIVE_RADIUS=0`, but, as established independently for F133, value 1 is
an explicitly documented and maintained AdvCiv configuration rather than an
invented unsupported retuning.

This root is adjacent to F133 because both involve advc.035 flipped-tile loss,
but the defects and repair loci are independent. F133 concerns the OUTER
`netLostRivalAssetScore` numerator/denominator ordering. F142 is already present
INSIDE `lossesFromFlippedTiles` even if that outer ordering is repaired.

PRODUCER CONTRACT -- THE STORED LOST-TILE COUNT IS TEAM-WIDE
-------------------------------------------------------------
`UWAICache::updateLostTilesAtWar()` begins from the cache owner's TEAM:

    CvTeam const& kOwnerTeam = GET_TEAM(m_eOwner);

For every other major team it computes contested plots through:

    contestedPlots(apFlipped, kOwnerTeam.getID(), itOther->getID());

and counts a plot according to its current TEAM owner and the war relation of
those two teams:

    TeamTypes ePlotTeam = apFlipped[j]->getTeam();
    if (ePlotTeam == (kOwnerTeam.isAtWar(itOther->getID()) ?
        itOther->getID() : kOwnerTeam.getID()))
    {
        iLost++;
    }

The resulting value is stored by opposing TeamTypes:

    m_aiPlotsLostAtWar.set(itOther->getID(), iLost);

Nothing in this computation depends on which particular `m_eOwner` player inside
`kOwnerTeam` owns a city, plot, army or share of the team's land. Consequently,
two player caches belonging to the same team store the SAME team-wide
`numPlotsLostAtWar(otherTeam)` value for the same opposing team.

This is not an inferred interpretation. The original advc.035 implementation
introduced the backing array as:

    int lostTilesAtWar[MAX_CIV_TEAMS]; // per team

and current storage remains indexed by TeamTypes.

CONSUMER CONTRACT -- THE AUTHOR ALREADY TRIES TO APPORTION A TEAM QUANTITY
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
`WarUtilityAspect::lossesFromFlippedTiles(eVictim, eTo)` retrieves that cached
team quantity through the current victim player's cache and accumulates it for
relevant war teams. It then says explicitly:

    int const iRivalMembers = kTheirTeam.getNumMembers();
    ...
    // Tiles are counted per team, but this function gets called once per rival player.
    r /= iRivalMembers;

The original advc.035 comment was equivalent and even more direct:

    // Tiles are counted per team, but this is a per-civ function.

So the `/ iRivalMembers` is not a speculative team-game redesign. It is the
original implementation's own normalization contract: one team-wide lost-tile
signal is being consumed once per rival player and therefore needs apportioning.

THE DOMAIN MISMATCH OCCURS BEFORE THAT SPLIT
--------------------------------------------
Before dividing by the member count, however, the helper normalizes the shared
team-wide lost-tile count by the CURRENT RIVAL PLAYER'S own land:

    int iVictimLandTiles = GET_PLAYER(eVictim).getTotalLand();
    r = scaled(125 * iVictimLostTiles,
               std::max(5, iVictimLandTiles));
    r /= iRivalMembers;

`CvPlayer::getTotalLand()` is player-local. By contrast, the matching team-domain
quantity exists directly:

    int CvTeam::getTotalLand(bool bCheckVassals) const
    {
        ...
        return m_iTotalLand + iVassalLand;
    }

and with `bCheckVassals=false` it returns the team's stored aggregate
`m_iTotalLand`.

The code therefore performs:

    (team-wide lost tiles / player-local land) / team members

rather than either of the ownership-consistent alternatives:

* player-local lost tiles / player-local land, or
* team-wide lost tiles / team-wide land, apportioned across per-player callbacks.

DETERMINISTIC EQUAL-PARTITION REPRODUCTION
------------------------------------------
Hold the physical/team state constant:

* the victim side controls 100 total land tiles;
* it would lose 10 contested tiles under OWN_EXCLUSIVE_RADIUS;
* no other inputs change.

Case A -- one-player victim team:

    lost-tile cache = 10
    player land     = 100
    team members    = 1

    score = 125 * 10 / 100 / 1 = 12.5

Case B -- the SAME 100 team land split evenly between teammates B and C:

Each player's UWAICache still stores the SAME team-wide lost count 10, because
`updateLostTilesAtWar` depends only on Team B+C versus the opposing team. Each
player owns 50 land:

    B pass = 125 * 10 / 50 / 2 = 12.5
    C pass = 125 * 10 / 50 / 2 = 12.5

The aspect is evaluated once for B and once for C, so aggregate utility becomes:

    12.5 + 12.5 = 25

The explicit `/ 2` normalization has not normalized the team partition at all;
the halved player-land denominator cancels it. Merely splitting the same team's
land between two members doubles the resulting total flipped-tile severity.

With an even n-member partition, the same algebra makes each member reproduce the
solo severity and the aggregate grows approximately n-fold. With uneven land
shares, the sum instead depends on a harmonic-like combination of the members'
land counts and can be dominated by a small-land teammate -- even though the
numerator is still the same undivided team-wide lost-tile count for every member.

THE SIGNIFICANCE GATE IS PARTITION-SENSITIVE TOO
-------------------------------------------------
Before scoring, the helper also uses:

    if (std::abs(iVictimLostTiles) <= 4 * iRivalMembers)
        return 0;

Again `iVictimLostTiles` is one team-wide physical count. Changing only the
number of player members changes whether the same lost plots are considered
significant at all.

For example, five team-wide lost plots:

* one-member team: 5 > 4, so the loss is scored;
* two-member team: 5 <= 8, so BOTH per-player calls return zero.

Thus roster partition can not only multiply the score after the gate; it can
switch the entire team-wide physical loss on or off before scoring.

ANCESTRY -- PRESENT FROM advc.035 BIRTH; BASE 1.14 IDENTICAL
------------------------------------------------------------
The retained practical-1286 / advc.035 introducing diff adds all components of
the defect together:

* `lostTilesAtWar[MAX_CIV_TEAMS] // per team`;
* team-vs-team contested-plot counting;
* `victimLandTiles = GET_PLAYER(victimId).getTotalLand()`;
* division by `teamSz` with the explicit comment that tiles are counted per team
  while the helper is per civ.

Current SAS and Base AdvCiv 1.14 `lossesFromFlippedTiles` are normalized-text
identical. This is therefore an inherited original-design defect, not an SAS
regression.

SUPPORTED-CONFIGURATION REACHABILITY
------------------------------------
Current GlobalDefines_advc.xml documents OWN_EXCLUSIVE_RADIUS directly:

    [advc.035] If set to 1, tiles that are only within the radius of one city
    belong to the owner of that city regardless of culture. Recommended: 0 ...

The implementation remains wired through CvPlot, CvCity, CitySiteEvaluator,
CvPlayerAI, UWAICache and WarUtilityAspect. As with F133, recommended/default 0
masks the defect in ordinary SAS play, but 1 remains a maintained supported
AdvCiv configuration. This meets the album's supported-config bar.

INDEPENDENCE FROM F133
----------------------
F133 repairs the fact that `netLostRivalAssetScore` freezes `rTotal` before
adding flipped-tile loss to `rNetLoss`. One possible F133 repair is to extend the
outer returned denominator so numerator and denominator remain comparable.

That does NOT change the value returned by `lossesFromFlippedTiles` itself. The
same team-wide 10 lost tiles would still produce 12.5 for a solo 100-land team
and aggregate 25 for two 50-land teammates before entering the repaired outer
asset accounting. F142 therefore survives a complete F133 outer-denominator
repair.

Conversely, repairing F142's ownership domain would not stop F133 from adding the
now-correct flipped-tile score to the numerator after freezing its outer asset
denominator. Both roots must be addressed independently.

COLLISION / ROOT ACCOUNTING
---------------------------
The current reviewed Known-Issues ledger reaches KI#426; no reviewed entry owns
this internal team-wide-lost-tiles / player-land normalization defect. Searches
for OWN_EXCLUSIVE_RADIUS, flipped/lost tiles and the specific helper establish
F133's outer-denominator issue but no existing root for this partition error.

F142 is also not another generic F096 dead-member issue. The equal two-LIVING-
member reproduction above already fails. Using `getNumMembers()` can add an F096
secondary distortion when dead assigned members exist, but replacing it with an
alive count alone does not fix the team/player land mismatch.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Preserve one ownership domain from producer through normalization. Two coherent
architectures are possible:

1. Keep the current TEAM-WIDE cache:
   * normalize the lost-tile count against the victim TEAM's land (normally
     `GET_TEAM(eVictim).getTotalLand(false)` or the equivalent team-domain
     quantity intended by the model),
   * apply the significance threshold in that same team domain,
   * then apportion the resulting team-level utility across the LIVING rival
     members because the aspect still receives one callback per player.

2. Change the producer to attribute lost plots to individual players, then use
   each player's own lost-tile numerator with that same player's land denominator
   and remove the artificial team-wide split.

The first is much smaller and preserves advc.035's explicit "tiles counted per
team" design. Whatever exact tuning is chosen, do not merely replace
`getNumMembers()` with an alive count, and do not treat an F133 outer-denominator
repair as sufficient.

F119 -> F114 ADVERSARIAL REREAD -- ALL REMAIN LIVE
---------------------------------------------------
F119 / KI#442 -- team-indexed capitulation vector written by PlayerTypes

The raw storage mismatch survives exactly. MilitaryAnalyst declares
`vector<TeamSet> m_capitulationsAcceptedPerTeam`, sizes it by MAX_CIV_TEAMS and
exposes it through a TeamTypes accessor. prepareResults nevertheless loops
PlayerTypes ePlayer and writes directly to:

    m_capitulationsAcceptedPerTeam[ePlayer]

Unlike the retracted F113 GET_TEAM syntax, raw std::vector::operator[] has no
type-aware overload that can convert PlayerTypes through TEAMID. InvasionGraph
copies a master team's accepted capitulations into each live member node, so
those player-node sets must be unioned into TEAMID(ePlayer), not scattered into
player-numbered slots. Current source and Base AdvCiv 1.14 still contain the
same line.

F118 / KI#441 -- negative revolt asset value can become positive war utility

Revolts still multiplies a city's possibly-negative cache asset score by a
positive revolt-loss multiplier. Risk in the same file explicitly documents
that per-city asset score can be negative because of maintenance and prevents a
negative expected LOSS from becoming a gain. Revolts has no such protection;
with positive total assets elsewhere, a negative threatened city can make
`rLossesFromRevolts` negative and `m_iU -= rRevoltCost` increase war utility.
The event being modeled is revolt damage/occupation/population harm, not the
voluntary shedding of a maintenance liability. F118 remains independent of
F132's later subset/denominator-order problem.

F117 / KI#440 -- PublicOpposition mixes hypothetical religion anger with current
angryPopulation

The scenario deliberately calls `getReligionPercentAnger(eThey)` for a rival
that the military simulation may make into a FUTURE enemy. The cap is still the
real current city's `angryPopulation`, whose religion-anger construction only
includes ACTUAL current enemies. A currently content city can therefore cap a
hypothetical new-war religion anger contribution to zero. Conversely, separate
enemy passes can reuse the same current angry citizens. The scenario/current-
state domain mismatch remains direct and does not depend on F113.

F116 / KI#439 -- DramaticArc's eight-turn HasMet tolerance masks real short wars

The source still comments that the HasMet counter is "not exact", while
CvTeamAI::AI_doCounter explicitly treats HasMet and atWar as exact counters.
TurnsAtPeace is reset by war and then counts exact peaceful turns. A short recent
war can leave HasMet-TurnsAtPeace < 8 and therefore be classified as if the pair
had always been peaceful. The direct counter lifecycle remains a stronger
contract than any approximate-tuning defense of the hard 8.

F115 / KI#438 -- computed game-speed-normalized peace duration is discarded

ThirdPartyIntervention still computes `rAtPeaceTurns` from GoldenAgePercent and
then never reads it. The long-peace gate and decay continue to use raw
`iAtPeaceTurns`. The normalization equals raw turns only at Normal speed and was
present, unused, from the original aspect introduction. The final dead-local
scan found no second comparable computed-but-unused normalization variable.

F114 / KI#437 -- FairPlay includes target teammates as alleged third parties

The adversarial self-contact challenge remains resolved in FAVOR of F114.
CvGame::initDiplomacy establishes self-contact through `meet(self,false)`, so a
second player on eTheirTeam passes FairPlay's `kTheirTeam.isHasMet(...)` test.
The filter excludes only player ID `eThey`, not the whole eTheirTeam. The target
teammate can therefore inflate the potential-other-enemy denominator and, when
the target team has a war, satisfy `AI_shareWar(ownTeam)` and be logged/subtracted
as an "ally" of its own team. The entire target team must be excluded from the
independent-third-party loop.

No root in F114-F119 was merged or retracted during this challenge.


F112 -> F104 ADVERSARIAL REREAD -- ALL REMAIN LIVE
---------------------------------------------------
F112 / KI#435 -- wrong side used for war-anger per-civ normalization

UWAICache::updateWarAnger still builds the contribution by ENEMY TeamTypes:

    aiAngerContrib[enemyTeam] = ourTeam.getWarWeariness(enemyTeam, true)

and immediately comments:

    // Turn per-team into per-civ

but divides each enemy-team contribution by the OWNER team's getNumMembers().
The consumer is per living enemy player. A solo owner versus two-player enemy
therefore duplicates the same team contribution, while a two-player owner versus
solo enemy can halve it. This is an explicit producer/comment/denominator
contract, not merely a preferred team-game model. The natural split is across
living members of the enemy team; F096 additionally owns dead-member dilution.

F111 / KI#434 -- AP/Diplomacy city-conquest weighting tests wrong player

The loop stores `eCityOwner` and labels the block "Weight for old owner"; its
attitude lookup also uses eCityOwner. The full-membership test in the middle
still asks `kThey.isFullMember(eVS)`, i.e. the conqueror/current rival. Third-
party conquest makes these players genuinely different. The wrong-object test
survives unchanged.

F110 / KI#433 -- KingMaking models team-owned victory candidacy with player state

The direct controls remain CvGame team score and team-owned victory conditions.
KingMaking ranks current/predicted player scores for Time/score leadership and
uses individual population to decide whether a team-derived Domination
trajectory has been thwarted. Its set<PlayerTypes> winner representation can
also count two members of one winning team as two competitors. This is not a
blanket request to replace all player inputs: culture and several heuristics are
legitimately player-local. The proven team-owned victory-state portions remain
mis-modeled.

F109 / KI#432 -- theirRelativeLoss iterates allies but reuses current rival

`theirRelativeLoss` still loops `eTheirAlly`, but both ordinary ally/vassal and
new-vassal branches call `netLostRivalAssetScore(...)`, whose implicit victim is
current aspect opponent eThey and which has no eTheirAlly parameter. The loop
therefore reuses eThey's assets/losses for teammates and vassals. Predicted new
vassals also retain the coupled full-weight-vs-half-weight error. The wrong-
object construction is unchanged.

F108 / KI#431 -- varargs mismatch

The live call remains:

    log("Attitude level towards %s: %d, refusal thresh: %d",
        m_kReport.leaderName(eThey), towardThem());

Three conversions, two arguments. A balanced scan of every log(...) call in
WarUtilityAspect.cpp found no second format/argument-count mismatch. F108 remains
one bounded inherited C/C++ varargs defect.

F107 / KI#430 -- PreEmptiveWar present/predicted side construction mismatch

The rival side still includes an existing vassal at half weight in both current
and predicted states. Our side initializes a team-wide current and predicted city
base, then adds an existing vassal only to `rOurCurrentCities`; it adds only a NEW
predicted capitulation to `rOurPredictedCities`. Thus an unchanged existing
vassal disappears from our future side. The team-wide base also subtracts losses
of only current eWe. F137 later proves an independent repeated team-threat
problem; repairing F137 does not repair this present-vs-future construction.

F106 / KI#429 -- adjusted best score compared against raw candidates

The first pass still adds commerce/tech strength and possible 4/3 peaceful-
overseas-victory weighting before updating `rBestScore`. The second pass still
divides raw predicted/current player score by that adjusted rBestScore. The
player that established the adjusted maximum can therefore fail its own 70/75%
cutoff. This candidate was briefly rediscovered late in the audit and correctly
recognized as F106 rather than assigned a new number.

F105 / KI#428 -- exact Domination population threshold equality

The real CvGame victory test fails population only when:

    100 * teamPopulation < totalPopulation * adjustedPopulationPercent

so equality satisfies the population requirement. WarUtility instead treats the
component as completed only for `iPopToGo < 0`; equality (`iPopToGo == 0`) enters
the unfinished branch and divides by iPopToGo. ScaledNum's Win32 MulDiv backend
means the release symptom need not be a native integer trap; that nuance does not
repair the semantic boundary. Equality belongs in the already-satisfied branch.

F104 / KI#427 -- first-four resource cap has both boundary and unit errors

Current code still says "Count only the first four resource trades", increments
before testing `>= 4`, and therefore keeps only three resource-containing deals.
It also reduces all resource TradeData items in one deal to one boolean
`bWeReceiveResource`, even though Civ4 can bundle and process several
TRADE_RESOURCES items in one deal. The cap therefore both rejects the fourth
resource-containing deal and counts bundled resource ITEMS in the wrong unit.
No current-source change from KI#426's technology threshold repair touches this
trade-deal defect.

No root in F104-F112 was merged or retracted during this challenge.

F101 / reviewed KI#424

WarUtilityAspect::evaluate now snapshots `iPriorUtility`, computes this member's
raw delta, applies the XML aspect weight only to `iMemberUtility`, restores:

    m_iU = iPriorUtility + iMemberUtility

and returns only that member's weighted contribution. Earlier members are not
reweighted again. This matches the reused-aspect-object team architecture and
also fixes the per-player diagnostic total.

F102 / reviewed KI#425

Risk owns one `m_bSASContactGateEvaluated` latch per aspect/scenario. The hard
contact gate executes once and scans every alive MemberIter of eOurTeam. Land
