F120 -> F142 POST-WIP31 ADVERSARIAL STATUS
------------------------------------------
The newer block had already received repeated pairwise/team/state challenges
through WIP12-WIP31. The final closure pass rechecked the producer/consumer
contracts rather than merely rereading the prose. No root was retracted or
merged.

Key hard controls that remain decisive:

* F120/KI#443 FairPlay start-turn: CvGame::setStartTurnYear creates the ordinary
  later-era getStartTurn baseline from total game turns and StartPercent, while
  FairPlay separately subtracts StartPercent. The historical nonzero-start fix
  therefore conflates extra start delay with ordinary later-era position.
* F121/KI#444 terminal-era startup clock: KingMaking and UWAICache threat use
  `currentEra <= startEra` as a TEMPORARY early-game reliability gate. Future is
  terminal, so the gate has no exit for a Future-era start.
* F122/KI#445 TacticalSituation: one physical agent unit/city can be reused in
  rival-player-specific engagement, exposure and evacuation accounting across
  teammates. The repair locus is physical asset deduplication, not global
  teamification of every tactical input.
* F123/KI#446 Bellicosity: the historical anti-third-party loss budget is the
  same agent loss amount but resets separately for each target member.
* F124/KI#447 ThirdParty severity: intervention probability already uses team
  danger/power, while the nonlinear <=50% severity gate is built from ordinary
  member-local ARMY power on BOTH war sides. Ordinary teammates are omitted.
* F125/KI#448 DramaticArc: a human member's explicit safety return can be bypassed
  by the AI teammate pass for the same team-wide war; the too-little-action gate
  has the same player partition.
* F126/KI#449 Distraction: team-war duration/alternative-war opportunity cost,
  including a fixed +5.5 actual-war-plan nudge, can be recharged per target
  member. The later winning-war SAS cap does not normalize that inherited root.
* F127/KI#450 MilitaryVictory: Domination/Diplomacy global remaining thresholds
  are independently capped/completed per player/member pass. Conquest also
  returns 1 when one rival PLAYER is eliminated although CvGame::testVictory
  requires every other non-vassal TEAM to have zero cities; full completion can
  repeat across agent members too.
* F128/KI#451 HiredHand: sponsorAgainst/bountyAgainst and obligation age are
  explicitly target-TeamTypes state but are consumed once per target member.
* F129/KI#452 vassal current-tech score: technology ownership/transfer is team-
  owned; member caches can hold the same current technology value and
  acceptVassal explicitly sums them. Resource score is a negative control because
  resource availability is player-owned.
* F130/KI#453 Risk: team-owned capitulation/vassal costs are emitted through
  member/rival callbacks. The fixed 100 capitulation cost gives an exact 2-v-2
  multiplication reproduction.
* F131/KI#454 GreedForSpace: AI city sites are stored independently per player and
  teammates can recommend the exact same plotNum; one physical plot then becomes
  two orphaned expansion sites if both members disappear. Distinct plots remain
  legitimately additive.
* F132/KI#455 Revolts: persistent m_countedCities spans rival passes but numerator
  and denominator reset locally each evaluate call. Overlapping primary areas
  make the result dependent on which rival player is iterated first.
* F133/KI#456 supported OWN_EXCLUSIVE_RADIUS=1: netLostRivalAssetScore freezes the
  returned total-assets denominator before adding flipped-tile loss to the
  numerator; Assistance's explicit `FAssert(r <= 1)` can then be violated.
* F134/KI#457 IllWill: revenge military capability is tested by nonlinear
  thresholds using current player army power despite a revenge declaration being
  a team war. Real CvTeamAI war valuation uses team power; attitude/motivation
  can remain player-specific.
* F135/KI#458 ThirdParty decisive-target shortcut: one proxy tests only the
  target team's pre-simulation leader PLAYER; the other accepts any capitulation
  anywhere in the simulated network, not necessarily the current target.
* F136/KI#459 partnerUtilFromTech: near-future technology opportunity is derived
  from team ownership/research and one tech trade changes the whole team, yet the
  same opportunity can be counted for B and teammate C. Player-owned trade-route,
  resource and deal terms are negative controls.
* F137/KI#460 PreEmptiveWar: player-keyed threatRating resolves to the same
  teamThreat for teammates, and the aspect reconstructs the same full master-
  team/vassal city side again, producing an exact duplicate team-threat utility.
  This is independent of F107's present/predicted side construction.
* F138/KI#461 Tactical evalOperational: the branch explicitly evaluates OUR
  readiness for the one target TEAM but is entered once for each reachable target
  member. The same preparation/readiness cost can therefore repeat.
* F139/KI#462 IllWill evalAngeredPartners: MilitaryAnalyst records wars-declared-
  by as PlayerTypes, so one target-team DoW yields B and C; the real
  AI_preDeclareWar path creates one declared-war-on-friend memory per victim
  TEAM. Deduplication must be by victim team, while genuinely separate cascaded
  victim teams remain separate.
* F140/KI#463 GreedForVassals: the fixed -5 capitulated-vassal diplomatic/forced-
  war downside represents one team vassal relationship. Real rival-vassal
  attitude iterates vassal teams and their aggregate cities, but the fixed proxy
  is charged once per vassal member. Player-owned vassal benefits stay additive.
* F141/KI#464 C++ lifetime: WarUtilityAspect is polymorphic but has no virtual
  destructor; WarEvaluator allocates derived aspects and deletes them through
  WarUtilityAspect*. KingMaking/Revolts own std::set members requiring real
  derived destruction. This is standard C++ undefined behavior and survives from
  the original advc.104 hierarchy. C++03-compatible repair: public
  `virtual ~WarUtilityAspect() {}`.
* F142/KI#465 supported OWN_EXCLUSIVE_RADIUS=1: lost tiles are explicitly cached
  per TEAM and then, inside a per-player helper, normalized by current PLAYER land
  before dividing by team size. Equal partition of the same physical team land
  doubles aggregate severity; the significance threshold is roster-partition
  sensitive too. F133's outer denominator repair does not fix this internal
  producer/denominator domain mismatch.

The low-level ScaledNum check changed only consequence wording for zero divisors;
it did not invalidate any of these semantic boundaries.

CHANGED-METHOD CLASSIFICATION -- NO F143 ESTABLISHED
----------------------------------------------------

1. clearUnits / deleteUnitNode -- EXISTING KI#163 HARDENING

Current clearUnits deliberately no longer tears a whole group down by repeatedly invoking
the normal single-unit deleteUnitNode callback path. It directly resets group-owned
activity/automation/mission state and then clears m_units once. deleteUnitNode separately
adds a null-node guard while preserving its ordinary single-unit-removal behavior.

This is exactly the independently documented KI#163 rare group-teardown crash hardening.
The Known Issues entry explicitly describes the same re-entrancy/lifetime concern and the
same direct-full-teardown repair. Do not duplicate it as a new file-015 finding.

2. getEspionageUnit / startMission MISSION_ESPIONAGE -- EXISTING KI#398 FIX

Current source adds getEspionageUnit(), which returns the first selected unit that can
currently perform Espionage. startMission's MISSION_ESPIONAGE case also skips a selected
unit that cannot currently perform Espionage before allowing the eligible Spy to try.

This is exactly independently reviewed/fixed KI#398: inherited BtS group-Espionage actor
identity could expose a valid Spy mission but let an earlier movable non-Spy abort it.
Callers in help/popup code use the same centralized actor helper. No new root here.

3. doTurn -- WORKER DIAGNOSTICS + SAFE STATIC DEFINE CACHE

The material additions are level-3 Worker diagnostics around turn-boundary group state and
a static-local cache of MIN_TIMER_UNIT_DOUBLE_MOVES. The diagnostic reads/logs state but
does not mutate gameplay state.

A repository-wide runtime-define-setter scan found no setter for
MIN_TIMER_UNIT_DOUBLE_MOVES. Current runtime setDefineINT/FLOAT/STRING calls modify other
names (camera/minimap/map-generation defines). Caching this define therefore does not
currently freeze a dynamically mutated supported value. No behavioral defect established.

4. groupBuild -- SAFE COLOR LOOKUP HOIST

Current source caches GC.getColorType("WHITE") in a static local and uses the result in the
same UI message. This is a lookup of fixed XML type identity, not a mutable GlobalDefine.
No gameplay/UI semantic change established.

5. continueMission_bulk -- THREE DISTINCT CLASSES, ALL ACCOUNTED FOR SO FAR

(a) Level-3 Worker execution diagnostics are observational.

(b) The stale AI build-target guard is already present in the local AdvCiv 1.14 comparison
source and is independently documented as KI#176 in SAS history. MISSION_BUILD stores a
build type but no target coordinates, so non-route builds are canceled if the group is no
longer on AI_getMissionAIPlot. This prevents a stale queued build from executing on the
wrong physical plot.

(c) Current SAS additionally preserves a queued follow-up after a MISSION_BUILD consumes
all Worker movement:

    if (missionData.eMissionType != MISSION_BUILD || readyForMission())
        activateHeadMission();
    else setActivityType(ACTIVITY_MISSION);

Practical 6018 introduced this deliberately after observed Berlin/Beijing/Cologne feature-
removal follow-ups were discarded: immediate activation deleted the queued improvement,
while simply doing nothing left the group AWAKE and exposed it to AI turn-start cleanup.
The current branch instead keeps the waiting follow-up in MISSION activity until a later
turn. The original short-circuit semantics around groupBuild remain preserved, and current
history documents this as an empirically validated Worker reliability change. No current
contract failure has been established from it in this opening pass.

6. read -- REMOVED LEGACY SAVE MIGRATION ONLY

write() still writes uiFlag=3 and serializes, in order:

    ID, mission timer, force-update, owner, activity, automation,
    unit list, known-enemy list, current MissionData queue.

Current read() consumes exactly that current-format sequence. Relative to Base 1.14 it
removes only old uiFlag migration branches (pre-knownEnemies saves, MissionDataLegacy,
and pre-v3 MOVE_ROUTE_TO conversion).

This matches the project's already-established serialization policy from earlier file
reviews: same-version current read/write pairing is authoritative; cross-version save
migration is not a supported requirement. No same-version misalignment established.

7. groupPathTo / groupRoadTo / updateTimers -- FALSE CHANGE SIGNALS

The robust token/body comparison finds no executable difference at all. They remain Base
AdvCiv 1.14 behavior in current source after comment/format normalization.

C015-WIP02 APPEND -- F143 / Sea Patrol mixed-group persistence contract
================================================================================

F143 / provisional KI#466 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED ADVCIV SEA-PATROL GROUP DEFECT
MIXED SEA GROUP CAN ACCEPT PATROL, THEN AN INELIGIBLE MEMBER WAKES THE WHOLE GROUP
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: NEW CURRENT DEFECT ROOT, inherited from the interaction created by AdvCiv
advc.004k. Static reachability/data evidence strong; no runtime game test performed by
this audit.

Mission-availability contract:

CvSelectionGroup::canDoMission(MISSION_SEAPATROL) treats the order as valid when at least
one member can Sea Patrol. With the ordinary canStartMission path bCheckMoves is false, so
once a qualifying member is found the function returns true immediately. An earlier
non-qualifying member is tolerated so long as it can still move.

    if (!bValid && pUnit->canSeaPatrol(pPlot, true))
    {
        if (!bCheckMoves)
            return true;
        bValid = true;
    }
    if (!pUnit->canMove())
        return false;

CvSelectionGroup::startMission then handles MISSION_SEAPATROL as a WHOLE-GROUP activity:

    setActivityType(ACTIVITY_PATROL);
    bDelete = true;

Unlike MISSION_AIRPATROL and MISSION_PARADROP, Sea Patrol does not collect unsuitable
members into apUnitsLeftBehind and does not split them from the group. The mission node is
deleted, but the mixed selection group remains intact in ACTIVITY_PATROL.

Turn-boundary contradiction:

CvUnit::isSeaPatrolling() is group-activity based. Every sea-domain member of such a group
therefore reports itself as Sea Patrolling regardless of whether that unit individually
satisfies CvUnit::canSeaPatrol:

    getGroup()->getActivityType() == ACTIVITY_PATROL &&
    getDomainType() == DOMAIN_SEA

CvUnit::doTurn then contains AdvCiv's advc.004k validity cleanup:

    if (isSeaPatrolling() && !canSeaPatrol())
        getGroup()->setActivityType(ACTIVITY_AWAKE);

The default canSeaPatrol call here deliberately ignores the current activity, but still
rejects a sea unit that cannot fight, is OnlyDefensive, is on an invalid patrol plot, etc.
Consequently one ineligible companion wakes the ENTIRE selection group, terminating the
persistent patrol of the member that made the group command legal in the first place.

Current-data supported reproduction:

- CvUnit::canJoinGroup permits units to join when owner, plot and DOMAIN match; it does not
  require common mission capability.
- UNIT_DESTROYER is DOMAIN_SEA, combat-capable and not OnlyDefensive, and can satisfy Sea
  Patrol on a normal valid water plot near a guardable owned water improvement.
- UNIT_TRANSPORT is DOMAIN_SEA but current XML has bOnlyDefensive=1, so canSeaPatrol rejects
  it.
- UNIT_WORKBOAT is also DOMAIN_SEA and has iCombat=0, so canSeaPatrol rejects it.

Thus a human can form e.g. Destroyer + Transport (or Destroyer + Work Boat), with both
members still able to move, on a valid patrol plot. The qualifying Destroyer makes
MISSION_SEAPATROL available and startMission sets the whole mixed group to PATROL. At the
next unit turn, the Transport/Work Boat satisfies isSeaPatrolling() by group activity but
fails canSeaPatrol(), so its doTurn changes the whole group's activity to AWAKE. The valid
Destroyer silently loses its patrol after only that turn boundary.

Ancestry/control:

- Civ4CE/BtS already uses the broad group-availability shape where one qualifying unit can
  expose Sea Patrol.
- AdvCiv practical 3866 / ffbe05255f, title "Usability improvements for Sea Patrol"
  (advc.004k), introduced the per-unit doTurn wake when a patrolling unit no longer passes
  canSeaPatrol and changed the availability query to ignore the current patrol activity
  appropriately when displaying the command.
- The commit's stated intent was to make Sea Patrol available only when there is actually
  something to guard and to improve patrol visibility/usability. It did not add mixed-
  member separation or change the inherited any-member group availability rule.
- Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS practical 6267 both retain the resulting interaction.
- No existing KI or earlier audit finding mentioning Sea Patrol/ACTIVITY_PATROL collides
  with this root.

Why this is not merely a UI/tuning preference:

The same group-level API first says the order is executable and places the group in a
persistent activity, then a member that was explicitly tolerated by that availability
contract invalidates the persistent state for the qualifying member. Repartitioning the
same selected ships into two groups makes the valid warship patrol persist; grouping them
causes it to stop despite a successful accepted command.

Repair direction:

Reconcile mission availability, group activity and turn-boundary cleanup. Plausible
repairs include:

1. At mission start, split unsuitable Sea Patrol members from the patrol group, analogous
   to Air Patrol's apUnitsLeftBehind handling; or
2. Require every member of a group to be individually Sea-Patrol-capable before accepting
   the group mission (less friendly for mixed escort groups); or
3. Keep mixed groups intact, but make the doTurn cleanup wake the group only when NO member
   remains able to Sea Patrol rather than when the current member cannot.

Any repair should preserve advc.004k's intended wake when the patrol as a whole is no
longer meaningful (e.g. no reachable guarded improvement), rather than simply deleting the
validity cleanup.

C015-WIP03 APPEND -- CvSelectionGroup.cpp persistent blockade lifecycle
===============================================================================

F144 / provisional KI#467 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED ADVCIV BLOCKADE GROUP DEFECT
ONE FORMER BLOCKADER BECOMING INVALID WAKES/CANCELS STILL-VALID GROUP BLOCKADERS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: NEW CURRENT INHERITED DEFECT ROOT. Independent of F143/KI#466.

Root contract:
- Blockade state is legitimately unit-local (`CvUnit::m_bBlockading`), while the
  waiting/activity state is group-local (`ACTIVITY_PLUNDER`).
- `CvUnit::doTurn` was changed by advc.033 so a blockading unit that can no longer
  legally plunder clears its own flag and wakes its group:

      if (isBlockading())
      {
          if (canPlunder(kPlot))
              collectBlockadeGold();
          else
          {
              setBlockading(false);
              getGroup()->setActivityType(ACTIVITY_AWAKE);
          }
      }

- `CvSelectionGroup::setActivityType` always calls `setBlockading(false)` before
  changing activity. The group helper applies that call to EVERY member.
- Therefore one former blockader becoming invalid does not merely wake/remove that
  unit's blockade; it clears every still-valid member's blockade too.

Concrete supported current-data reproduction:
1. Human groups a Destroyer and Privateer on the same valid water plot during war.
   `CvUnit::canJoinGroup` requires only same owner/plot/domain; hidden nationality
   and blockade eligibility are not grouping restrictions.
2. Current UNIT_DESTROYER and UNIT_PRIVATEER are both DOMAIN_SEA and bPillage=1.
   During the war both can pass `canPlunder` and MISSION_PLUNDER calls `plunder()`
   on each member, setting each unit's own m_bBlockading=true.
3. Peace is then made while the group remains on a legal neutral/unowned blockade
   plot. `CvTeam::makePeace` calls `updatePlunder(-1,false)` before changing war
   state and `updatePlunder(1,false)` afterward, but these calls only rebuild the
   blockade-count effects; they do NOT clear m_bBlockading or separate the group.
4. After peace, Destroyer can no longer plunder because it is not a pirate and the
   owner team has no wars. Privateer remains eligible because current XML gives it
   bHiddenNationality=1 and bAlwaysHostile=1; `canPlunder` deliberately exempts a
   pirate from the no-war rejection (subject to the ordinary plot restrictions).
5. When the Destroyer reaches CvUnit::doTurn, advc.033 detects that its existing
   blockade is no longer legal. It clears the Destroyer's local flag, then wakes
   the whole selection group.
6. The group wake calls CvSelectionGroup::setBlockading(false), which clears the
   still-valid Privateer's blockade as well. If the Privateer had not been grouped
   with the Destroyer, its blockade would legally persist after peace.

The result therefore depends on grouping unrelated persistent blockaders: one unit
whose legal state changes can terminate another member's still-valid blockade.
This is not merely visual/activity UI state; the Privateer's actual blockade flag
and plot blockade effects are removed.

Ancestry:
- Civ4/BtS already has unit-local blockade state and group PLUNDER activity.
- AdvCiv change advc.033 (visible in the local practical-1407 ancestry diff and in
  Base AdvCiv history) added the `canPlunder` recheck in CvUnit::doTurn and, on
  failure, `setBlockading(false); group->setActivityType(ACTIVITY_AWAKE);`.
- The corresponding history explicitly says non-Privateers can no longer blockade
  when at peace with everyone and "blockading units are awoken if a blockade is no
  longer allowed" so forgotten ships stop blockading after war.
- That intent is sound for the invalid unit, but the inherited group-wide wake
  also clears other members whose blockade remains allowed.
- Base AdvCiv 1.14 and practical-6267 SAS retain this interaction.

Why this is separate from F143/KI#466:
- F143 Sea Patrol accepts a mixed group where some members were NEVER individually
  eligible, represents patrol through one group activity, and then lets an
  ineligible companion interpret itself as patrolling and wake everybody.
- F144 Blockade starts with multiple individually valid per-unit blockades. The
  failure occurs later when eligibility diverges and one unit's correct local
  invalidation is escalated into group-wide blockade cancellation.
- Fixing Sea Patrol mission admission/splitting does not repair this blockade
  lifecycle, and fixing this lifecycle does not repair F143's initial mixed-group
  patrol contract.

Repair direction:
- Preserve advc.033's requirement that an invalid former blockader stop blockading.
- Do not wake/clear the whole PLUNDER group merely because one member becomes
  invalid while another member can still legally maintain a blockade.
- One conservative shape is: clear the invalid unit's local blockade, then wake the
  group only if no remaining member is still blockading/can legally plunder;
  otherwise separate the invalid unit or preserve the valid members' PLUNDER state.
- Be careful that `setActivityType(ACTIVITY_AWAKE)` itself clears every member's
  blockade, so simply moving that call without changing its condition is not
  sufficient.

C015-WIP04 APPEND -- CvSelectionGroup.cpp COMMAND_LOAD shared-capacity contract
================================================================================

F145 / provisional KI#468 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED ADVCIV GROUP-LOAD DEFECT
THE ALL-SELECTED LOAD PRECHECK REUSES THE SAME FREE CARGO SLOT FOR EACH UNIT
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: NEW CURRENT INHERITED DEFECT ROOT. Static UI/executor reproduction strong;
no runtime game test performed by this audit.

Intended AdvCiv contract is explicit:

CvSelectionGroup::canDoCommand normally accepts a group command when ANY selected
unit can execute it. `COMMAND_LOAD` is deliberately special-cased by advc.123c:

    if (pUnit->canDoCommand(...))
    {
        if (eCommand != COMMAND_LOAD)
            return true;
    }
    /* Normally, a group can do a command if any unit can do it,
       but in the case of loading, it seems easier to make an exception than
       to have the load command fail for some of the selected units. */
    else if (eCommand == COMMAND_LOAD)
        return false;
    ...
    return (eCommand == COMMAND_LOAD);

Thus `COMMAND_LOAD` is accepted only if every selected/group unit individually
passes `CvUnit::canDoCommand(COMMAND_LOAD)`.

The individual check is not a group-capacity reservation:

- CvUnit::canDoCommand(COMMAND_LOAD) calls `canLoadOntoAnyUnit(getPlot(), ...)`.
- `canLoadOntoAnyUnit` returns true as soon as it finds one transport for which
  `canLoadOnto` succeeds.
- `canLoadOnto` in turn tests the transport's CURRENT
  `cargoSpaceAvailable(specialCargo, domainCargo)`.
- Repeating that independent query for the next selected unit does not reserve
  the slot that the previous unit would consume.

Therefore several selected cargo units can all answer "yes" by pointing at the
same one remaining cargo slot.

Concrete supported reproduction:

1. Put one friendly sea transport on a plot with exactly one compatible free
   cargo slot (for example a normal multi-slot transport already carrying all
   but one of its capacity).
2. Put two movable compatible land units on the same plot and select/group both.
3. Before execution, unit A's `canLoadOntoAnyUnit` sees the one free slot and
   returns true. Unit B independently sees that SAME unchanged slot and also
   returns true. The special group `COMMAND_LOAD` test therefore succeeds even
   though the transport cannot carry both selected units.
4. The UI handles generic Load through `BUTTONPOPUP_LOADUNIT`. With only one
   eligible transport, `launchLoadUnitPopup` auto-selects that transport and
   sends `GAMEMESSAGE_DO_COMMAND, COMMAND_LOAD_UNIT` without requiring a choice.
5. `CvGame::selectionListGameNetMessage(GAMEMESSAGE_DO_COMMAND, ...)` iterates
   every selected unit and sends the command sequentially.
6. Unit A executes first and fills the final slot. Unit B then revalidates
   `COMMAND_LOAD_UNIT`; `cargoSpaceAvailable` is now zero, so its command fails.

The result is a partial load from a command whose AdvCiv group-level exception
was introduced specifically to avoid a load command failing for some selected
units.

The same root can occur with multiple transports or special-cargo constraints:
checking that each selected unit has *some* individually legal destination does
not prove that a simultaneous assignment of all selected units to the finite
transport slots exists. The one-transport/one-free-slot/two-unit example is the
minimal deterministic reproduction.

Popup-target contract strengthens the proof:

`launchLoadUnitPopup` lists a candidate transport when

    pSelectionGroup->canDoCommand(COMMAND_LOAD_UNIT,
        pUnit->getOwner(), pUnit->getID())

is true. Unlike the special generic `COMMAND_LOAD` branch,
`COMMAND_LOAD_UNIT` uses the ordinary ANY-member group rule. Thus even when the
Load button's preliminary test happens to have enough aggregate capacity spread
across several ships, the popup can still offer a particular transport that can
load only a subset of the selection and then issue that target command to all
selected units.

Ancestry/control:

- Vanilla/BtS/Civ4CE already has the ordinary per-unit loading/execution model.
- AdvCiv advc.123c added the current all-selected `COMMAND_LOAD` exception and
  the move-left loading restriction. The local pre-SAS history contains the
  exact introducing comment quoted above.
- Base AdvCiv 1.14 and practical-6267 SAS retain the independent per-unit
  precheck plus ordinary ANY-member `COMMAND_LOAD_UNIT` popup filtering.
- The earlier C006/CvDLLWidgetData closure had recorded "Load deliberately
  requires all selected units to be loadable" as a negative control. F145 does
  not contradict the local statement that each unit is checked; it overturns
  the stronger implicit conclusion that those independent checks guarantee an
  all-units load. Shared finite cargo capacity was not reserved in that earlier
  pass.
- No reviewed KI or earlier F-root found in the current ledger covers this
  shared-capacity feasibility failure.

Why this is not merely UI preference:

The source states the desired group semantic explicitly: avoid a Load command
that succeeds for only part of the selected units. The implemented precondition
is mathematically insufficient for that stated goal because each unit is tested
against the same unconsumed capacity. The deterministic one-slot/two-unit case
violates the comment without relying on AI tuning, unusual XML or stale state.

Repair direction:

- Make group Load feasibility capacity-aware rather than checking each unit in
  isolation. For a generic Load command, reserve compatible transport slots
  while validating the selected units (potentially an assignment/matching
  problem when transports have different special/domain cargo restrictions).
- For `COMMAND_LOAD_UNIT`, offer/accept a target transport for a multi-unit
  selection only when that transport can accommodate every selected unit that
  the command is supposed to load; alternatively make partial loading explicit
  in UI/semantics instead of claiming the all-selected invariant.
- Preserve advc.123c's separate rule that land cargo must have movement left at
  command time, including its first-check/after-move nuance.

F146 / provisional KI#469 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED K-MOD / ADVCIV UI-LIFECYCLE DEFECT
SLEEPING-SPY MAX-BONUS WAKE TESTS ONLY THE GROUP HEAD, SO A GROUPED NON-HEAD SPY NEVER WAKES
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Root contract:
- K-Mod practical 1243 / commit 85efabbf9f is explicitly titled
  "Sleeping spies now wake when they reach their maximum bonus."
- Its CvSelectionGroup::doTurn implementation deliberately checks the wake before
  CvUnit::doTurn increments fortify turns, so a sleeping Spy at
  MAX_FORTIFY_TURNS - 1 is awakened exactly as it reaches the capped stationary
  espionage preparation bonus.
- Current Base AdvCiv 1.14 and SAS retain the same implementation and even the
  explicit limitation in the source comment: "I'm only checking the head unit."

Current implementation:

    if (isHuman() && getActivityType() == ACTIVITY_SLEEP)
    {
        if (pHeadUnit->isSpy() && pHeadUnit->getPlot().getTeam() != getTeam())
        {
            if (pHeadUnit->getFortifyTurns() ==
                GC.getDefineINT(CvGlobals::MAX_FORTIFY_TURNS) - 1)
            {
                setActivityType(ACTIVITY_AWAKE);
            }
        }
    }

Why a real Spy can be outside that test:
- CvUnit::canJoinGroup permits same-owner, same-plot units of the same domain to
  group; it has no Spy-vs-combat-unit exclusion.
- MISSION_SLEEP is a group mission exposed when ANY member passes canSleep(). A
  Spy is not fortifyable and therefore canSleep(); startMission then sets the
  WHOLE selection group to ACTIVITY_SLEEP.
- CvSelectionGroup::addUnit orders members by descending AI_groupFirstVal.
  UNITAI_SPY has first value 9. Current UNIT_SWORDSMAN / UNIT_MACEMAN default to
  UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY, whose first value is 13-19 depending combat capability;
  UNIT_AXEMAN defaults to UNITAI_ATTACK and likewise outranks a Spy in ordinary
  cases. Thus an escort can deterministically be the group head while the Spy is
  a later member.
- Such same-owner land units can coexist and group in a foreign open-borders plot.

Concrete reproduction:
1. Human Spy and Swordsman/Maceman share a foreign open-borders plot and are
   grouped. The attack-city escort sorts ahead of UNITAI_SPY and is group head.
2. The Spy makes MISSION_SLEEP available; the command sets the whole group to
   ACTIVITY_SLEEP.
3. Each stationary, non-cargo unit independently increments its fortify turns in
   CvUnit::doTurn, and setFortifyTurns caps the value at MAX_FORTIFY_TURNS.
4. The espionage mission cost modifier uses the ACTING Spy's own fortify turns:

       iModifier *= 100 - pSpyUnit->getFortifyTurns() *
           ESPIONAGE_EACH_TURN_UNIT_COST_DECREASE;

5. At the turn boundary where the Spy has MAX_FORTIFY_TURNS - 1, the group-level
   convenience check looks only at the non-Spy escort head. It therefore does not
   wake the group.
6. The Spy's own doTurn increments/caps it at the maximum stationary bonus, but
   the group remains asleep. The advertised K-Mod wake behavior can remain absent
   indefinitely until some unrelated wake condition occurs.

This is not an espionage-mission actor-selection duplicate:
- KI#398 repairs choosing/reacquiring the acting Spy for MISSION_ESPIONAGE and its
  popup chain.
- F146 occurs before any espionage mission is selected and concerns the persistent
  sleeping-group lifecycle after a non-head Spy reaches its stationary bonus.

Ancestry:
- K-Mod practical 1243 / 85efabbf9f introduced the feature and the head-only test
  together.
- Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains it; current SAS retains it unchanged apart from nearby
  logging/formatting changes.

Consequence:
- The human convenience feature fails for a supported mixed land group, so the
  player may leave a fully prepared Spy asleep instead of receiving the intended
  wake/reminder at maximum discount.
- This is primarily a UI/usability defect rather than an AI-strength defect, but
  its promised behavior and deterministic current-data reproduction are strong.

Repair direction:
- While a human group is ACTIVITY_SLEEP, scan all members for a Spy in foreign
  territory whose fortify turns equal MAX_FORTIFY_TURNS - 1; wake the group when
  any such Spy reaches the threshold.
- Alternatively split/wake only the qualifying Spy if preserving the escort's
  sleep is preferable, but that is a larger behavior change.
- Preserve the pre-CvUnit::doTurn timing so the notification/wake still occurs
  exactly as the qualifying Spy reaches the capped bonus.


CARGO / AMPHIBIOUS / SPLIT-MERGE NEGATIVE CONTROLS
---------------------------------------------------
1. getLandCargoGroups duplicate group pointers are inefficient but currently inert.
   - The helper appends one group pointer per land cargo UNIT rather than
     deduplicating groups. handleBoarded can therefore put the same group into
     aAwake more than once and eventually call mergeIntoGroup on itself.
   - CvUnit::joinGroup immediately returns when the destination is the unit's
     existing group.
   - mergeIntoGroup's only other potentially behavioral branch changes UnitAI when
     a source member has greater AI_groupFirstVal than the target head. addUnit
     maintains descending AI_groupFirstVal ordering, so no member of a group can
     outrank its own head under the tested invariant.
   - Result: self-merge is wasted traversal / robustness cleanup, not a current
     gameplay defect. Do not allocate F147 for it.

2. setTransportUnit split-by-head-capacity did not yield a shipped-data defect.
   - The only C++ selection-group caller is CvUnitAI::AI_load.
   - Current AI_load callers are land-unit loading paths targeting ordinary
     land-domain transports. Those ships use SpecialCargo=NONE and accept the
     relevant land members, so the feared case where splitGroup selects members
     incompatible with the head-compatible capacity could not be established in
     current supported data/callers.
   - Specialized Carrier/Missile cargo restrictions apply to DOMAIN_AIR and are
     not reached by this land AI_load family.

3. groupAmphibMove already deduplicates cargo groups.
   - K-Mod explicitly repaired the old per-cargo-carrying-unit repetition by
     collecting distinct CvSelectionGroup pointers with std::find.
   - It requires each cargo group canAllMove before issuing the landing mission.
     Ordinary groupMove then peels units that cannot enter the actual destination
     into behind-groups, which is the intended general movement behavior rather
     than a stale-pointer/cargo-group failure.

4. canCargoAllMove matches its current transport-AI consumers.
   - It checks every LAND cargo unit whose transport belongs to this entire sea
     selection group, not merely cargo of one head ship; the K-Mod comment states
     that this whole-group replacement was intentional.
   - Current ferry/assault/missionary/spy-sea callers use it as a readiness gate
     before moving/landing the transport group. No contradictory per-ship contract
     was established.

5. splitGroup / mergeIntoGroup linked-list mutation is structurally safe in the
   reviewed core paths.
   - FOR_EACH_UNIT_VAR_IN caches the next CLinkList node before executing the loop
     body specifically so deleting/moving the current unit is safe.
   - splitGroup reserves representation for the old head AI in the remainder and
     the requested new head AI in the split group; current ppOtherGroup callers
     either initialize their pointer or do not request it.
   - No current iterator invalidation, empty-remainder dereference, or head-loss
     root was established in this pass.

C015-WIP06 APPEND -- CvSelectionGroup.cpp sentry actor-semantics audit
===============================================================================

F147 / provisional KI#470 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED BTS/ADVCIV SENTRY HOSTILITY-ACTOR MISMATCH
SENTRY ALERT BORROWS ONE MAX-RANGE UNIT'S ALWAYS-HOSTILE SEMANTICS FOR THE WHOLE GROUP
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: NEW CURRENT INHERITED GAMEPLAY/UI-LIFECYCLE DEFECT ROOT. Static/current-data proof strong.

Root contract:
- CvSelectionGroup::sentryAlert first scans every member only to choose ONE pHeadUnit:
  the member with greatest visibilityRange()+1.
- It then uses that same unit both as the LOS/range representative and as the combat-
  hostility actor in every visible-enemy test:

      if (!kPlot.isVisibleEnemyUnit(pHeadUnit, pLoopUnit))
          continue;

- The LOS/range optimization is valid for ordinary same-plot group members: canSeePlot
  uses the shared team plus range, and invisibility visibility is team-scoped.
- Enemy classification is NOT necessarily shared. CvPlot::isVisibleEnemyUnit(attacker,
  potentialEnemy) passes attacker->isAlwaysHostile(plot) into PUF_isEnemy. Thus an
  always-hostile/hidden-nationality member can legally treat a neutral foreign unit as
  an enemy while an ordinary teammate does not.

Current supported reproduction:
1. Current UNIT_PRIVATEER is DOMAIN_SEA, UNITCOMBAT_NAVAL, bHiddenNationality=1 and
   bAlwaysHostile=1.
2. Current UNIT_DESTROYER is DOMAIN_SEA and ordinary (both flags 0).
3. CvUnit::canJoinGroup imposes no hidden-nationality/always-hostile compatibility
   rule; same owner, plot and domain are sufficient here. A Privateer and Destroyer can
   therefore legally share a human selection group.
4. Current PROMOTION_SENTRY is available to UNITCOMBAT_NAVAL and gives
   iVisibilityChange=+1. Give it to the ordinary Destroyer while the Privateer lacks it.
   sentryAlert then deterministically selects the Destroyer as pHeadUnit because it has
   the strictly greatest visibilityRange().
5. Put the group on MISSION_SENTRY in neutral/open sea and let a visible ship belonging
   to a team with which the owner is at peace newly enter even the Privateer's ordinary
   visibility radius.
6. For the chosen Destroyer, isAlwaysHostile is false, so PUF_isEnemy reduces to actual
   team war state and says the neutral ship is not an enemy.
7. For the Privateer on the same tile, isAlwaysHostile is true outside a friendly/base
   plot; PUF_isEnemy therefore regards the same foreign combat owner as hostile even
   without a declared war. That ship is a legally attackable hostile target for one
   member of the sentry group.
8. Because sentryAlert tests hostility only through the max-range Destroyer, the group
   remains asleep instead of waking for the Privateer's newly visible enemy.

Why this is not a generic visibility-range problem:
- All members occupy the same plot/team. Using the largest range for geometrical LOS is
  a valid optimization and does not need to be replaced with N complete radius scans.
- Invisible detection is also team visibility in the called path.
- The mismatched quantity is specifically the UNIT-local attacker hostility semantics
  (notably isAlwaysHostile / hidden-nationality combat behavior). The scan actor was
  selected for range, a property unrelated to that combat relationship.

Ancestry:
- Local Civ4CE BtS CvSelectionGroup::sentryAlert already chooses one maximum-range unit
  and calls pPlot->isVisibleEnemyUnit(pHeadUnit). Thus the root predates AdvCiv.
- AdvCiv advc.004l replaced the immediate boolean scan with known-enemy identity
  tracking so units already in range would not wake Sentry repeatedly, but retained the
  same one-unit hostility actor. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS therefore preserve the
  inherited mismatch.
- Current Known Issues contains hidden-nationality/always-hostile issues in other
  producer contexts, but no collision with this sentry group-actor contract was found.

Consequence:
- A legal heterogeneous sentry group can fail to wake when a newly visible unit is an
  enemy for an always-hostile member but not for whichever member happened to have the
  greatest visibility range.
- Promotion assignment can change this behavior without changing the Privateer's own
  visibility or hostility: adding Sentry (+1 visibility) to the ordinary escort can make
  that escort become the sole hostility representative for the entire stack.

Repair direction:
- Preserve the max-range geometry optimization, but determine whether a visible
  potential enemy is hostile to ANY relevant group member rather than borrowing the
  max-range unit's isAlwaysHostile semantics for everybody.
- A cheap implementation can separate LOS/team-invisibility filtering from hostility:
  only members whose own visibility range reaches the candidate plot need be considered
  for member-specific PUF/isVisibleEnemyUnit hostility, or otherwise derive the union
  of actual group combat-hostility semantics carefully.
- Keep advc.004l knownEnemies tracking group-wide after that corrected predicate.

CONTROLS / NON-FINDINGS FROM THE SAME PASS
------------------------------------------
- sentryAlert's single maximum-range member is sufficient for ordinary LOS geometry:
  all group members share plot and team; canSeePlot receives only that plot/team/range.
- Invisible-unit visibility in CvPlot::isVisibleEnemyUnit ultimately uses the viewer
  team, so a dedicated see-invisible member contributes to team visibility; the defect
  above is not that the max-range member personally lacks the detection promotion.
- The doTurn Sentry-Heal wake test's pHeadUnit->canSentryHeal(plot()) initially looks
  like another head-only actor bug, but current canSentryHeal is purely
  !GET_TEAM(getTeam()).isRevealedCityHeal(plot). Same team + same plot makes its result
  identical for every group member.
- groupAttack's bBlitz / !bBlitz logic is intentional inherited K-Mod behavior. AdvCiv
  merely rewrote K-Mod's `bNoBlitz = !isBlitz() || !isMadeAttack()` as the algebraically
  equivalent `bBlitz = isBlitz() && isMadeAttack(); ... !bBlitz` when advc.164 expanded
  Blitz counts. No new F-root was established there.

WIP06 CURRENT CURSOR
--------------------

F148 / provisional KI#471 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED ADVCIV GROUP-ACTOR DEFECT
AIR-GROUP REBASE CLEARS LIVE RECON VISIBILITY ONLY FOR THE HEAD AIRCRAFT
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status:
- NEW CURRENT INHERITED DEFECT ROOT.
- Static/lifecycle evidence strong; current-data reproduction is supported.
- Introduced by the AdvCiv advc.029 rebase/recon cleanup itself, not by SAS.

Intended behavior / history:
- AdvCiv practical 1282 / commit 20703b98c917750d406f388e169309be3aa251b9
  introduced the CvSelectionGroup::startMission hook.
- Its v0.91 commit message explicitly says:
    "Tiles made visible by recon are fogged when the recon unit is rebased."
- The source comment likewise distinguishes an air attack from a rebase and says
  that the recon plot should be cleared for rebase.

Current implementation:
- When an air selection group's MISSION_MOVE_TO destination is recognized as a
  revealed air base, startMission executes:
      getHeadUnit()->setReconPlot(NULL);
- No loop clears the other air units in the group.

Why the head-only assumption is invalid:
1. Multiple same-owner air units can legally share one CvSelectionGroup.
   CvUnit::canJoinGroup requires compatible owner/plot/domain but does not impose
   a one-aircraft-per-group restriction.

2. Recon state is per UNIT, not per selection group.
   CvUnit::recon calls:
      setReconPlot(pPlot);
   and each CvUnit stores its own recon coordinates / m_iLastReconTurn.

3. A live recon plot has gameplay state, not merely presentation state.
   CvUnit::setReconPlot removes/adds:
      changeReconCount(...)
      changeAdjacentSight(getTeam(), RECON_VISIBILITY_RANGE, ..., this, true)
   Thus a stale non-head recon plot continues to reveal map tiles.

4. Recon deliberately survives into the next player turn.
   CvUnit::doTurnPost clears only when:
      GC.getGame().getGameTurn() > m_iLastReconTurn
   CvPlayer::doTurn calls unit doTurnPost at the END of that player's turn.
   Therefore a recon performed on turn T remains live throughout turn T+1 until
   that next turn ends unless an earlier action such as rebase explicitly clears it.

5. A grouped rebase moves every eligible air unit, not only the head.
   CvSelectionGroup::groupPathTo treats DOMAIN_AIR as a direct destination move,
   then groupMove loops the group's movable members and calls each unit's move().
   CvUnit::move does NOT call setReconPlot(NULL).

Concrete supported reproduction:
- On turn T, aircraft A and aircraft B perform separate Recon missions (they may
  target different plots). Both now have independent live recon plots.
- Those recon effects survive through the beginning of turn T+1 by design.
- On turn T+1, place/join A and B into the same air selection group. Same-owner,
  same-plot, same-domain grouping is legal.
- Give the group a MOVE_TO order to another revealed valid air base while both
  aircraft can rebase.
- startMission clears the recon plot of whichever aircraft happens to be the
  group head.
- groupPathTo/groupMove then rebases both aircraft.
- The non-head aircraft's old recon plot is never cleared by the rebase path.
  Its old remote tiles therefore remain visible until end-of-turn doTurnPost,
  despite that aircraft having already relocated to another base.

Why ordinary end-of-turn cleanup does not rescue the contract:
- The advc.029 rebase hook exists precisely to remove recon visibility WHEN the
  recon aircraft rebases, rather than letting the effect linger until the normal
  lifetime expires.
- Delayed cleanup at the end of T+1 therefore still violates the feature's stated
  behavior and can leave stale remote military/map visibility during the rest of
  the player's active turn after the aircraft has moved elsewhere.

Ancestry:
- The head-only cleanup was introduced with the advc.029 fix itself in practical
  1282; the original patch already used getHeadUnit()->setReconPlot(NULL).
- Later AdvCiv refactors changed the air-base predicate but retained the same
  head-only actor.
- Current SAS inherits that structure unchanged in this path.

Relation to existing findings:
- This is distinct from KI#398 / the Espionage actor repair: that issue selected
  the wrong executor for a one-spy mission; F148 is per-unit persistent map
  visibility that must be cleared for every aircraft participating in a group rebase.
- It is also distinct from F146's head-only sleeping-Spy wake convenience: both
  expose a head-only assumption, but one repairs group wake semantics and the
  other repairs per-unit recon visibility ownership.
- No collision with the current reviewed Known Issues ledger was found.

Repair direction:
- When an air MISSION_MOVE_TO is identified as a rebase, clear recon state for
  every group member that will actually participate in that rebase, not merely
  getHeadUnit().
- A conservative implementation can iterate current group members and apply
  setReconPlot(NULL) to each air unit that is movable / valid for the same
  destination. Clearing all group's air recon plots at accepted rebase start is
  also semantically close to the existing head-only behavior, but participation
  matching is preferable if immobile/left-behind aircraft can coexist.
- Preserve the distinction between rebase and air attack; ordinary MOVE_TO air
  attacks should not prematurely clear recon through this hook.

C015-WIP08 APPEND -- F148 participation broadening + head/mutation controls
===============================================================================

F148 / provisional KI#471 -- PARTICIPATION BROADENING
------------------------------------------------------
The head-only rebase cleanup has a second deterministic manifestation that
strengthens the repair requirement.

CvSelectionGroup::canDoMission(MISSION_MOVE_TO) deliberately treats DOMAIN_AIR
differently from ordinary groups:

    if (pUnit->getDomainType() != DOMAIN_AIR)
        bValid = true; // air units don't have to move as a group
    if (pUnit->canMove() != bValid)
        return !bValid;

For an air group, bValid remains false; encountering any movable aircraft can
therefore make the mission available even if another aircraft in the same group
(including the head) has no moves. groupPathTo/groupMove later moves only the
members that can actually participate.

Consequently the current accepted-rebase hook:

    getHeadUnit()->setReconPlot(NULL);

is wrong in both directions when the head is not a participant:

- an immobile head aircraft can have its still-live recon plot cleared even
  though it does NOT rebase and remains at the old air base;
- a movable non-head aircraft that DOES rebase retains its own old recon plot
  and stale remote sight until normal end-of-turn cleanup.

This makes the preferred F148 repair more precise: clear recon state for the
aircraft actually participating in the rebase (or otherwise reconcile cleanup
with the same participation predicate used by group movement), rather than
blindly clearing either only the head or every aircraft regardless of movement.


HEAD-UNIT / GROUP-REPRESENTATIVE INVENTORY -- NO ADDITIONAL ROOT
-----------------------------------------------------------------
A full current CvSelectionGroup.cpp getHeadUnit() inventory was re-challenged
after F146/F148.

Clean / intentional representative uses:
- doTurn Worker logging: diagnostic only.
- showMoves: head-unit hostility can be presentation-ambiguous for mixed
  always-hostile groups, but this controls move display/timing only; no hard
  gameplay-hostility contract was established, so no F149.
- playActionSound: one representative action sound for the selection group.
- groupCycleDistance: explicitly compares group heads for UI cycling/order.
- getX/getY/plot/area/getDomainType/getHeadOwner/getHeadTeam: grouping contracts
  make these properties shared by all legal group members.
- setTransportUnit: the earlier special-cargo/head-capacity concern remains
  unreachable in shipped callers/data; current AI_load family uses ordinary
  land cargo transports.
- isAmphibPlot: head is used only to establish the sea-domain group contract;
  same-domain grouping makes that safe.
- split/merge/regroup bookkeeping: head identity is intentionally the group AI
  representative and was already checked for ordering/lifetime safety.

The K-Mod Spy wake (F146) and advc.029 recon cleanup (F148) remain the only
current head-only shortcuts in this file for which the queried state is
demonstrably UNIT-local while the code assumes the head represents all members.


MUTATING-EXECUTOR LIFETIME CONTROL -- GOLDEN AGE
-------------------------------------------------
The startMission individual-unit loop was re-audited for actions that can delete
OTHER members rather than merely the current unit.

Golden Age is the strongest apparent case:
- CvUnit::goldenAge calls CvPlayer::killGoldenAgeUnits(this).
- killGoldenAgeUnits can select another Great Person, including another member
  of the same selection group.
- FOR_EACH_UNIT_VAR_IN would be unsafe if that action synchronously removed a
  cached future linked-list node.

However, killGoldenAgeUnits uses pBestUnit->kill(true), and CvUnit::kill with
bDelay=true only calls startDelayedDeath() after finishMoves and RETURNS.
It does not remove the unit from its group/list at that point. The initiating
unit likewise uses kill(true). Actual list removal occurs later through
doDelayedDeath()/kill(false), where VAR traversal safely removes the current
node.

Therefore the outer startMission traversal does not retain a pointer to a freed
future node in this path. No new iterator-lifetime root was established.

C015-WIP09 APPEND -- F149 amphibious attempted-vs-successful cargo contract
===============================================================================

F149 / provisional KI#472 -- CONFIRMED -- CURRENT SAS AMPHIBIOUS GROUP DEFECT
MOVABLE BUT ILLEGAL CARGO CAN CONSUME A DEFERRED LANDING WITHOUT ANY UNIT LANDING
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status:
- NEW CURRENT DEFECT ROOT in inherited K-Mod/BtS group-amphib execution.
- Current SAS data supplies a deterministic supported reproduction.
- The structural executor behavior is inherited; SAS's deliberate land-unit
  feature-impassability makes the false-positive "landing attempted" state easy
  to reach in current gameplay.

Relevant K-Mod intent:
- K-Mod practical 461 / 7200489b5d added special handling so amphibious landings
  can execute even if the TRANSPORT group itself has no moves. The commit's
  example is a transport already on the coast: ordering it onto land should
  unload cargo despite the ship having no movement left.
- Practical 462 / a83a53016a moved that handling into startMission because the
  first implementation did not work.
- The resulting behavior intentionally preserves the transport MOVE_TO order
  when no cargo group is currently ready to land: groupAmphibMove returns false,
  so the transport mission is not consumed and can be retried on a later turn.
- K-Mod practical 428 / 85a83db596 later deduplicated cargo groups, but retained
  the same success accounting described below.

Current executor:
- groupAmphibMove gathers distinct land cargo groups.
- For every cargo group with canAllMove()==true it executes:
      kCargoGroup.pushMission(MISSION_MOVE_TO, target, ...);
      bLanding = true;
- It does NOT establish that the cargo group can legally enter/attack the target,
  nor does pushMission return whether the pushed mission actually moved/landed.
- Its return contract is documented as:
      "Returns true if attempted an amphib landing..."
- startMission interprets a true return by setting bDelete=true for the transport
  group's MOVE_TO mission. continueMission/groupPathTo likewise treat the true
  result as reason to stop the enclosing transport movement.

Why canAllMove is insufficient:
- It tests movement-point readiness only.
- canStartMission(MISSION_MOVE_TO, ..., bCheckMoves=false) deliberately accepts a
  different destination without checking path/terrain legality.
- readyForMission/canDoMission for MOVE_TO likewise checks movement-point
  uniformity, not destination entry legality.
- The pushed cargo mission therefore can start synchronously and only later have
  groupPathTo/pathfinding reject the destination.

Concrete current SAS reproduction:
1. Put at least two LAND cargo groups aboard one adjacent sea-transport group.
2. Cargo group A is a current Chariot (or Catapult/Trebuchet) with movement
   points remaining.
3. Cargo group B is an ordinary infantry-type land unit that is legally able to
   enter the target coastal Forest/Jungle, but has already spent its moves.
4. Target a coastal Forest/Jungle outside our own cultural borders.
5. Current SAS UNIT_CHARIOT (also Egyptian War Chariot, Catapult and Trebuchet)
   has FEATURE_FOREST and FEATURE_JUNGLE marked impassable with no passable tech;
   CvUnit::canMoveInto rejects those features outside own-team borders.
6. The transport destination/path is nevertheless a legitimate amphibious
   landing target because cargo B can legally enter it. This is exactly the kind
   of heterogeneous cargo group for which the group path/landing machinery must
   distinguish individual cargo groups.
7. groupAmphibMove skips B because B.canAllMove()==false.
8. A.canAllMove()==true, so it pushes MOVE_TO on A and immediately sets
   bLanding=true.
9. A's pushed mission starts immediately for a manual/non-appended command, but
   its own groupPathTo cannot generate a legal path into the impassable feature;
   its cargo mission is therefore canceled without landing.
10. groupAmphibMove has already returned true. The enclosing transport mission
    is consequently consumed/deleted even though NO cargo unit landed.
11. On the following turn cargo B would again have movement and could legally
    land, but the transport's deferred landing order has been lost.

Partition/control:
- If cargo A is absent, the same state with only immobile-but-legal cargo B makes
  groupAmphibMove return false. The transport landing mission is retained and can
  succeed when B regains moves.
- Adding the independently ILLEGAL but currently movable cargo A therefore
  changes "wait until a legal cargo group can land" into "consume the landing
  order now although nobody lands." That is not a tuning choice; it is a
  false-success signal in the executor contract.

Current-data proof:
- Base AdvCiv 1.14 has no land UnitInfo FeatureImpassable entries, while current
  SAS deliberately defines Forest/Jungle impassability for Chariot, Egyptian War
  Chariot, Catapult and Trebuchet. Thus the concrete feature reproduction is a
  current SAS-supported state even though the groupAmphibMove machinery itself
  is inherited.
- The structural issue is more general than those XML additions: any movable
  cargo group whose destination mission later fails can set the false landing
  result before execution success is known.

Relation to earlier findings:
- Distinct from F145/KI#468. F145 is shared transport LOAD capacity being tested
  independently before sequential loading. F149 concerns the later UNLOAD /
  amphibious side, where a pushed-but-illegal cargo mission is counted as a
  successful reason to consume the enclosing transport order.
- Distinct from the earlier cargo-group deduplication negative control: K-Mod's
  deduplication prevents the same group from being pushed multiple times, but
  does not validate whether a unique group can actually execute the landing.

Repair direction:
- Do not set/return the group-amphib "landing happened / consume enclosing order"
  signal merely because a cargo MOVE_TO mission was pushed.
- Prevalidate that a candidate cargo group can legally enter/attack the landing
  tile under the same movement/attack assumptions that its mission will use, or
  otherwise obtain an execution-success result from the cargo action.
- Preserve K-Mod's important deferred-order behavior: if no CURRENTLY READY and
  LEGALLY LANDING cargo group exists, leave the transport MOVE_TO queued so a
  temporarily immobile legal group can land on a later turn.
- Be careful with mixed attack/nonattack cargo; the repair should use the actual
  amphibious move/attack legality rather than simply checking movement points.

C015-WIP10 APPEND -- F150 Air Patrol moveless-participant regression
===============================================================================

F150 / provisional KI#473 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED K-MOD REGRESSION
IMMOBILE UNSUITABLE AIRCRAFT IS NOT SPLIT FROM A NEW AIR-PATROL GROUP
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status:
- NEW CURRENT INHERITED DEFECT ROOT.
- Introduced by K-Mod practical 1205 / 7027bf8ed2 during startMission
  reorganization; current SAS and Base AdvCiv inherit it.
- Current Fighter/Bomber data provides a deterministic human reproduction.

Mission contract:
- CvSelectionGroup::canDoMission(MISSION_AIRPATROL) returns true when a member
  canAirPatrol and (when moves are checked) that eligible member can move.
- The source comment explicitly says:
      "this mission will automatically ungroup any unsuitable units."
- startMission implements that concept through apUnitsLeftBehind and later splits
  those units into a separate group.

Historical control:
- K-Mod practical 732 / 58beb5a942 (2012-05-09), which rewrote mission readiness,
  explicitly had:
      case MISSION_PARADROP:
      case MISSION_AIRPATROL:
          bAbandonMoveless = true;
  Thus a unit with no moves was put into units_left_behind for BOTH missions.
- The same implementation separately checked movable Air Patrol members with
  canAirDefend and also put unsuitable ones into units_left_behind.
- K-Mod practical 1205 / 7027bf8ed2 (2015-09-26), commit message
  "Reorganised CvSelectionGroup::startMission for consistency", retained the
  per-movable-unit Air Patrol canAirDefend split but changed the moveless
  abandonment switch to:
      case MISSION_PARADROP:
          bAbandonMoveless = true;
  Air Patrol silently disappeared from that first-stage split.
- The commit itself says the reorganization was for consistency and that the
  author suspected it fixed an older bug but no longer remembered which one;
  there is no stated design decision to retain immobile non-interceptors in an
  Intercept group.
- AdvCiv's later advc.004c restructuring deleted the generic
  bAbandonMoveless helper and explicitly replicated moveless handling in its
  Paradrop block, while retaining the inherited Air Patrol per-movable check.
  It therefore preserves rather than creates the K-Mod 1205 regression.

Current executor:
1. A valid Air Patrol command sets the WHOLE selection group to
   ACTIVITY_INTERCEPT.
2. The individual-unit loop begins with:
       if (!pUnit->canMove())
           continue;
3. Only after that skip does MISSION_AIRPATROL run:
       if (!pUnit->canAirDefend(plot()))
           apUnitsLeftBehind.push_back(pUnit);
4. Therefore an unsuitable aircraft with no moves is never considered for the
   split.
5. apUnitsLeftBehind is later detached, but the skipped immobile aircraft stays
   in the original ACTIVITY_INTERCEPT group.

Concrete current-data reproduction:
- Current UNIT_FIGHTER:
    Domain=DOMAIN_AIR
    iInterceptionProbability=100
- Current UNIT_BOMBER:
    Domain=DOMAIN_AIR
    iInterceptionProbability=0
- Same-owner air units on the same plot may legally share one selection group.
- Let the Bomber perform an action first so it cannot move; keep a Fighter in
  the same group with movement remaining.
- Air Patrol remains available because the Fighter canAirPatrol and can move.
- Issue Air Patrol.
- startMission sets ACTIVITY_INTERCEPT for the whole group.
- The Fighter is a valid defender.
- The Bomber hits the upfront !canMove() continue and never reaches the
  !canAirDefend split.
- No later turn-start code repairs the composition. On the next turn the Bomber
  regains movement points, but ACTIVITY_INTERCEPT is a waiting activity and the
  group remains on patrol; the Bomber has maxInterceptionProbability()==0 and
  can never be selected as an interceptor.
- The Bomber therefore remains hidden/parked inside the intercept group until
  the player manually wakes or separates the group.

Why ordinary intercept logic does not rescue this:
- CvUnit::bestInterceptor requires canAirDefend and therefore simply ignores the
  Bomber; it does not split or wake it.
- CvSelectionGroup::doTurn has no "invalid Air Patrol member" reconciliation
  equivalent to Sea Patrol's per-unit invalidity wake.
- setActivityType(ACTIVITY_INTERCEPT) is group-wide and remains unchanged on
  later turns.

Relation to other file-015 roots:
- Distinct from F143/KI#466. F143 Sea Patrol accepts a mixed group and then an
  ineligible companion wakes/cancels the valid patrol on the next unit turn.
  F150 Air Patrol was explicitly designed to split unsuitable members, but one
  class of unsuitable member (no moves at command time) bypasses the split and
  becomes trapped in the valid patrol group.
- Distinct from F146/KI#469, which is a head-only Spy convenience wake.
- No current reviewed Known-Issues collision found.

Repair direction:
- Restore the original K-Mod participation contract: for MISSION_AIRPATROL,
  put nonparticipating/moveless members into apUnitsLeftBehind as well as movable
  members that fail canAirDefend.
- Prefer one explicit Air Patrol participation loop that classifies ALL group
  members before/while setting Intercept, so future outer canMove shortcuts
  cannot bypass the split.
- Preserve the valid K-Mod behavior that one movable eligible Fighter may enter
  patrol even when other selected aircraft cannot act; those others should be
  left behind rather than block the command.


POST-F149 MISSION / PATH / LIFETIME CONTROLS
---------------------------------------------
- Mission timer / mission queue ownership: no stale mission-node dereference
  established. deleteMissionQueueNode deactivates the head before deletion;
  K-Mod deliberately leaves next activation to callers. continueMission_bulk
  refreshes pHeadMission after groupPathTo and before later queue use.
- Build-completion cross-group mission deletion is plot-unit-list safe and
  getMissionType/getMissionData1 are sentinel-safe on an empty queue.
- CvSelectionGroup::doTurn caches pHeadUnit before calling each CvUnit::doTurn,
  but CvUnit::doTurn only uses delayed death for turn-damage death and does not
  synchronously unlink/regroup/upgrade the head. Actual removal occurs later in
  doDelayedDeath; no dangling cached-head root established.
- Shared GroupPathFinder composition caching remains a robustness candidate:
  setGroup does not notice group membership changes and canReuseInitialPathData
  intentionally admits that its movement-state key is incomplete; add/remove/
  join do not invalidate the finder. However, a shipped same-group reuse sequence
  producing a stale returned path has NOT yet been proven, so F151 is not spent
  on that concern.
- Serialization read/write remains paired for current uiFlag=3. Removed pre-v3
  migration branches are old-save compatibility, which this project does not
  promise; no current-format serialization defect established.

C015-WIP11 APPEND -- F151 upgrade action-cache representative defect
===============================================================================

F151 / provisional KI#474 -- CONFIRMED -- INHERITED BTS ACTION-CACHE DEFECT
UPGRADE CACHE COLLAPSES SAME-TYPE UNITS DESPITE PER-UNIT UPGRADE PRICE/ELIGIBILITY
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status:
- NEW CURRENT INHERITED DEFECT ROOT.
- Present already in BtS/Civ4CE; Base AdvCiv and current SAS inherit the same
  one-representative-per-UnitType action-cache design.
- Current SAS PROMOTION_LEADER gives a deterministic same-type eligibility
  difference through its 100% upgrade discount.

Cache contract:
- CvGame::setupActionCache is DllExport and forwards to the currently selected
  CvSelectionGroup. CvGame::canHandleAction is likewise DllExport and accepts the
  bUseCache fast-path flag used by the executable/UI action-update path.
- CvSelectionGroup::setupActionCache scans units that are isReadyForUpgrade(),
  but stores only the FIRST unit encountered for each UnitTypes value:
      if (eUnitType == m_aDifferentUnitCache[i]->getUnitType())
          bFound = true;
      ...
      if (!bFound)
          m_aDifferentUnitCache.push_back(pUnit);
- CvSelectionGroup::canEverDoCommand(COMMAND_UPGRADE,...,bUseCache=true) then
  tests only those cached representatives.
- If none of the representatives can execute the requested target upgrade, it
  returns false immediately. CvSelectionGroup::canDoCommand therefore never
  reaches its later full FOR_EACH_UNIT_IN scan.

Why UnitType is not a sufficient cache key:
- CvUnit::canUpgrade first requires isReadyForUpgrade, but then, for a real
  (bTestVisible=false) command, also compares the OWNER'S gold against this
  individual unit's upgradePrice(eUnit).
- upgradePrice subtracts:
      (iPrice * getUpgradeDiscount()) / 100
  where getUpgradeDiscount() is per-unit accumulated state from promotions.
- Two units with identical UnitType, owner and plot can therefore have different
  real upgrade affordability.

Concrete current-data reproduction:
1. Select/group two human units of the same upgradeable UnitType on the same
   owned-team plot, both with movement available.
2. Unit A is an ordinary copy.
3. Unit B is otherwise the same type but carries PROMOTION_LEADER from a Great
   General attachment.
4. Current CIV4PromotionInfos.xml defines:
      PROMOTION_LEADER
      iUpgradeDiscount = 100
5. Therefore, for the same target upgrade:
      B.upgradePrice(target) = 0
   while A retains the ordinary positive upgrade cost (absent another discount).
6. Choose a treasury below A's ordinary price; zero gold itself is sufficient.
   A cannot perform the real upgrade because canUpgrade fails the affordability
   check, while B can.
7. If setupActionCache encounters A first for this UnitType, it stores A and
   suppresses B as a duplicate type.
8. Cached canEverDoCommand(COMMAND_UPGRADE,target,...,true) tests A, gets false,
   exhausts the one-element type representative set and returns false.
9. canDoCommand returns false before its ordinary full-group scan can reach B.
   The action fast path can therefore disable/hide a valid free upgrade present
   in the selected group.
10. If group ordering instead makes B the representative, the same selected set
    returns true. Cache correctness consequently depends on which same-type unit
    happens to be retained.

Independent current-data control:
- Reviewed SAS KI#220 already documents and fixes another UI/statistics defect
  whose reproduction is precisely that a combat unit carrying PROMOTION_LEADER
  can validly upgrade for ZERO gold. That independently confirms the free-upgrade
  state is current and intentional rather than hypothetical XML.
- isReadyForUpgrade does not erase the distinction; it checks movement and
  own-team plot only, which A and B share.

Ancestry:
- Civ4CE BtS already contains the same setupActionCache:
  one ready unit per UnitType.
- BtS canEverDoCommand(COMMAND_UPGRADE,bUseCache) likewise tests only those
  representatives and returns false when none can perform the target upgrade.
- Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains the same design; current SAS changes are formatting,
  constness and unrelated guards only.
- This is therefore inherited from Firaxis BtS rather than introduced by K-Mod,
  AdvCiv or SAS.

Relation to existing issues:
- Distinct from KI#220: that issue was Military Summary statistics dropping
  zero-cost upgrades from a Python sample; F151 is the engine/UI action-cache
  feasibility result for the selected group.
- Distinct from AI upgrade-routing/ROI issues (KI#188.x / KI#217): this fast path
  concerns action availability and collapses same-type HUMAN units before normal
  unit-by-unit command testing.
- No collision with the current reviewed Known-Issues ledger found.

Repair direction:
- Do not collapse real COMMAND_UPGRADE feasibility solely by UnitType.
- Simplest correctness-first repair: cache every isReadyForUpgrade unit and let
  canEverDoCommand test all cached ready candidates.
- If retaining compression for UI performance, the key must include every
  per-unit property that can change real upgrade legality/price; in practice that
  is brittle (upgrade discount now, and potentially other per-unit state later),
  so retaining all ready units is safer.
- Preserve the purpose of the action cache (avoid repeated busy/readiness work)
  without changing the result of the uncached full-group command test.


PATHFINDER COMPOSITION-CACHE STATUS -- STILL NOT PROMOTED
---------------------------------------------------------
The shared GroupPathFinder concern remains a real robustness smell but still
does not meet the current-root bar:
- setGroup/cache reuse does not key on group membership;
- add/remove/join do not reset the global pathfinder;
- GroupStepMetric itself warns that its reuse condition misses significant
  group changes.
However, current human movement uses the explicitly cleared alternate finder,
and no deterministic shipped AI sequence has yet been established where the same
group pointer changes composition and then reuses a stale main-finder destination
without an intervening reset/rebind. Keep this as a closure challenge rather than
spending F152 from API possibility alone.
