F188 / provisional KI#511
-------------------------
TITLE
    Imminent TOTAL-war target switching temporarily rewrites the plan to
    WARPLAN_PREPARING_LIMITED, so the alternative is evaluated as a limited war and
    a successful switch can permanently downgrade TOTAL to PREPARING_LIMITED.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED. Inherited AdvCiv defect introduced by commit
    e04adaf0a58e53f474e9c6ca4e8eaa6ce7eb19cf (2018-07-31), "UWAI can switch to a
    different target when war remains imminent". Retained by Base AdvCiv 1.14 and
    current SAS. Current SAS KI#189 makes the comparison deterministic and therefore
    makes the inherited state-loss path easier to encounter, but did not create it.

ROOT
    reviewPlan handles a non-war imminent plan (WARPLAN_LIMITED or WARPLAN_TOTAL) by
    temporarily changing the target's plan before calling considerSwitchTarget:

        kAgent.AI_setWarPlanNoUpdate(eTarget, WARPLAN_PREPARING_LIMITED);
        bool const bSwitch = !considerSwitchTarget(eTarget, iU, 0);
        ...

    The temporary plan is hardcoded to PREPARING_LIMITED even when the saved eWP is
    WARPLAN_TOTAL.

    considerSwitchTarget is not merely a predicate. It reads the current target plan:

        WarPlanTypes const eWP = kAgent.AI_getWarPlan(eTarget);

    and uses that value both to evaluate every alternative target:

        int iAltU = eval.evaluate(eWP, iTurnsRemaining);

    and, after a successful switch, to install the new target plan:

        kAgent.AI_setWarPlan(eBestAltTarget, eWP);

    Therefore the temporary rewrite changes both the comparison semantics and the
    persistent result of a successful switch.

HISTORY / INTENDED-CONTRACT PROOF
    The introducing 2018 commit added this exact mechanism and describes it as a
    workaround because considerSwitchTarget had been written for preparation plans:

        "considerSwitchTarget was written under the assumption that no war is
        imminent. Could be difficult to rectify; instead, change the war plan
        temporarily."

    The implementation then always chose WARPLAN_PREPARING_LIMITED. There is no
    corresponding reason to erase TOTAL vs LIMITED: considerSwitchTarget already
    accepts the current preparation plan generically and WarEvaluator can evaluate
    either PREPARING_LIMITED or PREPARING_TOTAL.

DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCTION SHAPE
    1. Agent has an imminent WARPLAN_TOTAL against target A and positive utility.
    2. The imminent-plan branch reaches target switching.
    3. reviewPlan temporarily changes A to WARPLAN_PREPARING_LIMITED.
    4. Alternative target B is legal and sufficiently more attractive to satisfy the
       switch threshold.
    5. considerSwitchTarget reads PREPARING_LIMITED, evaluates B under that plan, then
       clears A and assigns PREPARING_LIMITED to B.

    The original TOTAL character is restored only when there is no switch (or while
    running in the background). On a real successful switch it is lost.

CONSEQUENCE
    * A TOTAL-war plan can choose its replacement target using LIMITED-war utility,
      which can change which target wins the comparison.
    * If the switch succeeds, the new target receives WARPLAN_PREPARING_LIMITED rather
      than WARPLAN_PREPARING_TOTAL. The AI has therefore changed both target and war
      type even though this path is intended only to reconsider the target.
    * SAS's deterministic KI#189 target comparison makes this inherited defect more
      reproducible because the old preliminary random roll no longer suppresses many
      switch attempts.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    Preserve the original plan character in the temporary preparation mapping:

        WARPLAN_TOTAL   -> WARPLAN_PREPARING_TOTAL
        WARPLAN_LIMITED -> WARPLAN_PREPARING_LIMITED

    Then call considerSwitchTarget exactly as today. If no switch occurs, restore the
    saved imminent plan as before. If a switch occurs, the helper naturally installs
    the matching preparation type on the new target.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS
    * This is not an argument that an imminent plan must stay "imminent" after a
      target change. Re-entering preparation for the new target is coherent; the bug
      is loss of TOTAL vs LIMITED intent.
    * Background simulation already restores eWP after the helper, so the persistent
      downgrade concerns the real successful-switch path.
    * The defect predates SAS; KI#189 changes reachability/frequency, not the faulty
      mapping itself.

F189 DISPOSITION -- AI_negotiatePeace success vs actual war end
---------------------------------------------------------------
STATUS
    REJECTED AS A NEW FINDING after the current-source contract pass.

WHY IT LOOKED SUSPICIOUS
    considerPeace now logs both:

        bPeace    = AI_negotiatePeace(...)
        bWarEnded = !kAgent.isAtWar(eTarget)

    but still returns !bPeace rather than !bWarEnded. A previous SAS victory-denial
    safety guard in CvDeal could reject an AI-AI treaty after AI_negotiatePeace had
    already returned true, producing exactly bPeace == true && bWarEnded == false.

CURRENT-SOURCE CLOSURE
    The 20:49 source has closed that concrete mismatch at both earlier layers:

    * UWAI::Team::considerPeace skips ordinary peace when either team satisfies the
      shared configured victory-threat predicate.
    * CvPlayerAI::AI_negotiatePeace repeats the same shared pre-check for non-UWAI AI
      callers before constructing or implementing the deal.
    * CvDeal retains the final guard as defense in depth for human/unusual trade paths.

    For the AI-AI AI_negotiatePeace path, the selected gold/tech/city items are checked
    before implementation and CvDeal performs its full canTradeItem preflight before
    mutating the deal. No other stable current path was established where the helper
    returns true yet an AI-AI peace deal is silently rejected.

    Human peace offers intentionally remain different: AI_negotiatePeace returns true
    when the diplomacy offer is sent, before the human accepts it, so bWarEnded is
    expected to remain false. Returning based on bWarEnded would therefore be wrong
    for that branch. The separate diagnostic remains useful, but it is not itself a
    correctness defect.

F189 / provisional KI#512 -- scheme can start LIMITED war from TOTAL-only positive utility at the exact zero boundary
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv defect.

CURRENT CODE / ROOT
    UWAI::Team::scheme evaluates both preparation types and then selects which plan
    character to carry forward:

        bool bTotal = false;
        if (iLimitedU < 0 && iTotalU > 0)
            bTotal = true;
        if (iLimitedU < 0 && iTotalU < 0) // Only relevant for logging
            bTotal = (iTotalU > iLimitedU);
        if (iLimitedU > 0 && iTotalU > 0)
        {
            ... personality-weighted total-vs-limited choice ...
        }
        int iU = std::max(iLimitedU, iTotalU);

    The three conditions leave one consequential sign combination uncovered:

        iLimitedU == 0 && iTotalU > 0

    bTotal therefore remains at its default false, while iU takes the positive total
    utility. The target survives the `iU <= 0` rejection and can be selected, but the
    resulting plan is WARPLAN_PREPARING_LIMITED (or the corresponding direct LIMITED
    plan in the SAS victory-denial path).

WHY ZERO IS A REAL INPUT
    WarEvaluator utility is an ordinary integer sum/difference, initialized from zero
    and returned directly. Zero is not a sentinel and requires no exceptional game
    state. Thus an exact neutral limited-war evaluation with a positive total-war
    evaluation is a legitimate boundary case.

HISTORY / REGRESSION PROOF
    Before AdvCiv commit 0fb74a859b720ab67c1148573fa5b9ab32770bf0
    (2018-08-31, "Various minor changes"), scheme simply used:

        bool total = (uTotal > uLimited);

    so `uLimited == 0 && uTotal > 0` correctly selected total war.

    That commit's log explicitly describes the UWAI change as:

        "Increased the impact of AI leader preferences for limited vs. total war."

    It replaced the simple comparison with the current sign-partitioned / weighted
    selector, but used strict `< 0` and `> 0` tests and omitted the neutral-limited,
    positive-total boundary. AdvCiv 1.14 retains the same conditions, so this is an
    inherited upstream defect rather than a SAS regression.

DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCTION SHAPE
    1. A legal scheming target evaluates to exactly 0 utility for
       WARPLAN_PREPARING_LIMITED.
    2. The same target evaluates to positive utility for WARPLAN_PREPARING_TOTAL.
    3. No other gate removes the candidate and its final drive wins its selection roll.
    4. bTotal is still false even though the only positive evaluated plan was TOTAL.
    5. scheme therefore installs a LIMITED plan whose own evaluated utility was 0.

CONSEQUENCE
    * The AI can start the wrong war type at an exact but ordinary utility boundary.
    * Its positive drive is supplied entirely by the TOTAL evaluation while its stored
      plan character is LIMITED.
    * Follow-up preparation/review logic then evaluates and develops the LIMITED plan,
      so this is not merely a misleading log label.

NARROW REPAIR DIRECTION
    Include the neutral limited case when total war is positive, e.g. conceptually:

        if (iLimitedU <= 0 && iTotalU > 0)
            bTotal = true;

    Keep the personality-weighted branch for the genuinely competing case where both
    utilities are positive. No broader change to the existing max-utility drive rule
    is required to fix this finding.

NEGATIVE CONTROL / SCOPE
    The broader question whether `iU = max(iLimitedU, iTotalU)` should always be tied
    to the personality-selected plan when both utilities are positive is intentionally
    NOT folded into F189. That may be deliberate separation of overall war drive from
    war-type preference. F189 needs no such interpretation: at the omitted zero
    boundary the selected LIMITED type has no positive utility at all.

  weighting semantics remain unnumbered unless a stronger contract proof appears.

  then perform a whole-file adversarial closure pass before closing UWAIAgent.cpp.

F190 / provisional KI#513 -- isLandTarget leaks one member's no-ocean-cargo distance exemption into later team members
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv team-game defect.

CURRENT CODE / ROOT
    UWAI::Team::isLandTarget keeps a single mutable distance limit outside its loop
    over the agent team's player members:

        int iDistLimit = getUWAI().maxLandDist();
        for (MemberAIIter itMember(m_eAgent); itMember.hasNext(); ++itMember)
        {
            UWAICache const& kCache = itMember->uwai().getCache();
            // Sea route then unlikely to be much slower
            if (!kCache.canTrainDeepSeaCargo())
                iDistLimit = MAX_INT;
            ...
            if (kCacheCity.canReachByLand())
            {
                ...
                if (kCacheCity.getDistance() <= iDistLimit)
                    return true;
            }
        }

    Once an earlier member cannot train deep-sea cargo, iDistLimit becomes MAX_INT
    for the remainder of the team-member loop. It is never restored for a later
    member that *can* train deep-sea cargo.

PER-PLAYER CONTRACT PROOF
    `canTrainDeepSeaCargo()` is a UWAICache property. UWAICache::updateTransports
    computes it from that cache owner's own civilization units and
    `kOwner.canTrain(eUnit)`, so it is deliberately player-specific.

    A sibling consumer, InvasionGraph::Node::canReachByLand, applies the same rule
    locally to the cache being queried:

        pCacheCity->getDistance() <= getUWAI().maxLandDist() ||
        !m_kCache.canTrainDeepSeaCargo()

    This is strong internal evidence for the intended semantics: the unlimited-land
    exemption belongs to the particular player whose cache lacks ocean-capable cargo,
    not to all later members of that player's team.

DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCTION SHAPE
    Consider a multi-player team with members A then B in MemberAIIter order:

    1. A cannot train deep-sea cargo, so the shared iDistLimit becomes MAX_INT.
    2. A has no target city that is reachable by land, so A does not itself establish
       the target as a land target.
    3. B can train deep-sea cargo.
    4. B has a target city reachable by land, but its distance exceeds maxLandDist.
       With B's own transport capability, that route should fail the land-distance
       test so a sea approach can remain preferable.
    5. Because A's MAX_INT leaked forward, B's distant route passes and the team is
       classified as having a land target.

    Reordering otherwise equivalent team members so B is visited before A removes
    that classification. The result is therefore iteration-order dependent.

CONSEQUENCE
    AI_isLandTarget feeds UWAI and other team war decisions, including whether war
    evaluation treats a target as naval/land. In team games the leak can classify a
    distant target as land for the wrong member, changing preparation assumptions and
    war valuation merely because another earlier teammate lacks deep-sea cargo.

HISTORY
    The shared mutable limit is already present in AdvCiv practical commit
    f6ff6a182f5187541fff6e5bbbe12f9573b3778c (2017-04-16, "Initial commit
    (cont.)"), which introduced the early WarAndPeaceAI/UWAI implementation. AdvCiv
    1.14 still has the same loop and current SAS inherited it unchanged.

NARROW REPAIR DIRECTION
    Keep the base configured limit immutable and derive a member-local limit, e.g.:

        int const iBaseDistLimit = getUWAI().maxLandDist();
        for (... each member ...)
        {
            UWAICache const& kCache = ...;
            int const iMemberDistLimit = (kCache.canTrainDeepSeaCargo() ?
                    iBaseDistLimit : MAX_INT);
            ... compare this member's cached city distance to iMemberDistLimit ...
        }

    Equivalently, inline the per-cache condition as InvasionGraph already does.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS
    * If the no-cargo member itself has a reachable-by-land target city, treating its
      route as unlimited is intentional; F190 does not challenge that policy.
    * Single-player teams are unaffected because there is no later teammate to inherit
      the modified limit.
    * This is not about team technology sharing. The relevant cache flag explicitly
      depends on each player owner's `canTrain` result and is consumed per owner in
      InvasionGraph.

-----------------------

F191 / provisional KI#514 -- emergency-peace path calls ScaledNum::uround on a peace threshold that is explicitly allowed to be negative
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STATUS
    CONFIRMED SAS regression; debug-assert / signed-rounding contract defect.

CURRENT CODE / ROOT
    UWAI::Team::considerPeace obtains the signed peace threshold and, for the
    preferred emergency-peace target, forces iU below it so normal negotiation code
    cannot early-out:

        scaled rPeaceThresh = peaceThreshold(eTarget);
        ...
        if (bEmergencyPeace)
        {
            ...
            iU = std::min(iU, rPeaceThresh.uround() - 100);
        }

    `ScaledNum::uround()` is not the signed rounding API. Its implementation says
    explicitly:

        BOOST_STATIC_ASSERT(bSIGNED); // Use round() instead
        ...
        FAssert(m_i >= 0 && ...);

    Therefore calling uround() requires a nonnegative scaled value even though the
    type itself is signed.

NEGATIVE-THRESHOLD CONTRACT PROOF
    peaceThreshold() is intentionally a signed threshold, not a nonnegative amount:

        scaled r = fixp(-7.5); // To give it time

    It can receive further negative adjustments for total war, having been attacked,
    and leader pride. Most decisively, for an AI target it finishes with:

        if (!kTarget.isHuman())
            iR = std::min(0, iR);

    Thus inter-AI peace thresholds are explicitly constrained to be nonpositive, not
    nonnegative. Negative values are ordinary and expected. Emergency peace is not
    human-only, so a negative rPeaceThresh can reach uround() directly.

DETERMINISTIC FAILURE SHAPE
    1. An AI team is in SAS emergency-peace mode and the reviewed AI opponent is the
       preferred emergency-peace target.
    2. peaceThreshold(eTarget) is negative -- for example its normal -7.5 starting
       bias remains negative after the other terms.
    3. considerPeace enters bEmergencyPeace and calls rPeaceThresh.uround().
    4. A debug build violates `FAssert(m_i >= 0)` inside ScaledNum::uround().

    No unusual corrupt state is needed; the caller feeds a value whose legal range
    contradicts the rounding helper's documented/asserted precondition.

RELEASE-BUILD NOTE
    With assertions compiled out, the signed arithmetic still executes, but uround()
    uses the positive-value rounding formula. Around negative fractional values this
    can differ from round() (for example by one integer). Because SAS then subtracts
    100 solely to force the utility clearly below the threshold, that one-point
    rounding difference is unlikely to alter normal release gameplay here. The main
    concrete consequence is therefore the invalid API use and debug assertion, not a
    claim of a large release-balance effect.

HISTORY
    The line is absent from base AdvCiv and was introduced by SAS practical commit
    bf56a70088f859b853c9e72df7fcb8350672d364 (2025-09-17,
    "Seemingly tremendously improved multi-war threat management by adding sanity
    \"emergency peace\" pre-checks in UWAI::Team::considerPeace..."). The introducing
    diff contains the same call:

        iU = std::min(iU, rPeaceThresh.uround() - 100);

    The defect therefore originates in the SAS emergency-peace addition rather than
    inherited UWAI.

NARROW REPAIR DIRECTION
    Use the signed rounding helper already used elsewhere for this exact threshold:

        iU = std::min(iU, rPeaceThresh.round() - 100);

    No emergency-peace policy or threshold tuning needs to change.

RECONCILIATION NOTE -- F185 STILL LIVE IN THE 20:49 SOURCE
    The current diagnostics correctly log reciprocal target war success as:

        kTarget.AI_getWarSuccess(kAgent.getID())

    but the actual inherited peaceThreshold() formula still contains the F185 typo:

        kTarget.AI_getWarSuccess(eTarget)

    This is the already-durable F185 / KI#508 root, not a new finding. Its presence in
    the reconciled source simply means the documented fix has not yet reached this
    snapshot (or is still awaiting the user's/Codex implementation pass).

NEGATIVE CONTROL / SCOPE
    Other uround() calls in this file are not automatically F191 siblings. Most
    consume explicitly nonnegative prices, utilities clamped with max(0,...), or
    positive weighting factors. They require individual sign proof before any finding
    can be promoted.

F183 / provisional KI#506 -- REPAIR-BOUNDARY CLARIFICATION
----------------------------------------------------------
The earlier root remains confirmed, but the closure pass found an important nuance in
its proposed repair. Merely resetting bScheme and the four land/naval aggregate flags
at the start of each do/while retry is not sufficient.

reviewWarPlans uses abTargetDone to prevent a target whose plan already changed from
being reviewed a second time. Some plan changes remove or redirect the target, where
that omission is appropriate; however, other false-return paths leave the same target
with a live changed plan. In particular, considerConcludePreparations can replace
WARPLAN_PREPARING_LIMITED/TOTAL with WARPLAN_LIMITED/TOTAL and return false, and the
SAS victory-denial review path can declare the war and return false. The target is then
marked done and omitted from later retry evaluations even though its final live war
plan should still contribute to the final AreaAI / bad-war summary.

Therefore a per-retry reset alone can trade the original stale-bit defect for a new
omission: the final no-change pass would describe only targets that were not marked
done, rather than all surviving current plans.

CORRECTNESS-FIRST REPAIR DIRECTION
    Keep the retry/mutation machinery and abTargetDone semantics for reviewPlan, but
    derive bScheme and the four AreaAI aggregate flags from a distinct final read-only
    evaluation of all surviving current non-vassal plans after the mutation loop has
    stabilized (or implement equivalent summary-only evaluation for done targets).
    That final pass must not call reviewPlan again. This matches the trailing contract
    that reviewWarPlans is the "last word on AreaAI" and also lets bScheme describe
    the actual final current-war set rather than any superseded pass.

This clarification strengthens F183; it is not a new root.


F189 / provisional KI#512 -- ZERO-BOUNDARY CLARIFICATION
---------------------------------------------------------
The earlier confirmed scheme() zero-boundary root is broader once the current SAS
victory-denial boost is considered.

The inherited 2018 selector currently partitions only strict signs:

    if (iLimitedU < 0 && iTotalU > 0)
        bTotal = true;
    if (iLimitedU < 0 && iTotalU < 0)
        bTotal = (iTotalU > iLimitedU);
    if (iLimitedU > 0 && iTotalU > 0)
        ... leader-preference comparison ...

The already-recorded case iLimitedU == 0 && iTotalU > 0 starts LIMITED even though
TOTAL is the only positive evaluation. Current SAS exposes the opposite missed zero
boundary too: when iTotalU == 0 and iLimitedU < 0, bTotal remains false; the later
victory-denial utility boost can lift max(iLimitedU, iTotalU) above zero and make the
candidate actionable, at which point the AI starts LIMITED even though TOTAL was the
strictly better underlying plan. The wrong bTotal also selects the limited-plan naval
flag for the direct-war eligibility gate.

CORRECTNESS-FIRST REPAIR DIRECTION
    Handle all cases with at least one nonpositive utility by selecting the plan with
    the larger evaluated utility, e.g. conceptually:

        if (iLimitedU <= 0 || iTotalU <= 0)
            bTotal = (iTotalU > iLimitedU);
        else
            ... existing both-positive leader-preference comparison ...

    Preserve the existing both-positive preference logic; history shows that policy
    was the purpose of the 2018 change. This is a repair-boundary clarification of
    F189, not a second finding.


F192 / provisional KI#515
-------------------------
TITLE
    SAS victory-denial target selection can install a direct WARPLAN_LIMITED/TOTAL
    while a peace treaty still makes immediate declaration illegal.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED. AdvCiv-SAS regression introduced by commit 4210d5586a
    (2026-07-14), KI#184 victory-denial direct-war work; absent from Base AdvCiv 1.14.

ROOT
    Ordinary UWAI deliberately allows planning during temporary force peace:
    canSchemeAgainst calls canEventuallyDeclareWar, and CvTeam::canEventuallyDeclareWar
    does not reject isForcePeace. The separate CvTeam::canDeclareWar check does reject
    force peace. scheme() therefore attenuates target drive by treaty time remaining
    rather than excluding the target entirely.

    KI#184 computes:

        bool const bVictoryDenialDirect =
            (iVictoryDenialBoost > 0 &&
             isSASVictoryDenialDirectWarAllowed(...));

    isSASVictoryDenialDirectWarAllowed checks victory urgency, target power, distance
    and naval/land access, but not kAgent.canDeclareWar(eTarget). A treaty-time target
    can consequently enter TargetData with bDirect=true and a positive adjusted drive.

    Once selected, scheme() builds eWP from bDirect, so that target receives
    WARPLAN_LIMITED or WARPLAN_TOTAL. The execution branch is:

        if (aTargets[i].bDirect &&
            aTargets[i].iVictoryDenialBoost > 0 &&
            kAgent.canDeclareWar(eTarget))
        {
            kAgent.declareWar(eTarget, false, eWP);
        }
        else kAgent.AI_setWarPlan(eTarget, eWP);

    When force peace is the only blocker, canDeclareWar is false and the shared else
    installs that direct plan instead of the preparation plan that treaty-time UWAI
    normally uses.

REACHABILITY
    This does not require an impossible API combination. CvTeam::canChangeWarPeace
    and canEventuallyDeclareWar permit a future war despite an ordinary temporary
    treaty, while CvTeam::canDeclareWar separately rejects isForcePeace. scheme() even
    computes rPeacePortionRemaining specifically to leave a reduced, nonzero chance
    of beginning preparations during that period. A strong KI#184 utility boost can
    therefore make such a victory threat win the target-selection roll before the
    treaty expires.

CONSEQUENCE
    * A feature whose comments describe conversion to "immediate" war can create an
      imminent direct war plan without declaring war at all.
    * The same code then suppresses showWarPrepStartedMsg because bDirect is true; its
      comment says direct victory-denial wars "are already declared", which is false
      on this reachable branch.
    * The target bypasses the normal PREPARING plan state while declaration is still
      prohibited. CvTeamAI::AI_mayAttack prevents treaty violation, so this is not an
      illegal attack, but it is still the wrong strategic state and can enter the
      inherited imminent-plan timeout/review path rather than ordinary preparation.

ANCESTRY / INTENT EVIDENCE
    Commit 4210d5586a introduced both the direct-plan conversion and the guarded
    declareWar call. Its source comments say qualifying targets are converted to
    "immediate limited/total war" and that direct victory-denial wars "are already
    declared". The fallback-to-AI_setWarPlan branch existed for ordinary preparations
    and was reused without converting eWP back to PREPARING when declaration is
    temporarily impossible.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    Keep the victory-denial utility pressure during force peace, but make bDirect true
    only when an actual declaration is legal now (equivalently, fall back to the
    corresponding PREPARING_LIMITED/PREPARING_TOTAL plan when canDeclareWar is false).
    This preserves treaty-time preparation and the KI#184 urgency boost while making
    the "direct" state mean what its declaration/message logic assumes it means.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS
    * This is distinct from the previously rejected general observation that direct
      plans can coexist briefly with force peace: considerConcludePreparations
      intentionally allows an existing preparation to become direct within a narrow
      <=3-turn treaty window. F192 is about fresh KI#184 selection marking a target
      direct for any treaty duration without first establishing that declaration is
      legal now.
    * CvTeamAI::AI_mayAttack does prevent units from violating the treaty. The finding
      is therefore not "AI attacks through force peace"; it is the direct-vs-preparing
      state mismatch and the resulting wrong review/message contract.


NEGATIVE CONTROLS SINCE C017-WIP07
-----------------------------------
* acceptVassal's apparently contradictory empty-new-enemy assertion is protected by
  CvTeamAI::AI_vassalTrade, which calls UWAI acceptance only after finding at least one
  new major-civ war for the prospective master using the same enemy class;
* warConfidenceLearned's sign-sensitive bIgnoreDefOnly equality is intentional: the
  v0.86 history explicitly repaired ignored past-war success while retaining the rule
  that defensive victories should not easily embolden future aggression;
* amendTensions' late-era ask-for-help multiplier can become nonpositive, but this is
  inherited original-UWAI policy and ScaledNum::randSuccess intentionally converts
  nonpositive probabilities to no contact;
* the local-target nearest-city sentinel -1 is guarded in gameplay paths by mutual
  UWAI land-target tests (zero-city teams cannot satisfy UWAI::Team::isLandTarget),
  while the victory-direct helper explicitly rejects negative distance;
* no additional signed-rounding sibling of F191 survived: the other uround() sites in
  this file have nonnegative inputs at their call sites.

F193 / provisional KI#516
-------------------------
TITLE
    Inverted human-master test prevents AI vassals from timing out the very
    human-instructed war preparations that UWAI says should expire after 20 turns.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED. Inherited AdvCiv defect present from the initial UWAI integration,
    commit f6ff6a182f (2017-04-16, "Initial commit (cont.)"), and unchanged in
    Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.

ROOT
    UWAI::Team::doWar contains the explicit contract:

        /* Non-human vassals abandon human-instructed war prep. after 20 turns.
           Humans can have war preparations from AI Auto Play that they should
           also abandon ... */

    but gates the timeout with:

        (kAgent.isHuman() || !GET_TEAM(kAgent.getMasterTeam()).isHuman())

    doWar enters this block only for a human team or a vassal. For the exact first
    case named by the comment -- a non-human vassal whose master is human -- both
    operands are false, so the timeout can never run. Conversely, a non-human
    vassal of an AI master passes the negated second operand.

REACHABILITY / CALLER CONTRACT
    This is not a dead theoretical combination. CvDiplomacy.py retains K-Mod's UI:

        "Allow masters to tell their vassals to prepare for war"

    and exposes that option to a human master whose AI vassal is currently at peace.
    USER_DIPLOCOMMENT_WARPLAN_TARGET sends DIPLOEVENT_SET_WARPLAN, and
    CvPlayer::handleDiploEvent directly executes:

        kOurTeam.AI_setWarPlan((TeamTypes)iData1, (WarPlanTypes)iData2, false);

    Thus a human master can install PREPARING_LIMITED/PREPARING_TOTAL on an AI
    vassal exactly as the UWAI timeout comment describes.

INTERNAL CROSS-CHECK
    The master synchronization immediately below reinforces the intended split:

        else if (kMaster.AI_getWarPlan(eTarget) != NO_WARPLAN &&
                 !kMaster.isHuman()) // Human master will have to instruct us
            kAgent.AI_setWarPlan(eTarget, WARPLAN_PREPARING_LIMITED);

    AI masters continuously propagate their own preparations to AI vassals; human
    masters deliberately do not, because the human must issue the instruction.
    Therefore the expiring/manual preparation is specifically the human-master case,
    while the AI-master case is maintained automatically.

CURRENT WRONG-SIDE CONSEQUENCE
    For an AI-master vassal older than 20 turns, the current condition does enter:

        considerAbandonPreparations(eTarget, -1, 0);

    With iU=-1 and iTurnsRemaining=0, that helper deterministically clears the
    preparation. If the AI master still has a war plan, the synchronization block
    immediately afterward reinstalls WARPLAN_PREPARING_LIMITED. CvTeamAI::AI_setWarPlan
    resets the target's war-plan state counter to 0 whenever the plan value changes.
    The inverted gate can therefore periodically clear/reinstall/reset an AI-master
    vassal's inherited preparation while leaving a stale human-instructed preparation
    untouched indefinitely.

ANCESTRY / INTENT EVIDENCE
    The condition and the explanatory comment entered together in the initial UWAI
    AdvCiv commit f6ff6a182f on 2017-04-16. Later refactors retained the same boolean
    logic. The adjacent master-sync comment and the pre-existing diplomacy UI both
    independently agree with the prose contract, not with the negated condition.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    The narrow repair is to remove the negation from the master-human test:

        kAgent.isHuman() || GET_TEAM(kAgent.getMasterTeam()).isHuman()

    This keeps the AI-AutoPlay human-team timeout, enables the advertised timeout for
    AI vassals manually instructed by human masters, and avoids independently timing
    out the preparations that AI masters continuously propagate to their vassals.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS
    * The condition is safe for an ordinary non-vassal human: short-circuiting on
      kAgent.isHuman() means getMasterTeam() need not establish vassal semantics.
    * This is not merely a stale comment. The K-Mod/AdvCiv diplomacy path still lets a
      human master issue the preparation, and the adjacent synchronization code still
      explicitly treats human-master instructions as manual rather than inherited.
    * The finding does not require changing the 20-turn policy itself; only which
      master type is eligible for that already-documented policy is inverted.


NEGATIVE CONTROLS SINCE C017-WIP08
-----------------------------------
* respondToRebuke(false) does not become F193: UWAI has deliberately represented the
  non-preparation rebuke response as a direct WARPLAN_LIMITED since its first AdvCiv
  integration; the older generic CvPlayerAI comment saying "immediately declares war"
  is not enough to prove that UWAI's distinct war-plan contract is defective;
* isPeaceDealPossible's apparently reversed endWarVal direction is consistent with
  endWarVal's human/AI normalization: the helper computes the human-side payment need
  and then tests exactly the human assets that could satisfy it;
* Civ4CE-main in the supplied snapshot contains no UWAI/UWAIAgent/WarEvaluator
  implementation, so it cannot provide an independent later implementation or fix for
  file 017; Base AdvCiv 1.14 plus the supplied AdvCiv/SAS history mirrors remain the
  applicable ancestry controls here.

F194 / provisional KI#517
-------------------------
TITLE
    doWarReport's background-mode toggle does not update UWAI::Team's cached
    background state, so the supposedly diagnostic report run can mutate real war
    plans, peace, capitulation and declarations.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED. Inherited AdvCiv developer/debug-path defect. The cached Team
    background state dates to the initial UWAI integration; doWarReport was later
    added by AdvCiv commit a8a7e75c6c ("Some bugfixes (in K-Mod, Kek-Mod, AdvCiv
    code)") without synchronizing that cache. The same mismatch survives in Base
    AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.

ROOT
    UWAI::Team::reset stores background mode in a member cache:

        m_bInBackground = getUWAI().isEnabled(true);

    and every Team-side mutation guard reads only that cache:

        bool isInBackground() const { return m_bInBackground; }

    doWarReport is documented as:

        "Runs 'scheme' as if UWAI was running in the background ... Intended for
         debugging."

    but implements the temporary mode only through the global UWAI object:

        bool bInBackground = getUWAI().isEnabled(true);
        getUWAI().setInBackground(true);
        setForceReport(true);
        doWar();
        setForceReport(false);
        getUWAI().setInBackground(bInBackground);

    It never updates or resets this Team's m_bInBackground around doWar().

REACHABILITY / STATE PROOF
    doWarReport first requires getUWAI().isEnabled() with the default argument. By
    UWAI::isEnabled's contract, that is true only when UWAI is fully enabled and the
    global m_bInBackground is false. In that normal mode, Team::reset has cached
    m_bInBackground=false. doWarReport then changes the global value to true but
    leaves the Team cache false, and immediately invokes doWar().

    This is precisely the mode in which the documented manual debugging recipe is
    intended to be used: insert a doWarReport call, load the save to inspect, trigger
    the call, read the report, then remove the instrumentation.

CONSEQUENCE
    doWar and its subroutines currently contain many side-effect gates of the form:

        if (!isInBackground())

    Because the stale Team cache remains false, those branches are active during the
    report run. Reachable effects include, depending on the evaluated state:

    * canceling or changing existing war plans;
    * switching preparation targets;
    * setting new preparation/direct plans;
    * declaring an eligible direct victory-denial war;
    * negotiating/implementing peace;
    * capitulation and voluntary-vassal actions;
    * spectator war-plan messages associated with those real state changes.

    At the same time the global UWAI mode has been changed to background, so helpers
    that consult the global state can be evaluating under background assumptions while
    Team-side code still commits the result as though this were a real synchronized
    doWar turn. A diagnostic call can therefore perturb the very save state it is
    supposed to inspect.

ANCESTRY / INTENT EVIDENCE
    The original Team cache comment says the background value is cached during reset
    rather than queried repeatedly. Later commit a8a7e75c6c added doWarReport and its
    explicit "as if ... running in the background" contract, but toggled only the
    global object. Subsequent renames/refactors preserved both pieces independently;
    the 2021 UWAI rewrite still assigns m_bInBackground only in Team::reset.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    Keep global and Team-local background state synchronized for the whole report
    scope. A narrow repair can save m_bInBackground, set it true alongside
    getUWAI().setInBackground(true), then restore both after doWar(); alternatively,
    call/reset the Team cache after each global mode change. Preserve setForceReport
    independently, since forcing output and suppressing mutations are separate jobs.

    Do not merely change the comment or remove the global toggle: WarEvaluator and
    other UWAI code can consult the global background mode, while Team mutation gates
    consult the cached member. Both views need to agree.

SEVERITY / SCOPE
    This is developer-facing rather than ordinary autonomous gameplay: doWarReport is
    a manual diagnostic helper and has no normal production caller in the supplied
    source. It is nevertheless a real correctness defect because its documented use
    can alter the loaded save while investigating it, potentially invalidating the
    report/reproduction being debugged.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS
    * This is not the disabled-UWAI case. doWarReport returns immediately unless
      getUWAI().isEnabled() is true, which strengthens the proof: its reachable entry
      mode starts with the global and Team cache both false, then only the global flag
      is flipped.
    * setForceReport only overrides report cadence; it does not alter
      m_bInBackground and therefore cannot suppress state mutation.
    * Merely restoring the global flag at function exit does not undo war-plan,
      diplomacy or declaration mutations that already occurred during doWar().


NEGATIVE CONTROLS SINCE C017-WIP09
-----------------------------------
* KI#184.2's shared SAS_UWAI_VICTORY_DENIAL_DIRECT_MAX_DISTANCE is intentionally
  interpreted in two different distance representations: nearest-city plot distance
  in target selection and cached path/travel turns in WarUtilityAspect's contact
  guard. Commit 85b3818317 and the XML/source comments explicitly document this dual
  use, so the unit difference is policy rather than an accidental mismatch;
* the preferred-local-target and "roll only best eligible target" passes both use the
  same aAdjustedDrives values after AI_isAvoidWar hesitation and repeat the same local
  skip predicate; no preselection/eligibility drift survived that cross-check;
* the 2019 human-peace iDelta==0 arithmetic guard remains present after the 2021 UWAI
  rewrite, and the later capitulation skip-probability fixes inspected in ancestry are
  likewise still represented in current code;
* the remaining direct AI_setWarPlan / declareWar transition sweep found no new
  independent gameplay root beyond F188, F192 and F193 already recorded.

F195 / provisional KI#518
-------------------------
TITLE
    AdvCiv's 2021 random-team-member diplomacy change left amendTensions with its
    old leader-only assertion, so valid nonleader diplomats trip a debug assertion.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED. Inherited AdvCiv regression introduced by commit f016996eb6
    (2021-03-27), "Let UWAI negotiate with a random team member"; present in Base
    AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.

ROOT
    UWAI::Player::amendTensions begins with:

        FAssert(GET_PLAYER(eHuman).isHuman());
        FAssert(GET_TEAM(m_eAgent).getLeaderID() == m_eAgent);

    That second invariant was originally valid: initial UWAI scheme() contacted the
    human through leaderUWAI().amendTensions(...).

    AdvCiv commit f016996eb6 deliberately changed war-related diplomacy away from
    team leaders. In scheme(), it replaced the leader call with:

        PlayerTypes eTargetPlayer = GET_TEAM(eTarget).getRandomMemberAlive(true);
        CvPlayerAI& kAgentPlayer = GET_PLAYER(kAgent.getRandomMemberAlive(false));
        ...
        kAgentPlayer.uwai().amendTensions(eTargetPlayer);

    but did not remove or adapt amendTensions' leader-only assertion.

REACHABILITY / INTENT PROOF
    CvTeam::getRandomMemberAlive explicitly documents its purpose:

        "pick members for conducting war-related diplomacy -- instead of using the
         team leaders"

    The introducing commit is titled "Let UWAI negotiate with a random team member"
    and says "... instead of the team leader. Human members strictly preferred."
    Thus selecting a nonleader is not an accidental caller state; it is the feature.

    On any non-human team with more than one alive AI member, scheme() can select a
    nonleader whenever a human target survives the target checks, the preparation
    roll fails, utility is <=23 and contact is possible. Current SAS's KI#207 repair
    to getRandomMemberAlive also makes the eligible-member selection genuinely
    uniform instead of relying on the older broken iterator-index comparison, so the
    nonleader path is straightforwardly reachable.

CONSEQUENCE
    In debug/assert-enabled builds, a legitimate multi-player-team diplomacy path can
    stop on a false assertion even though the caller is behaving exactly as the 2021
    feature intended. This can disrupt team-game/autoplay debugging and misleadingly
    suggest state corruption.

    In release builds the assertion is normally absent and the function proceeds.
    The called CvPlayerAI diplomacy helpers (AI_demandTribute, AI_askHelp,
    AI_contactReligion, AI_contactCivics) operate on the selected player and do not
    impose a team-leader requirement, reinforcing that the stale assertion rather
    than the random-member caller is the inconsistent piece.

ANCESTRY
    * 2017 initial UWAI: amendTensions asserts that its agent is the team leader;
      scheme calls leaderUWAI(), so the invariant is valid.
    * 2021-03-27 f016996eb6: scheme is intentionally changed to a random alive team
      member and calls that member's uwai().amendTensions; the assertion is untouched.
    * Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS both retain the random-member caller plus the
      obsolete leader-only assertion.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    Remove the leader-only assertion (or replace it with an invariant that actually
    matches the random-member contract, such as ordinary alive/team membership if a
    defensive assertion is still desired). Do not revert scheme() to the team leader:
    the commit history and CvTeam helper comment explicitly establish random-member
    diplomacy as intentional.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS
    * This is not a claim that every amendTensions call must use a nonleader; single-
      member teams and random selection of the leader remain fine. The defect is that
      a valid nonleader selection contradicts a leftover assertion.
    * doWar returns early for human teams, so the agent-side scheme path here concerns
      AI-only teams; getRandomMemberAlive(false) may select any alive AI member.
    * The human target side is separately constrained by getRandomMemberAlive(true),
      matching amendTensions' first assertion that eHuman is human.

* The final FAssert/Tbd/Hack sweep was reopened rather than closed when the

  independent root rather than a split of F183-F194.
* The remaining contact helpers called by amendTensions were inspected and do not
  require the acting AI player to be its team's leader.

F196 / provisional KI#519
-------------------------
TITLE
    Human-capitulation readiness persists across peace, so a later war can inherit
    an obsolete considerPeace authorization and bypass UWAI's AI-turn surrender gate.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED. Inherited AdvCiv lifecycle defect dating to the initial UWAI
    integration; present in Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.

ROOT
    UWAI uses the leader cache's m_readyToCapitulateTo set as a temporal authorization
    for surrender to a human master. considerCapitulation deliberately sets the bit
    before AI_surrenderTrade and leaves it set when capitulation is genuinely accepted:

        if (bHumanMaster)
            leaderCache().setReadyToCapitulate(eMaster, true);
        ...
        if (eDenial != NO_DENIAL)
        {
            ...
            if (bHumanMaster)
                leaderCache().setReadyToCapitulate(eMaster, false);
            return true;
        }

    The accompanying comment on the denial clear states the purpose explicitly:

        "To ensure that the capitulation decision is made on an AI turn;
         so that tryFindingMaster and AI_doSplit are called by considerPeace."

    CvTeamAI::AI_surrenderTrade enforces that contract for a human prospective master:

        /* Make sure that UWAI::Team::considerPeace has been called before surrendering. */
        if (getUWAI().isEnabled() && kMasterTeam.isHuman() &&
            !uwai().leaderUWAI().getCache().isReadyToCapitulate(eMasterTeam))
        {
            return DENIAL_RECENT_CANCEL;
        }

    The problem is lifecycle reset. reviewWarPlans clears the bit for a human target
    only inside its target loop, after an earlier no-war-plan return:

        if (!kAgent.AI_isAnyWarPlan())
            return true;
        ...
        if (kTarget.isHuman())
            leaderCache().setReadyToCapitulate(eTarget, false);

    If an authorized war ends before a later review, neither Team::reportWarEnding,
    UWAICache::reportWarEnding, CvTeamAI::AI_preMakePeace nor AI_postMakePeace clears
    m_readyToCapitulateTo. AI_preDeclareWar / AI_postDeclareWar do not clear it either.
    Consequently the old authorization can survive peace and enter a later war.

REACHABILITY / CONSEQUENCE
    A concrete lifecycle is:

    1. During war A against human team H, considerCapitulation reaches NO_DENIAL and
       leaves ReadyToCapitulate(H) true so a human capitulation deal can be offered.
    2. H does not accept that capitulation; war A later ends by ordinary peace.
    3. AI_postMakePeace resets war success and both war plans, but the readiness bit
       survives. If there are no other plans, reviewWarPlans' early return also leaves
       it untouched.
    4. H later starts war B. Before the victim AI gets its next considerPeace pass,
       the stale true bit can satisfy AI_surrenderTrade's explicit temporal gate once
       the other surrender criteria become true.

    This is not a claim that the AI necessarily capitulates immediately at zero war
    success. AI_surrenderTrade still has the ordinary power, war-success, city and
    diplomatic gates, and war success was reset at the old peace. The concrete defect
    is that the old war's authorization is reused in the new war. For example, a human
    can declare war and inflict enough losses/city captures during the same human turn
    for the normal surrender criteria to become true before the victim's AI turn.

    UWAI::Player::willTalk makes that stale authorization more consequential because
    surrender is tested before the one-turn refusal-to-talk gate:

        if (GET_TEAM(m_eAgent).AI_surrenderTrade(TEAMID(eToPlayer)) == NO_DENIAL)
            return 1;
        if (iAtWarCounter <= 1 || ...)
            return -1;

    Thus, once the normal surrender checks pass, the stale bit can make the AI willing
    to talk/capitulate before considerPeace has run in the current war -- precisely
    what the original AI-turn safeguard says it is intended to prevent.

PERSISTENCE / RESET PROOF
    Exhaustive setReadyToCapitulate call-site search in the current source found only:

    * reviewWarPlans: clear per human target during a review;
    * considerCapitulation: set before the human-master surrender check;
    * considerCapitulation: clear again on denial;
    * UWAICache implementation / leader migration plumbing.

    There is no peace-end or war-start clear. UWAICache::reportWarEnding clears bounty
    and sponsor state and records past-war success, but not readiness.

    m_readyToCapitulateTo is also written to and restored from the savegame stream.
    Therefore this is persistent cache state, not temporary stack/turn state; saving
    during the stale interval does not repair it.

ANCESTRY
    The initial AdvCiv UWAI integration introduced the same combination of behaviors:

    * the no-war-plan early return in reviewWarPlans;
    * the per-human readiness clear inside the later target loop;
    * set true before a human-master surrender check;
    * clear on denial specifically to keep the decision on an AI turn;
    * the AI_surrenderTrade readiness gate.

    Later UWAI rewrites/refactors preserve the lifecycle. Searches of current Base
    AdvCiv 1.14 and SAS show no later war-end/new-war clear.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    Clear this authorization when the corresponding war ends, rather than waiting for
    a future review. A file-017-local repair fits naturally in UWAI::Team::reportWarEnding:

        if (GET_TEAM(eEnemy).isHuman())
            leaderCache().setReadyToCapitulate(eEnemy, false);

    before or after forwarding reportWarEnding to member caches. That lifecycle point
    is called from CvTeamAI::AI_preMakePeace while the old war context still exists and
    is semantically exact: authorization produced for that war expires with that war.

    Clearing during an actual capitulation is harmless: AI_surrenderTrade has already
    approved the deal and the relationship is transitioning to vassalage. A clear on
    new declaration can be useful defense-in-depth, but it is weaker as the primary
    repair because the stale state should not survive the preceding peace at all.

    Merely moving the reviewWarPlans clear ahead of the no-war-plan early return is
    also insufficient: there can still be a peace-to-new-DoW window before that team's
    next review.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS
    * The finding does not remove or weaken the normal capitulation criteria; it only
      restores the intended current-war/AI-turn authorization lifetime.
    * The persistent bit is intentionally kept true after NO_DENIAL while the current
      war remains live so a human can receive/accept the capitulation; clearing it at
      every function exit would break that feature.
    * The correct boundary is therefore war lifetime, not function lifetime.

C017-WIP13 APPEND -- F197 / provisional KI#520

F197 / provisional KI#520 -- INHERITED ADVCIV DEBUG ASSERTION DEFECT:
UWAI brokered-peace valuation asserts that war duration is strictly positive even
though a valid brokered-peace valuation can occur on the declaration turn with an
at-war counter of 0; the formula itself is already safe for 0.

LOCATION / LIVE CODE
    CvGameCoreDLL/UWAIAgent.cpp, UWAI::Team::makePeaceTradeVal:

        int iWarDuration = kAgent.AI_getAtWarCounter(eEnemy);
        FAssert(iWarDuration > 0);
        /*  warDuration could be as small as 1 I think. Then the mark-up is
            +175% in the Ancient era. None for a Renaissance war after 15 turns. */
        scaled rTimeModifier = (fixp(5.5) - kAgent.AI_getCurrEraFactor() / 2) /
                scaled(iWarDuration + 1).sqrt();

    The asserted invariant is stronger than both the actual trade API contract and
    the arithmetic requirement. The expression is perfectly defined at 0 because it
    takes sqrt(iWarDuration + 1).

REACHABILITY / CALLER CONTRACT
    CvTeamAI::AI_makePeaceTradeVal requires only that the two relevant teams are at
    war before forwarding to UWAI. It has no minimum-war-age precondition.

    TRADE_PEACE likewise has no age gate. CvPlayer::canTradeItem accepts a peace-
    brokerage item whenever the AI's team is at war with that third team and the
    ordinary contact/team-status conditions hold. CvPlayer::getTradeDenial forwards
    the item to CvTeamAI::AI_makePeaceTrade; UWAI::Team::makePeaceTrade contains no
    minimum at-war-counter check either.

    The normal human-AI trade table exposes third-party TRADE_PEACE items from the AI
    side when they are otherwise tradeable. If the AI's makePeaceTrade denial returns
    NO_DENIAL, AI_considerOffer proceeds to AI_dealVal, whose TRADE_PEACE case calls
    AI_makePeaceTradeVal and therefore reaches this assertion.

ZERO-COUNTER LIFECYCLE
    CvTeamAI::AI_doCounter increments AI_getAtWarCounter only during CvTeam::doTurn
    when the teams are already at war. An ended war has its counter reset to 0 in
    AI_postMakePeace. A declaration later in a turn does not pre-increment that
    counter; AI_postDeclareWar resets peace/share-war state and installs war plans,
    but leaves the new war duration at its legitimate initial value 0.

    Therefore a war declared after the team's counter update has a real interval in
    which isAtWar(eEnemy) is true while AI_getAtWarCounter(eEnemy) == 0. A broker can
    reach diplomacy in that interval (particularly straightforward in human / network
    turn-order cases). There is no denial-side age rule that excludes it.

    NO_DENIAL at age 0 is also not forbidden by UWAI semantics. makePeaceTrade bases
    the decision on the two teams' reluctanceToPeace values and contact state, not on
    iWarDuration. For example, a modestly reluctant aggressor (<55) and an enemy whose
    reluctance is nonpositive satisfies the normal no-denial branch; defensive-pact,
    vassal/cascade and otherwise unattractive fresh wars provide ordinary ways for
    immediate peace utility to be low or negative.

ANCESTRY / INTERNAL CONTROL
    This assertion and the accompanying "could be as small as 1" comment date to the
    initial AdvCiv UWAI integration (practical commit 1253, f6ff6a182f, 2017-04-16)
    and remain in Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS.

    The legacy CvTeamAI::AI_makePeaceTradeVal path is useful independent evidence that
    the public valuation contract never required a positive age: it computes with

        AI_getAtWarCounter(ePeaceTeam) + 10

    and therefore naturally accepts a 0-turn war. UWAI changed the pricing formula but
    did not add a caller-side minimum-age rule.

CONSEQUENCE / SEVERITY
    In assertion-enabled builds, a legitimate same-round brokered-peace valuation can
    trip FAssert(iWarDuration > 0). This is a debug/developer correctness defect.

    This is NOT a claim of a release-build divide-by-zero or invalid square root. The
    current formula is safe at 0 and produces a defined, deliberately high early-war
    markup. With assertions compiled out, the mathematical path continues normally.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    The narrow repair is to relax/remove the invalid positive-age assertion. If an
    invariant check is desired, the actual domain is nonnegative:

        FAssert(iWarDuration >= 0);

    No denominator clamp or behavioral age gate is required; adding one would alter
    valid pricing semantics rather than merely repair the assertion contract.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS
    * No TRADE_PEACE_TREATY/direct bilateral-peace behavior is implicated here; this
      finding concerns the third-party TRADE_PEACE brokerage valuation.
    * No claim is made that every declaration-turn brokerage is accepted. The defect
      needs only one legal NO_DENIAL state; makePeaceTrade has no rule excluding age 0.
    * The arithmetic itself is already robust at zero, so this root is intentionally
      classified as assertion/debug-path scope rather than inflated into a gameplay
      crash or numeric corruption finding.

FINAL NEGATIVE CONTROLS / REJECTIONS
------------------------------------
The following late candidates were intentionally NOT assigned F198:

1. Background review helpers can report a simulated plan change while suppressing the
   real mutation. That is part of the normal background-evaluation design; the proven
   defect remains F194, where doWarReport toggles only the global background flag while
   Team::m_bInBackground stays stale and therefore fails to suppress those mutations.

2. The 2021 random-member peace/vassal diplomacy conversion does not create a
   team-global contact-timer bypass. The underlying diplomacy system intentionally
   stores CONTACT_PEACE_TREATY timers per player pair, and ordinary non-UWAI diplomacy
   can likewise contact another member of the same enemy team while one pair is on
   cooldown. F195 remains the isolated stale leader-only amendTensions assertion.

3. scheme's sorted TargetData/aAdjustedDrives metadata stays index-aligned through the
   preferred-local-target prepass, best-eligible-target pass and final selection. The
   best-target logging also initializes eBestEligibleTarget before any dereference in
   the non-best-only mode.

4. scheme's skipped-total INT_MIN value is never fed into the later victory boost,
   divisor or ScaledNum arithmetic. It participates only in comparisons/logging until
   iU takes max(iLimitedU, iTotalU). The real zero-partition plan-type defect remains
   F189; no independent sentinel root survives.

5. considerSwitchTarget's ratio denominator is positive whenever an alternative
   target exists. Its padding lifts the smaller utility to 20 when necessary, while a
   no-padding path requires the selected alternative to exceed a current utility of at
   least 20.

6. The apparently strict confidenceFromWarSuccess reciprocal at-war-counter assertion
   is not promoted. War declaration/peace reset reciprocal counters together, ordinary
   team-turn ordering explains the documented small skew, and permanent-alliance
   merging explicitly re-synchronizes the counterpart counters. No reachable >2 skew
   was established.

7. tradeValJointWar's non-human-ally assertion is preserved. Both normal AI diplomacy
   and Rise & Fall replacement valuation call it with an AI ally; no human-ally caller
   was found.

8. uEndAllWars/acceptVassal empty-vector assertions remain caller-protected rather than
   hidden crashes. Vote validity and AI_vassalTrade respectively establish the
   applicable enemy set before the UWAI entry points are used.

9. getSASBBAINearestCityDistance returning -1 for no city pair does not create a
   preferred-local phantom target because the mutual AI_isLandTarget eligibility gate
   rejects the no-source-city case before the distance threshold is decisive.

10. The diagnostic WAR_TARGET_PLAN_SET row can also be emitted after the direct
    declaration branch. The label/comment is somewhat broader than the nearby wording,
    but the declaration really does install that war plan; this is logging naming,
    not a gameplay/state root.

11. report ownership is balanced: every path after startReport in doWar reaches
    closeReport, and the Team destructor remains a final safety delete. setForceReport
    has no independent persistent-state leak beyond F194's background-cache mismatch.

12. Civ4CE supplied with this audit contains no UWAI/UWAIAgent/WarEvaluator
    implementation, so there is no independent CE-side implementation or later UWAI
    fix to compare for file 017. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and the bundled AdvCiv history mirrors
    remain the appropriate ancestry controls here.

F198 / provisional KI#521 -- CONFIRMED
--------------------------------------
Inherited AdvCiv debug assertion defect: a legal human BOMBARD mission against an
undefended city can trip AI_bestUnitForMission's iDefenders > 0 assertion.

Root:
    CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_bestUnitForMission(MISSION_BOMBARD)

The human-only branch computes the number of defending units on the bombard target
and then asserts:

    FAssertMsg(iDefenders > 0, "AI bombards undefended city");

That invariant is false for a legal human command. The full caller/legality chain was
checked rather than inferred from the local function:

1. CvSelectionGroup::canDoMission(MISSION_BOMBARD) exposes the mission when any
   movable group unit satisfies CvUnit::canBombard.
2. CvUnit::canBombard requires positive bombard rate, attacks remaining, no cargo,
   and a non-null bombardTarget. It does not require a defending unit.
3. CvUnit::bombardTarget accepts an adjacent CvCity when CvCity::isBombardable does.
4. CvCity::isBombardable also has no defender requirement. In particular, its
   advc.004c human behavior deliberately permits legal bombardment of a city whose
   defenses can still be reduced/kept at zero even when no unit defends it.
5. CvSelectionGroup's MISSION_BOMBARD executor calls
   AI_bestUnitForMission(MISSION_BOMBARD) for the human command too.
6. Therefore a human can legally issue Bombard with iDefenders == 0 and reach this
   human-only assertion.

The assertion text itself is additional evidence of a stale invariant: it says
"AI bombards undefended city" despite sitting in the else branch of if (!isHuman()).

Release-build arithmetic is already safe. The later attacker/defender ratio uses
std::max(iDefenders, 1), so zero defenders do not create a divide-by-zero. This root
should therefore remain scoped as a debug/assertion correctness defect, not described
as a release crash or as invalid Bombard gameplay.

Ancestry/control:
- The block comes from AdvCiv's advc.004c mission-selection rewrite and survives in
  Base AdvCiv 1.14.
- The local Civ4CE branch does not carry this AdvCiv selector/assertion rewrite.
- No existing KI#521 collision was found in the reconciled album/Known Issues at the
  time of promotion.

Narrow repair boundary:
- Remove or relax the iDefenders > 0 assertion for the human path.
- Do NOT add a defender requirement to canBombard/isBombardable; undefended-city
  bombardment is intentionally legal for humans.
- Existing std::max(iDefenders, 1) arithmetic protection can remain.

  AI_counterMove -> AI_separate looked promising, but AI_separate removes the head
  first into a fresh group, so the old group's head ID changes/disappears and the
  tripwire correctly detects progress. Other split/load cases either replace the
  head similarly or queue a mission. No generic "snapshot group size too" root.
- SAS low-power / obsolete-sacrifice attacker ordering: the low-power mode is used by
  the real post-declaration attack loop, so its inherited canMoveInto(..., true)
  legality does not accidentally need the potential-enemy mode. iUnitOdds == -1

  alias the stale ID because the full ID contains a generation component and getAt

C018-WIP02 -- PRIORITY FILE 041 CvSelectionGroupAI.cpp -- SECOND DURABLE HANDOFF

SOURCE / CURSOR

C018-WIP01 is an exact byte prefix of this checkpoint. Investigation continued from

F199 / provisional KI#522 -- CONFIRMED
--------------------------------------
AdvCiv-SAS regression in the KI#319/5093 no-progress safeguard: legitimate AI sea-
transport unloads can be mistaken for "no progress" because the tripwire does not
observe cargo-state changes, so the transport receives MISSION_SKIP instead of
immediately reconsidering its next action.

Root:
    CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_update

Current tripwire snapshots only:
- head unit ID;
- head UnitAI role;
- head x/y;
- head remaining moves;
- selection-group mission-queue length.

If all those values are unchanged after CvUnitAI::AI_update, the group is not busy and
can still move, the safeguard pushes MISSION_SKIP and breaks the update loop.

That predicate misses an inherited and explicitly intentional class of progress:
unloading cargo at the destination without pushing a mission.

The cleanest concrete path is CvUnitAI::AI_specialSeaTransportSpy:

    if (atPlot(pTargetPlot))
    {
        getGroup()->unloadAll();
        getGroup()->setActivityType(ACTIVITY_AWAKE);
        // no actual mission pushed, but we need to rethink our next move.
        return true;
    }

AI_spySeaMove calls AI_specialSeaTransportSpy while carrying UNITAI_SPY cargo and
returns after this helper returns true. Control then returns through CvUnitAI::AI_update
to CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_update.

The unload is real state progress but does not alter any field currently observed by
the SAS tripwire:

1. CvSelectionGroup::unloadAll iterates the group's transports and calls
   CvUnit::unloadAll.
2. On a legal coastal-land destination, the Spy cargo can unload. Its
   setTransportUnit(NULL) call decrements the old transport's cargo count through
   changeCargo(-1).
3. This does not move the sea transport, consume the transport's remaining moves,
   change its UnitAI role or head identity, or push a mission on the transport group.
4. The helper explicitly leaves the transport group ACTIVITY_AWAKE.
5. Therefore, if the transport still has movement left, !isBusy() and
   readyToMove(true) remain true while every currently snapshotted field compares
   equal.
6. The tripwire consequently pushes MISSION_SKIP and breaks, suppressing the immediate
   same-turn reconsideration that the inherited helper explicitly requests.

This is not limited to the Spy helper. Current CvUnitAI retains the same missionless
unload + ACTIVITY_AWAKE + return-true pattern in multiple transport paths, including:
- AI_transportGoTo;
- the at-destination AI_settlerSeaTransport branches (now using SAS's
  AI_unloadSettlerCargoForDestination helper);
- AI_settlerSeaFerry;
- AI_specialSeaTransportMissionary;
- AI_specialSeaTransportSpy.

Historical intent is unusually strong. K-Mod commit bc00e144af6b2cf937eee0a7dea246907c048652
(practical 849), titled "Told the AI to explicitly wake their group in a few places.",
added setActivityType(ACTIVITY_AWAKE) to six such at-destination unload branches. The
Spy branch already carried the literal explanation that there is "no actual mission
pushed" because the unit needs to rethink its next move. In inherited pre-SAS
CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_update, the still-awake/movable group therefore naturally
iterates again after the cargo transition.

The conflicting SAS safeguard arrived much later in commit
1798ac76f438e0c42602efb5e09819192efc06b2 (practical 5093), whose no-progress
predicate initially observed only head geometry/moves and mission-queue length.
KI#319, fixed in commit 47ddc58905f42ffb8724b436c976ccf33c6f572d (practical 6211),
correctly expanded that predicate with head identity and UnitAI role after a different
legitimate state transition exposed the same design weakness. Cargo progress remains
unobserved, so F199 is a second concrete incomplete-predicate case in the same
safeguard family rather than a new inherited transport bug.

Reachability is concrete rather than theoretical. AI_specialSeaTransportSpy searches
coastal land owned by known civs and explicitly values a target city when not at war;
a sea transport can legally occupy an accessible coastal city, arrive with Spy cargo,
unload there, and retain movement. The helper's own atPlot branch exists specifically
for that reached-destination state.

Narrow repair boundary:
- Preserve the no-progress safeguard; it fixes a real inherited Scout/Explorer loop.
- Count cargo-state change as progress. A direct low-risk repair is to snapshot the
  selection group's total getCargo() value at loop entry and require it to be
  unchanged before pushing MISSION_SKIP.
- Prefer group cargo rather than only pHeadUnit->getCargo(), because a multi-transport
  group can unload cargo from a non-head transport as well.
- The post-action getCargo() comparison can remain late in the conjunction so the
  extra group scan is only performed after the cheaper identity/role/geometry/move/
  queue tests have already matched; the initial cargo snapshot still costs one small
  group scan per loop iteration.
- Do NOT "fix" the transport helpers by removing ACTIVITY_AWAKE or forcing them to
  consume their turn; K-Mod deliberately added the wake-up behavior so they can
  reconsider immediately after unloading.

No existing KI#522 or F199 collision was found in the current reconciled snapshot at
promotion time.

C018-WIP03 -- PRIORITY FILE 041 CvSelectionGroupAI.cpp -- THIRD DURABLE HANDOFF

SOURCE / CURSOR

F200 / provisional KI#523 -- CONFIRMED
--------------------------------------
Inherited AdvCiv arithmetic/contract defect in CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_getWeightedOdds:
the function explicitly tries to remove the personality AttackOddsChange before
applying nonlinear opportunity/value adjustments, but it subtracts that bonus from an
attack-odds value that has ALREADY been clamped to the public 1..99 range. Once the
upper clamp has fired, subtraction cannot reconstruct the pre-personality combat odds.

Root:
    CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_getWeightedOdds

Cross-function source of the lossy value:
    CvUnitAI::AI_attackOdds
    CvUnitAI::LFBgetBetterAttacker

The AdvCiv source states the intended contract directly:

    "We shouldn't adjust the odds based on an optimistic estimate
     (increased by AttackOddsChange) ...
     I'm subtracting the AttackOddsChange temporarily;
     adding them back in after the adjustments are done."

Current code therefore does, conceptually:

    adjustedAndClamped = clamp(rawOdds + attackOddsChange, 1, 99);
    supposedRawOdds    = adjustedAndClamped - attackOddsChange;
    weighted           = AI_opportuneOdds(supposedRawOdds, defender);
    result             = clamp(weighted + attackOddsChange, 1, 99);

Both producers of iUnitOdds perform the upper clamp before returning it:
- CvUnitAI::AI_attackOdds adds AI_getAttackOddsChange(), then range(..., 1, 99);
- with default LFB combat-odds selection, CvUnitAI::LFBgetBetterAttacker likewise adds
  AI_getAttackOddsChange() and clamps to 1..99 before storing iAIAttackOdds.

Thus the subtraction is invertible only when rawOdds + attackOddsChange <= 99. Once
that sum exceeds 99, information has been destroyed. For example:

    true raw odds          = 99
    AttackOddsChange       = +16
    producer returns       = clamp(115, 1, 99) = 99
    AI_getWeightedOdds uses= 99 - 16 = 83   // not 99

+16 is reachable for ordinary current SAS leaders: e.g. Ragnar and Napoleon have
BaseAttackOddsChange 6 and AttackOddsChangeRand 8; CvPlayerAI::AI_doTurn can therefore
set 6 + 7 + floor(7/2) = 16. The Barbarian setting can reach an even larger +23.
LFB_ENABLE and LFB_USECOMBATODDS both default enabled, so the lossy LFB producer is the
normal current path rather than a disabled compatibility branch.

This is behaviorally material because AI_opportuneOdds is intentionally nonlinear in
its input. It applies production-value, LFB-value, defensive-plot, wound/heal and city-
opportunity adjustments using iOdds and (100-iOdds). Adding the personality bonus back
at the end therefore does NOT undo feeding the wrong 83 instead of the true 99 into
those calculations.

A deterministic arithmetic example shows that this can change an attack decision,
not merely the displayed score. Take a land attacker with:
- true raw odds 99;
- AttackOddsChange +16;
- production cost 200 against a 50-cost defender;
- a defender plot with defenseModifier 200;
- one defender in a city; and no other differing opportunity modifiers.

The current reconstruction feeds 83 into AI_opportuneOdds:
- production term: x = 83*17*2/(200+50+20) = 10, giving -15;
- defensive-plot term: -(17*200/300) = -11;
- one-city-defender opportunity bonus: +17/3 = +5;
- 83 - 15 - 11 + 5 = 62;
- add personality bonus back: 62 + 16 = 78.

With the intended true raw 99:
- the production x term truncates to 0;
- the defensive-plot penalty truncates to 0;
- the one-defender city bonus truncates to 0;
- adding +16 afterward clamps back to 99.

So the same genuinely near-certain combat can be weighted 78 instead of 99. That is
large enough to fail live AI_anyAttack thresholds such as 90 despite the underlying
combat odds being essentially certain. The exact numerical scenario is illustrative;
the defect exists for every upper-clamped value because the lost excess cannot be
recovered and the downstream transform is nonlinear.

This is inherited unchanged from base AdvCiv 1.14; current SAS did not introduce the
root. The nearby advc.114b comment itself is strong provenance evidence because the
implementation violates the stated purpose of that change.

Narrow repair boundary:
- Do NOT try a different subtraction after the public/clamped value; the missing raw
  odds are mathematically unrecoverable once the clamp has fired.
- Give AI_getWeightedOdds access to the pre-AttackOddsChange odds BEFORE the final
  1..99 clamp. A small helper or optional parameter in the underlying attack-odds
  calculation that suppresses the personality adjustment until after
  AI_opportuneOdds would preserve the intended advc.114b design.
- Keep the final AttackOddsChange addition and final 1..99 clamp unless deliberately
  redesigning the personality behavior; the bug is specifically the lossy attempted
  inverse before the nonlinear opportunity adjustment.
- The LFB and non-LFB producers need consistent treatment because both currently add
  and clamp the personality bonus before returning iUnitOdds.

No existing KI#523 or F200 collision was found in the reconciled album at promotion
time.
