F200 / provisional KI#523 -- SAME ROOT, LOWER-CLAMP PROOF ADDED
---------------------------------------------------------------
The lossy AI_attackOdds round-trip documented in C018-WIP03 fails at the lower clamp
as well as the upper clamp. This strengthens F200; it is not a new F201 root.

AI_getWeightedOdds contains an explicit advc.114b safety rule that is intended to use
the actual/unbiased combat odds:

    if (iOdds == 0 && getNumUnits() < 3)
        return 0;

However, the quantity received from CvUnitAI::AI_attackOdds has already had
AI_getAttackOddsChange applied and has already been clamped to the public 1..99 range.
Therefore a genuinely rounded raw 0% result behaves inconsistently:

    raw odds = 0, AttackOddsChange = 0
    producer = clamp(0 + 0, 1, 99) = 1
    subtraction in AI_getWeightedOdds = 1 - 0 = 1

The explicit iOdds == 0 safeguard can never activate in that state. With a positive
optimism bonus, the same raw 0 can sometimes survive the attempted inverse, e.g.
0 + 6 -> 6, then 6 - 6 -> 0. The supposedly personality-independent small-stack
safety rule can therefore itself depend on personality merely because the clamp is
applied before the attempted subtraction.

Repair implication is now stronger than in WIP03: AI_getWeightedOdds needs the
pre-personality, pre-final-1..99-clamp odds. Repairing only upper saturation would
leave the explicit sub-1%/rounded-0 safety contract broken.

F201 / provisional KI#524 -- CONFIRMED
--------------------------------------
SAS KI#319 no-progress tripwire can misclassify AdvCiv's deliberate non-head bombard
unit split as "no progress" and force MISSION_SKIP on the surviving assault stack.

Primary root:
    CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_update

Cross-file trigger:
    CvUnitAI::AI_bombardCity

Immediate callers confirmed:
    CvUnitAI::AI_attackCityMove
    CvUnitAI::AI_attackCityLemmingMove

The current SAS tripwire snapshots only the original group's:
- head unit ID;
- head UnitAI role;
- head x/y;
- head moves left;
- mission queue length.

If all remain unchanged after CvUnitAI::AI_update returns, while the group is still
ready and not busy, SAS pushes MISSION_SKIP and breaks.

AdvCiv advc.004c deliberately changed K-Mod's bombard behavior. K-Mod pushed
MISSION_BOMBARD on the whole assault group. AdvCiv instead selects one unit:

    CvUnit* pBombardUnit = AI_getGroup()->AI_bestUnitForMission(MISSION_BOMBARD);
    ...
    if (AI_getUnitAIType() == UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY)
        pBombardUnit->joinGroup(NULL);
    pBombardUnit->getGroup()->pushMission(MISSION_BOMBARD, ...);
    return true;

The selected bombard unit is therefore split into its own group before the bombard
mission is issued. pushMission starts an AI mission immediately; the detached unit
bombards and spends its own movement through CvUnit::bombard. The original group does
not receive that mission.

This becomes a KI#319 false positive when pBombardUnit is NOT the original group head:
1. The non-head bombard unit leaves the original group.
2. CvSelectionGroup::removeUnit/deleteUnitNode changes membership and clears/wakes the
   old group, but the old head survives unchanged.
3. The detached unit's new group executes MISSION_BOMBARD and spends that unit's moves.
4. AI_bombardCity returns true; AI_attackCityMove / AI_attackCityLemmingMove return
   immediately; CvUnitAI::AI_update then returns false to CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_update.
5. The original group can still be awake, missionless, non-busy and ready to move.
6. Its head ID/role/x/y/moves and mission queue length can all equal their snapshots.
7. SAS therefore pushes MISSION_SKIP on the surviving original group solely because
   the tripwire does not observe that getNumUnits() decreased.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 has no SAS tripwire at this point. After exactly the same non-head
split/bombard, its CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_update while-loop tests readyToMove again and
can immediately reconsider the surviving stack. Thus the behavior suppressed by SAS
is not speculative extra processing; it is the inherited control flow that
advc.004c's split leaves available.

NON-HEAD REACHABILITY IS ORDINARY, NOT A CONTRIVED POINTER STATE
---------------------------------------------------------------
Current group ordering and current SAS XML provide a concrete normal composition:

CvUnitAI::AI_groupFirstVal:
    UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY + bombardRate() > 0  -> 19
CvUnitAI::AI_groupSecondVal:
    base combat strength

Current generic siege includes:
    Catapult   -- DefaultUnitAI ATTACK_CITY, strength 5, bombard 8
    Trebuchet  -- DefaultUnitAI ATTACK_CITY, strength 4, bombard 16

For an ATTACK_CITY group containing both, the Catapult can be the group head because
both have first-value 19 and the Catapult has higher second-value/base strength.
AI_bestUnitForMission(MISSION_BOMBARD), however, does not simply choose the head. Its
bombard priority increases with useful bombard damage and with (1 - attack odds),
while both examples share the same basic collateral dimensions. A Trebuchet's doubled
bombard rate and lower combat odds can therefore make it the selected bombard unit
while the Catapult remains the head.

The broader code explicitly anticipates mixed assault stacks as well: the
ATTACK_CITY movement logic contains the inherited BBAI grouping path for a stack led
by a bombard unit to join another stack "probably not lead by a bombard unit." More
generally, multiple bombard-capable members with different promotions/strengths make
selection of a non-head unit routine; AI_bestUnitForMission exists precisely to pick
a mission unit independently of head identity.

PROVEN STATE DETAILS
--------------------
- CvUnitAI::AI_update asserts that the acting unit is the group head, dispatches
  UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY to AI_attackCityMove and UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY_LEMMING to the
  corresponding lemming routine, then normally returns false.
- Both attack-city routines return immediately when AI_bombardCity returns true.
- CvUnit::joinGroup(NULL) creates/rejoins a separate group by default
  (bRejoin = true).
- Removing a non-head does not set AI_forceSeparate; joinGroup sets that flag only
  when the removed unit was the old head and the replacement head has a different
  UnitAI role.
- The old group's head identity, role, location and moves therefore need not change.
- pushMission on the detached AI group is started immediately; MISSION_BOMBARD calls
  CvUnit::bombard, which sets made-attack and consumes one movement denominator from
  the detached bombard unit only.
- The original group's mission queue remains empty after the split and can still pass
  readyToMove(true).

BEHAVIORAL EFFECT
-----------------
At minimum, the SAS tripwire can consume the surviving attack-city stack's turn after
one non-head siege piece was detached to bombard, instead of letting inherited AdvCiv
re-enter the still-ready group. That can suppress additional same-turn bombard/
reassessment/attack behavior by the rest of the stack and alter city-assault tempo.
The exact next inherited action is intentionally recalculated after the first
bombard; the bug is that SAS prevents that recalculation by mistaking membership
change for zero progress.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
F201 needs a group-composition progress dimension. The narrow repair is to snapshot:

    const int iNumUnitsBefore = getNumUnits();

and require getNumUnits() == iNumUnitsBefore before the no-progress MISSION_SKIP.

This should be combined with, not substituted for, F199's group-total getCargo()
snapshot:
- F199: cargo can change while membership count stays constant;
- F201: membership can change while cargo and every current head snapshot stay
  constant.

A more general state-signature redesign is possible, but the conservative repair is
to add these two proven missing dimensions rather than guess at every mutable group
field.

No existing KI#524 collision was found in the current reconciled album or Known
Issues snapshot at promotion time.

SOURCE / CURSOR RECONCILIATION
------------------------------

C018-WIP04 is an exact byte prefix of this checkpoint. Investigation continued from
F202 unused, with a second-proof pass over queued group attacks and a systematic
search for synchronous non-head actions that can defeat the SAS KI#319 no-progress
tripwire. The earlier WIP04 rejection of AI_getBombardTurns' synthetic global air
support was also reopened against all live callers and current SAS air-unit data.

F202 / provisional KI#525 -- CONFIRMED
--------------------------------------
AdvCiv-SAS KI#319 regression: consuming a stale queued group-attack flag can be a
legitimate state transition that leaves every currently snapshotted field unchanged.
The tripwire can therefore push MISSION_SKIP on a still-movable group immediately
after K-Mod's queued-combat retry state has served its purpose.

Primary root:
    CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_update

Cross-file mechanics:
    CvSelectionGroup::groupAttack
    CvSelectionGroup::updateTimers
    CvUnit::updateCombat
    CvSelectionGroup::groupMove

IMPORTANT CORRECTION TO THE EARLY WIP HYPOTHESIS
-------------------------------------------------
The first exploratory explanation was wrong in one important respect and is explicitly
superseded here: a unit waiting to attack while another combat occupies the source or
destination plot IS busy. CvUnit::attack stores an attack plot; CvUnit::isAttacking
therefore returns true, CvUnit::isInCombat includes isAttacking, and
CvSelectionGroup::isBusy sees that combat state. The KI#319 tripwire is gated by
!isBusy(), so it cannot misfire merely while the queued attacker is waiting.

The surviving defect occurs later, after the wait has resolved.

REACHABLE STATE SEQUENCE
------------------------
1. CvSelectionGroup::groupAttack tries to attack a defended adjacent target while
   another combat is already using the source or destination plot.
2. K-Mod intentionally still calls pBestAttackUnit->attack so the unit receives an
   attackPlot and will retry through combat-timer processing. For an AI stack with
   more than one unit it also calls AI_queueGroupAttack(targetX, targetY), setting
   m_bGroupAttack = true.
3. While attackPlot remains set, the group is busy. This part is safe and is NOT the
   KI#319 failure.
4. The preceding combat can eliminate the final defender before the waiting attacker's
   CvUnit::updateCombat retry runs.
5. CvSelectionGroup::updateTimers later calls updateCombat on the waiting attacker.
   With pDefender == NULL, updateCombat:
       - clears the unit's attackPlot/combat unit;
       - calls getGroup()->groupMove(pPlot, true, ..., true) onto the now-vacant tile;
       - clears the normal mission queue;
       - returns.
6. Neither setAttackPlot(NULL), groupMove nor clearMissionQueue cancels
   CvSelectionGroupAI::m_bGroupAttack. The queued group-attack state therefore
   survives after the group has already advanced onto its old attack target.
7. groupMove's bEndMove=true does not call finishMoves. It controls move animation;
   CvUnit::move still charges ordinary plot movement cost. A unit with more than one
   move can remain movable after the automatic advance.

The remaining-movement condition is live in current SAS rather than theoretical.
Current land attackers include, among others:
    SELF_PROPELLED_ARTILLERY -- 2 moves, UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY
    LEVITATION_ARTILLERY    -- 3 moves, UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY
and multiple 2+ move UNITAI_ATTACK units. On an ordinary one-move-cost advance, at
least one unit can therefore remain ready after the queued combat resolves.

THE KI#319 FALSE POSITIVE
-------------------------
On the next CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_update for that still-movable group:

1. The while condition admits the group because AI_isGroupAttack is still true and
   the group is no longer busy (and in the demonstrated fast-unit case it is also
   still movable).
2. SAS takes its current no-progress snapshot BEFORE consuming the queued attack:
       head ID / UnitAI / x / y / head moves / mission-queue length.
3. The queued-attack branch executes:
       AI_cancelGroupAttack();
       groupAttack(oldTargetX, oldTargetY, MOVE_DIRECT_ATTACK, ...);
4. The group is already standing on oldTargetX/Y after the no-defender auto-advance.
   groupAttack therefore fails immediately at its non-air adjacency guard because
   stepDistance(currentPlot, oldTargetPlot) == 0 rather than 1.
5. No unit moves, no mission is queued, and the head identity/role/plot/moves remain
   exactly as snapshotted. The only intentional state change is
       AI_isGroupAttack(): true -> false.
6. If any unit can still move, !isBusy() && readyToMove(true) is true. Because the
   SAS tripwire does not snapshot the queued-attack flag, it classifies the iteration
   as no progress and pushes MISSION_SKIP.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 has the same K-Mod queued-combat machinery but not the SAS KI#319
tripwire. After the stale retry is consumed, its while-loop can continue and let the
still-ready group choose a normal action. SAS therefore suppresses inherited
same-turn reassessment solely because the progress predicate omits a live AI state
transition.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
F202 needs the queued group-attack state in the no-progress signature, e.g. snapshot:

    const bool bGroupAttackBefore = AI_isGroupAttack();

and require:

    AI_isGroupAttack() == bGroupAttackBefore

before applying the fallback MISSION_SKIP.

This is independent of the already-proved KI#319 dimensions:
- F199 / KI#522: group cargo can change with all current head snapshots stable;
- F201 / KI#524: group membership can change with all current head snapshots stable;
- F202 / KI#525: queued group-attack state can be intentionally consumed with all
  current head/membership/cargo state otherwise stable.

No existing KI#525 or F202 collision was found in the reconciled album / Known Issues
snapshot at promotion time.


F203 / provisional KI#526 -- CONFIRMED
--------------------------------------
AdvCiv-SAS KI#319 regression: a synchronous immediate mission can deliberately spend
movement on a NON-HEAD member, change the game world, and return with an empty mission
queue while the head remains completely unchanged. The current head-centric progress
snapshot then pushes MISSION_SKIP at exactly the point K-Mod explicitly intended the
AI group to reconsider its action.

Primary root:
    CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_update

Concrete cross-file trigger:
    CvUnitAI::AI_pillageRange
    CvSelectionGroup::pushMission / startMission / continueMission
    CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_bestUnitForMission(MISSION_PILLAGE)
    CvUnit::pillage

PILLAGE HAS AN EXPLICIT K-MOD SAME-TURN RECONSIDERATION CONTRACT
---------------------------------------------------------------
For MISSION_PILLAGE, CvSelectionGroup::startMission repeatedly asks
AI_bestUnitForMission for the best movable pillager. After a successful AI pillage it
contains the explicit K-Mod rule:

    // AI groups might want to reconsider their action after pillaging
    if (!isHuman() && canAllMove())
        break;

That is not an inferred preference. K-Mod deliberately stops the immediate pillage
loop while the whole group can still move so normal unit AI can reconsider what to do
with the remaining movement.

The mission lifecycle is synchronous for an AI command:
1. CvUnitAI::AI_pillageRange, when already standing on its chosen enemy pillage plot,
   calls getGroup()->pushMission(MISSION_PILLAGE, ...) and returns true.
2. pushMission inserts the AI mission with immediate activation.
3. startMission executes the pillage before pushMission returns.
4. CvUnit::pillage changes the route/improvement and charges exactly one
   MOVE_DENOMINATOR of movement to the selected unit.
5. If all members can still move, the K-Mod break above stops further immediate
   pillaging so the group can reconsider.
6. Because the group is not busy, startMission enters continueMission. The immediate
   MISSION_PILLAGE is a one-step mission; continueMission marks it done and deletes
   the mission node.
7. Control therefore returns to CvUnitAI with the mission queue back at its original
   length (normally zero).

NON-HEAD REACHABILITY IN THE CURRENT 08:49 SAS SNAPSHOT
-------------------------------------------------------
The first exploratory example incorrectly described Catapult and Horse Archer as both
UNITAI_ATTACK. Current XML explicitly prevents Catapult from using UNITAI_ATTACK.
That stale role claim is discarded here.

The actual current mixed-role route is ordinary and explicitly supported by K-Mod:
- Catapult:
      DefaultUnitAI = UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY
      1 move, strength 5, collateral damage, bombard 8
      AI_groupFirstVal as ATTACK_CITY + bombard = 19
- Horse Archer:
      DefaultUnitAI = UNITAI_ATTACK
      2 moves, strength 6, withdrawal 20
      AI_groupFirstVal as ATTACK + withdrawal = 14

CvUnitAI::AI_attackMove for a UNITAI_ATTACK unit repeatedly calls
AI_omniGroup(UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY, ...). AI_canGroupWithAIType permits this outside the
small newly-acquired-city exception, AI_allowGroup selects a target whose head really
is UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY, and AI_omniGroup can merge the caller's group into that target
group. The member UnitAI roles are not homogenized merely by this merge.

Once merged, CvSelectionGroup::addUnit ordering makes the Catapult the group head
(first-value 19 versus Horse Archer 14). CvUnitAI::AI_attackCityMove consequently
drives the mixed group and contains live AI_pillageRange paths in enemy territory.

AI_bestUnitForMission(MISSION_PILLAGE) is intentionally independent of head identity
and strongly favors fast units. Its priority is multiplied by movesLeft after other
adjustments. On an eligible enemy improvement:
- the 2-move non-head Horse Archer can therefore be selected ahead of the 1-move
  Catapult head;
- Horse Archer pillages and spends one movement denominator, leaving one move;
- the Catapult has not moved;
- canAllMove() remains true, activating K-Mod's explicit "reconsider" break.

THE KI#319 FALSE POSITIVE
-------------------------
Before the head's CvUnitAI::AI_update call, SAS snapshots:
    head ID / UnitAI / x / y / HEAD moves / mission-queue length.

After the synchronous non-head pillage returns:
- the route/improvement has changed;
- Horse Archer movement has decreased;
- group membership is unchanged;
- cargo is unchanged;
- queued-group-attack state is unchanged;
- Catapult head ID, role, x/y and moves are unchanged;
- the transient MISSION_PILLAGE has already been deleted, so queue length is again
  the same as before;
- the group is awake/non-busy and can still move.

Thus every field in the current KI#319 predicate compares equal. SAS immediately
pushes MISSION_SKIP and ends the group's turn, overriding the inherited K-Mod comment
and control flow that deliberately left the group movable so it could reconsider.

This is an independent missing state dimension. F199 cargo, F201 membership and F202
queued-attack snapshots would all still compare equal in the pillage case.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
The no-progress signature needs to observe movement progress by the group as a whole,
not only movesLeft() on the current head. A conservative low-cost dimension is an
aggregate of member remaining movement before and after the attempted AI action, e.g.
a sum of movesLeft() across current group members, combined with F201's explicit
membership-count check.

Conceptually:

    iGroupMovesBefore = sum(movesLeft() for every member)

and the fallback MISSION_SKIP is allowed only if the corresponding aggregate is still
identical afterward.

The exact implementation can be kept local to the KI#319 guard. There is no need to
change MISSION_PILLAGE itself; its K-Mod reconsideration behavior is coherent. The SAS
tripwire is the layer suppressing it.

MISSION_PILLAGE is the clean proof because K-Mod states the intended reconsideration
in a comment and current mixed groups make non-head selection ordinary. Other
immediate missions selected through AI_bestUnitForMission can be checked as same-root
siblings, but they should not receive separate F numbers merely for exercising the
same omitted non-head-movement dimension.

No existing KI#526 or F203 collision was found in the reconciled album / Known Issues
snapshot at promotion time.


KI#319 PROGRESS-SIGNATURE STATUS AFTER F199/F201/F202/F203
----------------------------------------------------------
The investigation no longer supports treating KI#319 progress as a head-only concept.
Four independent, concretely reachable state dimensions have now crossed the bar:

    F199 / KI#522  group cargo total          -- getCargo()
    F201 / KI#524  group membership           -- getNumUnits()
    F202 / KI#525  queued group-attack state  -- AI_isGroupAttack()
    F203 / KI#526  non-head movement progress -- aggregate member movesLeft()

These should be combined with the already-existing head ID / UnitAI / plot / head
moves / queue-length checks. A small local "progress signature" helper would be a
reasonable cleanup if implementation review prefers it, but the audit does not need a
large generic state hash: the four additions above each have a proved caller and can
be added conservatively.


REOPENED NEGATIVE CONTROL -- GLOBAL AIR SUPPORT IN AI_getBombardTurns
---------------------------------------------------------------------
WIP04 had rejected AI_getBombardTurns' synthetic global air-bomber support as an
intentional BBAI approximation rather than a correctness root. The full-history pass
reopened that judgment because the helper's comment says it approximates how many
turns "this group" would need, while its air support test is completely global:

    GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).AI_isDomainBombard(DOMAIN_AIR)

AI_isDomainBombard is AI_calculateTotalBombard(DOMAIN_AIR, 1) > 0.
AI_calculateTotalBombard counts owned unit classes across the entire civilization; it
has no target, range, area, air-base or mission-legality test. Any one air-bombard
unit anywhere therefore gives every evaluated land group:
- a synthetic bombard rate of 16; and
- bIgnoreBuildingDefense = true.

Current SAS confirms the locality mismatch is live:
    Fighter         bomb rate  8, air range  6
    Jet Fighter     bomb rate 12, air range 10
    Bomber          bomb rate 16, air range  8
    Stealth Bomber  bomb rate 20, air range 12
    Guided Missile  bomb rate 16, air range  5

A Fighter on another continent can therefore count as immediate support for a city it
cannot target. Quantitatively, even without invoking building-defense suppression,
an 80-defense city with no local group bombard can be estimated at roughly 80 turns
without the synthetic air flag but 5 turns with it. In AI_attackCityMove's projected
post-bombard formula, an immediate stack comparison of 80 can consequently be lifted
to about 112, enough to cross the ordinary 110 attack-city readiness ratio. The same
helper also affects AI_pickTargetCity valuation and AI_bombardCity's bombard threshold.

Despite that material effect, this pass STILL does not promote the seam to an F root.
The fixed +16 and empire-wide presence test are visibly inherited BBAI/K-Mod synthetic
strategic support rather than an accidental local coding error. A distant aircraft
may be intended as a crude proxy for air power that can be rebased by the time a land
stack reaches its target. The final direct city assault also rechecks real current
stack strength rather than blindly attacking on the projected value.

Without a save/log case showing the approximation causing a pathological target or
siege decision, changing it would be an AI-design refinement (e.g. target-local
reachable air support), not a sufficiently objective queue-041 defect under this
audit's current bar. The deeper caller/range analysis is preserved here so the seam
does not need to be rediscovered later.

Ancestry: the global-presence + fixed-16 behavior is inherited from BBAI through
K-Mod. AdvCiv moved the helper from CvSelectionGroup to CvSelectionGroupAI and used
the equivalent AI_isDomainBombard wrapper; it did not make the air-support test local.

- CvUnit::setAttackPlot(NULL) likewise only clears attack coordinates / air-combat
  state; it does not clear the selection group's queued group-attack flag.

- The current Catapult XML role correction above supersedes the exploratory

F204 / provisional KI#527 -- CONFIRMED
--------------------------------------
Inherited AdvCiv debug assertion / diagnostic contract defect: Debug Mode combat
help explicitly accepts a selected DOMAIN_AIR group, then its Shift-hover stack
comparison calls AI_compareStacks -> AI_sumStrength even though AdvCiv explicitly
asserts that AI_sumStrength does not support DOMAIN_AIR.

Root boundary:
    CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_compareStacks / AI_sumStrength
Caller exposing the false invariant:
    CvGameTextMgr::setCombatPlotHelp debug Shift-hover diagnostics

CURRENT SOURCE CONTRACT
-----------------------
CvGameTextMgr::setCombatPlotHelp deliberately accepts air selections:

    switch (kSelectionList.getDomainType())
    {
    ...
    case DOMAIN_AIR:
        bValid = true;
        break;
    ...
    }

For a visible defended target that the selected aircraft can attack, the helper
successfully obtains an air pAttacker and pDefender. In Debug Mode while Shift is
held it later executes:

    szTempBuffer.Format(L"\\nStack Compare Value = %d",
        kSelectionList.AI_compareStacks(pPlot, false, true));

AI_compareStacks preserves the group's domain when it is DOMAIN_AIR and passes that
domain to AI_sumStrength. AdvCiv's AI_sumStrength begins with:

    FAssert(eDomainType != DOMAIN_AIR && eDomainType != DOMAIN_IMMOBILE);
    // advc: Air combat strength isn't counted

Therefore a legal debug/developer UI path reaches a false assertion invariant:

    debug/assert-enabled DLL
      + in-game Debug Mode
      + Shift combat hover
      + selected Fighter/Bomber/etc.
      + valid defended air target
        -> AI_compareStacks(DOMAIN_AIR)
        -> AI_sumStrength(DOMAIN_AIR)
        -> FAssert fires.

This is not hypothetical domain data. Current SAS aircraft such as Fighter,
Jet Fighter, Bomber and Stealth Bomber use DOMAIN_AIR, iCombat=0 and a separate
positive iAirCombat value. The combat-help domain switch explicitly treats them as
valid rather than rejecting the UI path first.

RELEASE-BUILD CONSEQUENCE / SCOPE
---------------------------------
This should be described narrowly as a debug/assertion and diagnostic defect, not a
release gameplay crash. Without assertions, current AdvCiv/SAS AI_sumStrength also
filters out units for which canFight() is false; canFight() is based on baseCombatStr
and current aircraft have iCombat=0. The resulting air "Stack Compare Value" is
therefore not a meaningful air-power comparison even when execution continues.

Normal strategic AI callers examined in this file use land/sea groups and do not
rely on DOMAIN_AIR AI_compareStacks. The confirmed defect is the debug UI exposing a
function whose AdvCiv contract explicitly excludes air.

ANCESTRY / CONTROLS
-------------------
- K-Mod and Civ4CE already carry the debug "Stack Compare Value" combat-help family.
- K-Mod's older AI_sumStrength still contains an air branch, although it ultimately
  relies on the same land-style currEffectiveStr machinery.
- AdvCiv practical 1941 (60e9fadec3, "Some misc. refactoring, fixed assertion.")
  explicitly introduced:

      FAssert(eDomainType != DOMAIN_AIR && eDomainType != DOMAIN_IMMOBILE);

  and removed the old air branch with the comment that air combat strength is not
  counted / currEffectiveStr is 0 for air units.
- That AdvCiv change did not correspondingly gate the existing debug combat-help
  Stack Compare diagnostic for DOMAIN_AIR selections.
- Current SAS inherits both sides of that mismatch unchanged in substance.
- No existing KI#527 or F204 collision was found in the reconciled album / Known
  Issues snapshot at promotion time.

NARROW REPAIR BOUNDARY
----------------------
The smallest safe repair is at the diagnostic boundary: do not call/display the
land/sea Stack Compare value for DOMAIN_AIR selections (or display an explicit N/A).
A broader alternative would be to implement a genuinely air-aware stack-strength
metric using air combat strength, but merely removing the assertion while retaining
AI_sumStrength's current air filtering would only hide the contract problem and keep
showing a meaningless diagnostic.


POST-WIP05 KI#319 CLOSURE / NEGATIVE CONTROLS
----------------------------------------------
The no-progress tripwire was challenged against additional mutable state rather than
blindly expanding its snapshot.

1. forceUpdate -- REJECTED AS AN OMITTED PROGRESS DIMENSION
   Current source has only one setForceUpdate(true) producer, in
   CvSelectionGroup::doTurn before AI_update. AI_update clears that flag at loop
   entry. No current CvUnitAI decision silently sets it again while returning through
   the KI#319 guard, so snapshotting forceUpdate would be redundant in current SAS.

2. Activity / MissionAI changes -- NO INDEPENDENT ROOT
   Worker wake/recovery paths that clear retreat/hold state fall through into normal
   worker decision logic in the same CvUnitAI call. Sea-transport wake-and-return
   paths with a meaningful same-group state change are the cargo-unload family already
   covered by F199. Direct MissionAI mutations examined either accompany ordinary
   mission/group progress or operate on another joining group.

3. Immediate best-unit missions -- SAME-ROOT COVERAGE FOR F203
   MISSION_BOMBARD, MISSION_AIRBOMB and MISSION_PARADROP can also act with members
   selected independently of the head. Their successful paths spend member action /
   movement and/or alter membership/plot state. They reinforce the need for F203's
   group-wide movement observation (plus F201 membership) rather than creating a new
   omitted state dimension. MISSION_PILLAGE remains the strongest proof because K-Mod
   explicitly says the still-movable AI group should reconsider afterward.

4. Global declaration-of-war state -- REJECTED AFTER CALLER TRACE
   AI_considerDOW can change team state without itself moving a group, so it was a
   plausible nonlocal progress class. Its live callers were traced. They continue in
   the same move routine after the declaration and subsequently issue an action/skip,
   queue movement, or encounter the normal bump/immobilization effects. No current
   route was found where declaration alone returns to the KI#319 no-progress test
   with every local signature field unchanged while same-turn reconsideration is
   still required.

5. MISSION_SKIP fallback cargo semantics -- CAUTION, NOT A NEW ROOT
   The fallback mission has inherited semantics beyond a bare finishMoves in some
   cargo contexts, but no case was proved where a *correctly detected* no-progress
   state is uniquely harmed by those semantics. The known false positives should be
   fixed at the KI#319 progress predicate rather than by redefining MISSION_SKIP.


SAS LOW-POWER ATTACKER ORDER -- AIR-DOMAIN NEGATIVE CONTROL
------------------------------------------------------------
A real metric mismatch was found but is dormant under current normal AI grouping, so
it is deliberately NOT F205.

AI_currEffectiveStr calls the land-style currEffectiveStr/maxCombatStr path. The
latter returns zero when baseCombatStr()==0. Current SAS aircraft confirm the mismatch:

    Fighter          iCombat 0, iAirCombat 12
    Jet Fighter      iCombat 0, iAirCombat 24
    Bomber           iCombat 0, iAirCombat 16
    Stealth Bomber   iCombat 0, iAirCombat 20
    Guided Missile   iCombat 0, iAirCombat 40

AI_currEffectiveStr ultimately clamps its result to at least 1, so SAS's custom
bPreferLowPower branch would not meaningfully rank different aircraft by their true
air strength if several AI aircraft were in one attacking selection group.

Reachability review prevents promotion:
- CvPlayer::initUnit / CvUnit::setXY creates each new unit in its own selection group.
- AI_attackAirMove / AI_defenseAirMove / AI_carrierAirMove / AI_missileAirMove do not
  use AI_group or AI_omniGroup to merge aircraft attackers.
- Carrier loading changes transport linkage, not selection-group membership.
- AI_setUnitAIType separates the unit from its group on role conversion.
- SAS's low-power mode is disabled for human-owned groups.

Thus normal current AI air attacks are effectively singleton-group selections; there
is no attacker-order choice for the bad metric to corrupt. Preserve this as a dormant
robustness hazard if future SAS AI work ever groups aircraft, not as a current root.

The low-power branch's current numeric ranking itself also remained bounded: the
AI_currEffectiveStr contribution is capped at 25,000 and the tactical
bombard/collateral -1,000,000 offset cannot approach signed underflow. No arithmetic
root survived there.


OTHER POST-WIP05 NEGATIVE CONTROLS
----------------------------------
- AI_bestUnitForMission's SAS KI#394 Air Bomb repair was rechecked. Requiring
  canAirBombAt(target) before ranking is symmetric for city and improvement targets
  and prevents the inherited invalid-first-aircraft selection without blocking a
  valid group member. No regression found.
- AI_attackOdds' 100 return for a defenderless plot remains a strategic "nothing to
  fight" convention for its live group-level bombard caller, not proof that an
  attacker exists; attack legality is handled elsewhere.
- AI_compareStacks integer scaling still has only a theoretical extreme-stack
  overflow ceiling. Current per-unit effective strength is capped and no ordinary
  SAS-reachable stack size near the dangerous range was established.
- AI_bestUnitForMission(MISSION_BOMBARD) deriving bombardTarget through a group member
  remains safe because actual per-unit canBombard filtering is applied before the
  selected unit acts.

F205 / provisional KI#528 -- CONFIRMED
--------------------------------------
Inherited AdvCiv debug assertion contract defect: a legal human Bombard mission
against an undefended enemy city reaches AI_bestUnitForMission(MISSION_BOMBARD),
whose human-only branch falsely asserts that the city must have at least one
defender.

Root boundary:
    CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_bestUnitForMission(MISSION_BOMBARD)
Legal caller:
    CvSelectionGroup::startMission for an ordinary human Bombard command
Underlying legality contract:
    CvUnit::canBombard -> CvUnit::bombardTarget -> CvCity::isBombardable

CURRENT SOURCE CONTRADICTION
----------------------------
AI_bestUnitForMission first resolves the bombard target and counts defenders:

    iDefenders = pMissionPlot->plotCount(
            PUF_canDefendEnemy, getOwner(), false);

For an AI group it may use AI_isEvacuating. For a human group it instead enters:

    else
    {
        FAssertMsg(iDefenders > 0, "AI bombards undefended city");
        ...
    }

The asserted invariant is not part of Bombard legality. CvUnit::canBombard only
requires a positive bombard rate, remaining attack capacity, non-cargo status and a
non-NULL bombardTarget. bombardTarget selects an adjacent city for which
CvCity::isBombardable(this) is true.

CvCity::isBombardable deliberately does NOT require a defending unit. In current
AdvCiv/SAS it returns true for an enemy city with positive defense and additionally
contains human-only support for bombarding a defenseless city so recovered defense
can be kept at zero:

    /* Allow bombarding defenseless cities (to keep their def at 0), ... */
    (getTotalDefense(false) > 0 && pUnit->isHuman() && !isBombarded())

The normal mission UI / mission execution path preserves that contract:

    CvSelectionGroup::canDoMission(MISSION_BOMBARD)
      -> any movable member with pUnit->canBombard(*pPlot) makes the mission legal

    CvSelectionGroup::startMission()
      -> MISSION_BOMBARD
      -> AI().AI_bestUnitForMission(MISSION_BOMBARD)

Thus a human siege unit adjacent to an enemy city that has bombardable defense but
zero defenders is a supported mission state and reaches the assertion directly.

CONSEQUENCE / SEVERITY
----------------------
This is a debug/assert-enabled DLL defect, not a release-gameplay crash. In a debug
build the legal human Bombard command can fire the assertion. In a release build the
surrounding calculations remain bounded:
- the attacker/defender ratio uses std::max(iDefenders, 1) where division needs a
  nonzero denominator;
- the bombard-priority denominator is 15 + min(iDefenders, collateralMaxUnits), so
  zero defenders is safe;
- empty-target attack odds may drive some ordering terms to zero, but selection still
  has a valid finite priority and Bombard itself remains legal.

The finding should therefore be described narrowly as a false debug invariant / bad
assertion on a legal human mission, analogous in severity class (not root cause) to
F204's legal debug UI -> unsupported air stack-comparison assertion.

ANCESTRY
--------
- AdvCiv's human-only ability to bombard defenseless cities predates the assertion;
  it is already present in the early advc.004c history (practical 1253).
- AdvCiv practical 2778 (4098fbb248, "Various UI improvements for bombard and air
  bomb missions") further preserves/extends the human Bombard UI contract.
- AdvCiv practical 2809 (1ce5042732, "Smarter code for order of group bombardment")
  introduced AI_bestUnitForMission's current bombard-order logic and the assertion:

      FAssertMsg(iDefenders > 0, "AI bombards undefended city");

  This was added inside the explicit isHuman() branch despite the already-supported
  human undefended-city bombard case.
- Current SAS inherits both the mission legality and the false assertion unchanged in
  substance.

NARROW REPAIR BOUNDARY
----------------------
Remove or relax the iDefenders > 0 assertion. Do not forbid the human mission in
canBombard/isBombardable: AdvCiv deliberately supports it, and the surrounding
ordering math is already zero-defender-safe. No broader behavior change is required
for this finding.


POST-WIP06 REJECTIONS / CLOSURE EVIDENCE
-----------------------------------------

1. K-Mod undefended-city AI_sumStrength + no-city-capture units -- REJECTED

K-Mod change 522 deliberately skips target-specific canMoveInto filtering in
AI_sumStrength(..., bCheckCanAttack=true) when the target has no visible defender.
That means a no-city-capture unit such as a Gunship can contribute nominal attack
strength against an empty enemy city.

The local oddity is real, but no distinct wrong decision survived the caller trace:
- an all-Gunship/no-capture group cannot actually enter an empty enemy city;
  CvUnit::canMoveInto rejects isNoCityCapture() against an enemy city, while the
  attack alternative has no defender to attack;
- AI_stackAttackCity checks group canMoveOrAttackInto before committing the assault;
- if a mixed stack has at least one real capturer, the destination is legal and
  AdvCiv's groupMove explicitly moves capture-capable units first, then advances
  no-city-capture units such as Gunships afterward;
- AI_attackCityMove's readiness logic also requires a meaningful city-capture-capable
  fraction before treating a city-assault stack as ready;
- UNITAI_ATTACK groups may still approach a city as offensive support, but that
  behavior exists independently of this empty-city strength exception and is part of
  K-Mod's broader city-target logic;
- AI_stackVsStack only evaluates plots with enemies, so the empty-target exemption is
  irrelevant there.

Therefore the extra Gunship strength against an empty city is a coarse K-Mod
estimate, not a demonstrated independent defect. F205 was left unused until the
separate bombard assertion crossed the bar.


2. AI_getBombardTurns global air-support approximation -- REJECTED AGAIN

The earlier reopened BBAI seam remains deliberately unpromoted. AI_getBombardTurns
uses owner-wide AI_isDomainBombard(DOMAIN_AIR) and can therefore grant a land group a
synthetic air bombard rate / building-defense bypass even when the aircraft is
nowhere near the target. Caller math proves that this can bias projected target and
approach values, but the final assault rechecks real stack strength and the code is
visibly written as a strategic synthetic approximation inherited from BBAI.

Without save/log evidence showing a pathological strategic consequence, retain this
as an intentional coarse heuristic rather than manufacturing a root.


3. AI_isFull assumptions validated against current SAS XML

The two-pass special-cargo code assumes that units with SpecialCargo are actual cargo
hulls. Current CIV4UnitInfos.xml was checked mechanically. Every non-NONE
SpecialCargo unit has positive cargo capacity:

    Missile Cruiser     SPECIALUNIT_MISSILE   iCargo 4
    Attack Submarine    SPECIALUNIT_PEOPLE    iCargo 1
    Carrier             SPECIALUNIT_FIGHTER   iCargo 3

There is no current special-cargo / zero-capacity unit that can inflate
specialCargoCount independently of cargoCount and falsify the >= comparison. Caller
review in assault-sea and missile-carrier AI also remains consistent with the old
intended two-pass behavior. No root.


4. MissionAI-only progress -- NO NEW KI#319 SIBLING

Direct AI_setMissionAI producers were revisited. Relevant current-unit paths do not
produce a missionless false-return state requiring an independent MissionAI snapshot:
- AI_upgrade returns success/abort semantics after replacing/splitting the acting
  unit and, when needed, assigns MISSIONAI_GROUP to the new unit's new group;
- worker retreat/HOLD recovery clears MissionAI and wakes the group but falls through
  to ordinary worker decision logic; its fallback ultimately takes an action or
  queues MISSION_SKIP;
- assault-transport cancellation of MISSIONAI_GROUP acts on *other* joining groups;
- the current transport's unload-and-wake return is the cargo-state family already
  captured by F199.

MissionAI therefore remains metadata accompanying already-observed progress, not an
independent missing dimension under current callers.


5. Remaining assertion inventory mostly proved sound

After F204 and F205, the other live assertions in CvSelectionGroupAI.cpp were checked
against their producer/caller contracts:
- AI_getBestGroupAttacker attack odds are positive because the public unit odds path
  clamps attack odds to at least 1;
- AI_sacrificeValue is non-negative by its producer contract;
- bMaxSurvival implies !bSacrifice and human ownership at every current caller (the
  mode is used by human combat-help / Alt-key selection paths);
- owner/head assertions are reached on owned nonempty groups;
- the AI_isDeclareWar default switch has no uncovered current UnitAITypes (42/42 were
  enumerated earlier in this audit).

The two legal-caller contradictions found in this file are therefore specifically
F204's air debug Stack Compare and F205's human undefended-city Bombard assertion.


AI_UPDATE / KI#319 HISTORICAL CONTRACT — STRONGER CONTEXT
----------------------------------------------------------
AdvCiv practical 2219 (5e2d002497, "Fix false positive 'unit stuck in loop'") is an
important upstream signal. It changed the permanent AI_update fallback from:

    6 * (era + 1) + range(getNumUnits(), 4, 14)

to:

    6 * (era + 1) + max(getNumUnits(), 4)

because legitimate work by larger groups could require more loop iterations than the
old capped term allowed. Current SAS preserves this uncapped unit-count contribution.

SAS history then shows the same contract evolving again:
- SAS practical 5093 introduced KI#319's no-progress tripwire using only head x/y,
  head moves and mission-queue length after a Scout/Explorer spin was observed;
- SAS practical 6211 (KI#319 follow-up) added head identity and UnitAI role because a
  legitimate AI_setUnitAIType/head-replacement transition proved that the first
  signature was incomplete;
- the current audit has now confirmed further legitimate state dimensions:

      F199  group cargo count / unload progress
      F201  group membership count / non-head split progress
      F202  queued group-attack state
      F203  non-head member movement consumed by synchronous immediate missions

This lineage strongly argues against tightening the legacy attempt ceiling or merely
adding a one-off field for each testcase. The robust repair direction is a compact
*group progress signature*: preserve the already-tracked head identity/role/position,
then include group membership, cargo, queued group-attack state and a group-wide
movement/action summary sufficient to notice non-head work. The inherited attempt
ceiling should remain the ultimate fallback for genuinely unproductive loops.

This is architectural repair guidance only; no repository patch was made by this
audit checkpoint.

F205 / provisional KI#528 -- SAME ROOT, RELEASE-BUILD CONSEQUENCE ADDED
------------------------------------------------------------------------
WIP07 correctly proved the false debug assertion in the human branch of
AI_bestUnitForMission(MISSION_BOMBARD): a legal human Bombard of an undefended city
can reach

    FAssertMsg(iDefenders > 0, "AI bombards undefended city");

The deeper mission-order trace shows that the same bad assumption also has a release
build consequence; F205 is therefore stronger than the WIP07 description "debug
assertion only."

For an undefended target, CvUnitAI::AI_attackOdds returns 100 immediately because
there is no defender. The smart human bombard ordering then computes roughly:

    scaled rOdds = per100(pUnit->AI_attackOdds(pMissionPlot, false));
    rPriority *= (1 - rOdds);

Thus rOdds == 1 and EVERY eligible bombarder has the promotion/intent-derived
priority multiplied by zero. The code that AdvCiv practical 2809 added specifically
to derive a sensible human group-bombard order therefore collapses to equal zero
priority in exactly the supported undefended-city case.

This is consequential because CvSelectionGroup::startMission(MISSION_BOMBARD)
repeatedly asks AI_bestUnitForMission for the next unit and executes that unit's
bombard until the mission can no longer continue. Group iteration order can therefore
determine which bombarders spend their attack/movement state and which bombard
capacity is wasted once city defense reaches the stopping condition.

REVISED CONSEQUENCE / REPAIR BOUNDARY
-------------------------------------
F205 should no longer be described as debug-only:
- debug DLL: legal human undefended-city Bombard reaches the false assertion;
- release DLL: the same state zeros the intended smart bombard priorities and
  degenerates selection to iteration/tie order.

The root remains the same, so no new F-number is consumed. A correct repair must
handle iDefenders == 0 as a supported human bombard state rather than merely deleting
the assertion while leaving rOdds == 1 to erase the priority signal. One narrow
option is to bypass/neutralize the attack-odds attenuation when there is no defender;
the exact patch is left to implementation review.


POST-WIP07 REJECTION — SACRIFICE bPotentialEnemy MISMATCH
---------------------------------------------------------
The inherited AI_getBestGroupSacrifice helper and SAS's obsolete-sacrifice subscan
both call canMoveInto(..., attack=true) without forwarding bPotentialEnemy. This is
locally suspicious because AI_getBestGroupAttacker itself does use bPotentialEnemy
for ordinary attacker eligibility.

The exact live caller contract makes the omission consequence-neutral:

1. CvSelectionGroup::groupAttack first probes the prospective target through
   AI_getBestGroupAttacker(pDestPlot, true, ...), but this call uses the default
   bSacrifice=false.
2. groupAttack then requires pDestPlot->hasDefender(...) to establish a real enemy.
3. Only inside the subsequent real-combat loop does it call AI_getBestGroupAttacker
   with bSacrifice=true; that call explicitly passes bPotentialEnemy=false.
4. Human combat-help/selection callers that use the sacrifice/max-survival modes also
   pass false.

Therefore no reachable sacrifice-enabled caller relies on potential-war legality.
The stale/over-general bPotentialEnemy parameter in AI_getBestGroupSacrifice is API
awkwardness, not F206. Do not revive this candidate unless a new caller is added that
combines bSacrifice=true with bPotentialEnemy=true.

F206 / provisional KI#529 -- CONFIRMED
--------------------------------------
AdvCiv-SAS / inherited-contract interaction: CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_isDeclareWar
assumes that ANY cargo aboard a UNITAI_ASSAULT_SEA group is invasion cargo and
therefore authorizes war. K-Mod/AdvCiv also allow assault transports to rescue any
stranded land-unit role. SAS KI#193 then added a below-threshold opportunistic launch
whose documentation says "military cargo" but whose implementation checks only
`iCargo > 0`. A rescued noncombat Missionary or Great Person can therefore make an
assault transport evaluate an invasion with zero actual attack strength. With Open
Borders to an imminent sneak-attack target, the pre-war amphibious path can be legal,
AI_considerDOW can declare war, and the post-DoW path can then become impossible.
The AI has declared war but cannot execute the assault that triggered it.

ROOT / INTERACTION BOUNDARY
---------------------------
Current queue-041 contract:

    CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_isDeclareWar
      case UNITAI_ASSAULT_SEA:
          return hasCargo();

Cross-file reachability that violates the inherited assumption:

    CvUnitAI::AI_handleStranded
    CvUnitAI::AI_pickupStranded
    CvUnitAI::AI_assaultSeaMove
    CvUnitAI::AI_assaultSeaTransport
    CvUnitAI::AI_transportGoTo / AI_considerPathDOW

SAS activation:

    SAS_AI_ASSAULT_SEA_OPPORTUNISTIC_TARGET_ENABLE = 1

The define and source comment say that "military cargo below those broad
army-assembly thresholds" should receive the target-specific launch test. The actual
gate is:

    if (bOpportunisticTargetEnable && iCargo > 0 &&
        iCargo < iTargetReinforcementSize)
        AI_assaultSeaTransport(bNoWarPlans);

`iCargo` is total cargo, not military/capture-capable cargo.

CONCRETE REACHABILITY PROOF
---------------------------
1. Noncombat units really can become stranded.

   AI_missionaryMove and AI_greatPersonMove both call AI_handleStranded after their
   normal useful actions / retreat attempts fail. AI_handleStranded treats access to
   an enemy city as proof of being non-stranded only for:

       (canFight() || isSpy())

   A Missionary is neither. If it cannot reach an owned city in its land area, it can
   therefore advertise MISSIONAI_STRANDED at a coastal pickup plot.

2. Assault transports really can rescue those roles.

   AI_assaultSeaMove contains generic calls to:

       AI_pickupStranded()

   with NO_UNITAI filtering. AI_pickupStranded only requires the target group to have
   MISSIONAI_STRANDED; it does not require a military UnitAI. Normal Galley/Galleon/
   Transport assault ships have SpecialCargo=NONE and DomainCargo=DOMAIN_LAND, so
   current Missionaries / Great People (DOMAIN_LAND, SPECIALUNIT_PEOPLE) are loadable.

3. The "inappropriate cargo" purge does not remove them.

   At the top of AI_assaultSeaMove the special cleanup only detects:

       getUnitAICargo(UNITAI_SETTLE) > 0 ||
       getUnitAICargo(UNITAI_WORKER) > 0

   Missionary and Great Person cargo survives into normal assault logic.

4. SAS KI#193 makes a single rescued civilian sufficient to enter target evaluation.

   Base K-Mod/AdvCiv broad invasion thresholds are normally several units
   (AI_neededCityAttackers has a base around four before further scaling). The SAS
   opportunistic branch intentionally bypasses those broad thresholds for a small
   capable military load, but tests only total iCargo. Thus a single rescued
   Missionary can call AI_assaultSeaTransport.

5. AI_assaultSeaTransport computes zero real attack strength but does not reject an
   undefended target for that reason.

   Cargo attack strength is accumulated only after:

       if (!pLoopUnit->canAttack() || pLoopUnit->isDead())
           continue;

   so a Missionary contributes zero landed/amphibious attack strength. However the
   defender-strength rejection executes only when iEnemyDefenders > 0. An undefended
   revealed coastal city can therefore remain a candidate with zero attack strength.

6. Open Borders makes the PRE-WAR amphibious destination legal to the civilian.

   GroupPathFinder validates an amphibious destination through the cargo group's
   canMoveOrAttackInto. Before war, a Missionary can ordinarily enter the rival city
   under Open Borders. Open Borders does not prevent canDeclareWar, and
   CvTeamAI::AI_mayAttack accepts an imminent undeclared war plan. Thus the target can
   pass both strategic and path legality while the teams are still at peace.

7. AI_considerPathDOW deliberately declares war at the amphibious target.

   AI_transportGoTo calls AI_considerPathDOW for MOVE_DECLARE_WAR paths.
   AI_considerDOW contains a special rule that if the group destination is an
   amphibious plot, "lets just assume that our cargo will need a DoW!" If the target
   team is sneak-attack-ready and canDeclareWar succeeds, it calls declareWar.

   CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_isDeclareWar compounds the same assumption for the assault
   ship by treating mere hasCargo() as sufficient war intent.

8. The same destination becomes illegal AFTER the DoW.

   Once war is declared, the foreign city is now an enemy city and the Open Borders
   relationship is gone. A Missionary cannot attack, and non-attack movement into an
   enemy city is rejected. AI_transportGoTo regenerates the path after declaring war;
   that regeneration can therefore fail and AI_assaultSeaTransport returns false.

The observable semantic failure is consequently stronger than "civilian cargo is
valued poorly": the transport can trigger a real war declaration and then discover
that the cargo cannot perform the landing that caused the declaration.

ANCESTRY / REGRESSION CLASSIFICATION
------------------------------------
- K-Mod already has the broad UNITAI_ASSAULT_SEA -> hasCargo() declaration rule.
- K-Mod and AdvCiv already let an assault transport fall back to generic
  AI_pickupStranded(), so the assumption that assault cargo is necessarily military
  was never perfectly encoded.
- In ordinary upstream flow, however, a single rescued civilian is far below the
  normal reinforcement/invasion threshold and normally does not launch an assault.
- SAS practical 6063 / KI#193 deliberately added the below-threshold launch path to
  let a *small military cargo* attack a target it can actually beat, but used total
  iCargo rather than a military/capture-capable cargo count. That turns the inherited
  loose cargo assumption into a much more directly reachable current-SAS defect.
- Civ4CE retains the old `UNITAI_ASSAULT_SEA` `hasCargo()` declaration rule; no
  downstream CE repair for this interaction was found. CE does not contain SAS
  KI#193's opportunistic activation path.

CONSEQUENCE / SEVERITY
----------------------
This is gameplay-visible and can affect diplomacy/war timing rather than merely a
log or assertion:
- a rescued civilian can be mistaken for the "military cargo" promised by KI#193;
- an undefended coastal city can pass assault target selection with zero attack
  strength;
- an imminent sneak war can be declared when the transport reaches the amphibious
  target window;
- after declaration, the civilian cargo cannot enter/attack the city, so the target
  path can disappear immediately after the irreversible diplomatic action;
- the AI may therefore start a war without executing the naval assault that justified
  that declaration, while also carrying a valuable civilian in the assault fleet.

The scenario is conditional (notably stranded civilian rescue + an imminent war and
path legality such as Open Borders), but every link is supported by current code and
normal engine states. No save-file reproduction is required to establish the
contract failure, though a targeted debug save would be useful implementation-side
confirmation.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
Do not fix this merely by special-casing Missionaries. The broken assumption is "any
cargo == invasion cargo."

Implementation review should require actual assault-capable cargo at one or both of
these boundaries:

1. SAS KI#193 opportunistic launch: replace total `iCargo > 0` as the capability gate
   with a military/capture-capable cargo measure and refuse zero landed attack
   strength before target selection; and/or
2. CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_isDeclareWar UNITAI_ASSAULT_SEA: do not authorize a DoW
   solely from hasCargo(); require cargo whose post-DoW movement/attack role can
   actually support the intended invasion.

A robust target-local repair should ensure the cargo can execute the post-DoW
amphibious destination, not merely enter the same city pre-war under Open Borders.
Keep generic stranded rescue available; rescuing civilians is useful and is not the
bug.

F206 / provisional KI#529 -- POST-DoW FAILURE MECHANICS HARDENED
----------------------------------------------------------------
WIP08 proved the full pre-war reachability chain for rescued civilian cargo aboard a
UNITAI_ASSAULT_SEA transport and showed that AI_considerPathDOW can declare war for
that prospective amphibious landing. The remaining challenge was whether the engine
might preserve enough movement/path legality after the declaration that the
Missionary/Great Person could still execute the landing, which would weaken the
finding to merely an odd declaration trigger.

The current SAS implementation closes that objection:

1. CvTeam::declareWar removes bilateral deals BEFORE switching the teams to war.

   The function iterates all deals between the two teams and kills them at the top of
   the declaration sequence. Open Borders therefore disappears before setAtWar is
   installed.

2. declareWar then invalidates/rebuilds movement state.

   After the diplomatic/war state changes it verifies unit-valid plots, updates
   active paths, and calls CvSelectionGroup::resetPath(). The pre-war path cannot be
   treated as authoritative after the declaration.

3. AI_considerDOW itself resets the unit pathfinder immediately after declareWar.

   Its successful declaration branch does:

       kOurTeam.declareWar(...);
       getPathFinder().reset();
       return true;

4. AI_transportGoTo explicitly regenerates the assault path after a DoW.

   Immediately after AI_considerPathDOW returns true:

       if (!canMove())
           return true;
       if (!generatePath(kTargetPlot, eFlags, false))
           return false;

   Therefore the transport does not blindly execute the Open-Borders path that was
   valid before the declaration.

5. The rescued Missionary has no legal post-war amphibious destination mode.

   After Open Borders is gone and the city is hostile, ordinary non-attack entry is
   rejected for an enemy city. The Missionary cannot use the attack alternative
   either because it cannot attack. Thus the regenerated amphibious destination can
   fail immediately after the irreversible declaration.

This makes F206 a genuine declaration-then-no-executable-assault contract failure,
not merely a target-scoring curiosity. The repair recommendation from WIP08 stands:
capability must be based on actual military/capture-capable cargo (ideally target-
local post-DoW landing legality), while generic civilian stranded rescue should
remain available.


POST-WIP08 REJECTION — "ZERO BOMBARD RATE DIVISION" IN AI_getBombardTurns
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
AI_getBombardTurns uses max(1, iTotalBombardRate) in the denominator. At first glance,
a stack with no usable bombard unit therefore appears to receive a finite bombard-
turn estimate instead of an explicit infinity/failure state.

The live caller math makes the encoding intentional/consequence-safe:

- the important city-attack caller caps the returned estimate at 20 turns;
- the projected-defense formula credits progressively more defense removal only for
  smaller bombard-turn counts;
- a capped value of 20 corresponds to essentially NO useful projected defense
  removal and the target-value path also penalizes the remaining/max defense.

So the max(1, rate) denominator is functioning as an "effectively cannot bombard"
large-turn sentinel rather than pretending that defenses will disappear. This is not
F207.

The separate global-anywhere-bomber approximation remains the earlier recorded
heuristic rejection: it can bias strategic estimates but is visibly inherited BBAI
coarse modeling, and the final assault gate rechecks real current strength.


POST-WIP08 KI#319 PROGRESS-SIGNATURE CLOSURE
--------------------------------------------
The remaining mutable-state classes were challenged against the actual tripwire
entry contract rather than simply enumerating every field in CvSelectionGroup.

The tripwire can act only when the group is not busy and readyToMove(true). Current
readyToMove semantics require:

    (canAnyMove()) &&
    (isForceUpdate() ||
        (headMissionQueueNode() == NULL && getActivityType() == ACTIVITY_AWAKE)) &&
    !isBusy() && !isCargoBusy()

The remaining candidate classes therefore close as follows:

- activity changes: self-protecting. A non-AWAKE activity prevents readyToMove unless
  forceUpdate is active; wake-up paths that return immediately are already represented
  by the F199 cargo-unload family or continue into another decision in the same call.
- forceUpdate: no hidden in-loop progress source. Current SAS has only one
  setForceUpdate(true) producer, in CvSelectionGroup::doTurn before AI_update begins;
  AI_update consumes/clears it and UnitAI decision code does not silently set it back.
- delayed death: already protected by finishMoves / explicit delayed-death handling.
- head identity / UnitAI / position / head moves: covered by current KI#319 snapshots.
- membership: F201.
- cargo count: F199.
- queued group-attack state: F202.
- non-head member action/movement during a synchronous immediate mission: F203.
- MissionAI-only changes: reviewed live callers either accompany queue/activity/action
  state or are intentionally persistent cross-turn metadata (e.g. STRANDED/EXPLORE),
  not an independent false-return ready-group transition.
- global/team state such as declaration of war: all live AI_considerDOW callers traced
  so far proceed into movement/action, path invalidation/bumping, or another decision;
  no DoW-only local-no-change return reaches the tripwire independently.

This is strong evidence that F199/F201/F202/F203 form a coherent and close-to-complete
family of KI#319 blind spots rather than an unbounded list of arbitrary group fields.

Repair guidance remains architectural: use a compact GROUP progress signature rather
than continuing to add one testcase-specific field at a time. At minimum it should
cover head identity/role/position, group size/cargo, queued group-attack state, and a
small aggregate/hash of member identity + movement/action state. Keep the inherited
attempt ceiling as the ultimate safety fallback.

F206 / provisional KI#529 — SAME-ROOT BLAST RADIUS: AI_enemyTargetMissions
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
WIP08-WIP09 proved that UNITAI_ASSAULT_SEA::AI_isDeclareWar uses hasCargo() as a
proxy for having invasion-capable cargo, while generic stranded rescue can place a
noncombat Missionary or Great Person aboard that transport. The same capability
assumption also leaks into strategic mission counting.

CvPlayerAI::AI_enemyTargetMissions scans selection groups whose mission plot belongs
to a prospective enemy team and counts a group when either war already exists or:

    pLoopSelectionGroup->AI_isDeclareWar(*pMissionPlot)

is true. When counted, it adds BOTH:

    pLoopSelectionGroup->getNumUnits();
    pLoopSelectionGroup->getCargo();

Therefore a rescued civilian cargo unit can be counted as committed military pressure
against the target team merely because the transport head is UNITAI_ASSAULT_SEA and
hasCargo() is true. This is not a separate root from F206: the same invalid assumption
("any assault-sea cargo is invasion-capable cargo") authorizes both the premature DoW
path and the strategic target-mission count.

Current known consumers include CvTeamAI war/counteroffensive logic. Treat this as
additional F206/KI#529 blast radius, not F207.


F207 / provisional KI#530 — HUMAN SMART BOMBARD COUNTS FOREIGN PEACEFUL UNITS AS ATTACKERS
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT / ANCESTRY
---------------
Inherited from AdvCiv, introduced by practical commit 2809
("Smarter code for order of group bombardment"). K-Mod and Civ4CE do not contain
this AdvCiv smart group-bombard selector. Current AdvCiv 1.14 retains the same logic.

LIVE CODE
---------
In CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_bestUnitForMission(MISSION_BOMBARD), the human-only
"easy city capture" precheck intentionally scans the whole current plot rather than
only the selected group:

    int iAttackers = 0;
    FOR_EACH_UNIT_IN(pUnit, kAt)
    {
        if (!pUnit->canBombard(kAt) &&
            pUnit->canMoveOrAttackInto(*pMissionPlot))
        {
            iAttackers++;
            if (iAttackers >= 2 * iDefenders)
                break;
        }
    }

There is NO owner/player/team filter on pUnit.

WHY canMoveOrAttackInto IS NOT AN ATTACKER FILTER
-------------------------------------------------
CvUnit::canMoveOrAttackInto is:

    canMoveInto(kPlot, false, bDeclareWar) ||
    canMoveInto(kPlot, true, bDeclareWar, ...)

The first half is ordinary movement, not attack capability. Therefore a unit owned by
an unrelated third civilization can satisfy this predicate merely because it is at
peace with the target and Open Borders allows it to enter the target city normally.
It need not be at war with the target and need not be capable of helping the human
capture the city.

A legal state is:

- human A is at war with target B and is bombarding a defended B city;
- third-party C is at peace with both A and B and has the necessary Open Borders to
  share A's siege tile and to enter B's city;
- a non-bombarding C unit is on A's tile;
- for C, B's defenders/city are not enemies, so ordinary peaceful canMoveInto can
  succeed and canMoveOrAttackInto returns true;
- AdvCiv increments A's iAttackers for C's unit.

This directly contradicts the quantity being estimated: how many of the human's units
can help capture the city immediately.

CONCRETE THRESHOLD FLIP
-----------------------
The false count can change bEasyCityCapture, not merely an unused diagnostic.
For example, with one visible defender and a current selected-group stack comparison
of about 200%:

- one genuine human non-bombarding attacker gives iAttackers=1;
- the later test is roughly 1/1 * 2.0 = 2.0, below the >2.5 immediate-conquest gate;
- one peaceful foreign unit falsely counted as an attacker raises iAttackers to 2;
- the same test becomes 2/1 * 2.0 = 4.0 and bEasyCityCapture becomes true.

The foreign unit therefore flips a live control-flow decision.

PLAYER-VISIBLE BOMBARD-ORDER CONSEQUENCE
----------------------------------------
When bEasyCityCapture is true, every bombard candidate receives an extra factor:

    rPriority *= per100(pUnit->currHitPoints());

That can reverse which of the human's siege units performs the bombard action.
Current SAS Catapult bombard rate is 8, so a city with 8 defense remaining can be
reduced to zero by whichever Catapult is selected first; later candidates then need
not spend their action.

A representative legal ordering boundary uses two otherwise comparable Catapults:

- one damaged ordinary Catapult that the normal priority logic prefers to spend on
  bombardment because its attack odds are poorer;
- one full-health City Raider Catapult, whose +city-attack promotion is intentionally
  penalized by the human-intent bombard formula so it can be preserved for combat.

For representative resulting attack odds of 10% vs 30%, the relative pre-common-factor
priorities with 8 non-wasted bombard damage are approximately:

    damaged ordinary, no easy-capture flag:
        1.00 * (1 - .10) = .90
    full-health City Raider I, no easy-capture flag:
        .75 * (1 - .30) = .525

so the damaged ordinary unit is selected first. At 50% HP, a falsely enabled
bEasyCityCapture multiplies the first value by .50:

        .90 * .50 = .45 < .525

and the City Raider is selected first instead. Because one Catapult can remove the
remaining 8 defense, the false foreign attacker can determine which human siege unit
spends its action that turn.

The exact odds are state-dependent; the important proof is structural: the HP factor
is applied only when bEasyCityCapture is true, and there are ordinary legal priority
states on opposite sides of that multiplier boundary. The foreign unit can therefore
alter real mission ordering.

INTENT / REPAIR BOUNDARY
------------------------
Scanning the whole tile is defensible: other selection groups belonging to the SAME
human player can also attack after the bombardment, so restricting the estimate to
this one group would lose useful information. What is not defensible is counting units
the human does not own and cannot order, especially units whose predicate succeeds
through peaceful movement rather than attack.

Narrow repair: require pUnit->getOwner() == getOwner() before counting it as an
attacker, then retain the existing move-or-attack legality test for that owner's units.
A more explicit attack/capture-capability predicate could be reviewed separately, but
ownership alone fixes the demonstrated foreign-unit false positive without discarding
the intended whole-tile same-player information.

SEVERITY
--------
Human-control / mission-order defect, modest but real. It does not create an illegal
attack or crash; it can make AdvCiv's "smarter" group bombard order depend on neutral
third-party units and choose a different human unit to consume the bombard action.

STATUS: CONFIRMED as F207 / provisional KI#530.


POST-WIP09 HISTORY NOTE — practical 2809 intent
------------------------------------------------
The commit title is explicitly "Smarter code for order of group bombardment." It
introduced bEasyCityCapture, the whole-plot iAttackers scan, and the human promotion-
based bombard priority together. Later refactors retained this code. This supports the
interpretation that the whole-plot scan is meant to inform HUMAN bombard sequencing,
not to estimate unrelated civilizations' possible movement into the target.

F208 / provisional KI#531 — HUMAN SMART BOMBARD COUNTS LOADED CARGO AS CITY DEFENDERS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT / ANCESTRY
---------------
Inherited from AdvCiv practical 2809, "Smarter code for order of group bombardment."
The same commit introduced the human bEasyCityCapture precheck, including this raw
plot defender count. K-Mod/Civ4CE do not contain this AdvCiv smart group-bombard
selector. Current AdvCiv 1.14 retains the same code.

LIVE CODE
---------
CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_bestUnitForMission(MISSION_BOMBARD) computes:

    iDefenders = pMissionPlot->plotCount(
            PUF_canDefendEnemy, getOwner(), false);

For the human branch, iDefenders controls both the attacker-count gate and the final
immediate-conquest test that decides bEasyCityCapture.

WHY PUF_canDefendEnemy IS TOO BROAD HERE
----------------------------------------
PUF_canDefendEnemy is essentially:

    PUF_canDefend(pUnit) && PUF_isEnemy(...)

and PUF_canDefend calls CvUnit::canDefend(). CvUnit::canDefend checks combat ability
and domain validity on the unit's current plot, but it does NOT reject isCargo().

By contrast, CvPlot::getBestDefender — the actual combat defender-selection path —
explicitly does:

    if (kUnit.isCargo())
        continue;

before considering a unit as defender.

Therefore a loaded LAND combat unit aboard a transport in an enemy coastal city can
satisfy PUF_canDefendEnemy on that land city tile even though, while still cargo, it
cannot be selected to defend the city in combat.

REACHABILITY
------------
Cargo is not automatically detached merely because its transport is in a friendly
city. CvUnit::setXY retains the transport link whenever the transport remains on the
same destination plot; unloading is an explicit operation (or occurs in other
specific transport-handling paths). Thus a coastal city can legally contain an enemy
transport with loaded land military cargo while the human bombards that city.

The earlier naval-domain suspicion is explicitly rejected: an ordinary SEA or AIR
unit in the land city fails CvUnit::canDefend's domain check, so ships/aircraft by
themselves are not the false defenders. The demonstrated false population is loaded
same-domain land combat cargo.

INDEPENDENT CONTROL-FLOW CONSEQUENCE
------------------------------------
This local count defect can flip bEasyCityCapture even if the separate cross-file
AI_localDefenceStrength cargo issue is left exactly as current code computes it.

Example legal state:

- target coastal city has 1 genuine unloaded land defender;
- the city also contains 1 enemy loaded land combat unit aboard a transport;
- the human bombard tile has 2 genuine non-bombarding attackers;
- the current AI_compareStacks result (including whatever current strength accounting
  produces) is about 200%, i.e. rStackCmp ~= 2.0.

Actual combat-defender population is 1. With the correct count:

    2 attackers / 1 defender * 2.0 = 4.0 > 2.5

and the >1.5 stack-ratio condition is also met, so bEasyCityCapture becomes true.

The current raw PUF count reports 2 defenders because the loaded cargo is included:

    2 attackers / 2 reported defenders * 2.0 = 2.0 <= 2.5

so bEasyCityCapture remains false. The loaded unit cannot defend the city, yet it
changes the smart-bombard control-flow decision.

PLAYER-VISIBLE ORDERING EFFECT
------------------------------
As established for F207, bEasyCityCapture is not merely diagnostic. When true, each
bombard candidate receives:

    rPriority *= per100(pUnit->currHitPoints());

That extra HP factor can reverse the order of two otherwise legal siege candidates.
When the target has only enough defense left for one bombard action (e.g. current SAS
Catapult bombard damage matching the remaining defense), the false defender count can
therefore decide which human siege unit consumes its action and which remains free.

DISTINCT FROM F205 AND F207
---------------------------
- F205/KI#528 is the no-real-defender assumption: legal undefended bombard asserts in
  debug and release smart priority collapses through the 100%-attack-odds convention.
- F207/KI#530 contaminates iAttackers with foreign units because the whole-plot scan
  has no owner filter and accepts peaceful canMoveOrAttackInto movement.
- F208/KI#531 contaminates iDefenders with loaded combat cargo that actual defender
  selection explicitly excludes.

These are independent populations and independently demonstrated control-flow flips.

CROSS-FILE FOLLOW-UP — DO NOT MERGE INTO F208
----------------------------------------------
During the proof, CvPlayerAI::AI_localDefenceStrength was found to filter canFight(),
domain, death, etc. but not isCargo(). It can therefore also count loaded same-domain
combat cargo as defensive strength, and AI_compareStacks consumes that routine.
That is broader than this local human-bombard count and belongs to the later
CvPlayerAI.cpp audit/resweep. Preserve it as a cross-file candidate; do not claim F208
fixes the strength-estimation root.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
The bEasyCityCapture defender population should follow actual combat-defender
eligibility at least far enough to exclude loaded cargo (and should ideally be derived
from the same defender semantics used by combat rather than an unrelated raw PUF
count). A minimal demonstrated repair is to exclude isCargo() from the counted units.
Visibility can be reviewed separately; current CvUnit source notes that there are no
invisible defenders that can defend, so invisibility is not needed to prove this root.

SEVERITY
--------
Human-control / mission-order defect, modest but real. It does not permit illegal
combat; it can cause AdvCiv's smart group-bombard ordering to preserve/spend the wrong
siege unit because a loaded enemy unit that cannot defend is treated as a defender.

STATUS: CONFIRMED as F208 / provisional KI#531.
