F224 / provisional KI#547
-------------------------
TITLE
    Mid-turn city conquest keeps the detailed UWAICache city set current but leaves
    m_rTotalAssets at its pre-conquest value, so live human-turn war/peace evaluation
    combines new city ownership with an old asset denominator.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv/UWAI cache-coherency defect. Current in Base AdvCiv
    1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS. The mid-turn ownership callback was introduced in
    practical AdvCiv commit 1289 (ed1826faf1); practical commit 2605 (f788c46a21,
    "Various optimizations for UWAICache") refactored it into the modern destroy/create
    callbacks. Neither form refreshes the cache owner's total-asset aggregate.

CURRENT ROOT
    UWAICache::update() performs the normal complete city rebuild and then computes:

        updateCities(...);
        sortCitiesByAttackPriority();
        updateTotalAssetScore();

    updateTotalAssetScore() derives m_rTotalAssets from the current cached cities owned
    by m_eOwner (plus the Palace/national-wonder adjustment).

    City ownership changes, however, are deliberately propagated during a turn. The
    modern callbacks are:

        UWAICache::reportCityDestroyed(CvCity const& kCity) { remove(kCity); }

    and:

        void UWAICache::reportCityCreated(CvCity& kCity)
        {
            ...
            if (kCity.getTeam() == TEAMID(m_eOwner) ||
                GET_TEAM(m_eOwner).AI_deduceCitySite(kCity))
            {
                add(kCity);
                sortCitiesByAttackPriority();
            }
        }

    remove/add keep m_cityList, m_cityMap and m_aiReachableCities coherent; creation
    also restores the attack-priority ordering. But neither callback updates
    m_rTotalAssets.

    A mechanical current-source caller check finds updateTotalAssetScore() called only
    by the ordinary per-turn UWAICache::update(). There is no second city-acquisition
    hook that restores the aggregate later in the same human turn.

SUPPORTED MID-TURN LIFECYCLE
    CvCity::kill notifies every major AI cache through AI_cityKilled while the old
    CvCity object is still alive. CvPlayer::acquireCity later constructs the replacement
    city and notifies every major cache through AI_cityCreated. This deliberately gives
    UWAICache a current ownership/city-set view without waiting for another team turn.

    The source comment states the reason explicitly:

        "It's important that the cache keep up with ownership changes
         so that the AI is aware of conquests made throughout a human turn."

    Full UWAI cache refresh, by contrast, occurs from UWAI::Team::turnPre /
    UWAI::Player::turnPre at the relevant team's next turn. Thus a human can capture an
    AI city and negotiate/evaluate peace before the victim's next cache refresh.

MIXED-SNAPSHOT FAILURE
    After such a conquest:

      * the lost city has been removed from the victim's UWAICache city set;
      * the newly acquired city has been inserted into the conqueror's city set;
      * target ownership, reachability and attack ordering reflect the new position;
      * the victim's m_rTotalAssets still includes its pre-conquest asset baseline;
      * the conqueror's m_rTotalAssets still excludes the newly acquired city.

    This is stronger than ordinary one-turn heuristic staleness: the same cache
    intentionally updates one representation of city ownership immediately while
    retaining a derived aggregate computed from the old representation.

LIVE WAR-EVALUATION CONSUMERS
    totalAssetScore() is read directly by several current WarUtilityAspect paths,
    including Risk, GreedForAssets, Loathing/Rebuke-related ratios, nuclear-loss
    valuation, vassal-loss normalization and blockade/loss normalization.

    Human-AI peace valuation calls UWAI::Team::reluctanceToPeace / endWarVal, which
    constructs a fresh WarEvaluator. Therefore an immediate post-conquest diplomacy
    query can consume the already-updated city list together with stale total assets;
    no later per-turn cache update is required to reach the consumer.

NUMERIC CONSEQUENCE
    Consider a victim whose pre-conquest cached total assets are 100 and whose captured
    city contributes 30 to that position. After the city callbacks, the current cached
    city set represents roughly 70 assets, but totalAssetScore() remains 100.

    If a continuation scenario in WarUtilityAspect::Risk predicts another 20 asset
    points lost, its principal normalization is approximately:

        stale current:   400 * 20 / 100 = 80
        coherent state:  400 * 20 /  70 = 114.3

    The exact final war utility also includes blockade, nuclear and other terms, but the
    denominator discrepancy itself is deterministic. Losing a valuable city can
    therefore leave the AI materially under-normalizing subsequent danger until its
    next turn. The reverse stale direction occurs for the conqueror, whose aggregate
    does not yet include its newly acquired city.

ANCESTRY / INTENT
    Practical commit 1289 (ed1826faf1) introduced reportCityOwnerChanged during the
    early WarAndPeaceCache implementation. Its source comment already says:

        "I didn't think I'd need to update the city cache during turns, so this
         is awkward to write ..."

    That callback immediately replaced the cached city owner representation and
    reachable-city counts, but did not update totalAssets.

    Practical commit 2605 (f788c46a21, "Various optimizations for UWAICache") replaced
    the in-place owner-change routine with the modern remove/add lifecycle and
    strengthened the comment to the current human-turn-conquest wording. The same
    commit retained updateTotalAssetScore as an ordinary update-only operation.

    The omission therefore predates SAS and survives both the original callback and its
    later pointer/lifecycle cleanup.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
    Keep m_rTotalAssets coherent only when the cache owner's own city set changes.

    A narrow repair can recompute updateTotalAssetScore after the old-owner cache has
    removed one of m_eOwner's cities, and after the new-owner cache has added/sorted a
    city now owned by m_eOwner. The callbacks already run for every major cache, so do
    not recompute the aggregate unnecessarily for observers whose own city holdings did
    not change.

    For reportCityCreated, perform the refresh after add() and
    sortCitiesByAttackPriority(), because updateTotalAssetScore relies on own-team cities
    sorting to the end. For destruction, removal preserves the existing order of the
    remaining list, so recomputation after remove is sufficient.

    Do not turn F224 into a full mid-turn UWAICache::update. Other per-turn heuristic
    fields intentionally have their normal refresh cadence; the proven root is the
    derived city-asset aggregate becoming inconsistent with the city set that these
    special conquest callbacks explicitly maintain.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS / SCOPE
    * The detailed City object added for the conqueror computes a fresh per-city asset
      score. The defect is not failure to construct the new City; it is failure to fold
      the changed own-city set back into m_rTotalAssets.
    * Reachable-city counts are independently adjusted by add/remove and are not part of
      F224.
    * The cache-owner extinction guard in reportCityCreated is unrelated; a player with
      no cities has no useful continuing war evaluation to repair there.
    * One-turn drift in values such as goldPerProduction is not automatically promoted
      under F224. The stronger contract here comes from m_rTotalAssets being directly
      derived from the exact city list that the conquest callbacks intentionally keep
      current during a human turn.

DEFERRED OLD-SAVE COMPATIBILITY NOTE -- NOT F225
-------------------------------------------------
The City distance serialization history contains a real but very old compatibility
quirk, retained as a closure note rather than spending F225 at this point.

Practical commit 1287 (ad5faf8aa2) introduced the first City save-version encoding.
The pre-version format had written raw `distance`. The new decoder always performs:

    iSaveVersion = iTmp / 10000;
    m_iDistance = (iTmp % 10000) - 1;

For an old version-0 raw distance d, this restores d-1. In particular, the old
unreachable sentinel -1 becomes -2.

Practical commit 1326 (5e6aa1c42d) explicitly acknowledged this supported state by
changing the writer to:

    FAssertMsg(distance >= -1 && distance < 10000,
        "-2 is OK if loaded from an old savegame version");
    distance = ::range(distance, -1, 9999);

The release clamp lets -2 be re-saved as the canonical -1 value, but the assertion
condition itself still rejects the value its message calls OK. Current read only
rebuilds CvCity pointers after all players load; normal cache recomputation happens
later at team turnPre, so the compatibility value can persist for a while after load.

This is a genuine old-format off-by-one/debug-assert compatibility issue, but it affects
only saves from the initial unversioned UWAI format and is far less relevant to current
SAS gameplay than F224. Keep it available for later cleanup/closure review rather than
promoting it as F225 without a reason to prioritize ancient-save compatibility.

LOW-MENTION MILITARY-COUNT NOTE -- NOT A FINDING
------------------------------------------------
The remaining m_iNonNavalUnits population mismatch was challenged before promoting
F225. reportUnit deliberately excludes units whose XML DefaultUnitAI is
UNITAI_EXPLORE ("exclude Recon"), while the ARMY MilitaryBranch still includes
combat-capable land/air recon power. HomeGuard::initTotals therefore derives its
guard-unit fraction from a count population with Recon removed and applies that fraction
to an Army-power pool that still includes Recon.

Current SAS has several military-production, non-sea, default-Explore combat units
(Scout, Explorer, Airship and Robotic Recon Drone), so the asymmetry is live. However,
the exact split and the "exclude Recon" comment are already present in the initial UWAI
implementation, and no concrete incorrect branch decision beyond a coarse HomeGuard
allocation approximation has yet been proved. Keep this as a tuning/contract note rather
than spending an F-root unless a deterministic wrong decision is later found.

F225 / provisional KI#548
-------------------------
TITLE
    Reviving a player after units already exist initializes an empty UWAI military
    inventory and never reconstructs those units, so the revived civ is modeled with
    zero military and later unit destruction can drive incremental cache counts/power
    negative.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv revival-cache reconstruction defect, still present after
    the current SAS KI#475.3 crash repair. KI#475.3 correctly fixes the dead-at-load
    owner/branch initialization crash; F225 is the remaining logical reconstruction
    half of the same lifecycle rather than a reason to revert that repair.

CURRENT SUPPORTED REPRODUCTION / ORDER
    A dead player can be revived by receiving a unit (the exact KI#475.3 WorldBuilder
    reproduction used a Robotic Tank).

    CvPlayer::initUnit allocates and fully initializes the unit without setting the
    player alive. CvUnitAI::finalizeInit calls CvUnit::finalizeInit, which reports the
    newly created unit to UWAI:

        kOwner.uwai().getCache().reportUnitCreated(getUnitType());

    This occurs while the player is still dead.

    Later CvGame::testAlive calls CvPlayer::verifyAlive. For a dead player:

        if (getNumCities() > 0 || getNumUnits() > 0)
            setAlive(true);

    The already-created unit is therefore the reason revival occurs; the creation
    callback necessarily precedes setAlive(true).

DEATH / REVIVAL CACHE LIFECYCLE
    On elimination AdvCiv deliberately calls:

        AI().uwai().uninit();

    UWAICache::uninit performs a full clear(). Full clear resets
    m_iNonNavalUnits and deletes all MilitaryBranch objects. This is the historical
    reason for the advc.104r comment "UWAI data gets deleted upon death."

    A player dead when a save is loaded is even less initialized: CvPlayerAI::read
    correctly skips player UWAI deserialization for a dead major, leaving the cache
    constructor state (m_eOwner == NO_PLAYER, no branch vector). This was the immediate
    KI#475.3 crash root.

    Current SAS correctly repairs that crash by calling, on revival:

        getUWAI().initRevivedPlayerInGame(getID());
        getUWAI().processNewPlayerInGame(getID());

    initRevivedPlayerInGame calls Player::init -> UWAICache::init. UWAICache::init:

        m_eOwner = eOwner;
        clear();
        updateTraits();
        createMilitaryBranches();

    The full clear sets m_iNonNavalUnits = 0 and deletes any branch data; the subsequent
    createMilitaryBranches creates brand-new branches with zero unit count and zero
    total power.

LOST CREATION CALLBACK
    In the dead-at-load case the revival-causing unit's earlier reportUnitCreated cannot
    be retained meaningfully because the cache was never deserialized/initialized.
    In a dead-during-session case it can increment residual scalar state before revival,
    but UWAICache::init then clears that state anyway.

    In both cases, once current revival initialization completes, the physically
    existing revival-causing unit is absent from the new military inventory.

    This is not repaired by processNewPlayerInGame:

        GET_PLAYER(eNewPlayer).uwai().getCache().update(true);
        for (TeamAIIter<MAJOR_CIV> it; it.hasNext(); ++it)
            it->uwai().turnPre();

    UWAICache::update rebuilds cities, transports, typical trainable units, threat,
    vassal/adjacency/asset/economic fields, etc. It does NOT enumerate owned units to
    rebuild MilitaryBranch::m_iUnits / m_rTotalPower or m_iNonNavalUnits. Those fields
    are intentionally maintained through reportUnitCreated/reportUnitDestroyed
    callbacks.

    Team::turnPre -> Player::turnPre -> m_cache.update() repeats the same kind of update
    and likewise cannot reconstruct the missing unit inventory.

CURRENT-SAS CONCRETE EXAMPLE
    The exact KI#475.3 WorldBuilder reproduction used UNIT_ROBOTIC_TANK. Current XML
    gives it:

        Domain             DOMAIN_LAND
        DefaultUnitAI      UNITAI_ATTACK
        bMilitaryProduction 1
        iCombat            56
        iPower             56

    It therefore should increment m_iNonNavalUnits and contributes nonzero ARMY power.

    After current revival initialization, however:

        actual units owned:        1 Robotic Tank
        cached m_iNonNavalUnits:   0
        cached ARMY units/power:   0 / 0  (apart from any subsequently created units)

    processNewPlayerInGame immediately runs team turnPre for all major teams. A fresh
    WarEvaluator/InvasionGraph can therefore consume this state in the same revival
    processing sequence.

LIVE CONSUMER
    InvasionGraph::Node::initMilitary copies present military directly from the cache:

        vector<MilitaryBranch*> const& kCacheMilitary = m_kCache.getPowerValues();
        pHomeGuard->initTotals(m_kCache.numNonNavalUnits(),
            kCacheMilitary[ARMY]->power() - kCacheMilitary[NUCLEAR]->power());

    It then copies the ARMY/FLEET/LOGISTICS/CAVALRY/NUCLEAR branch totals. The revived
    player can consequently be modeled as having no present army despite physically
    owning the unit that caused its revival.

DETERMINISTIC LATER UNDERFLOW
    CvUnit::kill/destruction always reports:

        kOwner.uwai().getCache().reportUnitDestroyed(getUnitType());

    reportUnitDestroyed calls reportUnit(eUnit, -1). If the revived Tank was never
    replayed into the freshly initialized cache, its later destruction has no matching
    retained +1:

        m_iNonNavalUnits: 0 -> -1

    Every MilitaryBranch that can employ the unit similarly applies -1 to a branch that
    started at zero, making its m_iUnits and m_rTotalPower negative. The ordinary
    incremental contract therefore becomes permanently unbalanced, not merely stale
    for one turn.

ANCESTRY
    Practical AdvCiv commit 2010 / 56af3a8dfa introduced explicit dead-player revival
    support. Its CvPlayer::setAlive addition already states:

        // advc.104r> (UWAI data gets deleted upon death)
        if (getUWAI.isEnabled())
            getUWAI.processNewCivInGame(getID());

    Thus the inherited design already knew that elimination deletes UWAI state, but
    revival only called the "process/update" stage. That stage did not recreate or scan
    the deleted military inventory.

    The later scaled/UWAI rewrite renamed this to processNewPlayerInGame without
    changing that reconstruction contract.

    Base AdvCiv 1.14 therefore contains the deeper omission. For a player dead during
    the running session, m_eOwner can remain valid but the MilitaryBranch vector deleted
    by uninit is not rebuilt by processNewPlayerInGame. For a player dead when a save
    loads, the skipped deserialization additionally leaves m_eOwner == NO_PLAYER; that
    second condition is what made the current WorldBuilder reproduction crash before
    KI#475.3.

    SAS practical commit 6283 / 5b2c6d1a63 (KI#475.3) correctly adds
    initRevivedPlayerInGame before processNewPlayerInGame, restoring the owner and branch
    objects. It converts the inherited crash/uninitialized-object failure into a safe
    but still incomplete zero-inventory state. F225 therefore extends rather than
    contradicts KI#475.3.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
    After revival-specific UWAICache::init has created a clean cache and MilitaryBranch
    vector, rebuild the incremental military inventory from the player's units that
    already exist.

    A narrow repair can iterate the revived player's current units once and replay the
    equivalent of reportUnitCreated(unit.getUnitType()) before
    processNewPlayerInGame/its immediate war-evaluation refresh.

    This restores:
      * m_iNonNavalUnits;
      * MilitaryBranch unit counts;
      * MilitaryBranch present-power totals.

    Do not make ordinary per-turn UWAICache::update scan every unit merely to repair
    this exceptional lifecycle. Incremental creation/destruction reporting is otherwise
    intentional and cheaper.

    Do not move or duplicate team initialization into the player repair. KI#475.3's
    distinction remains correct: CvTeam::changeAliveCount initializes a team returning
    from zero alive members, while a surviving teammate's team UWAI must remain intact.

    If a dedicated "rebuild unit-derived military cache" helper is introduced, it
    should run only after full player-cache initialization and before consumers, and it
    should start from known zero branch/count state to avoid double-reporting.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS / SCOPE
    * New colonial players are not the same lifecycle. They receive normal player UWAI
      initialization before their later processNewPlayerInGame stage; units created
      after initialization can be tracked incrementally.
    * F225 does not reopen KI#475.3's owner/cache crash repair. The initialization call
      is necessary.
    * Typical-unit refresh is not a reconstruction of owned-unit power; it scans what
      unit type is representative/trainable. F214 concerns stale typical-unit identity
      and is independent.
    * Generic CvPlayer power is updated correctly by CvUnit::finalizeInit; F225 is
      specifically the differentiated UWAI MilitaryBranch/non-naval cache.
    * The earlier conversion +1/-1 staging concern remains rejected: ordinary unit
      conversion paths resolve delayed death and preserve a matching incremental pair.
      Revival is different because a full cache clear occurs between the +1 creation
      event and all later consumers/destruction.

IMPLEMENTATION-SIDE NUMBERING NOTE
    Album continuity uses F225 / provisional KI#548. Because this was found by extending
    the exact KI#475.3 revival lifecycle and the practical repair likely belongs beside
    that crash fix, the implementation/reconciled Known Issues side may prefer a decimal
    follow-up such as KI#475.4. Preserve the root and proof; the public KI number can be
    reconciled independently.

F226 / provisional KI#549
-------------------------
TITLE
    City::updateDistance conflates "a sea route exists" with "sea is the fastest
    pairwise route": a valid naval route from a secondary/non-primary colony can be
    ignored because a shorter local land path is present even though that land path is
    explicitly forbidden from establishing strategic reachability, causing the target
    city to be cached as wholly unreachable.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited UWAI reachability/route-selection invariant mismatch. Present
    from the initial 2017 WarAndPeaceCache implementation and still present in current
    AdvCiv 1.14 and AdvCiv-SAS. Later practical commit 2767 broadened qualifying land
    reach from the capital to any primary area and therefore reduced the incidence, but
    did not remove the underlying mismatch. Practical 2929 added a sea-search
    optimization that gives the same mismatch an additional skip path when the
    non-qualifying land route is already short.

CURRENT ROOT
    UWAICache::City::updateDistance tracks two logically distinct things:

      1. iPairwDuration -- the best/shortest deployment duration found from a source
         city to the target;
      2. m_bReachByLand / bReachBySea -- whether at least one strategically acceptable
         route exists so that the target is not globally classified unreachable.

    A land path from any qualifying source city is allowed to populate
    iPairwDuration. But only a source in an AI primary area establishes
    m_bReachByLand:

        if (landFinder.generatePath(...))
        {
            iPairwDuration = ...;
            if (kCacheOwner.AI_isPrimaryArea(pCity->getArea()))
                m_bReachByLand = true;
            ...
        }

    This primary-area restriction is deliberate. AI_isPrimaryArea currently means a
    non-water area with either more than two of the player's cities or the capital.
    It prevents a small/peripheral colony near a rival from making that rival look like
    a normal land target for the whole empire.

    The sea branch, however, uses the existing iPairwDuration as both a performance
    shortcut and the condition for setting the *existence* flag:

        if (bAnyTransports &&
            kStart.isCoastalLand(-1) &&
            iPairwDuration > iSeaPenalty + 2)
        {
            ...
            if (iPathLength > 0)
            {
                int iPathTurns = ...;
                if (iPathTurns < iPairwDuration)
                {
                    iPairwDuration = iPathTurns;
                    bReachBySea = true;
                }
            }
        }

    Thus a legal sea path sets bReachBySea only when it also beats the local land
    duration. If the local land path came from a non-primary area, that land path can
    suppress the only flag that would make the target strategically reachable even
    though the same land path is explicitly not allowed to set m_bReachByLand.

    The final gate then discards every collected duration:

        if ((!m_bReachByLand && !bReachBySea) || aiPairwDurations.empty())
            return; // m_iDistance remains -1

SUPPORTED CURRENT MAP STATE
    A straightforward current-data state is enough:

      * the cache owner has an inland capital/main area, so no main-area naval launch
        route establishes reach to the target;
      * it also owns exactly two substantial cities on a secondary landmass. With only
        two cities and no capital there, AI_isPrimaryArea is false for that area;
      * at least one of those secondary cities is coastal and passes updateDistance's
        population/production filters;
      * an enemy coastal city is on that same secondary landmass;
      * a normal land path from the colony to the enemy exists and is short;
      * the player genuinely has cargo transports and a valid water path also exists
        from that colony to the enemy, but the naval trip is slower than the local land
        trip.

    For example, a local land duration of 4 and a legal naval duration of 6 produces:

        land path found:
            iPairwDuration = 4
            m_bReachByLand = false      // secondary area

        naval path:
            either not searched if the sea-penalty shortcut deems it unable to improve,
            or searched but 6 < 4 is false
            bReachBySea = false

        final:
            !m_bReachByLand && !bReachBySea
            => return with m_iDistance == -1

    Yet the target has a mechanically valid sea route from a city that the same
    function accepts as a naval source.

DESIGN NEGATIVE CONTROL
    This is not merely disagreement with the deliberate primary-area policy.

    The sea branch contains no AI_isPrimaryArea restriction. A secondary coastal city
    *is allowed* to establish bReachBySea when its sea route happens to be faster than
    its local land route. Therefore current policy already says that a peripheral port
    may establish naval reachability.

    The defect is that the exact same valid sea route stops counting as reachability
    solely because a shorter land path is also present -- even though that shorter land
    path has independently been declared insufficient to establish strategic land
    reachability.

    Route existence and route-speed selection are separate contracts; the implementation
    accidentally couples them.

LIVE CONSEQUENCES
    City::canReach is simply:

        return (m_iDistance >= 0);

    UWAICache::add increments m_aiReachableCities for foreign owners only when
    kCacheCity.canReach() is true. Therefore the false -1 propagates to the player/team
    reachability API:

        UWAI::Player::canReach(eTarget)
            -> cache.numReachableCities(eTarget) > 0

        UWAI::Team::canReach(eTarget)
            -> any member cache has numReachableCities(targetMember) > 0

    InvasionGraph::Node::targetCity stops at the first cached city that is not reachable
    and never chooses such a city as a target. Reachability counts also feed current
    WarUtilityAspect paths such as operational Readiness and elimination/hopeless-war
    logic.

    A valid target can therefore disappear from UWAI's target set because the legal sea
    route was slower than a deliberately non-qualifying local land route.

ANCESTRY
    The invariant mismatch already exists in practical initial AdvCiv commit 1253 /
    f6ff6a182f, in WarAndPeaceCache::City::updateDistance.

    The original comments are particularly diagnostic:

        "reachByLand refers to our (AI) capital. This is to ensure that the
         AI can still detect the need for a naval assault when it has a
         colony near the target civ."

    and immediately afterward:

        "// Reach by sea from c (whereas reachBySea refers to any city of agent)"

    Yet the original sea code sets the global reachBySea flag only inside:

        if (pwd < 0 || d < pwd)
        {
            pwd = d;
            reachBySea = true;
        }

    Thus from the initial implementation a non-capital colony could have a valid land
    path that does not establish reachByLand, while a valid but slower sea path also
    fails to establish reachBySea.

    Practical 2663 removed reachBySea from the serialized/external City interface and
    kept it only as a local updateDistance reachability flag; this does not change the
    root.

    Practical 2767 ("UWAI: Relax conditions for enemy cities being land targets")
    deliberately broadens qualifying land reach from only the capital to any
    AI_isPrimaryArea and adds the separate capital-area flag. That reduces the number of
    source cities exposed to the mismatch, but secondary areas still retain it.

    Practical 2929 ("Fix some issues with the calc of UWAI deployment distances") adds:

        iPairwDuration > iSeaPenalty + 2

    to avoid naval pathfinding when sea cannot be much faster. That is a valid speed
    optimization only when the existing land route already satisfies the reachability
    contract. For a secondary-area land route it can now prevent the sea existence
    check entirely.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
    Separate "valid sea route exists" from "sea is the duration chosen for this source."

    In particular:

      * when a coastal source's land route does NOT itself establish strategic land
        reachability (e.g. source area is non-primary), do not let the
        iPairwDuration/sea-penalty optimization skip the naval existence test solely
        because that local land route is short;
      * once a valid water path is found, let that fact establish bReachBySea
        independently of whether iPathTurns is faster than the current
        iPairwDuration;
      * continue to replace iPairwDuration with iPathTurns only when the sea route is
        actually faster. The shorter local land duration may still contribute to the
        weighted deployment estimate once the target is known to be strategically
        reachable; this is consistent with the existing design that allows secondary
        city durations to influence the aggregate without making them land targets.

    One narrow implementation shape is to track whether the current land route
    qualifies for m_bReachByLand, force the sea-path existence test for a non-qualifying
    coastal source, set bReachBySea whenever the water finder succeeds, and keep the
    `iPathTurns < iPairwDuration` comparison only around the duration replacement.

    Do not "repair" F226 by simply allowing every secondary-area land path to set
    m_bReachByLand. Practical 2767 and its downstream InvasionGraph/ArmamentForecast
    changes show that the primary-area distinction is deliberate.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS / SCOPE
    * If any qualifying primary-area source has a land path, m_bReachByLand is already
      true and the target remains reachable; F226 concerns cases where only
      non-qualifying land paths coexist with a legal naval route.
    * If the sea route is already faster than the local land route, current code sets
      bReachBySea and no false-unreachable result occurs.
    * If no valid sea route exists, preserving distance=-1 under the primary-area policy
      is intentional.
    * F218 is independent: it concerns falsely claiming transport trainability. F226
      assumes genuine cargo capability and a water path that the current water finder
      can actually generate.
    * The earlier primary-area-only land-reachability concern remains rejected as an
      intentional strategic heuristic. F226 is the interaction between that deliberate
      heuristic and the unrelated fastest-route test.

F227 / provisional KI#550
-------------------------
TITLE
    Mid-turn city destruction removes an entry from UWAICache's stateful
    area-clustering attack order without re-sorting the survivors, so a raze can leave
    the next invasion target in an order that a fresh cache build would never produce.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv UWAICache lifecycle/refactor defect. Current in Base
    AdvCiv 1.14 and AdvCiv-SAS. The modern destroy/create callback split was introduced
    by practical AdvCiv commit 2605 / f788c46a21 ("Various optimizations for
    UWAICache"). A capture that creates a replacement city eventually re-sorts on the
    create half; a pure destruction/raze has no create half and therefore leaves the
    greedily sorted vector stale until the next full cache update.

CURRENT ROOT
    sortCitiesByAttackPriority is not an ordinary fixed-key sort. It is a greedy
    selection pass whose score for each candidate depends on the area of the city
    selected immediately before it:

        if (i > 0 && pPrevArea != NULL &&
            !m_cityList[j]->city().isArea(*pPrevArea) &&
            rPriority.isPositive())
        {
            rPriority /= 2;
        }

    This deliberately clusters consecutive invasion targets in the same area.

    The modern destruction callback is:

        void reportCityDestroyed(CvCity const& kCity) { remove(kCity); }

    remove() erases the City object from m_cityMap and m_cityList but performs no
    sortCitiesByAttackPriority() afterward.

    The creation callback, by contrast, explicitly does:

        add(kCity);
        sortCitiesByAttackPriority();

    Thus a normal ownership transfer that destroys the old CvCity and creates a new
    CvCity is eventually re-sorted, but a razed/disbanded city is not.

DELETION DOES NOT PRESERVE THIS SORT
    Consider three currently reachable foreign cities with raw attack priorities:

        A1 = 100   area A
        A2 =  60   area A
        B1 =  90   area B

    A fresh greedy sort gives:

        i=0: no area penalty -> choose A1 (100)
        i=1: previous area A
             A2 = 60
             B1 = 90 / 2 = 45
             -> choose A2
        result: A1, A2, B1

    If A1 is then destroyed, vector erasure produces:

        A2, B1

    But a fresh sort of the surviving set must begin with raw priorities because
    position zero has no previous-area penalty:

        B1 = 90 > A2 = 60
        -> correct fresh order: B1, A2

    Therefore simple erasure is not order-preserving under the algorithm's own
    comparison semantics.

SUPPORTED HUMAN-TURN REPRODUCTION
    CvCity::kill notifies every major AI cache through AI_cityKilled before deleting the
    CvCity object, so a raze reaches reportCityDestroyed/remove immediately.

    A particularly ordinary path is:
      1. human captures an enemy city;
      2. acquisition creates the replacement CvCity and reportCityCreated re-sorts;
      3. human chooses to raze that newly acquired city;
      4. the new city is killed and reportCityDestroyed removes it;
      5. no replacement city is created, so no later reportCityCreated re-sort occurs;
      6. the rest of the human turn continues with a stale attack-order vector.

    This is exactly within the special mid-turn cache contract documented beside these
    callbacks:

        "It's important that the cache keep up with ownership changes
         so that the AI is aware of conquests made throughout a human turn."

LIVE CONSUMER
    InvasionGraph::Node::targetCity() iterates m_kCache.cityAt(i) in cached order and
    returns the first reachable, target-owned city that has not already been lost in the
    simulation.

    Thus the stale A2,B1 order above can make military analysis select A2 as the next
    target whereas a cache rebuilt from the same post-raze game state selects B1.

    Human-AI peace and other immediate war evaluations construct fresh WarEvaluator /
    InvasionGraph objects during the human turn, before the affected AI's next
    UWAICache::update. The stale vector is therefore behaviorally observable rather
    than merely an internal ordering discrepancy that is always repaired before use.

ANCESTRY
    The initial practical 1289 ownership-change callback updated/replaced one cached
    city and called sortCitiesByAttackPriority() at the end.

    Practical 2605 / f788c46a21 refactored the lifecycle to modern pointer-safe
    reportCityDestroyed/reportCityCreated callbacks. The old replacement callback's
    final unconditional sort was moved to reportCityCreated:

        add(c);
        sortCitiesByAttackPriority();

    while reportCityDestroyed became remove-only.

    This split is appropriate for captures because the creation callback follows the
    destruction callback and performs the final sort. It accidentally drops the old
    re-sort guarantee for destruction with no replacement. F227 is therefore best
    classified as an inherited AdvCiv 2605 lifecycle/refactor edge, not SAS-specific.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
    Re-establish the ordering invariant after a successful mid-turn removal when no
    later creation can be assumed.

    The simplest safe repair is to call sortCitiesByAttackPriority() after remove()
    actually erased a cached City, either from reportCityDestroyed or as part of a
    removal helper whose callers require current ordering.

    Do not rebuild City distances/asset scores merely for F227; the proven invariant is
    only the ordering of the surviving already-cached entries.

    Be aware that every major AI cache receives AI_cityKilled, so a blind re-sort after
    every notification has some cost. A small refinement could make remove return
    whether an entry was actually erased and sort only then. This remains far cheaper
    than a pathfinding/cache rebuild and occurs only on city destruction.

    F224 is independent: it concerns the cache owner's aggregate total assets not being
    reconciled with the changed own-city set. A practical implementation can update the
    aggregate and restore the sort in the same destruction callback, but the invariants
    are separate.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS / SCOPE
    * A standard city ownership transfer that creates a replacement is eventually
      sorted by reportCityCreated; F227's clearest live case is destruction/raze with no
      creation half.
    * Removing an element preserves the broad partition of reachable/own/unreachable
      priorities well enough that targetCity's break-on-invalid assertion is not the
      root. The defect is which valid target comes first.
    * If the removed city was late enough that the survivor order coincidentally
      remains equal to a fresh greedy sort, no behavioral difference occurs. The
      A1/A2/B1 construction proves that preservation is not guaranteed.
    * Capital relocation and other expensive city-derived changes after a conquest are
      separate cache-cadence questions. F227 requires only the existing cached
      priorities and the sort's own stateful area penalty.

SPONSORED-WAR MIXED-BUNDLE REJECTION -- NOT F228
-------------------------------------------------
The previously open reportSponsoredWar mixed-bundle seam was not promoted.

Human-AI trade-list filtering prevents the strongest reciprocal-overvaluation cases:
TRADE_WAR is nonannual, while Open Borders, Defensive Pact and Permanent Alliance are
annual dual items; at peacetime the trade UI hides annual/nonannual mixing once an item
from the opposite class is on the offer.

The remaining legal nonannual compensation items (gold, technology, city, maps, etc.)
are all things the sponsor can genuinely transfer to the hireling as part of the same
deal. If the hireling also gives an unrelated nonannual item back, whether its later
sense of obligation should remember gross received payment or marginal/net surplus is
a policy question, not a demonstrated contract violation. reportSponsoredWar's own
comment describes remembering the utility/deal value of the payment and even explicitly
allows overpayment to increase reluctance to end the war.

More than one TRADE_WAR item in a normal UWAI-valued deal remains intentionally blocked
by AI_dealVal's +1,000,000 second-war price. Do not spend an F-root on these bundle
shapes without a stronger supported contract.

    m_aiVassalResourceScore.read(pStream);

AGGRESSIVE / LEADERSHIP TRAIT RECHECK -- NOT F228
--------------------------------------------------
The low-mention updateTraits helper initially looked stale under current SAS XML:
Base AdvCiv Aggressive grants Combat I, while SAS practical 4856 changes its free
promotion to Leadership. updateTraits recognizes an "offensive trait" only when one of
the trait's free promotions has positive generic combat percent.

Current Leadership has:
    iCombatPercent = 0
    iCityDefense   = 0
    iExperiencePercent = 100

so current Aggressive leaders correctly no longer trip m_bOffensiveTrait.

This is not a correctness regression. The only live hasOffensiveTrait consumer in
InvasionGraph explicitly models the old direct Combat-I effect by adding +10% to
simulated army power. Leadership no longer grants that immediate +10% combat strength;
continuing to classify it as the old offensive-trait bonus would overstate current SAS
army strength. Leadership's faster experience gain may deserve separate long-term
modeling, but that is an AI-enhancement/design question rather than a stale cache bug.

The m_bDefensiveTrait flag is used elsewhere (e.g. distrustRating), and current
Protective/City Garrison data still trips its intended city-defense test. No F-root.

PERMANENT-ALLIANCE STALE CITY-OBJECT RECHECK -- NOT F228
---------------------------------------------------------
After a Permanent Alliance, existing UWAICache::City objects can temporarily retain
their pre-merge `m_iDistance` classification, so a newly absorbed teammate's cities can
still look "foreign" (`distance > 0`) to a survivor member's cache until its next normal
refresh.

This is real staging, but no current wrong target result was proved:
InvasionGraph re-checks the cached city's live owner/team/war-opponent status before
accepting it as a military target, and totalAssetScore only sums cities actually owned
by m_eOwner. The stale teammate entries may be scanned past but do not become valid
enemy targets under the tested consumers. Do not promote a full post-PA City-cache
rebuild without a stronger behavioral contract.

F228 / provisional KI#551
-------------------------
TITLE
    Permanent Alliance migration is one-way for persistent team-keyed UWAI history:
    members of the surviving team inherit the absorbed leader's history, but outsider
    caches that store past-war or sponsored-war state *against the absorbed team* are
    never remapped to the surviving team. A paid hireling can therefore forget its
    live war obligation immediately when its target joins a Permanent Alliance, and
    outsiders permanently forget war-experience history against the absorbed half.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv/UWAI Permanent-Alliance state-migration defect.
    The one-way merge is present from the initial WarAndPeace/UWAI integration.
    Current AdvCiv 1.14 and AdvCiv-SAS retain it.

PERSISTENT STATE
    UWAICache::clear(true) deliberately preserves:
        m_aiPastWarScore
        m_aiBounty
        m_aeSponsorPerTarget
    because these are event-maintained historical/obligation fields rather than
    ordinary per-turn derived cache values.

    reportWarEnding updates m_aiPastWarScore and clears sponsorship for the specific
    enemy TeamTypes key.

    reportSponsoredWar stores:
        m_aiBounty[eTarget]
        m_aeSponsorPerTarget[eTarget]

    HiredHand and confidenceFromPastWars later query these fields using the *current*
    target TeamTypes.

CURRENT PA MERGE
    CvTeam::addTeam(eAbsorbedTeam) saves the absorbed team's leader id, transfers the
    absorbed players onto the surviving team and merges the core team relations.

    In particular it explicitly propagates differing wars in both directions through
    queueWar/triggerWars. If the absorbed team B was at war with outsider C and the
    surviving team A was not, C becomes at war with A as part of the alliance merge.

    Near the end of CvTeam::addTeam current code calls only:

        AI().uwai().addTeam(eTeamLeader);

    UWAI::Team::addTeam then iterates the *members of the newly merged surviving team*:

        for (MemberAIIter it(m_eAgent); it.hasNext(); ++it)
            it->uwai().getCache().addTeam(eOtherLeader);

    UWAICache::addTeam copies the absorbed leader's own persistent history into each
    surviving-team member:

        m_aiPastWarScore.add(eTeam, kOther.m_aiPastWarScore.get(eTeam));

    and chooses/merges the absorbed leader's sponsorship/bounty for each target.

    No corresponding loop visits major-civ players outside the alliance and remaps
    values whose *key* is the absorbed TeamTypes to the surviving TeamTypes.

SUPPORTED SPONSORED-WAR REPRODUCTION
    Let:
        A = team that will survive the Permanent Alliance
        B = team that will be absorbed
        C = AI hireling outside the alliance
        D = sponsor

    1. D pays C to declare war on B.

       CvDeal reports the sponsorship to C's cache:
           sponsorAgainst[B] = D
           bountyAgainst[B]  > 0

    2. Later A and B form a Permanent Alliance.

       CvTeamAI::AI_permanentAllianceTrade does not require the two teams to have
       identical current wars. CvTeam::addTeam explicitly contains the machinery for
       transferring differing wars.

    3. Because B was at war with C, the core team merge makes C at war with surviving
       team A as well.

    4. The UWAI addTeam call updates A/B's newly merged member caches only. C's cache
       remains:
           sponsorAgainst[B] = D
           bountyAgainst[B]  > 0

       while:
           sponsorAgainst[A] = NO_PLAYER
           bountyAgainst[A]  = 0
       in the clean reproduction where C had no prior sponsorship against A.

    5. C subsequently considers peace with the war opponent that now actually exists,
       team A.

       HiredHand::evaluate uses:
           eTheirTeam = A
           ourCache().sponsorAgainst(eTheirTeam)
           ourCache().bountyAgainst(eTheirTeam)

       and therefore sees no sponsorship.

    The paid-war obligation can vanish immediately solely because the target team
    changed identity through a Permanent Alliance. The payment, sponsor, hireling and
    continuing physical war all still exist.

LIVE CONSEQUENCE
    HiredHand is specifically designed to make an AI "inclined to fight for 20 turns"
    after being hired. It turns the remembered original payment utility into positive
    utility for continuing the war.

    Under F228 that utility disappears for the transferred war against A. C can become
    willing to make peace substantially earlier than it would have if B had remained a
    standalone team, despite D having paid for the same continuing conflict.

PAST-WAR HISTORY SIBLING UNDER THE SAME ROOT
    m_aiPastWarScore is likewise keyed by target TeamTypes and preserved across turns.

    UWAI::Player::confidenceFromPastWars(eTarget) reads exactly:
        m_cache.pastWarScore(eTarget)

    and maps a negative history into reduced future war confidence (first lost-war scale
    roughly -15%, bounded over repeated history).

    If outsider C had a strongly negative past-war score against B but no history
    against A, B's absorption makes all future evaluations target A. C then reads
    pastWarScore[A] and the B history is orphaned under the dead TeamTypes key.

    This is especially diagnostic because UWAICache::addTeam already treats
    `m_aiPastWarScore` as persistent team-related data that *must* be merged for the
    surviving alliance members. The omission is the reverse direction: outsiders'
    histories about the absorbed target are never merged/remapped.

ANCESTRY
    The initial practical AdvCiv WarAndPeace implementation (1253 /
    f6ff6a182f) already defines WarAndPeaceCache::addTeam as a one-way operation:
    it obtains the absorbed team's leader cache and adds that leader's past-war and
    sponsorship data to the surviving cache.

    CvTeam::addTeam then invokes WarAndPeaceAI::Team::addTeam only for the surviving
    team. There is no outsider reverse migration.

    Practical 1268 changes the API from an absorbed TeamTypes to the saved absorbed
    leader PlayerTypes so the source cache remains accessible after player reassignment;
    it preserves the same one-way semantics.

    At that time CvTeam::addTeam also called getWPAI.update() after the merge. That
    function merely rebuilt the global lists of alive major teams/civs and team-member
    vectors. It did not rewrite any UWAICache/WarAndPeaceCache history maps, so it did
    not repair the outsider direction.

    Practical 1818 replaces cached team-member vectors with live AgentIterators and
    removes the old global registry refresh. F216 is a separate regression caused by
    that live iterator including the absorbed leader itself. F228 predates 1818: the
    missing outsider-key migration exists from the original design.

    Current CvTeam::addTeam contains extensive reverse-direction migration for core
    bilateral counters/relations (war counters, contact history, war success,
    espionage, etc.), which further demonstrates the general team-identity contract.
    UWAI's persistent outsider maps remain an exception.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
    During Permanent Alliance absorption, before the absorbed team identity becomes
    unusable as a live target, migrate persistent outsider cache entries keyed by
    eAbsorbedTeam to eSurvivingTeam.

    At minimum cover the fields that UWAICache::addTeam itself classifies as persistent
    team-related history:
        * m_aiPastWarScore
        * m_aiBounty
        * m_aeSponsorPerTarget

    For each major-civ player outside the merged team:
      * combine pastWarScore[absorbed] into pastWarScore[survivor] using the same
        additive policy already used when survivor-side member histories are merged;
      * if sponsorship against the absorbed team exists, preserve it under the
        surviving target. If both keys already contain sponsorships, use a coherent
        conflict policy (the existing UWAICache::addTeam policy chooses the higher
        bounty when both have sponsors);
      * clear/reset the absorbed-team entries afterward if practical, to avoid retaining
        dead-key duplicate history.

    Keep the direction conceptually separate from survivor-member `addTeam` to avoid
    reintroducing F216 self-addition. A dedicated "target team absorbed" helper on
    outsider caches would make the two directions explicit.

    Derived per-turn maps (threat, reachable cities, vassal scores, war utility, etc.)
    need not all be folded into F228; they have normal refresh semantics or live-team
    checks. The proven root concerns persistent event-maintained history/obligation
    that otherwise never migrates itself.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS / SCOPE
    * If C already has a sponsorship against surviving A, the conflict needs a merge
      policy; the clean reproduction intentionally starts with none.
    * If C's war against B ends normally before the alliance, reportWarEnding can clear
      the B sponsorship. F228 concerns a war transferred by the alliance itself.
    * The second HiredHand branch ("we've hired someone") also uses current-team keys,
      but the direct loss of C's own paid obligation is sufficient proof.
    * F216 is different: it concerns self-add/doubling inside the surviving merged
      team's member loop after the AgentIterator refactor. F228 is the missing outsider
      target-key direction and exists even in the original vector-based implementation.
    * The temporarily stale UWAICache::City team classification after a PA is not part
      of F228; no concrete wrong target was proved from it.

maps. Revisit only if another event-maintained field is proved to have the same orphaned
target-team lifetime.

No repository source files were modified by ChatGPT-5.6-Sol during this audit.

F228 SAME-ROOT REFINEMENT -- READY-TO-CAPITULATE TARGET KEY
-----------------------------------------------------------
F228's persistent outsider target-team migration root also covers
m_readyToCapitulateTo.

This state is not an ordinary per-turn heuristic. It is an event-maintained team-level
handshake used specifically for AI capitulation to a human master. Non-leader member
queries redirect to the current team leader's cache, and AI_surrenderTrade refuses a
human master with DENIAL_RECENT_CANCEL unless the current leader cache says the team is
ready.

Supported target-absorption reproduction:

    A = surviving team in a Permanent Alliance
    B = absorbed human team
    C = outside AI team currently at war with B

Before the alliance, C's UWAI has already decided to capitulate to the human side:

    C.readyToCapitulateTo contains B

The core Permanent-Alliance merge can transfer C's war with B onto surviving team A.
Because B's human member is moved onto A, A is now a human team. The physical war and
the already-made UWAI capitulation decision therefore concern the same human side, now
under TeamTypes A.

But C's persistent set is untouched by UWAI::Team::addTeam:

    contains(B) == true
    contains(A) == false

A subsequent AI_surrenderTrade(A) asks isReadyToCapitulate(A), which returns false and
can therefore produce DENIAL_RECENT_CANCEL solely because the prospective master was
renumbered by the Permanent Alliance.

This belongs under F228 rather than a new F-number. The same proven invariant applies:
persistent event-maintained state whose key denotes a target team must survive
absorption of that target team.

F228's outsider migration repair boundary should therefore include, at minimum:

    m_aiPastWarScore
    m_aiBounty
    m_aeSponsorPerTarget
    m_readyToCapitulateTo

For readiness, the natural merge policy is set-union under the surviving human target:
if an outsider was ready to capitulate to either side and the merged surviving team is
human, preserve readiness under the surviving TeamTypes. Remove the absorbed dead-key
entry afterward when practical.

Do not apply F228 mechanically to m_aiWarUtilityIgnoringDistraction or ordinary
threat/reachability maps. Those are derived/reset by normal update cadence; F228 is
about state that otherwise has no producer capable of recreating the lost historical
meaning after the target TeamTypes disappears.

COMPACT-MAP BOUNDS PASS -- NEGATIVE CONTROLS
--------------------------------------------
Several current UWAICache integer maps use compact short storage:

    CivPlayerMap<int,short> m_aiReachableCities
    CivPlayerMap<int,short> m_aiTargetMissions
    CivTeamMap<int,short>   m_aiPlotsLostAtWar
    CivTeamMap<int,short>   m_aiBounty

EnumMap's normal compactValue path is a plain cast unless ENUM_MAP_EXTRA_ASSERTS is
enabled; that macro is currently commented out. Therefore each such field needs its
own producer-range argument rather than assuming the template protects it.

No new root is promoted for the first three at this checkpoint:

* Default SAS48 world dimensions are 99x70 terrain cells, and current AdvCiv map reset
  uses two plots per cell for ordinary world-size dimensions: 198x140 = 27,720 plots.
  Thus even an intentionally absurd "every plot lost against one rival" upper bound
  stays below signed-short max on the default largest SAS world size.
  Custom map scripts that override grid dimensions can use a different scale and remain
  a future robustness concern, but no current F-root is assigned solely on that basis.

* m_aiReachableCities is bounded more tightly than the total plot count under ordinary
  city-placement rules, so the default SAS48 geometry is also a strong negative control.

* m_aiTargetMissions counts units/cargo rather than plots and therefore lacks the same
  mathematical map bound. A gigantic unit population could in principle exceed 32767,
  but no supported current-SAS reproduction near that threshold has been established.
  Keep this as robustness only unless concrete unit-count evidence appears.

m_aiBounty is materially different and is F229 below.

F229 / provisional KI#552
-------------------------
TITLE
    Sponsored-war bounty is compacted from int utility to signed short without a range
    check; a sufficiently large legal positive overpayment wraps negative and makes
    reportSponsoredWar erase the sponsorship entirely.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED AdvCiv enum-map compression regression. The sponsored-war value was an int
    in the original UWAI/WarAndPeace cache. Practical AdvCiv commit 3183 /
    59a3e3190061 ("Rewrite of enum map classes") changed m_aiBounty from
    CivTeamMap<int> to CivTeamMap<int,short> as part of a nominally non-functional
    compact-storage rewrite. Current AdvCiv 1.14 and AdvCiv-SAS retain the short.

CURRENT STORAGE / CAST CONTRACT
    UWAICache.h:

        CivTeamMap<int,short> m_aiBounty;

    EnumMap's compact conversion is:

        #ifdef ENUM_MAP_EXTRA_ASSERTS
            return safeCast<ToType>(fValue);
        #else
            return (ToType)fValue;
        #endif

    ENUM_MAP_EXTRA_ASSERTS is currently disabled/commented out. Thus assigning an int
    outside signed-short range performs the target compiler's narrowing conversion
    without assertion or clamping. On the supported MSVC/Windows target, signed short
    is 16 bit and the practical result is low-16-bit/two's-complement wrapping.

SUPPORTED PAYMENT PATH
    CvPlayer::canTradeItem(TRADE_GOLD) imposes no special diplomatic upper bound on a
    specified human gold amount:

        if (getGold() >= item.m_iData)
            bValid = true;

    The amount is an int. A human sponsor can therefore intentionally overpay for a war
    declaration up to their actual treasury.

    This is not contrary to UWAI's intended contract. reportSponsoredWar explicitly
    comments:

        "As it is now, paying more than the AI demands makes it a bit
         more reluctant to end the war."

    Large positive overpayment is therefore a supported semantic direction, not an
    invalid-input case.

VALUE PIPELINE
    reportSponsoredWar stores:

        m_aiBounty.set(eTarget,
            tradeValToUtility(kOwner.AI_dealVal(eSponsor, kWeReceive)).round());

    For received TRADE_GOLD, current CvPlayerAI::AI_dealVal applies
    AI_goldTradeValuePercent(), which returns 200:

        iValue += (iGold * 200) / 100;

    UWAI::Player::tradeValToUtility then multiplies by:

        3 * speedFactor /
        (max(10, estimated commerce) + 2 * max(1, estimated production))

    The rate is positive and can be as high as 0.25 when the denominator is at its
    minimum 12. At that upper rate:

        65,536 gold
        -> AI_dealVal 131,072
        -> utility 32,768

    already exceeds SHRT_MAX by one. A slightly larger example such as utility 35,000
    narrows to a negative signed-short value on the target platform.

    Even for stronger economies with a lower conversion rate, there is no short-based
    cap on the legal human payment; a sufficiently large positive treasury/payment can
    reach the same storage boundary.

IMMEDIATE BEHAVIORAL FAILURE
    The wrapped value is consumed immediately by the same function:

        if (m_aiBounty.get(eTarget) > 0)
            m_aeSponsorPerTarget.set(eTarget, eSponsor);
        else
        {
            m_aiBounty.set(eTarget, 0);
            m_aeSponsorPerTarget.set(eTarget, NO_PLAYER);
        }

    Therefore a positive payment that crosses the compact boundary can become negative,
    fail the >0 test and be normalized to:

        bountyAgainst(target)  = 0
        sponsorAgainst(target) = NO_PLAYER

    A smaller overpayment below the boundary is remembered correctly, while a larger
    overpayment can make the AI remember no sponsorship at all.

LIVE CONSEQUENCE
    WarUtilityAspect::HiredHand reads sponsorAgainst/current-target and bountyAgainst
    to keep a paid AI inclined to continue the sponsored war for roughly 20 turns.
    F229 therefore removes the intended obligation immediately at deal creation.

    This is the opposite of the source comment's monotonic intent: overpaying should
    increase reluctance to end the war, not erase the obligation.

ANCESTRY
    The original WarAndPeace/UWAI cache stored sponsorship value in a full int.

    Practical 3183 / 59a3e3190061 ("Rewrite of enum map classes") changes, in
    UWAICache.h:

        CivTeamMap<int> m_aiBounty;
        ->
        CivTeamMap<int,short> m_aiBounty;

    The commit message characterizes the broad XML/serialization changes as
    non-functional and introduces compact enum-map storage generally. No saturation
    policy was added around reportSponsoredWar.

    Current save version 9 serializes the compact short representation, so the narrowed
    value is also the persistent representation once it has survived the immediate
    sign check (values that wrap nonpositive are cleared before that).

REPAIR BOUNDARY
    Keep sponsored-war obligation monotonic under large positive payment.

    Lowest-risk repair while preserving current save width:
      * compute the bounty utility in a full int/scaled temporary;
      * clamp/saturate it explicitly to [0, SHRT_MAX] before assigning m_aiBounty.

    Saturation is semantically reasonable here: HiredHand only needs a bounded positive
    measure of the original obligation, and any payment above the cap can simply mean
    "maximal remembered bounty." It preserves the current version-9 short save format
    and prevents overpayment from becoming less obligation.

    Alternative:
      * restore m_aiBounty to full int;
      * but then bump/adapt UWAICache save serialization so current version-9 short
        saves remain readable and new saves have an unambiguous width.

    Do not enable ENUM_MAP_EXTRA_ASSERTS globally as the sole repair. That would turn a
    deterministic release logic bug into an assertion but would not define safe release
    behavior.

    Do not clamp only after m_aiBounty.set; by then narrowing has already lost the sign
    and magnitude. Clamp the full-width temporary before compact assignment.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS / SCOPE
    * This is not the same as F228. F228 loses a correctly stored bounty when a target
      team identity is absorbed; F229 can erase sponsorship at the moment the deal is
      recorded, without any team merge.
    * The earlier mixed-bundle sponsorship question remains rejected. F229 needs only a
      single ordinary WAR declaration compensated by legal gold.
    * Extremely huge gold can encounter unrelated int-arithmetic limits in other trade
      formulas at much larger amounts. F229's signed-short boundary occurs far earlier
      and is independently sufficient.
    * Compact short storage is not automatically defective. Default-SAS48 plot/city
      geometry gives useful bounds for other fields; each compact field must be judged
      by its producer domain.

F230 / provisional KI#553
-------------------------
TITLE
    Pre-v4 past-war save conversion scales only teams alive at load; legacy history
    against a dead rival remains at the old granularity and becomes mis-scaled if that
    rival is later revived.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv backward-save / revival compatibility regression.
    Present in current base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.

CURRENT CODE
    UWAICache::read restores the legacy pre-v9 past-war array first:

        if (iSaveVersion >= 9)
            m_aiPastWarScore.read(pStream);
        else m_aiPastWarScore.readArray<int>(pStream);

    It then performs the pre-v4 granularity migration only for teams that are alive at
    load time:

        if (iSaveVersion < 4)
        {
            for (TeamIter<CIV_ALIVE> it; it.hasNext(); ++it)
                m_aiPastWarScore.multiply(it->getID(), 100);
        }

    The two operations have different domains. readArray<int> restores the serialized
    CivTeamMap slots; the migration subsequently touches only the currently living
    subset.

ORIGINAL COMPATIBILITY CONTRACT
    AdvCivPreSAS commit 1378, 2348464189, introduced save version 4 specifically for
    the increased granularity of pastWarScore.

    Its migration was deliberately slot-complete:

        if(savegameVersion < 4)
            for(int i = 0; i < MAX_CIV_TEAMS; i++)
                pastWarScores[i] *= 100;

    The same change made the live consumer interpret the stored value in hundredths
    and changed new reportWarEnding contributions to roughly +/-100 instead of +/-1.

    Therefore the migration contract was not "convert currently relevant teams."
    It was "convert every serialized legacy team slot."

REGRESSION POINT
    AdvCivPreSAS commit 1818, 854cb8058c,
        "Use AgentIterators in all UWAI classes"
    replaced the all-slot loop with:

        for (TeamIter<CIV_ALIVE> it; it.hasNext(); ++it)
            pastWarScores.multiply(it->getID(), 100);

    That iterator substitution is harmless for many live-game loops, but not for a
    save-format migration whose input contains values for identities that can be dead
    at load time.

WHY THE SKIPPED VALUE IS REALLY STILL DESERIALIZED
    Current EnumMap::readArray reads the full stored key range one value at a time and
    calls setUnsafe for each key. It does not filter the data according to current
    alive status.

    Therefore a dead team's pre-v4 pastWarScore can be present in m_aiPastWarScore
    immediately after deserialization and still escape the required x100 conversion.

SUPPORTED OBSERVABLE STATE
    1. Team A and team B fight and finish a war in a save-format version older than 4.
       A therefore has a nonzero legacy pastWarScore entry for B.
    2. B is later eliminated before that game is saved.
    3. The old save is loaded by current AdvCiv / AdvCiv-SAS.
    4. readArray restores B's serialized legacy score, but TeamIter<CIV_ALIVE> skips B,
       so B's entry remains in old +/-1-scale granularity rather than the new
       +/-100-scale granularity.
    5. B is later revived. AdvCiv explicitly supports player revival; current
       CvPlayer::setAlive(true) reports playerRevived and refreshes UWAI state.
    6. Other players can again evaluate B, and confidenceFromPastWars(B) consumes A's
       still-mis-scaled history.

    Revival is not merely hypothetical dead data. AdvCivPreSAS commit 2010,
    56af3a8dfa, "Fix issues with AI Auto Play ending upon player defeat", added the
    explicit playerRevived lifecycle, and current SAS retains and extends that path.

LIVE CONSEQUENCE
    UWAI::Player::confidenceFromPastWars currently does:

        scaled rPastWarScore = per100(m_cache.pastWarScore(eTarget));
        int iSign = (rPastWarScore < 0 ? -1 : 1);
        scaled r = 1 + iSign * rPastWarScore.abs().sqrt() * fixp(0.15);
        r.clamp(fixp(0.5), fixp(1.5));

    For the simplest old score of +1:
        correct migration: +1 -> +100 -> per100 = 1
        confidence term:   1 + sqrt(1) * 0.15 = 1.15

        skipped migration: +1 remains +1 -> per100 = 0.01
        confidence term:   1 + sqrt(0.01) * 0.15 = 1.015

    Likewise for -1:
        correct: 0.85
        skipped: 0.985

    The stored score is therefore 100x too small. Because confidence uses sqrt, the
    displacement from neutral is 10x too small for the same legacy score before clamp.

WHY THIS IS NOT JUST A DEAD-SLOT CLEANLINESS ISSUE
    If the skipped team remained permanently dead, the stale scale would normally be
    behaviorally irrelevant. The explicit revival lifecycle makes the old key live
    again without rerunning the save-version migration. The defect therefore becomes
    observable precisely in the compatibility state that the current reader claims to
    support.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    For iSaveVersion < 4, multiply every valid CivTeam key represented by the legacy
    serialized map, not TeamIter<CIV_ALIVE>.

    Conceptually:

        if (iSaveVersion < 4)
        {
            FOR_EACH_ENUM(CivTeam)
                m_aiPastWarScore.multiply(eLoopCivTeam, 100);
        }

    Use the project's exact all-CivTeam enum iteration spelling after compile review.
    An explicit 0 .. MAX_CIV_TEAMS-1 loop is also semantically faithful to the original
    migration if that is safer for this old-format branch.

    No save-version bump should be needed: this repairs the read conversion of an
    already-supported old format.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS / SCOPE
    * Current-format saves are unaffected.
    * Pre-v4 entries for teams alive at load are converted correctly.
    * A skipped dead entry matters only if it contains legacy history and later becomes
      behaviorally reachable again, e.g. through revival.
    * This is separate from F228. F228 concerns one-way migration of persistent
      team-keyed history during a Permanent Alliance team absorption. F230 concerns a
      backward-save conversion whose domain was accidentally narrowed.
    * This is also separate from F225 / KI#548, which concerns reconstruction of the
      revived player's own military cache from already-existing units.


REMAINING C019-WIP17 CURSOR -- RESULTS SO FAR
---------------------------------------------

1. totalAssetScore positivity / denominator seam -- NOT PROMOTED
    updateTotalAssetScore starts from a +5 Palace baseline and then adds own-city asset
    scores plus national-wonder contributions.

    Individual per-city AI_assetVal(..., true) scores can indeed be negative because
    maintenance is subtracted. Historical commit 3038, 23545fcd6e,
        "Fix two minor issues with UWAI asset score values"
    explicitly notes that a per-city score can be negative and defensively clamps a
    vassal-loss calculation.

    However, the historical totalAssetScore == 0 observation was subsequently traced
    to an incomplete new-player refresh. Commit 3044, 8a2a75e1e0,
        "Fix two minor inconsistencies in the UWAI cache"
    changed UWAI::processNewPlayerInGame from a partial typical-unit refresh to a full
    cache.update(true), and its comment says the bad total "Had not worked correctly
    when called from UWAI::processNewPlayerInGame. Should be fixed now".

    Risk::evaluate still divides by totalAssetScore + epsilon rather than max(1,...),
    so a genuinely nonpositive aggregate would be dangerous. But this audit has not
    established a supported normal full-refresh state that makes the aggregate
    nonpositive. Mathematical possibility from a negative constituent is not enough.

    RESULT:
        Keep as a robustness seam / historical check, not a new root.

2. remaining compact EnumMap producer bounds -- NO NEW ROOT AFTER F229
    F229 remains the concrete compact-type defect because a legal full-width human
    sponsored-war payment can cross signed-short range before assignment to m_aiBounty.

    The other reviewed compact fields have substantially tighter domains in the
    supported default geometry, or require only an extreme theoretical count with no
    supported reproduction established here.

    In particular, the prior WIP17 bound for the default SAS48 standard map remains
    useful: 198 * 140 = 27,720 plots, below signed-short max 32,767. That gives a real
    default-world upper bound for plot-loss counts and an even tighter practical bound
    for reachable-city counts.

    targetMissions could only overflow a signed short through an extreme number of
    simultaneously counted units / missions; no supported practical state was proved.

    RESULT:
        No F230-style "short is suspicious, therefore bug" finding is manufactured.

3. remaining old-version read defaults -- CLEAN EXCEPT F230
    * pre-v3 m_abCanBeHiredAgainst omission inherits the map's intended true reset from
      clear(), so old saves receive the correct default.
    * pre-v5 m_bFocusOnPeacefulVictory omission inherits false from clear(), matching
      the feature's introduction semantics.
    * pre-v1 relative-navy reconstruction calls updateRelativeNavyPower(), but the
      feature remains explicitly "Not implemented; work in progress" and has no live
      consumer found in the current source.
    * City pre-v4 capital-area fallback from reach-by-land is deliberate compatibility
      behavior; no defect established.
    * pre-v3 / pre-v1 discarded City fields are consumed only to preserve stream
      alignment; no live state was found to depend on them.

4. City construction / target-value initialization -- CLEAN
    City construction computes distance/reachability and asset score before passing
    the cache-city pointer into AI_targetCityValue. The fields needed by the current
    target-value path are therefore initialized first.

    No use-before-initialization root was found in this pass.

5. reportCityCreated human-cache asymmetry -- OBSERVED, NOT PROMOTED YET
    Full updateCities includes a foreign city for a human cache without requiring
    AI_deduceCitySite, while reportCityCreated requires same-team or deducible city and
    has no corresponding human override.

    City transfer also reports destruction of the old city before creation of the
    replacement, so a human cache can transiently lose a newly transferred foreign
    city until a full refresh when it is not deducible.

    However, the report callbacks are explicitly motivated by keeping AI caches aware
    of changes during a human turn, and this pass has not yet proved a live
    post-transfer-before-refresh consumer for the human cache whose behavior is wrong.

    RESULT:
        Preserve as an open cadence/contracts question for F231+, not a finding.

6. F224 refinement -- NO NEW ROOT
    Normal city founding also calls AI_cityCreated for major caches, so the same
    reportCityCreated path that does not recompute m_rTotalAssets is reached outside
    conquest as well.

    This broadens the producer side of F224's stale-total-assets mechanism, but the
    strongest already-proved behavioral reproduction remains the mid-turn
    conquest/diplomacy path recorded under F224. Do not duplicate it as a new root.

      counts stale for surviving cached foreign cities after the cache owner's own
