F251 / provisional KI#574
-------------------------
TITLE
    A node simulated as eliminated or capitulated does not remove its outgoing invasion
    edge; recursive loss resolution can therefore let a defeated civ attack its own
    target later in the same graph component.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited UWAI graph-lifecycle defect.
    Present in current Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.
    The core lifetime mismatch is present from the initial InvasionGraph design.

GRAPH ORDER THAT MAKES THE DEFECT LIVE
    InvasionGraph edges point:
        attacker -> primary target

    resolveLossesRec resolves incoming attackers recursively BEFORE resolving the
    current node itself:

        for each player in m_targetedBy:
            attacker.resolveLossesRec();

        resolveLosses();

    Consider an ordinary acyclic component:

        A -> B -> C

    C is the sink.
    C.resolveLossesRec therefore calls:
        B.resolveLossesRec
            -> A.resolveLossesRec
            -> B.resolveLosses()    // A attacks B
        -> C.resolveLosses()        // B attacks C

    This ordering is explicitly part of the graph simulation; it is not an unusual
    re-entry or external callback.

HOW B BECOMES SIMULATED-DEAD
    During B.resolveLosses, an A attack can successfully conquer one of B's cached
    cities.

    applyStep then records:

        addCityLoss(kStepCity);

    and if the simulated city losses equal B's actual city count:

        if (m_cityLosses.size() == iCurrentCities)
            setEliminated(true);

    Simulated capitulation likewise calls:

        setCapitulated(...)
            -> setEliminated(true);

    `setEliminated` is only:

        void setEliminated(bool b) { m_bEliminated = b; }

    It does not remove B's outgoing primary-target edge.

    `setCapitulated` likewise marks the node eliminated but does not call
    changePrimaryTarget(NULL).

OUTGOING EDGE THEREFORE SURVIVES
    B's existing primary target is C.

    B was inserted into:
        C.m_targetedBy

    when the edge B -> C was established.

    Neither setEliminated nor setCapitulated removes B from C.m_targetedBy.

    applyStep has two later edge-removal checks, but both are based on ARMY power being
    fully exhausted:

        if (our Army power <= our lost Army power)
            changePrimaryTarget(NULL);

    A civ can lose all simulated cities or capitulate while retaining substantial Army
    power. In that common shape the B -> C link survives.

DOWNSTREAM C THEN INVOKES THE DEAD B
    After B.resolveLossesRec returns, C.resolveLossesRec continues and calls
    C.resolveLosses().

    C's m_targetedBy still contains B.

    C.resolveLosses iterates those invaders and calls:

        B.step(...)

    The first thing Node::step checks is only whether a non-clash attack can find a
    target city:

        pCacheCity = targetCity();
        if (pCacheCity == NULL && !bClashOnly)
            return NULL;

    It does NOT reject:
        isEliminated()
        hasCapitulated()

    B's primary target is still C, real map cities remain physically present because
    InvasionGraph is only a simulation, and B's cache still contains C's target cities.

    Therefore B.step can construct a normal attack step despite B having already been
    simulated as completely eliminated or capitulated.

SUPPORTED REPRODUCTION
    1. Three simulated war parties form A -> B -> C.
    2. B has enough remaining Army power that its army is not completely destroyed.
    3. A's attack in B.resolveLosses takes B's final simulated city, or causes B to
       capitulate.
    4. B is marked eliminated.
    5. B -> C is not unlinked.
    6. Control returns to C.resolveLosses.
    7. C still regards B as an incoming attacker.
    8. B.step uses B's surviving military and C's still-existing real/cache city data.
    9. C can suffer predicted losses/conquests from a civ that the same simulation has
       already declared defeated.

    No stale external cache or another known finding is needed.

CAPITULATION VARIANT
    setCapitulated explicitly comments:

        "Treat capitulated as eliminated, i.e. assume no further losses."

    Yet the same outgoing-edge survival lets a capitulated node remain an attacker of a
    third party later in the component.

    This is especially contradictory because the comment immediately states that the
    real rules would make the vassal join its master's wars but that such follow-up is
    intentionally NOT modeled. The current graph nevertheless lets the node continue
    its pre-capitulation offensive.

BEHAVIORAL CONSEQUENCES
    The defeated node can:
        * inflict additional military losses;
        * conquer cities;
        * alter later simulated elimination/capitulation;
        * affect graph distraction and clash state;
        * change MilitaryAnalyst's final lost-power/city-loss/conquest results;
        * feed downstream WarUtilityAspect utilities.

    This can make third-party war projections materially too favorable or too damaging
    depending on which side the zombie attacker belongs to.

WHY ARMY-ELIMINATION CLEANUP DOES NOT FIX IT
    Current applyStep correctly removes a primary target when a node's Army branch is
    completely exhausted.

    Simulation elimination and capitulation are different predicates:
        city count / surrender state, not zero Army power.

    Surviving mobile military is exactly what makes the stale edge behaviorally active.

ANCESTRY / HISTORICAL CONTROL
    The initial InvasionGraph implementation already represented elimination as a
    boolean setter without automatic edge cleanup.

    Later practical 1726 / 04eceb5fab,
        "Bugfix in UWAI invasion graph"
    corrected an edge-removal bug when the ATTACKER's Army was eliminated:

        wrong:
            changePrimaryTarget(NULL);          // on defender/this

        fixed:
            attacker.changePrimaryTarget(NULL);

    This historical fix is useful evidence that outgoing-edge removal must occur on the
    node whose offensive has ended and is an explicit graph-lifecycle operation.

    No later commit found adds the corresponding cleanup when the node itself becomes
    eliminated/capitulated through city-loss/surrender simulation.

DISTINCTION FROM EARLIER ROOTS
    F227/F231/F233/F236:
        concern UWAICache ordering/geometry/knowledge state.
        F251 reproduces with a perfectly current cache.

    F250:
        controls whether simulated capitulation is entered based on victory stages.
        F251 occurs after either a legitimate capitulation OR complete simulated city
        elimination and therefore survives an F250 fix.

    F119:
        concerns team-indexed storage of capitulation results in MilitaryAnalyst.
        F251 concerns graph-edge lifetime before result extraction.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    When a node transitions to a terminal simulated state, remove its outgoing edge
    immediately.

    A natural invariant is:

        eliminated/capitulated node => m_pPrimaryTarget == NULL

    `setEliminated(true)` could enforce:
        if (m_pPrimaryTarget != NULL)
            changePrimaryTarget(NULL);

    but implementation review should ensure that all existing callers can safely mutate
    the reverse adjacency set at that point.

    Alternatively, call changePrimaryTarget(NULL) explicitly in the city-elimination and
    capitulation transitions.

    Adding an `isEliminated() || hasCapitulated()` guard to step() is a useful defensive
    backstop, but by itself leaves stale reverse adjacency and component/threat state.
    Repairing the edge invariant is preferable; a guard can be added as robustness.

NEGATIVE CONTROLS / SCOPE
    * Losing a city without elimination/capitulation does not necessarily imply that the
      attacker should permanently abandon all offense; F251 is scoped to terminal
      simulated state.
    * If Army power is also fully exhausted, the existing Army-elimination cleanup can
      happen to remove the outgoing edge and mask F251.
    * updateTargets between simulation phases can later clear/reassign terminal nodes,
      but F251 occurs inside one resolveLossesRec component before such a phase boundary.
    * The real game's CvPlayer/CvTeam elimination callbacks are irrelevant here; this is
      wholly simulated InvasionGraph state.


OTHER CHECKS SINCE WIP01
-------------------------
1. m_iCacheIndex cross-opponent cursor suspicion -- REJECTED
    addConquest advances one node-global cache cursor past the conquered city, which at
    first looks capable of skipping higher-ranked cities of another opponent.

    During one simulation phase a node does not normally retarget from a defeated
    primary target to a different opponent; target removal produces NULL and retargeting
    occurs through updateTargets at the phase transition.

    Each simulate() call invokes prepareForSimulation(), which resets m_iCacheIndex=0.
    Existing simulated city losses are still filtered by targetCity/hasLost.

    Therefore the cursor does not establish an independent cross-opponent permanent
    skip under the current phase contract.

2. phase-one -> phase-two conquest persistence
    m_conquests/m_cityLosses intentionally survive across phases while m_iCacheIndex
    resets. targetCity consults the target owner's hasLost set, so already simulated
    lost cities are not attacked again. No duplicate conquest root.

3. breakCycle ScaledNum initialization
    Default ScaledNum is zero-initialized; no uninitialized rSumOfEnemyThreat.

4. reversed teammate-capitulation recursion
    Remains a real dormant 2920 regression, but current only caller requires defender
    team aliveCount <= 1, so no living teammate exists to exercise the broken recursive
    branch. Not numbered.

PURPOSE
-------
Preserve the post-F251 phase-state / retargeting checks before continuing deeper into
InvasionGraph.cpp.


PHASE-STATE / RETARGETING CHECKS
--------------------------------

1. `isContinuedWar` cross-opponent m_conquests candidate -- NOT PROMOTED
    Current:

        bool Node::isContinuedWar(Node const& kOther) const
        {
            return (actual teams are at war && m_conquests.empty());
        }

    m_conquests is node-global rather than target-specific. Therefore if phase 1
    produces a conquest against A and phase 2 updateTargets retargets the same node to
    C, `isContinuedWar(C)` is false even when the node was already at war with C in the
    real game.

    This initially looked like a target-domain leak because the deployment-time shortcut:

        if (isContinuedWar(kDefender))
            iDeployTurns /= 2;

    is described as accounting for units already deployed in an ongoing real war.

    However the alternative interpretation is coherent:
        * a conquest against A proves that the simulated force has already spent time/
          position on another front;
        * the one-time "already deployed" advantage may intentionally be considered
          consumed once the simulated campaign has begun;
        * switching to C can reasonably require fresh deployment even if war with C
          already existed.

    No historical comment or predecessor was found requiring the discount to be
    per-opponent after simulated conquests.

    RESULT:
        coarse approximation, not a demonstrated correctness defect.
        Keep F252 unused.

2. m_iCacheIndex phase reset -- CLEAN
    prepareForSimulation resets m_iCacheIndex=0 on every simulate() call.

    m_cityLosses and m_conquests intentionally persist from phase 1 into phase 2, but
    targetCity filters previously lost cities through the target owner's hasLost set.

    Therefore:
        * phase-two retargeting does not inherit the phase-one cache cursor;
        * already simulated conquered cities are not simply attacked a second time.

3. terminal node state across phase boundary
    F251 is specifically a SAME-PHASE graph-edge lifetime bug.

    MilitaryAnalyst calls updateTargets between the preparation phase and phase 2.
    findAndLinkTarget sees isEliminated()/hasCapitulated() and clears terminal nodes'
    primary targets there.

    Thus phase transition happens to clean the stale edge; it does not repair the
    A->B->C same-component attack that occurs before the boundary.

4. m_arLostPower / m_conquests / m_cityLosses persistence -- INTENTIONAL
    These represent cumulative simulated physical losses/results across phases and are
    deliberately not reset by prepareForSimulation.

    ArmamentForecast adds new production to the military branches between loss phases.

5. m_rTempArmyLosses reset -- INTENTIONAL/PLAUSIBLE
    Temporary clash damage is documented as sidelined until the end of a simulation
    phase. Resetting it at prepareForSimulation matches that stated lifetime.

6. distraction fields reset -- INTENTIONAL/PLAUSIBLE
    m_rDistractionByConquest / m_rDistractionByDefense model current-front allocation
    inside one graph-loss phase. Reassignment/updateTargets between phases supplies a
    natural reset boundary.

7. m_bHasClashed persists -- INTENTIONAL/PLAUSIBLE
    A physical clash already simulated in phase 1 should not be assumed never to have
    occurred merely because phase 2 begins. No contradictory consumer was found.

8. m_rEmergencyDefPow phase reset -- OPEN APPROXIMATION, NOT A ROOT
    Emergency defenders are accumulated after city losses because ordinary armament
    forecasting does not perfectly model units trained while an invader heals/moves.

    prepareForSimulation resets this auxiliary power at the next simulation phase.
    Those defenders could conceptually survive into phase 2, but phase boundaries also
    run additional ArmamentForecast production and represent a coarse time-model reset.

    No clean no-double-count/no-loss contract was found that proves the reset wrong.
    Preserve as an approximation question only.


HISTORICAL CONTROLS
-------------------
* Practical 1726 ("Bugfix in UWAI invasion graph") fixed removal of the WRONG node's
  primary target when the attacker's Army was eliminated. This reinforces F251's
  graph-edge ownership invariant but does not supply another phase-state root.

* Practical 3045 clamps negative simulated power/loss inputs and fixes defender fleet
  power floor. Current source retains those corrections.

* Practical 3477's uniform-garrison threat mode remains current and is specifically
  used by breakCycle so lightly defended cities do not artificially inflate threat.
  No regression established in this pass.

F252 / provisional KI#575
-------------------------
TITLE
    Successful conquest makes the ATTACKER leave Army power behind, but converts the
    unit count with the DEFENDER node's typical Army power; the attacker's remaining
    simulated offensive force therefore depends on the victim's representative unit.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited UWAI/AdvCiv ownership defect.
    Present in current Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.
    Present already in the first tracked AdvCiv/UWAI import (practical 1253).

CURRENT PRODUCER -> STATE -> CONSUMER PATH
    Node::applyStep is invoked on the DEFENDER node. It explicitly recovers the
    attacker separately:

        Node& kAttacker = *m_kOuter.m_nodeMap[kStep.getAttacker()];

    On a successful city conquest the source then says:

        // The conquerer leaves part of his army behind to protect the city
        scaled rUnitsLeftBehind = 2 + GET_PLAYER(m_ePlayer).AI_getCurrEraFactor();
        ...
        scaled rPowLeftBehind = rUnitsLeftBehind *
                m_military[ARMY]->getTypicalPower(TEAMID(m_eAgent));
        rPowLeftBehind.decreaseTo(kAttacker.m_military[ARMY]->power()
                - kAttacker.m_arLostPower[ARMY]);
        kAttacker.m_arLostPower[ARMY] += rPowLeftBehind;
        kAttacker.m_arShiftedPower[ARMY] += rPowLeftBehind;

    `m_military` without a qualifier belongs to `this`, i.e. the DEFENDER.

MILITARYBRANCH OWNERSHIP PROOF
    MilitaryBranch stores:

        PlayerTypes m_eOwner;
        scaled m_rTypicalPower;

    and its constructor is owner-specific. updateTypicalUnit scans the civilization and
    trainability of m_eOwner, then caches that owner's representative unit/power.
    getTypicalPower merely returns that receiver object's m_rTypicalPower (possibly
    reduced for an observer that cannot know the typical unit).

    Therefore:

        m_military[ARMY]->getTypicalPower(...)

    in defender::applyStep is unambiguously the DEFENDER's representative Army power,
    while:

        kAttacker.m_military[ARMY]->getTypicalPower(...)

    is the attacker branch that matches the source comment and the state being reduced.

LIVE EFFECT
    rPowLeftBehind is not only logged. It is added to the attacker's m_arLostPower, so
    that power becomes unavailable to subsequent SimulationStep calculations in the
    same and later phases. It is simultaneously recorded in m_arShiftedPower so the
    final public lostPower result does not misreport the garrison as combat casualties.

    Thus the wrong receiver changes the simulated invasion trajectory:

      * advanced/strong attacker vs weak victim:
            weak defender typical power -> too little attacker Army shifted away ->
            attacker can unrealistically snowball through more cities;

      * weak/obsolete attacker vs advanced victim:
            strong defender typical power -> too much attacker Army shifted away ->
            attacker can be clipped to its entire remaining Army and stop early.

    The error is especially artificial because the victim's unit technology -- not the
    conqueror's actual/representative troops -- controls how much of the conqueror's
    force disappears from its offensive pool.

ADJACENT OWNERSHIP SMELL
    The unit-count term also reads:

        GET_PLAYER(m_ePlayer).AI_getCurrEraFactor()

    i.e. the DEFENDER's era factor despite describing how many conqueror units are left
    behind. This is very likely the same receiver-context slip, and practical 1253
    already used the defender's `id` for both current era and typical Army power.

    The typical-power receiver alone proves F252. Treat switching the era-factor owner
    to kAttacker as part of implementation review rather than requiring that secondary
    point in order for the root to stand.

ANCESTRY
    Initial tracked practical 1253 already contains:

        int nUnitsLeftBehind = 2 + GET_PLAYER(id).getCurrentEra();
        ...
        double powLeftBehind = military[ARMY]->getTypicalUnitPower()
                * nUnitsLeftBehind;
        ...
        attacker.lostPower[ARMY] += powLeftBehind;

    where `id` / `military` are the defender Node and `attacker` is separate.

    The 2920 ScaledNum rewrite preserves the same ownership. No later targeted
    InvasionGraph repair changes it. Base AdvCiv 1.14 still has the same structure.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    At minimum, derive the representative power from the force being shifted:

        kAttacker.m_military[ARMY]->getTypicalPower(TEAMID(m_eAgent))

    Review the adjacent era-factor receiver at the same time. A more ambitious model
    could use the attacker's surviving actual average Army-unit power, but that is a
    design change; correcting the owner of the existing typical-unit model is surgical.


F253 / provisional KI#576
-------------------------
TITLE
    Node::step is used as a speculative/query calculation, but a predicted successful
    city attack permanently halves the defender's emergency-defense state INSIDE step;
    discarded priority/cycle probes therefore weaken later real simulations merely by
    being evaluated.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited UWAI/AdvCiv query-side mutation defect.
    Present in current Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.
    Present already in the first tracked AdvCiv/UWAI import (practical 1253).

ROOT
    Node::step(...) is declared const and conceptually builds/returns a SimulationStep.
    Most of its outputs are correctly written only into that temporary object.

    In the successful city-attack branch, however, it contains the persistent write:

        /* Assume that not all emergency defenders were able to reach this city
           (i.e. their true power is actually 2 * emergencyDefPow) */
        kDefender.m_rEmergencyDefPow /= 2;

    kDefender is reached through the graph's Node pointer, so the const qualifier on
    the attacking Node does not prevent this mutation.

SPECULATIVE CALL SITE A -- INVASION PRIORITY
    resolveLosses first evaluates EVERY current invader with the defending Army ignored:

        apSteps[*it] = ...->step(0, ...);

    The resulting steps are only probes used to calculate duration/threat and pick the
    next invader. They are then all deleted:

        SAFE_DELETE(apSteps[it->getID()]);

    If one of those provisional attacks predicts city success, merely computing its
    priority halves m_rEmergencyDefPow even though no attack has been selected/applied.

    This can happen once the defender has already lost a city in the phase, because
    applyStep intentionally accumulates emergency power after a successful city loss:

        m_rEmergencyDefPow += typicalHomeGuardPower * duration / (2 or 3);

    On the next resolveLosses iteration the query-side halving is live.

SPECULATIVE CALL SITE B -- CYCLE THREAT ESTIMATION
    breakCycle likewise calls:

        pStep = m_nodeMap[*it]->step(0, 1, false, true);

    solely to measure a threat value, then deletes pStep. A successful probe can thus
    alter the persistent defender state while the graph is only deciding which edge/
    clash should break a cycle.

NON-APPLIED ACTUAL STEP PATH
    The selected step is computed again at resolveLosses::1962 before the time-horizon
    check. Therefore even a step later deleted because:

        Simulation step exceeds time limit; not executed

    may already have halved m_rEmergencyDefPow. The world-state mutation can survive an
    explicitly NON-EXECUTED attack.

DETERMINISTIC MULTIPLICATIVE CONSEQUENCE
    Let the defender have emergency power E after its first simulated city loss.

    On the next city-resolution iteration with one invader whose provisional and actual
    attacks both predict success:

        priority probe: E -> E/2       (probe discarded)
        actual step:    E/2 -> E/4     (before applyStep)

    Only then is the actual conquest applied and new emergency power accumulated.

    With multiple successful provisional invaders, the same state can be halved once
    per discarded probe before the chosen actual attack is even evaluated. Outcome can
    therefore depend on how many candidates were inspected and their iteration order,
    not just on attacks that occurred.

DISTINCTION FROM C021-WIP03'S EMERGENCY-POWER RESET QUESTION
    WIP03 left `prepareForSimulation` resetting m_rEmergencyDefPow between phases as a
    coarse-model approximation, not a root.

    F253 is independent and much stronger: within ONE phase, a function used for
    counterfactual measurement changes persistent combat state even when its result is
    thrown away or rejected by the time limit.

ANCESTRY
    Practical 1253 already has `defender.emergencyDefPow /= 2` inside the step function,
    while the same initial implementation also uses step objects as disposable
    resolveLosses probes. The 2920 rewrite carries this forward as
    `kDefender.m_rEmergencyDefPow /= 2`. Base AdvCiv 1.14 remains identical here.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    Keep Node::step side-effect-free with respect to persistent graph state.

    If halving emergency defense is still desired after an ACTUALLY APPLIED successful
    city conquest, move that state transition to applyStep (or encode it as an explicit
    SimulationStep state delta and apply it only there). It must not execute during
    threat/duration probes or during a step rejected by the time horizon.

    A useful regression invariant is:
        calling step(...) and deleting the result without applyStep must leave every
        Node's persistent simulation state byte-for-byte/field-for-field unchanged.


F254 / provisional KI#577
-------------------------
TITLE
    resolveLosses treats zero-defense probe duration as an optimistic lower bound and
    aborts the whole defender when that bound or one selected actual step misses the
    horizon; naval probes can be LONGER than the real repelled landing, and one blocked
    invader does not prove that other concurrent invaders are out of time.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited UWAI/AdvCiv time-horizon scheduling defect.
    Present in current Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.
    Core logic and even the unresolved per-node-time-limit comment are present in the
    first tracked practical 1253 implementation.

MANIFESTATION A -- THE DOCUMENTED "LOWER BOUND" IS NOT A LOWER BOUND FOR NAVAL WAR
    resolveLosses creates priority probes with:

        step(0, attackerPortion)

    where the first argument is the DEFENDER Army portion. step deliberately reuses that
    same portion for the defending Fleet in a naval battle:

        rDefFleetPow = (defender fleet - losses) * confidence *
                rArmyPortionDefender;

    Therefore every priority probe has rDefFleetPow == 0.

    For a viable attacking fleet (rFleetPow > 1), the probe necessarily wins the naval
    battle and proceeds to the landing/city-siege path. That path can include deployment,
    healing and bombardment turns.

    The REAL selected step has a nonzero defender share. Its defender fleet can instead
    repel the landing. On that branch step terminates immediately with:

        setDuration(iDeployTurns + (bSneakAttack ? 0 : 2));
        return;

    while still recording genuine Fleet/Logistics and potentially drowned-Army losses.

    Hence a feasible shape is:

        priority probe, defender fleet forced to zero:
            landing succeeds -> city siege -> duration 13

        real step, defender fleet participates:
            landing repelled -> duration 7

    Yet resolveLosses states:

        "Shortest duration is an optimistic lower bound ...
         If the shortest duration exceeds the time limit, all actual durations ..."

    and executes:

        if (iShortestDuration > iTimeLimit)
            break;

    With a 10-turn horizon the example above is therefore discarded before the actual
    7-turn naval combat is ever computed. Real in-horizon fleet/logistics/army losses
    and the failed invasion can disappear from the analysis.

MANIFESTATION B -- ONE SELECTED ACTUAL OVERFLOW ABORTS OTHER INVADERS
    Even when the shortest probe is inside the horizon, resolveLosses recomputes only
    that selected invader with its assigned defender share. If its actual cumulative
    duration exceeds the limit, current code does:

        delete &kNextStep;
        log("Simulation step exceeds time limit; not executed");
        break;

    The `break` abandons ALL remaining invaders targeting this defender.

    That inference is not valid. Candidate ordering was based on each invader's
    zero-defense probe, while the actual-duration increase depends on that invader's
    defender share, route (land/naval), target city, bombardment/cavalry path and prior
    simulated turns. A second invader can still have an actual step within the horizon.

    The source itself flags this area as unresolved:

        "Per-node time limit. Not sure if really needed. Would have to
         toggle isTargeting and unset m_pPrimaryTarget as well in the
         else branch (instead of breaking)."

    The comment has survived since the first tracked implementation.

WHY THIS IS NOT JUST A LONG-HORIZON APPROXIMATION
    The first manifestation can suppress a combat that the same step model says occurs
    BEFORE the horizon. This is not merely choosing not to model events after the
    horizon; it is an invalid bound used to decide whether to evaluate the event at all.

    The second manifestation is a scheduling/selection problem among independent
    concurrent invaders: one candidate being too late does not make every other
    candidate too late.

F253 INTERACTION
    Before F253 is repaired, even a provisional/actual step rejected by these horizon
    branches may already mutate emergency-defense power. F253 and F254 therefore amplify
    each other, but remain independent:

        F253 = speculative calculation mutates persistent state;
        F254 = invalid horizon bound / global abort can skip valid combat.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    Do not rely on the current zero-defender step duration as a universal lower bound.
    A safe lower bound would have to remain <= every possible actual branch (e.g. a
    carefully defined deployment-only bound), or the code can compute actual candidates
    before concluding that no step fits.

    When one selected actual step exceeds the per-node horizon, do not `break` the whole
    defender's loop merely for that reason. Mark/exclude that invader locally for this
    resolveLosses pass and continue considering the others, without necessarily changing
    its persistent graph target. Exact scheduling policy deserves implementation review,
    but the current global inference is unsound.

ANCESTRY
    The initial practical 1253 InvasionGraph already contains:
        * priority `step(0, ...)` calls;
        * the "optimistic lower bound" comment and global shortest-duration break;
        * the later actual-step time check;
        * the comment questioning the per-node limit;
        * `break` when the selected actual step exceeds it.

    The 2920 rewrite largely renames/types this logic rather than creating it. Later
    2928/2943/3045/3477/3946 repairs do not remove the horizon assumptions.

F255 / provisional KI#578
-------------------------
TITLE
    Two-node cycle clash stores the LOSER'S army portion as the WINNER'S
    conquest-distraction portion; asymmetric outside pressure is transferred to the
    wrong civilization after the clash.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited UWAI/AdvCiv ownership/accounting defect.
    Present in current Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.
    Present from the first tracked UWAI/AdvCiv InvasionGraph implementation.

CURRENT PRODUCER -> STATE -> CONSUMER PATH
    breakCycle computes two independent portions for a two-node cycle:

        rFirstArmyPortion  = portion of first node's own army available for clash
        rSecondArmyPortion = portion of second node's own army available for clash

    and invokes:

        kFirst.clash(rFirstArmyPortion, rSecondArmyPortion)

    Node::clash names those values correspondingly:

        clash(scaled rArmyPortion, scaled rTargetArmyPortion)

    It then executes the symmetric combat by asking the target node to construct the
    clash step:

        SimulationStep& kClashStep =
                *kTarget.step(rArmyPortion, rTargetArmyPortion, true);
        applyStep(kClashStep);

    The arguments are therefore still:
        rArmyPortion       = THIS node's own committed portion
        rTargetArmyPortion = TARGET node's own committed portion

    But the post-clash distraction bookkeeping swaps ownership:

        if (kClashStep.isAttackerSuccessful())
        {
            // kTarget (the step attacker) won
            kTarget.m_rDistractionByConquest = rArmyPortion;       // WRONG owner
            m_rDistractionByDefense = rTargetArmyPortion;
        }
        else
        {
            // this node won
            m_rDistractionByConquest = rTargetArmyPortion;         // WRONG owner
            kTarget.m_rDistractionByDefense = rArmyPortion;
        }

    m_rDistractionByConquest is later consumed when computing how much of a node's Army
    is available to defend against a third party. It is therefore not merely a log or
    naming error.

WHY THE PORTIONS ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE
    They are only equal in a symmetric two-node cycle. breakCycle derives each from that
    node's own outside threats and clamps each independently. For example:

        A can devote 80% of its Army to B
        B can devote 35% of its Army to A

    If A wins, the surviving Army continuing the conquest of B is A's 80% commitment.
    Current bookkeeping instead records 35% as A's conquest distraction. A third-party
    attacker against A will therefore be allowed to use too much of A's Army for
    defense. If the asymmetry is reversed, A can instead be made too distracted.

ANCESTRY
    The original tracked implementation documents the same parameter ownership directly
    (armyPortion1 = this node, armyPortion2 = target node) yet performs the same swapped
    winner assignment. The later 2920 type/renaming rewrite preserves it. Base AdvCiv
    1.14 and SAS remain equivalent here.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    Preserve ownership when assigning the winner's conquest distraction:

        if target wins:
            kTarget.m_rDistractionByConquest = rTargetArmyPortion
            this->m_rDistractionByDefense    = rArmyPortion

        if this wins:
            this->m_rDistractionByConquest   = rArmyPortion
            kTarget.m_rDistractionByDefense  = rTargetArmyPortion

    Recheck the exact intended meaning of m_rDistractionByDefense at implementation time,
    but the currently documented ownership of both clash portions makes the conquest-side
    swap itself unambiguous.


F256 / provisional KI#579
-------------------------
TITLE
    Practical 2923 changed the ally-confidence army-portion adjustment from assignment
    to multiplication, accidentally squaring every partial portion at neutral confidence.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED Base AdvCiv regression, inherited by AdvCiv-SAS.
    Regression boundary: practical 2923, commit 9ee1db509d
    ("Minor adjustments to the revised UWAI code").

CURRENT CODE
    The comment says the absent portion -- 1 minus the supplied portion -- should be
    adjusted for confidence in allies:

        /* Adjust the portion of the army that is assumed to be absent,
           i.e. 1 minus portion */

        rArmyPortionDefender *= scaled::max(0,
                1 - (1 - rArmyPortionDefender) * rConfAlliesAtt);
        rArmyPortionAttacker *= scaled::max(0,
                1 - (1 - rArmyPortionAttacker) * rConfAlliesDef);

    Let p be the incoming army portion and c the relevant ally-confidence factor.
    The intended expression described by the comment and used immediately before 2923 is:

        p' = max(0, 1 - (1 - p) * c)

    Current code instead computes:

        p' = p * max(0, 1 - (1 - p) * c)

NEUTRAL-CONFIDENCE INVARIANT
    With c = 1, confidence is neutral and should leave p unchanged:

        intended: p' = 1 - (1-p) = p
        current:  p' = p * p = p^2

    Examples:
        p = 0.50 -> 0.25
        p = 0.70 -> 0.49
        p = 0.90 -> 0.81

    Only the trivial endpoints 0 and 1 survive unchanged.

HISTORY / REGRESSION BOUNDARY
    * the pre-rewrite UWAI implementation used assignment;
    * practical 2920's revised/scaled implementation still used assignment;
    * practical 2923 changes ONLY these operators from `=` to `*=` while retaining the
      same explanatory comment and the same right-hand expression;
    * current Base AdvCiv 1.14 and SAS retain the 2923 multiplication.

    The local tracked diff is explicit:

        - rArmyPortionDefender = scaled::max(...)
        + rArmyPortionDefender *= scaled::max(...)

        - rArmyPortionAttacker = scaled::max(...)
        + rArmyPortionAttacker *= scaled::max(...)

EFFECT
    The distortion is concentrated in partial allocations -- exactly the multi-front and
    cycle cases where army portions carry the most information. It can substantially
    understate Army/Fleet participation before the actual combat model is even entered,
    and F255 can then mis-attribute the already-distorted portion after a cycle clash.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    Restore assignment (`=`) for both expressions, matching the original semantics,
    practical 2920, and the still-present comment. Add a regression invariant that
    neutral ally confidence maps every p in [0,1] to itself.


F257 / provisional KI#580
-------------------------
TITLE
    Open-field/cycle Army-clash casualties are stored in confidence-scaled units because
    combat/trait modifiers are divided back out but rConfAtt/rConfDef are not; naval and
    city-siege paths explicitly undo confidence and establish the intended unit convention.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited UWAI/AdvCiv dimensional/accounting defect.
    Present in Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.
    Present in the initial tracked UWAI implementation.

PRODUCER
    The Army clash first constructs perceived/modified combat powers:

        rArmyPowModified    = rArmyPow    * rArmyModAttCorr * rConfAtt;
        rDefArmyPowModified = rDefArmyPow * rArmyModDefCorr * rConfDef;

    clashLossesWinnerLoser and clashLossesTemporary operate on those modified powers, so
    their returned quantities are in the same modified/confidence-scaled power space.

CONVERSION BACK TO BRANCH POWER -- CURRENT CLASH PATH
    After the clash, current code removes only the combat modifier:

        rLossesLoser  /= rArmyModDefCorr; // or attacker corr depending on winner
        rLossesWinner /= rArmyModAttCorr;
        kStep.reducePower(..., ARMY, rLosses...);

    Temporary losses likewise divide only by the corresponding Army modifier:

        kStep.setTempLosses(rTempLosses / rArmyMod...Corr);

    The confidence multiplier remains embedded.

INTERNAL CONTROL -- OTHER PATHS IN THE SAME FUNCTION
    Naval losses explicitly divide by confidence when converting perceived battle losses
    back to stored branch power:

        rLossesAtt = rrLosses... / rConfAtt;
        rLossesDef = rrLosses... / rConfDef;

    Later city-siege losses likewise divide by both the Army correction and confidence,
    e.g. denominator `(rArmyModAttCorr * rConfAtt)`.

    The source comment immediately above the Army clash also says:

        "These bonuses are removed again (through division) when applying losses"

    Confidence is part of the multiplication that created the modified power, but is not
    removed in this one path.

WHY THIS IS NOT JUST 'CONFIDENCE SHOULD AFFECT EXPECTED LOSSES'
    Confidence already affects which side appears stronger and therefore the clash result
    in the perceived-power space. Once a returned quantity is converted into the stored
    `m_arLostPower` unit, leaving the epistemic multiplier in the measurement changes the
    branch-power unit itself.

    For the same physical force and same combat modifier, merely changing rConf from
    1.0 to 1.5 can inflate the recorded branch-power loss; changing it to 0.7 can shrink
    it. Naval and siege code deliberately undo exactly that scaling.

CONSUMERS
    SimulationStep losses are applied directly to m_arLostPower in applyStep. Those
    cumulative losses reduce Army/Cavalry availability in later simulated attacks and
    can trigger the "Army eliminated" target unlink. Temporary losses additionally reduce
    within-phase Army availability. The error therefore propagates beyond reporting.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    Convert clash losses and temporary losses back with both factors, consistently with
    the naval and city-siege branches:

        / (rArmyMod...Corr * rConf...)

    Review the cavalry proportional loss after this conversion, but do not apply a second
    confidence correction there because Cavalry loss is derived from the corrected Army
    loss.


F258 / provisional KI#581
-------------------------
TITLE
    City-defense trait bonus is read from the graph-wide evaluating agent instead of the
    defending player, giving or denying +30% city-defense modifier based on the wrong civ.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited UWAI/AdvCiv owner-identity defect.
    Present in current Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.
    Present in the first tracked UWAI implementation under the older Protective-trait name.

CURRENT CODE
    During city-garrison strength calculation:

        MilitaryBranch const& kDefHomeGuard =
                *kDefender.m_military[HOME_GUARD];
        ...
        scaled rCityDefenderMod = ...;
        if (GET_PLAYER(kDefender.m_eAgent).uwai().getCache().hasDefensiveTrait())
            rCityDefenderMod += 0.3;

    But Node construction assigns:

        m_eAgent(kOuter.m_eAgent)

    i.e. every node receives the SAME analyst/evaluating player ID. `m_eAgent` is not the
    node's owner. The defender's owner is `kDefender.m_ePlayer`.

MANIFESTATIONS
    * Agent has Defensive trait, actual defender does not:
        every simulated defender can receive the +30% city-defense adjustment.
    * Agent lacks Defensive trait, a third-party/target defender has it:
        that defender receives no trait adjustment.
    * Only when defender == agent (or both happen to have the same trait state) is the
      result accidentally correct.

    rCityDefenderMod subsequently enters the garrison/city-defense power calculation and
    can alter whether the attacker succeeds, losses, threat and duration.

ANCESTRY
    The first tracked UWAI implementation used the same wrong identity via its graph-wide
    `defender.weId` and checked `hasProtectiveTrait()`. The later rewrite renamed the
    field to `m_eAgent`; the mod's later trait abstraction renamed the cached trait concept
    to Defensive, but ownership remained unchanged. This is not introduced by SAS.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    Query the defender owner:

        GET_PLAYER(kDefender.m_ePlayer).uwai().getCache().hasDefensiveTrait()

    A regression test should evaluate A attacking B from the viewpoint of C and vary
    Defensive trait independently on B and C; only B's trait may change city-defense power.


ADDITIONAL CONTROLS / REJECTIONS BETWEEN WIP04 AND WIP05
---------------------------------------------------------
1. SimulationStep omitted scaled initializers -- SAFE
    m_rThreat and m_rTempLosses are not named in the constructor initializer list, but
    `scaled`/ScaledNum has a zeroing default constructor. Paths that do not call the
    corresponding setter therefore observe zero rather than indeterminate memory.
    No F-number assigned.

2. GET_TEAM(PlayerTypes) suspicion -- SAFE IN ADVCIV/SAS
    Calls such as GET_TEAM(m_ePlayer) are not raw indexing of a team array by PlayerTypes.
    AdvCiv's CoreAI helper deliberately overloads GET_TEAM(PlayerTypes) and converts via
    TEAMID. This is the already-known false-positive family behind the retracted
    F113/KI#436 concern; do not recycle it in queue 023.

3. Garrison-only priority probe allegedly zeroing garrison -- CURRENT CODE SAFE
    A short-lived historical revision around practical 2943 capped too much, but the
    subsequent revised-UWAI merge leaves full garrison power in place and caps only the
    additional defender-advantage component. Current `step(0, ...)` still ignores the
    mobile defender Army as intended while retaining garrisons. No F-number assigned.

4. isContinuedWar uses global m_conquests.empty() rather than opponent-specific conquest
    history -- NOT PROMOTED
    Cross-front state flow is real, but UWAI uses one aggregate Army pool and the code can
    plausibly intend the initial "already deployed" advantage to be consumed once the
    aggregate Army has achieved any conquest. This is too model-policy-dependent for the
    audit's bug threshold without stronger contradictory evidence.

F259 / provisional KI#582
-------------------------
TITLE
    MaxWarMinAdjacentLand personality scaling can push the clash meeting point past the
    defender, producing a negative defender deployment distance; debug logging then
    violates scaled::uround's non-negative contract and release arithmetic can boost
    defender Army power above 100% instead of applying a deployment penalty.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED Base AdvCiv/UWAI regression introduced in practical 1341
    (a5724ff58159f2c073fe9b3b55ddcc30210dbf13, "Some small AI changes").
    Present in Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.

PRODUCER / CURRENT CLASH GEOMETRY
    For bClashOnly, current code begins with one fixed clash distance for each side:

        rDeploymentDistAttacker = rClashDist;
        rDeploymentDistDefender = rClashDist;

    It then allocates the attacker's share by Army-power ratio, multiplies THAT spatial
    share by the evaluating leader's MaxWarMinAdjacentLand personality factor, and
    subtracts the inflated result from the defender's fixed distance:

        rDeploymentDistAttacker *= rArmyPow / (rArmyPow + rDefArmyPow);
        rDeploymentDistAttacker *= rMaxWarMinAdjLandFactor;
        rDeploymentDistDefender -= rDeploymentDistAttacker;

    `rMaxWarMinAdjLandFactor` is derived from an XML value documented as [0,4]. Current
    SAS XML actually uses all values 0,1,2,3,4. The resulting factors are approximately:

        XML 0 -> 4/6 = 0.667
        XML 1 -> 1.000
        XML 2 -> 7/6 = 1.167
        XML 3 -> 8/6 = 1.333
        XML 4 -> 9/6 = 1.500

NEGATIVE-DISTANCE THRESHOLDS
    Let s = attackerArmy / (attackerArmy + defenderArmy). The defender distance becomes
    negative whenever s * factor > 1.

        factor 1.50  -> s > 2/3 -> attacker Army > 2x defender Army
        factor 4/3   -> s > 3/4 -> attacker Army > 3x defender Army
        factor 7/6   -> s > 6/7 -> attacker Army > 6x defender Army

    These are reachable power ratios, not mathematical edge cases. Multiple shipped
    leader personalities use XML 3 and 4.

CONSUMERS / TWO CONCRETE FAILURE MODES
    1. Debug-domain violation
       The result is logged through:

           rDeploymentDistDefender.uround()

       ScaledNum::uround explicitly documents that it works only on non-negative values
       and asserts `m_i >= 0`. A sufficiently one-sided clash therefore trips the debug
       invariant solely because the meeting-point arithmetic crossed below zero.

    2. Release semantic inversion
       The defender deployment modifier is then:

           max(100 - 2 * rDeploymentDistDefender, 50) / 100

       A negative distance makes `100 - 2*negative` GREATER than 100, so the defender's
       Army power is multiplied above its original value. Moving the estimated meeting
       point beyond the defender's origin therefore becomes a combat-power bonus.

ANCESTRY
    The first tracked UWAI code split the fixed clash distance by Army-power share without
    this personality multiplier, keeping both sides' spatial portions within the original
    distance. Practical 1341 introduced MaxWarMinAdjacentLand scaling and specifically
    added the multiplier between the attacker's share calculation and subtraction from
    the defender. The later scaled-number rewrite preserved the arithmetic. Practical
    2923 changed relevant logging to uround, making the pre-existing negative-domain
    state explicitly assertable. Current Base AdvCiv and SAS retain it.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    Keep physical meeting geometry bounded and non-negative. The cleanest interpretation
    is to split rClashDist by Army-power share first:

        meetingAtt = clashDist * attackerShare;
        meetingDef = clashDist - meetingAtt;

    and apply MaxWarMinAdjacentLand only to the attacker's deployment penalty/time if the
    personality effect is still desired. If personality is intended to shift the meeting
    point itself, cap the spatial attacker share at rClashDist before deriving the
    defender share. Merely changing uround to round would hide the debug symptom while
    retaining the >100% defender-power inversion and is not a sufficient repair.


F260 / provisional KI#583
-------------------------
TITLE
    Attacker battle-area weighting scales total Army power but not its overlapping
    Cavalry sub-branch, breaking Cavalry<=Army and allowing inflated Cavalry availability
    and losses; the corresponding defender omission was explicitly fixed in practical
    1366 but the attacker sibling remains.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv/UWAI branch-accounting omission.
    Attacker area weighting introduced in practical 1289 (ed1826faf1...) with the omission.
    Defender-side sibling fixed in practical 1366
    (82ed992626a03f21b42345058cfdea526337641e).
    Present in Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.

BRANCH INVARIANT BEFORE AREA WEIGHTING
    CAVALRY is an overlapping subset/sub-branch of ARMY. Current step() explicitly clamps
    both sides before battle-area weighting:

        rCavPow.decreaseTo(rArmyPow);
        rDefCavPow.decreaseTo(rDefArmyPow);

    This encodes the expected Cavalry<=Army invariant for the force represented by the
    step.

PRODUCER -- ASYMMETRIC AREA FILTER
    `rAreaWeightAtt` and `rAreaWeightDef` estimate the fraction of each civ's military
    actually available in the battle area. Current attacker path:

        if (rAreaWeightAtt < 1)
            rArmyPow *= rAreaWeightAtt;

    Current defender path:

        if (rAreaWeightDef != 1)
        {
            rDefArmyPow *= rAreaWeightDef;
            rDefCavPow *= rAreaWeightDef;
        }

    The attacker Cavalry value is therefore left at whole-force scale while its enclosing
    Army value is reduced to local-area scale.

CONCRETE INVARIANT BREAK
    Example before weighting:
        Army = 100, Cavalry = 80, areaWeightAtt = 0.5

    Current result:
        Army = 50, Cavalry = 80

    This is impossible under the model's own overlapping-branch interpretation and
    directly undoes the earlier `rCavPow.decreaseTo(rArmyPow)` safety clamp.

DOWNSTREAM CONSUMERS
    * Open-field/cycle loss partition derives Cavalry ratios from this unweighted Cavalry
      against weighted Army. A clamp to 1 prevents an unbounded ratio there, but can make
      all local Army losses appear Cavalry-heavy.
    * City combat uses:

          rLossesAttArmy * rCavPow / rArmyPow

      without a ratio clamp. Once rCavPow > rArmyPow, a 20 Army-power casualty estimate
      can record more than 20 Cavalry power of casualties. Later cumulative branch clamps
      do not restore the per-step dimensional consistency and can prematurely exhaust the
      Cavalry branch for subsequent simulation.
    * Naval landing first scales Army and Cavalry together by the landing ratio, but later
      attacker area weighting can recreate the mismatch.

HISTORY / STRONG INTERNAL CONTROL
    Practical 1289 introduced area weighting and initially multiplied only Army power on
    BOTH attacker and defender sides. Practical 1366 later added exactly:

        targetCavPow *= areaWeightDef;

    to the defender path. Its commit message explicitly says UWAI fixed a v0.93 bug where
    military power was "grossly underestimated" for defenders with cities on several
    landmasses and many Mounted/fast units. That establishes that overlapping Cavalry has
    to follow the same area projection as Army. No corresponding `cavPow *= areaWeightAtt`
    was added, and the attacker omission remains in Base AdvCiv 1.14 and SAS.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    Apply the same battle-area factor to the attacker Cavalry sub-branch whenever Army is
    filtered:

        rArmyPow *= rAreaWeightAtt;
        rCavPow  *= rAreaWeightAtt;

    Reapplying `rCavPow.decreaseTo(rArmyPow)` afterward is a cheap defensive invariant,
    though mathematically it should become redundant once both values are scaled by the
    same non-negative factor.


ADDITIONAL CONTROL / REJECTION AFTER WIP05
------------------------------------------
Target-city cache cursor across phase-II retargeting -- REJECTED
    `findBestTarget()` searches the cache independently while `targetCity()` advances a
    monotonic `m_iCacheIndex`, which initially suggested that cities skipped while fighting
    one opponent might become unreachable after phase-II retargeting. Lifecycle tracing
    disproved that path: `prepareForSimulation()` resets m_iCacheIndex to 0 at the start of
    every simulate() phase, and a node does not retarget across opponents inside a single
    simulate() call after advancing the cursor. Phase-II therefore begins with a fresh
    cursor and explicitly skips already-lost cities. The nearby assertion remains useful
    diagnostics but does not establish the proposed cross-opponent failure. No F-number.

F261 / provisional KI#584
-------------------------
TITLE
    Attacker Logistics losses in naval combat retain an inverse confidence factor while
    defender Logistics losses are confidence-neutral; confidence therefore changes the
    physical amount of transport capacity destroyed on the attacking side.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv/UWAI dimensional-accounting asymmetry.
    Present in the first tracked UWAI import (practical 1253), Base AdvCiv 1.14 and
    current AdvCiv-SAS. Practical 1335 fixed a separate defender Logistics-owner error
    but did not repair this confidence mismatch.

MODEL / UNITS
    MilitaryBranch::Logistics::power() is explicitly cargo capacity, not combat power.
    Fleet power, by contrast, is a combat-power rating. The existing source FIXME already
    acknowledges that taking a Logistics/Fleet ratio is a rough dimensional approximation;
    that approximation is NOT this finding. F261 concerns an additional confidence factor
    that appears on only one side of an otherwise symmetric conversion.

PRODUCER -- ATTACKER
    Current naval setup uses confidence-scaled Fleet power:

        rFleetPow = physicalFleetPower * rConfAtt * rArmyPortionAttacker;

    but attacker Logistics portion is computed as:

        rLogisticsPortion = rCargoCap / rFleetPow;

    with no compensating rConfAtt in the numerator. Fleet losses returned by
    clashLossesWinnerLoser are in confidence-scaled Fleet-power units and are subsequently
    converted back to physical Fleet power by division by rConfAtt. The attacker transport
    loss paths then effectively apply confidence twice in opposite places:

        win path:
            rrLossesWL.first * rLogisticsPortion / rConfAtt

        loss path:
            rLossesAtt * rLogisticsPortion
            where rLossesAtt = rrLossesWL.second / rConfAtt

    Since rLogisticsPortion itself already contains 1/rConfAtt through rFleetPow, physical
    Logistics losses retain an extra inverse-confidence factor.

INTERNAL CONTROL -- DEFENDER
    Defender setup explicitly includes confidence in the numerator:

        rLogisticsPortionDef = physicalCargoCapacity * rConfDef / rDefFleetPow;

    Because rDefFleetPow already contains rConfDef, this ratio is confidence-neutral.
    Later division of confidence-scaled Fleet casualties by rConfDef therefore converts
    defender cargo losses back to physical capacity without leaving a confidence factor.

ALGEBRAIC CONSEQUENCE
    Holding the physical Fleet/cargo composition and battle casualty fraction fixed:

        defender physical Logistics loss  ~ actual cargo casualty fraction
        attacker physical Logistics loss  ~ actual cargo casualty fraction / rConfAtt

    Thus an otherwise identical attacking force can lose roughly twice as much physical
    transport capacity at rConfAtt=0.5 as at rConfAtt=1, while rConfAtt=1.5 produces only
    about two-thirds as much transport loss. Confidence is epistemic/perceptual in this
    simulation and is explicitly divided back out of physical Fleet losses; it should not
    silently change the measurement unit of the transport casualties on only one side.

ANCESTRY
    The first tracked UWAI import already computes attacker logisticsPortion as
    cargoCap/fleetPow while fleetPow contains confAtt, and later divides the loss by
    confAtt. Practical 1335 repairs a concrete neighboring defender bug:

        military[LOGISTICS] -> defender.military[LOGISTICS]

    in logisticsPortionTarget, but preserves the defender-side *confDef and leaves the
    attacker omission unchanged. The 2920 scaled-number rewrite preserves the asymmetry.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    Preserve the existing cargo-vs-Fleet approximation if desired, but make the confidence
    conversion symmetric. For example:

        rLogisticsPortion = rCargoCap * rConfAtt / rFleetPow;

    Do this in the ratio only; do not globally confidence-scale rCargoCap, because that
    variable later represents actual landing capacity. Then both sides convert perceived
    Fleet casualties to physical cargo losses under the same dimensional convention.

F255 / provisional KI#578 -- ADDENDUM: BOTH CYCLE-DISTRACTION ASSIGNMENTS SWAP OWN ARMY PORTIONS
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The earlier F255 wording emphasized the winner's conquest distraction. A deeper consumer trace
shows that the same ownership swap affects the loser's defense distraction too, so the root is
broader but remains one bug.

MODEL / CONTRACT
    InvasionGraph.h defines the fields as temporary distraction of a node's OWN military effort:

        m_rDistractionByConquest  -- defense less effective while this node tries to conquer
                                     cities of a third player
        m_rDistractionByDefense   -- conquest less effective while this node fends off a
                                     third player

    breakCycle/clash parameters likewise represent the portions of the two nodes' respective
    armies committed to the mutual clash:

        rArmyPortion        = this node's own committed Army portion
        rTargetArmyPortion  = target node's own committed Army portion

CURRENT PRODUCER
    clash calls the target as the SimulationStep attacker:

        SimulationStep& kClashStep =
            *kTarget.step(rArmyPortion, rTargetArmyPortion, true);

    If kTarget wins, current code writes:

        kTarget.m_rDistractionByConquest = rArmyPortion;
        m_rDistractionByDefense = rTargetArmyPortion;

    If this node wins, current code writes:

        m_rDistractionByConquest = rTargetArmyPortion;
        kTarget.m_rDistractionByDefense = rArmyPortion;

    In both branches each surviving distraction field receives the OTHER node's committed
    portion rather than its owner's portion.

DOWNSTREAM CONSEQUENCE
    The conquest-distraction field reduces the node's later defensive availability, while
    m_rDistractionByDefense reduces that node's later attacking portion (e.g. the invader
    portion in resolveLosses). Thus asymmetric outside pressure is transferred between the two
    civs whichever side wins the clash; this is not limited to the winner bookkeeping described
    in WIP05.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    Keep the clash result logic, but assign each node's own committed portion to its own
    distraction field. This is an extension of F255/KI#578, not a new root/F-number.


F262 / provisional KI#585 -- REPEAT-TRIP CARGO MULTIPLIER IS APPLIED BEFORE NAVAL TRANSPORT LOSSES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TITLE
    Sunk transports can still contribute to post-battle repeat-trip landing capacity because
    the cargo relay multiplier is applied to the pre-battle transport pool and losses are
    subtracted only afterward.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited UWAI/AdvCiv ordering/accounting bug.
    Present in the first tracked UWAI import (practical 1253), Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current
    AdvCiv-SAS.

MODEL / UNITS
    MilitaryBranch::Logistics::unitPower() returns getCargoSpace(); InvasionGraph.h explicitly
    states that Logistics "power" is cargo capacity. Therefore both rCargoCap and
    rLogisticsLosses below are expressed in the same one-trip cargo-capacity unit.

CURRENT PRODUCER / ORDERING
    Before the naval battle is resolved, current code computes base usable cargo capacity C:

        rCargoCap = 0.73 * (LOGISTICS power - lost LOGISTICS power);

    It then immediately applies the post-battle repeat-trip factor M:

        // Cargo units can go multiple times once the naval battle is won
        rCargoCap *= 1 + 1 / max(2, rReinforcementDist);

    Only after battle casualties have been calculated is destroyed transport capacity L
    subtracted:

        rCargoSize = rCargoCap - rLogisticsLosses;

    Hence the current effective landing capacity is:

        M * C - L

    But the source comment itself says the extra trips happen *once the naval battle is won*.
    Transports destroyed in that battle cannot perform those later relay trips. Physical
    surviving transport capacity should therefore be formed first, then allowed to repeat:

        M * (C - L)

ERROR MAGNITUDE
    Current overstatement is exactly:

        L * (M - 1)

    M can reach 1.5, so as much as half of the cargo capacity destroyed in the naval battle can
    effectively reappear in the subsequent landing calculation.

    Example: C=10, M=1.5, L=4

        current:       10 * 1.5 - 4 = 11
        survivor-first:(10 - 4) * 1.5 = 9

    Two units of effective landing capacity are supplied by transports that were already sunk.

CONSUMER PATH
    rCargoSize -> rLandingRatio = rCargoSize / rArmySize
               -> attacker Army/Cavalry landing power
               -> city invasion odds/result and subsequent losses/conquest state.

    The distortion can therefore change whether the simulated naval invasion succeeds; it is
    not only a reporting discrepancy in "surviving cargo".

ANCESTRY / CONTROL
    The first tracked UWAI implementation already has the same semantic sequence and the same
    explanatory comment: multiply cargo capacity for repeat trips first, then later compute
    cargoSize = cargoCap - logisticsLosses. The 2920 scaled-number rewrite preserves it.
    Base AdvCiv 1.14 and SAS remain equivalent here.

    This is separate from F261/KI#584. F261 concerns the confidence unit leaked into attacker
    Logistics casualty magnitude; F262 remains present even if L itself is calculated perfectly.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    Keep physical one-trip cargo capacity separate until naval losses are known. For example,
    retain a repeat-trip factor and calculate the landing capacity as conceptually:

        rCargoSize = max(0, rCargoCap - rLogisticsLosses);
        rCargoSize *= rRepeatTripFactor;

    or equivalently defer the existing multiplication until after loss subtraction. Do not
    multiply rLogisticsLosses a second time; it already denotes physical one-trip capacity
    destroyed in the battle.

F263 / provisional KI#586 -- FAILED INVADER IS NOT REMOVED AND CAN ATTACK AGAIN
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TITLE
    resolveLosses says a failed attacker receives no further step, but leaves that invader
    in the live targeting set; the same failed force can therefore attack again, while its
    previous threat is simultaneously counted as `rPastThreat` and reduces the defending
    Army assigned to the retry.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited UWAI/AdvCiv control-flow/state defect.
    Present in the first tracked UWAI import (practical 1253), Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current
    AdvCiv-SAS. The relevant comment and loop structure have survived essentially unchanged.

INTENDED CONTRACT -- SOURCE STATES IT EXPLICITLY
    After applying an actual step, resolveLosses says:

        /* If attack fails, the attacker doesn't get another step. However,
           the defending army portion assigned to that attacker mustn't
           be assumed to instantaneously redeploy to another front. */

    It then stores the failed attacker's threat in `rPastThreat` so that the defender
    remains partly tied down for the immediately following invasion resolution.

LIVE CONTROL FLOW
    At the top of every do/while iteration, resolveLosses walks ALL entries still in
    `m_targetedBy` and constructs a new preliminary step for each:

        for (... it = m_targetedBy.begin(); it != m_targetedBy.end(); ++it)
            apSteps[*it] = node[*it]->step(...);

    An ordinary failed city attack does not remove the invader from that set.

    `applyStep` only unlinks the attacker here when its Army is completely eliminated:

        if (attacker Army power <= attacker lost Army power)
            kAttacker.changePrimaryTarget(NULL);

    The generic failure path does not call changePrimaryTarget(NULL), does not clear a
    local active flag and does not otherwise exclude `eNextInvader` from later iterations.
    The target city also remains unconquered, so `targetCity()` can simply return it again.

PRODUCER -> STATE -> CONSUMER FAILURE
    Suppose attacker A assaults defender D and the actual step fails without eliminating A.

    1. `applyStep(kNextStep)` records the casualties but leaves A -> D live.

    2. Because the step failed:

           rPastThreat = rNextInvaderThreat;

       Let that prior threat be T_A.

    3. The do/while loop repeats. A is still in D.m_targetedBy, so A receives another
       preliminary step and contributes a fresh threat T'_A to `rSumOfThreats`.

    4. A can be selected as `eNextInvader` again and the actual defender-Army portion is:

           T'_A / (rSumOfThreats + rPastThreat + m_rDistractionByConquest)

       For the simplest one-invader case this is approximately:

           T'_A / (T'_A + T_A)

       rather than 1. The same failed attacker is therefore not merely retried; its OLD
       threat is treated as if it belonged to another front and diverts defending Army
       away from its OWN retry.

MULTI-INVADER CONSEQUENCE
    The same double representation occurs with several attackers: after A fails, A remains
    a live contributor to the new `rSumOfThreats` while T_A is also carried separately as
    `rPastThreat`. This contradicts the comment's model, where A is supposed to receive no
    second step and only its already-committed defensive distraction should carry over for
    the next OTHER invasion.

DOWNSTREAM EFFECT
    A first failed assault can therefore be followed by another simulated assault by the
    same force within the same horizon. Because the retry can receive a smaller defender
    Army portion, a force that was repelled once can become more likely to conquer the same
    city on its retry. Repeated failures also consume `aiTurnsSimulated[A]` until the time
    horizon finally stops them; ordinary failure itself does not.

ANCESTRY
    Practical 1253 already contains all three necessary pieces together:
        * the do/while reconstruction of steps from the unchanged `targetedBy` set;
        * the explicit comment that a failed attacker "doesn't get another step";
        * `pastThreat = nextInvaderThreat` with no removal/exclusion of that invader.

    Later refactors, including the revised-UWAI/scaled-number work, preserve the behavior.
    Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS are equivalent in this block.

DISTINCTION FROM OTHER QUEUE-023 ROOTS
    * F251 concerns an ELIMINATED/CAPITULATED node retaining its outgoing edge and later
      attacking a different downstream target during recursive graph resolution.
    * F263 concerns a still-alive attacker whose ordinary FAILED city assault is explicitly
      supposed to end its attacks for this loss-resolution pass but does not.
    * F254 concerns time-horizon pruning. F263 remains live with a generous horizon.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    Enforce the existing stated contract by excluding the failed invader from subsequent
    step generation in this resolveLosses pass while retaining its threat solely as the
    carry-over distraction for the next other attacker. This can be done with explicit
    local active/finished state; alternatively unlinking the failed attacker's target may
    fit the intended graph semantics, but should be reviewed against phase-II retargeting.

    Crucially, do not leave the same invader simultaneously represented both in the live
    threat sum and in `rPastThreat`.


CONTROL / NON-PROMOTION: EMERGENCY HOME-GUARD LOSS ATTRIBUTION
--------------------------------------------------------------
The city-defense formula combines baseline HOME_GUARD power, emergency defender power and
recorded Home-Guard losses, and a successful city defense loss is then stored through the
HOME_GUARD branch while emergency power is also reduced. This can look dimensionally odd,
particularly once emergency power becomes large. However, the original UWAI implementation
contains the same virtual-defender model and the adjacent comment indicates intentional
coarse handling of emergency units that could/could not reach the city. No clean invariant
was found that uniquely determines how casualties should be split between baseline and
virtual emergency defenders. This remains a modeling question, not F264.

C021-WIP10 CONTINUATION -- AUTHORITATIVE F263 RETRACTION + queue-023 controls

IMPORTANT CORRECTION -- F263 / provisional KI#586 RETRACTED
------------------------------------------------------------
DO NOT IMPLEMENT KI#586 FROM C021-WIP09.

The WIP09 diagnosis that an ordinary failed city attacker remains linked and can
receive another step was a false positive caused by reading the Army-elimination
cleanup at the end of Node::applyStep without carrying the immediately preceding
success/failure branch through to its `else`.

Current Node::applyStep is explicit:

    if (kStep.isAttackerSuccessful())
    {
        ...
    }
    // Remove link from graph
    else kAttacker.changePrimaryTarget(NULL);

That `else` belongs to `if (kStep.isAttackerSuccessful())`, not to either of the
later Army-elimination tests. Therefore EVERY applied unsuccessful step -- an
ordinary failed city attack as well as an unsuccessful clash -- immediately
unlinks the attacker from its current primary target. changePrimaryTarget(NULL)
removes the attacker's player ID from the defender's `m_targetedBy` set.

Consequently, the WIP09 producer -> state -> consumer chain does not exist:

* after A's ordinary failed attack, A -> D is removed;
* the next resolveLosses iteration does NOT construct another preliminary A step;
* A does NOT contribute a fresh threat to `rSumOfThreats` while its old threat is
  carried as `rPastThreat`;
* the source comment "If attack fails, the attacker doesn't get another step" is
  in fact implemented by applyStep.

`rPastThreat` therefore has the intended role: for one following resolution it
keeps part of D's Army tied to the just-failed attack even though that attacker
has been removed from the live incoming-edge set.

The first tracked UWAI implementation also contains this generic failure unlink;
the supposed inherited defect was an audit-reading error, not a source defect.

Preserve C021-WIP09's F263 section only as rejected-history evidence so that the
same hypothesis is not rediscovered. F263 is no longer a live queue-023 root.
The provisional KI#586 number remains historical/retracted; later KI numbering
is NOT renumbered.

ADVERSARIAL IMPACT CHECK
------------------------
F250-F262 do not depend on F263 and remain live. In particular:
* F251 is about a successfully eliminated/capitulated defender retaining its OWN
  outgoing edge; it does not rely on ordinary attack failure.
* F254 is about horizon pruning before an actual step is applied.
* F261/F262 are local naval Logistics arithmetic roots.


CONTROL / NON-PROMOTION -- findBestTarget/targetCity INVALID-SUFFIX BREAK IS SAFE
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Both findBestTarget and targetCity stop when they encounter an unreachable or
own-team city because the cache is sorted by attackPriority. UWAICache proves the
required ordering invariant:

    unreachable city -> attackPriority() == -1
    own-team city     -> attackPriority() == -2
    reachable rival   -> attackPriority() >= 0

sortCitiesByAttackPriority is descending selection sort (with only a positive
rival's cross-area priority diluted by 1/2, which remains nonnegative). Thus a
negative-priority own/unreachable city cannot precede a reachable rival city.
The `break` is valid; no F264 here.


CONTROL / NON-PROMOTION -- NAVAL LOGISTICS LIMIT * AREA AVAILABILITY
--------------------------------------------------------------------
A tempting arithmetic objection is that a naval landing can first be reduced by
cargo support and later again by `rAreaWeightAtt`, so the two factors multiply.
History makes that insufficient for a bug finding. Practical 1289 deliberately
introduced the battle-area projection AFTER the existing Logistics-supported
landing calculation and explicitly described two separate constraints:

* the naval attack can focus "as many as are supported by LOGISTICS";
* independently, the AI "struggles badly with deploying units from different
  areas."

Practical 1371 retained that separation while changing the human/AI weighting.
Multiplying two explicitly distinct availability approximations may be crude, but
is compatible with the stated model. Without a stronger invariant or concrete
state/unit mismatch, do not promote this as F264.

C021-WIP11 CONTINUATION -- queue 023 InvasionGraph.cpp

F264 / provisional KI#587 -- COASTAL DEFENDER FLEET LOSSES DO NOT REDUCE ITS OVERLAPPING LOGISTICS CAPACITY
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TITLE
    A defender can lose transport ships in the coastal-bombardment sea battle, but that
    step records only FLEET loss and deliberately records zero LOGISTICS loss. Because
    LOGISTICS is persistent graph state and overlaps FLEET for proper transports, the same
    defender can later launch a naval invasion with cargo capacity belonging to transports
    that the preceding simulation step has already destroyed as Fleet power.

STATUS
    CONFIRMED inherited UWAI/AdvCiv overlapping-branch state omission.
    Present from the initial tracked InvasionGraph import, practical 1253
    (f6ff6a182f...), and still present in Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS.
    This is separate from the explicitly acknowledged cargo-capacity-vs-combat-power
    approximation and from F261's confidence conversion error.

BRANCH MODEL / HARD OVERLAP
    MilitaryBranch.h defines FLEET as any sea ship with combat strength, including
    transports, and LOGISTICS as ships transporting Army units. Therefore a proper
    combat-capable transport belongs to BOTH branches:

        FLEET       -> combat-power representation
        LOGISTICS   -> cargo-capacity representation

    MilitaryBranch::Fleet::unitPower uses the ship's military power, whereas
    MilitaryBranch::Logistics::unitPower returns getCargoSpace(). The units differ, but
    both branches describe the same physical transport hulls.

PRODUCER -- COASTAL BATTLE
    In Node::step, a land-reachable city attack can still trigger a coastal sea battle
    when the attacker can bombard from sea. The source explicitly says:

        "Only defender is assumed to bring cargo units into battle."

    The attacker removes its Logistics component from the Fleet estimate (approximately),
    whereas the defender uses its entire remaining FLEET power, therefore including
    combat-capable transports.

    The calculated sea-battle casualties are then recorded only as:

        kStep.reducePower(attacker, FLEET, rLossesAtt);
        kStep.reducePower(defender, FLEET, rLossesDef);

    No LOGISTICS loss is recorded. The nearby rationale is:

        "Losses in logistics don't matter b/c no naval landing is attempted,
         and the cost (of having to rebuild units) is already included in the fleet losses."

    That rationale is local to the present step and does not hold for the persistent
    graph state consumed by later steps.

CONCRETE HARD CASE
    Let defender D's naval force consist entirely of proper combat-capable transports
    (e.g. the model-equivalent of Galleons/Transports), so every ship contributes to both
    FLEET and LOGISTICS.

    A coastal battle can record positive FLEET loss for D. With no non-transport combat
    ship available to absorb that loss, the model has necessarily destroyed some of the
    physical transports represented by LOGISTICS as well. Yet D's m_arLostPower[LOGISTICS]
    remains unchanged, so all original cargo capacity survives in simulation state.

PRODUCER -> STATE -> CONSUMER PATH
    A simple acyclic component is enough:

        A -> D -> T

    where A attacks a land-reachable coastal city of D and D's own primary target T
    requires a naval landing.

    resolveLossesRec is post-order over incoming edges:

        T.resolveLossesRec()
            -> D.resolveLossesRec()
                -> A.resolveLossesRec()
                -> D.resolveLosses()      [A attacks D first]
            -> T.resolveLosses()          [D attacks T afterward]

    Thus A's coastal attack on D is applied BEFORE D's later outgoing attack on T.
    D's FLEET losses persist in m_arLostPower[FLEET], but the omitted Logistics losses do
    not. When D later performs a naval step, its landing capacity is recomputed from:

        D.m_military[LOGISTICS]->power() - D.m_arLostPower[LOGISTICS]

    and therefore still includes the cargo capacity of transports already represented as
    destroyed by the earlier FLEET loss.

WHY THE EXISTING COMMENT DOES NOT MAKE THIS SAFE
    It is reasonable not to care about cargo capacity for the *current* land attack, and
    the FLEET loss does already charge rebuilding cost. But SimulationStep losses are also
    availability state for later graph steps. Cost accounting cannot make a destroyed
    transport available for a subsequent landing. This is the same reason overlapping
    CAVALRY/ARMY branches are updated together elsewhere: overlapping branches must remain
    mutually consistent when the same physical unit is lost.

    The pre-existing FIXME about LOGISTICS using cargo slots while FLEET uses corrected
    combat power makes the exact proportional conversion approximate; it does not justify
    an exact zero LOGISTICS update in the all-transport hard case.

HISTORY
    Practical 1253 introduces the coastal battle with both comments above and with FLEET-
    only losses. The behavior survives later cleanup/scaled rewrites (including 2920/2954)
    and remains in Base AdvCiv 1.14 and SAS. No K-Mod/Civ4CE cognate exists because UWAI's
    InvasionGraph is not present there.

REPAIR DIRECTION
    When the coastal defender's Fleet loss can include proper transports, propagate an
    estimated overlapping loss into LOGISTICS as well. Reusing a defender-side cargo/Fleet
    ratio analogous to the full naval-battle path is the smallest structural repair, while
    retaining the existing documented dimensional approximation. Clamp the resulting
    Logistics loss to remaining cargo capacity.

    A more exact long-term repair would track transport combat power and cargo capacity
    separately so the same physical transport casualties can update both branch measures
    without dividing unlike units.

INTERACTIONS / NON-DUPLICATION
    * F261: confidence leaks into attacker Logistics casualty conversion in the full naval
      battle. F264 exists even at confidence 1 and concerns the coastal-battle path where
      defender Logistics casualties are omitted entirely.
    * F262: repeat-trip capacity is applied before transport losses during an actual naval
      landing. F264 concerns stale Logistics state created by an earlier coastal battle.
    * The longstanding "cargo capacity vs Fleet power" FIXME is an approximation/control;
      F264 is the independently provable persistence failure when destroyed overlapping
      transports remain fully available in a later step.

C021-WIP12 CONTINUATION -- queue 023 InvasionGraph.cpp
