PUF / TRANSPORT / STRING-HELPER CONTROLS FROZEN
-----------------------------------------------
1. PUF callback argument-type audit:
   Despite generic int callback slots and some legacy/misleading names, traced live callers
   supply the semantic type expected by each predicate. In particular,
   PUF_isOtherTeam expects a PlayerTypes value and callers pass players; PUF_isCombatTeam
   expects TeamTypes and callers pass teams. No live player/team reinterpretation root was
   established.

2. PUF_isEnemyCityAttacker transport proxy:
   Its treatment of generic cargo transports as potential city threats is longstanding and
   intentional-looking, not a hard defect. The helper was introduced to classify units that
   can endanger a city, and cargo vessels can carry city attackers even when the hull itself
   cannot attack cities. Current consumers are conservative city-safety/trade gates. Do not
   make F272 merely from empty transports satisfying this proxy without an independent
   contract contradiction.

3. eAssumePeaceTeam hidden-nationality edge:
   The hypothetical-peace parameter could deserve care with always-hostile/hidden-nationality
   combat ownership, but every live isVisibleEnemyCityAttacker caller currently passes
   NO_TEAM. This is dormant in current SAS and is not F272.

4. setListHelp(NULL, ...) concern:
   The live NULL-start calls resolve to the CvWStringBuffer overload. CvWStringBuffer::append
   explicitly ignores a NULL wchar pointer. No current NULL-start call into the less-tolerant
   CvWString overload was found. This is safe by current caller/overload contract.

5. Debug enum/string helpers:
   Preliminary automated enum-vs-switch comparison suggests some MissionTypes/MissionAITypes
   lack dedicated symbolic names, but these diagnostic helpers have numeric UNKNOWN fallbacks.
   This remains under challenge; omission alone is not a gameplay/root finding.

CONTROLS / NON-FINDINGS ADDED SINCE WIP04
=========================================

A. `handicapFromDifficulty` exact-midpoint tie -- CONTROL
---------------------------------------------------------
The SAS helper scans handicap XML in enum order and updates only on strictly smaller
absolute distance. Therefore an exact midpoint between two current scores chooses the
earlier/lower entry; e.g. Noble 50 + Prince 58 average to 54 and map to Noble.

This differs from some pre-SAS averaging callers, but there is no single inherited tie
contract to preserve:

  * AdvCiv `CvGame::initGameHandicap` averaged enum-derived difficulty and used
    `intdiv::round`, so an exact adjacent .5 generally rounded upward;
  * AdvCiv `CvGame::updateAIHandicap` averaged enum IDs with `intdiv::uround`, likewise
    generally choosing the upper adjacent enum on a .5;
  * AdvCiv `CvTeam::getHandicapType`, however, deliberately used integer division and
    therefore chose the lower entry for the comparable midpoint.

SAS commit 5970 replaced these assumptions because Rookie/Deity+ and XML `iDifficulty`
scores make enum-index arithmetic invalid. "Nearest XML score, earlier/lower on an exact
tie" is internally coherent, and the old callers themselves disagreed about tie direction.
Do not promote F272 merely from the changed tie-break outcome.

B. live-unit selection-group assumptions in PUF helpers -- CONTROL
-------------------------------------------------------------------
`PUF_isAirIntercept`, `PUF_isMissionAIType`, `PUF_isGroupHead` and the group-head helper
family dereference a unit selection group without local NULL guards. This initially looks
fragile because `CvUnit::getGroup()` can technically return NULL for an invalid group ID.

Lifecycle tracing does not establish a live bug:

  * normal live units are attached/re-attached to selection groups;
  * `CvUnit::isGroupHead()` itself unconditionally dereferences `getGroup()`, making group
    existence a broad core live-unit invariant rather than a special PUF assumption;
  * the deliberate `joinGroup(NULL, false, false)` no-rejoin path occurs during
    `CvUnit::kill`, after the unit is removed from the map and immediately before
    `unitLost`/deletion, so normal plot-count PUF callers cannot encounter that detached
    dying unit as a live plot unit.

No transient live caller violating the invariant was proved. Keep as contract control.

C. `PUF_isFiniteRangeAndNotJustProduced` uses `> 1` -- CONTROL
-------------------------------------------------------------
Despite the helper name, it excludes units whose creation turn is either the current turn
or the immediately preceding game turn. The sole current gameplay use is the inherited
BBAI/K-Mod transport-pickup valuation, whose own comment says it wants units that "have
had a chance to move since being built." The condition is inherited together with that
caller. Without proving the intended turn-order window is only one global turn, the name
alone is insufficient evidence of an off-by-one defect. Do not allocate F272 on this basis.

D. `setListHelp` integer-list-ID sentinel -- CONTROL
---------------------------------------------------
The int-reference overload treats `iLastListID == iListID` as a continuation and otherwise
emits `szStart`. Many callers initialize `iLast = 0`, which would be wrong if the first
actual list ID could also be zero.

All current caller families inspected either explicitly skip zero-valued modifiers before
calling the helper or sit inside an outer nonzero-value condition. Negative nonzero values
also correctly differ from the zero sentinel. Thus current first-item formatting is safe;
no uninitialized/zero-key caller was found.

E. hotkey description mapping -- CONTROL
----------------------------------------
The legacy mapping declares `iNumKeyBoardMappings = 108` and contains exactly 108 mapping
initializers. The longest `KB_*` token is well below the fixed 25-TCHAR storage capacity.
A scan of all current SAS XML found 49 distinct nonempty `<HotKey>` codes, and every one is
present in the mapping. No current hotkey-description omission or array-count mismatch.

F. `applyColorToString` self-format alias -- CONTROL
----------------------------------------------------
The helper calls `s.Format(..., s.GetCString())`. `CvWString::Format` first formats into a
separate local `std::wstring result` and only assigns `*this = result` afterward, so the
source pointer is not invalidated before formatting consumes it. No self-alias corruption.

G. debug Mission string omission -- DIAGNOSTIC CLEANUP, NOT F272
----------------------------------------------------------------
Current `getMissionTypeString` lacks an explicit `MISSION_RANGE_ATTACK` case while that
mission is live (`CvUnitAI::AI_rangeAttack` queues it). Debug plot help therefore falls
back to `UNKOWN_MISSION(<numeric id>)` rather than the symbolic mission name. The numeric
fallback remains unique and no gameplay state depends on the string. K-Mod, AdvCiv and
Civ4CE carry the same omission. Useful cleanup for diagnostics, but below the current root
bar unless an independent diagnostic failure is demonstrated.

H. `intHash` / coordinate-key controls remain unchanged
-------------------------------------------------------
No supported deterministic OOS failure was established from signed 32-bit polynomial
wrap on the fixed legacy MSVC/Win32 target, and `contestedPlots`' x*1000+y key remains far
outside the collision regime for all shipped SAS world sizes. Both remain future-proofing
notes rather than live roots.

CURRENT ASSESSMENT
==================
The inherited utility/PUF body has now had argument types, hidden-nationality ownership,
group lifecycle, list formatting, hotkey data, direction helpers, hash callers, calendar
boundaries, and K-Mod/Civ4CE cognates challenged. The late pass is increasingly yielding
controls rather than uncovered state/consumer contradictions.

F272 remains deliberately UNUSED.

    * finish SAS victory-helper evolution / caller-unit consistency;
    * finish Civ4CE explicit-fix divergence scan for surviving utility helpers;
    * re-check queue-039 live roots F270/F271 for overlap/repair bounds;
    * if no independent hard root emerges, perform a closure/saturation pass rather than
      manufacturing F272.

ADDITIONAL CONTROLS / CROSS-CHECKS
==================================

I. SAS victory-denial helper evolution and callers -- CONTROL
--------------------------------------------------------------
The post-6037 helper chain was traced through the current callers rather than assuming that
later refactoring kept all thresholds aligned.

`getSASVictoryStageLevel` itself correctly checks cumulative victory bits from stage 4 down
to stage 1. This strengthens the earlier F250 boundary: F250 belongs to InvasionGraph's
separate ancient local macro, not this shared helper.

The team-level stage, spaceship-parts and stage-3-Space helpers are internally coherent for
current SAS XML:
    * the current Space component maxima total 16 parts;
    * current VictoryThreshold values match the component maxima for the complete ship;
    * lower VictoryMinThreshold values intentionally permit an incomplete launch, whereas
      the stage-3 emergency heuristic explicitly measures progress toward the full ship
      (the source comment itself reasons in terms of 8/16 parts).

`getSASVictoryDelayTurnsFromNormalGameSpeed` intentionally does not cache the game-speed
result. Current victory-denial Normal-speed countdown defines are 20 turns, and every
shipped VictoryDelayPercent maps 20 to an exact integer, so its nearest-integer scaling and
`CvGame::victoryDelay`'s truncating arithmetic do not currently diverge on those gates.

`isSASUWAIVictoryDenialPeaceThreat` returns early before writing optional diagnostic output
pointers when the feature is globally disabled. The current `CvDeal` caller is safe:
    * disabled => both team calls return false and the deal helper returns before reading
      any output variables;
    * enabled => both calls populate their outputs before the logging path.
No asymmetric enable exists because the define is global/static.

The no-output callers in CvPlayerAI/UWAIAgent consistently ask whether either party is a
configured victory threat. CvTeamAI's older brokered-peace denial block duplicates the same
countdown/stage4/stage3-Space criteria with the same game-speed scaling. No one-sided
threshold/unit drift was found.

-------------------------------------------------------------------
The historical design treats a generic cargo transport as a conservative city threat even
when the hull itself is not a land attacker. Current SAS unit XML supports that intended
proxy rather than exposing a cargo-domain counterexample:

    generic (`SpecialCargo == NONE`) cargo units with positive cargo space:
        Galley, Galleon, Transport, Privateer
        -> all use DomainCargo = DOMAIN_LAND

    Missile Cruiser, Attack Submarine and Carrier use a non-NONE SpecialCargo and are
    therefore excluded from the helper's generic-transport shortcut.

Thus the shortcut does not currently classify an air-only/missile-only special transport as
an invasion transport. Its empty-transport conservatism remains intentional-looking city

F270 / KI#593 -- collateral attacker-team role in AI_localAttackStrength
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
Root:
    `estimateCollateralWeight` defines its first team argument as the team dealing
    collateral damage. `CvPlayerAI::AI_localAttackStrength`, however, hardwires the
    evaluating player's `getTeam()` into that role while the actual candidate attackers
    are selected by `eAttackTeam` (or by all teams currently at war when eAttackTeam is
    NO_TEAM).

Why this is independently live:
    * the helper uses the supplied attack team in defender-bonus context and when
      excluding the attacking side from the resistance sample;
    * explicit enemy-team calls therefore evaluate hostile collateral using the defender's
      team identity;
    * explicit own-team offense calls and default all-hostiles calls demonstrate that this
      cannot be repaired safely by blindly swapping one hardcoded team for another.

History:
    K-Mod 448 introduced collateral weighting into local attack-strength valuation.
    K-Mod 1200 made the helper contract explicit as attacking team first, defender team
    optional, while the local-attack-strength caller retained the evaluator-team argument.
    The mismatch survives K-Mod -> AdvCiv -> SAS. Selection-group callers are not affected
    by the same root because there `getTeam()` genuinely is the attacking group team.

Repair boundary:
    * when `eAttackTeam` is explicit, collateral attacker semantics must use that team;
    * when AI_localAttackStrength is aggregating all hostile teams (`NO_TEAM`), there is no
      single truthful attack-team identity, so use an explicitly generic/per-team policy
      rather than silently treating the evaluator as the attacker;
    * defender-team sampling must likewise follow whether the evaluator is defending the
      target, attacking it, or merely estimating nearby hostile strength.
Do not mechanically replace `getTeam()` with `eAttackTeam` in every mode without preserving
these caller semantics.

F271 / KI#594 -- negative fractional BC year division
-----------------------------------------------------
Root:
    `getTurnMonthForGame` can produce negative month counts not divisible by the number of
    months per year for supported fractional-year calendars. `getTurnYearForGame` converts
    months to years with ordinary signed C++ integer division, which truncates toward zero
    rather than flooring the calendar year.

Concrete supported example:
    With a monthly calendar around the BC/AD boundary, turn-month -1 represents the final
    month of 1 BC. `-1 / 12` becomes 0 in C++, and the year formatter intentionally renders
    year 0 as 1 AD. The chronology can therefore display a month of 1 AD before January
    1 AD. CALENDAR_MONTHS, CALENDAR_SEASONS and CALENDAR_WEEKS are first-class Civ4
    calendar modes and WorldBuilder scenarios serialize Calendar/StartYear, so this is not
    merely an impossible custom-mod input.

Non-display consumer:
    `CvGame::getGameTurnYear()` feeds the building-age comparison used for the 1000-year
    building commerce/culture doubling mechanic, so a fractional BC scenario can also shift
    that threshold by a calendar year.

History:
    Civ4/K-Mod/AdvCiv and Civ4CE retain the truncating quotient. AdvCiv separately repaired
    the sibling negative `%` problem in `CvGameTextMgr::setDateStr` by introducing
    `intdiv::umodulo`, but the quotient half remained unchanged.

Repair boundary:
    Let `m = getTurnMonthForGame(...)` and `n = max(1, GC.getNumMonthInfos())`.
    A clean integer floor quotient is:

        (m - intdiv::umodulo(m, n)) / n

    For nonnegative and exact-year dates this is identical to existing behavior. For a
    negative fractional year it subtracts the positive calendar remainder before exact
    division, giving the mathematically correct floor year.

F270 vs F271:
    DISTINCT / INDEPENDENT.
    F270 is a combat-AI caller-role bug in collateral valuation. F271 is calendar arithmetic
    used by date/API/gameplay year consumers. Either reproduces with the other subsystem
    absent; their repairs share no state or contract.

I. SAS-vs-Base AdvCiv semantic delta — BOUNDED / CONTROL
--------------------------------------------------------
Normalized current SAS vs Base AdvCiv 1.14 comparison is very small. Current SAS mainly:

    * replaces terse missing-GlobalDefine assertions with richer diagnostics;
    * retains the Base AdvCiv global/cache/info-array implementation otherwise.

This makes inherited CvGlobals lifetime, cache and XML registration contracts the primary

II. SetGlobalDefines -> cacheGlobals -> m_pPythonCaller — OPEN LIFECYCLE CANDIDATE
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CvXMLLoadUtility::SetGlobalDefines() finishes with:

    GC.cacheGlobals();

CvGlobals::cacheGlobals() performs full integer/float cache initialization and then:

    m_pPythonCaller = new CvPythonCaller();
    CvEventReporter::getInstance().initPythonCallbackGuards();

m_pPythonCaller is deleted in CvGlobals::uninit(), but cacheGlobals() itself does not first
free an existing object.

Important narrowing:
    * K-Mod/Civ4CE also called cacheGlobals() from runtime define setters;
    * AdvCiv intentionally replaced those full recaches with targeted cacheGlobalInts /
      cacheGlobalFloats updates before introducing/retaining the Python-caller allocation;
    * therefore current runtime setDefineINT/FLOAT does NOT itself repeat the allocation.

The remaining question is whether the EXE can invoke SetGlobalDefines() multiple times in a
single CvGlobals lifetime (e.g. supported XML reload). That call is external to the DLL-side
source available here. Without proving repeat execution, this is not F272.

III. info/type-map reset orchestration — CONTROL / EXTERNAL CONTRACT
-------------------------------------------------------------------
CleanUpGlobalVariables() calls deleteInfoArrays(), which deletes info objects/string arrays
and clears m_typesMap through clearTypesMap(). m_infosMap is instead cleared by the separately
exported CvGlobals::infoTypeFromStringReset().

The latter contains the inherited diagnostic:

    FErrorMsg("Just to see if and when CvGlobals::infoTypeFromStringReset is ever called");

This looks awkward, but the function is DllExport and therefore can be part of the EXE's XML
reload orchestration. A stale removed-info mapping would be real if arrays were reloaded
without this callback, but the available DLL source cannot establish that omission. Keep as
an external-lifecycle control; do not infer F272 from absence of an in-DLL caller.

IV. CvAgents ownership — REAL CLEANUP OMISSION, CURRENT IMPACT NOT YET PROVED
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
CvGlobals::init() allocates:

    m_agents = new CvAgents(MAX_PLAYERS, MAX_TEAMS);

CvGlobals::uninit() frees CvPlayer/CvTeam statics but never deletes m_agents. The CvAgents
object therefore remains allocated and retains vectors of pointers to player/team instances
that have just been freed.

This is a genuine ownership asymmetry, but no supported same-DLL init->uninit->init cycle has
yet been established. If uninit occurs only at process/DLL shutdown, the OS reclaims the
allocation and no later consumer dereferences the stale cache. Keep below gameplay-root bar
unless a re-init path is proved.

V. getDirectionTypes indexed overload — INHERITED TYPE-SIGNATURE MISMATCH / LATENT CONTROL
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Neighboring accessors are:

    getAutomateTypes(AutomateTypes e)
    getDirectionTypes(AutomateTypes e)

The second clearly ought, by semantic type, to take DirectionTypes. This exact copy/paste
signature exists in Civ4CE and K-Mod and survives Base AdvCiv/SAS.

However:
    * current DLL source uses only the pointer-returning getDirectionTypes() overload when
      loading/deleting the array;
    * no indexed current DLL caller was found;
    * K-Mod/Civ4CE exported the indexed overload, whereas current AdvCiv/SAS no longer marks
      it DllExport.

So the signature is incorrect as an API contract but no current caller-visible failure has
been proved. Keep as latent cleanup/control, not F272.

VI. define-cache update preliminaries — CONTROL
-----------------------------------------------
ReadGlobalDefines writes directly into FVariableSystem during startup, then cacheGlobals()
initializes the cached arrays. Runtime setDefineINT/FLOAT uses targeted update helpers in
current AdvCiv/SAS, so the old K-Mod/CE full-cache recache behavior no longer causes repeated
m_pPythonCaller allocation.

cacheGlobalFloats' startup recursion through updateCityCamDist is bounded: the outer call
stores the new FIELD_OF_VIEW before updateCityCamDist -> setDefineFLOAT triggers the inner
cacheGlobalFloats call, so the inner pass observes unchanged FoV and does not recurse again.

CvGlobals::getFootstepAudioTypeByTag(strTag) searches m_paszFootstepAudioTypes rather than

AnimationOperatorTypes enum constants start at ANIMOP_FIRST = 1001, while

CvGlobals::getPlotGroupFinder() lazily initializes an FAStar instance with current map width,

CvGlobals.h defines, under `#ifndef _USRDLL`, macros such as:

while CvGlobals.cpp defines:

This looks recursively self-referential in a textual read. It is not recursive in the DLL

C023-WIP03 — QUEUE 040 CvGameCoreDLL/CvGlobals.cpp
F272 / provisional KI#595 CONFIRMED
Date: 2026-08-28
Model: GPT-5.6-Sol

F272 / provisional KI#595 — FOREIGN-REPLAY COLOR REMAP WRAPS BACK INTO THE
"SKIPPED" SYSTEM-COLOR PREFIX
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: CONFIRMED; inherited AdvCiv feature bug (advc.106i), optional/config-gated.
Primary file: CvGameCoreDLL/CvGlobals.cpp
Same-root consumer/input contract: CvGameCoreDLL/CvReplayInfo.cpp

Current CvGlobals::getColorInfo(ColorTypes eColor) contains an out-of-range replay fallback:

    if (eColor >= getNumColorInfos())
    {
        FAssert(m_bHoFScreenUp || eColor < getNumColorInfos());
        // +7: Skip colors from COLOR_CLEAR to COLOR_LIGHT_GREY
        eColor = (ColorTypes)((eColor + 7) % getNumColorInfos());
    }

The stated invariant is explicit: remapped foreign colors should skip indices 0..6
(COLOR_CLEAR through COLOR_LIGHT_GREY). The arithmetic does not preserve that invariant after
one wrap of the normal color table.

CURRENT SAS COUNTEREXAMPLE
--------------------------
Current CIV4ColorVals.xml contains 128 ColorVal entries:
    0 COLOR_CLEAR
    1 COLOR_ALPHA_GREY
    2 COLOR_WHITE
    3 COLOR_BLACK
    4 COLOR_DARK_GREY
    5 COLOR_GREY
    6 COLOR_LIGHT_GREY
    7 COLOR_RED
    ...

CvReplayInfo::read accepts a foreign-mod player color through:

    checkBounds(info.m_eColor, 0, GC.getNumColorInfos() - 1)

and checkBounds deliberately doubles its upper bound when HOF_DISPLAY_OTHER_MOD_REPLAYS is
enabled. With 128 local colors, foreign replay IDs 0..254 are therefore accepted.

For the accepted high foreign IDs:
    249 -> (249 + 7) % 128 = 0  -> COLOR_CLEAR
    250 -> 1                    -> COLOR_ALPHA_GREY
    251 -> 2                    -> COLOR_WHITE
    252 -> 3                    -> COLOR_BLACK
    253 -> 4                    -> COLOR_DARK_GREY
    254 -> 5                    -> COLOR_GREY

Thus six IDs that the parser intentionally accepts as valid foreign extra colors are mapped
straight into the very prefix that getColorInfo says it is skipping. COLOR_CLEAR is especially
bad for replay/Hall-of-Fame display because the mapped marker/color can become transparent.

PRODUCER -> STATE -> CONSUMER
-----------------------------
1. HOF_DISPLAY_OTHER_MOD_REPLAYS enables permissive loading of replay data produced by another
   mod.
2. CvReplayInfo::checkBounds allows foreign player-color IDs up to twice the local normal upper
   bound.
3. CvReplayInfo stores the accepted foreign m_eColor unchanged.
4. Hall-of-Fame/replay UI consumes those stored ColorTypes (e.g. color markers, graph/minimap
   layers); m_bHoFScreenUp deliberately permits CvGlobals::getColorInfo to receive an ID beyond
   the local array.
5. getColorInfo remaps it with `(eColor + 7) % N`.
6. For the final accepted IDs of the doubled range, the result is 0..5, violating the explicit
   skip-system-colors contract.

This is config-gated in current SAS because HOF_DISPLAY_OTHER_MOD_REPLAYS defaults to 0, but it
is a real defect in the supported/configurable compatibility feature, not merely hypothetical
bad input.

ANCESTRY / BOUNDARY
-------------------
K-Mod does not contain this remapping feature; it simply asserts a normal in-range ColorTypes.
AdvCiv practical 1430 (8377887745-family history around advc.106i introduction; exact tracked
file AdvCivPreSAS_1430_efd11afbeb.diff) introduced the foreign-replay fallback already as:

    // +7: Skip COLOR_CLEAR to COLOR_LIGHT_GREY
    e = (ColorTypes)((e + 7) % getNumColorInfos());

Later AdvCiv changes only refactored/renamed the accessor and comment. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and
current SAS retain the same arithmetic, while CvReplayInfo retains the generous doubled bound.
Therefore this is inherited from AdvCiv's advc.106i replay-compatibility feature, not SAS.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Map out-of-range IDs into the intended usable suffix [7, N) rather than shifting then taking
modulo N. For N > 7 and eColor >= N, a direct form is conceptually:

    7 + ((eColor - 7) % (N - 7))

(or equivalently offset relative to N). This guarantees every fallback result is >= 7 and < N.
Keep a defensive fallback/assert for pathological N <= 7 even though current assets have 128.

Do not merely lower CvReplayInfo's generous upper bound enough to hide the arithmetic problem;
that would unnecessarily reject foreign colors that can safely be represented through a
correct suffix remap.

SEVERITY / SCOPE
----------------
Low-to-moderate UI/compatibility severity; optional because display of other mods' replays is
disabled by default. No normal current-game ColorTypes are affected because the remap branch
runs only for eColor >= local color count.

DUPLICATE CHECK
---------------
No earlier album root was found for replay extra-color remapping/getColorInfo. This is separate

C023-WIP04 — QUEUE 040 CvGameCoreDLL/CvGlobals.cpp

F273 / provisional KI#596 — SAS RICH GLOBALDEFINE DIAGNOSTICS ACCIDENTALLY
DISABLE THE INHERITED ASSERTION IN THE OPTIMIZED ASSERT BUILD
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Status: CONFIRMED; SAS-specific diagnostic/build-configuration regression.
Primary file: CvGameCoreDLL/CvGlobals.cpp
Same-root sibling: CvGameCoreDLL/CvSelectionGroupAI.cpp
Build contract: CvGameCoreDLL/Project/Makefile + CvGameCoreDLL/FAssert.h

ROOT CONTRACT
-------------
AdvCiv's build system intentionally supports two assertion-capable configurations:

    Debug  = _DEBUG (which in FAssert.h also defines FASSERT_ENABLE)
    Assert = Release flags + /DFASSERT_ENABLE, without _DEBUG

The Makefile is explicit:

    Debug_DEFINES=/DWIN32 /D_WINDOWS /D_USRDLL /D_DEBUG
    Release_DEFINES=/DWIN32 /D_WINDOWS /D_USRDLL /DNDEBUG
    ...
    !IF "$(TARGET)" == "Assert"
    CFLAGS  = $(Release_CFLAGS) /DFASSERT_ENABLE

and FAssert.h independently gates the assertion macros on FASSERT_ENABLE:

    #ifdef _DEBUG
        #define FASSERT_ENABLE
    #endif
    ...
    #ifdef FASSERT_ENABLE
        #define FAssert(...)
        #define FAssertMsg(...)
    #else
        #define FAssert(...) (void)0
        #define FAssertMsg(...) (void)0
    #endif

Therefore `_DEBUG` is a sufficient condition for assertions, but it is NOT the assertion
feature flag. `FASSERT_ENABLE` is the actual contract and can intentionally be enabled in an
optimized/non-debug DLL.

PRIMARY FAILURE: CvGlobals GlobalDefine accessors
-------------------------------------------------
Base AdvCiv retains a cheap FAssert/FAssertMsg after the GlobalDefine lookup. Current SAS
replaced those plain assertions with richer lazy diagnostics in all three accessors:

    CvGlobals::getDefineINT
    CvGlobals::getDefineFLOAT
    CvGlobals::getDefineSTRING

The lookup status itself is correctly compiled whenever FASSERT_ENABLE is active, e.g.:

    #ifdef FASSERT_ENABLE
    bool bSuccess =
    #endif
    getDefinesVarSystem()->GetValue(...);

but the new diagnostic/assert block is guarded by `_DEBUG` instead:

    #ifdef _DEBUG
        if (!bSuccess) { ... FAssertMsg(...); }
    #endif

(or the FLOAT equivalent with CAMERA_MIN_DISTANCE exempted).

That changes the inherited build behavior:

    Build      Base AdvCiv                 current SAS
    -----      -----------                 -----------
    Debug      assertion active            richer assertion active
    Assert     assertion active            assertion SILENTLY REMOVED
    Release    assertion compiled out      assertion compiled out

The Assert target exists specifically to preserve assertions while running release-like code.
Missing/mistyped GlobalDefines therefore lose the inherited detection exactly in that useful
configuration. The lookup still falls back to the normal default, so this is a diagnostic
regression rather than a gameplay-state defect by itself; however it can materially hide XML
or refactor mistakes from the Assert DLL (the richer INT diagnostic was added precisely after
such a define typo was caught during SAS development).

REPAIR DIRECTION — CvGlobals
----------------------------
Gate the rich failure-only diagnostic on `FASSERT_ENABLE`, not `_DEBUG`:

    #ifdef FASSERT_ENABLE
        if (!bSuccess) { ... FAssertMsg(...); }
    #endif

and analogously for FLOAT/STRING. This keeps:

    * Debug: rich assertion, unchanged;
    * Assert: rich assertion restored;
    * Release: no assertion/formatting machinery;
    * normal successful lookups: no expensive message formatting, because the existing
      failure condition remains outside/around the formatting work.

No need to revert to the old uninformative Base assertion merely to fix the build guard.

SAME-ROOT SIBLING: CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_update
-------------------------------------------------
The same SAS optimization pattern was applied to AdvCiv's inherited stuck-loop assertion.
Base AdvCiv executes:

    FAssertMsg(iAttempts != iMaxAttempts, "Unit stuck in a loop");

outside `_DEBUG`, so it remains active in the Assert target. SAS moved the richer version
inside:

    #ifdef _DEBUG
        const bool bAssertCondition = (iAttempts != iMaxAttempts);
        if (!bAssertCondition) { ... FAssertMsg(...rich state...); }
        iMaxAttempts += 4; // restore Debug-only early-trigger adjustment
    #endif

The result is the same root: the Assert DLL no longer has the inherited stuck-loop assertion.

IMPORTANT REPAIR BOUNDARY FOR THE SIBLING
-----------------------------------------
Do NOT blindly replace that entire `_DEBUG` block with `FASSERT_ENABLE`: the
`iMaxAttempts += 4` line repairs an earlier `_DEBUG`-only `iMaxAttempts -= 4` adjustment and
must remain Debug-only. A safe conceptual split is:

    #ifdef FASSERT_ENABLE
        // lazy rich assertion block
    #endif
    #ifdef _DEBUG
        iMaxAttempts += 4; // restore only the Debug-only subtraction
    #endif

This restores Assert-build detection without changing its normal iteration limit.

CORRECTION TO THE ALREADY-CLOSED QUEUE 041 AUDIT
-------------------------------------------------
The queue-041 closure currently contains this rejected-control statement:

    "This does not disable an assert-enabled non-debug configuration: FAssert.h defines
     FASSERT_ENABLE only when _DEBUG itself is defined. Outside _DEBUG the old assert was
     already a no-op."

That statement is WRONG because it considered only FAssert.h's automatic `_DEBUG` enablement
and missed the Makefile's separate Assert target (`Release_CFLAGS /DFASSERT_ENABLE`).

Amend that old control as follows:

    * the expensive-formatting concern was valid;
    * moving message construction behind the failure condition was good;
    * moving the assertion itself behind `_DEBUG` was not equivalent to the inherited
      behavior and disabled it in the optimized Assert build;
    * reopen that rejected diagnostic candidate only as SAME-ROOT evidence for F273, not as
      a new independent numbered root and not as a retraction of queue-041's established
      gameplay findings.

ANCESTRY / INDEPENDENCE
-----------------------
Base AdvCiv has the plain assertions and the two-build assertion contract. The loss occurs in
SAS's richer diagnostic replacements, so F273 is SAS-specific. It is independent of F272:
F272 is an inherited Hall-of-Fame/replay color-remapping arithmetic bug; F273 is a build-guard
diagnostic regression affecting assertion coverage.

II. WAR_SUCCESS_CITY_CAPTURING LOWER-BOUND ASYMMETRY — LATENT ROBUSTNESS CONTROL
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Full cache initialization special-cases WAR_SUCCESS_CITY_CAPTURING with iLower = 1 because the
source explicitly says 0 can crash AI code. A later runtime setDefineINT of that same name would
use cacheGlobalInts(szChangedDefine, iNewValue), which stores iNewValue directly and therefore
does not reapply the >=1 normalization.

This is a real API robustness asymmetry, but current SAS contains no runtime setter for this
define. XML startup goes through the normalized full-cache path. Do not allocate F274 without
a supported/live mutation path; record the invariant for any future generic define editor.

III. CvGlobals init/uninit / CvAgents — OWNERSHIP OMISSION STILL BELOW ROOT BAR
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Rechecked the whole init/uninit pair and CvAgents implementation.

CvGlobals::init allocates m_agents after CvPlayer/CvTeam statics and CvAgents stores vectors of
raw player/team pointers plus installs itself into AgentIteratorBase's global cache pointer.
CvGlobals::uninit frees CvPlayer/CvTeam statics but does not delete m_agents.

So the ownership omission is genuine, and the leaked object contains stale pointers during
teardown. init/uninit are DllExport, but the current DLL source contains no second local init
call, no post-uninit AgentIterator consumer, and no proof that the Civ4 EXE performs a supported
same-loaded-DLL reinit cycle rather than unloading the DLL/process. Keep as cleanup/lifecycle
debt rather than inventing a live F274.

IV. CvXMLLoadUtility RAW POINTER — HISTORICALLY ACKNOWLEDGED EXTERNAL-LIFETIME CONTROL
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
CvGlobals retains m_pXMLLoadUtility for lazy optional/throne-room XML. CvXMLLoadUtility's own
destructor explicitly comments that the EXE appears to destroy it only when exiting from the
opening menu and that deleting it from another path risks double deletion. Current source does
not clear GC.m_pXMLLoadUtility in that destructor.

The pointer can therefore look dangling in isolation, but its only lazy consumers are meaningful
before that menu-exit teardown. No local post-destruction consumer is proved. Preserve as an
external-lifetime seam, not F274.

V. DISABLED XML BINARY INFO CACHE — CURRENTLY NON-LIVE
------------------------------------------------------
The readInfoArray/writeInfoArray branch in CvGlobals is guarded by ENABLE_XML_FILE_CACHE and
current CvInfo_Base.h defines ENABLE_XML_FILE_CACHE 0. AdvCiv history also records that this
cache was effectively unused for mods. Compilation-repair history for this branch does not make
it a current runtime root.

VI. CAMERA_START_DISTANCE STATIC BASELINE — INTENTIONAL, NOT A CACHE BUG
------------------------------------------------------------------------
The current source comment questions the function-local static
m_fCAMERA_START_DISTANCE_Override. History resolves the intent: the automatic/default-camera
feature deliberately captures the original XML CAMERA_START_DISTANCE before the function starts
overwriting that same GlobalDefine. BUG's "Custom (XML)" option calls updateCameraStartDistance
with bReset=true specifically to restore this captured XML baseline. Re-reading the already
mutated define instead would lose the original custom XML value.

The static is therefore the persistence mechanism for the baseline, not accidental stale caching.
No F274.

C023-WIP06 — QUEUE 040 CvGlobals.cpp — FIXED-GLOBAL-TYPE COUNT RECHECK

- F274 / KI#597: UNUSED.

CONTROL / CORRECTION — FunctionTypes does NOT numerically match GlobalTypes.xml, but this is a stock dormant asymmetry rather than a current SAS defect

The earlier broad fixed-string-array control was too strong when it said that every inherited fixed GlobalTypes count matched its C++ enum. Rechecking the current enum against an independent Civ4CE BtS GlobalTypes.xml exposed one exception:

Current SAS CvEnums.h contains six FunctionTypes:

    FUNC_NOINTERP,
    FUNC_LINKEY,
    FUNC_BEZKEY,
    FUNC_TCBKEY,
    FUNC_EULERKEY,
    FUNC_STEPKEY,

so NUM_FUNC_TYPES is 6 in the DLL build.

CvXMLLoadUtility::SetGlobalTypes() deliberately calls:

    int iEnumVal = NUM_FUNC_TYPES;
    SetGlobalStringArray(&GC.getFunctionTypes(),
            "Civ4Types/FunctionTypes/FunctionType",
            &iEnumVal, true);

With bUseEnum == true, SetGlobalStringArray does not replace iEnumVal with the number of XML nodes. It allocates exactly *iNumVals CvString objects, reads siblings until there are no more, and breaks. Therefore a five-entry FunctionTypes XML section leaves the sixth allocated CvString default/empty rather than overflowing memory.

Independent Civ4CE comparison proves this is not a SAS or AdvCiv regression:
- Civ4CE's stock/BtS CvEnums.h also has the same six FunctionTypes including FUNC_STEPKEY.
- Civ4CE's loader uses the same NUM_FUNC_TYPES + bUseEnum=true loading pattern.
- Civ4CE's BtS GlobalTypes.xml contains only five FunctionType entries: NOINTERP, LINKEY, BEZKEY, TCBKEY and EULERKEY.
- A scan of Civ4CE BtS assets found no STEPKEY / FUNC_STEPKEY reference.

Current SAS evidence is equally non-live:
- The current light-source XML snapshot contains no STEPKEY / FUNC_STEPKEY reference.
- Current C++ references to FUNC_STEPKEY are only the enum declaration itself.
- getFunctionTypes is present in CvGlobals and the CyGlobalContext wrapper, but no current SAS Python caller of getFunctionTypes was found.
- Thus the empty sixth string is not consumed by current repository code/assets, and no current type lookup requires a FUNC_STEPKEY string mapping.
- Commit history shows FUNC_STEPKEY predates SAS and AdvCiv; it is already present in the imported K-Mod/BtS enum lineage.

Disposition:
- Correct the earlier blanket "all fixed counts match" wording: all checked fixed arrays match except this longstanding FunctionTypes 6-enum/5-XML asymmetry.
- Do NOT allocate F274. The actual load is memory-safe, the asymmetry is inherited from stock BtS/Civ4CE, and no current consumer reaches the empty FUNC_STEPKEY slot.
- Keep as latent API/data-contract debt only: a future Python/C++ caller asking GC.getFunctionTypes(FUNC_STEPKEY), or future XML relying on that token through this mapping, would get an empty/unregistered sixth string unless GlobalTypes.xml were extended.

RELATED ASSERT-BUILD CONTROL — duplicate-info-type detection is deliberately/inheritedly _DEBUG-only, but current XML has no trigger

CvGlobals::setInfoTypeFromString contains an additional duplicate-type assertion under #ifdef _DEBUG rather than FASSERT_ENABLE. This superficially resembles F273, but it is not the same SAS regression:
- commit history shows the _DEBUG guard already existed in pre-SAS AdvCiv;
- SAS did not replace an inherited FAssert-visible-in-Assert-build check here;
- the current non-text XML Type scan found 3,869 Type tokens and zero duplicate tokens across files and zero duplicates within a file.
Therefore there is no current duplicate-map overwrite trigger and no independent F274. It remains inherited diagnostic coverage debt if the project ever wants all assertion diagnostics available in the optimized Assert target.

F272 FINAL REPAIR-BOUNDARY CHECK
--------------------------------
Current SAS has N = 128 ColorInfos and the foreign-replay compatibility path accepts foreign
player-color IDs through 254 when HOF_DISPLAY_OTHER_MOD_REPLAYS is enabled. The current remap:

    (eColor + 7) % N

was intended to skip reserved/system colors 0..6 but maps foreign IDs 249..254 to 0..5.

The narrow suffix-domain repair:

    7 + ((eColor - 7) % (N - 7))

for N > 7 was exhaustively compared across the current accepted foreign range 128..254:

    * 121 already-good mappings, IDs 128..248, remain EXACTLY unchanged;
    * only the six bad mappings change:
          249: 0 -> 7
          250: 1 -> 8
          251: 2 -> 9
          252: 3 -> 10
          253: 4 -> 11
          254: 5 -> 12
    * the repaired result range is 7..127, so the promised reserved prefix is actually skipped.

Thus the repair can preserve every current mapping that already satisfied the contract while
correcting only the proven wrap-back cases. Keep a defensive N <= 7 fallback/assert so the
modulo denominator can never become zero or negative in malformed/future data.

F273 FINAL REPAIR-BOUNDARY / SIBLING CHECK
------------------------------------------
Re-proved the project build contract rather than relying on the prior album statement:

    Debug  -> _DEBUG, which causes FAssert.h to enable FASSERT_ENABLE
    Assert -> release-like flags + /DFASSERT_ENABLE, WITHOUT _DEBUG
    Release-> neither assertion mode

Therefore SAS's richer getDefineINT/FLOAT/STRING diagnostics must be guarded by
FASSERT_ENABLE, not _DEBUG, if they are to preserve Base AdvCiv's optimized Assert-build
coverage.

The already-closed queue-041 CvSelectionGroupAI::AI_update has the same SAS regression root.
Its rich stuck-loop diagnostic can also be guarded by FASSERT_ENABLE, but its
`iMaxAttempts += 4` must remain under _DEBUG because it compensates an earlier _DEBUG-only
`iMaxAttempts -= 4`.

A useful independent in-tree model is CvGame::updateMoves:

    int iMaxUnitUpdateAttempts = 18;
    FAssertMsg(...);              // assertion remains available in Assert
    #ifdef _DEBUG
        iMaxUnitUpdateAttempts += 4; // Debug-only behavioral adjustment
    #endif

This is exactly the separation the CvSelectionGroupAI sibling needs.

A targeted repository-wide scan of assertions near _DEBUG/custom SAS diagnostic blocks found
no second SAS replacement of an inherited always-assert-capable check beyond the already-known
CvGlobals and CvSelectionGroupAI cases. Other hits were inherited Debug-only invariant sweeps
or deliberately SAS-added diagnostic probes that have no Base assertion contract to preserve.
The inherited CvGlobals::setInfoTypeFromString duplicate-type assertion is also _DEBUG-only,
but it predates SAS and current XML contains no duplicate Type trigger; it remains diagnostic
coverage debt, not F273 ancestry and not F274.

FINAL HIGH-FANOUT CONTROLS / REJECTIONS
---------------------------------------
1. GlobalDefine mutation and caches
   Every current literal setDefineINT/FLOAT/STRING path was matched against CvGlobals caching.
   MINIMAP_RENDER_SIZE receives the intended targeted integer-cache update; river generation
   controls are uncached and read directly; current camera/FoV float mutations refresh the
   float cache or deliberately defer and then refresh it. No current stale-cache path survived.

   WAR_SUCCESS_CITY_CAPTURING is clamped to >=1 during full caching because 0 can crash AI,
   while a hypothetical targeted runtime setter would bypass that clamp. Current repository
   code has no such setter, so this is latent API robustness debt, not F274.

2. Type/info maps and current XML
   A current non-text XML scan found 3,869 <Type> tokens and zero duplicate tokens, both within
   individual files and across files. The fixed GlobalTypes string categories likewise contain
   no current cross-category duplicate token that would silently overwrite m_typesMap.

3. FunctionTypes count correction
   The earlier blanket statement that every fixed GlobalTypes count matches its C++ enum was
   corrected. FunctionTypes has six C++ values including FUNC_STEPKEY but stock/current XML has
   five strings. Civ4CE independently reproduces the same six-enum/five-XML contract and the
   same NUM_FUNC_TYPES loader behavior. The sixth CvString remains default-empty safely, and
   neither current SAS nor CE assets/code use FUNC_STEPKEY. Longstanding dormant stock contract
   debt; no F274.

4. Direction / animation string accessor shapes
   getDirectionTypes takes AutomateTypes instead of DirectionTypes, a genuine copy/paste API
   mismatch, but there is no current indexed DLL/Python caller exposing it. AnimationOperator
   constants start at 1001 while the string accessor operationally expects a 0-based array index;
   current CyGlobalContext passes ordinary indices and no C++ caller passes real 1001+ constants.
   Both remain latent API defects rather than current roots.

5. Footstep audio
   getFootstepAudioTypeByTag is badly named but correct. Unit-art RunLoopSoundTag/RunEndSoundTag
   values such as LOOPSTEP_TANK are FootstepAudioTypes tokens; the resulting index is then used
   to fetch the parallel actual sound-script tag such as AS3D_LOOPSTEP_TANK.

6. CvAgents ownership
   CvGlobals::init allocates m_agents and uninit does not delete it. CvAgents retains player/team
   pointers, so this is a real shutdown ownership leak/stale-pointer object. However, no local
   same-loaded-DLL second init or post-uninit consumer could be established. Without the EXE
   lifecycle proof needed to turn it into a live re-entry failure, it stays cleanup debt.

7. cacheGlobals / CvPythonCaller / XML-loader lifetime
   cacheGlobals allocates m_pPythonCaller without first deleting an existing one, and CvGlobals
   retains a raw CvXMLLoadUtility pointer for lazy loading. Both are potentially dangerous under
   an undocumented repeated EXE bootstrap/reload cycle, but current DLL source does not prove
   that cycle. CvXMLLoadUtility's own destructor history explicitly discusses EXE ownership and
   double-deletion risk. Do not infer a root from external lifecycle speculation.

8. Lazy throne-room sequencing
   AdvCiv advc.003v deliberately introduced the lazy-load call specifically in exported
   getNumThroneRoomInfos(), with the comment "Load it as late as possible." LoadThroneRoomInfo
   atomically loads camera, room and style arrays and guards repeat loading with bThroneRoomLoaded.
   Other exported room/style accessors do not independently force the load, so this relies on the
   known EXE enumeration order. No current DLL-side caller violates that order and this exact
   sequencing is the original AdvCiv design; keep as an external-engine contract, not F274.

9. Main-menu / landscape exported bounds
   getMainMenus repairs a saved index >= current menu count because switching to a mod with fewer
   menu backgrounds is the known producer. It does not repair a negative index, but current UI
   producers emit valid nonnegative indices and the Python wrapper checks both bounds. Negative
   handling would harden corrupted/external profile input; no current producer was found.

   setActiveLandscapeID has no local bounds check and the derived plot-cell getters index by the
   active ID. It is EXE-owned state with no DLL setter caller; no invalid current producer was
   proved. Add an assertion if desired for robustness, but not as F274.

10. Plot-group FAStar
    getPlotGroupFinder contains an advc.test FError and lazily initializes geometry once, which
    initially raised stale-map-size concerns. AdvCiv explicitly marks it unused inside the DLL
    after CvPlotGroup::recalculatePlots stopped using it. No current internal consumer exists;
    exported legacy contract only, so no live stale-geometry root.

11. XML binary cache
    The binary info-cache read/write machinery is behind ENABLE_XML_FILE_CACHE == 0 in current
    SAS. Historical compile fixes for the branch do not make it a current runtime issue.

12. Camera baseline
    The function-static CAMERA_START_DISTANCE override is intentional: it preserves the original
    XML baseline while runtime camera logic overwrites the GlobalDefine, enabling the BUG
    "Custom (XML)" reset. Treating the static as stale and replacing it with repeated define reads
    would destroy the very baseline it is meant to preserve.

13. History / independent implementation scan
    AdvCiv repair streams touching CvGlobals were challenged for adjacent misses: async-random
    memory corruption/type ownership, startup audio EVENT_MESSAGE_TIME caching, optional/throne
    assertion-variable compile fixes, XML-info refactors/cache compilation, invalid menu-profile
    guard, camera evolution and replay compatibility. K-Mod/Civ4CE comparisons did not expose an
    additional surviving current root. The normalized SAS-vs-Base semantic delta in CvGlobals is
    tiny; beyond F273 it is predominantly comments/formatting rather than a broad SAS rewrite.

F274 / provisional KI#597
-------------------------
TITLE: USE_DO_GOODY_CALLBACK can null-dereference when a goody hut is removed by plot ownership

CURRENT CODE ROOT
-----------------
CvPythonCaller::doGoody accepts a nullable unit pointer:

    bool CvPythonCaller::doGoody(CvPlot const& kPlot, CvUnit const* pUnit,
        PlayerTypes ePlayer) const

and its own adjacent comment explicitly preserves the old contract:

    // Note: pUnit can be NULL, but pyUnit can still be initialized (and is expected by Python).

but current AdvCiv/SAS then does:

    CyUnit* pyUnit = new CyUnit(*pUnit);

Dereferencing pUnit is undefined/crashing when pUnit == NULL.

LIVE NULL CALLER
----------------
This is not merely a misleading nullable signature. CvPlot::setOwner still contains a live call:

    if (isOwned())
    {
        if (isGoody())
            GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).doGoody(this, NULL);
        ...
    }

CvPlayer::doGoody immediately calls the wrapper before ordinary hut handling:

    if (GC.getPythonCaller()->doGoody(*pPlot, pUnit, getID()))
        return;

Therefore, when USE_DO_GOODY_CALLBACK is enabled, an owned goody plot that reaches this
ownership path invokes CvPythonCaller::doGoody with NULL and crashes while constructing the
CyUnit Python wrapper. Typical exposure is a goody hut being absorbed/removed through plot
ownership or culture rather than being entered by a unit.

CONFIGURATION / SEVERITY BOUNDARY
---------------------------------
Current Assets/XML/PythonCallbackDefines.xml sets:

    USE_DO_GOODY_CALLBACK = 0

so stock SAS defaults do not execute the bad dereference. This remains a real supported callback
configuration defect rather than a default-game crash: the define exists specifically to enable
this Python override, and enabling it exposes the live NULL caller immediately when the
ownership-hut path occurs.

ANCESTRY / INDEPENDENT CONTROL
------------------------------
K-Mod 1.46 uses the safe nullable-pointer form directly in CvPlayer::doGoody:

    CyUnit kGoodyUnit(pUnit);

CyUnit has a pointer constructor:

    CyUnit::CyUnit(CvUnit* pUnit) : m_pUnit(pUnit) {}

so NULL is a deliberate representable Python-wrapper state.

AdvCiv practical 2066, commit ffe04c3efd, is titled "Avoid some const_casts". Its CvPythonCaller
change is exactly:

    - CyUnit* pyUnit = new CyUnit(const_cast<CvUnit*>(pUnit));
    + CyUnit* pyUnit = new CyUnit(*pUnit);

The surrounding comment saying pUnit can be NULL was left unchanged. Thus the root is narrowly
identified: a const-cast cleanup replaced the nullable pointer constructor with the reference
constructor and broke the preserved NULL contract. Current Base AdvCiv 1.14 still contains the
same regression; SAS inherits it unchanged.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
The repair must preserve both existing modes:

1. non-NULL unit: Python receives a CyUnit wrapper for that unit;
2. NULL unit: Python still receives a CyUnit Python object whose internal unit pointer is NULL,
   matching BtS/K-Mod and the explicit comment/contract.

The smallest historical repair is to restore the pointer constructor (requiring the old
const_cast because the wrapper stores CvUnit*), e.g. the exact pre-2066 form. An alternative
without dereferencing NULL is to explicitly choose default/null CyUnit construction for the NULL
case and the reference constructor for non-NULL. Do not "fix" this by refusing the callback when
pUnit is NULL; that would change the inherited Python callback contract on the ownership path.

ROOT INDEPENDENCE
-----------------
F274 is independent of queue-040 F272/F273. It is a nullable Python-wrapper construction
regression in AdvCiv's callback refactor/const cleanup, not replay-color arithmetic or assertion
build gating.

EARLY QUEUE-037 CONTROLS / COVERAGE
-----------------------------------
- Normalized SAS-vs-Base AdvCiv semantic delta in CvPythonCaller.cpp is very small. The current
  substantive SAS changes are already-reviewed repairs such as the int AI_foundValue contract,
  riverValue hybrid/default handling and minStartingDistanceMod lower-bound restoration.
- The four central call(...) overloads initialize m_bLastCallSuccessful on both the module-missing
  and actual-call paths; no stale-success carryover was found in those wrappers in this opening
  pass.
- The F274 trigger is not inferred from the signature alone: the live CvPlot::setOwner NULL caller,
  current callback define, CyUnit constructors, K-Mod predecessor and precise AdvCiv regression
  commit were all checked locally before promotion.

NEXT CURSOR
-----------
Continue queue 037 from F275 unused / provisional KI#598 next. Audit all Python-object wrapper
constructions for nullable/lifetime mismatches; then callback result/default semantics,
isOverride/pythonUsingDefaultImpl state, exceptional or missing-function paths, random-event
object mutation, map-script vector/enum bounds, and practical-history sibling regressions.

F275 / provisional KI#598
-------------------------
TITLE: CvPythonCaller::canBuild rejects positive Python override values above 1 despite the
       inherited callback contract

CURRENT CODE
------------
CvPythonCaller::canBuild contains the preserved contract comment:

    "Returning -1 means ignore; 0 means Build cannot be performed; 1 or greater means it can"

but after handling -1 it does:

    bOverride = true;
    FAssertBounds(-1, 2, lResult);
    return toBool(lResult);

CvPythonCaller::toBool is:

    static bool toBool(long l) { FAssert(l >= 0); return (l == TRUE); }

Therefore a valid positive callback result such as 2 has two wrong consequences:

- Assert DLL: FAssertBounds(-1, 2, 2) fires because the upper bound is exclusive;
- Release DLL: the assertion disappears, but toBool(2) returns false because 2 != TRUE (1).

The wrapper thus interprets 2+ as "cannot build" even though its own inherited contract says
1 or greater means the build can be performed.

PRE-REFACTOR / K-MOD CONTROL
----------------------------
The practical-1648 source immediately before extraction into CvPythonCaller used:

    long lResult = 0;
    callFunction(..., "canBuild", ..., &lResult);
    if (lResult >= 1)
        return true;
    else if (lResult == 0)
        return false;

Current K-Mod 1.46 retains the same >= 1 interpretation. Civ4CE's stock BtS CvGameUtils.py also
documents the same callback contract: -1 ignore, 0 deny, 1 or greater allow.

ANCESTRY
--------
The mismatch was introduced directly by AdvCiv practical 1648 (commit 553b1a0f8d, "Moved
DLL-to-Python calls and logging into separate classes"). The new wrapper copied the correct
contract into a comment but immediately narrowed it to {-1,0,1} through FASSERT_BOUNDS and then
used the exact-one helper. Base AdvCiv 1.14 still contains the regression; SAS inherits it.

CONFIGURATION BOUNDARY
----------------------
USE_CAN_BUILD_CALLBACK is 0 in current SAS defaults, as are all 54 callback defines cached by
CvPythonCaller. The defect becomes live when the supported canBuild callback is enabled and the
Python override returns a positive value greater than 1. This is therefore configuration-gated,
not a default-gameplay regression.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
Preserve all three documented states:

    -1      -> no Python override; continue C++ canBuild logic
     0      -> Python override denies build
    >= 1    -> Python override allows build

A narrow repair should therefore return lResult >= 1 once lResult != -1 and remove/relax the
incorrect exclusive upper-bound assertion. Do not change CvPythonCaller::toBool globally on the
strength of this finding: several other inherited callbacks historically used exact == 1, and
queue 037 is auditing those contracts individually rather than assuming one universal Python
truthiness convention.

ADDITIONAL CONTROLS
-------------------
- The callback-define table itself is internally complete: all 54 DO_FOR_EACH_CALLBACK_DEFINE
  entries have exactly one matching USE_*_CALLBACK integer define in current
  PythonCallbackDefines.xml. Eight additional USE_* event callbacks belong to the separate
  CvDllPythonEvents path, so they are not omissions from this table. All 62 current callback
  defines are 0 by default.
- K-Mod controls show that many UI callbacks really did use exact == 1, so the existence of
  CvPythonCaller::toBool is not itself enough to report a broad defect. F275 is promoted because
  canBuild has a specific explicit >= 1 contract and direct pre-refactor comparison.
- `updateColoredPlots` is the only wrapper-local `long lResult;` without initialization. Its
  Python function is expected to exist and the pre-refactor K-Mod code also depended on a
  successful call after setting the local result to 0. Current uninitialized-on-Python-error
  behavior is being retained as an error-path robustness lead, not yet F276.

NEXT CURSOR
-----------
Continue from F276 unused. Highest-value active checks:
- doPillageGold's negative/error sentinel versus K-Mod's old `lPillageGold < 0` fallback;
- callback call-failure defaults and uninitialized return storage;
- random-event mutable EventTriggeredData and pointer-output refresh consistency;
- map-script `isOverride()`/usingDefaultImpl and result validation;
- history commits that fixed post-1648 callback regressions, looking for unfixed siblings.

F275 SAME-ROOT SIBLING EVIDENCE
-------------------------------
The exact-one narrowing introduced by practical 1648 is not limited to canBuild. The two map
placement callbacks were also moved behind CvPythonCaller::toBool by the same refactor:

    CvPythonCaller::canPlaceBonusAt -> canPlaceItemAt
    CvPythonCaller::canPlaceGoodyAt -> canPlaceItemAt

Current canPlaceItemAt validates only negativity and then does:

    if (lResult < 0)
    {
        ...
        bOverride = false;
        return false;
    }
    return toBool(lResult);

Before practical 1648, both CvMapGenerator callbacks did this directly:

    if (result >= 0)
        return result;

where the function return type is bool. C++ therefore treated every nonzero positive long as
true. Practical 1648 replaced that implicit nonzero truth conversion with toBool(result), which
returns true only for exactly 1. Hence a custom map callback that historically returned 2 (or
another positive integer) changes from true to false after the refactor.

This is recorded as SAME-ROOT SUPPORT for F275 rather than a new finding. The canBuild case is the
strongest proof because its Python documentation explicitly says "1 or greater"; the canPlace*
case has direct predecessor behavior but no equally explicit current Python contract. Current SAS
ships only one script defining those hooks, Planet_Generator_0_68.py, and it delegates to the
default implementation rather than returning a custom positive integer, so no shipped default
trigger was found. The evidence nevertheless confirms that toBool cannot safely be assumed to
preserve every pre-refactor callback contract.

F276 / provisional KI#599
-------------------------
TITLE: Enabled doPillageGold callback suppresses the inherited C++ gold fallback on negative or
       failed Python results

CURRENT CODE ROOT
-----------------
CvPythonCaller::doPillageGold initializes a distinct error sentinel but returns true whenever the
callback define is enabled:

    int const iError = MIN_INT;
    ARGSLIST(iError);
    ...
    call("doPillageGold", argsList, lResult);
    ...
    if (lResult != iError)
        iPillageGold = toInt(lResult);
    else FAssert(lResult != iError);
    return true;

Its caller in CvUnit treats the wrapper's bool as "Python supplied the pillage result":

    int iPillageGold = 0;
    if (!GC.getPythonCaller()->doPillageGold(*this, kPlot, iPillageGold))
    {
        // K-Mod C++ fallback calculation
        ...
    }

Consequences when USE_DO_PILLAGE_GOLD_CALLBACK is enabled:

1. Python returns -1 (or any other negative value except MIN_INT): the wrapper copies the negative
   value to iPillageGold and returns true. The C++ fallback is skipped; the later `> 0` test then
   awards no pillage gold.
2. The Python call fails and leaves the MIN_INT initializer unchanged: the wrapper asserts in an
   assertion build but still returns true. In Release, iPillageGold remains the caller's 0 and the
   C++ fallback is again skipped, yielding no pillage gold.

PRE-REFACTOR / K-MOD CONTRACT
------------------------------
The practical-1648 diff shows the exact displaced K-Mod logic:

    long lPillageGold = -1;
    int iPillageGold = -1;
    if (GC.getUSE_DO_PILLAGE_GOLD_CALLBACK())
    {
        ... callFunction(..., &lPillageGold);
        iPillageGold = (int)lPillageGold;
    }
    if (lPillageGold < 0)
    {
        // K-Mod. C version of the original python code
        ... calculate pillage gold in C++ ...
    }

Thus negative values were explicitly the fallback state, not merely an accidental result of a
particular Python implementation. Initialization to -1 also meant a failed/no-result Python call
fell through to the C++ calculation.

The stock BtS/Civ4CE CvGameUtils.doPillageGold implementation returns an ordinary nonnegative gold
amount, so default Python does not intentionally exercise the negative sentinel. The regression is
therefore a callback/error-path compatibility defect, not a default-config gameplay problem.
Current SAS sets USE_DO_PILLAGE_GOLD_CALLBACK = 0 by default.

SIBLING CONTROL: captureGold PRESERVES ITS ERROR FALLBACK
---------------------------------------------------------
The same practical-1648 refactor created CvPythonCaller::captureGold with an almost identical
MIN_INT sentinel, but that wrapper correctly distinguishes failure:

    if (lResult != iError)
    {
        iCaptureGold = toInt(lResult);
        return true;
    }
    else FAssert(lResult != iError);
    return false;

Its caller performs the C++ capture-gold calculation when false is returned. This sibling design
supports the interpretation that doPillageGold's unconditional `return true` is an accidental
loss of fallback semantics rather than an intentional policy that callback enablement must suppress
C++ fallback after Python failure.

ANCESTRY
--------
The root is introduced directly by AdvCiv practical 1648 (commit 553b1a0f8d), which extracted the
old CvUnit Python call into CvPythonCaller. Later AdvCiv history moves/reformats the pillage caller
but does not repair CvPythonCaller::doPillageGold's result contract. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current
SAS retain it.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
Preserve the inherited and current successful modes:

- callback disabled -> return false so C++ computes pillage gold;
- callback enabled and Python returns a valid nonnegative amount -> write it, return true;
- callback enabled but Python returns a negative sentinel or the call fails -> return false and
  leave iPillageGold untouched so the existing C++ fallback runs.

A narrow repair can therefore treat `lResult < 0` as "no valid Python amount" and return false.
That naturally includes the MIN_INT call-failure initializer and restores K-Mod's old any-negative
fallback. Do not blindly clamp negative Python results to zero; zero is a valid explicit override
meaning no pillage gold, while a negative result historically requested/defaulted to C++ logic.

ROOT INDEPENDENCE
-----------------
F276 is independent of F274's nullable CyUnit construction and F275's positive-boolean narrowing.
It is a lost fallback/sentinel contract in the output-valued pillage callback, though all three
were exposed by auditing the practical-1648 extraction boundary.

ADDITIONAL CONTROLS / COVERAGE
-------------------------------
- History grep found no later CvPythonCaller doPillageGold repair after practical 1648; later
  commits touching the call site reorganize CvUnit pillaging but retain the wrapper contract.
- `captureGold` provides an internal same-refactor control showing that an output callback can and
  should return false when its Python result remains at an error sentinel.
- `updateColoredPlots` still has an uninitialized `long lResult` unlike the pre-refactor `= 0`;
  this remains a separate failure-path robustness lead, not folded into F276 without further
  sibling/error-contract review.

NEXT CURSOR
-----------
Continue from F277 unused / provisional KI#600 next. Highest-value active checks:
- determine whether updateColoredPlots's uninitialized result is an isolated failure-path defect
  or part of a wider practical-1648 default-initialization regression;
- systematically compare all map-script callback result/default/override semantics against the
  pre-1648/Civ4CE implementations, especially enum and pointer-return outputs;
- audit random-event mutable EventTriggeredData copy-back and output-pointer refresh contracts;
- inspect central call(...) exception/missing-module behavior and callback recursion guards;
- use later AdvCiv callback-fix commits (1662, 1677, 1850, 1917, 1966, 2460, 2531, 2571) as
  repair-boundary probes for unfixed siblings.

F277 / provisional KI#600
-------------------------
TITLE: CvPythonCaller::addFeatures falsely asserts when a valid map script omits the optional
       Python hook and falls back to C++ feature generation

CURRENT CODE ROOT
-----------------
Most optional map-generation phase wrappers explicitly suppress call-success assertions because
absence of the Python override is a normal signal to run the inherited C++ implementation:

    bool CvPythonCaller::addBonuses() const
    {
        call("addBonuses", m_python.getMapScriptModule(), false);
        return isOverride();
    }

    bool CvPythonCaller::addGoodies() const
    {
        call("addGoodies", m_python.getMapScriptModule(), false);
        return isOverride();
    }

    bool CvPythonCaller::addLakes() const
    {
        call("addLakes", m_python.getMapScriptModule(), false);
        return isOverride();
    }

    bool CvPythonCaller::addRivers() const
    {
        call("addRivers", m_python.getMapScriptModule(), false);
        return isOverride();
    }

But addFeatures uniquely leaves the default bAssertSuccess=true:

    bool CvPythonCaller::addFeatures() const
    {
        call("addFeatures", m_python.getMapScriptModule());
        return isOverride();
    }

The central no-result call wrapper does:

    m_bLastCallSuccessful = m_python.callFunction(...);
    FAssert(!bAssertSuccess || m_bLastCallSuccessful);

Thus a selected map module that simply omits addFeatures produces an assertion in an
assertion-enabled DLL even though `isOverride()` then correctly returns false and
CvMapGenerator::addFeatures continues with the normal C++ fallback.

LIVE CURRENT SAS TRIGGER
------------------------
Current SAS ships 50 PrivateMaps scripts. A direct current-data scan finds exactly one without a
`def addFeatures(` callback:

    PrivateMaps/SAS_Simple_Flat_Grass.py

This is not an accidental empty/broken script. It is a deliberately minimal playable SAS map
wrapper. Its only wildcard import is SAS_WorldSizeUtils, whose exported functions are world-size
helpers and do not define addFeatures. Therefore selecting this current map script reaches the
missing-hook path.

The practical consequence is build-dependent:

- Debug / Assert DLL: the missing optional hook makes m_bLastCallSuccessful false and triggers the
  FAssert in CvPythonCaller::call;
- Release DLL: the assertion is absent; isOverride() is safely false and CvMapGenerator performs
  its inherited C++ feature placement as intended.

This is therefore a false-positive diagnostic/assertion regression on a supported current SAS map,
not a Release-gameplay failure.

PRE-REFACTOR CONTRACT
---------------------
Immediately before practical 1648, CvMapGenerator::addFeatures used:

    if (gDLL->getPythonIFace()->callFunction(mapModule, "addFeatures", NULL))
    {
        if (!gDLL->getPythonIFace()->pythonUsingDefaultImpl())
            return;
    }
    // C++ feature generation follows

A missing/failed Python function therefore did not assert; it simply left the function in the C++
fallback path. Practical 1648 replaced that block with:

    if (GC.getPythonCaller()->addFeatures())
        return;

and the newly extracted wrapper accidentally retained call()'s assertion-on-success default.

INTERNAL / HISTORY CONTROL
--------------------------
The neighboring addBonuses/addGoodies/addLakes/addRivers wrappers created in the same extraction
all pass `false`, matching their optional/fallback nature. This makes addFeatures the local outlier.

AdvCiv practical 1662 provides an independent meaning-of-the-flag control: it explicitly changed
applyEvent to pass `false` because “Many of the apply functions named in XML don't exist.” That
history confirms callFunction failure for a missing Python function is exactly the condition the
bAssertSuccess parameter is meant to tolerate when absence is valid.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 currently bundles eight PrivateMaps scripts and all eight define addFeatures, so
the inherited wrapper bug is latent under Base's shipped map set. SAS's new minimal map script
makes the defect live without changing CvPythonCaller itself.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
Make addFeatures consistent with the other optional map phase hooks:

    call("addFeatures", m_python.getMapScriptModule(), false);

Do not force SAS_Simple_Flat_Grass.py to define a dummy function merely to satisfy the wrapper;
omitting the hook is an inherited valid way to request/default to C++ generation. Preserve
isOverride()/pythonUsingDefaultImpl behavior for scripts that do implement addFeatures.

ROOT INDEPENDENCE
-----------------
F277 is separate from F273. F273 accidentally removes legitimate assertions from the optimized
Assert build by gating richer diagnostics with `_DEBUG`; F277 is the opposite kind of diagnostic
contract error: it emits an assertion on a valid optional-callback fallback. The repairs and code
roots are independent.

ADDITIONAL RANDOM-EVENT CONTROL
-------------------------------
The doEventTrigger pointer-output refresh was rechecked against practical 1648 and later practical
1966 (“Fix recently introduced bug in random event processing”). Practical 1966 added guards for
invalid city/unit IDs. Its pOtherPlayerCity assignment can leave the pre-call pointer unchanged
when Python changes the other-city ID to INVALID_INDEX, whereas pre-1648 getCity(-1) would normally
clear it. Current shipped random-event Python was searched for mutations of the actual triggered
data. Several callbacks mutate city/player/plot fields, but no current can-trigger callback was
found that changes an initially valid other-player-city ID to -1. Keep this as a mutation/output
consistency control, not F278 at present.

NEXT CURSOR
-----------
Continue from F278 unused / provisional KI#601. Revisit updateColoredPlots's uninitialized
failure result; audit all map enum/index return bounds and missing/default behavior; then move
through event mutation, ordinary callback return sentinels and later practical-history repairs.

F278 / provisional KI#601
-------------------------
TITLE: CvPythonCaller::updateColoredPlots consumes an uninitialized Python result when the
       callback call fails, losing the inherited deterministic C++ fallback

CURRENT CODE ROOT
-----------------
CvPythonCaller::updateColoredPlots is the only function in the current file that declares a bare
uninitialized result variable:

    bool CvPythonCaller::updateColoredPlots() const
    {
        long lResult;
        call("updateColoredPlots", lResult);
        return toBool(lResult);
    }

The central call wrapper records Python call success separately:

    m_bLastCallSuccessful = m_python.callFunction(..., &lResult);
    FAssert(!bAssertSuccess || m_bLastCallSuccessful);

and CvDLLPythonIFaceBase exposes callFunction as a bool-returning interface with an output pointer;
there is no DLL-side contract that the output is written when the call returns false. Therefore,
if Python fails before producing a long result, updateColoredPlots still evaluates the untouched
stack value through toBool().

The behavior depends on build/error handling:

- Debug / Assert: the central FAssert reports the failed call, but if execution continues/Ignore is
  chosen then the indeterminate result is still consumed;
- Release: the assertion vanishes and the uninitialized value is consumed immediately. It can
  spuriously return true and skip all inherited C++ colored-plot generation, or false by accident.

This is undefined behavior in C++, not merely an arbitrary fallback choice.

PRE-REFACTOR / K-MOD CONTROL
----------------------------
Immediately before AdvCiv practical 1648 extracted this callback, CvGame::updateColoredPlots used:

    long lResult = 0;
    gDLL->getPythonIFace()->callFunction(PYGameModule,
            "updateColoredPlots", NULL, &lResult);
    if (lResult == 1)
        return;

Thus a failed/no-result Python call deterministically left zero in place and continued into the
normal C++ colored-plot implementation. Current K-Mod 1.46 retains that same `lResult = 0`
initialization, and BUG's current default for updateColoredPlots is false, matching the fallback.

ANCESTRY
--------
The bug is introduced directly by AdvCiv practical 1648 (553b1a0f8d, "Moved DLL-to-Python calls
and logging into separate classes"). The same commit removes `long lResult = 0` from
CvGameInterface.cpp and creates CvPythonCaller::updateColoredPlots with `long lResult;`.
Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains the regression; SAS inherits it unchanged.

TRIGGER / SEVERITY BOUNDARY
---------------------------
The normal SAS PYGameModule and CvGameInterface.updateColoredPlots function exist, and BUG supplies
an ordinary false default, so normal successful calls do not exercise the bad value. The live
trigger is a Python call failure/exception/no-result path (for example while developing/reloading
Python or after a script error). updateColoredPlots is invoked repeatedly by ordinary UI/game
state changes, so once the Python side is broken the path is reachable without special XML callback
enablement.

This is therefore best classified as an error-path robustness/undefined-behavior regression rather
than a default healthy-script gameplay defect. It is still stronger than a mere assertion issue:
Release builds can make a control-flow decision from indeterminate storage.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
Restore the inherited false/default state locally:

    long lResult = false; // or = 0

before the call. Do not attempt to solve this by globally changing call() to overwrite all output
arguments on failure; other wrappers intentionally use distinct sentinels such as MIN_INT, -1,
NO_TECH and caller-provided defaults. updateColoredPlots simply needs its own historical default
restored.

ROOT INDEPENDENCE
-----------------
F278 is independent of F274-F277. It is an uninitialized-output regression on Python call failure,
not nullable wrapper construction (F274), numeric boolean-contract narrowing (F275), lost negative
fallback sentinel (F276), or optional map-hook assertion policy (F277).

ADDITIONAL CONTROL
------------------
A file-wide declaration scan found no second bare `long lResult;` in current CvPythonCaller.cpp.
All other ordinary long-result wrappers initialize through ARGSLIST(default) or explicit sentinel/
default variables. Therefore F278 is a localized extraction omission, not evidence that every
callback return is uninitialized on failure.

NEXT CURSOR
-----------
Continue from F279 unused / provisional KI#602. Audit map-script enum/index/vector return bounds and
hybrid/default semantics; then random-event mutable output refresh, ordinary callback sentinel/
truthiness contracts, and later practical-history fixes. Keep malformed-script-only bounds issues
as controls unless current SAS assets or a supported fallback path make them live.
