F285 / provisional KI#608
-------------------------
TITLE
AI_stopTradingTrade checks only the AI team's own gives-list for BOTH the peace treaty and annual
reparations, so a normal one-sided saved treaty on the opposite list can make the AI accept an
embargo it cannot actually fulfill.

CURRENT DENIAL CODE
-------------------
CvPlayerAI::AI_stopTradingTrade contains the AdvCiv reparations safeguard:

    // Avoid canceling reparations
    if (GET_TEAM(getTeam()).isForcePeace(eTradeTeam))
    {
        FOR_EACH_DEAL(d)
        {
            if (!d->isBetween(getTeam(), eTradeTeam))
                continue;
            bool bPeaceTreaty = false;
            bool bAnnualPayment = false;
            FOR_EACH_TRADE_ITEM(d->getGivesList(getTeam()))
            {
                TradeableItems eType = pItem->m_eItemType;
                if (eType == TRADE_PEACE_TREATY)
                    bPeaceTreaty = true;
                if (eType == TRADE_RESOURCES ||
                    eType == TRADE_GOLD_PER_TURN)
                {
                    bAnnualPayment = true;
                }
            }
            if (bPeaceTreaty && bAnnualPayment)
                return DENIAL_RECENT_CANCEL;
        }
    }

`CvPlayer::getTradeDenial` really uses this for TRADE_EMBARGO:

    case TRADE_EMBARGO:
        return AI().AI_stopTradingTrade((TeamTypes)kTrade.m_iData);

So failure of this check changes whether the AI can agree to a stop-trading request.

LIVE SAVED DEAL ORIENTATION
---------------------------
A normal bilateral peace bundle can contain:
- peace-treaty entries on both incoming offer lists;
- GPT/resources as reparations from one side.

CvDeal processes the first side first. The first TRADE_PEACE_TREATY:
- enables team forcePeace;
- is saved.

When the second peace-treaty item is later processed:
- forcePeace is already active;
- startTrade calls resetDualDeal;
- if that finds the first saved treaty, the duplicate treaty item is not saved.

Thus an ordinary persisted deal can naturally have:
    firstList  = [TRADE_PEACE_TREATY, ...]
    secondList = [TRADE_GOLD_PER_TURN, ...]

or the mirror orientation.

No malformed deal construction is required.

CONCRETE FAILURE
----------------
Choose the orientation where:
- the AI is the SECOND player/team;
- the saved peace treaty is in the FIRST list;
- the AI pays GPT reparations in the SECOND list.

Then:
- `d->isPeaceDeal()` is already true even under current unfixed F281, because the treaty happens to
  be in firstList;
- `d->getGivesList(getTeam())` for the AI sees the GPT reparations but NOT the treaty;
- AI_stopTradingTrade therefore fails to set bPeaceTreaty and does NOT return DENIAL_RECENT_CANCEL.

Now suppose the AI also has any other ordinary cancellable trade with the embargo target
(e.g. a resource trade established separately). That makes:
    canStopTradingWithTeam(target) == true
and TRADE_EMBARGO can be offered.

If the AI accepts:
- the broker/requester gets the accepted-stop-trading diplomatic outcome;
- the target receives the corresponding hired-embargo memory;
- CvPlayer::stopTradingWithTeam executes.

But stopTradingWithTeam deliberately preserves peace deals:

    if (... && !pLoopDeal->isPeaceDeal() && !pLoopDeal->isDisengage())
        pLoopDeal->kill();

Therefore:
- the unrelated resource deal is canceled;
- the peace+GPT reparations deal is deliberately NOT canceled;
- the AI keeps paying the target despite having agreed/rewarded the request to stop trading.

This is the exact inconsistency the reparations safeguard exists to prevent.

HISTORY / REGRESSION PROOF
--------------------------
The safeguard was introduced by advc.130f, practical count 1383 / commit d4fd8b6277.
The original code explicitly examined both trade lists while determining whether a peace deal
contained annual reparations.

A later traversal refactor (practical count 1626) converted that to the old combined
headTradesNode()/nextTradesNode() traversal, still covering BOTH lists and allowing the
peace-treaty item and annual item to reside on opposite sides of the same deal.

During practical-count 2998's list-interface refactor, the combined traversal was replaced with:

    FOR_EACH_TRADE_ITEM(d->getGivesList(getTeam()))

This changed the semantic domain from "all items in this deal" to "only items given by the AI team."
The peace marker can live on the opposite side, so the representation invariant was lost.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 inherits this regression.

RELATION TO F281
----------------
F285 is independent of F281.

The concrete orientation above deliberately puts the treaty in FIRST list, so current
CvDeal::isPeaceDeal() already returns true:
- stopTradingWithTeam correctly preserves the reparations deal;
- only the AI denial precheck is wrong.

Fixing F281 does not fix F285 because AI_stopTradingTrade still scans only the AI gives-list for
the treaty marker.

Conversely, fixing F285 does not repair F281's second-list treaty expiry bug.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
The intended modern condition is more precise than simply restoring the old combined "any annual
item anywhere" scan.

The reason for denial is:
    "I am currently obliged to GIVE annual reparations under a peace treaty to the embargo target."

Therefore for each deal between the teams:
1. detect the peace treaty anywhere in the deal (both saved lists, or `d->isPeaceDeal()` after F281
   is fixed);
2. inspect the AI team's own gives-list for:
       TRADE_RESOURCES
       TRADE_GOLD_PER_TURN
3. if both conditions hold, return DENIAL_RECENT_CANCEL.

Conceptually:

    bool bPeaceTreaty = scanBothListsForPeace(*d); // or fixed d->isPeaceDeal()
    if (!bPeaceTreaty)
        continue;

    FOR_EACH_TRADE_ITEM(d->getGivesList(getTeam()))
    {
        if (pItem->m_eItemType == TRADE_RESOURCES ||
            pItem->m_eItemType == TRADE_GOLD_PER_TURN)
        {
            return DENIAL_RECENT_CANCEL;
        }
    }

This:
- handles treaty marker on either side;
- refuses only when the AI itself owes annual reparations;
- does not unnecessarily refuse because the OTHER side pays GPT/resources.

If implementation is deliberately independent of F281, scan both lists locally for the peace item.

ROOT INDEPENDENCE
-----------------
F285 root:
    reparations embargo-denial lost whole-deal treaty visibility during list-interface refactor.

Independent of:
- F281 deal classification/expiry;
- F282 memory accumulation;
- F283 renewal ownership;
- F284 player-death/team-proxy ownership.

ADDITIONAL CONTROLS FROM THIS SLICE
-----------------------------------
1. Empty persistent deal / CvDeal::doTurn head dereference:
   REJECTED. CvGame::implementAndReturnDeal checks both saved list lengths after addTradeItems.
   If both are empty it immediately kills the deal and returns NULL. Ordinary one-shot/rejected
   bundles do not survive as empty CvDeals.

2. Team-proxy implementation-time attitude/value multiplication:
   REJECTED. AI_processTradeValue calls AI_dealVal(..., bIgnoreAnnual=true), and OB/DP/disengage/
   vassal proxy items are annual for that calculation. Pure dual deals are also suppressed in
   CvDeal::doTurn. MxN proxy count does not multiply ordinary trade-history value.

3. Resource verify `< 0`:
   CLEAN. After one exported copy is consumed, zero can be a valid "last copy is being exported"
   state. Negative indicates oversubscription/lost source and is the proper cancellation threshold.

4. Permanent Alliance mixed-bundle reentrancy:
   BELOW BUG BAR. AI-generated PA offers are PA-only and current PA legality requires one-member
   teams. Human/EXE mixed-bundle behavior is not locally established strongly enough for F286.

5. First-list cleanup siblings in CvTeam::addTeam / CvTeam::setVassal:
   remain representation debt/control. No independent state consequence stronger than F281/F283
   established.

F283 SAME-ROOT EXPANSION — practical 2658 vote-prolongation proves all team proxies must share age
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Practical count 2658 explicitly added the `bProlong` paths to Open Borders and Defensive Pact so
diplomatic votes can reset the turns before those agreements become cancelable.

Current CvGame::processVote:

    if (kVote.isOpenBorders())
        itFirst->signOpenBorders(itSecond->getID(), true);
    if (kVote.isDefensivePact())
        itFirst->signDefensivePact(itSecond->getID(), true);

CvTeam::signOpenBorders / signDefensivePact call implementDeal using the two TEAM LEADERS. Their
startTrade paths contain:

    if (isOpenBorders(...))
    {
        if (kFromPlayer.resetDualDeal(eToPlayer, TRADE_OPEN_BORDERS))
            break;
    }

and the analogous DP path.

But the persistent OB/DP representation is an MxN set of player-pair proxy deals created by
startTeamTrade for every living member pair. resetDualDeal:
- searches only deals between the two leader players;
- scans only the first list;
- resets only the first matching proxy;
- then returns under the source assumption "at most one deal of eDealType."

For a multi-member team agreement, that assumption is false by construction.

Consequently a vote intended to "prolong the Open Borders / Defensive Pact agreement" resets only
the leader-leader proxy. Other proxies retain their older initial turns. Once one older proxy is
cancelable, canceling it can endTeamTrade the entire logical agreement even though the diplomatic
vote intended to refresh its minimum duration.

This is especially strong F283 evidence because practical 2658 is the feature that introduced the
renewal helper for OB/DP. The current player-pair implementation cannot fulfill that feature's
team-level intent on multi-member teams.

F283 repair contract therefore remains:
- locate the logical TEAM agreement;
- inspect both saved lists;
- update every proxy deal that owns the same team-level OB/DP lifetime, or replace proxy-local ages
  with one logical agreement age;
- for peace, locate the treaty across the two teams rather than one particular player pair.

A both-list-only patch remains incomplete.


F284 SAME-ROOT EXPANSION — PEACE_TREATY has the same player-owner/team-state mismatch, but no proxy fallback
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WIP05 proved the clean proxy-backed failure for OB/DP/DISENGAGE:
individual player death calls killAllDeals even while teammates survive, and deleting one proxy
clears team-level state plus kills surviving proxies.

TRADE_PEACE_TREATY has the same ownership mismatch:
- forcePeace is stored on CvTeam;
- the treaty timer/lifetime is stored in a CvDeal owned by two Players;
- unlike OB/DP, peace is normally represented by ONE saved treaty item rather than an MxN proxy set.

If the player owning that treaty dies while his team still has living members:
- setAlive(false) calls killAllDeals;
- endTrade(TRADE_PEACE_TREATY) unconditionally calls setForcePeace(..., false);
- the surviving teammate's team therefore loses the rest of the temporary peace period early.

This is the same conceptual F284 root:
    an individual-player deal lifetime is allowed to destroy team-level diplomatic state even
    though the participant team itself survives.

However its minimal repair differs from proxy-backed agreements.

For OB/DP/DISENGAGE:
- surviving member-pair proxy deals remain, so defeat cleanup can simply avoid team-wide teardown
  and let the surviving proxies continue owning the state.

For PEACE_TREATY:
- the dying player's deal may be the ONLY timer-bearing owner.
- merely skipping setForcePeace(false) and deleting the deal would leave forcePeace with no treaty
  left to expire it later.

Therefore a complete F284 repair should either:
1. re-home/migrate the surviving treaty duration to a deal between living members of the same two
   teams before deleting the dead player's deal; or
2. move temporary-peace lifetime ownership to team-level state independent of a particular
   player's CvDeal.

Do not patch peace by merely adding the OB/DP death guard.

The live consequence strengthens F284 but does not justify a separate F286: both cases arise from
the same player-object ownership being used to control team-object state during individual defeat.


REVIVAL / NEWLY ALIVE MEMBER — CONTROL
--------------------------------------
A revived player on an already-living team does not need a new proxy merely to USE existing
team-level Open Borders / Defensive Pact / Disengagement:
- the actual permission/state flags live on CvTeam;
- revived player units inherit those team relations immediately.

The absence of a newly materialized player-pair proxy can affect who carries cancellation age and
how later renewal/cancellation is represented. That is already F283's logical-team-agreement versus
player-proxy lifetime problem, not an independent root.

No separate F286 from revival.


EMPTY DEAL / TURN PROCESSING — CONTROL
--------------------------------------
CvDeal::doTurn dereferences firstList.head() in its pure-dual fast-path condition, which initially
looked unsafe for an empty persistent CvDeal.

The allocation wrapper closes that path:
CvGame::implementAndReturnDeal calls addTradeItems, then if BOTH saved lists are empty it
immediately kills the deal and returns NULL.

One-shot-only bundles and rejected/blocked bundles therefore do not survive as empty CvDeals into
the turn loop. No F286.


PROXY TRADE-VALUE MULTIPLICATION — CONTROL
-------------------------------------------
startTeamTrade creates MxN proxy CvDeals, but implementation-time AI trade-value accounting does
not multiply the ordinary attitude value per proxy:
- AI_processTradeValue uses AI_dealVal(..., bIgnoreAnnual=true);
- OB / DP / disengagement / vassal items are treated as annual for this purpose and skipped;
- CvDeal::doTurn separately skips pure one-item dual deals.

No F286.

F286 / provisional KI#609
-------------------------
TITLE
A human mixed Permanent Alliance + city/implied-peace bundle can delete the CvDeal from inside
CvDeal::addTradeItems and then CvGame::implementAndReturnDeal immediately dereferences the freed
pointer.

SUPPORTED TRIGGER
-----------------
Current CvPlayer::updateTradeList explicitly says:

    if (!isHuman() || !GET_PLAYER(eOtherPlayer).isHuman())
        ...
        // mixed annual/nonannual items restricted
    // everything allowed in human-human trades

Permanent Alliance is a normal inventory item when:
- GAMEOPTION_PERMANENT_ALLIANCES / PA trading is available;
- both teams are non-vassals, at peace, distinct;
- both teams currently have exactly one member.

A non-liberation city offer at peacetime is one of the current items that implies temporary peace.
Current updateTradeList therefore appends explicit TRADE_PEACE_TREATY entries to BOTH human offer
lists for display/implementation:

    TradeData item(TRADE_PEACE_TREATY);
    ...
    item.m_iData = eForcePeaceItemType;
    apOffersVar[i]->insertAtEnd(item);

Thus a supported human-human bundle can contain, for example:
- first side: city + permanent alliance + appended peace treaty;
- second side: appended peace treaty
(or equivalent orientation/order supplied by the trade screen).

No malformed direct-DLL call is needed.

EXECUTION CHAIN
---------------
CvGame::implementAndReturnDeal:

    CvDeal* pDeal = addDeal();
    pDeal->init(...);
    pDeal->addTradeItems(kOurList, kTheirList, !bForce);
    if (pDeal->getLengthFirst() <= 0 && pDeal->getLengthSecond() <= 0)
    {
        pDeal->kill();
        return NULL;
    }
    return pDeal;

Inside addTradeItems:

1. Trade items are processed before the Permanent Alliance merge.

2. The first explicit TRADE_PEACE_TREATY encountered:
       setForcePeace(..., true);
       bSave = true;
   and is inserted into the current CvDeal's saved list.

3. When the opposite-side peace-treaty item is later processed, forcePeace is already true.
   resetDualDeal can find the just-created current deal and the already-saved treaty, so the
   duplicate treaty normally is not saved. The current deal nevertheless contains at least one
   saved TRADE_PEACE_TREATY.

4. TRADE_PERMANENT_ALLIANCE itself sets:
       bAlliance = true
   and is not saved.

5. After both item loops:
       if (bAlliance)
           GET_TEAM(...).addTeam(...);

CvTeam::addTeam reassigns the absorbed team's players into the surviving team and then iterates
deals that are now internal to the merged team:

    if (!pLoopDeal->isBetween(getID(), getID()))
        continue;

    FOR_EACH_TRADE_ITEM(pLoopDeal->getFirstList())
    {
        if (eType == TRADE_OPEN_BORDERS ||
            eType == TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT ||
            eType == TRADE_PEACE_TREATY ||
            ...)
        {
            pLoopDeal->kill();
            break;
        }
    }

The currently executing CvDeal now has:
- both players on the same merged team;
- a saved first-list peace treaty.

Therefore addTeam can call `kill()` on the very `this` whose addTradeItems stack frame is active.

IMMEDIATE DELETION / UAF PROOF
------------------------------
CvDeal::kill -> killSilent -> GC.getGame().deleteDeal(getID()).

CvGame::deleteDeal:
    m_deals.removeAt(iID);

FFreeListTrashArray::removeAt:
    SAFE_DELETE(m_pArray[iIndex].pData);

So the CvDeal object is actually destroyed before CvTeam::addTeam returns.

CvDeal::addTradeItems then returns through a member function whose `this` is already freed.
Even if its final bBumpUnits block happens not to dereference members in the concrete path, the
caller unconditionally does:

    pDeal->getLengthFirst()
    pDeal->getLengthSecond()

immediately after addTradeItems returns.

That is an unambiguous use-after-free.

ANCESTRY
--------
The dangerous interaction is AdvCiv-specific.

Practical count 2691 / commit 195785f015f5e71cffa4b6c52e2307ad8cc08a94:
    "Show implied peace treaties on the trade table"

added explicit PEACE_TREATY entries to human-visible offers for city/war items that imply temporary
peace. Its own comment says that, for deals involving humans, the game will attempt to implement
the treaty twice and considers that harmless.

Before that display change, the underlying city trade could merely set an internal
`bPeaceTreatyImplied`/sign-treaty path; a PA bundle takes the `bAlliance` branch and does not
materialize an explicit saved treaty that addTeam's internal-deal cleanup can recognize.

Practical 3275 later deferred implied-treaty signing until all bundle items had been applied to
avoid two unilateral treaties, but explicit treaty items added by the human trade table remain
processed/saved before the PA merge. It does not close this self-deletion path.

K-Mod/Civ4CE do not contain AdvCiv's same implied-peace-display mechanism in this form, so they do
not independently reproduce this exact trigger.

WHY CURRENT PREVALIDATION DOES NOT SAVE IT
------------------------------------------
addTradeItems validates each individual item through canTradeItem before applying the bundle.
There is no bundle-level rule forbidding Permanent Alliance + city/explicit implied peace for
human-human trades.

updateTradeList deliberately skips the annual/nonannual combination restriction when both players
are human ("everything allowed in human-human trades").

TRADE_PERMANENT_ALLIANCE canPossiblyTradeItem checks the two teams are single-member BEFORE the
merge; that condition is satisfied at validation time.

So all items can pass individually while their combined execution causes reentrant deletion.

SEVERITY
--------
High when triggered:
- heap object is freed while its method remains active;
- caller immediately dereferences the dangling CvDeal*;
- outcome can be crash, assertion, allocator-dependent corruption or apparently surviving stale
  memory depending on build/runtime.

The trigger is specialized (human-human PA enabled + mixed implied-peace bundle) but uses supported
trade-screen mechanics.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
The core invariant should be:

    CvTeam::addTeam must not delete the CvDeal that is currently implementing the Permanent Alliance
    until addTradeItems / implementAndReturnDeal have completed using that object.

Evidence-supported repair shapes include:

1. Preferred transaction/order repair:
   - do not persist an explicit implied peacetime PEACE_TREATY inside a deal that also executes a
     Permanent Alliance, because after the teams merge the treaty is meaningless anyway;
   - still display it to humans if needed, but suppress its saved lifetime when PA is in the same
     bundle.

2. Deferred cleanup:
   - let addTeam identify internal deals for cleanup but defer deletion of the currently executing
     deal until implementAndReturnDeal is done with it.

3. Bundle pre-normalization:
   - strip/ignore redundant PEACE_TREATY items from PA bundles before startTrade saves them.

A weak patch such as "don't dereference pDeal after addTradeItems" is insufficient unless ownership
and return semantics are redesigned, because `addTradeItems` itself may continue after deletion and
the function still conceptually returns through a dead `this`.

Do NOT remove all addTeam internal-deal cleanup: stale OB/DP/vassal/etc. agreements between newly
same-team players still need normalization.

ROOT INDEPENDENCE
-----------------
F286 is independent of F281-F285.

It is a reentrant object-lifetime/use-after-free bug caused by:
- explicit implied treaty materialization in a PA bundle;
- addTeam's internal-deal cleanup;
- immediate free-list deletion;
- post-call use of the CvDeal pointer.

It reproduces even if:
- F281 both-list peace classification is fixed;
- F282 memory accumulation is fixed;
- F283 team-level renewal is fixed;
- F284 player-death ownership is fixed;
- F285 embargo reparations detection is fixed.

CONTROLS / CAVEATS
------------------
- A pure PA offer does not save any item in the implementing CvDeal and is safely discarded as an
  empty deal after the merge.
- PA + ordinary one-shot items without an explicit saved internal team-state item do not
  automatically trigger this exact self-delete path.
- The strongest current trigger is PA + non-liberation city, because updateTradeList itself inserts
  explicit peace treaty items for human-visible implied peace.

F287 / provisional KI#610
-------------------------
TITLE
Automatic invalidation of one annual item kills the entire mixed peace deal, so a broke GPT payer
can terminate the mandatory peace treaty before PEACE_TREATY_LENGTH expires.

CURRENT CODE
------------
CvDeal::verify:

    if (!verify(getFirstPlayer(), getSecondPlayer()) ||
        !verify(getSecondPlayer(), getFirstPlayer()) ||
        (isCancelable(NO_PLAYER) && isPeaceDeal()))
    {
        kill();
    }

The directional helper checks persistent annual items regardless of deal age.

For GPT:

    if (pItem->m_eItemType == TRADE_GOLD_PER_TURN)
    {
        if (kGiver.getCommercePercent(COMMERCE_GOLD) >= 100 &&
            kGiver.getGold() < pItem->m_iData && !kGiver.isAnarchy() &&
            kGiver.calculateGoldRate() < 0)
        {
            return false;
        }
    }

A false result kills the entire CvDeal immediately.

If that same persistent deal also contains TRADE_PEACE_TREATY, kill -> endTrade processes the
treaty and executes:

    GET_TEAM(eFromPlayer).setForcePeace(TEAMID(eToPlayer), false);

There is no independent remaining-turn field inside CvTeam::forcePeace; `isForcePeace` is simply
the stored team boolean. The CvDeal is the timer/lifetime owner.

SUPPORTED MIXED DEAL
--------------------
GPT is explicitly tradeable during war/peace negotiation:
- TRADE_GOLD_PER_TURN canPossiblyTradeItem only requires gold trading;
- canTradeItem itself accepts any nonnegative GPT amount;
- it does not require an existing peacetime trade network.

Human peace settlements can therefore legitimately contain:
    TRADE_PEACE_TREATY + TRADE_GOLD_PER_TURN reparations

in one persistent CvDeal.

The first PEACE_TREATY entry is saved as the temporary-peace lifetime item. GPT is also persistent
and saved in the same deal.

FAILURE CHAIN
-------------
Example:
- turn T0: peace signed with 10-turn treaty and 8 GPT reparations;
- T1/T2/... before T0+PEACE_TREATY_LENGTH: payer reaches 100% gold slider, cannot cover the GPT
  payment, is not in anarchy and still has a negative gold rate;
- CvGame::verifyDeals -> CvDeal::verify;
- GPT condition returns false;
- CvDeal::kill executes immediately despite `turnsToCancel() > 0`;
- GPT payment ends;
- TRADE_PEACE_TREATY teardown clears team forcePeace;
- the teams can resume war before the mandatory treaty duration has elapsed.

The normal treaty age protection:

    (isCancelable(NO_PLAYER) && isPeaceDeal())

only governs scheduled treaty expiry. It does NOT protect a peace deal from the earlier
resource/GPT invalidation branches.

ANCESTRY
--------
The general "invalid resource item kills whole deal" architecture is inherited from BtS/K-Mod/
Civ4CE.

The particularly common GPT trigger is AdvCiv-specific.

Practical count 2765 / commit c66c29025a3be4912b019a7b6128889ae07aacac:
    "Force-cancel gold-per-turn deals when broke"

added exactly the GPT false-return block to CvDeal::verify.

The patch did not special-case mixed peace deals or preserve the remaining treaty duration.
Therefore practical 2765 made ordinary GPT peace reparations capable of terminating temporary
peace early.

K-Mod/Civ4CE do not contain this GPT insolvency branch, though their inherited resource-invalid
whole-deal behavior shows the broader structural hazard.

RESOURCE SIBLING
----------------
Resource invalidation has the same whole-deal teardown behavior:
- lost trade network;
- oversubscribed resource;
- obsolete resource.

A resource + peacetime temporary treaty bundle could therefore exhibit the same lifetime problem.
For wartime peace negotiations, resource trading is often unavailable because canTradeNetworkWith
fails while enemies are at war, so GPT is the cleaner supported/default reproduction.

Treat resource invalidation as same-root structural evidence; F287 does not depend on proving a
wartime resource reparations case.

WHY THIS IS NOT NORMAL CANCELLATION
-----------------------------------
Manual cancellation is intentionally blocked while:
    turnsToCancel() > 0.

The GPT verify branch bypasses isCancelable entirely. So this is not simply "the payer is allowed
to cancel because insolvent." The engine itself tears down an uncancelable treaty as a side effect
of an annual payment failure.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
When an individual annual component of a deal becomes impossible during an uncancelable peace
period, the temporary peace lifetime must survive.

Possible evidence-supported designs:

1. Remove/end only the invalid annual item from the deal while retaining TRADE_PEACE_TREATY and its
   original initial turn.

2. If deal-level killing is retained, immediately re-home/recreate the treaty with the exact
   remaining duration before clearing forcePeace.

3. Split peace treaty lifetime from annual-payment deal lifetime when the bundle is implemented.

For the narrow GPT repair:
- cancel the impossible GPT obligation;
- do not clear temporary peace before its existing expiry.

Do NOT merely skip GPT verification while peace is active if that would leave an impossible payment
continuing indefinitely. The payment and the treaty have different failure/lifetime semantics.

ROOT INDEPENDENCE
-----------------
F287 is independent of F281-F286.

Even with:
- correct both-list isPeaceDeal;
- correct renewal;
- correct team-member death ownership;
- correct reparations embargo denial;
- no PA self-deletion;

an insolvent GPT component can still make `verify()` kill the whole still-young peace deal.

F286 SAME-ROOT EXPANSION — vassalization can self-delete the active transaction too
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WIP08 proved a high-confidence self-deletion path through Permanent Alliance.

The same transaction-lifetime invariant is violated by `CvTeam::setVassal(true)` under a supported
human peacetime mixed bundle.

SUPPORTED BUNDLE
----------------
At peacetime:
- human-human diplomacy permits mixed trade classes;
- a non-liberation city offer causes updateTradeList to append explicit PEACE_TREATY entries to
  both offer lists;
- voluntary TRADE_VASSAL is tradeable when neither team is already a vassal and the two sides are
  not at war.

Thus a supported bundle can contain:
    non-liberation city + voluntary vassal + displayed implied peace treaty.

EXECUTION
---------
addTradeItems deliberately processes non-vassal items in pass 0 and vassal items in pass 1.

Therefore before TRADE_VASSAL is executed:
- city transfer has occurred;
- the first explicit PEACE_TREATY has been saved in the current CvDeal.

TRADE_VASSAL then calls:

    startTeamTrade(...);
    GET_TEAM(eFromPlayer).setVassal(eToTeam, true, false);

Inside setVassal(true), current code iterates global deals involving the new vassal and kills
Defensive Pact / Peace Treaty deals whose FIRST list contains such an item:

    FOR_EACH_DEAL_VAR(pLoopDeal)
    {
        ...
        FOR_EACH_TRADE_ITEM(pLoopDeal->getFirstList())
        {
            if (pItem->m_eItemType == TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT ||
                pItem->m_eItemType == TRADE_PEACE_TREATY)
            {
                pLoopDeal->kill();
                break;
            }
        }
    }

The currently executing deal is already in the global free-list container and can satisfy this
test. Its first-list displayed implied treaty was saved before the vassal pass.

`kill()` therefore immediately SAFE_DELETEs the active CvDeal through `deleteDeal/removeAt`, exactly
as in the PA path.

Control then returns to the active `startTrade` / `addTradeItems` stack and ultimately to
implementAndReturnDeal, which dereferences the dangling pDeal pointer.

ROOT CLASSIFICATION
-------------------
Do not allocate F288.

The PA and vassal paths are the same root:
    a state transition invoked while applying a bundle is allowed to synchronously delete the
    CvDeal transaction object that is still executing that bundle.

The exact cleanup walker differs (`CvTeam::addTeam` vs `CvTeam::setVassal`), but the object-lifetime
contract and use-after-free consequence are identical.

This broadens the F286 repair requirement:
- transaction execution must survive all state-transition cleanup it invokes;
- implied/internal treaty normalization cannot synchronously destroy the active transaction.

WAR-BRIBE REENTRANCY CHALLENGE — CLEAN UNDER NORMAL DENIAL
-----------------------------------------------------------
TRADE_WAR calls `CvTeam::declareWar` synchronously, and defensive-pact cascades can themselves
declare additional wars and kill deals. This initially suggested another possible active-transaction
deletion.

A concrete dangerous shape would be:
- B brokers A into declaring war on C;
- B has a Defensive Pact with C;
- C's pact then causes B to declare war on A;
- B-vs-A war cleanup could kill the active A<->B bribe deal.

The trade denial closes the normal path.

`CvTeamAI::AI_declareWarTrade(eTarget=C, eSponsor=B)` begins with:

    if (GET_TEAM(eTarget).isVassal(eSponsor) ||
        GET_TEAM(eTarget).isDefensivePact(eSponsor))
        return DENIAL_JOKING;

TRADE_WAR can only be given by a non-human team through normal trade legality, and addTradeItems
prevalidates with denial checks unless the caller explicitly forces the deal.

Therefore the DP-with-sponsor cascade cannot occur through an ordinary accepted war-bribe deal.
A forced/malformed direct implementation could bypass this, but that is below the finding bar.

No F288.


`doTurn` ONE-ITEM DUAL FAST PATH — CLEAN
----------------------------------------
The condition:

    getLengthSecond() == getLengthFirst() &&
    getLengthSecond() <= 1 &&
    isDual(getFirstList().head()->m_data.m_eItemType)

looks as though it could skip peacetime-value processing based only on the first-side item even if
the second-side item were non-dual.

Current persistence semantics prevent the concerning normal shape:
- initial OPEN_BORDERS / DEFENSIVE_PACT / DISENGAGE items with m_iData<=0 are not saved in the
  initiating mixed deal; they create separate generated team-proxy deals;
- those generated dual proxies contain the same dual item on both sides;
- PEACE_TREATY is saved but `isPeaceDeal()` excludes the whole deal before this shortcut;
- PERMANENT_ALLIANCE is not saved;
- vassal items are not `isDual`.

So the live one-item-each dual case is the intended pure proxy agreement. No hidden GPT/resource
mixed deal is skipped by this shortcut.

No F288.


SMALL METHOD / ACCESSOR FAMILY — CONTROLS
-----------------------------------------
`isVassalTrade`
    whole-list scan; orientation-independent.

`isUncancelableVassalDeal`
    current generated vassal proxy representation gives exactly one vassal/master team side;
    getGivesList(team) contract is satisfied.

`isVassalTributeDeal`
    the static all-resources predicate is vacuously true for an empty list, but the persistent
    instance form cannot become a meaningful empty deal because empty CvDeals are deleted by
    implementAndReturnDeal. No live queue-042 root established.

`isDisengage`
    requires exactly one item on each side and generated disengagement proxies are dual, so the
    first-list head is guaranteed.

`getGivesList/getReceivesList(TeamTypes)`
    assert that exactly one participant belongs to the queried team. Same-team ordinary deals can
    exist after Permanent Alliance, but current team-overload callers first scope deals to two
    distinct relevant teams; no live assertion trigger found.

`isAllDual`
    empty-list true is mathematically vacuous but persistent empty deals are removed immediately;
    display/filter callers therefore see nonempty deals.

`isAnnual/isDual/hasData/isEndWar`
    current callers and trade categories line up with the persistence/valuation semantics examined;
    no omitted current trade enum found.

F287 SAME-ROOT EXPANSION — advc.104m deliberately creates peace+resource/GPT tribute deals
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
WIP09 proved the common supported wartime peace-settlement case:
    TRADE_PEACE_TREATY + TRADE_GOLD_PER_TURN

and showed that practical 2765's broke-GPT verifier can kill the whole still-young deal and thereby
clear temporary forcePeace before PEACE_TREATY_LENGTH.

The history-guided advc.104m pass proves that resource invalidation is not merely a theoretical
structural sibling. AdvCiv deliberately creates PEACETIME help/tribute deals in which an annual
resource can share the same persistent CvDeal with a temporary peace treaty.

HISTORY
-------
Practical count 2070 / commit 507332fd0f introduced:
    "Peace treaty in tribute/help deals; no treaty for vassals."

Its design is explicit:
- at peacetime, CvPlayer::buildTradeTable inserts a hidden TRADE_PEACE_TREATY so the EXE doesn't
  discard the treaty from tribute/help requests;
- AI_askHelp and AI_demandTribute add peace-treaty items to both sides when tradeable;
- the accepted help/tribute bundle is therefore meant to grant a minimum temporary peace period.

Current source preserves this architecture.

CURRENT RESOURCE TRIGGER
------------------------
Current CvPlayerAI::AI_demandTribute supports DEMAND_BONUS.

That branch can insert one or several:
    TradeData(TRADE_RESOURCES, eBonus)

into `humanGives`.

After the requested value is accepted, current code adds:
    weGive      += TRADE_PEACE_TREATY
    humanGives  += TRADE_PEACE_TREATY

when both sides can trade the treaty.

On implementation:
- the first treaty entry is saved as the temporary-peace lifetime owner;
- the demanded resources are persistent and saved in the same CvDeal;
- the duplicate treaty entry is normally collapsed through the existing treaty-reset logic.

The resulting live deal can therefore be:
    peace treaty + one/multiple demanded resources.

If, before the treaty's minimum duration expires, one demanded resource:
- becomes unavailable/oversubscribed;
- loses its trade network;
- becomes obsolete for either side;

CvDeal::verify(direction) returns false for that resource and the OUTER verify kills the ENTIRE
deal.

kill/endTrade then clears TRADE_PEACE_TREATY forcePeace immediately.

Thus a resource promised under an AdvCiv tribute-protected temporary peace can disappear and
prematurely end the very peace guarantee advc.104m added.

CURRENT GPT TRIBUTE SIBLING
---------------------------
AI_demandTribute also supports DEMAND_GOLD_PER_TURN.

That creates exactly the practical-2765 F287 trigger at peacetime:
    demanded GPT + advc.104m temporary treaty.

If the human payer later meets the "100% gold, can't cover payment, negative gold rate, not anarchy"
condition, verify returns false and kills the whole protected tribute deal.

This is independent support for the same root in addition to wartime reparations.

REPAIR IMPLICATION
------------------
F287 should therefore be framed generally:

    Failure of one persistent annual obligation is allowed to destroy a still-uncancelable
    temporary-peace lifetime that shares the same CvDeal.

The correct boundary must preserve the treaty while ending only the failed annual obligation, or
otherwise re-home the exact remaining treaty duration.

This is not a niche wartime-reparations-only problem.


PRACTICAL 1690 PEACE-CANCELLATION ORACLE — CURRENTLY CLEAN
-----------------------------------------------------------
Practical 1690 ("Fix recently introduced bug with peace treaty cancellation") repaired
CvDeal::isCancelable(NO_PLAYER).

The buggy form performed:
    involves(NO_PLAYER)
    isUncancelableVassalDeal(NO_PLAYER)

before calculating age. `verify()` legitimately calls isCancelable(NO_PLAYER) for global
peace-treaty expiry, so that broke expiry.

Current code preserves the fix:
- player-involvement and uncancelable-vassal checks are inside:
      if (eByPlayer != NO_PLAYER)
- then turnsToCancel is evaluated.

`isEverCancelable` is player-specific and all current callers pass a real player.
No new F288 from this history stream.


PRACTICAL 1882 PERMANENT-ALLIANCE ORACLE — CURRENT GUARD PRESERVED
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Practical 1882 ("Fix some recently introduced problems with Perm. Alliances") added an important
same-team guard in `isUncancelableVassalDeal`:

    if (TEAMID(getFirstPlayer()) == TEAMID(getSecondPlayer()))
        return false;

because the team-oriented gives-list helper cannot represent an internal same-team deal.

Current CvDeal preserves that guard.

This does not repair F286: F286 occurs earlier, while addTeam/setVassal synchronously deletes the
active transaction object. But the historical guard confirms that same-team deals can temporarily
survive team merging and that later deal code must be careful with team-oriented accessors.

No independent F288.


PRACTICAL 1997 OPEN-BORDERS ORACLE — CURRENT SENTINEL PRESERVED
---------------------------------------------------------------
Practical 1997 ("Open Borders deals had no effect") corrected team-trade startup tests from:

    trade.m_iData == 0

to:

    trade.m_iData <= 0

after the default TradeData value had changed to -1.

The same correction was applied to:
- TRADE_VASSAL / TRADE_SURRENDER;
- TRADE_OPEN_BORDERS;
- TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT;
- TRADE_DISENGAGE.

Current startTrade still uses the <=0 contract. Generated proxy items use positive m_iData=1 and
therefore save rather than recursively spawn another team trade.

No F288.


PRACTICAL 1577/1578 AI-CANCELLATION ORACLE — CURRENT ORIENTATION API IS COHERENT
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Those consecutive fixes introduced/cleaned the orientation-aware AI cancellation pipeline:
- ensure the deal is actually between the AI and the queried player before cancellation logic;
- derive our/their gives lists using deal orientation;
- treat resource denial specially;
- preserve renegotiation versus outright cancellation.

Current AI_checkCancel uses:
    kDeal.getGivesList(ePlayer)
    kDeal.getGivesList(getID())

after its caller has ensured:
    pLoopDeal->isBetween(getID(), eOther)

and cancellation eligibility.

The old flip/orientation duplication is gone without reintroducing a first-vs-second assumption.
No current list-orientation regression emerged there.


CANCELLATION `bForce` FIRST-LIST DUAL SCAN — REAL SAME-FAMILY DIAGNOSTIC DEBT, NOT F288
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Current CvDeal::kill decides whether cancellation UI should be forced/play the cancellation sound.

For dual items it scans ONLY getFirstList():

    FOR_EACH_TRADE_ITEM(getFirstList())
        if (isDual(...))
            bForce = true;

Resource-network failure is separately checked across both lists.

History proves this was another practical-2998 list-refactor loss:
- before practical 2998, kill used combined headTradesNode()/nextTradesNode(), scanning BOTH lists
  for duals;
- practical 2998 changed the dual test to firstList only, while explicitly preserving both-list
  resource scans.

Therefore a second-list-only peace treaty (normal representation already proved for F281) can be
announced as a non-forced/silent cancellation even though TRADE_PEACE_TREATY is dual.

This is a genuine UI/diagnostic consequence of the same representation/refactor family, but:
- it does not control gameplay state;
- current F281 can prevent the ordinary scheduled expiry of the same second-list treaty in the
  first place;
- when other teardown paths kill it, the main gameplay consequences are already captured by the
  stronger lifetime findings.

Record as repair-adjacent debt. When practical-2998 list-orientation bugs are corrected, restore
dual visibility across both lists here too. Do not allocate F288 merely for notification priority.


SERIALIZATION / FREE-LIST IDENTITY — CLEAN
------------------------------------------
CvDeal::write/read are symmetric:
    ID
    initial game turn
    first player
    second player
    first list
    second list

CvGame serializes the entire `FFreeListTrashArray<CvDeal>` through
Read/WriteStreamableFFreeListTrashArray.

The free-list stream includes:
- slot count;
- last index;
- free-list head/count;
- current ID;
- every next-free index;
- live object count.

Each CvDeal then reloads its serialized ID, and `FFreeListTrashArray::load` places the object back
into the slot encoded by that ID after asserting it is within the serialized container state.

No queue-042 save/load ID drift or "deal list reloads but ID does not" defect found.

AUDIT CORRECTION — F281 was introduced by practical 2623, not practical 2998
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Earlier queue-042 WIPs correctly proved F281's current behavior and repair boundary but attributed
the first-list-only regression too late.

The local reachable-history mirror gives a precise introduction point.

Before practical 2623, current-era AdvCiv's CvDeal::isPeaceDeal used the combined traversal:

    for (CLLNode<TradeData> const* pNode = headTradesNode(); pNode != NULL;
         pNode = nextTradesNode(pNode))
    {
        if (pNode->m_data.m_eItemType == getPeaceItem())
            return true;
    }

`headTradesNode()/nextTradesNode()` were specifically the combined first-then-second deal traversal.

Practical count 2623 / commit 72a2889d97a5962c893a97d778a45622a84b8829
Title:
    "Use CLinkList traversal macros throughout the DLL"

mechanically changed this exact function to:

    FOR_EACH_TRADE_ITEM(getFirstList())
    {
        if (pItem->m_eItemType == getPeaceItem())
            return true;
    }

and thereby silently dropped the second list.

Practical 2998 later carries/repeats the same modern-list form on a merged/divergent history path,
but it is NOT the earliest introduction.

Older ancestry is additionally reassuring:
- before the combined helper simplification, CvDeal::isPeaceDeal explicitly scanned first list and
  then second list;
- practical 1626 simplified those two loops into the combined headTradesNode traversal while
  preserving both-list semantics;
- K-Mod likewise scans both sides.

So the corrected F281 ancestry is:

    BtS/K-Mod/older AdvCiv: both lists
    practical 1626: still both lists, via combined traversal
    practical 2623: traversal-macro conversion accidentally narrows to first list only
    current Base AdvCiv/SAS: inherits that regression

The F281 gameplay proof and repair remain unchanged.


F285 HISTORY REFINEMENT — blind spot existed initially, was fixed, then reintroduced directionally
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Earlier WIP wording over-credited practical 2998 as the source of the AI reparations-embargo
visibility regression. The history is more informative.

1. advc.130f introduction — practical 1383
------------------------------------------
The original "Avoid canceling reparations" safeguard iterated BOTH trade lists, but evaluated each
list separately:

    for each list:
        bPeaceTreaty = false;
        bAnnualPayment = false;
        scan that list;
        if (bPeaceTreaty && bAnnualPayment)
            deny embargo;

Therefore its initial design already missed a deal where:
    peace treaty marker is on one list
    annual payment is on the opposite list.

So the representation hazard existed from the feature's introduction.

2. practical 1618 — blind spot temporarily removed
---------------------------------------------------
Practical 1618 replaced the per-list logic with one combined traversal:

    bPeaceTreaty = false;
    bAnnualPayment = false;
    for (pNode = d->headTradesNode(); pNode != NULL;
         pNode = d->nextTradesNode(pNode))
    {
        ...
    }

Now treaty and annual payment could be detected anywhere in the same deal, including opposite
lists. This temporarily fixed the cross-list correlation problem.

However, that whole-deal test was directionally overbroad: it could also deny the AI merely because
the OTHER side was making an annual payment under the treaty.

3. practical 2574 / commit 3db68c8950b7f878f94ab2965b8c60878b84ea78
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Title:
    "Fix a minor issue with AI refusal of trade embargo"

This changed the combined traversal from:

    d->headTradesNode() / nextTradesNode()

to:

    d->headGivesNode(getTeam()) / nextGivesNode(..., getTeam())

i.e. only items GIVEN BY THE AI.

That correctly made `bAnnualPayment` directional: the AI should refuse because IT owes reparations,
not because the other party does.

But it also made `bPeaceTreaty` directional, even though the peace marker is deal metadata whose
saved side is representational. The opposite-list treaty-marker blind spot was therefore
reintroduced.

A corresponding `getGivesList(getTeam())` conversion appears on the later/divergent traversal-macro
history path (practical 2620), and current Base AdvCiv/SAS retain the gives-side-only form.

Practical 2998 is therefore not the semantic introduction of F285; it only preserves the already
directional traversal in the newer list API.

CORRECT MODERN REPAIR, NOW EXPLAINED BY HISTORY
-----------------------------------------------
The history itself separates the two concepts that current code incorrectly binds to one scan:

- PEACE-TREATY EXISTENCE:
    whole-deal property; inspect both lists / fixed `d->isPeaceDeal()`.

- ANNUAL REPARATION OWED BY THIS AI:
    directional property; inspect `d->getGivesList(getTeam())` for RESOURCES/GPT.

That combines:
- practical 1618's correct whole-deal treaty visibility;
- practical 2574's correct payer-directionality.

This is stronger than simply reverting to any one historical implementation.

F285's current reproduction and independence from F281 remain unchanged:
choose an orientation with treaty in first list and AI GPT in second list; current isPeaceDeal
already sees the treaty, while AI_stopTradingTrade fails its own denial.


RELATED CANCELLATION bForce LINEAGE — CONTROL ONLY
---------------------------------------------------
The cancellation-notification `bForce` dual-item scan has a similar traversal history but remains
below the numbered-finding bar.

- advc.106j originally used first-list-oriented logic.
- practical 1626 broadened the dual/resource traversal to the combined headTradesNode sequence.
- practical 2623 converted the dual detection back to first-list-only while separately preserving
  resource-network checks across both lists.

So a normal second-list-only peace treaty can again be missed by the "force cancellation
notification/sound" classification.

That is real diagnostic/UI debt and should be considered alongside F281's list repair, but it does
not independently corrupt diplomatic state. Keep it unnumbered unless a stronger gameplay
dependency is established.

F288 / provisional KI#611
-------------------------
TITLE
A supported human Permanent Alliance + voluntary-vassal mixed bundle can make the surviving team
its OWN vassal (`m_eMaster == getID()`), leaving persistent team-state corruption.

SUPPORTED BUNDLE / PREVALIDATION
--------------------------------
Current diplomacy deliberately allows arbitrary mixed item classes when BOTH players are human:

    if (!isHuman() || !GET_PLAYER(eOtherPlayer).isHuman())
    {
        ... annual/nonannual hiding ...
    }
    // "everything allowed in human-human trades"

The trade inventory independently exposes both:
    TRADE_VASSAL
    TRADE_PERMANENT_ALLIANCE

when their ordinary individual conditions hold.

At peacetime between two separate one-member free teams:
- TRADE_VASSAL can pass because neither side is already a vassal and vassal-state trading is
  available;
- TRADE_PERMANENT_ALLIANCE can pass because neither side is a vassal, the teams are distinct and
  at peace, PA trading is available, and each team has one member.

`updateTradeList` has special mutual hiding for:
- vassal vs the OTHER side's vassal item;
- wartime vassal/surrender vs an end-war item;

but there is no PA-vassal incompatibility rule.

`CvDeal::addTradeItems` then validates every item while the two teams are still separate. Thus both
items can pass the bundle's prevalidation.

EXECUTION ORDER
---------------
The two-pass implementation intentionally postpones vassal/surrender items.

TRADE_PERMANENT_ALLIANCE:
- processed in pass 0;
- startTrade itself does nothing;
- `bAlliance = true`.

TRADE_VASSAL:
- processed in pass 1;
- startTeamTrade creates the ordinary team-vassal proxy deal(s);
- `GET_TEAM(eFromPlayer).setVassal(eToTeam, true, false)` establishes the vassal relation.

Only AFTER both item passes does addTradeItems execute the alliance:

    if (bAlliance)
    {
        if (eFirstTeam < eSecondTeam)
            GET_TEAM(eFirstTeam).addTeam(eSecondTeam);
        else if (eSecondTeam < eFirstTeam)
            GET_TEAM(eSecondTeam).addTeam(eFirstTeam);
    }

The lower team ID survives the Permanent Alliance.

CONCRETE CORRUPTION ORIENTATION
-------------------------------
Let:
    Team M = lower-ID surviving team
    Team V = higher-ID absorbed team

and let V give TRADE_VASSAL to M in the same bundle that contains the PA.

Immediately before addTeam:
    V.m_eMaster == M
    M.m_eMaster == NO_TEAM

Then:
    M.addTeam(V)

reaches AdvCiv's optimized single-master PA migration:

    if (GET_TEAM(eTeam).isAVassal())
    {
        bool bCapitulated = GET_TEAM(eTeam).isCapitulated();
        setVassal(getMasterTeam(), false, bCapitulated);
        setVassal(GET_TEAM(eTeam).getMasterTeam(), true, bCapitulated);
    }

Substitute the live values:

1. Survivor M is free, so:
       M.getMasterTeam() == M

2. First call:
       M.setVassal(M, false, ...)

   `M.isVassal(M)` is false while m_eMaster==NO_TEAM, so the early equality check sees:
       false == false
   and returns immediately. This does NOT clear anything.

3. Absorbed V's master is M:
       V.getMasterTeam() == M

4. Second call:
       M.setVassal(M, true, ...)

   This proceeds and writes:
       M.m_eMaster = M

The surviving team has become its own vassal.

WHY THE SELF-VASSAL DOES NOT SELF-CORRECT
-----------------------------------------
`setVassal(M,true)` updates the Agent caches as a real vassal relation, including inserting Team M
into the VASSAL_ALIVE cache for master M.

Its later "all our vassals now become free" loop can encounter the self relation. However
`freeVassal(M)` frees vassalage by finding and killing an actual TRADE_VASSAL/SURRENDER deal between
master M and vassal M.

At that point the real vassal proxy is still between distinct player teams M and V; there is no
M<->M vassal deal. Therefore `freeVassal(M)` does not clear M.m_eMaster.

The same loop subsequently frees the real V->M proxy relation, but that changes V's master state,
not M's newly-created self-master state.

Later, V's players are reassigned to M. V's alive count falls to zero.

CvTeam::changeAliveCount(0) frees living teams whose:
    kLoopTeam.isVassal(V)

But M now has:
    M.m_eMaster == M

not V. Therefore absorbed-team death cleanup also does not clear the self-vassal.

There is no later `m_eMaster = NO_TEAM` normalization in addTeam.

The corrupted state survives the merge.

MIRROR ORIENTATION — IMPORTANT BOUNDARY
----------------------------------------
If instead the LOWER-ID survivor was the vassal of the HIGHER-ID absorbed master immediately before
the PA:
    survivor.m_eMaster == absorbedTeam

the `GET_TEAM(eTeam).isAVassal()` branch is skipped because the absorbed master is free.

When absorbedTeam later reaches alive-count zero, CvTeam::changeAliveCount sees the survivor as a
living vassal of the dead absorbed team and calls:
    survivor.setVassal(absorbedTeam, false, ...)

So that mirror orientation happens to clean up.

F288 is therefore orientation-dependent on team IDs and which side gives voluntary vassalage, but
the bad orientation is fully supported and deterministic.

LIVE CONSEQUENCES
-----------------
Self-vassal is not cosmetic.

`isAVassal()` is:
    return (m_eMaster != NO_TEAM);

so it becomes true.

`getMasterTeam()` returns:
    m_eMaster == NO_TEAM ? getID() : m_eMaster

and therefore still returns M, hiding the corruption from some equality tests while the vassal flag
remains set.

Examples of broad consequences:
- CvTeam::canChangeWarPeace immediately returns false when `isAVassal()`;
- many diplomatic/trade gates reject vassals;
- population/land functions with vassal-aware accounting take the `isAVassal()` branch and can
  halve the team's own totals in those contexts;
- AI/iterator predicates classify the team as a vassal;
- CvAgents' VASSAL_ALIVE relation cache contains the team under itself;
- the relation is ordinary CvTeam state and is serialized, so the corruption can survive saves.

Additional downstream behavior may be worse, but these are already sufficient to establish a live
state bug.

ANCESTRY
--------
The human-human "everything allowed" mixed-trade behavior is inherited from K-Mod.

K-Mod's older vassal representation used a per-team boolean relation matrix. Its PA merge logic
iterated OTHER teams and explicitly excluded both merging team IDs while migrating vassal
relations. A direct vassal relation between the two teams being merged therefore was not converted
into a self-vassal relation.

AdvCiv later replaced the relation matrix with a single `m_eMaster`.

Practical count 1840 / commit 8cd5a498cfb33f035393333903c604d49410673c
Title:
    "Bugfixes: Vassals of Permanent Alliance; AgentIterator"

introduced the current single-master PA migration block:

    if (GET_TEAM(eTeam).isAVassal())
    {
        ...
        setVassal(getMasterTeam(), false, bCapitulated);
        setVassal(GET_TEAM(eTeam).getMasterTeam(), true, bCapitulated);
    }

This correctly handles an absorbed team that is vassal of some THIRD master, but it does not
special-case the master being the very team that is absorbing it.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 contains the same logic; SAS inherits it.

ROOT INDEPENDENCE
-----------------
F288 is independent of F281-F287.

It requires neither:
- list-orientation peace classification;
- cancellation-memory accumulation;
- deal-renewal lifetime;
- player-death proxy ownership;
- embargo reparations detection;
- active-deal self-deletion;
- annual-item verification.

Its root is bundle-level compatibility plus PA vassal-state migration:
    individually valid PA + vassal items create a transient direct master/vassal relation between
    the two teams immediately before those same teams merge.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
The cleanest repair is to reject/normalize the contradictory bundle BEFORE either state transition:

    A Permanent Alliance and a VASSAL/SURRENDER relation between the same two teams should not both
    be implemented as independent items in one transaction.

Possible approaches:
1. bundle validation:
   reject PA+VASSAL/SURRENDER combinations;
2. normalization:
   if PA is present, ignore/drop direct vassal/surrender items between the merging teams;
3. defensive addTeam hardening:
   when absorbed team's master is `getID()`, do NOT call `setVassal(getID(), true)`;
   likewise explicitly clear any direct survivor<->absorbed vassal relation before merge.

A robust repair should ideally do both:
- prevent contradictory trade construction;
- make addTeam resilient to an externally forced/directly constructed equivalent state.

Do not merely add `FAssert(eMaster != getID())` to setVassal: Release would still corrupt state, and
other legitimate callers should not have to absorb a malformed PA transaction after the fact.

- Static `isVassalTributeDeal(empty)` is vacuously true, but its AI_considerOffer call path requires
  positive received value from the tested list; an empty list cannot satisfy that gate. Persistent
  empty CvDeals are deleted immediately. No live empty-list trigger.
- Normal TRADE_PEACE / TRADE_WAR / TRADE_EMBARGO trade-table target generation excludes the
  negotiating partner's team and uses a third-team iterator. Ordinary brokered state changes
  therefore do not target the active deal partner and synchronously delete the active broker deal.
- Random-event BonusGift implementDeal calls currently come from Brothers In Need triggers whose
  other-player-war requirement is false; those resource gifts therefore occur at peacetime and do
  not bypass the SAS wartime victory-denial peace guard.

  signPeaceTreaty likewise supplies PEACE_TREATY; OB/DP/disengage and voluntary-vassal direct paths
  are peacetime. No normal wartime implementDeal route without the guard's treaty marker was found.
- PA + resource/GPT can leave a persistent deal between now-same-team players, but players retain
  separate gold/resource economies; no independent corruption was established from that alone.

F289 / PROVISIONAL KI#612
=========================
VOLUNTARY VASSAL SPONSOR CAN HIRE AN AI TO DECLARE WAR ON THE SPONSOR'S OWN
MASTER / SAME-MASTER COALITION, IMMEDIATELY MAKING THE SPONSOR AN ENEMY OF THE
HIRED TEAM

SUMMARY
-------
The brokered-war trade contract checks the relationship between the HIRELING and
the proposed target, but incompletely checks the relationship between the
SPONSOR and that target.

`CvTeamAI::AI_declareWarTrade(eTarget,eSponsor,...)` rejects:

    GET_TEAM(eTarget).isVassal(eSponsor)
    GET_TEAM(eTarget).isDefensivePact(eSponsor)

but does not reject the reverse master/vassal direction:

    GET_TEAM(eSponsor).isVassal(eTarget)

nor, more generally, a target in the sponsor's own master/vassal locus.

That leaves a supported live configuration in which a voluntary vassal asks an
AI civ to declare war on the vassal's own master. The requested declaration
then invokes the normal vassal-alignment cascade, which causes the hired AI to
declare war on the sponsor as well.

The accepted diplomatic transaction therefore destroys the diplomatic
relationship it was negotiated through and turns the sponsor into an enemy of
the team it just hired.

This is an independent diplomatic target-validity defect.

It ALSO provides a new concrete trigger for F286: the nested war declaration
kills the current sponsor/hireling CvDeal while `CvDeal::addTradeItems` is still
executing, after which `CvGame::implementAndReturnDeal` can dereference the
freed deal. That lifetime consequence remains under F286 rather than being
double-counted here.

LIVE CONSTRUCTION
-----------------
Let:

    A = AI hireling team
    B = voluntary-vassal sponsor team
    C = B's master team

Initial state:

    B.isVassal(C) == true
    B.isCapitulated() == false
    A is at peace with B and C
    A has met B and C
    A can otherwise declare war on C
    attitudes / power allow A to accept B's war request

B opens diplomacy with A and asks:

    A: declare war on C

This is not an artificial direct-C++ construction. Current trade-table and
trade-validity code can expose/accept it.

TRADE-TABLE REACHABILITY
------------------------
For an AI player, `CvPlayer::buildTradeTable` handles TRADE_PEACE, TRADE_WAR and
TRADE_EMBARGO by iterating every major third team except:

    - the AI's own team, through NOT_SAME_TEAM_AS;
    - the negotiating partner's exact team, through:

          if (itThirdTeam->getID() == TEAMID(eOtherPlayer))
              continue;

If B is a voluntary vassal of C, C is a distinct third team.

Therefore C is enumerated as a possible TRADE_WAR target while A negotiates
with B.

There is no corresponding exclusion for:

    itThirdTeam->getMasterTeam() == GET_TEAM(B).getMasterTeam()

so the sponsor's own master remains a candidate.

STRUCTURAL TRADE VALIDITY
-------------------------
`CvPlayer::canPossiblyTradeItem(... TRADE_WAR ...)` rejects the sponsor only
when the sponsor is CAPITULATED:

    return (!kOurTeam.isHuman() && !kOurTeam.isAVassal() &&
            !kToTeam.isCapitulated());

Here:
- kOurTeam = A, the AI hireling;
- kToTeam = B, the sponsor.

B is a voluntary vassal, not capitulated, so the broker role remains allowed.

Current SAS `CvPlayer::canTradeItem(... TRADE_WAR ...)` then checks the TARGET:

    bool const bValidTargetStatus =
        (!kTargetTeam.isAVassal() ||
         (getUWAI().isEnabled() && !kTargetTeam.isCapitulated()));

    if (bValidTargetStatus &&
        kOurTeam.isHasMet(eTargetTeam) &&
        kToTeam.isHasMet(eTargetTeam) &&
        kOurTeam.canDeclareWar(eTargetTeam))
    {
        bValid = true;
    }

For target C, the sponsor's FREE master:
- C is not a vassal, so target status passes even without UWAI;
- A and B naturally know C in the relevant configuration;
- A canDeclareWar(C) can be true.

Nothing here checks that B and C belong to the same master/vassal coalition.

AI DENIAL IS ASYMMETRIC
-----------------------
`CvPlayer::getTradeDenial(TRADE_WAR)` routes to:

    kOurTeam.AI_declareWarTrade(eTarget, TEAMID(eWhoTo))

so A evaluates C as target and B as sponsor.

The opening special relationship check is:

    if (GET_TEAM(eTarget).isVassal(eSponsor) ||
        GET_TEAM(eTarget).isDefensivePact(eSponsor))
        return DENIAL_JOKING;

For target C and sponsor B:
- `C.isVassal(B)` is false;
- master/vassal is not represented as a defensive pact;
- the REVERSE fact `B.isVassal(C)` is never tested.

The remainder of AI_declareWarTrade can therefore return NO_DENIAL when
attitude, war-load and power conditions are favorable.

This is not merely a trade-table cosmetic: the AI can genuinely accept.

WHY `canDeclareWar(C)` DOES NOT SAVE THE CONTRACT
-------------------------------------------------
`CvTeam::canDeclareWar(C)` answers whether A itself can legally enter war
against C.

It checks:
- team inequality / alive status;
- existing war;
- contact;
- permanent-war/peace constraints;
- force peace;
- game options;
- Python vetoes.

It does not and should not know that B is the sponsor of the proposed trade.

Thus A can perfectly legally declare war on C even though B, the broker asking
for that declaration, is C's voluntary vassal.

The missing invariant is specifically a WAR-TRADE sponsor/target relationship
constraint.

SYNCHRONOUS SELF-DEFEATING OUTCOME
----------------------------------
`CvDeal::startTrade(TRADE_WAR)` executes:

    GET_TEAM(eFromPlayer).declareWar(eAttackedTeam, ... eToPlayer);

For this example:

    A.declareWar(C, ..., sponsor=B)

`CvTeam::declareWar` sets A<->C at war, then iterates third teams.

For B:

    B.isVassal(C) == true

so it queues:

    queueWar(A, B, ..., WAR_DECLARATION_VASSAL_ALIGNMENT)

The function then calls:

    triggerWars(true);

BEFORE returning to `CvDeal::startTrade`.

`triggerWars` drains the queue synchronously and invokes:

    A.declareWar(B, ...)

That secondary declaration kills all active A<->B deals at the opening of
`CvTeam::declareWar`.

Therefore the sponsor who hired A to attack C immediately becomes an enemy of
A because B is C's vassal.

The diplomatic action defeats its own negotiating relationship in the same
call stack.

F286 SAME-ROOT LIFETIME EXPANSION
---------------------------------
The secondary A->B declaration also kills the CURRENT in-progress sponsor /
hireling deal.

That means:

    CvDeal::addTradeItems
      -> startTrade(TRADE_WAR)
        -> A.declareWar(C)
          -> triggerWars
            -> A.declareWar(B)
              -> kill all A<->B deals
                 -> current CvDeal deleted
      -> returns into methods still executing through `this`

and finally:

    CvGame::implementAndReturnDeal
        pDeal->getLengthFirst()
        pDeal->getLengthSecond()

can dereference a freed `pDeal`.

This is additional concrete evidence for F286's transaction-lifetime root.
Do NOT create another lifetime finding for the same deletion mechanism.

BROADER SAME-MASTER-LOCUS CASE
------------------------------
The clean invariant is broader than merely:

    sponsor.isVassal(target)

Current SAS, after KI#373 / F052 repair work, can also permit a VOLUNTARY
VASSAL as a TRADE_WAR target under full UWAI.

That means sibling voluntary vassals under the same master can also become
named sponsor/target pairs in configurations where the item otherwise passes.

War against one sibling aligns the common master and then the other sibling,
again turning the sponsor into the hireling's enemy.

The robust relation test is therefore the coalition identity:

    GET_TEAM(eTarget).getMasterTeam() ==
        GET_TEAM(eSponsor).getMasterTeam()

`CvTeam::getMasterTeam()` returns the team's own ID for a free team, so this
single comparison covers:
- sponsor -> own master;
- sponsor -> sibling vassal;
- other teams inside the same master/vassal locus.

Exact sponsor==target is already excluded by normal third-team generation and
caller assertions, but a structural guard can remain explicit if desired.

ANCESTRY
--------
Base AdvCiv 1.14 contains the same asymmetric AI denial:

    target.isVassal(sponsor) || target.isDefensivePact(sponsor)

K-Mod and Civ4CE likewise carry the inherited target-is-vassal-of-sponsor
check without the reverse/same-master-locus normalization.

Therefore the master-target form of F289 is inherited rather than SAS-created.

Current SAS's KI#373 / F052 voluntary-vassal target support can make the
broader sibling-vassal form reachable under UWAI, but that is an expansion of
the same underlying missing sponsor/target coalition check, not a separate
root.

RELATION TO F052 / KI#373
-------------------------
F052 was the opposite contract problem:

    intended FOREIGN voluntary-vassal targets were universally blocked.

Its repair deliberately made a voluntary vassal target legal under supported
UWAI conditions.

F289 does NOT argue that voluntary vassals should again be universally banned.

Instead, it distinguishes:
- FOREIGN voluntary vassal: valid supported war-trade target;
- sponsor's own master/vassal coalition: invalid self-defeating target.

Repairing F289 with a same-master-locus test preserves F052's intended foreign
voluntary-vassal feature.

ROOT INDEPENDENCE
-----------------
F289 is independent of F281-F288 as a gameplay/diplomacy defect.

Even if F286 is repaired perfectly so current deals cannot self-delete:
- B can still request war on its own master C;
- A can still accept;
- normal vassal alignment still makes A and B enemies immediately.

So the semantic defect survives the lifetime repair.

Conversely, rejecting malformed sponsor/target war trades would remove this
particular F286 trigger but would NOT fix F286's other confirmed self-deletion
paths (e.g. mixed Permanent Alliance state transitions).

The roots are therefore separate:
- F286 = transaction object lifetime under nested state changes;
- F289 = missing coalition constraint on brokered-war target semantics.

REPAIR BOUNDARY
---------------
A robust repair should enforce the sponsor/target coalition invariant at the
structural trade layer, not only as AI preference.

For TRADE_WAR, reject a target when:

    GET_TEAM(eTarget).getMasterTeam() ==
        kToTeam.getMasterTeam()

where kToTeam is the sponsor / negotiating partner.

This belongs naturally in `CvPlayer::canTradeItem(TRADE_WAR)` because
`canTradeItem(..., bTestDenial=false)` is widely used as game-rule validity and
trade-table construction.

Then harden `CvTeamAI::AI_declareWarTrade` with the same relationship rule
(or assert that structural callers already excluded it), so direct AI callers
cannot reintroduce the contradiction.

Do NOT repair by:
- banning all voluntary-vassal targets again;
- checking only `sponsor.isVassal(target)`, which misses sibling vassals;
- relying only on `DENIAL_JOKING`, because structural / forced callers may use
  `canTradeItem` without denial testing;
- suppressing the vassal-alignment war cascade, which is correct war-state
  behavior once a valid declaration occurs.
