F289 REPAIR-BOUNDARY REFINEMENT
===============================
THE SPONSOR/TARGET TEST MUST CANONICALIZE BOTH SIDES TO THEIR MASTER TEAMS
BEFORE CHECKING DEFENSIVE-PACT RELATIONSHIPS

WIP14 correctly established that a brokered war must not target the sponsor's
own master/vassal locus. A further cascade check shows that an exact
same-master comparison is necessary but not sufficient.

Additional live construction:

    A = AI hireling
    B = voluntary-vassal sponsor
    M = B's master
    C = proposed foreign target

with:

    B.isVassal(M) == true
    M.isDefensivePact(C) == true
    B and C are not directly in a Defensive Pact
    A is otherwise legally able/willing to declare war on C

Current `AI_declareWarTrade(C,B,...)` checks:

    C.isVassal(B)
    C.isDefensivePact(B)

Both can be false.

But when A executes the bought declaration against C:
1. C's Defensive Pact causes M to enter war against A;
2. B is M's vassal;
3. vassal alignment then brings B into war against A;
4. the sponsor B has again become an enemy of the civilization it just hired;
5. the current A<->B implementing deal can again be killed synchronously,
   expanding F286's trigger set.

The same issue generalizes when the named target is itself a voluntary vassal:
the meaningful target coalition is its master team, not merely the nominal
target team.

Therefore the robust F289 relation is approximately:

    TeamTypes const eSponsorMaster =
        GET_TEAM(eSponsor).getMasterTeam();
    TeamTypes const eTargetMaster =
        GET_TEAM(eTarget).getMasterTeam();

    if (eSponsorMaster == eTargetMaster ||
        GET_TEAM(eSponsorMaster).isDefensivePact(eTargetMaster))
    {
        reject;
    }

The exact implementation should preserve the normal symmetric DP invariant and
should be applied at the structural TRADE_WAR validity boundary as well as
AI denial hardening.

This refinement remains F289, not F290: it is the same missing
"sponsor must not buy a war that necessarily places the sponsor's coalition at
war with the hireling" contract.

F290 / PROVISIONAL KI#613
=========================
PERMANENT-ALLIANCE DEAL CLEANUP LOSES THE OLD TEAM IDENTITIES AFTER PLAYER
REASSIGNMENT; A VALID PRE-ALLIANCE DEFENSIVE PACT IS ENDED AS A SELF-PACT,
TRIGGERING ADVCIV/SAS ASSERTIONS

SEVERITY / SCOPE
----------------
Low severity, but confirmed.

The strongest current consequence is diagnostic:
- a normal Permanent Alliance formed while a Defensive Pact is active can hit
  `FAssert(getID() != eIndex)` in `CvTeam::setDefensivePact`;
- this assertion is active in both Debug and the project's separate optimized
  Assert configuration.

Release builds normally avoid a direct gameplay failure from the old DP bits
because the absorbed team is dead and alive-team iterators exclude it.
The cleanup also writes cancellation memory among the now-permanently allied
players, but same-team attitude is forced to 100 and a Permanent Alliance does
not later split, so that pollution is currently strategically inert.

This finding should therefore be treated as a real teardown-identity /
diagnostic defect, not overstated as a release gameplay corruption.

LIVE / INTENDED REACHABILITY
----------------------------
A Defensive Pact can legitimately still be active when a Permanent Alliance is
signed.

`CvPlayer::canPossiblyTradeItem(TRADE_PERMANENT_ALLIANCE)` requires:
- neither team is a vassal;
- distinct teams;
- no war;
- PA trading enabled;
- one member on each team.

It does NOT require the teams to lack Open Borders or a Defensive Pact.

More strongly, AI PA acceptance explicitly uses alliance history:

    AI_getDefensivePactCounter(eWithTeam) +
    AI_getShareWarCounter(eWithTeam) >= 40

and the Defensive Pact counter is incremented while:

    isDefensivePact(eOther)

is true.

Thus "active DP -> later PA" is not a synthetic malformed state; it is one of
the ordinary relationship histories the PA AI is designed around.

HOW THE OLD DP IS STORED
------------------------
Signing a DP calls:

    startTeamTrade(TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT, fromTeam, toTeam, true)

which creates persistent team-proxy `CvDeal`s for player pairs with a
Defensive-Pact item in both sides of each proxy deal.

The old pact therefore has live deals to clean up when the PA merges the teams.

THE K-MOD ORDERING CHANGE
-------------------------
BtS / Civ4CE cancel the inter-team OB/DP/peace/vassal deals before the members
of the absorbed team are reassigned.

K-Mod practical history commit 386 deliberately moved the entire cancellation
block *after* reassignment:

    "When forming a permanent alliance, deals are now canceled /after/ the team
     numbers have been reassigned. This is to prevent the new allies from being
     bumped..."

and its source comment says:

    "I've done this so that when open-borders is canceled,
     it doesn't bump our new allies out of our borders."

After the move, K-Mod identifies the old inter-team deals by the fact that both
participants are now on the surviving team.

AdvCiv and SAS inherit this ordering.

IDENTITY LOSS IN CURRENT ADDTEAM
--------------------------------
Current `CvTeam::addTeam(eTeam)` eventually does:

    for (...) {
        if (GET_PLAYER(i).getTeam() == eTeam)
            GET_PLAYER(i).setTeam(getID());
    }

Only afterward does it scan:

    if (!pLoopDeal->isBetween(getID(), getID()))
        continue;

and kill old OB / DP / peace / vassal / surrender / disengage deals.

That is enough to recognize which deals became internal, but it destroys the
old team identity needed by `CvDeal::endTrade`.

`CvDeal` stores player IDs, not historical team IDs.

When `kill()` later runs `endTrade`, every team lookup is based on the players'
CURRENT teams.

DEFENSIVE-PACT ASSERTION
------------------------
For an old M<->V DP proxy, after V's player has been reassigned to M:

    TEAMID(eFromPlayer) == M
    TEAMID(eToPlayer)   == M

`CvDeal::endTrade(TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT)` executes:

    GET_TEAM(eFromPlayer).setDefensivePact(
        TEAMID(eToPlayer), false);

which has become:

    M.setDefensivePact(M, false);

Current AdvCiv/SAS `CvTeam::setDefensivePact` begins:

    FAssert(getID() != eIndex); // advc

so the ordinary PA cleanup now calls a function under a condition that the
function explicitly asserts must not happen.

The subsequent equality early return does not save the diagnostic contract:
the assertion occurs first.

ASSERT BUILD IS REAL
--------------------
This is not Debug-only in the project.

The existing project configuration has an optimized Assert target using
`/DFASSERT_ENABLE` without `_DEBUG`, and `FAssert` is compiled whenever
FASSERT_ENABLE is present.

So a normal PA+DP teardown can fire in:
- Debug;
- optimized Assert.

This complements the earlier F273 finding: F273 found valid assertions that SAS
accidentally suppressed in the Assert configuration; F290 is the opposite
diagnostic problem, a valid game transition reaching an assertion whose
precondition was invalidated by teardown ordering.

ANCESTRY / COMBINATION
----------------------
Civ4CE retains the older ordering: relevant deals are killed before player-team
reassignment, so `endTrade` still sees the real old team pair.

K-Mod commit 386 introduced the post-reassignment cancellation specifically to
avoid Open-Borders unit bumping. K-Mod's `setDefensivePact` has only enum-range
assertions and no `getID() != eIndex` assertion, so the self-target teardown is
less visible there.

AdvCiv practical commit 1842 later added:

    FAssert(getID() != eIndex); // advc

to `CvTeam::setDefensivePact` while retaining K-Mod's post-reassignment PA
cleanup.

The confirmed false assertion is therefore an AdvCiv/SAS interaction between:
1. K-Mod's intentional PA cleanup ordering; and
2. AdvCiv's later self-team DP invariant assertion.

RELEASE-BUILD STATE EFFECT
--------------------------
With assertions disabled, `M.setDefensivePact(M,false)` ordinarily sees the
self DP bit already false and returns without touching the original M<->V
relation.

So the old DP bits keyed to absorbed team V are not actually cleared through
this path.

At that point V's final live member has already been moved to M, and
`CvPlayer::setTeam` has reduced V's alive count to zero.

Current live consumers such as `getDefensivePactCount` iterate ALIVE major
teams, which excludes V. A newly reused team is initialized/reset before normal
use.

Therefore no present release gameplay consequence from those stale DP bits has
been proved, and this checkpoint deliberately does not claim one.

SAME-TEAM CANCELLATION MEMORY
-----------------------------
AdvCiv's expanded `endTrade` also calls `addEndTradeMemory` when an OB or DP
team trade ends and both players are alive.

After PA reassignment, both the "ending" and "remembering" player team
iterators refer to the same newly merged team. This can write
MEMORY_CANCELLED_OPEN_BORDERS / MEMORY_CANCELLED_DEFENSIVE_PACT among the
permanent allies (including self-pairs through the nested member loops).

This is genuine teardown pollution, but currently inert for diplomacy:
`CvPlayerAI::AI_getAttitudeVal` returns 100 immediately for another player on
the same team, and a PA is irreversible.

It is evidence that the old identity is broadly lost during deal teardown, not
a separate finding.

WHY THIS IS NOT JUST "REMOVE THE ASSERT"
----------------------------------------
The assert is exposing a real mismatch:
- the deal being canceled semantically belonged to old teams M and V;
- the generic endTrade routine is being asked to interpret it after both
  participants have become M.

Deleting the assert would merely hide that mismatch and preserve the stale
old-team relation / same-team memory behavior.

ROOT / REPAIR BOUNDARY
----------------------
The repair should preserve the old team identities while ending the old
team-level agreement, or explicitly tear down the old M<->V team state rather
than asking generic `CvDeal::endTrade` to rediscover the old teams from players
whose team IDs have already changed.

Do not simply restore the entire pre-K-Mod cancellation block wholesale:
K-Mod moved it for a real reason -- canceling Open Borders before reassignment
can bump the soon-to-be allies out of each other's territory.

Safer repair families include:
- keep the old team IDs in a specialized PA teardown path;
- separate Open-Borders's unit-bump-sensitive ordering from DP/peace/etc.;
- explicitly clear the old M<->V relation after reassignment while suppressing
  generic same-team endTrade side effects, then delete the proxy deals.

The important invariant is:
    "tearing down an agreement keyed to old teams must not infer those old team
     IDs from participants after their team ownership has been rewritten."

ROOT INDEPENDENCE
-----------------
F290 is independent of F288.

F288:
- requires a mixed PA+vassal bundle;
- corrupts the surviving team into a self-vassal;
- is a release gameplay/state bug.

F290:
- needs only an ordinary pre-existing DP plus a later PA;
- arises when old team-proxy deals are canceled after participant reassignment;
- currently has its strongest consequence in Assert/Debug diagnostics.

Repairing the mixed-bundle self-vassal issue does not change the old DP teardown
path.

F290 is also independent of F286: no self-deletion/UAF is required. The old DP
proxy being canceled is intentionally being deleted; the problem is the team
identity used while ending it.

F291 / provisional KI#614
Title:
  Multiple civic changes in one diplomacy deal are executed as separate forced
  revolutions, overcharging anarchy and shortening the post-anarchy revolution
  cooldown.

Root / why this is one defect:
  A diplomacy bundle may contain one TRADE_CIVIC item for each different civic
  option/column. CvDeal::startTrade nevertheless executes every TRADE_CIVIC
  independently. Each item reconstructs the player's *current* CivicMap, changes
  one option, and calls CvPlayer::revolution(aeNewCivics, true) immediately.
  Thus one logical multi-civic diplomatic demand/exchange is fragmented into N
  separate revolutions instead of one CivicMap revolution.

Current execution path:
  CvDeal::addTradeItems traverses each trade list item-by-item and calls
  startTrade for every non-vassal item.

  CvDeal::startTrade(TRADE_CIVIC):
      CivicMap aeNewCivics;
      kFromPlayer.getCivics(aeNewCivics);
      eCivic = (CivicTypes)trade.m_iData;
      aeNewCivics.set(option(eCivic), eCivic);
      kFromPlayer.revolution(aeNewCivics, true);

  CvPlayer::revolution:
      iAnarchyLength = getCivicAnarchyLength(kNewCivics);
      if (iAnarchyLength > 0)
          changeAnarchyTurns(iAnarchyLength);  // additive
      ...
      setRevolutionTimer(iAnarchyLength + getMinTurnsBetweenRevolutions());
                                              // absolute overwrite

  CvPlayer::changeAnarchyTurns:
      m_iAnarchyTurns += iChange;

Why multiple civic items are a supported live state rather than a malformed list:
  * CvPlayer::buildTradeTable exposes all individually tradeable civic items.
  * CvPlayerAI::AI_checkCivicReligionConsistency explicitly rejects a second
    TRADE_CIVIC only when its CivicOptionType duplicates a civic already present.
    Civics from different columns are therefore deliberately permitted.
  * Both AI_considerOffer and the AI counterproposal path call that consistency
    check.
  * CvPlayer::updateTradeList explicitly says "everything allowed in human-human
    trades"; its AI-side filtering does not impose a one-TRADE_CIVIC total rule.
  * AdvCiv's own AI_anarchyTradeVal comment explicitly discusses "multiple
    TRADE_CIVIC and TRADE_RELIGION items ... on the table." So the codebase itself
    recognizes multi-item ideology trades as a real state.

Locally provable arithmetic:
  CvPlayer::getCivicAnarchyLength sums the iAnarchyLength of all changed civic
  columns and, if at least one changed, adds:
    * BASE_CIVIC_ANARCHY_LENGTH once; and
    * the city-count/world-size anarchy overhead once.
  It then applies modifiers/speed/start-era scaling and caps that one revolution.

  In the deal path, however, each TRADE_CIVIC sees only one changed column,
  because the previous item has already committed its civic before the next item
  reconstructs the CivicMap. The fixed base/city overhead is therefore charged
  once per traded civic instead of once per logical multi-civic revolution.

Current SAS data makes this live without exotic configuration:
  * 25 civic entries; every current <iAnarchyLength> is 1.
  * Five distinct civic options/columns:
      GOVERNMENT, LEGAL, LABOR, ECONOMY, RELIGION.
  * Standard world: iNumCitiesAnarchyPercent = 8.
  * Normal speed: iAnarchyPercent = 100.
  * Ancient start era: iAnarchyPercent = 100.
  * SAS does not override the inherited stock values:
      BASE_CIVIC_ANARCHY_LENGTH = 1
      MAX_ANARCHY_TURNS         = 100
      MIN_REVOLUTION_TURNS      = 5

Concrete current-data examples (ordinary player, no no-anarchy trait/modifier):
  Standard / Normal / Ancient, 5 cities:
    city overhead = floor(5 * 8 / 100) = 0

    One civic:
      1 civic + 1 base = 2 turns.

    Two civic columns as one CivicMap revolution:
      1 + 1 civics + 1 base = 3 turns.

    Current deal execution:
      2 + 2 = 4 turns.
    => 1 extra anarchy turn.

  Standard / Normal / Ancient, 13 cities:
    city overhead = floor(13 * 8 / 100) = 1

    Two civics combined:
      1 + 1 civics + 1 base + 1 city overhead = 4 turns.

    Current deal execution:
      (1 + 1 base + 1 city) + (1 + 1 base + 1 city) = 6 turns.
    => 2 extra anarchy turns.

  The current five-column data can magnify this further. At 13 cities, changing
  all five columns in one normal CivicMap revolution costs:
      5 civic + 1 base + 1 city = 7 turns.
  The deal path instead applies five 3-turn revolutions:
      5 * 3 = 15 turns.
  => 8 extra anarchy turns from the same accepted bundle.

Secondary timer consequence:
  Each forced revolution also executes
      setRevolutionTimer(iAnarchyLength + getMinTurnsBetweenRevolutions())
  rather than adding/preserving the timer for the already accumulated anarchy.
  Therefore the *last* civic item overwrites the timer while the anarchy turns
  from all earlier civic items remain additive.

  Example, 5 cities, two civics:
    accumulated anarchy after the deal = 4
    final revolution timer             = 2 + 5 = 7

  Both counters are decremented each player turn. When the four inflated anarchy
  turns have elapsed, only about three revolution-timer turns remain. A single
  proper combined revolution would be:
    anarchy = 3
    revolution timer = 3 + 5 = 8
  and would still leave the intended five-turn post-anarchy cooldown after the
  three anarchy decrements.

  With enough separately executed civic items, the overwritten timer can reach
  zero while the accumulated anarchy is still running. canRevolution is still
  blocked by isAnarchy, but once anarchy ends the normal post-anarchy cooldown
  can be partly or wholly gone. Thus the defect both lengthens the immediate
  forced anarchy and weakens the subsequent revolution lockout.

Order sensitivity / future-proofing:
  Current SAS gives all civics iAnarchyLength=1, so the final timer is currently
  insensitive to which civic happens to be last. Mods with unequal civic
  anarchy lengths make the final revolution timer depend on trade-list order,
  another sign that item-by-item execution is the wrong state boundary.

Ancestry:
  The per-item TRADE_CIVIC -> revolution(...) behavior is inherited. K-Mod and
  Civ4CE/BtS contain the same basic execution shape, and Base AdvCiv 1.14 still
  does too. This is not a SAS-specific regression.
  AdvCiv later added explicit multi-civic consistency/value code (advc.132) but
  did not aggregate execution. Its AI valuation comment acknowledges multiple
  TRADE_CIVIC items as a real trade-table state.

Why religion is NOT needed to establish F291:
  TRADE_RELIGION also has its own forced conversion/anarchy path, and a bundle
  containing both religion and civics may raise a broader design question about
  whether two distinct ideology systems should share one anarchy overhead.
  F291 does not rely on that judgment. Multiple civic *columns* are represented
  by one CivicMap and ordinary CvPlayer::revolution already defines the native
  combined-operation semantics unambiguously.

Repair boundary:
  Keep normal/manual CvPlayer::revolution semantics unchanged.
  In deal implementation, collect all TRADE_CIVIC items given by each player
  into that player's one CivicMap and execute one forced revolution per player,
  rather than one forced revolution per item.

  Important boundaries:
    * single-civic deals must behave exactly as before;
    * the two players' civic sets must remain independent;
    * retain the existing up-front whole-bundle canTradeItem validation;
    * preserve per-item logging/AI trade-value bookkeeping if desired, but do not
      let those force separate state transitions;
    * set the AI civic timer once after the combined forced civic change;
    * do not "fix" this by changing changeAnarchyTurns or revolution globally;
    * do not automatically merge TRADE_RELIGION into the same state transition
      unless that broader behavior is separately designed and reviewed.

Root independence:
  F291 is independent of the earlier queue-042 roots:
    F281/F283/F285  = peace-treaty list/lifetime/orientation
    F282            = end-trade memory accumulation
    F284            = player-death vs team-agreement lifetime
    F286            = active-deal reentrant self-deletion/UAF
    F287            = mixed annual verification killing protected peace
    F288            = PA + vassal self-vassal survivor
    F289            = brokered-war master-locus relation
    F290            = PA teardown after team identity reassignment
  F291 is instead a transaction aggregation/state-transition granularity error
  in forced civic execution.

Queue state after this checkpoint:
  queue 042 CvGameCoreDLL/CvDeal.cpp — still OPEN
  F281 / provisional KI#604 — confirmed
  F282 / provisional KI#605 — confirmed
  F283 / provisional KI#606 — confirmed
  F284 / provisional KI#607 — confirmed
  F285 / provisional KI#608 — confirmed
  F286 / provisional KI#609 — confirmed
  F287 / provisional KI#610 — confirmed
  F288 / provisional KI#611 — confirmed
  F289 / provisional KI#612 — confirmed
  F290 / provisional KI#613 — confirmed
  F291 / provisional KI#614 — confirmed
  F292 / provisional KI#615 — UNUSED / next

  Re-run the remaining CvDeal transaction families specifically for:

    * trade-list ordering dependence after one item mutates preconditions used

F292 / provisional KI#615
Title:
  A mixed city + resource deal can pass prevalidation and then invalidate its
  own resource export when the city transfer removes the giver's last copy.

Root:
  CvDeal::addTradeItems validates every offered item independently against the
  pre-deal world state, then mutates the world item-by-item. A TRADE_CITIES item
  can immediately change plot ownership and rebuild plot groups, including the
  giver's connected bonus counts. A sibling TRADE_RESOURCES item is nevertheless
  accepted based only on the *old* resource count and startTrade does not
  revalidate it after the city transfer.

Clean source-proven live producer:
  Human-human trade intentionally permits annual and nonannual items in one
  bundle. CvPlayer::updateTradeList wraps the annual/nonannual compatibility
  filter in:

      if (!isHuman() || !GET_PLAYER(eOtherPlayer).isHuman())
          ...

  with the explicit comment:
      "everything allowed in human-human trades"

  Therefore a multiplayer/hotseat deal can contain both TRADE_CITIES
  (nonannual) and TRADE_RESOURCES (annual). This finding does not need to assume
  that the ordinary human-AI peacetime UI permits the same mixture.

Concrete trigger:
  Let player A and player B be human players on different teams with a valid
  trade network.

  A has a non-capital city C that passes the normal city-trade rules. C can be,
  for example, a sufficiently eligible/contested city (current SAS requires at
  least CITY_TRADE_CULTURE_THRESH = 10% recipient culture outside liberation
  shortcuts).

  A has exactly one connected copy of bonus X, and transferring C to B removes
  that copy from A. The simplest deterministic geometry is that C itself is
  founded on bonus X; the city tile connects that resource for A before the
  transfer and belongs to B afterward.

  A places both:
      TRADE_CITIES(C)
      TRADE_RESOURCES(X)
  in the same accepted bundle.

Why both pass the existing preflight:
  CvDeal::addTradeItems first loops over all items and calls canTradeItem before
  executing any of them.

  At that time:
    * canTradeItem(TRADE_CITIES) sees C still owned by A and accepts it if the
      normal city-trade conditions pass.
    * canTradeItem(TRADE_RESOURCES) sees X still non-obsolete on both teams and
      A's getNumTradeableBonuses(X) > 0. AdvCiv's current bCanTradeAll=true path
      allows the last available copy to be offered.

  There is no bundle-level "what bonuses remain after the city gifts?" check.

Execution:
  CvDeal::addTradeItems later calls startTrade item-by-item.

  TRADE_CITIES:
      pCity->doTask(TASK_GIFT/TASK_CEDE, eToPlayer)

  CvPlayer::acquireCity(..., bUpdatePlotGroups=true, ...)
      ...
      kGame.updatePlotGroups();

  The old owner's bonus network is therefore recomputed immediately after the
  city changes hands.

  TRADE_RESOURCES:
      kFromPlayer.changeBonusExport(X, +1);
      kToPlayer.changeBonusImport(X, +1);
      bSave = true;

  startTrade does not repeat canTradeItem. Consequently, regardless of which of
  the two sibling items happens to execute first, the final state can contain
  one export backed by zero remaining copies:
    * city first: local copy becomes 0, then export bookkeeping pushes available
      trade state below zero;
    * resource first: export consumes the one copy, then the city transfer and
      plot-group rebuild remove that physical copy underneath the export.

Why this is not merely theoretical bookkeeping:
  CvDeal::verify explicitly treats a resource giver with
      getNumTradeableBonuses(eBonus) < 0
  as invalid and returns false; CvDeal::verify() then kills the deal.

  Thus the engine itself recognizes the final state produced by this accepted
  bundle as an impossible/oversubscribed resource trade.

Irreversible transaction consequence:
  The city transfer is one-shot and is not stored in the persistent deal, so it
  cannot be rolled back when verify later kills the deal.

  Any annual consideration saved in the same human-human deal can disappear
  with the invalid resource item (resource/GPT and other persistent components),
  while ownership of C remains changed. Even a deal whose only persistent item
  is X visibly accepts a resource promise that is invalid essentially from its
  creation and is removed at the next deal verification.

  AI_dealVal also values TRADE_RESOURCES and TRADE_CITIES as separate trade
  items. Where a producer permits such a bundle, the two pieces therefore enter
  valuation independently even though the post-city resource promise can be
  impossible. The guaranteed current producer established here is human-human;
  no single-player human-AI exploit is required for F292.

Relationship to F287:
  F287 is a *teardown granularity* bug: later failure of one annual component
  kills an entire mixed persistent deal, including a still-protected peace
  treaty.

  F292 is a *transaction precondition* bug: the deal is accepted even though
  another item in that same transaction deterministically destroys the resource
  condition needed by the annual item.

  They are independent:
    * repairing F287 to remove only the failed annual component would still leave
      F292's resource consideration invalid immediately after the accepted city
      transfer;
    * rejecting/repairing F292 does not prevent ordinary later resource/GPT
      failures from exercising F287.

Ancestry:
  The relevant shape is inherited:
    * Base AdvCiv 1.14, K-Mod and Civ4CE/BtS all retain the per-item city/resource
      execution model.
    * Their updateTradeList implementations also retain the explicit
      human-human "everything allowed" exception.
  SAS did not introduce the root.

Rejected sibling that helped bound this finding:
  A superficially similar "trade a tech that obsoletes the resource received
  from the other side" case is already blocked. Resource canTradeItem checks
  bonus obsolescence for *both* giver and recipient; the tech giver already owns
  the obsoleting tech before the bundle, so that resource cannot pass the
  initial resource check. F292 therefore stays focused on state mutations whose
  relevant postcondition is not represented by an already-existing predeal
  state, with city ownership/resource supply being the proven case.

Repair boundary:
  The deal must not commit a one-shot city transfer while relying on an annual
  resource promise that the same transaction will make unsustainable.

  Conservative options for implementation review:
    1. Add a bundle-consistency preflight for TRADE_CITIES + TRADE_RESOURCES from
       the same giver, predicting the giver's post-transfer resource
       availability before committing any item.
    2. If exact post-city plot-group simulation is too invasive (city transfer
       can change more than the city tile), prohibit same-giver city + resource
       mixtures unless a safe conservative test proves the resource remains.
    3. A broader transactional redesign could stage/validate state transitions,
       but simply revalidating after the city has already moved is too late
       because city ownership has no rollback here.

  Do not "repair" this only in CvDeal::verify; that merely changes how the
  already-broken accepted transaction is torn down.

Queue state after this checkpoint:
  queue 042 CvGameCoreDLL/CvDeal.cpp — still OPEN
  F281-F292 / provisional KI#604-KI#615 — confirmed
  F293 / provisional KI#616 — UNUSED / next

Next saturation cursor:
  Continue the repeated TRADE_WAR / TRADE_PEACE / TRADE_EMBARGO mutation-order
  challenge, then inspect remaining one-shot + persistent cross-item pairs and
  final Base/K-Mod/Civ4CE history divergence. Avoid allocating F293 unless an
  independent producer + consequence survives those checks.

No repository source files modified.

C025-WIP18 ADDENDUM — queue 042 CvDeal.cpp

F293 / provisional KI#616
Title:
  Brokered peace/war attitude bookkeeping keeps only the last political target,
  making otherwise identical multi-target deals semantically order-dependent.

Root:
  CvDeal::addTradeItems scans both offered lists before implementation and stores
  political context in only two scalar TeamTypes:

      TeamTypes eWarTradeTarget = NO_TEAM;
      TeamTypes ePeaceTradeTarget = NO_TEAM;

  Every TRADE_WAR simply overwrites eWarTradeTarget and every TRADE_PEACE simply
  overwrites ePeaceTradeTarget. The resulting single last-seen target of each
  class is then passed to AI_processTradeValue for BOTH trade directions.

  AI_processTradeValue evaluates the value of the complete item list and forwards
  that same scalar target context to CvPlayerAI::AI_processPeacetimeValue, which
  in turn asks each third-party team for
  CvTeamAI::AI_enemyTradeResentmentFactor(...).

  The latter has target-specific branches:
    * eWarTradeTarget == observer makes the observer count the source as sharing
      its war;
    * ePeaceTradeTarget == observer/master-locus suppresses rival-trade anger;
    * a peace target liked by the observer can also suppress anger.

  Therefore a list containing more than one brokered peace or war target cannot
  be represented correctly by the scalar metadata. Which target happens to be
  encountered last controls the attitude treatment of the entire deal value.

Why multi-target political lists are a supported/reachable state:
  * CvPlayer::buildTradeTable creates a distinct TRADE_PEACE / TRADE_WAR /
    TRADE_EMBARGO inventory item for every eligible third team.
  * CvPlayer::updateTradeList does not impose a one-item-per-political-heading
    restriction.
  * CvPlayerAI::AI_checkCivicReligionConsistency exists specifically to reject
    duplicate/incompatible civic/religion items; there is no analogous
    one-TRADE_PEACE check.
  * CvPlayerAI::AI_dealVal simply sums every TRADE_PEACE item:
        iValue += kOurTeam.AI_makePeaceTradeVal(target, eFromTeam);
    with no count limit.
  * The same function explicitly counts TRADE_WAR items and, under UWAI, adds an
    unaffordable 1,000,000 value when iWars > 1, with the source comment
        "Can't be hired for more than one war at a time"
    This is particularly strong evidence that multiple political items can
    coexist in an offered list; the code had to impose policy in valuation rather
    than relying on the trade representation to make a second item impossible.
    (Legacy/non-UWAI valuation does not even apply that multi-war policy.)
  * Human trade-table proposals are the clean producer for multiple brokered
    peace items; the DLL has no bundle-consistency rejection for that case.

Concrete order-sensitive brokered-peace example:
  Let:
    H = sponsor / paying player
    B = AI player being paid to make peace
    E = independent third team currently at war with B
    D = another third team currently at war with B

  Suppose E regards B as its worst enemy and H is not itself at war with E.
  H constructs one deal in which:
    H gives economic consideration to B; and
    B gives TRADE_PEACE(E) plus TRADE_PEACE(D).

  Both peace items are independently valid and AI_dealVal values both.

  When B receives H's consideration, B's AI_processTradeValue records rival-trade
  consequences for third parties. For observer E:

    CvTeamAI::AI_enemyTradeResentmentFactor(
        eTo = B,
        eFrom = H,
        ePeaceTradeTarget = <last TRADE_PEACE seen>)

  contains:
      if (ePeaceTradeTarget == getMasterTeam())
          return 0;

  For an independent E, getMasterTeam() == E.

  Hence:
    list order [PEACE(D), PEACE(E)]
      -> scalar ePeaceTradeTarget = E
      -> E correctly sees that H paid its enemy B to make peace with E
      -> target-specific rival-trade resentment is suppressed.

    list order [PEACE(E), PEACE(D)]
      -> scalar ePeaceTradeTarget = D
      -> E's own peace settlement is invisible to the context calculation
      -> provided D does not independently trigger the "liked peace target"
         exemption, E can apply positive rival-trade resentment to H for the
         value of the same economic/political bundle.

  The set of players, teams, items and values is identical. Only list order /
  last-target selection changes the diplomatic-memory result.

  Even if a particular UI path happens to insert targets in a stable enum order,
  the semantic defect remains: one valid peace target receives the intended
  exemption while another valid target is discarded solely because the metadata
  has room for one TeamTypes value. There is no normalization that defines the
  last target as semantically privileged.

War-side sibling:
  eWarTradeTarget has the same scalar overwrite architecture. The observer-side
  factor treats
      isAtWar(eFrom) || eWarTradeTarget == observer
  as "the source also shares our war." With several TRADE_WAR items, only the
  last target can receive that target-specific treatment.

  UWAI deliberately makes a second hired war economically impossible through
  AI_dealVal's +1,000,000 guard, so current default/full-UWAI exposure is much
  narrower on the war side. The inherited legacy/non-UWAI path does not have
  that valuation block. This sibling therefore strengthens the root but is not
  needed to establish F293; multiple TRADE_PEACE is sufficient.

Additional asymmetry:
  addTradeItems derives ePeaceTradeTarget/eWarTradeTarget from BOTH lists, then
  passes the same final pair of targets to AI_processTradeValue for each side.
  Thus the metadata is deal-global while the value being processed is
  direction/list-specific. That was an intentional approximation for a single
  brokered political item, but it becomes undefined once several distinct
  targets exist.

Ancestry / history:
  This shape is AdvCiv-specific rather than a SAS regression.

  AdvCiv practical 1361
  "Rival-trade penalties, war trades on Glance tab, misc. changes"
  (advc.130p) introduced the scalar warTradeTarget / peaceTradeTarget variables
  in CvDeal::addTrades while refactoring fair-trade/rival-trade bookkeeping.

  The introduction comment explicitly explains that brokered TRADE_PEACE cannot
  simply be filtered out because other items may be traded alongside it, and the
  target was added so rival-trade penalties could react to whom peace was being
  brokered with. The design handled the one-target case, but the scan used simple
  assignment and never acquired a multi-target representation.

  Current Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains the same scalar target contract. SAS inherits
  it unchanged apart from unrelated game-record/victory-denial instrumentation.
  K-Mod/BtS do not contain this later AdvCiv target-sensitive rival-trade
  machinery in the same form.

Why this is independent of earlier queue-042 findings:
  * F289 is relationship validation for a single brokered WAR target: a voluntary
    vassal sponsor may hire war against its own master/master-locus.
  * F293 assumes every individual TRADE_PEACE/WAR item is valid. Its problem is
    lossy representation of multiple valid political targets during subsequent
    attitude bookkeeping.
  * F282 concerns additive vs absolute cancellation-memory updates.
  * F291/F292 concern bundle execution/precondition aggregation, not third-party
    rival-trade memory context.

Repair boundary:
  Do not merely choose first target instead of last; that preserves the same
  lossy/order-dependent root.

  The robust design needs multi-target context. Two increasingly exact options:

  1. Minimal deterministic representation:
     collect brokered peace/war targets in a set/small vector and teach
     AI_enemyTradeResentmentFactor (or a wrapper) to reason over the whole set.
     This removes arbitrary last-item privilege, though care is still needed
     because an observer may be affected differently by different targets.

  2. Semantically cleaner repair:
     partition the recorded deal value into target-neutral consideration and
     target-specific political-item value, then apply each peace/war target's
     resentment adjustment to the appropriate component. This avoids letting one
     target-specific exemption suppress or amplify the value attributable to
     unrelated political items in the same bundle.

  Whichever repair is chosen:
    * one-TRADE_PEACE / one-TRADE_WAR behavior should remain unchanged;
    * direct peace between the two negotiating teams (bPeace) is a separate
      dimension and must remain separate;
    * reparations/fair-trade suppression rules from advc.130p must be preserved;
    * do not solve this by globally forbidding multiple TRADE_PEACE unless that
      is an explicit gameplay-policy choice, because current valuation supports
      and prices each brokered peace separately;
    * UWAI's explicit one-hired-war policy can remain as policy even if the
      underlying bookkeeping becomes capable of multiple war targets.

Queue state after this checkpoint:
  queue 042 CvGameCoreDLL/CvDeal.cpp — still OPEN
  F281-F293 / provisional KI#604-KI#616 — confirmed
  F294 / provisional KI#617 — UNUSED / next

Final saturation cursor:
  * finish the remaining trade-type classification/accessor/serialization
    inventory;
  * challenge any remaining cross-item coalition cascade that changes state,
    rather than merely value;
  * complete the targeted historical repair-stream ledger, explicitly marking
    each old CvDeal fix as preserved, absorbed by F281-F293, or a control;
  * if no independent F294 survives, close queue 042 cleanly and move to the
    next reconciled priority queue.

C025-WIP19 ADDENDUM — queue 042 CvDeal.cpp / cross-file accessor consumer
F294 / provisional KI#617 confirmed; F295 unused
================================================================================

F294 / provisional KI#617
Title:
  Embargo valuation scans the hired player's whole team instead of the hired
  player's own deals, overpricing teammate trade that will survive the embargo
  and violating CvDeal's player-accessor contract on multi-member teams.

Root:
  CvPlayerAI::AI_stopTradingTradeVal describes its contract directly:

      "This player pays for the embargo and ePlayer stops trading
       with eTradeTeam."

  The actual embargo machinery has the same player-specific contract.

  CvPlayer::isTradingWithTeam documents:
      "- It checks if this player is trading with any member of eToTeam.
         Likewise, an embargo will affect only the enacting player - but the
         entire target team."

  CvPlayer::stopTradingWithTeam therefore filters:
      if (!pLoopDeal->isBetween(getID(), eTeam))
          continue;

  i.e. only deals involving the specific enacting player are candidates for
  cancellation.

  AI_stopTradingTradeVal instead scans:
      if (!pLoopDeal->isBetween(TEAMID(ePlayer), eTradeTeam))
          continue;

  That is a team-vs-team filter. On a team with more than one player it admits
  persistent deals owned by ePlayer's teammates even though those deals will not
  be canceled when ePlayer executes the embargo.

Concrete live topology:
  Let A1 and A2 be two living players on Team A (e.g. after a Permanent Alliance
  or in a preconfigured multi-player team), and let T be the embargo target team.

  A1 is the player being asked to stop trading with T. A1 has some valid
  outgoing trade to T, so:
      A1.canStopTradingWithTeam(T) == true.

  A2 independently has a valuable persistent resource/GPT deal with a member of
  T. Such player-level deals remain normal after the players share Team A.

  AI_stopTradingTradeVal(T, A1):
    * pLoopDeal(A2,T) passes isBetween(Team A, T);
    * its incoming consideration can therefore be added to A1's embargo price.

  Actual execution:
      A1.stopTradingWithTeam(T)

  only visits deals satisfying isBetween(A1,T), so A2's deal survives.

  Result: the sponsor can be charged for trade value that the hired player does
  not give up and that the embargo does not cancel.

CvDeal accessor-contract failure introduced on top of the semantic root:
  Current AdvCiv/SAS refactored the duplicated orientation branches into:

      pLoopDeal->getReceivesList(TEAMID(ePlayer))
      pLoopDeal->getOtherPlayer(ePlayer)
      pLoopDeal->getGivesList(ePlayer)

  The first call is deliberately team-scoped, but the latter two require the
  exact player to participate:

      CvDeal::getOtherPlayer(PlayerTypes ePlayer):
          FAssert(ePlayer == getFirstPlayer() ||
                  ePlayer == getSecondPlayer());

      CvDeal::getGivesList(PlayerTypes eGivingPlayer):
          same exact-participant assertion.

  Therefore, for an admitted A2<->T deal while ePlayer=A1:
    * Debug/Assert DLLs trip getOtherPlayer(A1);
    * if execution continues, getGivesList(A1) trips too.

Release behavior is not merely "assert removed":
  getOtherPlayer uses:
      return (ePlayer == getFirstPlayer() ?
              getSecondPlayer() : getFirstPlayer());

  When A1 is absent, it always falls through to getFirstPlayer.

  Thus result quality becomes deal-orientation dependent:
    * if A2 is first, getOtherPlayer(A1) returns A2 itself and A1.AI_dealVal is
      asked to value target-supplied items as though teammate A2 supplied them;
    * if T's player is first, the returned "other" happens to be the target
      participant by accident.

  getGivesList(A1) has the analogous absent-player fall-through to the second
  list, so the 5-vs-3 gift/trade multiplier can likewise inspect the wrong side
  depending on orientation.

  The underlying overcount exists even if those fall-through results happened
  to be benign: the teammate deal should not have entered this loop at all.

Direct normal embargo consequence:
  CvPlayerAI::AI_dealVal prices each TRADE_EMBARGO by:
      AI_stopTradingTradeVal(targetTeam, eFromPlayer)

  so this inflated/misoriented result feeds ordinary trade valuation and can
  alter whether/how much an AI sponsor is willing to pay for the embargo.

War-bribe lower-bound sibling:
  CvTeamAI::AI_declareWarTradeVal deliberately computes an embargo lower bound:

      "an embargo ... would only compel one player to stop trading with the
       (whole) target team, so we need to sum up the embargo trade values of
       the members of this team."

  It loops each hireling-team member that canStopTradingWithTeam(eTarget) and
  calls:
      sponsorLeader.AI_stopTradingTradeVal(eTarget, member, true);

  That design confirms the unit of cancellation/value is one player at a time.

  With a multi-member team, however, every one of those per-player calls scans
  the whole team's T-deals. If A1 and A2 each have cancelable player-level trade
  with T, A1's call can count A2's deal and A2's call can count A1's deal; the
  sum can therefore count the same trade losses repeatedly. This can inflate
  the lower bound used for a declaration-of-war bribe in addition to the direct
  embargo-price error.

Ancestry:
  The semantic player-vs-team mismatch is inherited from BtS/K-Mod/Civ4CE.

  Their AI_stopTradingTradeVal loops classify a deal as relevant whenever a
  participant's TEAM equals ePlayer's team. That already counts teammate-owned
  deals on multi-member teams, despite stopTradingWithTeam being player-scoped.

  AdvCiv practical 1352
  "Bugs fixed in AI war trade behavior; tech cost adjustments"
  (advc.130f/advc.001q) improved the inherited scan by adding the missing
  opposite-side target-team condition. Before that, BtS effectively checked only
  whether one participant belonged to ePlayer's team; the AdvCiv source comment
  records this explicitly:
      "BtS had only checked for ePlayer's team"

  That repair correctly stopped unrelated third-team deals from entering the
  price, but retained TEAMID(ePlayer) rather than the exact ePlayer identity.

  AdvCiv practical 1618
  "FOR_EACH macros everywhere; changes to AI class design."
  later rewrote the two orientation branches with the new CvDeal accessors.
  The refactor preserved the team-level filter but then called exact-player
  getOtherPlayer/getGivesList, turning the older semantic mismatch into a
  deterministic assertion-contract violation as well.

  Current Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains this shape. SAS inherits it; SAS's nearby
  local change merely caches GET_PLAYER(ePlayer) as kPlayer.

Why multi-member teams are not exotic malformed state:
  Permanent Alliance is a shipped trade item and deliberately combines players
  onto one team; scenario/team-game setups can also begin with multiple players
  sharing a team. Player-level resource/GPT deals remain represented by their
  individual player IDs. The embargo APIs themselves are explicitly documented
  around this distinction, so the code cannot assume one player per team here.

Independence from earlier findings:
  * F285 is an embargo-DENIAL/list-orientation bug involving peace reparations.
    F294 can reproduce with ordinary resource/GPT deals and no peace treaty.
  * F290 concerns old team identities while tearing down agreements during a
    Permanent Alliance merge. F294 applies after a multi-member team already
    exists and concerns current player-owned trade valuation.
  * F284 concerns a player death tearing down team-owned agreements. F294 is the
    inverse scope error: team-wide scanning of player-owned persistent deals.
  * F293 concerns lossy multi-target political attitude context, not deal owner
    identity.

Repair boundary:
  For the persistent ordinary-deal loop in AI_stopTradingTradeVal, use the same
  player scope as the operation being valued:

      if (!pLoopDeal->isBetween(ePlayer, eTradeTeam))
          continue;

  Once that invariant is established, use player-scoped list accessors
  consistently:
      getReceivesList(ePlayer)
      getOtherPlayer(ePlayer)
      getGivesList(ePlayer)

  This simultaneously:
    * excludes teammate deals that survive ePlayer's embargo;
    * satisfies getOtherPlayer/getGivesList's exact-participant contracts;
    * removes orientation-dependent Release fall-through.

  Important boundary:
  Keep the separate Open Borders / Defensive Pact terms under review as
  team-level relationship costs. Those relationships are genuinely stored and
  torn down at team scope through their proxy/agreement machinery. Do not
  mechanically convert every TEAMID(ePlayer) use in the function to player
  scope; F294 is specifically the ordinary persistent-deal inventory whose
  actual cancellation path is player-specific.

  The war-bribe member-sum should then naturally aggregate disjoint per-player
  trade losses instead of recounting the full team inventory for every member.
  Its team-level OB/DP contribution may still deserve independent heuristic
  review, but that is not required to repair the proven F294 root.

Queue state after this checkpoint:
  queue 042 CvGameCoreDLL/CvDeal.cpp — still OPEN
  F281-F294 / provisional KI#604-KI#617 — confirmed
  F295 / provisional KI#618 — UNUSED / next

Remaining saturation cursor:
  * challenge the team-level OB/DP contribution in the multi-member war-bribe
    member sum without assuming it is a bug merely because it is repeated;
  * finish the historical repair-stream ledger and remaining classification /
    serialization / cancellation controls;
  * if no independent F295 survives, close queue 042 cleanly rather than
    manufacturing another root.

No repository source files modified.

C025-WIP20 ADDENDUM — queue 042 CvDeal.cpp / war-trade embargo lower bound
F295 / provisional KI#618 confirmed; F296 unused
================================================================================

F295 / provisional KI#618
Title:
  Multi-member war-bribe embargo lower bound counts shared team-level
  Open-Borders / Defensive-Pact loss once per player even though the first
  embargo tears the shared agreement down for the whole team.

Root:
  CvTeamAI::AI_declareWarTradeVal deliberately constructs an embargo-equivalent
  lower bound by summing AI_stopTradingTradeVal for every member of the hireling
  team that can stop trading with the target:

      int iEmbargoTradeVal = 0;
      for (MemberIter itMember(getID()); itMember.hasNext(); ++itMember)
      {
          if (itMember->canStopTradingWithTeam(eTarget))
          {
              iEmbargoTradeVal += sponsorLeader.AI_stopTradingTradeVal(
                      eTarget, itMember->getID(), true);
          }
      }
      iTradeVal = max(iTradeVal, 0.83 * iEmbargoTradeVal);

  This decomposition is valid for independent player-owned resource/GPT deals:
  an embargo by A1 cancels A1's deals, and a separate embargo by A2 cancels A2's
  deals.

  It is not additive for Open Borders or Defensive Pact. Those are team-level
  relationships represented by replicated player-pair proxy deals. Killing one
  qualifying proxy with normal bKillTeam=true tears down the relationship for
  the entire pair of teams and deletes all sibling proxies.

Source-proven shared state:
  CvDeal::startTeamTrade(TRADE_OPEN_BORDERS / TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT, ...)
  creates a proxy deal for every member-pair.

  CvDeal::endTrade for either item:
      GET_TEAM(eFromPlayer).setOpenBorders/DefensivePact(..., false);
      if (bTeam)
          endTeamTrade(...);

  CvDeal::endTeamTrade then finds all sibling proxies between those teams and
  kills them with kill(false).

  CvPlayer::stopTradingWithTeam kills a qualifying player deal with ordinary:
      pLoopDeal->kill();
  i.e. bKillTeam defaults true.

  Therefore the first member embargo that kills an OB/DP proxy removes the
  shared team relation and every other member's corresponding proxy. A second
  member does not independently lose another copy of that relationship.

How AI_stopTradingTradeVal nevertheless prices it on every member call:
  For each ePlayer member it derives:
      CvTeam const& kTeam = GET_TEAM(ePlayer);

  and applies the same team-level Open-Borders state:
      if (kTeam.isOpenBorders(eTradeTeam))
      {
          iModifier += 50;
          ...
      }

  followed by the same team-level Defensive-Pact state:
      if (GET_TEAM(ePlayer).isDefensivePact(eTradeTeam))
          iValue *= 3;

  All players on the same team therefore carry identical OB/DP relationship
  state into every pre-cancellation member valuation.

Concrete two-member Open-Borders case:
  Let A1 and A2 share Team A, and T be the proposed war target.

  Team A has Open Borders with T and no other ordinary trade is required.

  startTeamTrade has created OB proxies involving both A1 and A2, so both can
  satisfy canStopTradingWithTeam(T).

  AI_declareWarTradeVal computes:
      stopTradeVal(T, A1, true)
    + stopTradeVal(T, A2, true)

  Both calls independently include the Open-Borders modifier.

  But actual embargo execution is sequential state mutation:
      A1.stopTradingWithTeam(T)
        -> kills A1's OB proxy with bKillTeam=true
        -> setOpenBorders(T,false)
        -> endTeamTrade removes all remaining A<->T OB proxies.

  At that point A2 has no second Open-Borders relation left to sacrifice.
  The lower-bound sum has counted one shared loss twice.

  With N hireling-team members the same shared relationship contribution can be
  repeated N times.

Defensive-Pact magnification:
  Defensive Pact is also one team-level relation with replicated proxies, but
  AI_stopTradingTradeVal applies:
      iValue *= 3
  for every member call while the pact is present.

  Thus the same shared DP loss can magnify every component of the N-member sum,
  even though the first actual cancellation removes the pact for the whole team.
  This makes the non-additivity substantially larger than the OB-only case.

Why this is independent of F294:
  F294 is the ordinary persistent-deal inventory scope error inside
  AI_stopTradingTradeVal:
      isBetween(TEAMID(ePlayer), eTradeTeam)
  admits teammate-owned resource/GPT deals and can violate exact-player
  CvDeal accessor contracts.

  Repairing F294 to:
      isBetween(ePlayer, eTradeTeam)
  correctly makes player-owned annual losses disjoint across member calls.

  F295 survives unchanged after that repair because the Open-Borders modifier
  and Defensive-Pact multiplier are explicit team-state terms outside the
  ordinary-deal loop. Every member call still sees the same shared team
  relationship before any hypothetical cancellation has been applied.

History / introduced intent:
  AdvCiv practical 2930, commit
      a16555656d83d7bc92067d6c1156ce0303d1f69d
  "Fix minor issue with war trade val computation"
  changed the prior leader-only embargo lower bound into the current
  member-summed form.

  Commit message:
      "The lower bound based on the embargo trade value hadn't been calculated
       correctly at all. [advc.104o]"

  The introduced source comment is explicit about the model:
      "Don't charge much less than for an embargo. An embargo (weirdly)
       would only compel one player to stop trading with the (whole) target team,
       so we need to sum up the embargo trade values of the members of this team."

  That rationale correctly identifies the player scope of ordinary embargo
  cancellation. It does not account for the fact that OB/DP are team-level
  exceptions whose first member cancellation removes the relationship globally.

  No later substantive repair to that member-sum pattern was found in current
  Base AdvCiv 1.14; SAS inherits it. K-Mod/Civ4CE do not contain this later
  AdvCiv member-summed lower-bound design in the same form.

Cross-check against normal relationship valuation:
  CvTeamAI::AI_openBordersTradeVal(eTeam) returns:
      getNumCities() + target.getNumCities()

  CvTeamAI::AI_defensivePactTradeVal(eTeam) returns the same team quantity * 3.

  Both are naturally team-scoped and priced once for the relationship, which is
  consistent with the actual state lifetime and inconsistent with treating OB/DP
  as N independently cancelable player assets.

Why this is not merely a heuristic disagreement:
  AI_stopTradingTradeVal is heuristic, but F295 does not assert that its absolute
  OB/DP price is objectively correct or incorrect. The provable defect is the
  decomposition boundary used by AI_declareWarTradeVal:
    * the comment says member values are summed to model the losses of multiple
      player-scoped embargoes;
    * ordinary player deals are disjoint under that decomposition;
    * shared team agreements are not disjoint;
    * the code nevertheless evaluates their same pre-state contribution once in
      every member summand.

  Therefore the result changes with the number of players sharing the same team
  even when the team-level relationship being sacrificed is unchanged.

Gameplay consequence:
  The inflated sum is multiplied by 0.83 and used as a lower bound for
  AI_declareWarTradeVal. On multi-member hireling teams, especially with a
  Defensive Pact to the target, this can make a war bribe more expensive or
  unattainable because a shared relationship cost is counted repeatedly.

Repair boundary:
  Do not divide the whole embargo sum by team size. Player-owned resource/GPT
  losses really are additive and should still be summed per member.

  The robust decomposition is:
    1. Sum each member's player-owned cancelable ordinary-deal loss, using the
       exact-player scope required by F294.
    2. Evaluate shared team-level relationship loss (Open Borders / Defensive
       Pact and any analogous team agreement) once for the hireling team.
    3. Combine those once before applying the 0.83 embargo lower bound.

  Implementation could expose a flag/helper that suppresses shared OB/DP terms
  in per-player AI_stopTradingTradeVal calls, then add one team-level component;
  or separate AI_stopTradingTradeVal into player-deal and team-relationship
  components explicitly.

  Preserve:
    * normal one-player-team behavior;
    * ordinary direct TRADE_EMBARGO valuation, where one player's embargo really
      can terminate the shared relation and should still charge for doing so;
    * the member sum for genuinely separate player-owned trades;
    * UWAI/legacy base war valuation before the embargo lower bound.

Queue state after this checkpoint:
  queue 042 CvGameCoreDLL/CvDeal.cpp — still OPEN
  F281-F295 / provisional KI#604-KI#618 — confirmed
  F296 / provisional KI#619 — UNUSED / next

Remaining saturation cursor:
  * finish the old-CvDeal repair-stream ledger and verify that each substantive
    historical fix is either preserved, absorbed by F281-F295, or explicitly
    rejected as a control;
  * rerun the complete method/classification/accessor/serialization inventory
    against the final finding set so no family was skipped;
  * re-challenge the last cross-item state transitions only where one item can
    invalidate a sibling after whole-bundle prevalidation;
  * if no independent F296 survives, close queue 042 rather than inventing one.

No repository source files modified.

C025-WIP21 ADDENDUM — queue 042 CvDeal.cpp / annual-deal attitude-cache timing
F296 / provisional KI#619 confirmed; F297 unused
================================================================================

F296 / provisional KI#619
Title:
  Annual-deal rival-trade attitude refresh is deferred for only one deal
  direction; the other direction updates third-party attitude caches mid-loop,
  making later resentment depend on CvDeal orientation / deal iteration order.

Root:
  AdvCiv practical 3309 added a bUpdateAttitude switch specifically to defer
  annual-deal attitude-cache refreshes until CvGame::doDeals has processed all
  deals. The current CvDeal::doTurn applies that switch only to the SECOND trade
  direction:

      if (getLengthSecond() > 0)
      {
          ...
          GET_PLAYER(getFirstPlayer()).AI_processPeacetimeTradeValue(
                  getSecondPlayer(), iValue);
          // or AI_processPeacetimeGrantValue(..., iValue)
          // ^ default bUpdateAttitude == true
      }

      if (getLengthFirst() > 0)
      {
          ...
          GET_PLAYER(getSecondPlayer()).AI_processPeacetimeTradeValue(
                  getFirstPlayer(), iValue, false);
          // grant path also passes false explicitly
      }

  The comment immediately below says the intended opposite:
      "we do not update attitudes of particular players here,
       but instead update all of them at the game turn boundary
       [advc: i.e. in CvGame::doDeals]."

  CvGame::doDeals indeed does:
      verifyDeals();
      FOR_EACH_DEAL_VAR(pLoopDeal)
          pLoopDeal->doTurn();
      CvPlayerAI::AI_updateAttitudes();

  Therefore first-direction annual value processing is the lone premature cache
  refresh inside the deal loop.

Why default true actually updates third-party caches:
  AI_processPeacetimeTradeValue / GrantValue forwards bUpdateAttitude into
  AI_processPeacetimeValue.

  For each third-party team that resents the trade:
      kThirdParty.AI_changeEnemyPeacetimeTradeValue(
          TEAMID(eFromPlayer), ..., bUpdateAttitude);

  CvTeamAI::AI_setEnemyPeacetimeTradeValue then does:
      if (bUpdateAttitude)
          AI_updateAttitude(eIndex, false);

  CvTeamAI::AI_updateAttitude iterates the member players and recomputes their
  cached m_aiAttitude toward the affected team.

  The false parameter there suppresses worst-enemy recomputation only; it does
  NOT suppress the attitude-cache refresh itself.

Why a later annual deal can observe that premature refresh:
  CvPlayerAI::AI_processPeacetimeValue calculates each new rival-trade increment
  through:
      kThirdParty.AI_enemyTradeResentmentFactor(
          eTo, eFrom, ...);

  AI_enemyTradeResentmentFactor reads cached attitude values:
      AI_getAttitude(...)
      AI_getAttitudeVal(eFrom)
      AI_getAttitudeVal(AI_getWorstEnemy())

  and builds:
      iAttitudeDiff =
          AI_getAttitudeVal(eFrom)
        - ...
        - AI_getAttitudeVal(AI_getWorstEnemy())
        + ...
      r = iAttitudeDiff / 5
  (clamped to the documented bounds).

  Meanwhile AI_updateAttitude includes AI_getRivalTradeAttitude, and
  AI_getRivalTradeAttitude is directly derived from the just-changed
  EnemyPeacetimeTrade/Grant values. A sufficiently large increment, or any
  increment crossing an existing rounding threshold, can therefore change the
  cached integer attitude that the next resentment-factor calculation reads.

Clean supported two-deal reproducer:
  Let:
    E = an AI third party
    W = E's current worst-enemy team
    X = another civ/team

  Suppose there are two mature cancelable annual deals whose recurring value
  includes X giving something valuable to W. Multiple persistent deals between
  the same player pair are supported by CvGame's deal container; AdvCiv's
  AI_foldDeals only folds the narrow AI-AI opposite GPT-for-single-resource case,
  and human-involved/resource arrangements remain ordinary separate deals.

  Deal D1 is stored:
      firstPlayer  = W
      secondPlayer = X
  with X's annual item in secondList.

  D1::doTurn therefore executes the FIRST processing branch:
      W.AI_processPeacetime*(X, value)
  with default bUpdateAttitude=true.

  Because W is E's worst enemy, E can record RivalTrade resentment against X for
  trading with W. That increment immediately recomputes E's cached attitude
  toward X.

  Deal D2, processed later in FOR_EACH_DEAL order, again evaluates X trading
  with W. Its call to:
      E.AI_enemyTradeResentmentFactor(W, X, ...)
  now sees the post-D1 cached E->X attitude rather than the turn-boundary cache.
  Since the factor explicitly uses attitude(X) relative to attitude(worstEnemy),
  D1 can alter D2's resentment multiplier.

Orientation proof:
  Store the economically same X->W annual item with participants reversed:
      firstPlayer  = X
      secondPlayer = W
  and X's item in firstList.

  W receives exactly the same recurring value, but it is now processed by the
  SECOND CvDeal::doTurn branch:
      W.AI_processPeacetime*(X, value, false)

  No E->X cache refresh occurs until the global CvGame::doDeals update.
  Therefore a subsequent deal in the same deal loop can receive a different
  rival-trade multiplier solely from which endpoint happened to occupy
  CvDeal::firstPlayer.

  This is not theoretical undefined list ordering: CvGame::implementAndReturnDeal
  preserves the caller's eWho/eOtherWho identities directly as first/second
  players, so storage orientation is part of deal construction rather than a
  canonical ordering by player/team ID.

Magnitude / threshold note:
  AI attitude is integer-cached, while rival-trade value uses a nonlinear
  diminishing-return calculation and rounding. Not every small annual increment
  changes the cached integer attitude. F296 does not require every deal to show
  the effect; an existing RivalTrade value near an attitude rounding boundary,
  or a sufficiently valuable recurring increment, makes the feedback live.
  Once the cached value changes, AI_enemyTradeResentmentFactor uses it
  immediately before the intended global refresh point.

History:
  This is an AdvCiv practical-3309 regression/partial fix, commit:
      a8192ca7faab182fa7dfa589c097c83a23f07509
      "Fix timing of attitude cache update during turn sequence"

  Commit message:
      "Needs to happen after each player turn; after the team turn isn't enough.
       [advc.001]

       There were also some unnecessary updates, in part due to change
       [advc.130p] (I think)."

  The commit:
    * added bUpdateAttitude to AI_processPeacetimeTradeValue,
      AI_processPeacetimeGrantValue and downstream enemy-value setters;
    * changed CvGame::doDeals from updating only direct trade participants to a
      global all-major-civ attitude refresh after all CvDeal::doTurn calls;
    * explicitly passed false in CvDeal::doTurn's SECOND-direction trade/grant
      calls;
    * did NOT change the symmetric FIRST-direction calls, which therefore kept
      the new default=true;
    * updated the local comment to explicitly identify CvGame::doDeals as the
      deferred refresh point.

  Base AdvCiv 1.14 still has this exact one-sided false/default-true shape.
  SAS inherits it unchanged.
  K-Mod predates the bUpdateAttitude mechanism; its doTurn comment already said
  attitudes should be updated at the game-turn boundary, but its enemy-value
  setters updated caches immediately. Practical 3309 was AdvCiv's attempt to
  repair/refine that timing and left one half behind.
  Civ4CE follows the older BtS/K-Mod-style path and does not contain this
  partial AdvCiv switch in the same form.

Why this is independent of F293:
  F293 is lossy scalar representation of multiple brokered political targets
  during initial trade-value processing.
  F296 concerns recurring annual CvDeal::doTurn processing with no brokered
  peace/war target at all; its defect is one-sided cache-update timing.

Why this is independent of F282:
  F282 is cancellation-memory accumulation (setter vs additive changer).
  F296 modifies neither cancellation nor memory. It changes third-party cached
  attitude timing while annual trade/grant values continue to accumulate.

Repair boundary:
  Make the two annual directions symmetric and honor practical 3309's own stated
  game-turn-boundary contract:

      GET_PLAYER(getFirstPlayer()).AI_processPeacetimeTradeValue(
          getSecondPlayer(), iValue, false);

      GET_PLAYER(getFirstPlayer()).AI_processPeacetimeGrantValue(
          getSecondPlayer(), iValue, false);

  The already-correct second-direction calls remain false.

  Do NOT globally change the default bUpdateAttitude to false. Other callers
  intentionally process immediate events outside the CvGame::doDeals batch,
  including unit gifts and newly implemented diplomacy, and rely on the normal
  default update semantics.

  Keep CvGame::doDeals' final CvPlayerAI::AI_updateAttitudes() call; it is the
  synchronization point practical 3309 established precisely so all recurring
  deal-value changes are visible together after the batch.

Queue state after this checkpoint:
  queue 042 CvGameCoreDLL/CvDeal.cpp — still OPEN
  F281-F296 / provisional KI#604-KI#619 — confirmed
  F297 / provisional KI#620 — UNUSED / next

  * finish the substantive CvDeal history ledger after practical 3309 and prove
    no later repair stream leaves another adjacent invariant;
  * complete the transaction-order matrix (tech / civic / religion /
    war / peace / embargo / city / PA / vassal) against F286/F288-F292;
  * re-run small method, serialization and cancellation-family inventory against
    the final finding map;
  * if no independent F297 survives, close queue 042 cleanly rather than
    manufacturing one.

F294 same-root extension — embargo denial also uses the wrong team scope
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

The final accessor-consumer sweep found a second live consumer of the same
player-vs-team embargo-scope invariant already established by F294.

CvPlayer::stopTradingWithTeam is explicitly player-scoped:
    if (!pLoopDeal->isBetween(getID(), eTeam))
        continue;

Only deals belonging to the particular player who enacts the embargo are
cancelled. This is also stated by the isTradingWithTeam source comment:
    "an embargo will affect only the enacting player - but the entire target
     team."

F294 already established that CvPlayerAI::AI_stopTradingTradeVal violates this
contract by selecting ordinary deals with:
    pLoopDeal->isBetween(TEAMID(ePlayer), eTradeTeam)

The denial path CvPlayerAI::AI_stopTradingTrade contains the same scope error
when trying to protect peace reparations:

    if (GET_TEAM(getTeam()).isForcePeace(eTradeTeam))
    {
        FOR_EACH_DEAL(d)
        {
            if (!d->isBetween(getTeam(), eTradeTeam))
                continue;
            ...
            FOR_EACH_TRADE_ITEM(d->getGivesList(getTeam()))
            {
                if (type == TRADE_PEACE_TREATY)
                    bPeaceTreaty = true;
                if (type == TRADE_RESOURCES || type == TRADE_GOLD_PER_TURN)
                    bAnnualPayment = true;
            }
            if (bPeaceTreaty && bAnnualPayment)
                return DENIAL_RECENT_CANCEL;
        }
    }

On a multi-member Team A, player A1 can therefore refuse an embargo against T
because teammate A2 has a reparations deal with T, even though
A1.stopTradingWithTeam(T) would not cancel A2's player-owned annual payment.

This does not warrant a new finding number:
  * the underlying invariant is identical to F294 — valuation/denial asks what
    one player loses by stopping trade, but searches the whole team;
  * exact-player scoping is the same repair boundary;
  * the previously established F285 list-orientation problem in reparations
    recognition is separate and still needs its own treaty-anywhere correction.

F294 repair review should therefore cover BOTH:
  1. AI_stopTradingTradeVal ordinary-deal inventory:
         isBetween(ePlayer, eTradeTeam)
     plus player-scoped getGivesList/getReceivesList/getOtherPlayer;
  2. AI_stopTradingTrade reparations-preservation scan:
         isBetween(getID(), eTradeTeam)
     and then recognize the peace marker anywhere in that exact player's deal
     while checking annual reparations actually given by getID() (F285 boundary).

Do not replace these with TEAMID/getTeam merely because the embargo target is a
team. Target scope is team-wide; enacting-owner scope is player-specific.

Final accessor / serialization / lifecycle controls
----------------------------------------------------

The small-method surface has now been rerun against the full queue-042 finding
map rather than merely assumed safe.

* CvDeal::write / read:
  ID, initial turn, first player, second player, first list and second list are
  serialized/deserialized in matching order. No missing current member.

* reset / uninit:
  both trade lists are cleared and all serialized scalar members reset. There is
  no extra owned heap state in CvDeal.

* getOtherPlayer(PlayerTypes), getGivesList(PlayerTypes),
  getReceivesList(PlayerTypes):
  exact-player assertions are intentional and useful. The F294 violation is in
  a caller that admits teammate deals before invoking these accessors.

* getGivesList(TeamTypes), getReceivesList(TeamTypes):
  deliberately require exactly one endpoint to belong to the queried team.
  Current live team-typed consumers were enumerated:
    - CvPlayerAI embargo valuation / denial: F294 family;
    - CvTeam::freeVassal: team distinction is valid before the vassal proxy is
      killed;
    - CvDeal::isUncancelableVassalDeal: explicitly returns before the accessor
      when both endpoints have become the same team.
  No additional independent same-team consumer survived beyond F290/F294.

* isDisengage:
  its first-list-only item check is safe for the real representation.
  Disengagement is created through startTeamTrade(..., bDual=true), so each
  proxy contains one TRADE_DISENGAGE item in both lists. The item also lies
  beyond NUM_TRADEABLE_ITEMS and is not an ordinary voluntary trade-table
  choice.

* isVassalTributeDeal(CLinkList*):
  returns true for an empty list vacuously, but meaningful callers additionally
  require the opposite/value conditions that make an empty persistent deal
  irrelevant. CvGame::implementAndReturnDeal immediately kills a newly-created
  CvDeal whose two saved lists are both empty.

* CvDeal::doTurn empty-list head access:
  for a persistent deal both lists cannot be empty under the normal creation /
  deletion lifecycle. The apparently unsafe getFirstList().head() expression is
  therefore protected by representation plus short-circuiting for one-sided
  deals. No live null-head root established.

* isAllDual / isAnnual / isDual / hasData / isEndWar:
  every current TradeableItems family has been reconciled. PA's "annual"
  classification does not create a recurring PA deal because the PA item itself
  is not saved; the classification is used by generic trade/UI/value machinery.
  No independent state-lifetime defect established there.

Representation-debt siblings absorbed by existing findings
-----------------------------------------------------------

Several final first-list-only observations are real asymmetries but not new
roots:

1. CvDeal::kill determines "forced" cancellation sound/visibility by looking for
   dual items only in getFirstList(). Normally this is sufficient because OB,
   DP and disengagement proxies are dual. A legitimate one-sided
   TRADE_PEACE_TREATY in the second list is the exception and can therefore miss
   the dual-item bForce path. This is a diagnostic/UI sibling of F281's
   one-sided peace-treaty representation, not a new gameplay root.

2. CvTeam::setVassal still contains first-list peace-treaty cleanup inherited
   from the same representation assumption. This belongs in the F281/F283
   repair review; fixing only CvDeal::isPeaceDeal or resetDualDeal would leave
   another consumer of the outdated "peace marker lives in first list" model.

3. Other first-list-only checks for OB/DP/disengagement remain safe because
   startTeamTrade creates those proxy items symmetrically or in a fixed
   orientation known to the consumer.

Rejected transaction candidate — Open Borders + Disengagement
--------------------------------------------------------------

A synthetic bundle containing TRADE_OPEN_BORDERS and TRADE_DISENGAGE would be
order-sensitive: setOpenBorders(true) cancels disengagement, then a later
TRADE_DISENGAGE start could restore the disengage flag without rechecking OB.

This is not a normal accepted trade state:
  * TRADE_DISENGAGE is declared after NUM_TRADEABLE_ITEMS;
  * ordinary trade-table iteration does not offer it;
  * its live producer is CvTeam::makePeace -> signDisengage ->
    startTeamTrade(TRADE_DISENGAGE, ..., true);
  * capitulation suppresses the disengagement producer;
  * while the negotiating teams are still at war, OB/DP cannot independently
    prevalidate.

No F297.

Rejected transaction candidate — brokered peace with master + vassal
--------------------------------------------------------------------

Raw TRADE_PEACE inventory construction iterates third teams and can enumerate a
vassal at the game-rule level, so a master+vassal pair initially looked capable
of being redundantly priced: CvTeam::makePeace(master) cascades peace to the
master's vassals.

The AI denial contract closes the producer:
    CvTeamAI::AI_makePeaceTrade:
        if (GET_TEAM(ePeaceTeam).isAVassal())
            return DENIAL_VASSAL;

TRADE_PEACE itself is only offered by nonhuman givers
(CvPlayer::canPossiblyTradeItem returns false when the giving team is human).
AI_considerOffer applies getTradeDenial to every item the AI gives.

Therefore an accepted ordinary deal cannot contain the redundant
TRADE_PEACE(master) + TRADE_PEACE(vassal) pair. No F297.

Tech / resource / civic / religion transaction controls retained
-----------------------------------------------------------------

* Tech + resource self-obsolescence:
  resource prevalidation checks bonus obsolescence for BOTH giver and recipient;
  if one side already owns the obsoleting tech needed for the cross-item
  scenario, the resource item is rejected before implementation.

* Tech that newly enables another item:
  whole-bundle prevalidation occurs before the tech is transferred, so the
  newly-enabled civic/tech/etc. item fails conservatively rather than being
  accepted and then invalidated.

* Same-column multiple civics and duplicate religions:
  AI_checkCivicReligionConsistency explicitly rejects these accepted-offer
  states.

* Different civic columns:
  deliberately supported and therefore remain the exact F291 case.

* Multiple GOLD / GPT instances:
  normal trade-table representation exposes one editable item of each kind
  rather than an arbitrary duplicated-item producer. No independent normal
  duplicate-obligation root established.

Remaining single candidate before closure
-----------------------------------------

The only transaction candidate still under active challenge is multiple
TRADE_WAR items under the supported legacy/K-Mod-war-AI configuration where
UWAI is disabled.

Full UWAI explicitly makes a second hired war unaffordable:
    "Can't be hired for more than one war at a time"
    iWars > 1 -> +1,000,000 value.

When UWAI is disabled, legacy valuation can accept multiple war items. If two
targets have a Defensive Pact, the first primary hired declaration can cause the
second target to enter the war through the DP cascade before its own prevalidated
TRADE_WAR executes. The second CvTeam::declareWar then returns because the teams
are already at war, while surrounding sponsorship-memory code still runs.

This is suspicious but not yet promoted:
  * the sponsor explicitly requested both war states;
  * both requested final war relationships do exist;
  * it remains to prove that the second item is semantically supposed to buy a
    distinct primary declaration rather than merely guarantee the war state;
  * full UWAI intentionally prohibits the multi-war bundle, narrowing exposure
    to the supported legacy/K-Mod-war-AI mode.

F297 remains UNUSED pending that last contract check.

C025-WIP23 ADDENDUM — queue 042 CvDeal.cpp / legacy multi-war bundle
F297 / provisional KI#620 confirmed; F298 unused
