QUEUE 001 DEEP RE-AUDIT — WIP18 ADDENDUM
=========================================

F333 / provisional KI#656 -- AI_checkCancel treats a dual item at the head of a mixed annual bundle as the whole deal and skips later resource/dual cancellation denials
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT / CONTRACT
---------------
AdvCiv's advc.133 cancellation refactor explicitly separates two kinds of checks:

1. AI_considerOffer(..., iChange=-1) decides whether the *aggregate economics* of the ongoing deal are still acceptable.
2. Because aggregate value is insufficient for resource cancellation policy, AI_checkCancel then explicitly re-runs cancellation-specific resource denial through AI_bonusTrade(..., iChange=0).

The source comment says this directly:

    Resource trades do need special treatment.
    For duals (Open Borders, Def. Pact, Perm. Alliance), getTradeDenial
    is all right.

But the implementation does not classify every item. It inspects only the first outgoing item:

    pNode = kDeal.getGivesList(getID()).head();
    if (pNode != NULL && CvDeal::isDual(pNode->m_data.m_eItemType, true))
    {
        DenialTypes eDenial = getTradeDenial(ePlayer, pNode->m_data);
        ...
        else return NO_CANCEL;
    }

That unconditional return means a dual item at the head converts the *entire outgoing list* into the dual-only path. The later loops that inspect every outgoing and incoming resource are never reached.

SUPPORTED MIXED-DEAL PRODUCER
-----------------------------
Mixed dual + resource/GPT annual bundles are supported, not a malformed-save construction.

- CvDeal::isAnnual classifies Resources, GPT, Open Borders, Defensive Pact and Permanent Alliance as annual.
- CvPlayer::updateTradeList deliberately allows AI-human peacetime offers to mix items so long as the first offered item and later items share annual/nonannual status. Therefore selecting a dual annual item does not hide Resources/GPT.
- CvDeal::doTurn explicitly documents the engine reality:

      "In multiplayer, dual deals can be mixed with e.g. gold per turn"

  and handles mixed dual deals separately from the one-item pure-dual fast path.
- CvDeal::addTradeItems persists the supplied list order by iterating the offer and insertAtEnd'ing each saved item. There is no deal-layer normalization that extracts dual items into a separate deal.

Therefore a persisted outgoing list whose head is Open Borders/Defensive Pact and which also contains a resource is a supported annual-deal representation. The bug does not require corrupt data or an unsupported item-class mixture.

CLEAN CURRENT REPRODUCTION
--------------------------
Alexander gives a particularly clean current-XML example:

    StrategicBonusRefuseAttitudeThreshold = ATTITUDE_CAUTIOUS
    OpenBordersRefuseAttitudeThreshold    = ATTITUDE_ANNOYED

1. Human H and Alexander A have accessible territory and relations high enough (e.g. Pleased) to establish a mature annual bundle:

       A gives: Open Borders + Iron
       H gives: Open Borders + enough GPT / other annual compensation

   The exact compensation is not important; it only needs to keep the whole deal economically acceptable when reviewed later.

2. After the deal becomes cancelable, A's attitude toward H falls to Cautious, while H is not A's worst enemy and the existing Open Borders still gives territorial access.

3. `AI_considerOffer(...,-1)` can still accept the *aggregate* bundle because H's compensation makes the package sufficiently valuable. Cancellation mode deliberately does not run ordinary per-item `getTradeDenial` for A's outgoing items.

4. Current Open Borders denial remains NO_DENIAL:
   - Cautious is above Alexander's Annoyed OB refusal threshold;
   - territory is accessible;
   - no recent-cancel / worst-enemy condition is required for the reproduction.

5. Current Iron resource denial is different. `AI_bonusTrade(IRON, H, 0)` identifies Iron as strategic from current unit prerequisites and rejects at Cautious because Alexander's strategic-resource refusal threshold is Cautious:

       eAttitude <= iRefusalThresh  -> DENIAL_ATTITUDE

6. If Open Borders is the saved outgoing head, AI_checkCancel enters the dual block. Because OB itself has NO_DENIAL, the function executes:

       else return NO_CANCEL;

   and never reaches the subsequent per-resource loop.

7. The AI therefore continues exporting Iron despite its current resource-trade policy explicitly saying that it should refuse/cancel that export. The identical Iron deal without a dual item at the head reaches AI_bonusTrade(...,0) and is canceled.

WHY AI_considerOffer DOES NOT REPAIR THIS
-----------------------------------------
This is not duplicate economics checking.

The whole reason advc.133 added the later resource loops is that `getTradeDenial` / resource policy and aggregate deal value are different contracts during cancellation. A human can compensate the AI generously enough that `AI_considerOffer` still considers the package fair while the AI nevertheless has a policy reason not to export a strategic/happiness/health resource anymore.

The head-dual early return bypasses that deliberate second contract.

BROADER SAME-ROOT CONSEQUENCE
-----------------------------
The same classifier mistake can hide later dual items too. Human-facing annual bundles may contain more than one dual item; checking only the head dual and returning NO_CANCEL means a later Defensive Pact/Open Borders/Permanent Alliance denial is not consulted either.

The resource case is the strongest reproduction because AdvCiv explicitly added full-list resource cancellation loops and the current source comment says those checks are necessary. Treat later-dual suppression as a same-root extension, not a second finding.

ANCESTRY
--------
- K-Mod cancellation primarily relied on aggregate `AI_considerOffer(...,-1)` and did not contain the current AdvCiv full resource-denial follow-up pipeline.
- AdvCiv advc.133 factored cancellation into AI_checkCancel and added the special per-resource cancellation checks, but placed them behind a head-only dual fast path with an unconditional NO_CANCEL return.
- Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current AdvCiv-SAS contain the same structure; SAS has not introduced this defect locally.

So F333 is an inherited AdvCiv cancellation-classification bug exposed by a supported mixed annual deal shape.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
No earlier album root found in the current sweep owns "head dual suppresses later resource/dual cancellation denials."

Distinct nearby roots:
- F321/KI#644: wrong *prospective resource valuation* when a cancellation is actually evaluated. F333 can prevent the resource-specific cancellation evaluation from happening at all.
- F332/KI#655: AI_foldDeals restarts deal maturity and temporarily prevents AI_checkCancel from running at all. F333 applies once a deal is mature and AI_checkCancel does run.
- F281-F287 / queue 042: CvDeal list-orientation / peace / transaction-lifetime problems; none owns AI_checkCancel's first-item whole-list classification.
- KI#241 confirms mixed resource/GPT deal representation but does not cover cancellation policy.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Do not use the first outgoing item as a whole-deal classifier.

A narrow robust structure is:
1. let AI_considerOffer perform aggregate economics as now;
2. iterate *all* outgoing dual items and evaluate each current getTradeDenial independently (preserving the DP immediate-cancel special case / probabilistic behavior as intended);
3. independently iterate *all* outgoing resources with AI_bonusTrade(...,0);
4. independently iterate all incoming resources for the recipient-side DENIAL_JOKING check;
5. return NO_CANCEL only after every relevant item class has been examined.

If the intended design is that a denial on any dual should govern the whole mixed bundle, that can still be expressed explicitly without preventing resource checks merely because another dual happens to be first.

QUEUE 001 DEEP RE-AUDIT — WIP19 CORRECTION / SUPERSEDING WIP18 F333
===================================================================

AUDIT CORRECTION — WIP18 F333 IS RETRACTED; F333 RETURNS TO UNUSED
------------------------------------------------------------------
WIP18 promoted a plausible `AI_checkCancel` mixed-dual/resource defect before the persistent-deal creation path had been fully reconciled. The next lifecycle pass invalidates the required current producer.

The raw source shape remains real:

    pNode = kDeal.getGivesList(getID()).head();
    if (pNode != NULL && CvDeal::isDual(pNode->m_data.m_eItemType, true))
    {
        ...
        else return NO_CANCEL;
    }

and would indeed skip later resource checks *if* a current persistent AI deal could contain a non-peace dual item followed by resources/GPT.

CURRENT PERSISTENT REPRESENTATION PREVENTS THAT NORMAL PRODUCER
--------------------------------------------------------------
The missing piece is `CvDeal::startTrade`.

Normal diplomacy items are created through `setTradeItem`, whose default `iData` is 0. For the non-peace dual/team items used by `AI_checkCancel`:

- TRADE_OPEN_BORDERS:
      if (trade.m_iData <= 0)
          startTeamTrade(..., true);
      else bSave = true;

- TRADE_DEFENSIVE_PACT:
      same contract;

- TRADE_DISENGAGE:
      same positive-proxy contract;

- TRADE_PERMANENT_ALLIANCE:
      never saved as a persistent trade item in `startTrade` at all.

`startTeamTrade` constructs its own fresh lists:

    TradeData item(eItem, 1);
    ourList.insertAtEnd(item);
    if (bDual)
        theirList.insertAtEnd(item);
    implementDeal(..., ourList, theirList);

Those generated proxy deals contain only the dual/team item. The outer negotiated deal continues separately and saves resources/GPT, but not the original zero-data Open Borders/DP item.

A repository-wide current-source search found no other DLL producer of positive-data Open Borders/Defensive Pact trade items. `resetDualDeal` only refreshes the lifetime of already-existing proxy deals; it does not merge resource/GPT terms into them. `AI_foldDeals` handles only resource/GPT deals and cannot create a mixed dual bundle.

WHY THE `CvDeal::doTurn` COMMENT IS NOT ENOUGH
----------------------------------------------
`CvDeal::doTurn` still contains the historical comment:

    "In multiplayer, dual deals can be mixed with e.g. gold per turn"

That is useful caution but not sufficient producer proof under the current representation. The current DLL construction path above actively splits normal team-agreement items into dedicated positive-data proxy deals. Without an identified current EXE/network path that supplies an already-positive dual item together with resource/GPT terms to an AI-party persistent deal, the old comment cannot justify numbering the hypothetical mixed-list behavior.

`TRADE_PEACE_TREATY` can genuinely coexist with annual reparations in one persistent deal, but `AI_checkCancel` deliberately calls:

    CvDeal::isDual(item, true)

which excludes peace treaties from this head-dual fast path. Therefore the known mixed peace/reparations representation does not revive WIP18 F333.

RESULT
------
- WIP18's F333 / provisional KI#656 is RETRACTED.
- F333 / provisional KI#656 is UNUSED again.
- The head-dual `AI_checkCancel` structure may deserve defensive hardening against malformed/legacy/custom-created mixed lists, but no supported current producer has been established.
- This correction is exactly the conservative audit standard: an attractive source shape is not a finding without a live representation path.

RELATED CONTROL — AI_stopTradingTradeVal FIRST-LIST OPEN-BORDERS SKIP
---------------------------------------------------------------------
The same representation reconciliation also prevents a tempting duplicate/new root in `AI_stopTradingTradeVal`:

    if (pLoopDeal->isPeaceDeal() ||
        pLoopDeal->getLengthFirst() > 0 &&
        pLoopDeal->getFirstList().head()->m_data.m_eItemType == TRADE_OPEN_BORDERS)
        continue;

For current normally-created Open Borders state, the persistent OB proxy is a dedicated pure dual deal, so skipping that proxy after pricing the team-level OB relationship is coherent. No current mixed OB+resource persistent producer has been proved here either.

Existing queue-042 F294/F295 remain the real independent `AI_stopTradingTradeVal` defects:
- F294: team-scoped ordinary-deal inventory where the embargo is player-scoped;
- F295: repeated team-level OB/DP loss across multi-member war-bribe member sums.
Do not create another root from the head-OB skip without a current mixed persistent producer.

CONTROL — AI_civicTradeVal / AI_religionTradeVal payer-side multiplier is intentional
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The final AdvCiv multipliers initially looked like a PlayerTypes orientation mistake:

    // This CvPlayer asks ePlayer to switch to eCivic.
    ...
    if (!isCivic(eCivic))
        iValue *= 2;

and:

    if (getStateReligion() != eReligion)
        iValue *= 2;

The target whose switching cost is otherwise evaluated is ePlayer / kPlayer, whereas
these final conditions deliberately inspect `this` (the requester/payor).

This is NOT a side-identity defect. AdvCiv history explicitly confirms the intended
contract. The 2024-10-27 advc.132 UI commit says the espionage cost breakdown should
warn that the cost is increased when the spy owner does not practise the chosen civic
or religion, and emphasizes that allowing a player to choose a civic/religion other
than its own is deliberate AdvCiv behavior rather than a bug.

That maps exactly to these payer-side conditions. `AI_civicTradeVal` and
`AI_religionTradeVal` are also reused by the force-civic / force-religion espionage
valuation path, where `this` is the spy owner and ePlayer is the target. Therefore no
F333 arises from the apparent requester/target asymmetry.


F333 / provisional KI#656 — AI_bonusTrade's "disregard obsolete units" filter runs after strategic classification and therefore has no effect
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

CLASSIFICATION
--------------
Independent inherited AdvCiv / Better-AI logic defect in CvPlayerAI::AI_bonusTrade.
Current SAS data provides a direct gameplay consequence. Not a tuning disagreement.

ROOT CAUSE
----------
`AI_bonusTrade` tries to classify a resource as strategically important only while it
still enables relevant military units. The imported Better-AI fragment says:

    // <advc.001> Fuyu, Better AI: Strategic For Current Era, 22.07.2010
    // disregard obsolete units
    if (pCapital != NULL && pCapital->allUpgradesAvailable(eUnit) != NO_UNIT)
        continue;

But the function has already inspected the same unit's resource requirements and set
`bStrategic` / `bCrucialStrategic` BEFORE this test:

    if (GC.getInfo(eUnit).getPrereqAndBonus() == eBonus)
    {
        bStrategic = true;
        bCrucialStrategic = true;
    }
    for (... prereq-or bonuses ...)
    {
        if (... == eBonus)
        {
            bStrategic = true;
            bCrucialStrategic = true;
        }
    }

    // disregard obsolete units
    if (pCapital != NULL && pCapital->allUpgradesAvailable(eUnit) != NO_UNIT)
        continue;

There is no executable code after that `continue` inside the unit loop. Consequently,
for strategic classification the supposed obsolete-unit filter is a complete no-op.
Once any historical unit has ever required eBonus, that unit can set `bStrategic=true`
even when all of its upgrades are available and the unit is obsolete for this civ.

The placement is especially conspicuous because `AI_baseBonusUnitVal`, elsewhere in
this same file, performs the equivalent `allUpgradesAvailable` test as an actual value
filter and sets an obsolete unit's bonus value to zero.

CURRENT-DATA REPRODUCTION — COPPER
---------------------------------
Copper is a clean current SAS example because:

1. Current CIV4UnitInfos.xml has Copper as an AND/OR requirement for historical units
   including Axemen/Spearmen/Macemen and their UUs, Houfnice and Privateer.
2. Every current Copper-consuming unit has a later upgrade path. Examples:
   - Axeman / early UUs -> Maceman
   - Maceman / Samurai / Viking / Zhuge Nu / Disciplined Crossbowman -> Musketman
   - Spearman / Hoplite -> Pikeman
   - Houfnice -> Field Gun
   - Privateer -> Attack Submarine
3. At sufficiently advanced technology, `pCapital->allUpgradesAvailable(eUnit)` can
   therefore be non-NO_UNIT for every Copper-consuming unit.
4. Current CIV4BuildingInfos.xml has no building whose PrereqAndBonus or
   PrereqOrBonuses requires Copper. (Iron Works requires Coal + Iron, not Copper.)
5. Copper has 0 happiness and 0 health, so if it is no longer military/building
   strategic, no happiness/health attitude denial substitutes for the erroneous
   strategic one.
6. `AI_corporationBonusVal(Copper)` can be zero for an AI that currently has none of
   the Copper-using corporations in its cities.

A concrete late-game trade therefore reaches the bad behavior:

- AI Alexander has at least two available Copper copies, no Copper-using corporation,
  and has reached tech/unit availability where all current Copper military uses have
  available upgrades.
- Human H has no Copper.
- Alexander is Cautious toward H.
- Current XML gives Alexander
  `StrategicBonusRefuseAttitudeThreshold = ATTITUDE_CAUTIOUS`.
- `getTradeDenial(H, TRADE_RESOURCES:Copper)` calls
  `AI_bonusTrade(Copper, H, iChange=1)`.

Intended/current-era classification:
- every Copper-consuming unit is filtered as obsolete/upgraded;
- no building reclassifies Copper as strategic;
- Copper supplies neither happiness nor health;
- an extra copy with no corporation value can therefore proceed to the ordinary
  value checks without a strategic-attitude veto.

Actual classification:
- the first historical Copper unit sets `bStrategic=true` before the obsolete test;
- every later `continue` is too late to undo that state;
- `eAttitude <= StrategicBonusRefuseAttitudeThreshold` is true at Cautious;
- the AI returns `DENIAL_ATTITUDE` and refuses the export solely because obsolete
  military units are still counted as current strategic uses.

ANCESTRY
--------
Stock/Civ4CE and K-Mod classify strategic resources from historical unit/building
requirements without this current-era filter. AdvCiv imported the Better-AI/Fuyu
"Strategic For Current Era" repair (`advc.001`) and added `allUpgradesAvailable`, but
placed it after the state mutation it is supposed to guard. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and
current SAS retain the same ordering unchanged.

This is therefore best described as an INCOMPLETE / NONFUNCTIONAL AdvCiv repair: the
source explicitly says obsolete units should be disregarded, but the inserted control
cannot affect the strategic-classification result.

CONSEQUENCE
-----------
Resources whose military role has ended can remain subject to strategic-resource
attitude refusal indefinitely. That can hide/refuse otherwise reasonable surplus
exports and reduces late-game resource trading. Copper gives a current shipped-data
reproduction; the flaw is generic to any unit-resource whose current strategic uses
all become obsolete while no still-relevant building reclassifies it.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Filter the unit before mutating `bStrategic` / `bCrucialStrategic`, e.g. conceptually:

    FOR_EACH_ENUM2(Unit, eUnit)
    {
        if (pCapital != NULL &&
            pCapital->allUpgradesAvailable(eUnit) != NO_UNIT)
        {
            continue;
        }
        // only now inspect AND/OR bonus requirements
        ...
    }

Then retain the existing building pass so a resource with no current unit role can
still be classified strategic when a building genuinely requires it.

A narrower alternative is to compute per-unit `bUsesBonus`, perform the obsolete test,
and only then OR that surviving unit into the aggregate flags. Do not merely clear
`bStrategic` on an obsolete unit, because an earlier/later nonobsolete unit may have
already established a legitimate strategic use.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
No earlier numbered album root covers this obsolete-unit ordering failure.

- F321/KI#644 concerns prospective `iChange` in the *value* multiplier for strategic
  resources during cancellation.
- KI#239/KI#240 concern SAS hard dominated-resource buy denials and substitutes.
- F333 concerns the inherited *classification* used by `AI_bonusTrade` refusal policy:
  the intended current-era obsolete-unit filter is placed after its side effect.

The earlier WIP18 F333 (mixed dual/resource `AI_checkCancel`) remains retracted. The
number F333 / provisional KI#656 is now reused for this independently proved root.


OTHER TRADE-HELPER CONTROLS IN THIS SLICE
-----------------------------------------
- `AI_checkResourceLimits`'s `getNumAvailableBonuses - iChange` orientation is
  coherent for both acquisition (`+1`) and cancellation (`-1`): cancellation adds
  the exported copy back when asking whether it was non-surplus.
- `AI_civicTradeVal` / `AI_religionTradeVal` requester-side x2 is deliberate advc.132
  policy as documented above.
- `AI_stopTradingTradeVal` / `AI_stopTradingTrade` remain cross-referenced to existing
  queue-042 F285/F294/F295; no duplicate root is allocated here.

F334 / provisional KI#657 — AdvCiv's same-team cancellation exemption reads an uninitialized-to-policy sentinel and is permanently dead for bilateral deals
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

CLASSIFICATION
--------------
Independent inherited AdvCiv logic defect in `CvPlayerAI::AI_considerOffer`, introduced by the
advc.155 human-AI team trade policy. The source contains an explicit same-team cancellation
exemption, but its threshold is never computed on the bilateral-deal path that reaches it.

ROOT CAUSE
----------
After computing both sides' deal values, AdvCiv declares:

    int iThreshold = -1; // advc.155: Declaration moved up

The only assignment that turns `iThreshold` into the help/gift allowance occurs inside the
one-sided-gift branch:

    if (iTheyReceive > 0 && kTheyGive.getLength() == 0 && iWeReceive == 0)
    {
        ...
        iThreshold = kOurTeam.AI_getHasMetCounter(kPlayer.getTeam()) + 50;
        iThreshold *= 2;
        if (bSameTeam)
            iThreshold *= 5;
        ...
        iThreshold -= kPlayer.AI_getPeacetimeGrantValue(getID());
        ...
        return bAccept;
    }

That branch always returns. Therefore every bilateral deal proceeds with `iThreshold == -1`.

Later, during cancellation (`iChange < 0`), advc.155 adds a same-team special case:

    if (bSameTeam)
    {
        if (iTheyReceive < iThreshold)
            return true;
        iTolerance = 150;
    }

For ordinary nonnegative deal values, `iTheyReceive < -1` is impossible. The explicit threshold
exemption is therefore dead code on exactly the bilateral cancellation path where it appears.

The comment "Declaration moved up" is strong archaeology: advc.155 moved the variable's scope so
the later cancellation block could read it, but did not move or duplicate the threshold
calculation needed to make that read meaningful.

SUPPORTED PRODUCER / CONCRETE CONSEQUENCE
-----------------------------------------
Human-AI teammates can create ordinary persistent annual trades. AdvCiv deliberately removed the
older K-Mod shortcut that automatically returned NO_DENIAL for teammate resources; advc.155's
published purpose was instead to make human-AI team trading bounded by normal utility while still
allowing bounded help.

A concrete supported resource-for-resource lifecycle is enough:

1. Human H and AI A are on the same team (ordinary team game or Permanent Alliance).
2. A has multiple spare Wheat copies. H has spare Copper.
3. While Copper still has military utility for A, H offers Copper and A gives Wheat. The bilateral
   deal can pass the normal proposal valuation because A values the first useful Copper highly.
4. The deal matures past the mandatory no-cancel window.
5. Later A reaches the state already established for F333: all Copper-consuming military units
   have available upgrades, A has no Copper-using corporation, and `AI_bonusVal(Copper, ..., true)`
   can fall to zero. Wheat remains useful to H.
6. `AI_checkCancel` calls `AI_considerOffer(..., iChange=-1, ...)`.

At this point:
- `iWeReceive` (A's value for continuing to receive Copper) can be 0;
- `iTheyReceive` (the proxy value of H continuing to receive Wheat) remains positive;
- the deal is bilateral, so the one-sided gift branch — the only place that computes
  `iThreshold` — is skipped;
- `bSameTeam` is true, but `iTheyReceive < -1` is false;
- the forced same-team fairness tolerance then tests roughly `150 * 0 >= positive * 100`, which is
  false;
- `AI_considerOffer` returns false and `AI_checkCancel` returns RENEGOTIATE.

For a human counterpart, `AI_doDeals` subsequently queues the deal for cancellation, kills it and
opens the combined CANCEL_DEAL diplomacy popup.

The resource-specific checks do not rescue this example:
- A can continue to have no denial for exporting a genuinely spare Wheat copy to its teammate;
- when H's outgoing Copper is checked from H's proxy `AI_bonusTrade(..., iChange=0)` perspective,
  A's zero recipient value produces `DENIAL_NO_GAIN`, whereas `AI_checkCancel` intentionally cancels
  an incoming resource at that stage only for `DENIAL_JOKING`.

Thus the dead threshold can change the actual lifetime of a normal, previously accepted teammate
trade rather than merely leaving unreachable bookkeeping behind.

INTENDED POLICY SIGNAL
----------------------
The advc.155 release note states:

    "In human-AI teams (team game or Permanent Alliance), the AI no longer accepts all trades
     proposed by the human; only accepts if the trade is at least somewhat even. Can reject gift
     requests."

Within `AI_considerOffer`, one-sided teammate help gets a deliberately enlarged threshold
(`* 5`). The later cancellation branch then explicitly tries to preserve a same-team deal when
`iTheyReceive < iThreshold` before applying the stricter 150% fairness test. That policy is not
being executed because the threshold remains the `-1` sentinel.

For example, before grant-memory subtraction and the small deterministic random perturbation, a
same-team threshold after only 20 met turns is already:

    (20 + 50) * 2 * 5 = 700 trade-value units

so ordinary small teammate resource support can naturally fall below the intended bound. The
current code never observes that bound on bilateral cancellation.

ANCESTRY
--------
K-Mod 1.46 has no advc.155 same-team cancellation exemption. Its cancellation path simply applies
the generic 125% fairness test after the one-sided gift logic.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 contains the same `iThreshold = -1`, the same assignment confined to the returning
one-sided branch, and the same later same-team comparison. Current SAS inherits the structure
unchanged. This is therefore an AdvCiv-introduced regression/incomplete implementation, not an SAS
addition and not a stock/K-Mod defect.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Ensure the same-team cancellation path receives the same bounded-help threshold that advc.155
intended, without altering non-team gift/demand behavior.

A conservative repair is to factor or precompute the same-team threshold before the one-sided gift
branch when `bSameTeam` is true, including the existing deterministic random adjustment and
peacetime-grant subtraction, then let the one-sided branch reuse it. Non-team/vassal threshold
logic can remain where it is.

Do not merely change the sentinel from `-1` to a large constant: the threshold is intentionally
age/contact/grant-sensitive, and the same-team `*5` policy should remain the controlling contract.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
No earlier numbered album root covers this dead advc.155 threshold.

- F332 concerns `AI_foldDeals` resetting the cancellation age of an equivalent AI-AI deal.
- F333 concerns obsolete-unit resource classification inside `AI_bonusTrade`.
- Earlier queue-042 deal roots concern deal representation, Permanent Alliance teardown and
  embargo valuation, not `AI_considerOffer`'s human-AI teammate fairness policy.

F334 is therefore independent.

---------------------------

   assumptions and the small-value/dual exemption, but do not revive WIP18's persistent mixed-dual

F335 / provisional KI#658 — AdvCiv's non-surplus counterproposal fallback can select an item that its own no-overshoot filter rejected
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

CLASSIFICATION
--------------
Independent inherited AdvCiv logic defect in `CvPlayerAI::AI_balanceDeal`, introduced with the
advc.036 resource-trade overhaul. The bug can make an AI-generated offer to a human demand a
non-surplus resource even though the same function explicitly rejected that resource for
overshooting the remaining balance gap.

ROOT CAUSE
----------
`AI_counterPropose` states the policy directly:

    So if their value is greater, we don't mind suggesting
    items which overshoot the balance. But if our value is greater, we will
    never suggest adding items which overshoot the balance.

The second case calls the side that needs to receive more through:

    AI_balanceDeal(..., bTheyGenerous = false, ...)

Inside `AI_balanceDeal`, AdvCiv separates non-surplus resources from ordinary items so that, when a
human is involved, GPT and ordinary surplus items can be preferred before asking for a player's
last resource copy.

Candidate admission initially respects the non-generous no-overshoot rule:

    if (iItemValue > 0 &&
        (bTheyGenerous || iTheyReceive >= iWeReceive + iItemValue || ...))
    {
        ...
        if (bNonsurplus)
            aNonSurplusItems.push_back(itemValue);
        else
            aItemValues.push_back(itemValue);
    }

Ordinary items are then applied first. In the non-generous branch each one is rechecked against the
CURRENT remaining gap before being appended:

    if (iTheyReceive >= iWeReceive + iItemValue)
    {
        kWeWant.insertAtEnd(it->first);
        iWeReceive += ...;
    }

Consequently, after one or more ordinary items have been added, a non-surplus resource that was
legal against the ORIGINAL gap can now be too large for the NEW gap.

The later non-surplus fallback appears to account for exactly that:

    for (best_it = it = aNonSurplusItems.begin();
         it != aNonSurplusItems.end(); ++it)
    {
        if (!bTheyGenerous && iWeReceive + it->second > iTheyReceive)
            continue;
        ...
    }

But `best_it` is initialized to `begin()` BEFORE any candidate passes the filter. If every remaining
non-surplus item overshoots, every iteration executes `continue`, yet `best_it` still points to the
first rejected item.

The post-loop code then treats that rejected element as selected:

    if (best_it->second <= 2 * (iTheyReceive - iWeReceive) || bTheyGenerous)
    {
        kWeWant.insertAtEnd(best_it->first);
        iWeReceive += best_it->second;
    }

Thus, when `bTheyGenerous == false`, a rejected resource whose value is greater than the remaining
gap but no greater than twice that gap is appended anyway. The explicit no-overshoot predicate and
the caller's stated contract are both defeated.

The defect is broader than the all-candidates-rejected case. If `best_it` starts on a rejected
overshooting first element and a later valid element does not happen to beat it under the distance
comparison, the rejected iterator can still win. The simplest proof, however, needs only one
remaining non-surplus candidate.

CONCRETE ARITHMETIC REPRODUCTION INSIDE THE FUNCTION
----------------------------------------------------
A simple trade-value state demonstrates the error without relying on rounding:

    iTheyReceive = 200
    iWeReceive   = 100
    original gap = 100

Available additional items from the side that needs to give more:

    ordinary tradable tech U = 70
    non-surplus resource R   = 40

Both are initially legal because 70 <= 100 and 40 <= 100, so U enters `aItemValues` and R enters
`aNonSurplusItems`.

The non-generous ordinary-item pass adds U first:

    iWeReceive = 170
    remaining gap = 30

R is now too large:

    170 + 40 > 200

so the non-surplus loop's explicit no-overshoot check rejects it. Because R is the only candidate,
`best_it` nevertheless remains R. The subsequent closeness check passes:

    40 <= 2 * 30

and R is appended:

    iWeReceive = 210

The allegedly non-generous / no-overshoot side has therefore been pushed 10 trade-value units past
balance by the very item its filter rejected.

SUPPORTED PRODUCER — AI TECH OFFER TO A HUMAN
---------------------------------------------
This state can reach a real diplomacy proposal; it is not merely an artificial direct call to the
helper.

`AI_doDiplo`'s AI-initiated tech-trade path first constructs a tech-for-tech offer. If the initial
pair is not mutually acceptable, it explicitly lets the other player counter-propose, including a
human:

    if (kPlayer.AI_counterPropose(getID(), weGive, theyGive, true, true))
        bDeal = true;

The source comment says:

    let the other team counter-propose (even if the other team is a human player)

For a human H receiving an AI P's offer, H's proxy `AI_counterPropose` can find that H receives more
value than P. It then calls **P's** `AI_balanceDeal` with H's inventory and
`bTheyGenerous = false`; i.e. P is trying to ask H for additional items without overshooting the
balance.

A supported offer shape is therefore:

1. P offers tech T1 to H and H initially offers tech T2 to P.
2. From the two proxy valuations, H's side is ahead enough that P needs additional value.
3. H owns another tradable tech U and exactly one copy of a tradable resource R that P values.
4. Both U and R individually fit the original value gap, so the initial candidate filter admits
   both. Because H owns only one tradable copy, R is deliberately placed in
   `aNonSurplusItems` by advc.036.
5. U is processed first as an ordinary item and shrinks the remaining gap until R is now too large,
   but still no more than twice the new gap.
6. The broken `best_it` fallback adds R anyway.

The human-last-copy resource is genuinely tradeable in current AdvCiv/SAS. `CvPlayer::canTradeItem`
uses `bCanTradeAll = true` for resources, allowing one tradeable copy, and a human giver's
`AI_bonusTrade` returns `NO_DENIAL` when the AI recipient values the resource at least the ordinary
trade threshold. This is exactly why advc.036 needed a separate `aNonSurplusItems` policy rather
than simply filtering last-copy resources out as K-Mod did.

No-gold states are also straightforward in current SAS: Writing enables technology trading while
Currency separately enables gold trading, so an AI tech proposal can occur in a period where gold
cannot simply fill the residual gap. Even with gold trading available, zero/insufficient available
gold can leave the same fallback active.

VISIBLE CONSEQUENCE
-------------------
After `AI_balanceDeal` mutates the counter list and the referenced value, control returns to the
human-proxy `AI_counterPropose` branch. That branch intentionally does not require the human to get
at least as much value; it only checks whether the AI's resulting side is acceptable before showing
the proposal to the actual human for confirmation.

Therefore the wrongly appended resource can survive into:

    gDLL->beginDiplomacy(... OFFER_DEAL ...)

The user can receive an AI-generated tech offer that asks for T2 + U + R even though the intended
non-generous balancing algorithm should have stopped at T2 + U rather than request R after R ceased
to fit the remaining gap.

This is not necessarily a huge exploit or catastrophic overcharge — the final `<= 2 * gap` guard
bounds this particular mistake — but it directly makes AI-generated offers less faithful to their
own fairness policy and can demand a player's last strategic/luxury/health resource unnecessarily.

ANCESTRY / ARCHAEOLOGY
----------------------
K-Mod 1.46 has the same high-level contract:

    if our value is greater, we will never suggest adding items which overshoot the balance.

Its corresponding non-generous item loop rechecks every candidate against the CURRENT gap before
adding it. K-Mod also excludes last-copy/corporation resources from the candidate list because it
does not yet evaluate the giver's loss there. It therefore has no `aNonSurplusItems` fallback and
not this bug.

AdvCiv practical commit 1287 / SHA `ad5faf8aa2740b991c49d8f35e14769d190a4c71`
(2018-02-15, "Test version incl. DLL and manual; needs some more work.") introduced the
`nonsurplusItems` vector and this exact fallback as part of the advc.036 AI-resource-trade overhaul.
The commit message explicitly describes an "Overhaul of AI resource trades". The original inserted
code already initialized `best_it` to `begin()`, skipped overshooting candidates with `continue`,
and then dereferenced `best_it` afterward without recording whether any candidate survived.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 still contains the same logic at its current `aNonSurplusItems` fallback. Current
SAS inherits it unchanged apart from surrounding refactors. This is therefore an inherited AdvCiv
regression introduced when extending K-Mod to reason about non-surplus resources.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Do not allow `best_it` to represent a candidate until that candidate has passed the current-gap
filter.

A conservative structure is:

    best_it = aNonSurplusItems.end();
    for (it = aNonSurplusItems.begin(); it != aNonSurplusItems.end(); ++it)
    {
        if (!bTheyGenerous && iWeReceive + it->second > iTheyReceive)
            continue;
        if (best_it == aNonSurplusItems.end() || better_than(*it, *best_it, ...))
            best_it = it;
    }
    if (best_it == aNonSurplusItems.end())
        break;

Then apply the existing `<= 2 * remaining gap` closeness rule only to a candidate that actually
passed the no-overshoot predicate.

For `bTheyGenerous == false`, breaking when no valid candidate exists is the natural contract: all
remaining non-surplus resources are now too large, and adding any of them would violate the exact
policy stated by `AI_counterPropose`.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
No earlier numbered album finding covers this selection failure. The old shallow Queue-001 control
merely listed `AI_balanceDeal` among functions where no semantic defect had yet been found; this
deeper producer/lifecycle pass supersedes that provisional clean note.

- F321 concerns prospective resource state in cancellation valuation.
- F332 concerns `AI_foldDeals` resetting deal age.
- F333 concerns obsolete-unit strategic classification.
- F334 concerns the dead advc.155 same-team cancellation threshold.
- The retracted WIP18 dual-head theory concerned persistent deal representation, not counterproposal
  item selection.

F335 is independent.


NEXT AUDIT CURSOR
-----------------
1. Continue the remainder of `AI_balanceDeal`, including the advc.705 `rLeniency` accounting and
   final-item paths; F336 / provisional KI#659 is UNUSED.
2. Continue the remaining `AI_counterPropose` callers and trade/value helpers, retaining the same
   producer -> contract -> consequence standard.
3. Then continue downward into `AI_unitValue` and its surrounding inherited unit-role valuation
   helpers.
4. Keep the proposal-only dual/head concern as an unnumbered control unless EXE/list ordering can
   be proved from a supported producer.
5. WIP22 is the latest physical checkpoint; WIP18 remains superseded/retracted.


===============================================================================
C031-WIP23 CONTINUATION — QUEUE 001 `CvPlayerAI.cpp`
===============================================================================

F336 / provisional KI#659 — CONFIRMED
-------------------------------------

TITLE
-----
`AI_balanceDeal` forgets the advc.705 `rLeniency` multiplier when accumulating
non-surplus resources, so the special Rise & Fall pre-Currency retry can count
AI resources at 100% instead of the documented 90% and stop balancing too early.

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv regression. Current SAS inherits the defect from Base
AdvCiv 1.14. K-Mod predates Rise & Fall/advc.705 and does not have this contract.
The defect was introduced by the later advc.036 non-surplus-resource balancing
code without carrying forward the already-existing leniency accumulator rule.

CONTRACT
--------
Rise & Fall change advc.705 deliberately gives the AI a second pre-Currency
attempt at a technology trade. If the first proposal/counterproposal fails and
neither team can trade gold, `AI_counterPropose` retries with:

    scaled const rSecondAttempt = fixp(0.9);
    ...
    return AI_counterPropose(..., rSecondAttempt);

The current AdvCiv manual states the user-facing rule directly:

    "The AI is a bit more lenient in pre-Currency tech trades – accepts if it
     receives only 90% of what the player receives."

The introduction history is equally explicit. Practical commit 1268 /
`e11525d303...` introduced the Rise & Fall option and refactored the
counterproposal accumulator with the comment:

    advc.705: Apply this to all assignments to iTheirValue

In the modern names this is `rLeniency`, and the current lower-level signature
still says:

    // advc.705: Applied to everything that's added to iValueForThem

The initial value of the human side is discounted:

    int iTheyReceive = (rLeniency *
            kPlayer.AI_dealVal(...)).round();

When the side being balanced adds ordinary items, gold, or GPT, current
`AI_balanceDeal` consistently discounts the accumulator too:

    iWeReceive += (rLeniency * iItemValue).round();

    iWeReceive += (rLeniency *
            iGoldData * per100(iGoldValuePercent)).round();

    iWeReceive += (rLeniency *
            AI_goldPerTurnTradeVal(iGoldData)).round();

Therefore `rLeniency` is not merely a final acceptance threshold. It defines the
value units of the accumulator throughout the 90% retry.

ROOT
----
The later advc.036 non-surplus-resource fallback is the sole item-addition path
in `AI_balanceDeal` that omits the multiplier:

    if (best_it->second <= 2 * (iTheyReceive - iWeReceive) || bTheyGenerous)
    {
        kWeWant.insertAtEnd(best_it->first);
        iWeReceive += best_it->second;
    }

At `rLeniency == 0.9`, a resource worth V to the human side is therefore added
as V rather than round(0.9 * V). The accumulator immediately ceases to represent
the discounted value used by the surrounding function.

The problem is not shared by the ordinary-item, gold or GPT paths; all three
carry the `rLeniency` multiplication explicitly. Nor is this merely a display
or logging mismatch: the inflated accumulator controls the `while
(iTheyReceive > iWeReceive)` continuation condition and is passed back to
`AI_counterPropose` for acceptance.

SUPPORTED PRODUCER
------------------
The special retry is reachable through the ordinary human trade-table path.
`CvPlayer::AI_counterProposeExternal` is the virtual wrapper explicitly called
by the EXE for "what would make this deal work?" and forwards the human's deal
and trade inventories into the AI's lower-level `AI_counterPropose`.

When Rise & Fall is enabled, the other party is human, the first attempt fails,
and neither team has gold trading, that exact AI instance recursively retries
with `rLeniency = 0.9`.

This is importantly different from the AI-initiated tech-offer helper path:
that path can call a human proxy. F336 does not need that ambiguous orientation;
the direct EXE `AI_counterProposeExternal` producer gives the required
AI-callee / human-counterparty shape explicitly.

INDEPENDENT ARITHMETIC REPRODUCTION
-----------------------------------
The effect can be demonstrated without relying on F335's rejected-iterator bug.
Use trade-value units that are legal for the current evaluators (tech values are
rounded to the configured diplomacy remainder; resource trade values are
ordinary integer trade values and can span from very small values to hundreds
as city count and resource utility rise).

Suppose a human asks "what would make this deal work?" in Rise & Fall before
Currency, with initial raw values:

    AI receives from human:         1380
    human receives from AI:         1400

On the first (`rLeniency = 1`) attempt, the human side leads by 20. If the human
has no additional permitted item that the AI can ask for, that attempt fails.

The advc.705 retry discounts the human side:

    1400 * 0.9 = 1260

so the direction flips:

    AI side:                         1380
    discounted human side:          1260
    gap to sweeten for human:         120

Assume the AI has two otherwise-legal last-copy/non-surplus resources valued by
the human proxy at 120 and 10 trade-value units. Both pass the *initial* current
gap admission test (120 <= 120 and 10 <= 120), and the 120-value resource is the
best gap filler.

Current buggy path:

    1260 + 120 = 1380

The loop considers the gap closed and stops. The resulting counterproposal adds
only the 120-value resource.

Correct advc.705 accounting:

    1260 + round(0.9 * 120) = 1260 + 108 = 1368
    remaining discounted gap = 12

The 10-value resource still passes the *current* no-overshoot filter:

    1368 + 10 <= 1380

so F335 is not involved. It should then also be appended, counted at
round(0.9 * 10) = 9, leaving the discounted human side at 1377. The documented
90% rule permits the trade and the corrected counterproposal gives the human
both resources instead of prematurely stopping after the first one.

The exact numbers are illustrative rather than a claim about one fixed leader
or savegame; the important constraints are all supported by the live value
functions. A large first resource whose value is the retry gap and a second
resource no larger than 10% of it produces the same divergence. Resource trade
value scales with empire/resource utility and is not restricted to a single
fixed XML price.

VISIBLE CONSEQUENCE
-------------------
The 90% retry can produce a counterproposal that is less generous to the human
than advc.705 intended. A non-surplus AI resource is counted at full value,
closing the discounted gap earlier than the same function's ordinary-item/gold/
GPT accounting would allow. Consequently later legal sweeteners can be omitted
from the "what would make this deal work?" response.

This is a behavioral change, not merely an internal valuation discrepancy:
`kWeWant` is the counterproposal list returned through the EXE trade-table
wrapper. The missing later resource therefore changes what the player is asked
to accept.

ANCESTRY / ARCHAEOLOGY
----------------------
The ordering of the two AdvCiv changes identifies the regression cleanly.

1. Practical commit 1268 / `e11525d303...` introduced Rise & Fall and advc.705.
   Its counterproposal refactor explicitly said to apply the leniency factor to
   *all* assignments to the discounted side's accumulator, and did so for the
   existing item/gold/GPT additions.

2. Practical commit 1287 / `ad5faf8aa2...` later introduced the advc.036
   non-surplus-resource vector/fallback as part of the AI-resource-trade
   overhaul. Its newly inserted fallback used:

       iSmallerVal += best_it->second;

   rather than the already-required leniency-scaled accumulation.

3. Base AdvCiv 1.14 still contains exactly the unscaled modern line:

       iWeReceive += best_it->second;

4. Current SAS inherits the same omission.

Thus this is not a SAS tuning disagreement and not a K-Mod defect. It is a
cross-feature AdvCiv regression: advc.036 added a new accumulator assignment
after advc.705 had established the 90% accounting contract, but failed to apply
that contract to the new path.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Make the non-surplus fallback use the same accumulator units as every other item
addition in `AI_balanceDeal`:

    iWeReceive += (rLeniency * best_it->second).round();

The surrounding selection comparisons deserve a separate review because they
currently compare raw `it->second` against a discounted remaining gap when
`rLeniency != 1`. F336 does not need that broader claim: the confirmed root is
the direct accumulator omission, and the reproduction above deliberately keeps
the second resource inside the raw current-gap filter so no selection-filter
repair is required for the demonstrated consequence.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
F336 is independent of F335.

F335 concerns `best_it` being initialized to `begin()` before a candidate passes
the no-overshoot filter, allowing a rejected resource to be appended. In the
F336 reproduction every selected resource passes that filter. The wrong result
exists solely because the first non-surplus resource advances the lenient
accumulator by 100% instead of 90%.

It is also independent of F321/F332/F333/F334; those concern cancellation state,
deal age, strategic classification and teammate cancellation respectively.

------------------------------

F337 / provisional KI#660 — UNUSED

NEXT CURSOR
-----------
1. Continue the remaining `AI_balanceDeal` / `rLeniency` selection comparisons,

2. Continue the public `AI_counterPropose` callers and nearby trade/value helpers.

C031-WIP24 CORRECTION / CONTINUATION — QUEUE 001 `CvPlayerAI.cpp`

STATUS
------
F336 / provisional KI#659 remains CONFIRMED.
F337 / provisional KI#660 remains UNUSED.
This checkpoint supersedes two overbroad current-source statements in WIP23; it does
not retract F336's root, producer or independent two-resource consequence.

CORRECTION TO F336 CURRENT-SOURCE DESCRIPTION
---------------------------------------------
WIP23 said that ordinary items, gold and GPT in current `AI_balanceDeal` consistently
apply `rLeniency`, and described the non-surplus fallback as the sole item-addition
path omitting the multiplier. That wording is too broad.

Current SAS (and Base AdvCiv 1.14) has TWO earlier monetary paths that are also
unscaled today:

1. Initial lump-sum gold, before item enumeration:

       iWeReceive += (iGoldData * iGoldValuePercent) / 100;

2. The advc.036 negative-income early-GPT path:

       int iGPTTradeVal = AI_goldPerTurnTradeVal(iGoldData);
       iWeReceive += iGPTTradeVal;

The later/final gold and GPT paths do still use:

       (rLeniency * ...).round()

and the ordinary non-generous item loop still uses:

       (rLeniency * iItemValue).round()

ARCHAEOLOGY OF THE CORRECTION
-----------------------------
The original advc.036 extraction in practical commit 1287 (`ad5faf8aa2...`) DID
preserve advc.705's multiplier for both the new initial-gold path and the new
early-GPT path. At that point the code contained the scaled assignments.

Practical commit 1420 / `c24d361ed8...` (2019-02-15, "UI conveniences for resource
trade") later removed the multiplier from exactly those two early assignments while
refactoring trade-value-to-GPT conversion for the new resource-trade UI/tooltips.
The same commit left the later/final GPT path scaled. No rationale for changing the
leniency contract is stated in the commit message; the user-facing changes concern
resource-trade display/help and factoring `AI_tradeValToGold`.

WHY F336 STILL STANDS
---------------------
F336's confirmed reproduction is the Rise & Fall pre-Currency `rLeniency = 0.9`
second attempt. That retry is explicitly gated on BOTH teams lacking gold trading, so
neither early gold nor early GPT is available there. The demonstrated divergence is
therefore still caused solely by the non-surplus-resource accumulator omission.

The ancestry of that omission also remains unchanged: advc.705 established the
"apply to all assignments" accumulator contract in practical commit 1268, and
advc.036 practical commit 1287 later added the non-surplus fallback as an unscaled
assignment. F336 does not depend on claiming that later code never introduced other
violations of the same contract.

F337 CONTROL / OPEN QUESTION
----------------------------
The 2019 removal of leniency from initial gold / early GPT is now a separate F337
candidate, not silently folded into F336.

It cannot be promoted merely from source inconsistency. The ordinary EXE Rise & Fall
0.9 retry is pre-Currency and therefore cannot exercise those monetary branches.
Non-default leniency also appears in AI-initiated city-trade and capitulation helpers,
but their public `AI_counterPropose` wrapper can invert the multiplier depending on
which side is allowed to add items. A real producer must therefore establish:

- a supported non-1 `rLeniency` reaching `AI_balanceDeal` on the side adding gold/GPT;
- gold/GPT being legally available there;
- and a visible proposal/acceptance difference caused by the unscaled early path.

Until that full orientation and consequence survives, F337 remains UNUSED.

C031-WIP25 CONTINUATION — QUEUE 001 `CvPlayerAI.cpp`
===============================================================================

F337 / provisional KI#660 — CONFIRMED
-------------------------------------

TITLE
-----
The 2019 AdvCiv resource-trade/UI refactor dropped advc.705 `rLeniency` from the
initial gold accumulator in `AI_balanceDeal`, so discounted AI-initiated city trades
can count an AI gold sweetener at 100% instead of 90% and omit another item that the
city-trade policy intended to give the human.

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED inherited AdvCiv regression. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS both contain
the unscaled initial-gold assignment. K-Mod has neither AdvCiv's advc.705 leniency
contract nor the later `AI_proposeCityTrade` producer.

A sibling omission exists in the same 2019 commit for the negative-income early-GPT
path. F337's confirmed reproduction uses lump-sum gold only; the GPT line is recorded
as the same historical contract break but does not need to be relied on for the
finding.

CONTRACT
--------
The lower-level counterproposal function still documents advc.705 as:

    // advc.705: Applied to everything that's added to iValueForThem

and its public wrapper describes `rLeniency` as the multiplier for the value counted
for items of the side that does not give more.

AdvCiv's AI-initiated city-trade helper makes deliberate non-default use of that
mechanism. When `bWeGiveMore` and the recipient is human it calls:

    AI_counterPropose(..., true, false,
            // The usual discount to make the offer worth considering
            fixp(1/0.9));

Because `bTheyMayGiveMore` is true, the public wrapper calls
`rLeniency.flipFraction()`, so the lower-level call receives 0.9. This is not a
Rise & Fall-only value: city-trade negotiation uses the multiplier explicitly even
when Currency/gold trading is available.

The city-pair sign is also source-defined rather than guessed. `AI_proposeCityTrade`
gets `iWeGiveVal` from the recipient's `AI_cityTradeVal` for our city and
`iTheyGiveVal` from our `AI_cityTradeVal` for their city, then sets:

    bWeGiveMore = (iWeGiveVal > iTheyGiveVal)

Thus a city pair where the human values our city slightly more than we value theirs
is exactly the `bWeGiveMore` path using the 0.9 human-side discount.

ROOT
----
Current `AI_balanceDeal`, before enumerating maps/techs/resources/cities, tries to
fill the gap with lump-sum gold. For a non-generous side it computes and rounds a
gold amount from the CURRENT discounted gap, then updates the accumulator with:

    iWeReceive += (iGoldData * iGoldValuePercent) / 100;

The `rLeniency` multiplier is missing.

Later ordinary items in this same non-generous balance path correctly use:

    iWeReceive += (rLeniency * iItemValue).round();

and the final-gold/final-GPT paths also still use scaled accumulation. Therefore the
initial gold update changes units in the middle of a single balancing operation.

SUPPORTED PRODUCER / LIST SHAPE
-------------------------------
`AI_proposeCityTrade` is a current shipped AI producer. A non-liberation city trade is
a nonannual deal. `CvPlayer::updateTradeList` permits other nonannual items alongside
it; lump-sum Gold and World Map are both nonannual (`CvDeal::isAnnual` returns false
for both), so an AI inventory can legally supply both as city-trade sweeteners.

Assume ordinary supported conditions:
- AI A and human H can trade cities, gold and maps;
- A has at least 25 tradeable gold;
- A's map has trade value 10 to H and has no denial;
- both candidate cities pass `AI_intendsToCede` / city-trade denial;
- H values A's city X at 1050 trade-value units;
- A values H's city Y at 1000.

These values need not correspond to one named save; `AI_cityTradeVal` is an integer
heuristic with many continuous empire/city inputs, and `AI_mapTradeVal` rounds to the
diplomacy remainder, so a 10-value map is an ordinary supported result.

EXACT CURRENT ARITHMETIC
------------------------
Because 1050 > 1000, `bWeGiveMore` is true. The public wrapper flips 1/0.9 to 0.9.
The lower-level values become:

    AI receives H's city:                  1000
    H receives A's city, discounted:       1050 * 0.9 = 945

The discount intentionally creates a 55-value sweetener gap for H.

The direction therefore calls the HUMAN proxy's `AI_balanceDeal` with A's inventory,
`rLeniency = 0.9`, and `bTheyGenerous = false`: A is the side that must add more.
This is the required non-1-leniency monetary producer.

Current AI gold is worth 200 trade-value units per 100 gold. The initial gold path
computes:

    55 * 100 / 200 = 27 gold

Because a human is involved, `AI_roundTradeValBounds` rounds the non-generous amount
down to the diplomacy multiple; with the standard remainder 5 this becomes 25 gold.
Its raw trade value is 50.

CURRENT BUGGY ACCUMULATOR:

    945 + 50 = 995
    remaining gap = 5

The subsequent 10-value map is rejected by the ordinary non-generous admission test:

    1000 >= 995 + 10    // false

So the generated city offer can stop with X + 25 gold for Y (apart from the automatic
peace-treaty representation used for city trades).

CORRECT / PRE-2019 ADVC.705 ACCUMULATOR:

    945 + round(0.9 * 50) = 990
    remaining gap = 10

Now the same map passes the CURRENT raw no-overshoot check exactly:

    1000 >= 990 + 10    // true

and the ordinary item path adds it as:

    990 + round(0.9 * 10) = 999

The resulting proposal contains X + 25 gold + World Map for Y. This example therefore
does not depend on F335's invalid-iterator fallback or F336's non-surplus fallback;
it stays entirely in the ordinary item path after the erroneous initial-gold update.

VISIBLE CONSEQUENCE
-------------------
The bug makes a current AI-initiated city trade less generous to the human than the
explicit 0.9 city-trade discount intends. Counting the initial gold at 100% closes
too much of the discounted gap and can suppress a legal map/tech/resource/city
sweetener that would have been added under consistent advc.705 accounting.

The proposal is not merely internal calculation: `AI_proposeCityTrade` places the
mutated `weGive` / `theyGive` lists into an `OFFER_DEAL` diplomacy popup for the human.
The omitted item therefore changes the offer the player actually sees.

ANCESTRY / ARCHAEOLOGY
----------------------
The regression can be dated precisely.

1. Practical commit 1268 / `e11525d303...` introduced advc.705 and explicitly changed
   counterproposal accumulator assignments to multiply by leniency.

2. Practical commit 1287 / `ad5faf8aa2...` extracted the balancing code for the
   advc.036 resource-trade overhaul. Its NEW initial-gold and negative-income GPT
   paths still preserved the multiplier:

       iSmallerVal += round(leniency * goldTradeValue);
       iSmallerVal += round(leniency * gptTradeVal);

3. Practical commit 1420 / `c24d361ed8...` (2019-02-15, "UI conveniences for resource
   trade") factored out `AI_tradeValToGold` for resource-trade display/tooltips and
   simultaneously changed those two early assignments to unscaled additions. The
   commit message documents resource-trade UI/help changes and the helper extraction;
   it gives no policy rationale for dropping advc.705. Importantly, the same commit
   left the later final-GPT assignment scaled.

4. Practical commit 2085 / `f54cc30550...` (2020-04-01, "AI code for initiating city
   trades") later added the current city-trade producer and its explicit "usual
   discount" non-1-leniency calls. By then the early-gold contract break was already
   present.

5. Base AdvCiv 1.14 still has the unscaled line. Current SAS inherits it.

K-Mod 1.46 has the older counterproposal machinery without advc.705 and without the
AdvCiv city-trade helper, so this is not a K-Mod root.

SIBLING EARLY-GPT OMISSION
--------------------------
The same practical commit 1420 also changed the negative-income early-GPT path from:

    iSmallerVal += round(leniency * gptTradeVal);

to the current equivalent of:

    iWeReceive += iGPTTradeVal;

This is the same dimensional/contract omission. F337 is already independently proved
through lump-sum gold, so no GPT-specific scenario is needed to establish the root.
For a repair, restoring the multiplier on BOTH early monetary assignments matches the
pre-1420 implementation and the still-current advc.705 signature contract. If review
prefers ultra-narrow changes, the initial-gold line alone is sufficient for the
confirmed city-trade reproduction.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Restore the accumulator to the same units as the surrounding path, conceptually:

    iWeReceive += (rLeniency *
            iGoldData * per100(iGoldValuePercent)).round();

and, for the sibling path:

    iWeReceive += (rLeniency * iGPTTradeVal).round();

Do not change the gold amount computation merely to force the accumulator to equality.
The pre-1420 design deliberately allowed the leniency-scaled addition to leave a
residual gap so another item could be considered; the city-trade reproduction above
shows that this affects the intended sweetener list.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
F337 is separate from F336 and F335.

- F335: rejected `best_it` can be dereferenced in the non-surplus fallback.
- F336: the later advc.036 non-surplus fallback itself omits `rLeniency`; its confirmed
  producer is Rise & Fall's pre-Currency retry where gold is unavailable.
- F337: the EARLY lump-sum gold assignment lost a multiplier in a later 2019 refactor;
  its confirmed producer is AI-initiated city trading where gold is available.

The two findings share the broader advc.705 accounting contract but have different
birth commits, branches and visible producer paths, so keeping them separate is useful
for review and archaeology.

C031-WIP26 ADDENDUM — 2026-08-30
F338 / provisional KI#661 CONFIRMED
===============================================================================

F338 — AI-HUMAN CANCELLATION QUEUE IS STILL LIVE WHEN ADVC.133 ENFORCES THE
PER-RIVAL GPT CAP, SO GPT FROM A DEAL ALREADY CHOSEN FOR CANCELLATION CAN FORCE
AN ADDITIONAL HEALTHY GPT DEAL TO BE CANCELED

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED current inherited Base AdvCiv bug. This is an ordering/state-projection
error introduced together with advc.133 in practical commit 2967. Current SAS and
Base AdvCiv 1.14 retain the same lifecycle. K-Mod predates this GPT-cap enforcement.

ROOT
----
`CvPlayerAI::AI_doDeals(eOther)` first runs `AI_checkCancel` over every mature deal
between the AI and `eOther`.

For an AI-human non-vassal deal that should be canceled, AdvCiv does NOT kill the
`CvDeal` immediately. It stores the live pointer in:

    apHumanDealsToCancel.push_back(pLoopDeal);

The source/history explicitly describes this as:

    // advc.133: Don't contact human (nor kill deal) yet

Deals for which `AI_checkCancel` returned `NO_CANCEL`, by contrast, are stored in
`aapDealsPerPlayer[eOther]` as candidates for the subsequent GPT-cap pass.

The bug is the order of the next two phases. Before `apHumanDealsToCancel` is
processed and killed, `AI_doDeals` executes:

    int iOverdraft = -AI_maxGoldPerTurnTrade(eOther, true);

`AI_maxGoldPerTurnTrade(..., true)` reads LIVE player state. In particular its
per-rival limit contains:

    rMaxGoldPerTurn += std::min(0, getGoldPerTurnByPlayer(ePlayer));

and its availability calculation also reads the current GPT state. A queued human
deal therefore still contributes to the exact state used to decide whether surviving
deals exceed the cap, even though `AI_checkCancel` has already decided that the deal
will disappear later in this same call.

The GPT enforcement loop only considers `NO_CANCEL` deals as possible victims. It
therefore cannot cure the stale contribution by selecting the already-doomed deal;
it can only cancel an additional surviving GPT deal. The queued deals are finally
killed afterward, while the combined human cancellation popup is assembled.

SUPPORTED PRODUCER
------------------
No exotic deal shape is needed. Consider an AI A and human H with two mature,
cancelable annual resource-for-GPT deals. Such resource/GPT deals are ordinary
supported objects throughout AdvCiv's resource-trading code.

- D_bad: A pays H 15 GPT for a resource. Since the deal was signed, A's resource
  valuation/state has changed enough that `AI_checkCancel(D_bad,H)` now returns a
  cancellation code. Because H is human, A can contact H and this is not a vassal
  deal, D_bad is appended to `apHumanDealsToCancel` but remains LIVE.
- D_good: A independently pays H 15 GPT for another resource that remains worthwhile.
  `AI_checkCancel(D_good,H)` returns `NO_CANCEL`, so D_good is placed in
  `aapDealsPerPlayer[H]`.

`CvDeal::startTrade` makes A's outgoing GPT negative in the bilateral accumulator:

    A.changeGoldPerTurnByPlayer(H, -trade.m_iData);

and `CvDeal::endTrade` reverses it only when the deal is actually killed. Thus both
15-GPT payments are still present when the cap check runs.

EXACT CLEAN ARITHMETIC
----------------------
Choose an ordinary state in which A's post-personality/post-attitude per-rival GPT
cap before the current bilateral-flow adjustment is 20 GPT, and make A's overall
available income comfortably nonbinding. At Cautious attitude the diplomacy
multiplier is 1, so no extra scaling is needed in the example.

Immediately before the cap check, because D_bad has only been QUEUED rather than
killed:

    current A -> H GPT = 15 + 15 = 30
    getGoldPerTurnByPlayer(H) = -30
    base per-rival cap = 20
    current additional GPT capacity = 20 + (-30) = -10

With `bCheckOverdraft=true`, `AI_maxGoldPerTurnTrade` deliberately preserves this
negative result. `AI_doDeals` negates it:

    iOverdraft = 10

which is above the function's 3-GPT tolerance.

The enforcement candidate list contains D_good but NOT D_bad. D_good pays 15 GPT,
so the loop cancels D_good to cover the apparent 10-GPT overdraft. Only afterward
does the combined-human-cancellation phase finally kill D_bad.

End result: BOTH deals are canceled.

POST-CANCELLATION STATE SHOWS THE ERROR
---------------------------------------
Had D_bad been removed from live player state before checking the cap, only D_good's
15 GPT would remain:

    projected A -> H GPT = 15
    projected additional GPT capacity = 20 - 15 = +5

There is no overdraft at all. D_good is already within the same negotiation limit
that advc.133 says it is enforcing and should survive.

The defect is therefore not a disagreement about the cap size or the 3-GPT tolerance.
The exact same cap, personality, attitude and financial state produce opposite
results solely because an already-doomed human deal remains live until after the
cap is evaluated.

The example deliberately assumes ample overall `iAvailable`, making the per-rival
`iMax` branch binding. Changes to total available-income state when D_bad ends can
therefore only be additional state-projection concerns; they are not needed for the
confirmed reproduction.

VISIBLE / GAMEPLAY CONSEQUENCE
------------------------------
A single ordinary AI-human cancellation can cascade into cancellation of a second,
otherwise healthy GPT/resource agreement. Both then appear in AdvCiv's combined
cancellation handling even though only one failed `AI_checkCancel` and the survivor
would satisfy the GPT cap after the first deal disappears.

This is especially contrary to the purpose of advc.133: the feature exists to stop
players from circumventing the AI's negotiated per-rival GPT limit through old
subsidy/payment state. Here it instead enforces that limit against payment state
that the same function has already decided is obsolete.

ANCESTRY / ARCHAEOLOGY
----------------------
The root entered in practical commit 2967 / `b1cf90d56b...` (2021-04-01),
"AI: cancel GPT deals when per-player limit exceeded" [advc.133]. The commit message
explicitly says the goal is to close the gold-subsidy loophole because per-rival GPT
limits "still exist and shouldn't be circumvented."

Crucially, that SAME patch made both relevant changes:

1. Human cancellations that had previously been processed immediately were changed
   to `apHumanDealsToCancel.push_back(pLoopDeal)`, with the source comment
   "Don't contact human (nor kill deal) yet."
2. The new `// Enforce GPT limit` phase was inserted BEFORE the later loop that walks
   `apHumanDealsToCancel` and calls `kDeal.kill()`.

The patch also added the `bCheckOverdraft` parameter to `AI_maxGoldPerTurnTrade`
specifically so the new enforcement phase could observe negative remaining capacity.
Thus this is an original advc.133 phase-ordering defect rather than a later SAS or
AdvCiv regression.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains the same ordering and helper logic. Current SAS inherits it.
K-Mod 1.46 has `AI_maxGoldPerTurnTrade` but not AdvCiv's advc.133 surviving-deal GPT
cap pass, so this is not a K-Mod root.

The AdvCiv manual also states the intended behavior directly: the AI should cancel
GPT deals when its total payments to a player exceed the limits that apply during
deal negotiation. The surviving D_good in the reproduction does not exceed that
limit after the independently canceled D_bad is removed.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
No existing album or current Known-Issues entry was found for this queued-cancellation
vs GPT-cap ordering root. Earlier GPT mentions in the album concern logging or trade
value/leniency, not advc.133's live-deal phase ordering.

F338 is independent of:
- F321/F333 resource valuation/classification bugs: D_bad merely needs any supported
  reason to fail `AI_checkCancel`; the stale-state root remains even when that reason
  is perfectly correct.
- F335-F337 counterproposal accounting: F338 runs on already-existing mature deals,
  not deal construction/balancing.
- F332 deal-fold age reset: neither deal needs to have been folded.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
The GPT-cap phase should evaluate the state that will exist after deals already chosen
for cancellation in this `AI_doDeals` call are gone.

The safest structural repair is to separate "remember data for one combined human
popup" from "keep the CvDeal economically active": capture the human-facing trade
items/cancellation metadata, kill already-doomed non-vassal human deals BEFORE the
GPT-overdraft computation, then enforce the GPT cap on the truly surviving deal set.
Any additional human deal selected by the cap pass can be captured/killed through the
same aggregation path before the single popup is opened.

A narrower manual projection would have to reproduce not only the bilateral
`getGoldPerTurnByPlayer(eOther)` delta but also every relevant total-GPT/availability
state change from all queued deals, including GPT flowing in the opposite direction.
That is easier to get subtly wrong than updating the actual deal state first.

Do not simply remove D_bad from `aapDealsPerPlayer`: it is already absent there. The
bug is that it remains present in PLAYER ECONOMIC STATE read by
`AI_maxGoldPerTurnTrade(..., true)`.

C031-WIP27 ADDENDUM — 2026-08-30
F339 / provisional KI#662 CONFIRMED
