F339 — `AI_unitValue(UNITAI_ICBM)` CAN COUNT THE OWNER'S OWN NUCLEAR
INTERCEPTION AS A CHANCE OF ITS OUTGOING NUKES BEING SHOT DOWN

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED current inherited K-Mod/AdvCiv AI valuation bug. Current SAS inherits the
same K-Mod nuclear-unit valuation logic. Civ4CE/BtS does not contain this K-Mod
interception-estimation block.

ROOT
----
The `UNITAI_ICBM` branch of `CvPlayerAI::AI_unitValue` estimates expected nuclear
losses from interception. In a neutral/non-war area it power-weights the
`getNukeInterception()` values of every live team `KNOWN_TO` the owner:

    bool const bWar = (pArea != NULL &&
            pArea->getAreaAIType(getTeam()) != AREAAI_NEUTRAL);
    int iInterceptTally = 0;
    int iPowerTally = 0;
    for (TeamIter<CIV_ALIVE,KNOWN_TO> itTeam(getTeam());
        itTeam.hasNext(); ++itTeam)
    {
        if (!bWar ||
            GET_TEAM(getTeam()).AI_getWarPlan(itTeam->getID()) != NO_WARPLAN)
        {
            int iPower = itTeam->getPower(false);
            iPowerTally += iPower;
            iInterceptTally += itTeam->getNukeInterception() * iPower;
        }
    }

AdvCiv's iterator contract explicitly documents `KNOWN_TO` as including the first
agent's own team ("agents know themselves"). Thus, whenever `bWar == false`, the
owner contributes its own power and its own nuclear-interception percentage to the
estimated chance that its outgoing nuclear unit will be intercepted.

That state is semantically impossible. Actual nuclear interception is computed by
`CvUnit::nukeInterceptionChance` from teams AFFECTED by the target detonation (plus
master-team protection). The launching team's own SDI does not intercept its own
nuclear strike merely because the launcher owns SDI.

The `bWar` subcase partly masks the defect: when the area is non-neutral, only teams
for which the owner has a war plan are accumulated, and the owner has no war plan
against itself. The confirmed root therefore concerns the neutral/peacetime branch
(and any NULL-area consumer), not every call to `AI_unitValue`.

SUPPORTED PRODUCER
------------------
This is reachable through ordinary AI production, not just a detached valuation
helper.

`CvCityAI::AI_chooseProduction` has both a high-priority AdvCiv nuclear-production
rule and the later K-Mod nuclear-production rule. Neither requires an active war;
`AI_nukeWeight()` only requires that nukes are valid and war is possible in the game.
Both rules can therefore call:

    AI_chooseUnit(UNITAI_ICBM)

while the city's land area is `AREAAI_NEUTRAL`.

`AI_chooseUnit(UNITAI_ICBM)` calls `AI_bestUnitAI(UNITAI_ICBM)`, which evaluates every
trainable nuclear candidate through:

    kOwner.AI_unitValue(eUnit, UNITAI_ICBM, area())

so the contaminated interception estimate directly participates in selecting which
nuclear unit the city trains.

CURRENT SAS DATA MAKES THE ERROR LARGE
--------------------------------------
Current SAS retains the two ordinary nuclear candidates:

- `UNIT_ICBM`: cost 500, nuke range 1, unlimited (`iAirRange = 0`), evasion 0.
- `UNIT_TACTICAL_NUKE`: cost 250, nuke range 1, air range 4, evasion 50.

Both use `UNITAI_ICBM`, require Fission + Rocketry + Uranium, and are suicide units.
Current `PROJECT_SDI` gives 60 nuclear interception.

Before the interception adjustment, the K-Mod `UNITAI_ICBM` role component is:

    ICBM:          100 + 1*40 = 140
    Tactical Nuke: (100 + 1*40) * 4/10 = 56

and `AI_unitValue` starts from 1, so with no interceptor present their relevant base
values are 141 and 57.

Consider a fully supported isolated/unknown-rivals state in which the AI has SDI.
The game can still have living rivals and therefore `AI_isWarPossible()==true`; the
AI simply has not met a foreign team. Its own team is nevertheless `KNOWN_TO`.
The buggy power-weighted mean interception is therefore exactly its own 60% SDI.

The code then values the same units approximately as:

    ICBM role component:
        140 - 140 * 60 * (100 - 0) / 10000 = 56
        AI_unitValue = 57

    Tactical Nuke role component:
        56 - 56 * 60 * (100 - 50) / 10000 = 40  [integer arithmetic]
        AI_unitValue = 41

The owner has therefore cut the estimated value of its own ICBM from 141 to 57 solely
because IT owns SDI, and also reduced Tactical-Nuke value from 57 to 41.

DIRECT CANDIDATE-SET CONSEQUENCE
--------------------------------
`CvCityAI::AI_bestUnitAI` first finds the largest `AI_unitValue`, then rejects ordinary
candidates below two thirds of that best base value:

    if (iValue < iBestBaseValue*2/3 ...)
        continue;

Without the erroneous self-SDI interception:

    best = ICBM 141
    Tactical Nuke = 57 < 141*2/3 (=94)

so Tactical Nuke is eliminated before production cost, randomization and unit-class
saturation are even considered. `AI_bestUnitAI(UNITAI_ICBM)` cannot choose it while
the ICBM is trainable.

With the erroneous 60% self-SDI interception:

    best = ICBM 57
    Tactical Nuke = 41 >= 57*2/3 (=38)

so Tactical Nuke suddenly enters the production candidate set. Owning a defensive
project has therefore changed which offensive nuclear units the AI is even allowed
to compare.

A natural lifecycle makes the visible choice change stronger: before SDI, the AI can
build an ICBM while Tactical Nuke is filtered out; after SDI, suppose it has one ICBM
and zero Tactical Nukes. `AI_bestUnitAI` then also applies K-Mod's unit-class
saturation factor and divides by remaining production cost. The cheaper unsaturated
Tactical Nuke receives both advantages. For ordinary city production values it can
therefore become the selected `UNITAI_ICBM` unit after SDI, whereas without counting
self-SDI it never reached that comparison at all. This does not require a different
tech/resource state: the changed input is the owner's own interception project.

The exact production winner can also vary through the function's intended random
100-149% factor and city-specific production modifiers; the confirmed defect does
not depend on one particular random draw. The deterministic candidate-set change is
already upstream of those legitimate tie-breaking/production considerations.

ACTUAL INTERCEPTION CONTRACT
----------------------------
`CvUnit::nukeInterceptionChance` constructs the teams affected by the chosen target
and selects the strongest interception coverage among those teams, with AdvCiv also
considering an affected vassal's master. The launcher's own team is not an
interceptor unless it is somehow an affected victim of the target itself.

Thus the production heuristic is not merely using a deliberately pessimistic
approximation of enemy SDI. It is incorporating a defensive capability that has no
corresponding interception path for a normal outgoing strike.

ANCESTRY / ARCHAEOLOGY
----------------------
Civ4CE/BtS has the older nuclear-unit value formula and does not attempt this
power-weighted interception estimate at all.

K-Mod 1.46 introduced the current block. It iterates every alive team for which:

    kTeam.isHasMet(i)

and, in the neutral-area branch, has no `i != getTeam()` exclusion. K-Mod's normal
visibility/contact code calls `GET_TEAM(getTeam()).meet(eTeam, true)` when a plot
becomes visible; on the owner's own visible plots those two team IDs are the same.
So the K-Mod representation can mark the owner as having met itself and feed it to
the new interception loop.

AdvCiv preserves the K-Mod behavior through its agent-iterator rewrite. Its
`AgentPredicates.h` contract explicitly says `KNOWN_TO` includes the first agent's
team, while `OTHER_KNOWN_TO` is the corresponding predicate that excludes it.
Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS both use:

    TeamIter<CIV_ALIVE,KNOWN_TO>

in this exact K-Mod block.

This is therefore best classified as an inherited K-Mod root retained/clarified by
AdvCiv, not a SAS-local change and not a vanilla BtS defect.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
No existing album or current Known-Issues root was found for self-SDI contaminating
`AI_unitValue(UNITAI_ICBM)`.

This is distinct from other nuclear AI work in AdvCiv (`advc.650` target valuation,
nuke deterrence and SDI project value): those systems explicitly examine rival or
affected-team interception. F339 is specifically the unit-production valuation
loop counting the OWNER as a possible interceptor.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
The narrow semantics-preserving repair is to exclude the owner's team from this
expected-enemy-interception tally, e.g. use:

    TeamIter<CIV_ALIVE,OTHER_KNOWN_TO>

instead of `KNOWN_TO`, or add an explicit self-team skip.

Do not remove the whole interception adjustment: K-Mod intentionally wanted rival
SDI/evasion to affect the relative desirability of nuclear units. The confirmed
error is only that the launcher's own interception is allowed into that rival-loss
estimate.

A broader redesign could weight only plausible nuclear target teams and model
vassal/master interception like `nukeInterceptionChance`; that would be a tuning/
accuracy project beyond this finding. F339 requires only the indisputable self-team
exclusion.

F340 — ADVciv's 2020 "SPECIAL CARGO" FIX ACCEPTS A SPECIAL-CARGO SHIP FOR
EVERY SPECIAL-CARRIER UnitAI ROLE, EVEN WHEN IT CANNOT CARRY THAT ROLE'S CARGO

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED current inherited AdvCiv regression. The defect was introduced by AdvCiv
commit 8c833b49222cf8a8dc16bd0f25a1fb7399e04832 (2020-01-01), titled:

    Fix BtS bug in AI evaluation of special cargo units

Civ4CE/BtS and K-Mod use the requested UnitAI role in the SpecialUnit carrier-role
check. AdvCiv changed that check to the loop variable and thereby broadened every
special-cargo carrier into every special-carrier sea role. Current SAS inherits that
AdvCiv change unchanged.

ROOT
----
`CvPlayerAI::AI_unitValue` starts by asking whether the unit is valid for the requested
`eUnitAI`. XML can establish validity directly through `u.getUnitAIType(eUnitAI)`.
When XML does not, the function has role-specific fallback tests.

For the four special-cargo sea roles, current Base AdvCiv and SAS execute:

    case UNITAI_MISSIONARY_SEA:
    case UNITAI_SPY_SEA:
    case UNITAI_CARRIER_SEA:
    case UNITAI_MISSILE_CARRIER_SEA:
        if (u.getCargoSpace() > 0 && u.getSpecialCargo() != NO_SPECIALUNIT)
        {
            FOR_EACH_ENUM(UnitAI)
            {
                // advc.001: was ...isCarrierUnitAIType(eUnitAI)
                if (GC.getInfo(u.getSpecialCargo()).
                    isCarrierUnitAIType(eLoopUnitAI))
                {
                    bValid = true;
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        break;

The loop never asks whether the unit's SpecialCargo supports THE REQUESTED `eUnitAI`.
It merely asks whether the SpecialUnit supports ANY carrier UnitAI anywhere in its
`CarrierUnitAIs` table.

All three shipped special cargo classes support at least one carrier role, so any ship
with any of those SpecialCargo values and positive cargo space passes all four cases.
For example, a Missile Cruiser carrying `SPECIALUNIT_MISSILE` becomes "valid" for
`UNITAI_MISSIONARY_SEA` merely because `SPECIALUNIT_MISSILE` supports
`UNITAI_MISSILE_CARRIER_SEA`.

That is not merely a role-label mismatch. The physical cargo contract remains strict.
`CvUnit::cargoSpaceAvailable` returns zero whenever the transport's `specialCargo()`
differs from the cargo unit's `SpecialUnitType`, and also checks DomainCargo. Therefore
a Missile Cruiser or Carrier selected as `UNITAI_MISSIONARY_SEA` cannot actually load
a missionary/spy/other `SPECIALUNIT_PEOPLE` land unit.

ANCESTRY / THE 2020 "FIX"
--------------------------
Civ4CE/BtS contains the same old redundant loop as K-Mod, but its condition is:

    isCarrierUnitAIType(eUnitAI)

K-Mod 1.46 preserves that condition. The loop variable is unused, which is ugly and
makes the loop itself unnecessary, but the SEMANTIC QUESTION is correct: does this
unit's SpecialCargo permit the role being evaluated?

AdvCiv practical commit 1897 / SHA 8c833b4922 changed exactly that parameter:

    - isCarrierUnitAIType(eUnitAI)
    + isCarrierUnitAIType(eLoopUnitAI)

and added:

    // advc.001: was ...isCarrierUnitAIType(eUnitAI)

The commit title calls this a BtS bugfix. Its full message says:

    "I think the error only meant that the AI had to rely on the Unit AI types set in
    Civ4UnitInfos.xml for special cargo units. So only a potential problem for
    mod-mods."

AdvCiv's manual repeats that diagnosis as a "Wrong parameter" bug.

The source semantics show the opposite for this parameter. If XML does not explicitly
list the requested role, the old fallback already recognizes a special-cargo unit when
its SpecialUnitInfo lists THAT REQUESTED carrier role. The pointless loop was a code
smell, but `eUnitAI` was the meaningful operand. Replacing it with the loop variable
turns a requested-role predicate into an existential "supports any carrier role"
predicate and introduces the cross-role acceptance.

CURRENT SAS DATA — THREE DISJOINT SPECIAL-CARGO SHIPS
------------------------------------------------------
Current SAS `CIV4SpecialUnitInfos.xml` keeps the carrier-role categories distinct:

    SPECIALUNIT_FIGHTER:
        UNITAI_CARRIER_SEA

    SPECIALUNIT_PEOPLE:
        UNITAI_SPY_SEA
        UNITAI_MISSIONARY_SEA
        UNITAI_ASSAULT_SEA

    SPECIALUNIT_MISSILE:
        UNITAI_MISSILE_CARRIER_SEA

Current SAS has three ordinary sea units with non-NONE SpecialCargo:

    Missile Cruiser
        SpecialCargo = SPECIALUNIT_MISSILE
        DomainCargo  = DOMAIN_AIR
        cargo = 4, moves = 7, combat = 26, cost = 250
        XML UnitAIs: ATTACK_SEA, RESERVE_SEA, MISSILE_CARRIER_SEA

    Attack Submarine
        SpecialCargo = SPECIALUNIT_PEOPLE
        DomainCargo  = DOMAIN_LAND
        cargo = 1, moves = 6, combat = 24, cost = 200
        XML UnitAIs: RESERVE_SEA, EXPLORE_SEA,
                     MISSIONARY_SEA, SPY_SEA

    Carrier
        SpecialCargo = SPECIALUNIT_FIGHTER
        DomainCargo  = DOMAIN_AIR
        cargo = 3, moves = 5, combat = 16, cost = 180
        XML UnitAIs: CARRIER_SEA

Thus the intended late people-carrier is the Attack Submarine. Carrier cannot carry
people because it accepts Fighters/Air; Missile Cruiser cannot carry people because it
accepts Missiles/Air.

SUPPORTED PRODUCTION CONSEQUENCE
--------------------------------
This reaches ordinary city production directly.

`CvCityAI::AI_chooseProduction` contains a shipped path that, when the AI is not in a
land war, is in financial trouble, has a land missionary, and lacks a missionary sea
unit in the water area, calls:

    AI_chooseUnit(UNITAI_MISSIONARY_SEA)

The default `iOdds` for this requested-role overload is -1, so once a best unit exists
there is no additional random "should we build it?" gate.

`AI_chooseUnit` calls:

    AI_bestUnitAI(UNITAI_MISSIONARY_SEA)

and `AI_bestUnitAI` evaluates every trainable civilization unit through the exact
`AI_unitValue(eUnit, UNITAI_MISSIONARY_SEA, area())` validation above.

Take an ordinary late-game civ/city that can train all three generic ships. Current
`UNITAI_MISSIONARY_SEA` role value is:

    1 + iAIWeight + iCombatValue/2 + moves*200 + cargo*500

(no current one of these ships has a relevant positive iAIWeight or impassable penalty).
Ignoring the small combat term for clarity gives approximately:

    Missile Cruiser:  1 + 7*200 + 4*500 = 3401 + combat/2
    Carrier:          1 + 5*200 + 3*500 = 2501 + combat/2
    Attack Submarine: 1 + 6*200 + 1*500 = 1701 + combat/2

The wrong-role Missile Cruiser is therefore the highest BASE role value. More
importantly, `AI_bestUnitAI` rejects any ordinary candidate below two thirds of that
best base value BEFORE cost/random/promotion comparison:

    if (iValue < iBestBaseValue * 2 / 3)
        continue;

The valid Attack Submarine is deterministically below two thirds of the Missile
Cruiser. This remains true for any positive `getBestLandUnitCombat()` denominator in
`AI_combatValue`; the tiny combat normalization cannot bridge the ~1700-point cargo/
movement gap.

The Carrier is above two thirds and therefore survives too. The result is especially
bad: once all three are trainable, the only physically valid `SPECIALUNIT_PEOPLE`
carrier is filtered out, while the surviving candidate set consists of ships that
cannot carry the missionary at all. Production-cost/random/saturation logic can choose
between Carrier and Missile Cruiser, but either result defeats the requested role.

So this is not a hypothetical mod-mod XML concern. Current SAS can ask for a missionary
transport and spend hammers on a Carrier or Missile Cruiser that is mechanically unable
to load the missionary, while excluding its actual Attack Submarine people carrier.
The same root can cross-contaminate SPY_SEA, CARRIER_SEA and MISSILE_CARRIER_SEA in the
opposite directions as well.

ADDITIONAL LIFECYCLE SUPPORT
----------------------------
The wrong broad `AI_unitValue` predicate is also reachable outside fresh production.
Some inherited sea-unit reclassification paths call `AI_unitValue(..., SPY_SEA)` or
`AI_unitValue(..., MISSIONARY_SEA)` directly when considering a new UnitAI role. Those
paths therefore can also regard a special carrier as suitable for cargo it cannot
transport. Not all transform paths are affected because some first require the unit's
XML UnitAI flag; this finding does not rely on those secondary paths.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
No existing album or current `README_Known_Issues.md` root was found for AdvCiv's
`isCarrierUnitAIType(eLoopUnitAI)` cross-role validation.

The earlier album control around `PUF_isEnemyCityAttacker` merely catalogued the same
three non-NONE-SpecialCargo ships to prove that a generic invasion-transport shortcut
does NOT classify them as generic land transports. That is a different function and
a different contract.

F340 is also separate from XML balancing choices such as giving Attack Submarine
MISSIONARY_SEA/SPY_SEA. Those XML flags are internally coherent with
`SPECIALUNIT_PEOPLE`; the bug is that C++ admits incompatible `SPECIALUNIT_FIGHTER` and
`SPECIALUNIT_MISSILE` carriers into those roles anyway.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Restore the requested-role predicate and delete the redundant loop entirely:

    if (u.getCargoSpace() > 0 && u.getSpecialCargo() != NO_SPECIALUNIT &&
        GC.getInfo(u.getSpecialCargo()).isCarrierUnitAIType(eUnitAI))
    {
        bValid = true;
    }

This keeps the useful fallback that the 2020 commit was trying to preserve: a mod-mod
need not explicitly add the UnitAI flag to every special carrier, provided its
SpecialUnitInfo says that the requested carrier role can carry that SpecialUnit class.
It simply prevents a Fighter carrier from satisfying a Missile/People role and vice
versa.

No XML change is required to fix the root.

===============================================================================
C031-WIP29 ADDENDUM — F341 CONFIRMED
===============================================================================

F341 / provisional KI#664 — `AI_isExcessSeaExplorers` subtracts a PLAYER-GLOBAL
sea-explorer training count from a WATER-AREA-LOCAL count, allowing explorer builds
for unrelated oceans to suppress excess-explorer retirement in this ocean.

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — inherited AdvCiv `advc.017b` scope mismatch; current SAS retains it.

ROOT
----
Current `CvPlayerAI::AI_isExcessSeaExplorers` does:

    int iHave = AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs(kWaterArea, UNITAI_EXPLORE_SEA) -
            AI_getNumTrainAIUnits(UNITAI_EXPLORE_SEA);
    return (AI_neededExplorers(kWaterArea) < iHave + iChange);

The first term is deliberately scoped to `kWaterArea`. The subtraction is not:
`AI_getNumTrainAIUnits` is the player's global count for that UnitAI across all cities.

BOOKKEEPING / NO HIDDEN DOUBLE-COUNT
------------------------------------
This is not compensating for a hidden global duplicate inside
`AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs`.

When a city queues a unit, `CvCity::pushOrder` increments:

    getArea().changeNumTrainAIUnits(getOwner(), eUnitAI, 1);
    GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).AI_changeNumTrainAIUnits(eUnitAI, 1);

For a coastal city, `getArea()` is the CITY'S LAND AREA. Thus a queued naval explorer
is not entered into the target water area's `CvArea::m_aaiNumTrainAIUnits` simply by
being naval.

`AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs(kWaterArea, ...)` compensates for exactly that by scanning
cities whose `waterArea() == &kWaterArea` and adding that city's local
`getNumTrainUnitAI`. Therefore only explorer orders in coastal cities attached to the
requested sea are added to the water-area count.

Subtracting the global player training counter correctly removes those LOCAL queued
explorers when the helper wants to judge already-existing explorers, but it also
subtracts explorer orders from every OTHER disconnected sea. There is no matching
foreign-area addition for those remote orders.

CONCRETE CURRENT CONSEQUENCE
----------------------------
Take two disconnected oceans A and B.

Ocean A:
    `AI_neededExplorers(A) == 0`
    one existing `UNITAI_EXPLORE_SEA`
    no explorer being trained for A

Ocean B:
    one coastal city is training one `UNITAI_EXPLORE_SEA`

Then for A:

    AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs(A, EXPLORE_SEA) == 1
    AI_getNumTrainAIUnits(EXPLORE_SEA)       == 1   // the unrelated B order
    iHave                                    == 0

and:

    AI_neededExplorers(A) < iHave
    0 < 0  -> false

So the explorer in fully explored ocean A is declared NOT excess solely because a
replacement/explorer is being built for disconnected ocean B.

Without the unrelated B order, `iHave == 1` and `0 < 1` is true, so exactly the same
unit is correctly recognized as excess.

LIVE UNIT-AI EFFECT
-------------------
`CvUnitAI::AI_exploreSeaMove` periodically (13% synchronized chance) asks this helper
whether its current sea explorer is excess. When true, AdvCiv deliberately tries to
re-purpose the ship into another useful naval role; if no suitable role survives, the
later excess path can scrap it when unit maintenance is positive.

The cross-ocean subtraction therefore suppresses a real retirement/reclassification
path. The effect is bounded by remote training state in a simple one-order example,
but it is systematic and can recur or persist when an empire has multiple disconnected
coasts successively training explorers. Each unrelated queued explorer can mask one
existing explorer from every other sea's local excess test.

This is exactly the kind of area isolation this helper otherwise tries to preserve:
`AI_neededExplorers` and `AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs` are both evaluated per water area.
The global subtraction breaks only the final reconciliation.

ANCESTRY
--------
K-Mod has `AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs` and the global/player training counter but does not
have `AI_isExcessSeaExplorers` in this AdvCiv form. Base AdvCiv 1.14 contains the same
`advc.017b` helper and the same global subtraction as current SAS. This root is therefore
inherited AdvCiv rather than created by SAS.

The older K-Mod changelog's sea-explorer fixes do not repair this later helper scope;
this specific `AI_isExcessSeaExplorers` reconciliation is AdvCiv code.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
No existing album/Known-Issues root was found for this exact explorer helper.

SAS already has a closely related design precedent elsewhere: global queued naval-role
guards have been rejected when they suppress valid behavior on unrelated seas, because
water-area helper counts already provide the correct local scope. F341 is the inherited
mirror image: a global queued explorer count suppresses local retirement rather than
local construction.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Preserve the apparent purpose — exclude explorers currently being trained for THIS sea
when deciding whether an existing explorer is excess — but subtract a water-area-local
training count rather than `AI_getNumTrainAIUnits`.

A simple robust direction is to expose/reuse the same coastal-city training component
that `AI_totalWaterAreaUnitAIs(kWaterArea, EXPLORE_SEA)` adds, e.g. sum
`getNumTrainUnitAI(UNITAI_EXPLORE_SEA)` only for this player's cities whose
`waterArea() == &kWaterArea`, then subtract that local sum.

Do not merely remove the subtraction without checking the original `advc.017b` intent:
local queued explorers would then make existing ships look excess while their
replacement is still under construction, reintroducing the oscillation/inconsistency
that the helper was designed to avoid.

CURRENT AUDIT STATE AFTER F341
------------------------------

Unique files complete — 30/169
Confirmed deep-reloop roots — F321 through F341
F342 / provisional KI#665 — UNUSED
Latest physical checkpoint — C031-WIP29
No repository source files modified.

   inherited worker-demand helpers, preserving producer->contract->consequence proof.


===============================================================================
C031-WIP30 ADDENDUM — F342 CONFIRMED
===============================================================================

F342 / provisional KI#665 — `AI_exploreSeaMove` retains AdvCiv's positive
`AI_countUnimprovedBonuses(..., 5)` look-ahead when converting an excess/outdated
exploring Work Boat into `UNITAI_WORKER_SEA`. Positive look-ahead deliberately calls
`canBuild(..., bTestVisible=true)` and can therefore admit an imminent-border resource
whose improvement tech is not actually known. The unit changes role immediately, but
`AI_workerSeaMove` then uses real executable `canBuild` checks and can have no work at
all. Current SAS already fixed the same future-tech false demand on the city-production
side by changing `AI_neededSeaWorkers` from look-ahead 5 to 0; the inherited transform
path was left unreconciled.

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — inherited AdvCiv transform bug still present in SAS; current SAS's explicit
Work Boat demand repair supplies especially strong contract evidence that this remaining
positive-look-ahead use is wrong for an immediate role change.

ROOT
----
Inside current `CvUnitAI::AI_exploreSeaMove`, when a non-human sea explorer is judged
excess or outdated, AdvCiv tries several alternative UnitAI roles. `UNITAI_WORKER_SEA`
is first. Immediately before changing the role it says:

    // Before transforming a Work Boat, check if there is sth. to improve.
    if(transformTypes[i] == UNITAI_WORKER_SEA &&
        kOwner.AI_countUnimprovedBonuses(*pWaterArea, plot(), 5) <= 0)
    {
        continue;
    }
    AI_setUnitAIType(transformTypes[i]);
    AI_update();
    return;

The comment calls this the "last check before changing the AI type", but the helper's
positive `iLookAhead` does not mean "work this unit can perform now".

`CvPlayerAI::AI_countUnimprovedBonuses` uses the positive look-ahead only for unowned
plots expected to enter the first cultural expansion soon. For those plots it calls:

    AI_isUnimprovedBonus(p, pFromPlot, false)

and `AI_isUnimprovedBonus(..., bCheckPath=false)` in turn tests connecting builds with:

    canBuild(p, eLoopBuild, false, !bCheckPath)

so this becomes `canBuild(..., false, true)` — `bTestVisible=true`.

`CvPlayer::canBuild` explicitly permits a missing build prerequisite tech in visible
mode unless that tech belongs more than one era beyond the player's current era. It
also skips the normal feature-tech and gold-cost checks in visible mode. Thus this
look-ahead is a UI/future-possibility style test, not an executable Work Boat mission
contract.

CURRENT SAS CONTRACT EVIDENCE
-----------------------------
Current `CvCityAI::AI_neededSeaWorkers` contains a SAS repair documenting this exact
problem and deliberately changed both inherited calls from look-ahead 5 to 0:

    const int iLookAhead = 0;

The accompanying source comment explains that positive look-ahead sets
`bCheckPath=false`, which makes `canBuild` use `bTestVisible=true`, and that this was
causing Work Boats for resources such as ocean Whales that could not actually be
improved yet. The stated intended production behavior is to count bonuses that are
owned, reachable and buildable NOW.

That repair did not change the separate `AI_exploreSeaMove` last-check, which still
passes literal 5 in current SAS.

CONCRETE CURRENT XML REPRODUCTION
---------------------------------
Current SAS supplies a direct early-game example without hypothetical mod-mod data:

* `UNIT_WORKBOAT`
  - prerequisite tech: `TECH_FISHING`
  - default/explicit role includes `UNITAI_WORKER_SEA`
  - can build `BUILD_WHALING_BOATS`
  - has two moves, no cargo, and `bNoRevealMap=0`
* `AI_unitValue(UNIT_WORKBOAT, UNITAI_EXPLORE_SEA, ...)` accepts it through the
  inherited sea-explorer fallback (`cargoSpace <= 1 && !isNoRevealMap()`), so ordinary
  city `AI_chooseUnit(UNITAI_EXPLORE_SEA)` can legitimately train a Work Boat as a sea
  explorer even though its XML default role is worker-sea.
* `BONUS_WHALE` has `TechReveal=NONE`, so the Whale is visible before Seafaring.
* `BUILD_WHALING_BOATS` requires `TECH_SEAFARING`.
* `TECH_SEAFARING` is Ancient Era.

Take an Ancient player that knows Fishing but not Seafaring. It has an exploring Work
Boat and no currently owned/buildable sea bonus. A Whale lies on an unowned city-radius
plot in the same water area, and the city's first border expansion is within the
look-ahead window.

`AI_countUnimprovedBonuses(..., 5)` examines that unowned Whale. Because Whale is
already revealed and Seafaring is in the current era, `canBuild(...,
bTestVisible=true)` does not reject the missing Seafaring prerequisite. The helper
therefore returns positive.

If the exploring Work Boat reaches the normal `bTransform` branch — e.g. the 13%
excess-explorer reconsideration succeeds — `UNITAI_WORKER_SEA` is its first transform
candidate. The Work Boat has that role flag and positive worker-sea `AI_unitValue`, so
the false-positive Whale passes the last check and the unit immediately changes from
`UNITAI_EXPLORE_SEA` to `UNITAI_WORKER_SEA`.

LIVE CONSEQUENCE AFTER TRANSFORMATION
-------------------------------------
`CvUnitAI::AI_workerSeaMove` does not use the future-visible test. Its first productive
choice is `AI_improveBonus()`, and that helper scans OWNED plots and ultimately requires
ordinary executable `canBuild(kPlot, eBestBuild)`.

In the reproduction there is no owned actionable sea bonus and the only anticipated
Whale cannot be improved without Seafaring anyway. `AI_improveBonus()` therefore
returns false. The worker-sea routine then only tries retreat/safety and finally:

    getGroup()->pushMission(MISSION_SKIP);

There is no `UNITAI_WORKER_SEA` -> `UNITAI_EXPLORE_SEA` recovery path in
`AI_workerSeaMove`. Repository-wide checks of this role path show the automatic
explorer conversions occur in other naval-role routines, not in worker-sea movement.
Thus the false-positive last check can take a useful explorer out of exploration and
leave it repeatedly idling as a worker until a genuinely executable sea-bonus job
appears. If the missing tech is the blocker, that can last far beyond the nominal
five-turn cultural look-ahead.

Even when the improvement tech is already known, the positive look-ahead can still
convert the explorer before the tile is actually owned, producing several turns of
avoidable worker idling. The missing-tech Whale case demonstrates that the mismatch is
not merely deliberate anticipation of an imminent border pop.

ANCESTRY
--------
Base AdvCiv 1.14 contains the same `AI_exploreSeaMove` transform check with literal
look-ahead 5. This is part of the AdvCiv sea-explorer transform/reclassification path
(`advc.017b` neighborhood), not a new SAS transform implementation.

Base AdvCiv also used positive look-ahead in `AI_neededSeaWorkers`; SAS later repaired
that production-side use by changing it to 0 after observing future-tech/unreachable
Work Boat demand. The transform-side use remained unchanged. Therefore the underlying
false-positive transform is inherited AdvCiv, while SAS currently contains an
incomplete reconciliation: its production contract has been corrected but its
explorer-role conversion still applies the old future-visible semantics.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
KI#157 covers later Work Boat production/availability and movement-target mismatches:
matching need to the correct water areas, avoiding unrelated global queued-boat
suppression, allowing owned off-BFC seafood to be resolved, and skipping already
connected targets. It does not document or repair an exploring Work Boat changing into
worker-sea because an unowned/future-tech look-ahead target passes visible-mode
`canBuild`.

The earlier SAS `AI_neededSeaWorkers` look-ahead=0 source comment is relevant evidence
for F342 but is not itself this finding; F342 is the still-live role-transition caller.

This is also separate from F341. F341 can incorrectly delay whether an explorer is
considered excess because of unrelated-ocean training. F342 starts only once
`bTransform` is already true and can choose the wrong replacement role from a
non-executable future target.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
For the narrow SAS-consistency repair, make the final `UNITAI_WORKER_SEA` transform
check use the same current-actionability semantics as current `AI_neededSeaWorkers`,
i.e. call `AI_countUnimprovedBonuses(..., 0)` rather than 5.

That is deliberately conservative for a role transition: do not convert an explorer
until there is an owned, pathable, currently buildable sea-bonus target. A city may
still produce/retain exploration normally until the work actually exists.

If retaining border-expansion anticipation is desired, do not reuse the current
positive-look-ahead helper unchanged. Split "future ownership / skip border path" from
"visible-mode build legality" so the anticipated plot can be tested without allowing
missing prerequisite techs. The core requirement is that the LAST CHECK before an
immediate UnitAI change must agree with the executable build contract used by
`AI_workerSeaMove`.

CURRENT AUDIT STATE AFTER F342
------------------------------

Unique files complete — 30/169
Confirmed deep-reloop roots — F321 through F342
F343 / provisional KI#666 — UNUSED
Latest physical checkpoint — C031-WIP30
No repository source files modified.

-----------
1. Continue downward through `AI_countCityFeatures`, `AI_neededWorkers`, and adjacent

   dormant mod-mod classification hazards remain control notes only.

   SAS worker/Work Boat changes before spending another finding number.


===============================================================================
F343 / provisional KI#666 — AI_countOwnedBonuses double-counts one neutral
shared-radius resource once per city, inflating physical resource multiplicity
===============================================================================

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — inherited BtS/K-Mod physical-count bug still present in AdvCiv/SAS.
Owned shared-radius resources are explicitly deduplicated through getWorkingCity(),
but the parallel neutral/easily-claimed branch has no unique-plot ownership and can
count the same physical plot from every overlapping city radius.

ROOT
----
Current `CvPlayerAI::AI_countOwnedBonuses` says it counts bonuses "inside city radius
or easily claimed" by summing the city helper independently for every city:

    FOR_EACH_CITYAI(pCity, *this)
    {
        iCount += pCity->AI_countNumBonuses(eBonus, true,
                pCity->getCommerceRate(COMMERCE_CULTURE) > 0, -1);
        if (iCount >= iMaxCount)
            return iMaxCount;
    }

`CvCityAI::AI_countNumBonuses` correctly makes an OWNED shared-radius plot belong to
only one city for counting purposes:

    if (bIncludeOurs && ePlotOwner == eOwner &&
        kPlot.getWorkingCity() == this)
    {
        iCount++;
    }

but its immediately following neutral branch is simply:

    else if (bIncludeNeutral && !kPlot.isOwned())
        iCount++;

There is no `getWorkingCity()` equivalent for an unowned plot and no visited-plot set
in the player-level sum. `CityPlotIter` visits the full workable radius of each city.
Therefore one unowned bonus lying in the overlapping radii of two culturally active
cities is added twice; three overlapping cities can add it three times, etc.

This is not compensating for some other omission. Bonuses already owned inside city
radii are deliberately assigned to one working city, while owned bonuses outside all
city radii are counted in a separate unique map-wide pass. Only the speculative
neutral/easily-claimed part lacks physical-plot uniqueness.

CURRENT CONTRACT EVIDENCE
-------------------------
The callers do not treat this return value as "number of city opportunities". They
explicitly use it as the number of physical resource copies.

In the improvement/resource part of `AI_techValue`, current SAS even labels the result:

    int iBonuses = (bRevealed ? AI_countOwnedBonuses(eLoopBonus) : // actual count
        ...);

and later adds value for extra copies through `(iBonuses - 1)`.

More decisively, the K-Mod resource-enabling branch caps the helper at 2 and uses the
result as a binary "one copy versus multiple copies" distinction:

    int iOwned = AI_countOwnedBonuses(eLoopBonus, 2);
    if (iOwned > 0)
    {
        int iEnableValue = 4;
        iEnableValue += AI_bonusVal(eLoopBonus, 1, true) * iCityCount;
        iEnableValue *= (iOwned > 1) ? 120 : 100;
        iEnableValue /= 100;
        iValue += iEnableValue;
    }

Thus a duplicate city-radius incidence is directly misinterpreted as a second physical
copy and earns the 20% multiple-copy modifier.

CURRENT SAS REPRODUCTION
------------------------
Current SAS supplies a clean ordinary example with `BONUS_WHALE`:

* `BONUS_WHALE` has `TechReveal=NONE`, so it is already visible.
* Its `TechCityTrade` is `TECH_SEAFARING`.
* Put one Whale on an unowned water plot that lies in the outer workable ring of two
  coastal cities belonging to the same AI.
* Both cities have positive culture commerce. They can already have their first border
  expansion while the shared outer-ring Whale remains neutral until the later border
  expansion; this need not be a one-turn founding edge.

When the AI evaluates `TECH_SEAFARING`, the resource-enabling branch calls:

    AI_countOwnedBonuses(BONUS_WHALE, 2)

Each city calls `AI_countNumBonuses(..., bIncludeNeutral=true, ...)`. The shared Whale
is unowned and therefore passes the neutral branch in BOTH city iterations. The
player-level helper reaches its cap and returns 2 although there is only one Whale on
the map in those two radii.

`AI_techValue` consequently applies the 120% "multiple copies" multiplier instead of
100%. The earlier build/improvement valuation can likewise see `iBonuses == 2` and add
an extra-copy term. This directly biases research ranking toward Seafaring based on a
nonexistent second resource copy.

The same helper is also used in corporation and civic valuation as literal resource
multiplicity. For `AI_corporationValue(pCity == NULL)`, prerequisite-resource counts are
summed through `AI_countOwnedBonuses` and then multiply the corporation's yield and
commerce effects (and maintenance). A neutral shared-radius corporation resource can
therefore also inflate global corporation estimates while it remains unowned. The
tech example is sufficient on its own and does not rely on that later-game state.

ANCESTRY
--------
This architecture is inherited all the way from BtS.

Civ4CE/BtS `CvPlayer::countOwnedBonuses` first counts owned bonuses outside city radii,
then loops every city and adds:

    AI_countNumBonuses(eBonus, true,
        pLoopCity->getCommerceRate(COMMERCE_CULTURE) > 0, -1)

K-Mod retains the same structure (plus its bonus-revealed shortcut). AdvCiv's
`advc.042` explicitly says `AI_countOwnedBonuses` was cut from `CvPlayer.cpp` "w/o
functional changes"; later AdvCiv optimizations added `iMaxCount` and cleaned up
Advanced Start handling but retained the per-city neutral sum.

So this is an inherited BtS/K-Mod root preserved by AdvCiv and current SAS, not a
SAS-local regression.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
This is distinct from the nearby `AI_countCityFeatures` overlap question. That helper
counts city-radius FEATURE incidences, and at least one important consumer (per-city
feature happiness) genuinely needs one incidence per affected city. Its semantics are
therefore mixed.

`AI_countOwnedBonuses`, by contrast, has direct callers that call the value an "actual
count", cap it at two to ask whether more than one copy exists, and multiply
corporation input effects by that count. One physical resource must therefore be unique
regardless of how many city radii overlap it.

This is also separate from F342. F342 concerns future-visible build legality when
turning an explorer into a worker-sea role. F343 concerns physical resource
multiplicity and requires no worker or pathfinding behavior.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Preserve the intended "easily claimed" anticipation, but count each neutral physical
plot at most once for the player.

A robust repair is to make the neutral part plot-unique at player scope rather than
blindly summing every city's neutral incidences. For example:

1. Keep owned in-radius bonuses deduplicated through the existing working-city rule.
2. Count neutral candidate plots in a separate unique map/plot pass, adding a plot only
   if at least one culturally active city would qualify it under the existing
   land/water city-radius rules.

Alternatively maintain an explicit visited-plot set while aggregating neutral city
radius candidates. In Civ4's C++03 environment a compact plot-index marker/vector is
safer than trying to assign an unowned plot to `getWorkingCity()`, because an unowned
plot normally has no working-city owner assignment.

Do NOT merely turn `bIncludeNeutral` off: the original helper intentionally anticipates
resources that are easy to claim, and tech valuation depends on that behavior. The
bug is duplicate physical multiplicity, not the anticipation itself.

------------------------------

1. Continue through `AI_neededWorkers` and adjacent worker/economic helpers with F344
   unused, preserving KI#157/KI#195/KI#216 as duplicate/control boundaries.
2. Continue downward through corporation/resource helpers after the immediate worker
   tranche; F343 already owns neutral-overlap physical-count duplication.
3. Keep distinguishing physical-count helpers from deliberately per-city incidence
   helpers rather than applying a blanket "overlap is bad" rule.


===============================================================================
F344 / provisional KI#667 — AI_isFocusWar never records the first pushover war,
so its explicit "multiple weak wars" focus exception can never trigger
===============================================================================

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — inherited AdvCiv one-line state bug introduced by the 2021 advc.105
pushover-war refinement; still present unchanged in Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS.

ROOT
----
Current `CvPlayerAI::AI_isFocusWar` intentionally avoids treating a war against a far
weaker civilization as something that should dominate the AI's economy. The source
explicitly preserves an exception when there are multiple such wars:

    // Much weaker targets aren't worth focusing on (except maybe when there are multiple)
    bool bFirst = true;
    for (TeamIter<CIV_ALIVE,KNOWN_POTENTIAL_ENEMY_OF> itTeam(getTeam());
        itTeam.hasNext(); ++itTeam)
    {
        if (kOurTeam.AI_getWarPlan(itTeam->getID()) != NO_WARPLAN)
        {
            if (!kOurTeam.AI_isPushover(itTeam->getID()))
                return true;
            ... find a member capital ...
            if (pEnemyCapital != NULL && pEnemyCapital->isArea(*pArea))
            {
                if (!bFirst) // Multiple wars
                    return true;
                bFirst = true;
            }
        }
    }
    return false;

`bFirst` starts true and is never assigned false. Consequently `if (!bFirst)` is
unreachable. The first matching pushover war leaves the flag exactly as it began, the
second matching pushover war sees true again, and any further matching wars do the
same.

The only coherent implementation of the written state machine is to mark the first
match as seen after it fails the `!bFirst` test — i.e. `bFirst = false` (or, more
readably, replace the variable with a `bFoundPushoverWarInArea` flag).

INTRODUCTION / ANCESTRY
-----------------------
The defect is directly visible at its introduction.

AdvCiv commit `29ec9f8034a42209c84136c2baca2491453f0e2b`, dated 2021-02-15, is titled:

    AI: Be less distracted by wars against far weaker civs
    [change id advc.105]

Before that commit `AI_isFocusWar` broadly returned true for chosen wars (plus the
existing defensive/alert cases). The commit introduced `CvTeamAI::AI_isPushover` and
replaced that broad behavior with the current per-war loop. The added diff contains
exactly:

    // Much weaker targets aren't worth focusing on (except maybe when there are multiple)
    bool bFirst = true;
    ...
    if (pEnemyCapital != NULL && pEnemyCapital->isArea(*pArea))
    {
        if (!bFirst) // Multiple wars
            return true;
        bFirst = true;
    }

Thus this is not an ambiguous later refactor or SAS edit. The typo entered in the
feature commit that created the exception. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and SAS retain it.
K-Mod/BtS do not contain this later AdvCiv pushover-focus loop.

SUPPORTED CURRENT REPRODUCTION
------------------------------
Take an AI that:

* has a capital and is not currently `AI_STRATEGY_ALERT2`;
* has chosen war plans against two enemy teams;
* both enemy teams satisfy current `CvTeamAI::AI_isPushover` (e.g. two almost-defeated
  one-city rivals against a much larger/more powerful AI);
* both enemy capitals are in the AI capital's land area; and
* the area is not independently `AREAAI_DEFENSIVE` in a state that makes the earlier
  checks sufficient by themselves.

`AI_isAnyChosenWar()` permits the function to enter the pushover loop. Both war-plan
teams are deliberately rejected by the `!AI_isPushover` fast return. The first capital
passes the area test, but `bFirst` remains true. The second capital passes too, yet
`!bFirst` is still false. The function returns false.

The source comment and branch structure say that the second such war is the intended
point at which the AI should return true.

LIVE CONSEQUENCES
-----------------
`AI_isFocusWar` is a central AdvCiv replacement for many older raw "has a war plan"
checks, so this false negative propagates beyond the helper itself.

A particularly direct consequence occurs in `AI_doTurnUnitsPost`:

    bool const bUpgradeFocusWar = AI_isFocusWar();
    if (bUpgradeFocusWar)
        iUpgradeBudget = std::min(getGold(), AI_goldTarget(true));
    else
        ... peacetime-style proportional budget ...

and `AI_goldTarget` itself divides the upgrade component by 4 (or by 10 in some states)
when `AI_isFocusWar()` is false. Thus an AI fighting the exact multiple-pushover case
that the source intended to count as war focus can reserve/spend only a fraction of its
intended emergency upgrade budget.

`AI_maxUnitCostPerMil(NULL)` is another explicit quantitative consumer. When focus-war
is true it adds:

    iMaxUnitSpending += 55;

whereas the false result omits that allowance (apart from unrelated total-war/dagger
adjustments). This can suppress military production/spending during two simultaneous
weak wars.

Other current consumers use `AI_isFocusWar` to:

* run CRUSH UnitAI conversions (`AI_doTurnUnitsPre`);
* tolerate a lower financial safety margin during war;
* double selected military/mobility tech value and mark tech-unit valuation as wartime;
* reduce infrastructure emphasis while fighting;
* alter civic/hurry valuation and a large number of production/mission heuristics.

The exact downstream effect depends on the surrounding strategy state, but the false
negative is therefore behaviorally live and broad.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
Earlier album controls around `AI_isPushover` concerned the heuristic definition and
possible asymmetric/tuning questions. F344 is not about whether the pushover threshold
is well tuned. It assumes `AI_isPushover` is correct and shows that the explicitly
written "multiple pushover wars" exception cannot execute because its local state flag
never changes.

This is separate from war-plan/area-AI approximations elsewhere. No alternative helper
can make `!bFirst` true; it is a local deterministic state bug.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
The surgical correction is the obvious one-line state transition:

    if (!bFirst)
        return true;
    bFirst = false;

A clearer formulation would avoid inverted naming altogether:

    bool bFoundPushoverWarInArea = false;
    ...
    if (pEnemyCapital != NULL && pEnemyCapital->isArea(*pArea))
    {
        if (bFoundPushoverWarInArea)
            return true;
        bFoundPushoverWarInArea = true;
    }

No broader tuning change is needed. This restores exactly the behavior described by
the introducing commit's own comment: one far weaker war can be ignored as a major
focus, but multiple relevant weak wars should collectively count.

===============================================================================
F345 / provisional KI#668 — area-specific AI_missionaryValue drops same-team
cities, so production can value a real teammate spread mission at zero
===============================================================================

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — inherited BtS/K-Mod team-internal missionary valuation inconsistency,
explicitly noticed but not repaired by AdvCiv; still live in current SAS.

ROOT
----
`CvPlayerAI::AI_missionaryValue` uses two different definitions of "our" cities
depending on whether the caller supplies an area.

For a global call (`pArea == NULL`) it is team-wide:

    iOurCitiesHave = kTeam.getHasReligionCount(eReligion);
    iOurCitiesCount = kTeam.getNumCities();

but for the area-specific call used by city production it becomes player-only:

    iOurCitiesHave = pArea->countHasReligion(eReligion, getID()) +
            countReligionSpreadUnits(pArea, eReligion, true);
    iOurCitiesCount = pArea->getCitiesPerPlayer(getID());

If all of this player's cities in the area already have the religion, the internal
spread value is therefore set to zero even when a teammate has reachable same-area
cities that lack it.

Those teammate cities are not recovered by the external-spread pass. Current AdvCiv
uses:

    for (PlayerIter<MAJOR_CIV,OTHER_KNOWN_TO> itOther(getTeam()); ...)

and `AgentIterator` defines `OTHER_KNOWN_TO` as a met player whose team is explicitly
NOT `m_eTeam`. `AI_isTargetForMissionaries`, called inside that loop, likewise asserts
that the target is on another team.

Thus with `pArea != NULL`, same-team cities belong to neither side of the valuation:
not player-internal and deliberately not external.

CURRENT SOURCE ACKNOWLEDGEMENT
------------------------------
AdvCiv itself leaves the inconsistency documented immediately above
`AI_isTargetForMissionaries`:

    Tbd.: AI_missionaryValue and AI_spreadReligion handle (team-)internal spread
    differently (they probably shouldn't)

The deeper producer/consumer trace confirms that this is behaviorally meaningful, not
just stylistic duplication.

SUPPORTED REPRODUCTION
----------------------
Take two AI players A and B on the same team (or otherwise in the ordinary Civ4
same-team configuration). Let:

* A own the holy city for religion R;
* all of A's cities in the relevant land area already contain R;
* B have a reachable city in that same area that does not contain R;
* there be no more valuable eligible foreign-team spread target in the area (for the
  cleanest example, no peaceful foreign target at all).

A city's `AI_bestSpreadUnit` calls:

    kPlayer.AI_missionaryValue(R, area())

The area branch counts only A's cities. `iOurCitiesHave == iOurCitiesCount`, so
`iSpreadInternalValue` becomes 0. The external loop excludes B because B shares A's
team. With no foreign target, the function returns 0.

`CvCityAI::AI_bestSpreadUnit` rejects the religion immediately when
`iReligionValue <= 0`; the normal high-value spread-unit production path therefore
cannot select an R missionary for B's city.

MOVEMENT AI PROVES THE MISSION IS VALID
---------------------------------------
An already-existing A missionary does not share that blind spot.
`CvUnitAI::AI_spreadReligion` loops all alive players and contains an explicit same-team
branch:

    else if (bHasHolyCity && kLoopPlayer.getTeam() == getTeam())
        iPlayerMultiplierPercent =
            (kLoopPlayer.getStateReligion() == eReligion ? 600 : 300);

It then iterates that teammate's cities, checks land access, `canSpread`, pathing and
mission reservations, and can assign the city a positive spread value and move there.

So in the reproduction the production evaluator says the religion has zero spread
value while the movement evaluator for the very unit being valued identifies B's city
as a valid, positively weighted target. This is a direct producer/consumer contract
mismatch.

`AI_neededMissionaries` does not repair the valuation. Its holy/state-religion external
need estimate can remain positive for the area, and `AI_unitValue(UNITAI_MISSIONARY)`
can therefore regard a missionary type as role-valid, but the dedicated
`AI_bestSpreadUnit` production path still skips the religion when
`AI_missionaryValue(..., area())` returns zero.

ANCESTRY
--------
The split is inherited from BtS.

Civ4CE/BtS `AI_missionaryValue` already uses team-wide `kTeam.getHasReligionCount` /
`kTeam.getNumCities` for the NULL-area branch, player-only area counts for non-NULL,
and explicitly excludes same-team players from external spread.

K-Mod rewrote and rebalanced much of missionary valuation but retained this exact
team/global versus player/area split. AdvCiv retained it and later factored target
checks into `AI_isTargetForMissionaries`, adding the explicit TODO quoted above rather
than changing the semantics. Current SAS remains the same in this respect.

This is therefore an inherited BtS/K-Mod bug, not a SAS regression.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
F345 is not a general claim that missionaries should always help teammates, nor a
balance complaint about the 600/300 same-team movement weights. The movement code
already establishes that AdvCiv intends those targets to be valid when the team has the
holy city. The bug is that area-specific production valuation omits the entire target
class that its own movement AI supports.

It is separate from F340's missionary-SEA special-cargo validation bug. F340 can select
a physically incompatible naval carrier for missionaries; F345 can fail to value the
land missionary itself for a same-team city even when no transport is involved.

It is also independent of F343 resource multiplicity and F344 war-focus state.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Make the area-specific internal-spread accounting consistent with the global branch's
team semantics, or explicitly add same-team target valuation equivalent to the movement
AI.

A team-wide area formulation would sum, over living members of `getTeam()`:

* the member's cities in `pArea`;
* those cities already containing `eReligion`; and
* preferably the team's relevant missionaries already in/spreading through the area so
  multiple teammates do not all train for the same missing city.

Alternatively retain player-local internal accounting but add a distinct teammate
spread component before the foreign-team external loop, using the same eligibility
principles as `AI_spreadReligion`.

The important contract is not a particular weight: a reachable same-team city that the
movement AI considers a valid positive mission must not disappear entirely from the
area-specific production value.

------------------------------

Latest physical checkpoint — C031-WIP33

===============================================================================
F346 / provisional KI#669 — AI_neededCityAttackers mistakes legitimate Ancient-era
war targets for "no targets" and contaminates their mean era with Barbarian era
===============================================================================

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — inherited AdvCiv `advc.104p` value/sentinel collision introduced by the
feature that changed city-attack stack sizing from own/game era to target era; still
present unchanged in Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS.

ROOT
----
`CvPlayerAI::AI_neededCityAttackers` intentionally estimates stack size from the mean
current era of civilizations against which this team has a war plan:

    scaled rMeanTargetEra;
    int iEnemies = 0;
    ...
    if (kOurTeam.AI_getWarPlan(itEnemy->getTeam()) != NO_WARPLAN)
    {
        rMeanTargetEra += itEnemy->getCurrentEra();
        iEnemies++;
    }

If no such target exists, the function wants a fallback era so that the calculation is
still defined. But it tests the accumulated *value* instead of whether any enemy was
found:

    if (rMeanTargetEra == 0)
    {
        rMeanTargetEra += GET_PLAYER(BARBARIAN_PLAYER).getCurrentEra();
        iEnemies++;
    }
    rMeanTargetEra /= iEnemies;

Era 0 is a legitimate civilization era. Therefore one or more real war-plan targets
can be present (`iEnemies > 0`) while `rMeanTargetEra == 0` simply because every target
is Ancient. Those targets are then treated as though none had been found: the Barbarian
player's era is injected and the divisor is incremented.

The correct sentinel already exists independently as `iEnemies`.

SUPPORTED REPRODUCTION
----------------------
Let an AI have exactly one known war-plan target T and let T still be in
`ERA_ANCIENT` (current-era index 0). Let the Barbarian player meanwhile have reached,
for example, era 4 through the ordinary AdvCiv Barbarian catch-up system.

The intended mean target era is:

    0 / 1 = 0

Current code executes the fallback because the sum is numerically zero:

    (0 + 4) / (1 + 1) = 2

So a real Ancient target is evaluated as though its era were 2 solely because unrelated
Barbarian technological progress exists elsewhere in the game.

With several Ancient targets the same collision remains: their summed era is still
zero, so the Barbarian era is added once and divided across `iEnemies + 1`.

CURRENT FORMULA CONSEQUENCE
---------------------------
The contaminated mean is not informational only. It feeds both deterministic and
random stack-size terms:

    scaled rEraRatio = (rMeanTargetEra + 1) / GC.getNumEraInfos();
    iModulus = round(strategyBase + rEraRatio * iFlavourExtra +
            rMeanTargetEra / 2);
    iR = floor(rMeanTargetEra / 2) + 4 + (hash % iModulus);

Current SAS has seven eras. For an ordinary military-flavoured AI, raising the mean
from 0 to 2 increases both the fixed term and the randomization range. For some
birthmarks the requested stack can jump by several units even before training-speed,
assault-area and colonial multipliers are applied.

The current SAS `SAS_MIN_ATTACK_CITY_STACK_UNITS = 9` can mask low-end differences in
one readiness comparison, but it does not neutralize the root:

* sufficiently high Barbarian-era contamination can make `AI_neededCityAttackers`
  exceed that floor;
* `AI_stackOfDoomExtra()` is also used directly as the target size for regrouping;
* assault transports use it directly to derive reinforcement and invasion cargo
  thresholds, without the SAS 9-unit city-attack readiness floor.

LIVE CONSUMERS
--------------
The main current `UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY` movement path obtains:

    iWarStackNeeded = AI_stackOfDoomExtra();

and requires a non-Barbarian real-war stack to meet `iWarStackNeeded` (plus the SAS
minimum) before setting `bReadyToAttack`. The same helper is used while under-sized
city-assault groups wait for or join other groups, including an `AI_omniGroup` target
of roughly twice `AI_stackOfDoomExtra()`.

`UNITAI_ASSAULT_SEA` also derives:

    rTargetReinforcementSize = AI_stackOfDoomExtra();
    rTargetInvasionSize = 2 * rTargetReinforcementSize;

so the false target-era increase can make naval invasion transports wait for more land
cargo even though the actual civilization target remains Ancient.

The result therefore affects real army assembly/readiness and amphibious launch
thresholds rather than merely a debug or advisory value.

ANCESTRY
--------
K-Mod's older stack-size formula scaled from the current/game era and therefore did not
have this particular value/sentinel collision.

AdvCiv practical commit 2710 (`168c4a2c799cef88f0461ed850ff1eaa34faa6a6`), titled:

    Tweak to AI the target size of AI city attack stacks

introduced the target-era calculation. The introducing diff explicitly says:

    We don't need more units as _we_ become more advanced.
    Instead check what era our potential targets are in.

and in that same new block adds:

    if (rMeanTargetEra == 0)
    {
        rMeanTargetEra += GET_PLAYER(BARBARIAN_PLAYER).getCurrentEra();
        iEnemies++;
    }

Thus the bug is present at the feature's introduction: zero was simultaneously made a
valid target-era result and used as the "no target" sentinel.

AdvCiv later moved this body from `CvUnitAI::AI_stackOfDoomExtra` into
`CvPlayerAI::AI_neededCityAttackers` (practical commit 3959, refactor only). Base
AdvCiv 1.14 retains the same `rMeanTargetEra == 0` condition verbatim, and current SAS
retains it too.

This is therefore inherited AdvCiv, not SAS-local.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
F346 is not about Barbarian-city expedition sizing; current SAS has a separate
`AI_neededCityAttackersVsBarbarians()` path for deliberate Barbarian-city attacks.
Here the actual intended target is a normal civilization, and the Barbarian player's
technological era leaks into that civilization-war stack estimate only because Ancient
has index 0.

It is also separate from earlier Barbarian-research findings such as KI#408/F086. Those
can affect how quickly Barbarians advance, but F346 remains a deterministic
misclassification whenever the Barbarian era is nonzero and all real war-plan targets
sum to era zero.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Use the actual presence/count sentinel:

    if (iEnemies == 0)
    {
        rMeanTargetEra = GET_PLAYER(BARBARIAN_PLAYER).getCurrentEra();
        iEnemies = 1;
    }

or equivalently retain the addition form while testing `iEnemies <= 0`.

This preserves the intended fallback when no civilization target exists while allowing
one or many legitimate Ancient targets to produce a mean era of exactly zero.

No retuning of stack-size coefficients is required; the repair only restores the
feature's stated target-era contract.

===============================================================================
F347 / provisional KI#670 — failed bounded path in AI_unitTargetMissionAIs can
MAX_INT++ into a negative "nearby" distance and count far joiners as imminent
===============================================================================

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — inherited K-Mod bounded-mission-census failure-path bug; retained by
AdvCiv and current SAS. Vanilla BtS/Civ4CE does not contain the bounded path-turn
extension that creates this root.

ROOT
----
`CvPlayerAI::AI_unitTargetMissionAIs` optionally counts only groups that can reach the
specified target unit within `iMaxPathTurns`:

    int iPathTurns = MAX_INT;
    if (iMaxPathTurns >= 0 && kUnit.plot() != NULL &&
        pLoopSelectionGroup->plot() != NULL)
    {
        pLoopSelectionGroup->generatePath(..., &iPathTurns,
                iMaxPathTurns);
        if (!pLoopSelectionGroup->canAllMove())
            iPathTurns++;
    }
    ...
    if (iMaxPathTurns < 0 || iPathTurns <= iMaxPathTurns)
        iCount += pLoopSelectionGroup->getNumUnits();

The return value of `generatePath` is ignored.

`CvSelectionGroup::generatePath` explicitly defines its output contract as:

    if (piPathTurns != NULL)
    {
        *piPathTurns = MAX_INT;
        if (bSuccess)
            *piPathTurns = kPathFinder.getPathTurns();
    }
    return bSuccess;

Therefore a path that does not exist *within the requested maximum* leaves
`iPathTurns == MAX_INT` by design.

The caller then increments that failure sentinel whenever the joining group cannot all
move. On Civ4's supported 32-bit MSVC/x86 runtime, incrementing `INT_MAX` wraps to the
negative signed endpoint. That negative value trivially satisfies every ordinary
nonnegative path window such as `<= 2` or `<= 3`.

So the exact branch intended to exclude a distant/unreachable group can instead count
it as nearby whenever that group has already spent movement this turn.

SUPPORTED REPRODUCTION
----------------------
No permanent physical disconnection is needed.

1. City-assault group A is the target group.
2. A second group B has an ordinary `MISSIONAI_GROUP` mission targeting A's head unit.
   Current `AI_omniGroup` producers can create such grouping missions with a maximum
   path of 10 turns, so B may legitimately be, for example, 5 turns away.
3. B acts earlier in the player turn and moves toward A. It therefore still has the
   same grouping target but `canAllMove()` is now false.
4. A later runs its city-assault movement and asks only for imminent joiners, e.g.:

       AI_unitTargetMissionAIs(*this, &eMissionAIType, 1,
               getGroup(), 2)

5. The helper asks B's group for a path capped at 2 turns. Because B is still about
   4 turns away, `generatePath` returns false and writes `MAX_INT`.
6. Because B has already moved, the helper executes `iPathTurns++` on that sentinel.
7. The wrapped negative value passes `iPathTurns <= 2`, and every unit in B is counted
   as a nearby joiner.

The same shape can arise from a truly unreachable target, but the ordinary
"longer than this caller's local wait window" case is sufficient and considerably
more common.

LIVE CONSEQUENCE
----------------
The main `UNITAI_ATTACK_CITY` path uses bounded mission counts specifically to decide
whether a stack should wait for backup.

For a ready attack stack, K-Mod/AdvCiv calculates a short `iMaxWaitTurns` (often 1-3)
and obtains:

    int iJoiners = AI_unitTargetMissionAIs(..., iMaxWaitTurns);

It can then `MISSION_SKIP` when the supposedly imminent joiners are large enough.

A concrete current shape is a 6-unit ready stack A and a 2-unit B group still more than
2 turns away. Correct bounded counting returns 0. With the failure-sentinel overflow,
B contributes 2 and the readiness check can become:

    2 * 5 > 6

causing A to wait despite the backup being explicitly outside the 2-turn horizon.

The not-yet-ready and nearby-joiner branches likewise use 2-turn bounded calls, so the
same false-positive census can make attack stacks park or avoid regrouping decisions
for distant groups.

This is a gameplay control-flow consequence, not merely an inaccurate diagnostic
count.

PRODUCER CONTRACT
-----------------
`MISSIONAI_GROUP` groups farther than the bounded query window are normal supported
state. `AI_omniGroup` selects a candidate after a successful path search using its own
caller-supplied maximum, and then pushes:

    MISSION_MOVE_TO_UNIT ... MISSIONAI_GROUP ... pBestUnit

Several attack-city grouping calls permit paths up to roughly 10 turns. The later
`AI_unitTargetMissionAIs(..., 2)` query is deliberately a *narrower* question:
"which of those joiners are close enough that we should wait now?"

Thus a 5-10-turn grouping mission presented to a 2-turn census is not stale or invalid
state; it is exactly why the helper has an `iMaxPathTurns` parameter.

Likewise `canAllMove()==false` is ordinary after B has already taken its movement for
the current turn. The function even contains the increment specifically to account for
that state on successful paths.

ANCESTRY
--------
Civ4CE/BtS `AI_unitTargetMissionAIs` has no path-turn filtering at all; it simply counts
groups whose MissionAI unit/type match. Therefore this particular failure sentinel does
not exist there.

K-Mod 1.46 adds the `iMaxPathTurns` overload. Its implementation already contains the
same sequence:

    int iPathTurns = MAX_INT;
    generatePath(..., &iPathTurns);
    if (!pLoopSelectionGroup->canAllMove())
        iPathTurns++;
    if (iMaxPathTurns == -1 || iPathTurns <= iMaxPathTurns)
        count ...

AdvCiv retained that logic while optimizing mission-type checks, passing the max path
directly to the newer pathfinder, adding the cargo-load kludge and adding `iMaxCount`.
Those changes do not repair the ignored failure return plus sentinel increment.

Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain the root. This is therefore inherited from
K-Mod/BBAI-era mission-count logic, not SAS-local.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
Earlier mission-census findings KI#534/F206 and KI#544/F221 concern empty-group
lifecycle and double-counted loaded cargo in `AI_enemyTargetMissions`. F347 is a
separate helper and a separate invariant: a failed bounded path is converted into a
small/negative path-turn result before the distance filter.

The previously closed multi-MissionAI-array concern is also unrelated; F347 reproduces
with the ordinary single `MISSIONAI_GROUP` request used by live attack-city callers.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Honor path failure before adjusting turns:

    if (iMaxPathTurns >= 0 && ...)
    {
        if (!pLoopSelectionGroup->generatePath(..., &iPathTurns,
                iMaxPathTurns))
            continue;
        if (!pLoopSelectionGroup->canAllMove())
            iPathTurns++;
    }

Alternatively guard the increment/result explicitly against `MAX_INT`, but using the
boolean return is clearer and preserves the pathfinder's contract.

If the "already moved" adjustment can push a successful path from the maximum to one
turn beyond it, the existing final `iPathTurns <= iMaxPathTurns` check correctly rejects
that group; no additional tuning change is required.

------------------------------

===============================================================================
C031-WIP36 — F348 / provisional KI#671 CONFIRMED
AI_espionageVal Counterespionage era-0 normalization can divide by zero for a
supported WorldBuilder/scenario Ancient Spy
===============================================================================

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED, but deliberately bounded to supported scenario / WorldBuilder state.
This is not an ordinary current-SAS random-game crash because the only normal
`UNITAI_SPY` unit requires Classical-era Monarchy.

ROOT
----
`CvPlayerAI::AI_espionageVal` values Counterespionage with:

    int const iEra = getCurrentEra();
    ...
    iCounterValue /= std::max(1, 50 * iEra * (iEra + 1) +
            GET_TEAM(getTeam()).getEspionagePointsAgainstTeam(eTargetTeam)) / 2;

The intended normalization floor is defeated by integer arithmetic. The divisor is
not:

    std::max(1, (...)/2)

but rather:

    std::max(1, X) / 2

because `/` is evaluated on the right-hand side before the compound assignment.
When `X` is 0 or 1, `std::max(1, X)` is 1 and integer `1 / 2` is 0. The subsequent
integer division is therefore a divide-by-zero fault.

At era 0:

    X = own espionage points against the target team

so an Ancient player with 0 or 1 EP against the target reaches the zero divisor.

WHY ORDINARY CURRENT-SAS TRAINING DOES NOT REPRODUCE
-----------------------------------------------------
Current SAS has exactly one unit that uses `UNITAI_SPY`: `UNIT_SPY`.
Its current XML has:

    <DefaultUnitAI>UNITAI_SPY</DefaultUnitAI>
    <bSpy>1</bSpy>
    <PrereqTech>TECH_MONARCHY</PrereqTech>

and current Monarchy belongs to the Classical era. Therefore a normally trained
current-SAS Spy has `iEra >= 1`; the era term alone makes the normalization quantity
at least 100 and the zero-divisor case disappears.

`UNIT_GREAT_SPY` does not supply a hidden normal-game producer. Current XML gives it
`bSpy=0` and `UNITAI_GREAT_SPY`; the UnitAI dispatcher sends it through
`AI_greatPersonMove`, not `AI_spyMove` / `AI_espionageSpy`.

SUPPORTED SCENARIO / WORLDBUILDER PRODUCER
------------------------------------------
The WorldBuilder save loader does not reconstruct units through `canTrain`. In
`Assets/Python/pyWB/CvWBDesc.py`, `CvUnitDesc.apply` resolves the serialized
`UnitType` and directly calls:

    player.initUnit(unitTypeNum, self.plotX, self.plotY,
            UnitAITypes(eUnitAI), self.facingDirection)

If the save leaves `UnitAIType` unspecified, it passes `NO_UNITAI`; `CvPlayer::initUnit`
then deliberately substitutes the unit XML's default UnitAI. Thus a WB scenario can
legitimately define an Ancient AI-owned `UNIT_SPY` and obtain `UNITAI_SPY` without the
player knowing Monarchy.

The same WB format independently serializes/sets the player's starting era, so
`ERA_ANCIENT + UNIT_SPY` is an ordinary supported scenario combination rather than
memory corruption or an invalid direct DLL call.

LIVE CRASH CHAIN
----------------
A minimal supported reproduction is:

1. WorldBuilder/scenario player A is AI-controlled and has current era Ancient.
2. A owns a normal `UNIT_SPY` / `UNITAI_SPY`, e.g. serialized directly in or moved to
   a city owned by major-civ player B.
3. A has 0 (or 1) espionage point against B.
4. On the AI turn, the Spy reaches the ordinary `AI_spyMove` city handling and invokes
   `AI_espionageSpy` once its normal mission-selection conditions are met (placing it
   already fortified in the target city makes this easy to reproduce).
5. `AI_espionageSpy` calls `AI_bestPlotEspionage`.
6. Current Counterespionage XML has no technology prerequisite, costs 100 EP and has
   `iCounterespionageNumTurns=10`.
7. `AI_bestPlotEspionage` deliberately evaluates missions that are unaffordable due
   only to insufficient EP so the AI can decide whether they are worth saving points
   for. Its guard is:

       if (iCost < 0 ||
           (iCost <= iEspPoints && !canDoEspionageMission(...)))
           continue;

   With cost 100 and current EP 0, the second condition is false; valuation proceeds
   even though the mission cannot yet be executed.
8. `AI_espionageVal` enters the Counterespionage branch because its duration is 10.
   At era 0 and own EP 0:

       std::max(1, 0) / 2 == 1 / 2 == 0

9. `iCounterValue /= 0` executes. On Civ4's supported 32-bit MSVC/x86 runtime this is
   an integer divide-by-zero exception / crash.

The mission does not need to be affordable; that is precisely why the valuation path
can encounter the low-EP state.

ANCESTRY
--------
Vanilla BtS / Civ4CE contains the Counterespionage branch but leaves it effectively
empty apart from the old commented attitude line. It therefore does not contain this
arithmetic crash.

K-Mod commit 161 (`f9e8a3c4ceeab74d8d33f1fe8a0323ac5d1bc5be`) introduced an actual
Counterespionage value. Its first normalization form used:

    iCounterValue /= std::max(1, 50*iEra*iEra + ownEP);

which retained a valid denominator floor.

K-Mod commit 162 changed the era scaling to `50*iEra*(iEra+1)` but still kept the
whole denominator inside `std::max`, so it remained safe.

K-Mod practical commit 228 (`285f6c4323e98fe3527a9f6659fcd9a05af9b83c`) changed the formula to the
current half-scale form:

    iCounterValue *= (...)/2 + targetEP;
    iCounterValue /= std::max(1, ... + ownEP)/2;

Moving `/2` *outside* the `std::max` introduced the zero-divisor state for a floored
value of 1. AdvCiv inherited that exact arithmetic; later AdvCiv changes to victory
strategy and memory weighting did not repair the divisor. Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current
SAS retain it.

This is therefore an inherited K-Mod regression, absent from vanilla BtS.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
The earlier team-lifecycle Counterespionage findings in the album concern migration or
persistence of Counterespionage turns/modifiers across team changes. F348 is unrelated:
it is a local arithmetic failure during AI mission valuation before any mission is
performed.

The `GET_PLAYER(eTargetPlayer)`-before-`NO_PLAYER` ordering at the top of
`AI_espionageVal` is also separate and is not being numbered here; the sole current
gameplay caller rejects unowned plots before calling this helper.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Keep the intended half-scale normalization but floor the *actual divisor*, e.g.:

    int const iCounterDivisor = std::max(1,
            (50 * iEra * (iEra + 1) +
             GET_TEAM(getTeam()).getEspionagePointsAgainstTeam(eTargetTeam)) / 2);
    iCounterValue /= iCounterDivisor;

Equivalently, if the historical intent was to halve after flooring but never below 1:

    iCounterValue /= std::max(1,
            std::max(1, 50 * iEra * (iEra + 1) + ownEP) / 2);

The first form is simpler. This repair only restores denominator safety; it does not
retune normal Classical+ Counterespionage valuation.
