C031-WIP49 — F359 CONFIRMED
===============================================================================

F359 / provisional KI#682 — AI_eventValue never values UnitClassPromotions even though
applyEvent grants them to all matching existing units and as permanent free promotions
for future units, so current multi-choice quest rewards can be ranked with an entire
reward branch missing

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — inherited stock BtS event-valuation field omission retained by K-Mod,
AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS. Several current quest-completion reward sets expose it.

ROOT
----
`AI_eventValue` has a dedicated promotion block, but it loops only UnitCombat:

    FOR_EACH_ENUM(UnitCombat)
    {
        if (NO_PROMOTION != kEvent.getUnitCombatPromotion(eLoopUnitCombat))
        {
            ... value existing matching units ...
            iPromotionValue += iNumCities * 50;
        }
    }

There is no corresponding `getUnitClassPromotion` read anywhere in the function.

The application layer explicitly supports both families. After applying UnitCombat
promotions, `CvPlayer::applyEvent` separately loops UnitClass and:

    - grants the event promotion to every existing unit of that UnitClass;
    - calls `setFreePromotion(eLoopUnitClass, eEventPromo, true)`, making the
      promotion available to future units of the class too.

Thus the runtime reward can be broad and permanent while AI valuation is exactly zero
for that field.

CURRENT-DATA REPRODUCTIONS
--------------------------
Current SAS contains many UnitClassPromotion events, including multi-choice quest
rewards where the omission can directly alter the selected reward.

A particularly clean pair is `EVENT_ELITE_SWORDS_DONE`:

    EVENT_ELITE_SWORDS_DONE_1
        UnitClassPromotion:
            UNITCLASS_SWORDSMAN -> PROMOTION_CITY_RAIDER1
        iAIValue = 1000

    EVENT_ELITE_SWORDS_DONE_2
        UnitCombatPromotions:
            UNITCOMBAT_MELEE_POLEARM -> PROMOTION_FIRST_STRIKE1
            UNITCOMBAT_MELEE_SHOCK   -> PROMOTION_FIRST_STRIKE1
        iAIValue = 1000

The second reward enters the existing promotion valuation block; the first reward's
promotion enters no valuation block at all. Yet the first reward is actually applied to
all current Swordsman-class units (including the civilization replacement for that
class) and becomes a permanent free class promotion for future Swordsman-class units.

Other current multi-choice examples include:

- `MASTER_BLACKSMITH_DONE_2`: Swordsman-class Counter Melee;
- `WAR_CHARIOTS_DONE_1`: Chariot-class Combat I;
- `WARSHIPS_DONE_1`: Trireme-class Combat I;
- `GUNS_BUTTER_DONE_1`: Musketman-class Counter Gun;
- `NOBLE_KNIGHTS_DONE_1`: Horse/Camel Knight class Retreat;
- `OVERWHELM_DONE_1`: Combat I for Destroyer, Battleship, Carrier, Fighter and Jet
  Fighter classes.

`OVERWHELM_DONE` is especially broad: reward 1 grants five permanent class promotions,
yet none of those promotion effects contributes to `AI_eventValue`.

ANCESTRY
--------
Civ4CE/BtS already contains only a `getUnitCombatPromotion` valuation loop and no
`getUnitClassPromotion` valuation. K-Mod retains the omission; AdvCiv retains it;
current SAS retains it while continuing to use UnitClassPromotion XML extensively.

This is therefore inherited BtS rather than a SAS-local regression.

CONSEQUENCE
-----------
The AI can systematically under-value UnitClassPromotion reward options and prefer
competing rewards whose fields happen to be represented in `AI_eventValue`. The bias
is not a minor coefficient disagreement: the entire current-unit benefit and the
permanent future free-promotion benefit are absent.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Add a UnitClass promotion valuation parallel to the existing UnitCombat block:

- value current owned units of the affected UnitClass that lack the promotion;
- include a reasonable future-production/free-promotion term;
- avoid double counting if an event grants the same promotion through both UnitCombat
  and UnitClass paths to the same units.

Ideally factor the common promotion-value logic so application and valuation continue
to support the same two field families.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
F359 is independent of F358's late PlotExtraYield ordering. Here the event field is
never read by the evaluator at all. It also differs from F354's non-city building
Yield/Commerce omission because UnitClassPromotion has its own distinct runtime and
multi-choice producers.

C031-WIP50 — F360 CONFIRMED
===============================================================================

F360 / provisional KI#683 — AI_eventValue values TechPercent as the full requested
percentage of total tech cost instead of capping it to remaining research like the
runtime, so near-complete tech rewards are overvalued

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — inherited stock BtS requested-progress-versus-executable-progress bug
retained by K-Mod, AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS. Current Airliner Crash supplies a clean
multi-choice reproduction with no minimum-turn guard.

ROOT
----
For a fixed event technology, `AI_eventValue` immediately adds:

    iValue += (kTeam.getResearchCost(kEvent.getTech()) *
            kEvent.getTechPercent()) / 100;

For flavor/current-research event technologies, the later `eBestTech` path uses the
same full-cost percentage formula.

The application layer does not award that amount blindly. `CvPlayer::applyEvent`
ultimately calls:

    CvTeam::changeResearchProgressPercent(...)

and that function explicitly caps a positive award:

    iBeakers = std::min(getResearchLeft(eIndex),
            getResearchCost(eIndex) * iPercent / 100);

Thus the executable value is:

    min(requested_percent_of_total_cost, research_left)

whereas AI valuation assumes the requested percentage is always fully usable.

CURRENT-DATA REPRODUCTION — AIRLINER CRASH
------------------------------------------
`EVENT_AIRLINER_CRASH_3` is one of three current choices and has:

    Tech              = TECH_FLIGHT
    iTechPercent      = 15
    iTechMinTurnsLeft = 0
    iGold              = 0
    iAIValue           = 1000

Its trigger selects another player who already knows Flight, so this option is a live
catch-up research reward while the AI itself can still research Flight.

Suppose the AI has already completed 90% of Flight. The option is legal: there is no
minimum-turn requirement, and Flight is still researchable before the event.

Runtime:

    requested award = 15% of total Flight cost
    research left   = 10%
    actual award    = 10%

Evaluator:

    credits 15%

The AI therefore overstates the immediate research benefit by 50% in this simple
state. At 99% progress it can credit fifteen times the research that will actually be
added.

Other current TechPercent events (City Ruins, Patron of Knowledge, Ancient Texts,
Secret Knowledge, Heresy and others) inherit the same cap mismatch whenever the
selected event tech has less remaining research than the XML percentage.

ANCESTRY
--------
Civ4CE/BtS already values `researchCost * TechPercent / 100` directly in
`AI_eventValue`; its application path caps positive progress to research remaining.
K-Mod and AdvCiv preserve that contract mismatch; current SAS does too.

This is therefore inherited BtS rather than SAS-local.

CONSEQUENCE
-----------
The AI can prefer or overpay for tech-progress event options near the end of a
technology because it prices beakers that cannot be applied. This is decision-level in
current multi-choice events such as Airliner Crash and Heresy.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Resolve the same event technology used by the application path, then value positive
TechPercent by the executable beaker amount:

    min(researchLeft(eTech), researchCost(eTech) * TechPercent / 100)

Negative TechPercent should likewise mirror `changeResearchProgressPercent`'s lower
bound rather than assuming the raw requested percentage if that branch is retained.

Prefer factoring/shared helper logic so legality, event cost, application and AI value
agree on the selected event tech and executable progress.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
F357 is the analogous city-conversion requested-count cap, but the state and runtime
contract here are independent: F360 concerns research progress and `researchLeft`.
F360 also exists before considering any AdditionalEvent follow-up; that post-state
problem remains a separate F361 candidate.

------------------------------

C031-WIP51 — F361 CONFIRMED
===============================================================================

F361 / provisional KI#684 — AI_eventValue recursively values AdditionalEvents against
the pre-parent-event state, while runtime rechecks their legality after the parent
has already changed state, so it can credit follow-up effects that cannot fire

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — inherited stock BtS recursive event-valuation state-transition bug retained
by K-Mod, AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS. Airliner Crash 3 -> 4 supplies a current,
independent reproduction.

ROOT
----
At the end of `AI_eventValue`, every non-self AdditionalEvent is valued directly from
the original triggered data and the player's *current pre-choice state*:

    iValue += chance * AI_eventValue(eAdditional, kTriggeredData) / 100;

No parent-event effects are simulated before that recursive call, and no
`canDoEvent(eAdditional, ...)` check is performed for the post-parent state.

Runtime ordering is different and explicit:

1. `CvPlayer::applyEvent(parent)` applies the parent's gold/research/city/etc. effects;
2. only near the end does it process AdditionalEvents;
3. for an immediate follow-up it requires:

       canDoEvent(eAdditional, *pTriggeredData)

   *after* the parent has already changed game state;
4. only then can it call `applyEvent(eAdditional, ..., false)`.

Therefore parent effects can invalidate or reduce a child event while the evaluator
still prices the child from the old state.

CURRENT-DATA REPRODUCTION — AIRLINER CRASH 3 -> 4
-------------------------------------------------
`EVENT_AIRLINER_CRASH_3` grants +15% Flight research and has:

    AdditionalEvent EVENT_AIRLINER_CRASH_4, chance 50%

`EVENT_AIRLINER_CRASH_4` grants +20% Flight research. Both require Flight to remain a
valid event tech through the ordinary `canDoEvent` -> `getBestEventTech` ->
`isValidEventTech` path; once the team has Flight, `canResearch(Flight)` is false and
the follow-up cannot execute.

Use a state with exactly 15% of Flight research remaining.

Parent runtime:

    Airliner Crash 3 applies +15%
    Flight completes

Follow-up runtime:

    50% chance branch is reached
    canDoEvent(EVENT_AIRLINER_CRASH_4) == false
    event 4 does not apply
    actual follow-up research value = 0

AI valuation:

    recursively calls AI_eventValue(EVENT_AIRLINER_CRASH_4)
    while Flight is still incomplete in the evaluator's real game state
    credits 50% of the follow-up's research value

This reproduction is deliberately independent of F360. At exactly 15% remaining, the
parent's requested +15% is itself fully executable, so fixing F360's research-left cap
does not remove F361. Even with F360 fixed, the child would still be valued from the
pre-parent state despite being illegal after the parent completes Flight.

The mismatch also occurs without full invalidation. If a parent reduces the amount of
research left, the child's executable reward can shrink before it fires; recursively
valuing the child from the original state still overstates it.

ANCESTRY
--------
Civ4CE/BtS already recursively calls `AI_eventValue` for AdditionalEvents without
simulating the parent state. Its runtime applies the parent before checking/performing
immediate additional events. K-Mod and AdvCiv retain that split; current SAS does too.

This is therefore inherited BtS.

CONSEQUENCE
-----------
The AI can choose an event partly for an expected follow-up that the parent event itself
makes impossible. Airliner Crash 3 can receive phantom expected Flight research when
its own research grant completes Flight first, biasing its ranking against the other
current Airliner Crash choices.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
AdditionalEvent expected value must be based on the state in which the child would
actually execute. Robust options include:

- simulate/project the relevant parent state before child valuation;
- create an event-value helper that accepts projected changes (research, bonus reveal,
  religion/city state, etc.); or
- for simple child contracts, explicitly compute post-parent legality/executable value.

Merely calling `canDoEvent` before the recursive call is insufficient because that
would still test the pre-parent state. The key requirement is post-parent state.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
F360 caps the parent's/child's requested TechPercent to research remaining in whatever
state is being evaluated. F361 concerns *which state* is evaluated. Fixing F360 still
leaves the exactly-15%-remaining Airliner reproduction above.

CURRENT AUDIT STATE AFTER F361
------------------------------

C031-WIP52 — F362 CONFIRMED
===============================================================================

F362 / provisional KI#685 — AI_roundTradeValBounds can leave a rounded value outside
its requested bounds when the preferred multiple is unavailable, so a generous
counterproposal whose lower bound is the original gold amount can be rounded *down*
below that lower bound

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — inherited AdvCiv helper-contract bug introduced with `AI_roundTradeValBounds`
and retained by current SAS. The two live `AI_balanceDeal` gold callers use exactly the
bound shape that exposes it.

ROOT
----
The helper's explicit contract says:

    Set iTradeVal to the nearest multiple of DIPLOMACY_VALUE_REMAINDER
    in [iLower,iUpper]. No change if no such multiple exists.

For `bPreferRoundingUp`, however, implementation does:

    int iTmpVal = iTradeVal;
    AI_roundTradeVal(iTradeVal);      // mutates iTradeVal DOWN immediately
    if (iTradeVal != iTmpVal)
        iTmpVal = iTradeVal + remainder; // preferred UP candidate
    if (iTmpVal within bounds)
        iTradeVal = iTmpVal;

If the upward candidate is outside the interval, nothing restores the original value
or validates the already-mutated downward value. The function can therefore return a
value outside `[iLower,iUpper]`, contradicting both its comment and its parameter
contract.

CURRENT CALLER REPRODUCTION
---------------------------
Current `AI_balanceDeal` has two equivalent gold-balancing sites. When
`bTheyGenerous` and either party is human, they call:

    AI_roundTradeValBounds(iGoldData, true, iGoldData, iMaxGold);

The original required gold amount is deliberately passed as `iLower`; i.e. generous
rounding may round UP but must not lower the balancing amount.

Current SAS defines:

    DIPLOMACY_VALUE_REMAINDER = 5

Take a fully ordinary state:

    computed iGoldData = 12
    iMaxGold           = 14
    bounds             = [12,14]

There is no multiple of 5 in [12,14]. The documented result is therefore “no change”:
12.

Current implementation:

    iTradeVal = 12
    AI_roundTradeVal -> 10
    preferred upward multiple -> 15
    15 is outside [12,14]
    assignment is skipped
    returned iTradeVal -> 10

The result is not merely the nonpreferred multiple; 10 is explicitly below the lower
bound 12.

CALLER CONSEQUENCE
------------------
`AI_balanceDeal` then sees `iMaxGold >= iGoldData` and can insert the accidental 10
gold into the counterproposal. In the generous branch, the caller's design is that the
side being balanced may overshoot / offer a larger treasury portion, not that the
required balancing amount may be rounded down. The helper reverses that policy in the
exact max-gold gap where the next display multiple is unaffordable.

The same defect exists at both the initial-gold and final-gold balancing sites.

INTRODUCTION HISTORY
--------------------
The AdvCiv commit that introduced/refactored the helper adds the exact comment quoted
above and the same implementation. The same change updates the generous balance caller
to pass:

    lower = original iGoldData
    upper = iMaxGold

So intent and failure were introduced together: the lower bound exists specifically to
protect the unrounded balancing requirement, but the helper can return below it.
Base AdvCiv 1.14 retains the same body; current SAS only modernizes surrounding style.

This root is AdvCiv-local rather than BtS/K-Mod: BtS/K-Mod did not have this bounded
rounding helper in this form.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Never mutate the caller's value until a valid candidate has been selected. For example:

    original = iTradeVal
    down = rounded-down multiple
    up = (down == original ? original : down + remainder)

Try candidates in requested preference order, assigning `iTradeVal` only if that
candidate lies within `[iLower,iUpper]`. If neither candidate lies in bounds, leave the
original unchanged exactly as documented.

A minimal patch can also store/restore the original on failure, but computing both
candidates independently is clearer and avoids the recursive false-path state mutation.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
F335 concerns invalid fallback selection of a non-surplus resource in `AI_balanceDeal`;
F336/F337 concern leniency accounting. F362 is independent: the correct gold amount is
computed and the correct bounds are supplied, but the rounding helper violates those
bounds before the caller sees the result.

------------------------------

C031-WIP53 — F363 CONFIRMED
===============================================================================

F363 / provisional KI#686 — AI_calculateConquestVictoryStage mis-parenthesizes the
"don't spare friends when only military victory is possible" exception, so a
nonpositive other-victory weight bypasses every level-3 Conquest gate instead of only
the friendly-rival gate

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — inherited AdvCiv precedence/regression bug introduced by advc.104c in the
2025 commit "AI doesn't try sparing friends when only military victory possible" and
retained by Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS.

ROOT
----
Current level-3 test ends with:

    if (iKnownCivs >= iStartCivs && bTopRank &&
        !bManyOffshoreRivals &&
        (bVeryStrong ||
         (bWarmonger && bHateful && 2 * iConqueredCivs >= iKnownCivs)) &&
        (iFriends == 0 || (iFriends == iRemaining && iFriends == 1)) ||
        iOtherVictoryWeight <= 0)

C++ `&&` binds more tightly than `||`, so this is parsed as:

    (all ordinary level-3 gates && friend gate) ||
    (iOtherVictoryWeight <= 0)

The introducing commit's stated purpose is much narrower. Its full commit message says:

    "I.e. it won't shy away from stages 3 and 4 of a military victory on account of
    friendly relations when all other victory conditions have been disabled."

The diff itself changes only the tail of the old friend condition, making the intended
logical grouping clear. The exception belongs *inside* the final friendship gate:

    ... &&
    (friend gate || iOtherVictoryWeight <= 0)

It was instead appended outside the whole conjunction.

REACHABILITY / CURRENT CONTRACT
-------------------------------
`AI_updateVictoryWeights` stores -1 for victory conditions that are invalid/disabled
and ordinary nonnegative personality weight for valid ones. `AI_calculateConquest...`
sums every non-Conquest victory into `iOtherVictoryWeight`.

Therefore a supported custom-game setup with Conquest enabled and all alternative
victory conditions disabled naturally makes `iOtherVictoryWeight <= 0`. This is exactly
the unusual-victory-settings case named by the introducing commit, not a hypothetical
personality state.

The outer level-2 conditions still have to succeed; this does *not* create Conquest 3
from an otherwise uninterested AI. The defect is the transition from stage 2 to stage 3.

CLEAN REPRODUCTION
------------------
Use a Conquest-only victory setup and a warmongering AI whose current state satisfies
the level-1/2 conditions, for example:

    iStartCivs      = 4
    iKnownCivs      = 3
    iConqueredCivs  = 1
    bWarmonger      = true

Then the level-2 progress tests can pass:

    4 * iKnownCivs >= 3 * iStartCivs
    4 * 3 >= 3 * 4                       -> true

    3 * iConqueredCivs >= iKnownCivs
    3 * 1 >= 3                           -> true

But the intended level-3 test should still fail immediately because:

    iKnownCivs >= iStartCivs
    3 >= 4                               -> false

It may independently also fail `bTopRank`, `!bManyOffshoreRivals`, or the stronger
power/warmonger+hateful threshold.

In a Conquest-only game, however, `iOtherVictoryWeight <= 0` is true. Due to operator
precedence the entire ordinary level-3 conjunction is bypassed, and the function enters
the level-3 block and ultimately returns at least 3.

This precisely exceeds the commit's intended exception: disabling other victories was
supposed to permit fighting Friendly rivals, not to erase knowledge, rank, geography,
power and conquest-progress requirements.

CONSEQUENCE
-----------
Conquest stage 3 is a broadly consumed strategy flag, not merely UI state. Current
consumers include, among others:

- `AI_maxUnitCostPerMil`: military stage 3 adds +20 to recommended unit spending;
- `AI_nukeBaseDestructionWeight`: Conquest 3 increases willingness to value civilian
  nuclear destruction;
- CvTeamAI war valuation: Conquest 3 reduces diplomacy cost in war calculations;
- additional team/UWAI/city-production and victory-strategy consumers throughout the
  DLL.

Thus unusual Conquest-only settings can push a stage-2 AI into materially more extreme
military behavior before the ordinary stage-3 readiness conditions are met.

INTRODUCTION / ANCESTRY
-----------------------
Commit 4baba59a4380e956452d6baf05c8ca36aa3d2b6d (2025-01-10), title:

    AI doesn't try sparing friends when only military victory possible

changed:

    ... && friend_condition)

to:

    ... && friend_condition ||
    iOtherVictoryWeight <= 0)

without adding parentheses around the intended final subcondition. The same precedence
shape is present in Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS.

K-Mod predates this advc.104c exception; this root is therefore an AdvCiv regression,
not a BtS/K-Mod inheritance.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Group the exception with the friendship test only:

    ... &&
    (bVeryStrong || ...) &&
    ((iFriends == 0 || (iFriends == iRemaining && iFriends == 1)) ||
     iOtherVictoryWeight <= 0)

Or factor the final friendship permission into a named boolean before the conjunction,
which would make precedence mistakes much harder to reintroduce.

The stage-4 inner checks should then remain unchanged; the purpose of advc.104c is still
preserved because a Conquest-only AI no longer has to satisfy the friendship blocker.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
This is independent of prior victory-weight tuning and of F344 (`AI_isFocusWar`). F363
is specifically an operator-precedence error in the stage-2 -> stage-3 Conquest
transition introduced by the "don't spare friends" exception.

------------------------------

C031-WIP54 — F364 CONFIRMED
===============================================================================

F364 / provisional KI#687 — AI_doCheckFinancialTrouble consumes the
false->true financial-trouble transition even when the shared production-dirty cooldown
suppresses the requested refresh, so the deferred refresh is never retried for the
rest of that trouble episode

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — inherited BtS transition/cooldown bug present in Civ4CE/BtS, K-Mod,
Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS.

ROOT
----
`AI_doCheckFinancialTrouble` is explicitly edge-triggered:

    bool bFinancialTrouble = AI_isFinancialTrouble();
    if (bFinancialTrouble != m_bWasFinancialTrouble)
    {
        if (bFinancialTrouble)
        {
            int iGameTurn = GC.getGame().getGameTurn();
            // only reset at most every 10 turns
            if (iGameTurn > m_iTurnLastProductionDirty + 10)
            {
                AI_makeProductionDirty();
                m_iTurnLastProductionDirty = iGameTurn;
            }
        }
        m_bWasFinancialTrouble = bFinancialTrouble;
    }

The cooldown timestamp is shared with other production-refresh producers, notably
`AI_nowHasTech`. Therefore entering financial trouble can legitimately happen while
`m_iTurnLastProductionDirty` is recent.

The bug is that the transition state is committed regardless of whether the intended
financial-trouble refresh was actually allowed. Once `m_bWasFinancialTrouble` becomes
true, persistent financial trouble no longer satisfies the outer transition test, so
expiration of the 10-turn cooldown cannot trigger the missed refresh later.

CLEAN REPRODUCTION
------------------
For example:

    turn 100: AI_nowHasTech dirties production
              m_iTurnLastProductionDirty = 100
              m_bWasFinancialTrouble = false

    turn 105: empire first enters financial trouble
              bFinancialTrouble = true
              105 > 100 + 10 -> false
              AI_makeProductionDirty is skipped
              m_bWasFinancialTrouble = true anyway

    turn 111+: cooldown is now old enough, but
               bFinancialTrouble == m_bWasFinancialTrouble == true
               outer transition branch never runs again

The refresh can therefore be skipped for the entire continuous financial-trouble
episode, not merely delayed to turn 111.

LIVE CONSEQUENCE / CITY CONTRACT
--------------------------------
`AI_makeProductionDirty` sets `chooseProductionDirty` on every AI city. `CvCity::doProduction`
checks that flag even when the city already has active production and calls
`CvCityAI::AI_chooseProduction`; that function can clear/reconsider the current queue.

Financial trouble materially changes that chooser. Current code, among other effects:

- makes a near-trouble empire seek `BUILDINGFOCUS_GOLD`;
- reduces ordinary unit-production pressure through `AI_buildUnitProb`;
- changes Settler continuation/production behavior;
- gates or suppresses multiple worker, naval and military production paths.

Thus the dirty refresh is not redundant bookkeeping: it is the mechanism intended to
make already-busy cities react promptly when the empire crosses into the financial-
trouble state. Normal production completion can eventually cause individual cities to
choose again, but that does not repair the missed empire-wide transition refresh and
long builds can remain selected under stale healthy-economy assumptions.

The source comment itself states the intended event:

    // if we just ran into financial trouble this turn

and, when the cooldown permits:

    // redeterimine the best things to build in each city

The implementation loses that event when the cooldown blocks the immediate action.

ANCESTRY
--------
The same state machine appears in the Civ4CE/BtS source, in K-Mod 1.46, in Base AdvCiv
1.14 and in current SAS. K-Mod inherited/retained the original structure and later
changed many financial-trouble heuristics without repairing this edge/cooldown
interaction.

This is therefore an inherited BtS root rather than a SAS or AdvCiv regression.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Preserve the cooldown, but do not consume the entering-trouble transition until its
requested refresh has occurred, or represent the missed action explicitly as pending.

A minimal state-oriented repair could keep `m_bWasFinancialTrouble == false` while
`bFinancialTrouble` is true and the cooldown blocks the refresh; then a later turn will
retry and finally set the remembered state once `AI_makeProductionDirty` succeeds.
That needs care on a true->false exit so the remembered state remains semantically
sound.

A clearer repair is to track a separate pending financial-trouble production refresh:
set it on the false->true transition, execute it once the shared cooldown permits, then
clear the pending flag. This keeps `m_bWasFinancialTrouble` as a pure observed-state
cache and makes deferred-work semantics explicit.

Simply removing the 10-turn rate limit is not necessary to fix the root.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
This is independent of SAS financial-trouble production tuning and of earlier unit-
spending findings. Those determine *what* cities choose once reevaluated. F364 concerns
the state-transition scheduler failing to deliver the intended reevaluation at all
when another recent producer has occupied the shared cooldown.

C031-WIP55 — F365 CONFIRMED
===============================================================================

F365 / provisional KI#688 — AI_updateGoldToUpgradeAllUnits caches a per-unit
upgradePrice by UnitType, so Great-General units with PROMOTION_LEADER's 100% upgrade
discount can be charged the ordinary same-type upgrade cost in the aggregate AI gold
reserve

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — inherited BtS bug present in Civ4CE/BtS, K-Mod 1.46, Base AdvCiv 1.14
and current SAS.

ROOT
----
`AI_updateGoldToUpgradeAllUnits` deliberately caches the estimated upgrade cost of each
unit type:

    // cache the value for each unit type
    std::vector<int> aiUnitUpgradePrice(GC.getNumUnitInfos(), 0);

For each owned unit it first checks:

    UnitTypes eUnitType = pLoopUnit->getUnitType();
    int iCachedUnitGold = aiUnitUpgradePrice[eUnitType];
    if (iCachedUnitGold != 0)
    {
        if (iCachedUnitGold > 0)
            iTotalGold += iCachedUnitGold;
        continue;
    }

When there is no cached value, the function discovers desirable/available upgrade
classes and accumulates the price by calling the *individual unit*:

    iUnitGold += pLoopUnit->upgradePrice(eUpgradeUnitType);

then stores the resulting average under only `eUnitType`:

    aiUnitUpgradePrice[eUnitType] = iUnitGold;

That cache key is invalid because `CvUnit::upgradePrice` is not type-invariant. It ends
with a per-unit promotion-derived adjustment:

    iPrice -= (iPrice * getUpgradeDiscount()) / 100;

Current SAS retains the standard Great-General promotion:

    PROMOTION_LEADER
        iUpgradeDiscount = 100

and attaching the Great General calls `promote(PROMOTION_LEADER, ...)`; promotion
processing feeds that XML value into the unit's `m_iUpgradeDiscount` through
`changeUpgradeDiscount`.

Thus an ordinary unit and a Great-General-attached unit of the exact same UnitType can
have different — in the leader case, radically different — `upgradePrice` values.
Caching that value by UnitType alone loses real per-unit state.

CLEAN CURRENT-DATA REPRODUCTION
-------------------------------
A Rifleman is a straightforward current example:

- `UNIT_RIFLEMAN` is `UNITCOMBAT_GUN` and upgrades to `UNITCLASS_INFANTRY`;
- `PROMOTION_LEADER` is valid for `UNITCOMBAT_GUN`;
- the promotion has `iUpgradeDiscount = 100`;
- therefore an attached Great-General Rifleman's real `upgradePrice(Infantry)` is 0,
  while an otherwise ordinary Rifleman's price is positive whenever the upgrade has a
  positive base cost.

Suppose the player's unit iteration encounters an ordinary Rifleman first. The normal
positive Infantry upgrade estimate is stored in:

    aiUnitUpgradePrice[UNIT_RIFLEMAN]

When a later Great-General Rifleman is reached, the cache branch adds that same positive
amount directly to `iTotalGold` and never calls the leader unit's own
`upgradePrice(Infantry) == 0`.

The iteration order does not make the root disappear. If the free-upgrade leader unit
happens to be encountered before any ordinary copy, its computed zero is also the
vector's "not cached" sentinel, so a later ordinary copy is recomputed and establishes
the positive type cache; any subsequent leader copy is again overcounted. The defect is
therefore fundamentally the cache key, not one particular order.

A second independent reason the UnitType key is too coarse is already present in the
same function: the set of upgrades regarded as useful is tested with the individual
unit's `UnitAI` and area:

    AI_unitValue(eUpgradeUnitType, eUnitAIType, pUnitArea)

so same-type units can also disagree about which upgrade candidates should contribute.
The Great-General discount is the cleaner shipped-data proof because it requires no
argument about AI-role valuation coefficients.

LIVE CONSEQUENCE
----------------
The result is saved in `m_iUpgradeUnitsCachedGold` by `AI_updateCacheData` and is used as
an important empire-level budget input rather than debug-only information.

`AI_goldTarget` begins with:

    int iUpgradeBudget = AI_getGoldToUpgradeAllUnits();

and folds a war/financial-trouble-adjusted fraction of that estimate into the AI's gold
reserve. `AI_doTurnUnitsPost` also derives its actual wartime/peacetime upgrade spending
budget from `AI_goldTarget(true)`; other consumers include hurry/armament logic and the
current SAS upgrade diagnostics.

Therefore a Great-General unit whose next upgrade is actually free can nevertheless
make the AI believe that another ordinary upgrade price must be reserved. Depending on
war/economic state, that can make it hoard too much cash, alter commerce allocation and
change other spending decisions. Actual per-unit upgrading still calls the real
`upgradePrice`, so the execution layer can know the leader upgrade is free while the
strategic reserve that enabled it remains inflated — exactly the estimator/executor
state mismatch at the root.

ANCESTRY
--------
The same UnitType cache and per-unit `upgradePrice` call are present in Civ4CE/BtS,
K-Mod 1.46, Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS.

The XML producer is equally old: Civ4CE/BtS and Base AdvCiv both define
`PROMOTION_LEADER` with `iUpgradeDiscount = 100`, including `UNITCOMBAT_GUN` among the
eligible combat classes. Great-General attachment applies the leader promotion to the
selected unit in the normal shipped gameplay path.

This is therefore an inherited BtS cache-key defect, not a SAS/K-Mod tuning regression.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Do not cache the final `upgradePrice` solely by UnitType.

Safe options include:

1. cache only type-invariant discovery data (e.g. reachable upgrade target classes),
   then call each physical unit's `upgradePrice` when adding its contribution; or
2. expand the cache key to include every state that affects the result — at minimum
   upgrade discount, UnitAI and relevant area/can-train context — though that is more
   complicated and less robust than option 1.

Given that `upgradePrice` is explicitly a `CvUnit` method and promotion state can alter
it, retaining the per-unit price call while caching only reusable candidate discovery
looks like the clearest repair.

Also avoid using literal 0 simultaneously as both "not cached" and a legitimate cached
free-upgrade value if any redesigned cache continues to store prices.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
This is independent of F151/KI#474, which concerned the engine/UI upgrade action cache.
F365 concerns the AI's aggregate strategic gold estimator in `CvPlayerAI` and its invalid
assumption that an individual `CvUnit::upgradePrice` can be memoized by UnitType.

It is also separate from SAS KI#160's actual upgrade-spending cap/diagnostics: those
operate when choosing and paying for concrete upgrades, whereas F365 corrupts the
cached amount the empire believes it should reserve before those per-unit decisions.

CURRENT AUDIT STATE AFTER F365
------------------------------

Latest physical checkpoint — C031-WIP55

2. Then continue into player closeness/paranoia/floating-defender and Advanced Start
   helpers, looking for current scope/state/cache errors rather than retuning heuristic
   coefficients.

C031-WIP56 — F366 CONFIRMED
===============================================================================

F366 / provisional KI#689 — AI_advancedStartPlaceExploreUnits selects a sea
explorer as UNITAI_EXPLORE_SEA but hard-codes UNITAI_EXPLORE when purchasing it, so
Advanced Start naval explorers are initialized with the land-explorer AI role

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — AdvCiv regression introduced by advc.250c and present in Base AdvCiv 1.14
and current SAS. BtS/Civ4CE and K-Mod predate the explicit UnitAI argument and do not
contain this hard-coded-role regression.

ROOT
----
`AI_advancedStartPlaceExploreUnits(bool bLand)` correctly derives the requested role:

    UnitAITypes eUnitAI = NO_UNITAI;
    if (bLand)
        eUnitAI = UNITAI_EXPLORE;
    else
        eUnitAI = UNITAI_EXPLORE_SEA;

That variable is used throughout selection:

- nearby explorer counting asks for `eUnitAI`;
- `AI_bestAdvancedStartUnitAI(kCityPlot, eUnitAI)` selects a unit that is valuable for
  precisely that requested role.

But the purchase call discards the variable and always supplies the land role:

    doAdvancedStartAction(ADVANCEDSTARTACTION_UNIT,
            pBestExplorePlot->getX(), pBestExplorePlot->getY(), eBestUnitType, true,
            UNITAI_EXPLORE); // advc.250c

Thus `bLand == false` performs selection under `UNITAI_EXPLORE_SEA` and execution under
`UNITAI_EXPLORE`.

EXECUTION CONTRACT
------------------
The last `doAdvancedStartAction` argument is not decorative metadata. In current
`CvPlayer::doAdvancedStartAction`, the unit case does:

    UnitAITypes eUnitAI = (UnitAITypes)iData2;
    ...
    CvUnit* pUnit = initUnit(eUnit, iX, iY, eUnitAI);

`CvPlayer::initUnit` then uses exactly that supplied role unless it is `NO_UNITAI`:

    pUnit->init(...,
        (eUnitAI == NO_UNITAI ? GC.getInfo(eUnit).getDefaultUnitAIType() : eUnitAI),
        ...);

There is no validation that a supplied `UNITAI_EXPLORE` is appropriate for a naval
unit. Therefore the mismatch survives unit creation exactly as written.

CURRENT-DATA PRODUCER
---------------------
The sea branch is live whenever Advanced Start reaches the Age of Exploration:

    AI_advancedStartPlaceExploreUnits(false);

Current SAS contains multiple units accepted for `UNITAI_EXPLORE_SEA`, including
Galley, Galleon, Trireme, Frigate, Destroyer and Attack Submarine. Their normal/default
naval roles are sea UnitAIs; none requires the land `UNITAI_EXPLORE` role selected by
the buggy purchase call.

A straightforward reproduction is therefore:

1. start an AI with enough Advanced Start points in an era where sea exploration is
   enabled and with a coastal city / useful unrevealed water area;
2. `AI_bestAdvancedStartUnitAI(..., UNITAI_EXPLORE_SEA)` selects a legal naval explorer;
3. the purchase call passes `UNITAI_EXPLORE`;
4. `initUnit` stores that land-explorer role on the newly created naval unit.

LIVE CONSEQUENCE
----------------
`CvUnitAI::AI_update` dispatches directly on the stored UnitAI:

    case UNITAI_EXPLORE:
        AI_exploreMove();
        break;
    ...
    case UNITAI_EXPLORE_SEA:
        AI_exploreSeaMove();
        break;

The wrongly initialized ship therefore executes the land-explorer routine instead of
the dedicated naval routine.

This affects more than naming:

- `AI_exploreSeaMove` has dedicated naval threat/retreat handling;
- it checks `AI_isExcessSeaExplorers`, sea-role obsolescence and the sea-specific
  transformation chain (Worker/Pirate/Assault/Settler/Missionary/Reserve Sea);
- sea explorer demand/counting uses `UNITAI_EXPLORE_SEA`, so the purchased ship is not
  counted as fulfilling the role it was bought to fill;
- the land `AI_exploreMove` instead uses `UNITAI_EXPLORE` counts and land-explorer
  retirement/attack logic even though the physical unit is naval.

The AI can consequently spend Advanced Start points specifically to fill sea-exploration
demand and immediately create a unit that both follows the wrong behavior tree and
remains invisible to that sea-role count, encouraging further incorrect demand.

INTRODUCTION / ANCESTRY
-----------------------
BtS/Civ4CE and K-Mod call:

    doAdvancedStartAction(..., eBestUnitType, true);

with no explicit UnitAI override. The normal `initUnit` default-role mechanism therefore
remains in control there.

AdvCiv commit dde66d276082911b61d2b966fc0b6cb347270f82, practical commit 1472,
title:

    AI explore units in Adv. Start, bugfix unit layer colors

introduced advc.250c's extra `iData2` argument and changed the unit action to initialize
with that explicit UnitAI. In the very same diff, the explorer purchase call was changed
to:

    ..., true, UNITAI_EXPLORE);

without using the already-computed `eUnitAI`. That introduced the sea-branch regression.
Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS retain the hard-coded value.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
The surgical repair is simply to preserve the role already used for selection:

    doAdvancedStartAction(ADVANCEDSTARTACTION_UNIT,
            pBestExplorePlot->getX(), pBestExplorePlot->getY(), eBestUnitType, true,
            eUnitAI);

This keeps the intended advc.250c explicit-role feature for land explorers while making
the sea branch initialize as `UNITAI_EXPLORE_SEA`.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
This is independent of F341/F342. Those concern normal-game sea-explorer retirement and
explorer->worker transformation bookkeeping after a correctly typed
`UNITAI_EXPLORE_SEA` exists. F366 occurs earlier during Advanced Start creation and
assigns the wrong UnitAI in the first place.

It is also independent of the retracted GET_TEAM(PlayerTypes) hypothesis immediately
preceding this finding; the `CoreAI` overload control remains valid.

CURRENT AUDIT STATE AFTER F366
------------------------------

C031-WIP57 — F367 CONFIRMED
===============================================================================

F367 / provisional KI#690 — advc.036 mutates the shared `iExtraPop` argument while
iterating cities in AI_getHappinessWeight / AI_getHealthWeight, so an espionage effect
in one city changes how all later cities are valued

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — AdvCiv regression introduced by advc.036 and present in Base AdvCiv 1.14
and current SAS. BtS and K-Mod do not contain the espionage-counter adjustment that
creates the cross-city state leak.

ROOT
----
Both helpers take one empire-level input parameter:

    int iExtraPop

and then iterate every city. advc.036 added a city-specific adjustment for temporary
espionage anger / sickness, but writes the result back into that shared parameter:

    if (iExtraPop > 0)
        iExtraPop = std::max(0, iExtraPop -
                pLoopCity->getEspionageHappinessCounter() / 2);

and analogously for `getEspionageHealthCounter()`.

Once an earlier city reduces `iExtraPop`, every later city inherits the reduced value,
regardless of its own espionage counter. The helper therefore ceases to be a sum of
independent per-city valuations and becomes dependent on city iteration order.

INTRODUCTION / INTENDED CONTRACT
--------------------------------
AdvCiv practical commit 1287, commit ad5faf8aa2740b991c49d8f35e14769d190a4c71,
introduced this advc.036 adjustment. The source comment explains the intended local
reasoning:

    "By the time iExtraPop matters, the espionage effect will be gone."

The same commit adds the adjustment inside the per-city loop for both happiness and
health. Nothing in the change says that an espionage effect in city A should alter the
future-population assumption for city B. The appropriate state is therefore a local
per-city derivative, e.g.:

    int iCityExtraPop = iExtraPop;
    if (iCityExtraPop > 0)
        iCityExtraPop = std::max(0, iCityExtraPop -
                pLoopCity->getEspionageHappinessCounter() / 2);

and then use `iCityExtraPop` for that city only.

CURRENT PRODUCERS
-----------------
Nonzero `iExtraPop` is common in current strategic valuation. Examples include:

- tech health valuation:

      AI_getHealthWeight(kTech.getHealth(), 1)

- tech happiness valuation:

      AI_getHappinessWeight(kTech.getHappiness(), 1)

- early-religion valuation:

      AI_getHappinessWeight(1, 2)

- multiple civic / war-weariness / trade valuation paths also pass 1 or larger values.

A minimal current reproduction therefore needs only two ordinary cities and one
city-specific espionage counter:

1. evaluator calls `AI_getHappinessWeight(..., 1)`;
2. city A is visited first and has `getEspionageHappinessCounter() >= 2`;
3. A changes the shared `iExtraPop` from 1 to 0;
4. city B has no espionage happiness counter at all;
5. B is nevertheless evaluated with `iExtraPop == 0` rather than the caller's 1.

If B is visited before A, B instead sees 1. Identical empire state can therefore produce
a different result solely from city iteration order / city-list ordering.

LIVE CONSEQUENCE
----------------
`iExtraPop` is used in several material terms of each city's score:

- `unhappyLevel(iExtraPop)` / `badHealth(false, iExtraPop)`;
- percent-happiness/health population scaling;
- the advc.036 severe-unhappiness / severe-unhealth correction.

So the leak is not merely an unused temporary. It changes the returned empire-average
happiness/health weight and therefore downstream tech, civic, religion, war-weariness
and other AI valuations.

The direction can also vary with city order: a temporary espionage effect in one city
can suppress the extra-pop assumption for all later unaffected cities, undervaluing or
otherwise distorting happiness/health effects across the empire.

ANCESTRY
--------
BtS/Civ4CE and K-Mod contain the underlying happiness/health helpers but do not perform
this advc.036 espionage-counter rewrite of `iExtraPop`. AdvCiv introduced the mutation
and Base AdvCiv 1.14/current SAS retain it unchanged. This is therefore an inherited
AdvCiv root, not SAS-local.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Keep the caller's `iExtraPop` immutable throughout the loop. Derive a local value for
each city:

    int iCityExtraPop = iExtraPop;
    if (iCityExtraPop > 0)
        iCityExtraPop = std::max(0, iCityExtraPop -
                pLoopCity->getEspionageHappinessCounter() / 2);

and use `iCityExtraPop` consistently for all formulas concerning that city. Apply the
same pattern to the health helper.

This preserves advc.036's intended temporary-espionage adjustment without leaking one
city's state into the next.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
This is independent of F355's event building-happiness multiplicity bug. F355 concerns
an event evaluator losing BuildingClass multiplicity; F367 is a general cross-city
mutable-state bug in the reusable happiness/health helper itself.

It is also independent of the preceding `AI_doEnemyUnitData` own-unit question, which
remains unpromoted because the baseline friendly-unit contribution may be intentional
smoothing/prior behavior and lacks a sufficiently explicit exclusion contract.

CURRENT AUDIT STATE AFTER F367
------------------------------

C031-WIP58 — F368 CONFIRMED
===============================================================================

F368 / provisional KI#691 — AI_getPlotAirbaseValue increments `iOtherCityCount` only
when a newly visited foreign city/airbase is closer than every previous one, so the
score counts traversal-order record minima rather than the number of nearby targets

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — inherited BtS root, present in Civ4CE/BtS, K-Mod, Base AdvCiv 1.14 and
current SAS. AdvCiv later changed the traversal/API representation but retained the
same misplaced count increment.

ROOT
----
The helper tracks both nearest-distance state and a count:

    int iMinOtherCityDistance = MAX_INT;
    int iOtherCityCount = 0;

For each revealed foreign/other airbase, current AdvCiv does:

    int iDist = it.currPlotDist();
    if (iDist < iMinOtherCityDistance)
    {
        iMinOtherCityDistance = iDist;
        iOtherCityCount++;
    }

The final score then explicitly scales by that supposed count:

    int iValue = iOtherCityCount * 50;

Therefore `iOtherCityCount` is not actually a count of nearby foreign cities/airbases.
It is the number of times traversal happens to encounter a new record-low distance.

CURRENT ITERATION MAKES THE UNDERCOUNT ESPECIALLY CLEAR
--------------------------------------------------------
Current AdvCiv/SAS uses `SquareIter(kPlot, 4, false)`, whose documented traversal is a
clockwise spiral away from the center. Once a nearby foreign city/base has been seen,
subsequent targets at equal or greater distance cannot increment the count. Even within
the first occupied spiral ring, only a later target that happens to have a smaller
`plotDistance` than the first one can increment it.

Thus two, three or many ordinary nearby foreign cities can all produce
`iOtherCityCount == 1`. The result depends on traversal record minima, not physical
multiplicity.

BtS/Civ4CE and K-Mod use nested coordinate scanning rather than `SquareIter`, but contain
the same root:

    if (iDistance < iMinOtherCityDistance)
    {
        iMinOtherCityDistance = iDistance;
        iMinOtherCityPlot = pLoopPlot;
        iOtherCityCount++;
    }

so their result is likewise scan-order-dependent rather than a true count.

LIVE CONSEQUENCES
-----------------
Current C++ has three gameplay consumers:

1. `CvUnitAI::AI_getPlotDefendersNeeded`

       iNeeded += AI_getPlotAirbaseValue(kPlot) / 50;

   Each additional 50 points is treated as another defender requirement. Multiple
   nearby cities/bases that collapse to one record minimum therefore fail to increase
   Fort/airbase guard demand as intended by the score scale.

2. `CvUnitAI::AI_fortTerritory`

       iValue += (bAirbase ? kOwner.AI_getPlotAirbaseValue(kPlot) : 0);

   This directly ranks worker Fort/airbase sites. SAS currently defaults
   `SAS_AI_WORKER_FORT_AIRBASE_ENABLE` to 0, so this particular producer is disabled by
   default, but the helper remains a supported optional path and is not the only
   consumer.

3. `CvUnitAI::AI_airOffenseBaseValue`

   For an existing non-city airbase in peacetime:

       iValue = GET_PLAYER(getOwner()).AI_getPlotAirbaseValue(kPlot);
       iValue /= 6;

   Existing/captured/preplaced Forts therefore receive too little offensive-air base
   value when several foreign cities/bases are nearby.

Current Forts remain normal game objects (`IMPROVEMENT_FORT`, `bActsAsCity=1`), can be
built by humans, captured, pre-existing, or used when the SAS worker-Fort option is
restored. The default-disabled worker-construction path therefore reduces frequency but
does not make F368 dead.

CONCRETE SHAPE
--------------
Take an owned Fort with no adjacent friendly city and two revealed foreign cities within
radius 4. Suppose the outward traversal encounters a distance-2 city first and another
foreign city at distance 2 or 3 later.

Intended physical count:

    iOtherCityCount = 2
    base airbase value = 100

Current code:

    first city: 2 < MAX_INT  -> count = 1, min = 2
    second:     2/3 < 2      -> false
    final count = 1
    base airbase value = 50

The second city can consequently add no guard demand and no additional airbase-site/base
value at all.

CONTRACT / INTENT EVIDENCE
--------------------------
The naming and downstream arithmetic are unusually explicit:

- variable: `iOtherCityCount`;
- zero gate: `if (iOtherCityCount == 0) return 0;`;
- magnitude: `iOtherCityCount * 50`.

Nearest-distance state is tracked separately in `iMinOtherCityDistance` (and BtS also
tracked `iMinOtherCityPlot`). There is therefore no coherent reason for the count itself
to be updated only when the nearest-distance record changes.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Separate the two operations:

    iOtherCityCount++;
    if (iDist < iMinOtherCityDistance)
        iMinOtherCityDistance = iDist;

If the nearest-distance variables are genuinely no longer consumed (as in current
AdvCiv, where their old downstream code remains commented), the cleaner current repair
may simply count every qualifying foreign/other revealed airbase and remove the dead
minimum-distance state entirely.

The exact qualifying-object semantics (`isRevealedAirBase`, including Fort-like bases)
should be preserved; F368 concerns only the misplaced multiplicity increment.

DUPLICATE / ROOT SEPARATION
---------------------------
This is independent of SAS's later policy of disabling routine AI Fort construction by
default. That define controls one producer (`AI_fortTerritory`), whereas F368 is an
inherited valuation/counting defect with additional existing-Fort consumers.

It is also independent of F367's cross-city happiness/health state mutation.

CURRENT AUDIT STATE AFTER F368
------------------------------

Unique files complete — 30/169
Confirmed deep-reloop roots — F321 through F368

C031-WIP59 — F369 CONFIRMED
===============================================================================

F369 / provisional KI#692 — advc.079 stores one randomized "best attack unit" as the
last unit bragged about, but the diplomacy text independently reruns the randomized
selection when expanding [OUR_BEST_UNIT], so the remembered unit and the unit actually
shown to the player can differ

STATUS
------
CONFIRMED — AdvCiv regression introduced by practical commit 1439
`65a1472094e89d913ccf565c76687027a530a30d` ("Changes to AI greetings"). The underlying
`getBestAttackUnitKey` / asynchronous unit-selection randomness is inherited from BtS /
K-Mod; advc.079 newly made the selected UnitType persistent state without carrying that
same selection into text rendering.

ROOT
----
The advc.079 greeting code now asks for a candidate and stores it:

    UnitTypes eBragUnit = AI_getBestAttackUnit();
    ...
    if (eBragUnit != m_aeLastBrag[ePlayer])
    {
        m_aeLastBrag[ePlayer] = eBragUnit;
        return GC.getAIDiploCommentType("UNIT_BRAG");
    }

But none of the returned diplomacy state carries `eBragUnit`. The selected XML text
contains `[OUR_BEST_UNIT]`, e.g.:

    Our numberless [OUR_BEST_UNIT] shall crush ...

and `CvDllTranslator::replaceOur` resolves that token later by calling:

    kPlayer.getBestAttackUnitName(iForm)
      -> getBestAttackUnitKey()
      -> AI().AI_getBestAttackUnit()

This is a fresh, independent second evaluation.

The evaluation is intentionally asynchronous/randomized. `AI_getBestAttackUnit` calls
`CvCityAI::AI_bestUnitAI(UNITAI_ATTACK, true)`, and `AI_bestUnitAI` multiplies every
surviving candidate by an independent asynchronous random factor:

    if (bAsync)
    {
        iValue *= (GC.getASyncRand().get(50, "AI Best Unit ASYNC") + 100);
        iValue /= 100;
    }

Thus there is no invariant that the second text-rendering call returns the UnitType
stored by the first greeting-selection call.

CURRENT-DATA REACHABILITY
-------------------------
Current SAS has many simultaneously trainable `UNITAI_ATTACK` alternatives. A simple
early example is Axeman (strength 5) and Swordsman (strength 6) when the civ has both
required resources/technologies. Before the async multiplier, candidates below 2/3 of
the best are discarded, so these close alternatives both survive. A 100..149% random
multiplier is then easily large enough to reverse their ordering between two calls.

The same structural possibility occurs throughout the unit tree; this does not depend
on a scenario-only unit.

LIVE CONSEQUENCES
-----------------
1. The player can literally be shown a different unit from the one that advc.079 records
   as having just been bragged about.

   Example shape:

       greeting-selection call -> Axeman
       m_aeLastBrag[human] = Axeman
       text-rendering call      -> Swordsman
       visible line says        -> Swordsman

2. On the next contact, another randomized selection can return Swordsman. The new
   advc.079 test then sees:

       Swordsman != m_aeLastBrag[human] (Axeman)

   and treats this as a "new best unit", immediately producing another brag despite no
   technology, resource or trainability change at all.

3. Conversely, a real change in the best-unit set can be hidden or delayed if the
   randomized identity happens to equal the stored previous candidate.

This directly defeats the introducing commit's stated purpose: "When a braggart AI has
a new best unit, it brags about that unit at the first opportunity" and the memory is
supposed to reduce repeated greetings rather than create them from renderer randomness.

ANCESTRY / ROOT SEPARATION
--------------------------
BtS/Civ4CE and K-Mod already use the capital-first `AI_bestUnitAI(UNITAI_ATTACK, true)`
logic for the `[OUR_BEST_UNIT]` text. That can make the phrase "best" somewhat noisy,
but there is no persistent `last brag` identity to contradict.

advc.079 refactored that old computation into `AI_getBestAttackUnit`, added
`m_aeLastBrag`, and calls the helper while deciding whether a unit is new. The existing
text token remained dynamic and calls the same helper again. F369 is therefore the new
state/display mismatch created when a randomized display helper was reused as stable
memory identity.

This finding does NOT currently promote the separate inherited question that
`AI_getBestAttackUnit` returns the first capital-trainable attacker rather than searching
for a global maximum. That may make the textual notion of "best" inaccurate in some
city-local prerequisite states, but it is a separate contract and remains unnumbered.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Do not rerun a randomized selector when expanding the brag that has just been chosen.
Preserve the exact `eBragUnit` for the active greeting and feed that UnitType to the
rendered line, or otherwise make the identity used by `m_aeLastBrag` and
`[OUR_BEST_UNIT]` come from one evaluation.

A second possible cleanup would make the selector deterministic when used as persistent
identity, but that is broader: BtS deliberately used asynchronous selection for this
UI-facing helper. The minimal advc.079 repair is simply to keep selection and display
atomic.

CONTROLS CLOSED BEFORE F369
---------------------------
- Sibling-vassal Privateer targeting is deliberate. AdvCiv's manual explicitly says
  that the vassal/master Privateer restrictions do not apply to vassals of the same
  master.
- `AI_isUnitNeedingOpenBorders` may inspect the group's head unit for domain, but
  `CvUnit::canJoinGroup` enforces a single domain for all units in a selection group;
  there is no mixed-domain producer.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F370 / provisional KI#693 — Advanced Start city setup counts a failed
improvement purchase as successful, then can buy population against phantom
improved plots
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
`CvPlayerAI::AI_advancedStartPlaceCity` chooses the plot with the highest
`AI_getBestBuildValue`, calls the void Advanced Start action, and then increments
`iPlotsImproved` unconditionally:

    doAdvancedStartAction(ADVANCEDSTARTACTION_IMPROVEMENT,
            pBestPlot->getX(), pBestPlot->getY(), eBestImprovement, true);
    iPlotsImproved++;

There is no Advanced Start affordability check in the candidate loop and no
post-action verification that `pBestPlot` actually received `eBestImprovement`.

`CvPlayer::doAdvancedStartAction`, however, explicitly permits the action to fail
silently. For `ADVANCEDSTARTACTION_IMPROVEMENT` it computes
`getAdvancedStartImprovementCost`; if the action is legal but the player lacks
that many points, the function simply leaves the plot unchanged and returns to
the caller. Its return type is `void`, so success is not communicated.

The local counter therefore changes even when the game state does not.

SUPPORTED PRODUCER
------------------
This is reachable through ordinary AI Advanced Start. `AI_doAdvancedStart`
checks whether it can afford the city itself before calling
`AI_advancedStartPlaceCity`, but it does not reserve enough points for that
helper's preferred culture/improvements/population package. Later cities in the
city-budget loop can therefore enter the helper with only a small remainder.

Current SAS data makes an affordability split easy to construct. For example:

* `IMPROVEMENT_FARM` has `iAdvancedStartCost = 30`;
* SAS `ADVANCED_START_WORKER_BUILD_MODIFIER = 67`, so the base Farm portion is
  about 20 points at Normal build speed;
* removing `FEATURE_JUNGLE` adds its current Advanced Start removal cost of 40,
  making that Farm roughly 60 points before other speed adjustment;
* population is bought through the independent Advanced Start population-cost
  formula (BtS default `ADVANCED_START_POPULATION_COST = 150`). On ordinary
  Normal-speed/100%-growth settings, population 1 has a growth threshold of
  `20 + 2 = 22`, hence the next population point costs about 33.

A late Advanced Start city with, for example, a remainder between those costs
can therefore afford population but not the AI's highest-valued Jungle Farm.
The exact numeric remainder is not an exotic API state: `AI_doAdvancedStart`
spends the common point pool incrementally on cities, techs, visibility and the
city helper's own actions.

CONSEQUENCE
-----------
Suppose the city has no improved plots and the Jungle Farm is its current
highest `AI_getBestBuildValue` target, but the remaining points are below that
Farm's Advanced Start cost.

1. The improvement action is attempted and silently fails.
2. `iPlotsImproved` nevertheless rises from 0 to 1.
3. On the next pass the same still-unimproved high-value plot remains the best
   target. The action can fail again and `iPlotsImproved` rises again.
4. Once the phantom count exceeds city population, the helper's final loop uses
   the real city plot and can spend any still-affordable points on population:

       while (iPlotsImproved > pCity->getPopulation())
       {
           int iPopCost = getAdvancedStartPopCost(true, pCity);
           ...
           doAdvancedStartAction(ADVANCEDSTARTACTION_POP,
                   pPlot->getX(), pPlot->getY(), -1, true);
       }

The AI can therefore grow a city because of improvements that do not exist.
Because candidate selection is based on build value rather than purchasability,
it can also keep retrying the same unaffordable high-value improvement while a
cheaper lower-valued improvement could actually have been bought with the
remaining points.

This is a genuine execution-state mismatch, not merely a subjective Advanced
Start allocation heuristic: the loop variable is explicitly named/counting
`iPlotsImproved`, and the runtime plot remains unimproved.

ANCESTRY
--------
The same unconditional post-action `iPlotsImproved++` structure is present in
BtS/Civ4CE, K-Mod, Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS. AdvCiv modernized iterators
and Advanced Start costs but preserved this state assumption. Classification:
inherited BtS Advanced Start execution-vs-assumed-success defect.

No existing current KI/F321-F369 root found for this behavior. Earlier Advanced
Start album items concern tech-refund reachability/cache effects, first-city
callbacks, or F366's forced land `UNITAI_EXPLORE` assignment; none owns failed
improvement purchases being counted as successful.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
The stronger repair is to make the candidate/action state coherent rather than
merely patch the later population loop:

* before selecting/attempting an improvement, require
  `getAdvancedStartImprovementCost(eImprovement, true, pLoopPlot)` to be
  nonnegative and no greater than the current Advanced Start points; and/or
* after the action, increment `iPlotsImproved` only if the plot now actually has
  `eBestImprovement`.

Skipping unaffordable candidates is preferable because it lets the AI consider
a cheaper second-best improvement instead of repeatedly retrying an action that
cannot execute. A post-action verification remains useful defensive hardening
because `doAdvancedStartAction` is void and can reject actions for other
legality/state reasons.

CONTROL NOTE
------------
The immediate population action inside the improvement loop uses the improved
plot coordinates rather than the city plot, so it is normally a no-op when that
plot is not itself a city. The later `while (iPlotsImproved > population)` loop
uses the city plot correctly. That oddity does not rescue F370; it makes the
phantom count survive until the later real population-purchase loop.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
F371 / provisional KI#694 — Advanced Start building phase treats one
unaffordable selected building as a global "done" state, so it can terminate
before later passes expose cheaper affordable buildings
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

ROOT
----
`CvPlayerAI::AI_doAdvancedStart` uses `bDoneBuildings` both as the outer-loop
termination condition and as a per-city affordability result:

    bool bDoneBuildings =
            (iLastPointsTotal - getAdvancedStartPoints() > iCityPoints);

    for (int iPass = 0; iPass < 10 && !bDoneBuildings; ++iPass)
    {
        FOR_EACH_CITYAI(pLoopCity, *this)
        {
            BuildingTypes const eBuilding =
                    pLoopCity->AI_bestAdvancedStartBuilding(iPass);
            if (eBuilding != NO_BUILDING)
            {
                bDoneBuildings = (iCityPoints < iLastPointsTotal -
                        (getAdvancedStartPoints() -
                        getAdvancedStartBuildingCost(
                                eBuilding, true, pLoopCity)));

                if (!bDoneBuildings)
                {
                    doAdvancedStartAction(
                            ADVANCEDSTARTACTION_BUILDING,
                            pLoopCity->getX(), pLoopCity->getY(),
                            eBuilding, true);
                }
                else
                {
                    //continue. there might be cheaper buildings
                    //in other cities we can afford
                }
            }
        }
    }

The condition itself is a valid projected-budget test for that particular
building. The defect is storing the result in the global phase-termination
flag.

`CvCityAI::AI_bestAdvancedStartBuilding(iPass)` deliberately changes what it is
willing to select across passes:

    pass 0: FOOD
    pass 1: + PRODUCTION
    pass 2: + EXPERIENCE
    pass 3: + HAPPY | HEALTHY
    pass 4+: + GOLD | RESEARCH | MAINTENANCE | (normally) ESPIONAGE

The threshold also falls from 20 to 0 across passes.

Therefore, "the selected building for this city on this pass exceeds the
remaining city budget" does not imply "no later-pass building is affordable."
Yet if that unaffordable candidate leaves `bDoneBuildings == true` at the end
of the city traversal, the outer loop terminates and those later selector
passes are never run.

The source comment already acknowledges the missing implication -- "there
might be cheaper buildings ... we can afford" -- but only continues the
current city traversal. It does not protect the next `iPass`.

SUPPORTED CURRENT-DATA SHAPE
----------------------------
Current SAS has an ordinary generic cost/focus split that demonstrates the
problem without relying on a mod-mod edge case:

* `BUILDING_COLOSSEUM`
  - production cost 90
  - Advanced Start cost percent 100
  - +1 happiness
  - prerequisite `TECH_CONSTRUCTION`

* `BUILDING_LIBRARY`
  - production cost 80
  - Advanced Start cost percent 100
  - +25% research
  - prerequisite `TECH_WRITING`
  - not a free start-era building until the Renaissance

`CvPlayer::getAdvancedStartBuildingCost` starts from production cost times the
building's Advanced Start percent and then applies AdvCiv's 1.5 multiplier.
On Normal speed, absent a city-specific production modifier, these are about:

    Colosseum: 90 * 1.5 = 135 points
    Library:   80 * 1.5 = 120 points

A pre-Renaissance Advanced Start city that knows both prerequisite techs and
currently values happiness can therefore reach the building phase with a
remaining city-budget allowance between 120 and 134 points.

On pass 3, the happiness/health focus can select the Colosseum. Its projected
135-point purchase exceeds the remaining city budget, so the code assigns
`bDoneBuildings = true` and does not buy it.

Pass 4 is exactly where RESEARCH is added to the selector. A 120-point Library
could be legal and affordable there, but pass 4 never executes because the
outer loop sees the `true` value left by the unaffordable pass-3 candidate.

The exact remainder does not require a special API state. `AI_doAdvancedStart`
uses one shared point pool and reaches the building phase only after incremental
spending on cities, improvements/population, visibility, technology, explorers
and routes. The city-budget remainder is not constrained to building-cost
multiples.

MULTI-CITY ORDER DEPENDENCE
---------------------------
The same variable is overwritten for every city that returns a building
candidate:

    bDoneBuildings = projectedPurchaseExceedsBudget;

Consequently, in a multi-city empire the decision to run the next building
pass can depend on which candidate-bearing city happens to be visited last.

For example, on the same pass:

* City A's selected building is affordable -> `bDoneBuildings = false`;
* City B's selected building is unaffordable -> `bDoneBuildings = true`.

If B is the last relevant city, the whole building phase stops after the pass.
If a later city instead has an affordable candidate, that later assignment can
reset the flag to false and the next pass runs.

Thus the flag is neither a monotonic "budget exhausted" state nor an
all-cities affordability result. It is effectively the affordability result of
the last candidate that happened to overwrite it.

CONSEQUENCE
-----------
The AI can leave Advanced Start points unspent on useful buildings even though
a later focus pass would identify an affordable legal building.

This is not merely a disagreement with building valuation. The ten-pass design
explicitly broadens the candidate set over time; F371 can prevent those
designed passes from executing at all based on the cost of one earlier selected
candidate.

The effect is strongest near the end of the city/economic budget, where an
expensive happiness/health building can block a cheaper research, maintenance
or espionage building that only becomes eligible on the next pass.

ANCESTRY
--------
The same `bDoneBuildings` structure and the same explanatory comment are present
in BtS/Civ4CE, K-Mod, Base AdvCiv 1.14 and current SAS. AdvCiv reformatted the
condition but preserved the control flow.

Classification: inherited BtS Advanced Start budget/control-flow defect.

This is independent of F370. F370 is an execution-state mismatch inside
`AI_advancedStartPlaceCity` where a failed improvement purchase increments
`iPlotsImproved`. F371 is a separate building-phase termination error even when
every attempted building action succeeds exactly as requested.

REPAIR DIRECTION
----------------
Do not use one candidate's affordability as the global outer-loop done flag.

A conservative repair is:

1. Keep the initial "city budget already exhausted" test if desired.
2. For each selected building, compute the projected city-budget spending.
3. If that particular building would exceed the budget, `continue` to the next
   city/candidate instead of setting a persistent phase-done state.
4. Allow the bounded later passes to run so that their broader focus flags can
   expose cheaper alternatives.

For example, conceptually:

    if (projectedCitySpending > iCityPoints)
        continue;

    doAdvancedStartAction(...);

Because the loop already has a hard ten-pass bound, no global "one selected
building was too expensive" flag is needed to prevent an infinite loop.

A stronger cleanup could track whether any building was purchased in a pass,
but "nothing was bought on pass N" still should not automatically terminate
before pass N+1 while the selector is intentionally gaining new focus flags.
Any early-exit optimization therefore needs a real proof that no later pass can
introduce a new affordable candidate.

CONTROLS CLOSED DURING THIS SLICE
---------------------------------
* The other void Advanced Start actions do not all share F370's false-state
  consequence. In particular, the final tech loop and the building action's
  projected-budget inequality imply affordability before execution; the
  earlier/interleaved tech attempts can fail when the common point pool is
  depleted, but the local variables changed afterward are allocation
  heuristics rather than a false representation of purchased game state. No
  independent F372 was assigned there in this slice.

* `AI_bestAreaUnitAIValue` does select only one representative city for a
  non-null area and can therefore miss a unit with a city-local prerequisite
  that is trainable elsewhere in the same area. Current SAS has Factory-gated
  Tanks that make the general hazard real, but the area-scoped sea/air cleanup
  consumers do not currently intersect such a local prerequisite. The only
  current-data intersection established here is K-Mod's gifted combat-unit
  valuation. That remains an inherited approximation / mod-mod hazard, not a
  numbered root at this checkpoint.

* `AI_getRankDifferenceAttitude`'s `iMajorCivsAlive - 1` denominator is protected
  on its live cached-attitude path: `AI_updateAttitude` asserts both participants
  are major civs and requires both to be alive before the rank helper is
  reached. No zero-divisor producer was established.
